# Agent Builder Lifecycle

An agent is the culmination of everything in the platform — it ties together prompts, skills (plugins, workflows, AI tasks), knowledge (documents, collections), deployments, and testing. Building an agent well requires reading and cross-referencing EVERY relevant skill doc, iteratively gathering information from the user, validating feasibility against the live platform, and testing at every milestone.

## Skills to Load Before Starting

When a user asks to build an agent, load ALL of these before doing anything:

| Skill | Why |
|---|---|
| `nexus-agent-management/SKILL.md` | Agent CRUD, tool configs, versions |
| `nexus-prompt-assistant/SKILL.md` + `AGENT_CONVERSATION_GUIDE.md` | Prompt generation |
| `nexus-prompt-assistant/reference/pa-system-prompt-summary.md` | What the PA asks (6 sections, ~14 questions/skill) |
| `nexus-prompt-assistant/reference/pa-output-schema.json` | JSON schema the PA populates |
| `nexus-prompt-assistant/reference/example-agent-spec.json` | Gold-standard example of a complete spec |
| `nexus-tool-connection/SKILL.md` | Marketplace discovery, credential validation |
| `nexus-knowledge-base/SKILL.md` | Documents, collections, knowledge vs skill mode |
| `nexus-skills-and-tasks/SKILL.md` | AI task creation |
| `nexus-workflow-builder/SKILL.md` | Workflow building |
| `nexus-deployments/SKILL.md` | Channel setup |
| `nexus-emulator/SKILL.md` | Testing |
| `nexus-workflow-builder/reference/internet-search-guide.md` | Search provider decision guide (load when agent/workflow needs internet search) |

## The Phases

Each phase has a **GATE** — explicit user confirmation or test pass required before proceeding.

### Phase 1: Validate Agent Concept (GATE: user confirms)

Before doing ANY work, validate the concept with the user:
1. Summarize: agent name, role, who it serves, what it does
1b. **Audience check** — list every distinct audience that will converse with it; ≥2 audiences × different task-types → propose the SPLIT (one agent per audience) HERE, before Phase 2 — splitting after PA re-does Phases 2-3 (→ SKILL.md "One agent or two?").
2. List skills/tools it will need (high-level)
3. **Knowledge GATE.** List knowledge sources. For domain-authority agents (legal/policy/medical/regulated/product-spec/brand/pricing), KB is **REQUIRED** — ASK if user didn't mention. See `NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md` Dimension 5 + CLAUDE.md G#16 (named-but-absent → acquisition fork via `nexus-knowledge-base/SKILL.md` Q0).
4. List deployment channel(s)
5. **For AI tasks the agent will use:** Define each task's single purpose. If a task does analysis AND generation, it must be split into two tasks (see workflow builder one-purpose rule). Mark new tasks as PA REQUIRED.
6. Ask: "Does this match what you had in mind?"

WRONG: Jumping straight to marketplace searches, credential lookups, or PA conversations.
RIGHT: Getting a 2-sentence confirmation that the agent concept is correct first.

### Phase 2: Iterative Discovery + Validation (GATE: user confirms complete spec)

For each planned skill, run the discovery-validation loop:

```
DISCOVER → VALIDATE against platform → COME BACK to user with findings → REFINE → repeat
```

**Per skill type:**

| Skill Type | Validation Steps | Skills to Read |
|---|---|---|
| PLUGIN | `nexus tool search` → tool exists? → `nexus tool get` → actions[] non-empty? → specific action exists? → `nexus tool credentials` → credential valid? → present findings to user | tool-connection, agent-management |
| WORKFLOW | Each node type has GUIDE.md → each plugin node validated as PLUGIN above → AI task nodes have existing tasks → trigger type confirmed with user | workflow-builder, tool-connection, skills-and-tasks |
| AI TASK | Input/output schema defined with user → model selected → **PA REQUIRED** (see prep step below) | skills-and-tasks, prompt-assistant |
| KNOWLEDGE | Source identified (file/URL/text) → document accessible → collection nameable → correct attachment method decided (knowledge vs skill — see Phase 6) | knowledge-base, agent-management |
| INTERNET SEARCH | Need structured data about known entity? → Parallel Task. Need to DISCOVER unknown entities? → Parallel Find All. Simple Q&A? → Perplexity plugin. Ask user about cost tolerance. | workflow-builder (internet-search-guide.md, parallel-ai GUIDE.md, parallel-output-schema-guidelines.md) |

**If validation fails** (action doesn't exist, credential expired, tool not in marketplace): come back to the user with findings and propose alternatives. Don't silently drop or assume.

**PA preparation step (for every new agent):**

Before proceeding to Phase 3, prepare the PA first message using the validated spec from Phase 2:

1. **Identify all skills** the agent will have — plugins, workflows, AI tasks, collections
2. **For each skill, prepare:** SkillId (name), BusinessPurpose, UserParameters (names + types), TriggerPhrases (3+ examples), ConfirmBeforeAction (yes/no), ExecutionStyle (sync/async)
3. **Prepare agent identity:** name, role, persona, tone, communication style
4. **Note any validated constraints:** from tool searches, credential checks, collection decisions
5. **Write the PA first message draft** — this becomes your opening message in Phase 3

WRONG: Arriving at Phase 3 with "I'll figure out the PA message as I go."
RIGHT: Arriving at Phase 3 with a drafted first message covering identity, all skills at depth, and tone — ready to paste.

**Build the spec** matching the PA output schema depth. Read `pa-system-prompt-summary.md` — the PA asks ~14 questions per skill covering: SkillId, BusinessPurpose, UserParameters (with types, validation, defaults), TriggerPhrases, ConfirmBeforeAction, ExecutionStyle, OperationalGuidelines (Optimizations, Prohibitions, BestPractices, CommonMistakes), AgentBehavior (confirmation, progress, success message), BusinessRules (permissions, limits, hours), ErrorMessages (6 types), Examples (conversation flows), RelatedSkills.

Read `example-agent-spec.json` to calibrate the expected depth.

Present the complete spec to the user section by section. Get explicit confirmation before proceeding.

WRONG: Presenting a 4-line table with skill names and calling it "validation."
RIGHT: Walking through each of the 6 PA sections with the user, getting confirmation on each.

### Phase 3: PA Conversation (GATE: non-generic prompt generated)

Read `AGENT_CONVERSATION_GUIDE.md` before starting.

Rules:
- Have the FULL multi-turn conversation (12-20 turns). NEVER cram everything into one message.
- Answer PA questions from the validated spec. Escalate business judgment questions to the user via AskUserQuestion.
- Keep pushing the conversation until the PA presents a final confirmation and generates. Don't stop at "generating" status with empty response.
- After generation: verify the prompt is substantive (not generic). Red flags: under 500 words, placeholder language, vague skill sections, generic tone adjectives. If generic, start a NEW thread.
- **Hard cap: 2 PA threads.** After 2 generic results, STOP PA and write the prompt manually from the spec assembled in Phases 1+2 (R#31 Escape Hatch 2: `nexus agent update <id> --body '{"prompt":"..."}' --json`). The goal is a wired agent, not a PA conversation.
- Save the generated prompt to a file. Present a summary to the user before applying.
- Compare skill references in the prompt against planned tool config labels — they must match.

### Phase 4: Create Agent + Set Model (GATE: agent responds correctly)

1. `nexus agent create --first-name ... --last-name ... --role ... --json`
2. **IMMEDIATELY** check available models: `nexus model list --json`
3. **IMMEDIATELY** set the model — CLI-created agents have NO model by default. Run `nexus model list --json` to find the frontier model, then set it:
   ```bash
   nexus agent update <agentId> --body '{"modelConfig":{"modelName":"<FRONTIER_FROM_LIST>","modelProvider":"OPEN_AI"}}'
   ```
4. Apply the generated prompt via versions API:
   ```bash
   nexus version create <agentId> --body '{"name":"v1.0","prompt":"<promptResult.prompt>","objective":"...","tone":"..."}'
   ```
5. Create a test deployment: `nexus deployment create --name "Test" --type API --agent-id <agentId>`
6. **TEST**: Send "Hello" via emulator. Verify the agent responds with the right tone.

WRONG: Creating the agent and moving straight to skills without verifying it can respond.
RIGHT: Verifying the agent responds before attaching any skills.

### Phase 5: Attach Skills — Test Each One (GATE: each skill works individually)

For each skill, follow the type-specific flow in `nexus-agent-management/SKILL.md`, then TEST IMMEDIATELY.

| After attaching... | Test by... |
|---|---|
| PLUGIN tool config | `nexus api POST /agents/:id/tools/:toolId/test --body '{"input":{...}}'` OR emulator message that triggers it |
| WORKFLOW tool config | Emulator message that should trigger the workflow |
| TASK tool config | `nexus task execute <taskId> --input '...'` to verify output structure |

After each test:
- If it works → proceed to next skill
- If it fails with a config error (wrong credential, bad param type) → **FIX IT immediately**, then retest
- If it fails with a 500 → file a ticket, note it as blocked, proceed to next skill

Verify tool config labels match what the prompt references. If the prompt says "the log-to-sheets capability" and the label is `log_to_sheets`, that's fine — the platform handles the mapping. But if names are completely different, update the prompt or label.

**Plugin parameter types**: The API accepts `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `object`, `array`. NOT `integer` (use `number`) or `string[]` (use `array`).

### Phase 6: Attach Knowledge (GATE: agent answers from KB)

Two attachment methods — choose the right one:

| Method | API | Runtime | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Knowledge** (always injected) | `nexus api POST /agents/:id/collections --body '{"collectionIds":["..."]}'` | Content ALWAYS in agent's prompt context | FAQ, policies, small reference docs |
| **Skill** (on-demand search) | `nexus agent-tool attach-collection --collection-id ... --label ...` | Agent searches ONLY when it decides to | Large document sets, product catalogs |

WRONG: Using `attach-collection` (skill) for a 10-page FAQ the agent should always know.
RIGHT: Using `nexus api POST /agents/<id>/collections` (knowledge) for always-needed content.

After attaching, TEST: send a knowledge question via emulator. Verify the agent answers from the collection, not from general knowledge.

### Phase 7: Deploy + Integration Test (GATE: end-to-end works)

1. Create deployment (read channel guide first — EMBED requires `--body '{"settings":{}}'`)
2. Run a full test scenario via emulator:
   - Greeting → skill trigger → knowledge question → edge case → out-of-scope redirect
3. For each failure: diagnose → fix → retest. Don't file a ticket and move on unless it's a confirmed 500.

### Phase 8: Post-Creation Verification Checklist

**STRUCTURAL ARTIFACT** — per CLAUDE.md R#27 Agent-completion gate, "agent created/ready/live/deployed" status claims MUST emit this checklist as a Wiring Table. Any `❌` → cannot claim ready/done.

!! After each deliverable → hand the discovery triggers below to the silent background consolidation subagent (CLAUDE.md R#34); never emit a user-facing ledger. !!

```
- [ ] Agent has model set (modelName is not null)
- [ ] Agent has prompt (prompt field is not empty/generic)
- [ ] Every skill label has a matching reference in the prompt
- [ ] Every tool config has been tested with sample input
- [ ] Knowledge collections attached with correct method (per agent-management SKILL.md — DEFAULT knowledge)
- [ ] Knowledge search returns results (indexing complete)
- [ ] At least one deployment exists and is active
- [ ] End-to-end emulator test passes
- [ ] Systematic eval passed (Phase 9 — SIMULATED verdict PASS per load-bearing behaviour)
- [ ] Version checkpoint created: nexus version create <agentId> --name "v1.0"
- [ ] Dashboard link provided to user
- [ ] User action items listed (OAuth connections, document uploads, etc.)
```

**R#44 completeness gate (post-wiring-table):** verify the agent's artifact set per `nexus-workspaces/domains/systems/GUIDE.md "## Completeness gate (Tier-2)" → Agent archetype`. For org-specific filing under `$GENERAL_CONTEXT_PATH/systems/<system>/agents/<name>/`: `identity.md` + `system-prompt.md` + `tools.md` + `tools/<slug>.json` (per attached tool) + `deployment-variations.md` (REQUIRED iff prompt has any `::: section: deploymentSpecific=true :::` section) + `evaluation/` (once evaluated — Phase 9). Silent-block on missing artifacts (CLAUDE.md R#44). If 3-Q ricochet (R#34 + R#35 boundary) fires generalisable=YES → parallel write to `$SYSTEMS_PATH/agents/<archetype>/` w/ R#44 3-step anonymisation protocol applied (detail → `nexus-workspaces/reference/prompt-anonymisation-protocol.md`).

### Phase 9: Evaluate — Build Gate AND Change Gate (regression + intended behaviour)

!! Before claiming an agent ready, AND before publishing any behavioural change: `Skill(nexus-evaluations)` and read "Mode B" FULLY (the HOW lives there — commands, body shapes, end-signal rule, compare loop). No ready-claim and no behavioural-change publish without a passing eval. !! (Draft-stage behavioural EDITS: the done-CLAIM itself gates on an emulator run — `nexus-agent-management/SKILL.md "## Modifying an existing agent prompt"`.)

**WHY:** one manual emulator chat (Phase 8) cannot prove a guardrail holds, that helpfulness actually improved, or that a change didn't regress a different behaviour. **WHEN:** at first "ready", and on every later prompt/tool/model/version change.

**STRUCTURAL ARTIFACT** (R#27-style) — emit per load-bearing behaviour:

| Behaviour | Tester persona | Judge criterion | Run id | Verdict | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- **Reuse-first** — if the agent's archetype (`$SYSTEMS_PATH/agents/<archetype>/evaluation/`) or its general-context instance already has an eval suite, start from it. Else run the discovery in `nexus-evaluations/evaluation-archetypes/evaluation-creation-mode.md` to establish what matters.
- Build one tester-persona + judge-rubric PAIR per load-bearing behaviour (guardrails, helpfulness, scope, tone, tool-use), each designed to REACH the behaviour — a test that never triggers it scores nothing. ‼ End-signal rule: one intent per tester turn; emit the end-signal only AFTER the agent replies — a turn-0 end-signal scores 0 on a working agent.
- Run SIMULATED → read the verdict from `run.summaryText` (`run.verdict` is null). PASS per load-bearing behaviour required; gating flags (jailbreak/PII/fabricated-success/missed-escalation) hard-fail. Below threshold → fix prompt/tools and re-run.
- **On a change:** baseline → change → re-eval → `run compare --baseline`; ship only if no `regressed:true` AND the intended criterion improved. Evaluation is the agent's regression test, not a one-time build step.
- On PASS, file the eval suite to the workspace (real → general-context `…/agents/<name>/evaluation/`; anonymised → archetype per the anonymisation protocol).

**HOW** (authoring personas/rubrics, run/execute/results, the compare loop, the archetype patterns) → `Skill(nexus-evaluations)` "Mode B" + `evaluation-archetypes/`. Do NOT reproduce the mechanics here — load the skill.

--- name: nexus-agent-management description: Creates, configures, and manages Nexus AI agents, their tool configurations, prompt versions, and folder organization via the Nexus CLI. Use when the user asks to create agents, configure agent tools, manage prompt versions, organize agents in folders, or attach workflows/collections/tasks to agents. --- > Building agent from scratch? → `AGENT_BUILDER_LIFECYCLE.md` (9-phase gated process, incl. Phase 9 systematic eval). # Nexus Agent Management Translate user intent → `nexus` CLI. User = org admin, not dev. ## Boundary Check — Is This Actually an Agent? Verify request requires CONVERSATION before creating an agent. | User signal | Actually needs | Why | Redirect | |---|---|---|---| | "Every time X happens, do Y automatically" | Standalone WF | Auto trigger ≠ conv | `nexus-workflow-builder` | | "Monitor and alert me" | Scheduled WF | Monitoring is autonomous | `nexus-workflow-builder` | | "Process every email/call/lead" | WF (+ optional agent skill) | "Every" = systematic | Ask trigger Q first | | "Answer questions" / "chat about" / "help users with" | YES → agent | Conv = agent | Continue | | "Summarize/classify/extract this" | AI task (standalone or agent skill) | One-shot transform → AI task | Ask context Q | | Domain-authority (legal/policy/medical/regulated/brand/pricing) | Agent + **KB required** | Source grounding prevents hallucination | Phase-1 KB scoping per `NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md` Dim 5 | Non-conversational → do NOT ask "should I build a WF instead?" User can't evaluate. Instead: (1) ask 2–3 contextual Qs (which tool, output, event types); (2) teach w/ user's words ("'each of my calls' = runs automatically on every call → workflow"); (3) switch to `nexus-workflow-builder`. Conversation Test → R#17 (full WR pair canonical there). ## One agent or two? One agent per AUDIENCE × TASK-TYPE. Same task-type for the same audience = the SAME agent regardless of headcount (channel identity — phone number, email — distinguishes people; don't over-split). Different audience OR different task-type OR different lifecycle (a configure-once-per-type surface vs an always-on operator) = SEPARATE agents. One user noun often bundles both (R#17 bundle clause; probes → `NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md` Dimension 7). ✗ one fused agent where field staff submit data AND managers define formats/query results → one prompt serving two masters, both badly → ✓ an intake agent (field staff) + a designer/query agent (managers) + a shared store. ## Quick Start ```bash nexus agent create --first-name "Support" --last-name "Bot" --role "Customer Support" --json # 1. Create nexus model list --json # 2. Pick frontier model nexus agent update --body '{"modelConfig":{"modelName":"","modelProvider":"

"}}' --json nexus agent update --prompt ./prompt.md --json # 3. Apply PA prompt (R#31) nexus agent-tool create --label "send_email" --type PLUGIN --body '{...}' --json # 4. PLUGIN nexus agent-tool create --label "Order Lookup" --type WORKFLOW --body '{...}' --json # 5. WF (PUBLISHED) nexus agent-tool attach-collection --collection-id "" --label "Product Docs" --json # 6. Collection nexus version create --name "v1.0" --description "Initial" --json # 7. Checkpoint ``` Full lifecycle → `AGENT_BUILDER_LIFECYCLE.md`. ## Agent CRUD **Search before creating** — `nexus agent list --search "" --json`. Present matches (name/role/date/bio). | Decision | Action | |---|---| | Existing fits | `nexus agent duplicate ` | | Create new | PA-generated prompt per R#31, then create | | User pastes complete prompt | Skip PA, create directly | **Prompt assistant gate** → R#31. PA mandatory for every new agent unless user EXPLICITLY types/pastes a complete prompt. Detail → `nexus-prompt-assistant/AGENT_CONVERSATION_GUIDE.md`. ```bash nexus agent create --first-name "Sales" --last-name "Assistant" --role "Sales Rep" --prompt ./prompt.md --body '{ "shortBio": "Handles product inquiries", "tags": "sales,product", "modelConfig": { "modelName": "", "modelProvider": "ANTHROPIC", "temperature": 0.7 } }' --json ``` ‼ The agent API REMOVED `objective` + `tone` + `behaviour` (each 400s on create AND update: "fields have been removed… Set the system prompt via the \"prompt\" field instead" — probed 2026-07). Behavioural rules live IN the system prompt (`--prompt ./file.md` or `"prompt"` inside `--body`), never in those fields. **Model:** Use `modelConfig` (not legacy `model`). `nexus model list --json` first → `modelId`→`modelConfig.modelName`, `provider`→`modelConfig.modelProvider`. **Thinking level:** branch on `model.thinkingDialect` before setting `thinkingLevel` (R#8 — `nexus-getting-started/reference/thinking-dialects.md`). **Prompt:** `--prompt ./file.md` or `--body '{"prompt":"…"}'`. ```bash nexus agent list --limit 20 [--status ACTIVE] [--search "kw"] --json nexus agent get --json nexus agent update --body '{"field":"value"}' --json # partial nexus agent duplicate --json nexus agent delete --yes # → { id, deleted: true } nexus api POST /agents//profile-picture --file avatar.png nexus api POST /agents//generate-profile-picture --json # AI-generated ``` ## Modifying an existing agent prompt Editing a LIVE agent's system prompt is scan-heavy, multi-region, and feasibility-sensitive → **dispatch the `agent-prompt-modifier` agent (R#45), FOREGROUND**, passing ONLY `{agentId, change_request, prior_qa?, approved_plan?}`. It runs the full Cue modification doctrine (feasibility preflight H1–H7 · 6-category scan · region-consolidation · exact-match edits on a local copy · re-fetch verify) in its own context and returns ONE of: `done` · `needs_clarification` · `plan_for_approval` · `infeasible` · `blocked`. - Non-`done` → AUQ the user with the returned questions/plan, then re-dispatch with `prior_qa`/`approved_plan` (the modifier has no AskUserQuestion — it asks THROUGH you). - The modifier edits the DRAFT only. **YOU own publish:** a behavioural change → `Skill(nexus-evaluations)` regression FIRST (publish-stale, see Version Management), then `version publish` on PASS, AUQ before publishing. - Do NOT edit a live prompt inline yourself — you will miss the enforcement rules / examples / cross-refs the scan catches. CREATION of a new prompt routes to PA (R#31), never the modifier. - Fallback if the named agent isn't loaded (fresh session): `general-purpose` + "Read `.claude/agents/agent-prompt-modifier.md` COMPLETELY and follow it". Verified CLI shape the modifier relies on: `nexus agent get --json` → prompt at **top-level `.prompt`**, body has raw control chars (`jq` fails — python-decode per G#11); `nexus agent update --prompt --json` → wrapped `{success,id}` with NO prompt echo → re-fetch + **Save-transform diff** (R#20): DIFF refetched vs sent — the platform single-escapes raw backticks/underscores on save (benign, report it); ANY re-escaping of EXISTING backslashes = an escaping CASCADE → STOP editing + ticket. `wc -c` BEFORE writing — the server rejects `prompt` >1,000,000 chars. The platform auto-wraps plain markdown into `::: section: … :::` / `::: tab: … :::`; a stored section may carry ~5 attributes (no `activeTab`) — preserve EXACTLY what's there (structure + content; runaway ESCAPE ARTIFACTS are corruption, NOT content to preserve). User explicitly forbids subagents → apply this same doctrine INLINE (feasibility scan · region-consolidation · verify + Save-transform diff); the gates travel, not the vehicle. A behavioural change to a live/staging agent gates its "done/works/live" CLAIM on ≥1 emulator run reaching the changed behaviour — even when publish (and the regression eval) is deferred. ## Code-interpreter agents (basic vs code-interpreter — pick by OUTPUT shape) Nexus has two agent archetypes. Pick the archetype BEFORE building — it is an OUTPUT-SHAPE decision, not a tone preference, and it is costly to change after the prompt and tools are wired. | Archetype | What it is | Output profile | Prompting burden | |---|---|---|---| | **BASIC** | prompt + model + Nexus skills (workflows / AI tasks / collections) + knowledge + deployments | fixed / templated — a known set of shapes | low — the skills do the work | | **CODE-INTERPRETER** | a `code-interpreter-claude-*` model + Claude skills (executable code bundles) + workspace read/write + arbitrary code execution | near-infinite — shapes vary per request; real computation | higher — it writes and runs code | **The fork (decide at Phase 1):** - FIXED or templated document output (a recurring report, one of a known set of layouts) → **BASIC**. A near-blank HTML `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE` renders most Word/HTML output a basic agent needs — reach for code-interpreter ONLY when the need EXCEEDS that. A basic agent is more reliable and cheaper; do NOT over-reach. - NEAR-INFINITE / code-driven / computational office output — spreadsheets with live formulas, image or OCR work, multi-format pipelines, arbitrary code over uploaded files → **CODE-INTERPRETER**. ✗ a near-infinite report need → one workflow + a DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE per document type (never finishes, rigid) → ✓ recognise near-infinite/code-driven office output → a code-interpreter agent with the office skills. **Model class.** `nexus model list --json` exposes the `code-interpreter-claude-*` models; set one via `modelConfig` exactly like any model (`modelName` + `modelProvider`). A code-interpreter agent is distinguished by this model class plus the three added capabilities below. **Three added capabilities** (vs a basic agent): (1) **Claude skills** that execute code; (2) **workspace read/write** — the workspace is a first-class resource (lifecycle / mount / paths → `nexus-workspaces/SKILL.md`; see the "Workspace surface (orthogonal)" note below); (3) **arbitrary code** — a specialised, in-product Claude-Code-for-office. **Skill mechanism (concrete).** The ready **office skills** — `pptx`, `xlsx`, `docx`, `pdf` — are AVAILABLE in the tools community workspace at `$TOOLS_PATH/skills//` (each is a `SKILL.md` + its scripts); reference a skill by its workspace path. They are the baseline for document and spreadsheet output. A **CUSTOM** skill is authored with the **skill-creator** (Anthropic skills repo) — a skill is a `SKILL.md` plus scripts — and authoring a new skill is ONLY meaningful for a code-interpreter agent (a basic agent cannot execute one). **Attach reality (present-tense).** A skill bundle reaches a code-interpreter agent by being present in the workspace it reads. There is NO `nexus agent` / `agent-tool` flag that attaches a skill to a code-interpreter agent today — do NOT invent one, and do NOT claim an attach step that does not exist. State the gap plainly when it bears on a build. **When NOT to use it.** A reliable, narrow agent (fixed Q&A, templated output, a known set of tools) is a BASIC agent — building it as a code-interpreter agent adds cost, latency, and prompting burden for no gain. The senior-engineer test (R#32) applies: if a competent reviewer would call the code-interpreter machinery over-built for this output, it is. ## Tool Configurations Five types — each agent-tool needs `agentInputSchema` (JSON Schema for runtime inputs; `{}` if none). **Workspace surface (orthogonal):** when an agent reads/writes workspace files, the workspace itself is a separate first-class resource — lifecycle/mount/paths/multi-writer → `nexus-workspaces/SKILL.md`. Workspace assignment is independent of the 5 tool-config types below. **Channel-granted card tools (orthogonal):** an agent deployed on an EMBED web widget auto-gains `send_html_template_` (per stored template) + `send_message` + `display_html` — no tool-config needed; steering + template design → `nexus-deployments/channels/embed.md "## HTML Message Templates"`. | Type | Description | Key config fields | |---|---|---| | `PLUGIN` | Marketplace action (Gmail, Slack…) | `toolId`, `action`, `toolCredentialId` | | `WORKFLOW` | Org workflow as tool | `toolId` (workflow ID — ‼ MUST be PUBLISHED; DRAFT silently fails) | | `TASK` | AI task as tool | `toolId` (task ID) | | `COLLECTION` | KB search | `collectionId` via `attach-collection` shorthand | | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE` | Generate formatted doc | `toolId` (template ID) | ### PLUGIN — 7-step configuration **Preflight:** before attaching, run `nexus external-tool execute --action --input '{…}' --credential --json` standalone to prove `toolId`/`action`/`credential` work. Agent runtime failures are silent. Full → `nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`. **Credential-deferred builds ("create everything, connect later"):** a tool-config SHELL (`toolId` + `action` + `agentInputSchema` + `description`) is creatable WITHOUT `toolCredentialId`; the credential + dynamic action params resolve when the user connects it. Defer the credential as a user TODO; a shell is NOT runtime-ready — never claim it tested. 1. **Search + select tool.** `nexus tool search --query gmail --json` → user picks. Not in marketplace → `nexus-tool-connection/reference/custom-tool-integration-guide.md`. 2. **Select action.** `nexus tool get --json` → `actions[]` w/ `key`/`name`/`parameters`. Present ALL w/ recommended marked. ✗ `"action":"send-email"` / `"Send Email"` → silent failure → ✓ `"action":"gmail-send-email"` (verbatim `actions[].key`, Pipedream `{app}-{action-slug}`). 3. **Select credential.** `nexus tool credentials --json`. 0 → start OAuth flow; 1 → confirm; 2+ → present ALL w/ names+dates, user picks. ✗ auto-pick most recent → may belong to coworker → ✓ "Found 2: (A) Mar 2026, (B) Dec 2025. Which is yours?" ‼ Credential ids are PER-TOOL: the same external account yields a DIFFERENT credential id under each tool that wraps it — list via THIS tool's `tool credentials `, never reuse an id seen under another tool ("Credential not found or does not belong to this tool"). 4. **(opt) Scope w/ access card.** `nexus access-card available-actions --credential-id --json` → `nexus access-card create --credential-id --name "Send Only" --data '{"policies":{"gmail-send-email":{"parameters":{"to":{"enabled":true},"subject":{"enabled":true},"body":{"enabled":true}}}}}' --json`. ✗ `{"policies":{"allowedActions":[…]}}` → validates, then denies every real action → ✓ a MAP keyed by `actionId`. Unlisted action = denied; unlisted parameter = STRIPPED, so list every parameter the action needs. 5. **Decide parameter handling.** For each `actions[].parameters`: agent-configured → `agentInputSchema.properties`; manually pre-set → `config.parameters` as `{ "type":"…", "handler":"manual", "value": }`. Types: `string`/`number`/`boolean`/`object`/`array` — NOT `"integer"` / `"string[]"`. Agent-FILLED fields should be FLAT SCALARS — the model fills `string`/`number`/`boolean` reliably but passes null/partial for nested `object`/`array` via `handler:prompt`; a needed non-scalar → `handler:manual` preset, or have the agent pass a scalar id the workflow expands (Universal Gotcha #1 handler selection). 6. **Write `description` (<20 words).** Format: `"Use [tool] when [trigger]. You MUST set [param] with [description]."` Only mention agent-configured params. A REQUIRED runtime input the agent cannot know from conversation (a URL, an id, a slug) is a wiring decision: mark it `required` in `agentInputSchema` AND tell the agent where to GET it ("resolve from , or ask") — an undeclared hard input fails at runtime while the agent narrates a plausible-sounding answer over the failure. 7. **Create + test.** ```bash nexus agent-tool create --label "send_email" --type PLUGIN --body '{ "description": "Use send_email when user asks to send an email. You MUST set body with well-formatted HTML content.", "agentInputSchema": { "type":"object", "properties":{ "body":{"type":"string","description":"HTML email body"} }, "required":["body"] }, "config": { "toolId": "", "action": "gmail-send-email", "toolCredentialId": "", "parameters": { "to": { "type":"array", "handler":"manual", "value":["fixed@example.com"] }, "subject": { "type":"string", "handler":"manual", "value":"Fixed subject" } } } }' --json # Test (ask user first — side effects real): nexus api POST /agents//tools//test --body '{"input":{"body":"

Test

"}}' --json ``` `input` carries only agent-configured params; manual params apply automatically. ### WORKFLOW — must be PUBLISHED ```bash nexus agent-tool create --label "Process Invoice" --type WORKFLOW --body '{ "agentInputSchema": { "type":"object", "properties":{ "invoiceUrl":{"type":"string"} } }, "config": { "toolId": "" } }' --json ``` ### Knowledge Collections — TWO methods (DEFAULT = knowledge) | Discriminator | Knowledge (always-injected) | Skill (on-demand search) | |---|---|---| | Every answer in domain must cite / respect source? | ✓ YES → knowledge | NO | | Source consulted only on specific Qs? | NO | ✓ YES → skill | | Source >50k tokens AND consulted <30% of conversations | Consider chunking → skill | ✓ skill | | Command | `nexus api POST /agents//collections --body '{"collectionIds":[""]}'` | `nexus agent-tool attach-collection --collection-id --label --instructions ` | **DEFAULT: knowledge.** Switch to skill ONLY when source is large AND consulted occasionally (catalogs, archives). For the agent to actually USE it, the prompt's Knowledge section must carry the injection marker `%%%%` on its own line — at runtime it is replaced by the retrieved chunks. # Agent Collections

## Two Attachment Methods

Collections can be attached to agents in two fundamentally different ways:

| Method | API | Runtime Behavior | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Knowledge** (always injected) | `nexus api POST /agents/<id>/collections --body '{"collectionIds":["..."]}'` | Content ALWAYS included in agent's prompt context | FAQ, policies, pricing — small docs needed every conversation |
| **Skill** (on-demand search) | `nexus agent-tool attach-collection` | Agent searches ONLY when it decides to, based on tool description | Large knowledge bases, product catalogs — searched when relevant |

**Decision rule:** If the agent needs this information in EVERY conversation → knowledge mode. If only for specific questions → skill mode.

WRONG: Using skill mode for a 10-page FAQ — agent won't search unless it "decides" to.
WRONG: Using knowledge mode for 500 documents — wastes tokens injecting everything.

## Knowledge Mode (Always Injected)

```bash
# Attach
nexus api POST /agents/<agentId>/collections --body '{"collectionIds":["<collId>"]}' --json

# List
nexus api GET /agents/<agentId>/collections --json

# Detach
nexus api DELETE /agents/<agentId>/collections --body '{"collectionIds":["<collId>"]}' --json
```

### In-prompt injection marker (`%%collection%%`) — REQUIRED for the agent to actually use the knowledge

Attaching a collection (`POST /agents/<id>/collections`) only REGISTERS it — `GET /agents/<id>/collections` is the authoritative census of what is registered. Registration alone does NOT place the content in the prompt. The agent only SEES the knowledge where the prompt's Knowledge section carries the injection marker:

```
%%collectionName%%
```

At runtime the platform embeds the user's message, retrieves the top-N most similar chunks from that collection, and REPLACES the `%%collectionName%%` marker with those chunks as plain text. No marker → no injection point → the registered collection NEVER reaches the model context (the agent behaves as if it has no knowledge, even though `GET` shows it attached).

Placement rules:
- The marker MUST sit ALONE on its own line/paragraph (chunks replace it; mid-sentence placement produces garbled output).
- Put it in a dedicated Knowledge section with a one-line intro, e.g.:

  ```
  Knowledge you can draw on (retrieved per question):

  %%base_knowledge%%
  ```
- One marker per collection; multiple collections → separate blocks, never crammed together.

WRONG: collection attached via `POST /collections`, prompt says "answer from the attached knowledge base" but has no `%%...%%` marker → the agent has ZERO knowledge at runtime.
RIGHT: collection attached AND `%%base_knowledge%%` present on its own line in a Knowledge section → chunks injected per question.

Note: PA-generated prompts usually OMIT the marker (PA is not told the collection slug). After applying a PA prompt to an agent with an attached collection, add the marker — see the wiring-verification step in the main SKILL.md "## Post-Creation Testing".

## Skill Mode (On-Demand Search)

See "Knowledge Collections — Two Attachment Methods" in the main SKILL.md.

```bash
nexus agent-tool attach-collection <agentId> \
  --collection-id "<collId>" \
  --label "Product KB" \
  --instructions "Search when user asks about product features" --json
```

# Conversation context

## Fields agents / workflows reference

| Field | Where / How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `conversation.id` / `conversation.nanoId` | List + Get response | Both accepted as input on every `/conversations/:id` endpoint. `nanoId` (5+5 uppercase alnum, e.g. `WLOX3_P18X5`) is user-surface-safe; nullable on pre-migration rows. |
| `conversation.satisfaction.latest` | `nexus conversation get <id> --satisfaction latest --json` (typed). Shape: `{ id, framework, source, rawScore, score, reasoning, comment, createdAt } \| null`. Frameworks: `LEGACY_5_STAR \| NPS \| CSAT \| AI_PASSIVE \| CUSTOM`. Sources: `CUSTOMER_PROMPTED \| AI_PASSIVE \| LEGACY`. | Detractor escalation, NPS gates, negative-feedback routing. Default omits the field — must opt in. |
| `conversation.satisfaction` (summary) | `nexus conversation get <id> --satisfaction summary --json` — adds `totalCount` alongside `latest`. Counts only; the full array surface from earlier `?satisfaction=all` is retired. | Trend gating ("only escalate if `totalCount > 3`"). Most agents only need `.latest`. |

WRONG: agent prompt references `{{conversation.satisfaction.latest.score}}` w/o opting in to `--satisfaction latest` first → field absent at runtime.
RIGHT: workflow node fetches via `nexus conversation get <id> --satisfaction latest --json` → passes `satisfaction.latest.score` to the agent prompt as a downstream variable.

## Update conversation topic

`nexus conversation update-topic <id> --topic "<text>" --json` (1–500 chars; accepts UUID or nanoId). Returns updated conversation. Use for programmatic relabeling / topic-from-summary patterns.

## Channel-injected runtime variables

Real deployment channels inject sender/context vars the agent prompt / workflow params can reference. Populated by the CHANNEL (not `conversation.*`), and EMPTY in the emulator (test in-message).

| Var | Channel(s) | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{{customerPhone}}` | WhatsApp / SMS / voice | Sender's number — key for per-sender lookups. |
| `{{wa_id}}` | WhatsApp | Sender's WhatsApp id. |

WRONG: reference `{{customerPhone}}` in the emulator → empty → "the var is broken".
RIGHT: emulator → pass the number in-message; prod → reference `{{customerPhone}}` in the tool param/prompt.
(Var names per observed live builds; extend the table only as channels surface more — verified-runs only, R#36.)

nexus agent delete <agentId> [--yes]
```

**Response:**

```json
{ "id": "uuid", "deleted": true }
```

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

### Duplicate Agent

```bash
nexus agent duplicate <agentId> --json
```

No additional flags. Creates a copy with all configuration including prompt and tool configs.

**Response (201):** Full detail of the new agent.

**Status codes:** 201 Created, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

### Upload Profile Picture

```bash
nexus api POST /agents/<agentId>/profile-picture --file avatar.png
```

| Field | Type | Required | Notes               |
| ----- | ---- | -------- | ------------------- |
| file  | file | yes      | Image file (binary) |

**Response:**

```json
{ "profilePicture": "https://..." }
```

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 400 No file, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

## 2. Agent Tools (6 commands)

### List Agent Tools

```bash
nexus agent-tool list <agentId> --json
```

**Response:**

```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "label": "Gmail - Send Email",
      "description": "Send emails via Gmail",
      "iconUrl": "https://...",
      "iconType": "url",
      "type": "PLUGIN",
      "agentInputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {} },
      "config": { "toolId": "google_gmail", "action": "send-email", "toolCredentialId": "cred-id" },
      "isActive": true,
      "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": null
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Get Agent Tool

```bash
nexus agent-tool get <agentId> <toolId> --json
```

**Response:** Single tool config object (same shape as list items).

---

### Create Agent Tool

```bash
nexus agent-tool create <agentId> --label <label> --type <type> [--config <json>] [--body <json>] --json
```

| Flag     | Type   | Required | Notes                                                 |
| -------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| --label  | string | yes      | Display name, min 1 character                         |
| --type   | enum   | yes      | PLUGIN, WORKFLOW, TASK, COLLECTION, DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE |
| --config | json   | no       | Tool config fields as JSON                            |
| --body   | json   | no       | Full JSON body for advanced fields                    |

Additional fields via `--body`:

| Field            | Type    | Notes                                         |
| ---------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| description      | string  |                                               |
| iconUrl          | string  | Tool icon URL                                 |
| iconType         | string  | Icon type identifier                          |
| agentInputSchema | object  | JSON Schema for agent input; use `{}` if none |
| config           | object  | See tool config fields below                  |
| isActive         | boolean | Default true                                  |

**Config object fields:**

| Field            | Type   | Notes                                        |
| ---------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| toolId           | string | Marketplace tool ID, workflow ID, or task ID |
| collectionId     | string | Collection ID (for COLLECTION type)          |
| action           | string | Action key (for PLUGIN type)                 |
| toolCredentialId | string | Credential ID (for PLUGIN type)              |
| instructions     | string | Usage instructions for the agent             |
| parameters       | object | Parameter definitions (advanced)             |

**Response (201):** Created tool config.

**Status codes:** 201 Created, 400 Validation error, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Agent not found

---

### Update Agent Tool

```bash
nexus agent-tool update <agentId> <toolId> [--label] [--config <json>] [--body <json>] --json
```

All fields from Create are optional (partial update).

**Response (200):** Updated tool config.

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 400 Validation error, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

### Delete Agent Tool

```bash
nexus agent-tool delete <agentId> <toolId> [--yes]
```

**Response:**

```json
{ "id": "uuid", "deleted": true }
```

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

### Attach Collection (Shorthand)

```bash
nexus agent-tool attach-collection <agentId> --collection-id <id> [--label <label>] [--instructions <text>] [--body <json>] --json
```

| Flag            | Type   | Required | Notes                                    |
| --------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| --collection-id | string | yes      | Collection UUID                          |
| --label         | string | no       | Display name (auto-generated if omitted) |
| --instructions  | string | no       | Usage instructions for the agent         |
| --body          | json   | no       | Full JSON body for advanced fields       |

**Response (201):** Created tool config with type COLLECTION.

**Status codes:** 201 Created, 400 Validation error, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Agent not found

---

## 3. Agent Versions (7 commands)

### List Versions

```bash
nexus version list <agentId> [--type AUTO|CHECKPOINT] --json
```

| Flag   | Type | Required | Notes              |
| ------ | ---- | -------- | ------------------ |
| --type | enum | no       | AUTO or CHECKPOINT |

**Response:**

```json
{
  "versions": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "type": "CHECKPOINT",
      "name": "v1.0 - Initial",
      "description": "First checkpoint",
      "isProduction": true,
      "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "createdBy": "user-uuid",
      "creator": { "id": "user-uuid", "firstName": "John", "lastName": "Doe" }
    }
  ],
  "meta": { "total": 15, "page": 1, "hasMore": false }
}
```

---

### Get Version

```bash
nexus version get <agentId> <versionId> --json
```

**Response:** Version detail including `prompt` field.

```json
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "type": "CHECKPOINT",
  "name": "v1.0",
  "description": "...",
  "isProduction": true,
  "prompt": "You are a helpful assistant...",
  "createdAt": "...",
  "createdBy": "...",
  "creator": {}
}
```

---

### Create Checkpoint

```bash
nexus version create <agentId> [--name <name>] [--description <text>] [--body <json>] --json
```

| Flag          | Type   | Required | Notes                       |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------- |
| --name        | string | no       | Min 1 character if provided |
| --description | string | no       |                             |

Creates a named CHECKPOINT version from the agent's current prompt state.

**Response (201):** Version detail with prompt snapshot.

**Status codes:** 201 Created, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Agent not found

---

### Update Version

```bash
nexus version update <agentId> <versionId> [--name <name>] [--description <text>] --json
```

| Flag          | Type   | Required | Notes |
| ------------- | ------ | -------- | ----- |
| --name        | string | no       | Min 1 |
| --description | string | no       |       |

**Response (200):** Updated version detail.

---

### Delete Version

```bash
nexus version delete <agentId> <versionId> [--yes]
```

Cannot delete the production version. Unset isProduction first by publishing a different version.

**Response:**

```json
{ "id": "uuid", "deleted": true }
```

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 400 Cannot delete production, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

### Restore Version

```bash
nexus version restore <agentId> <versionId> [--yes]
```

No additional flags. Overwrites the agent's current prompt with this version's prompt snapshot.

**Response:**

```json
{
  "prompt": "The restored prompt content...",
  "message": "Prompt restored from version 'v1.0'"
}
```

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

### Publish Version

```bash
nexus version publish <agentId> <versionId> --json
```

Marks this version as `isProduction: true` and un-marks the previous production version.

**Response:** Updated version detail with `isProduction: true`.

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

## 4. Folders (5 commands)

### List Folders

```bash
nexus folder list --json
```

No parameters. Returns all folders and all agent-folder assignments.

**Response:**

```json
{
  "folders": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "Production",
      "iconUrl": null,
      "parentId": null,
      "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": null
    },
    {
      "id": "uuid-child",
      "name": "Customer Support",
      "iconUrl": null,
      "parentId": "uuid",
      "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": null
    }
  ],
  "assignments": [
    { "agentId": "agent-uuid-1", "folderId": "uuid" },
    { "agentId": "agent-uuid-2", "folderId": "uuid-child" }
  ]
}
```

---

### Create Folder

```bash
nexus folder create --name <name> [--parent-id <id>] [--body <json>] --json
```

| Flag        | Type   | Required | Notes                        |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------- |
| --name      | string | yes      | Min 1 character              |
| --parent-id | uuid   | no       | Parent folder ID for nesting |

**Response (201):** Created folder object.

**Status codes:** 201 Created, 400 Validation error, 401 Unauthorized

---

### Update Folder

```bash
nexus folder update <folderId> [--name <name>] [--parent-id <id>] [--body <json>] --json
```

| Flag        | Type   | Required | Notes                              |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
| --name      | string | no       | Min 1 character if provided        |
| --parent-id | uuid   | no       | Set parent or null to move to root |

**Response (200):** Updated folder object.

---

### Delete Folder

```bash
nexus folder delete <folderId> [--yes]
```

Agents assigned to this folder are unassigned (not deleted).

**Response:**

```json
{ "id": "uuid", "deleted": true }
```

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

### Assign Agent to Folder

```bash
nexus folder assign --agent-id <agentId> --folder-id <folderId> [--body <json>]
```

| Flag        | Type | Required | Notes                           |
| ----------- | ---- | -------- | ------------------------------- |
| --agent-id  | uuid | yes      | Agent ID                        |
| --folder-id | uuid | yes      | Folder ID or `null` to unassign |

**Response:**

```json
{
  "agentId": "agent-uuid",
  "folderId": "folder-uuid",
  "assigned": true
}
```

To move an agent, call this again with the new folder ID. To unassign, pass `--folder-id null`.

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 400 Validation error, 401 Unauthorized

--- name: nexus-analytics description: Retrieves organization-wide analytics including conversation metrics, cost tracking, token usage, channel breakdowns, and satisfaction feedback via the Nexus CLI. --- # Nexus Analytics Org metrics, usage, satisfaction feedback. Setup/envelope → CLAUDE.md. ## CLI Setup — unique pattern Unlike other skills, analytics supports BOTH interactive login AND env var: ```bash nexus auth login # interactive (opens browser) # OR export NEXUS_API_KEY=nxs_... ``` Custom base URL: `nexus --base-url http://localhost:3001 ` or `export NEXUS_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001`. ## Commands ```bash nexus analytics overview [--time-period

] [--deployment-id ] --json nexus analytics export [--time-period

] [--deployment-id ] nexus analytics feedback [--time-period

] [--deployment-id ] [--score ] [--limit] [--page] --json ``` **Time periods:** `last_24_hours`, `last_7_days`, `last_30_days`, `last_90_days`, `last_12_months`, `all_time`. **`overview` response:** `totalConversations`, `totalMessages`, `totalCostUsd`, `tokenUsage`, `timeSeries`, `byChannel`, `byDeployment`, `byModel`. **`export` output:** streams CSV (summary + message data) → redirect to file (`> analytics.csv`). **`feedback` filter:** `--score 1` for negative-only. ## Cross-data join pattern (per R#19 parallel reads) Joining analytics w/ CRM/BI data? Pull complementary dataset w/ `nexus external-tool execute` (HubSpot deals, Stripe charges, Mixpanel events) → join locally on shared key (`conversation_id`, `user_email`, `session_id`). Avoids building a dedicated export workflow. E.g., `nexus external-tool execute --action stripe-list-charges --input '{"limit":100}' --credential --json > stripe.json` → join against `analytics-export.csv` on customer email. Full → `nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`. ## Fallback Untyped operations → `nexus api ` per R#1. E.g., `nexus api GET /analytics/overview --query timePeriod=last_7_days --json`.

nexus-app-builder.description: User = Nexus org admin. They describe outcomes; you translate → PRD → repo → `nexus vibe` CLI + git.

files.content:
---
name: nexus-app-builder
description: Builds, deploys, and operates hosted apps on Nexus (Vibe) — pure middleware/backends, Nexus modalities exposed to the world, and full front+back apps. Owns the PRD gate, repo/git discipline, build-deploy-watch-rollback, the dev loop, and register-as-tool. Use when the user asks to build, deploy, fix, or operate a hosted app, an API/middleware, or a web frontend.
---

# Nexus App Builder

User = Nexus org admin. They describe outcomes; you translate → PRD → repo → `nexus vibe` CLI + git.

Env/auth/envelopes/dashboard → CLAUDE.md. Operating rules cited as R#N. App archetypes summary → CLAUDE.md Platform Model (this skill owns the mechanics).

!! BEFORE THE FIRST SOURCE WRITE, ON EVERY PATH INCLUDING SOLO: count the UNITS in the brief, count the FILES exactly one lane could own end-to-end, and where units exceed files SPLIT THE TREE first, in the root's own commit. Record both numbers on the card (`Units + artifacts`). The procedure is `references/plan-format.md` "## HOW TO DECOMPOSE — the enumeration, in order" (Step 4b), and the per-stack rungs are `references/frontend-architecture.md` "## 2a. The frontend seam ladder — where a unit becomes a FILE somebody can own" and `references/backend-crew.md` "## The backend seam ladder — where a unit becomes a FILE somebody can own" — READ the one for your stack now, not when you fan out. The measured field report behind all of it is `references/parallel-agent-builds.md`. THIS CLAUSE IS HERE, IN THE ENTRY GATE, BECAUSE THAT IS THE ONLY PLACE A SOLO BUILD READS: measured across four real builds from plain user briefs, every one reached this SKILL.md and NOT ONE opened `plan-format.md` or `backend-crew.md`, because both sit behind dispatching the architect or the backend crew — roles a solo build never assumes. The build that followed shipped a 514-line module holding every use case. !!

!! THE REPO CONTRACT — the tree a stranger can navigate, and it is written at SCAFFOLD time, not at handover. Four rules, all checkable:

**1. The top level is the map.** Only what a newcomer needs to see first: `README.md`, `package.json` (or its equivalent), `.gitignore`, and the entry point. Everything else lives under a named directory whose name says what it holds — `src/` (source, split by the seam ladder) · `docs/` (the gate artifacts: PRD, BUILD-MODE, DESIGN, CONTRACT, lane-dag) · `journeys/` + `fixtures/` (the additive stores) · `scripts/` (things you run, never things you import) · `data/` (state, gitignored unless it is a seed). A loose `guard.sh` or `index.html` at top level is a file nobody assigned a home.

**2. `README.md` exists from the FIRST commit and answers SIX questions in this order** — measured: three real builds each wrote a good README and each invented its own shape, converging on four of these; a fourth build, the best-structured of them all, shipped with no README at all.
- **What is it, and who is it for** — two sentences, in the user's nouns, not the stack's.
- **Run it** — the exact commands, copy-pasteable, including any seed or first-run step.
- **Prove it** — the command that runs the suite, and what green means.
- **Where things are** — the directory map above, one line each, so nobody greps to orient.
- **What it deliberately does NOT do** — the non-goals, so every gap reads as a decision instead of an oversight.
- **What is not built yet** — the honest state. A README that describes seven screens while seven screens are stubs is the one defect here that actively misleads; a build shipped exactly that, and only the chat message said so.

**3. `.gitignore` before the first `npm install`.** `node_modules/`, caches, local databases, capture output. Verify with `git ls-files | wc -l` — the tracked count is the honest size of the repo, and a build measured 702 files on disk against 17 tracked.

**4. Headings are structure, never emphasis.** `#` levels nest; a numbered walkthrough is a list, not eleven `#` headings — one README used `#` for each step of a worked example and its outline became unreadable in every tool that renders one.

The repo is a deliverable. It is read by whoever inherits it, and the first thing they read is the tree. !!

!! ENTRY GATE — read BEFORE the phases. The ENGINE is the DEFAULT path for EVERY archetype-3 build (any human-facing surface), never an opt-in — and the entry DECISION is RECORDED before the first app-source write: `docs/BUILD-MODE.md` (the BUILD-MODE card → `references/build-mode-card.md`; no-repo builds record the same rows as a ledger DECISION row), naming archetype · ENGINE/SOLO · authority (the first `app-architect` dispatch, or the user's solo go QUOTED verbatim) · lanes+models · preview owner · repo git-init'd · contract deltas. P1 CLOSES by dispatching `app-architect` (the plan JSON is P1's deliverable — a LIGHT dispatch: signed PRD + repo path + design lock + plan-format pointer); the first unit of each surface is BUILT by the persistent `app-executor`; no P5 completion word lands without the review wave. Solo main-loop building is the EXCEPTION and takes an explicit user go after a one-line disclosure ("building solo, no crew — <reason>; ok?") — the toy-size instinct is not that go, "it's the platform-primitive track" does not cover app-SOURCE files, and "craft concurrency = 1" means the ONE persistent executor, never "build it myself". Default-solo without asking: archetype-1/2 (no human surface) and single-file fixes to an existing app — the card still records it. A build reaching its first `git push`/deploy with ZERO `app-*` dispatches and no carded go is OFF-DOCTRINE (BLD2 denies) — stop, enter the engine or get the go. The model-policy AUQ fires WITH the first crew dispatch. !!

‼ NAMING: an app "deploy" here = git push → auto-build → hosted swap. A channel **Deployment** (EMBED/WhatsApp/Slack…) is a DIFFERENT primitive → `nexus-deployments`. "Deploy the app" routes here; "deploy the agent to <channel>" routes there.

## Boundary check — is this actually an app?

| Signal | Route |
|---|---|
| "host/build an app / a site / a dashboard / an API / middleware" | HERE — pick the archetype (P1) |
| "a real desktop app / a Mac app / an .app or .dmg / install it on my machine" | HERE — archetype 3 delivered as a SHELL over the hosted app: Read `references/desktop-shell.md` BEFORE the shell repo |
| One automation on a trigger ("every time X, do Y") | `nexus-workflow-builder` |
| Conversational ("answers questions", "chat") | `nexus-agent-management` (an app can EMBED an agent later) |
| Expose an EXISTING workflow/agent to the outside world | HERE — archetype 2 (thin app, API key) |
| A doc/report artifact, no navigable surface | template/code-interpreter routes, not an app |

## Phases — hard gates

```
P0 PRD (SIGN-OFF GATE) → P0.5 Design lock (PICK GATE) → P1 Architecture (ENGINE ENTRY — card + architect dispatch) → P2 Repo+Scaffold →
  ┌─ P3 BUILD↔REVIEW LOOP (per surface): build a wave → the FIRST review round opens at the CLOSE OF
  │  WAVE 1 (never deferred to convergence) → collate → delta to the SAME executor → next wave; a
  │  review round is DUE at every wave boundary ("is a review round due?" in the per-wave duty list)
  └─ CONVERGENCE is the EXIT of this loop, never its entry → P4 Deploy (watch+verify; served from wave 1)
→ P5 Journeys + coverage gate → P6 Operate (+ register-as-tool)
Every phase's discoveries → the workstream LEDGER (R#34 sprint carve-out: ONE spine per
milestone/ship, not per event); the signed-off PRD files to the org GC (P0).
A build that never declares "done" cannot defer the council: round 1 is anchored to wave-1 close, not to a convergence signal that may never arrive.
```

### P0 — PRD gate
!! Before ANY scaffold, repo write, or vendor probe — an app is designed in a CONVERSATION, not a form: (1) run the co-design moves (Read `../nexus-getting-started/reference/design-conversation-canon.md` COMPLETELY, incl. its "Route-the-capability" move) — job & role first (who opens it, their day, what "at a glance" means), then Cue PROPOSES the AI-opportunity map; (2) route EVERY capability: app-view / workflow / agent / AI-task (incl. in-app "generate with AI" buttons) / native-Nexus — DEFAULT = the native primitive ("does Nexus already do this?" precedes "should the app?"); (3) Read `references/prd-template.md`, produce the tiered PRD (capability-routing block + ACCESS MODEL REQUIRED — the app is PRIVATE and its users are NEXUS IDENTITIES in a granted user GROUP; an app-side/third-party login is the FALLBACK the owner must choose, never the first answer, and PUBLIC still means AUTHENTICATED), get SIGN-OFF. A named surface ("a dashboard for X") is NOT convergence on its shape — run NEEDS_ASSESSMENT Dim 8 (levels · fixed-vs-composable · visual authority · review contract — PROBED means the USER answered; a Cue-filled row is marked inferred + confirmed) into the PRD. A surface-CLASS noun ("a CRM", "a ticketing board", "an inbox") additionally carries an implied OBJECT MODEL — probe it at PRD time (which entities, which relations, which canonical views: table / kanban / record page — INCLUDING the record/detail view + its primary interactions: click / double-click / row actions), because matching the class's conventions is what makes the build "feel like" one; inventing a layout for a class noun is a rejection-storm setup. A capability-routing row is IMMUTABLE after sign-off except by: ONE probe of the displaced primitive + a one-line disclosure/override to the user. Any skill-load that OWNS a routed capability re-arms the routing question for its rows ("does the primitive I just loaded change a routing?"); the "arbitrated by the user" heading covers ONLY rows byte-matching the approved table. !!
- Tier by consumer: humans open a URL → FULL PRD; another system calls it → LIGHT intake. Import STANDING ARBITRATIONS (forks the user already decided this engagement) as defaults-with-disclosure (R#6).
- **Pivotal-feature contract:** the PRD names the CORE LOOP in the user's words — the feature(s) the app exists for, plus the config surfaces that support them — and it is RE-READ before every major rework/redesign wave: polish or redesign never outranks an unstarted pivotal feature without an explicit user arbitration (AUQ). The user restating the core loop mid-build = the contract failed.
- **The OBJECTIVE is a PRD row, not a retrospective question:** what is this app/service FOR, how is success MEASURED, what do we expect it to produce (a number, a rate, a volume) — the deploy/test bundle must prove the OBJECTIVE, not just that code runs; done-states are **BUILT → COMMISSIONED → OPERATING** and every completion claim NAMES its state (a green suite over an empty store is BUILT; evidence per state → `references/commissioning.md`).
- **The starter's own `docs/feature-manifest.md` is a P0 grounding input for record-system classes** — read BEFORE proposing surfaces (it is the baseline you propose against; the user pointing at the boilerplate = this step was skipped).
- The signed-off PRD is an ARTIFACT: the next R#34 brief carries it; it files to `general-context/systems/<app-slug>/prd.md`. **Sign-off clauses become ledger BINDING rows** (each promise the user signed = one row) and the BUILD-MODE card's "Contract deltas" row tracks them: a PRD change later = a new sign-off, never a silent drift — and REVERSING a signed clause takes an inline before/after diff + the user's explicit go BEFORE any build lands on the reversed reading.
✗ "per-review analysis display" built straight into a card section → rejected on scope, rebuilt, rejected on paradigm → ✓ two Dim-8 questions before any code: levels + fixed-vs-composable; the first build is the right shape.
Gate-class artifacts (the PRD, the boards, the card) are RENDERED INLINE in the conversation — the full text/preview in the message; a file path or attachment is the COPY, never the presentation ("I don't see the PRD" = this failure).

### P0.5 — Design lock (PICK gate; any app with a human-facing surface)
A quality adjective ("award-winning", "beautiful", "premium") is NOT a spec — it is operationalized by a PICKED direction, never by iterating adjectives:
- Render **2-3 STATIC HTML direction boards** (one real screen each, the app's own nouns; each board = tokens: palette · type · density · motion posture + one composed view). Serve locally / publish as an Artifact and LINK them — AUQ labels cannot carry pixels, so the AUQ's options are the direction NAMES pointing at the rendered set (serve-then-link).
- User PICKS → commit **`docs/DESIGN.md`** (chosen tokens + the board snapshot + the named anti-references) BEFORE any build pixels. **The lock's binary axes (color scheme · density · motion posture) are MACHINE-READABLE** — a named value the static guard can grep against the code (a `prefers-color-scheme` boot vs a "Light mode only." lock goes RED at the introducing commit, not at user discovery). The lock is the visual authority P3 reads for EVERY surface; a re-pick is a NEW lock commit — design drift without a re-pick is the redesign-wave class.
- **‼ The app lock is the LANGUAGE; each surface still gets its own DESIGN ROUND — `references/design-round.md`.** The 2-3 boards above pick the app's visual language ONCE (palette · type · density · motion). They do NOT pick the SHAPE of each screen. Before the first build pixel of ANY human-facing surface, AND at every redesign of one, run the per-surface round: (1) write the surface's OBJECTIVE and get the owner's approval; (2) give it N genuinely-different alternatives on a NAMED axis (layout · interaction · density · the primary decision) — three variants of one idea is a false choice; (3) at least one alternative comes from a REQUIRED **blind lane** given only the objective + data model + design system, NEVER the current screen (a lane that sees it anchors — every "alternative" becomes the current screen with better spacing); (4) real populated plural data, mobile-primary named, each rendered at both viewports and labeled what it is WORSE at; (5) the OWNER picks before any executor lane fires, recorded in `docs/DESIGN.md` `## Pick provenance`. A **REDESIGN** (owner clearly rejects a surface) is a DIFFERENT process from the improvement loop — the round dispatches `app-redesigner` lanes (informed + a REQUIRED blind) on the highest model, capturing the owner's own reasoning (routing → `references/design-round.md`). A donor/inherited look is NOT a pick.
- A fork/donor's look is NEVER the default canon — de-branding a donor is not a direction. **Client-brand gate:** when the app is FOR a named client/org, their LIVE design language (site/product screenshots, brand canon in GC) is read BEFORE boards render — a scraped hex value is not a design language, and the client's light/dark posture is the default posture. Boards ride `Skill(frontend-design)` when the plugin is present; absent → `references/ux-canon.md` is the floor FOR BOARD RENDERING (at P3 the canon is read WITH the lock, never instead of it). The org starter ships direction-board scaffolds (`references/starter-guide.md`).

### P1 — Architecture
Read `references/archetypes.md` → pick 1/2/3 by CONSUMER. Then fix the data layer + secrets BEFORE the repo exists:
- !! - **Data spine — the org warehouse, from day 1:** every durable store the app owns (records, config, run results, team/user state) is a WAREHOUSE table the app dual-writes and boot-reads; agents/copilots query the SAME store (one SQL/query tool over the warehouse), never a private app API; **the container filesystem is NOT a store** — every file on it is rebuilt from the spine on boot or it does not exist, and a DATABASE on the container (`.sqlite`, `.db`, a JSON tank, an in-process engine like PGLite) is the anti-pattern this clause forbids, never a cache it permits. A read cache is a bounded copy of a value you already fetched; a database on the container is a second source of truth that diverges silently and dies on the next deploy swap. Proven default: one append-only `app_state` key-value table + latest-per-key restore on boot (append-only history doubles as clobber recovery). "The app as an API = the source of truth" is the anti-pattern; and the spine is a STANDING constraint — every LATER store added to the app lands in the warehouse by default, surfaced as default-with-disclosure, never silently re-decided per store (CLAUDE.md standing-dimension).
- **Warehouse-first**: big/volatile payloads = a backend endpoint assembling from the warehouse w/ a TTL cache, fetched by RELATIVE path (localhost serves a static twin, prod serves live — one code path). NEVER data files in git. After any data sweep lands, re-point live third-party reads at your OWN store (richer, keyless, cacheable); the live API demotes to fallback.
- **Third-party connections route through the platform:** every vendor connection the app needs is a PLATFORM credential (OAuth via the connector flow) consumed through platform tool-execution — the app backend never holds direct vendor OAuth/tokens. Canonical in-app connect flow (verified live): the app's server route calls `POST /tools/<toolId>/connect` → open the returned `authorizationUrl` in a popup → poll `GET /tools/<toolId>/credentials` until a credential NEWER than the handshake start appears (the APP-context variant — the popup's handshakeId doesn't round-trip to the app backend; an OPERATOR-driven connect can poll `GET /tools/connect/<handshakeId>/status` directly — pick by who holds the handshakeId) → store that credential id and execute actions through the platform (`POST /tools/<toolId>/execute`). Flow patterns + secret handling → `../nexus-tool-connection/SKILL.md`.
- **Secrets**: deployed = `nexus vibe env set` vars only; local = chmod-600 scratchpad files; NOTHING in the repo, ever. Enumerate every secret in ONE launch wrapper (a partial re-export half-breaks the app: UI fine, API 500). ‼ `env set`/`env list` store and RETURN values in PLAINTEXT to any org API key — they are config, not secrets-grade storage; a true secret still belongs in a platform credential (the connections rule above), never in an env var.
- **Inbound identity routes through the platform too** (the twin of the connections rule above): a human reaching the app arrives as a NEXUS IDENTITY — the app is PRIVATE and access is granted to a user GROUP (`vibe_app` × `group` × `viewer`); the app NEVER holds its own user table or login. PUBLIC + app-side auth is the FALLBACK, taking the owner's recorded go (`Access:` line in the PRD, R#6 quotable-go) — and it still means AUTHENTICATED, never open. The grant itself is a dashboard step (org API key → 403): hand it off with the exact clicks, never report it done. Ladder + endpoints → `references/archetypes.md` "Boundary notes".
- **Ports**: the server binds PORT + common fallbacks (3000, 8080) simultaneously. A `Dockerfile` with `EXPOSE` IS honoured and sets `detectedPort` (verified), but a defensive multi-bind costs nothing and removes the whole "allocation unhealthy" class (references/deploy-guide.md).
- **EVERY build path, SOLO INCLUDED, decomposes before it writes source.** The card's `Units + artifacts` row is where a solo build records it (`references/build-mode-card.md`), and that row's `!!` gate is the only forcing read of the decomposition doctrine that a solo build ever reaches — measured across four real builds from plain user briefs, all four read `frontend-architecture.md` and none opened `plan-format.md` or `backend-crew.md`, because those two are gated behind dispatching the architect or the backend crew. Count the units, count the ownable files, split the tree if they do not match, and only then choose ENGINE or SOLO.

Two hook read-paths and two checks (`FANOUT-ROOTS`, `PARTITION-VALID`) key off that file; with nothing writing it, `PARTITION-VALID` has never validated a single partition. The architect cannot write it (no write tools, by design), so it is the coordinator's — same moment as the card. Building on without all three needs the disclosed, card-quoted solo go.

!! Before the FIRST user-facing unit of EACH surface (a new tab/page/view is a new surface): read the VISUAL AUTHORITY — the app's own existing UI (its components/CSS are the canon), else the org brand canon (R#47) — AND Read `references/ux-canon.md` (IA + type scale + component-inventory: the app's existing components are REUSED and tweaked before any new control is written) AND `references/frontend-architecture.md` (where state lives, when a component splits, the CSS layering contract, the a11y floor — how the surface is BUILT, as against how it looks) AND the resolved `@agent-nexus/apps-ui` front door (`AGENTS.md` → `docs/CHOOSING.md` → `docs/MOTION.md`; resolution ladder + per-mode catalog → `references/starter-guide.md` "Navigation contract"). A compaction voids these reads — re-read on resume (R#13). !!
