Mechanics + parity traps → `references/dev-loop.md`; UI craft + mechanical sweeps → `references/frontend-craft.md`. !! Before diagnosing slowness or proposing ANY speed remedy: Read `references/performance-playbook.md` — measure → classify → lever, in that order. !!
- **A feature IS its primitive:** an app feature representing an automation or AI transform ships WITH the platform primitive behind it (workflow / AI task / agent) built and E2E-proven (execId) when the feature ships — UI over app-side faked logic is the anti-pattern, and any deliberately-mocked demo element is LABELED as mock to the user (the PRD's real-vs-mock column stays current). "Is there an actual workflow behind this?" must never be the user's question.
- **Adopt-before-hand-roll (data/infra):** when app code starts re-implementing a known infra concern — the tell is a bespoke hook holding a status union + a generation counter + a nonce-reload (a hand-rolled data layer) — that is a LIBRARY decision, not a per-surface one: a one-line AUQ to the owner BEFORE the 2nd surface consumes it. A hand-rolled loader consumed by N surfaces fans the same defect N times; the client data layer is a P0 PRD row (`references/frontend-architecture.md` §1a).
- **"Removed" means: code dropped AND dependency uninstalled AND journey retired.** Hiding a nav entry removes nothing; state the bundle delta (before → after) or do not use the word. A bundle-size budget lives in the guard suite — exceeding it fails the gate.
- **Capability ships WITH backfill + parity:** a new enrichment/data capability runs against EXISTING records at ship time (backfill), and lands with parity across sibling entity types (what one record class gets, its siblings get) — a capability without visible data on the records the user opens reads as the feature not existing.
- **Per-wave PRD/SPEC DELTA TABLE.** At EVERY wave boundary (a lane report consumed · a re-awaken · a user-visible status): RE-READ `docs/PRD.md` + `docs/SPEC.md` FROM DISK and emit ASKED (PRD commitments ∪ SPEC rows) · BUILT (evidence = a USER-REACHABLE path, never test-green) · REMAINING (owner + lane). SPEC rows cover PRD COMMITMENTS too, not only user asks; SPEC has ONE writer (Cue) — lanes report rows via their handoff (hook LEDGERW1).
- **Is a review round DUE?** — checked at EVERY wave boundary. The FIRST review round opens at the close of wave 1 (not at a convergence signal that may never come), and a round is owed at every boundary thereafter; DEFERRING a round past a boundary is a USER-approved call, never self-approved. Convergence is the loop's EXIT (the crew ENGINE, below), never its entry — a build that never declares "done" still gets its council on schedule (the stock-build deferred the whole council 14h by tying it to convergence). R#9's pivotal-outranks-polish ranking reads the REMAINING column.
- **Improvement vs REDESIGN — route the owner's verdict, don't default to polish.** A clear owner rejection of a SPECIFIC surface ("I really don't like this", "this is not usable", "none of this landed", "make it drastic") is a REDESIGN of that surface (`references/design-round.md`: the per-surface round dispatching `app-redesigner` on the highest model, 3 alternatives incl. a REQUIRED blind lane, the owner's reasoning captured) — NEVER another improvement round on the rejected shape. A whole-app "it feels assembled" routes to `app-design-director`. A scoped craft complaint on an accepted shape is the improvement loop. Reading a redesign as a polish is the measured failure (four "redesign" rounds that were all fixes; "there was no redesign per surface" e.g.).
- **Feature/test manifest from feature 1 — a REPO artifact:** `docs/feature-manifest.md`, one row per feature written the wave it ships: | Feature | Primitive (workflow/task/agent id, or `mock`) | How to exercise (exact click path) | VISIBLE outcome that proves it | Last verified (local / hosted) |. Repo-tracked so it survives sessions and the deploy gate can read it; it is the review gate's coverage list (the app twin of the R#27 Coverage Table) — rework waves DIFF against it (R#50(6)), a feature with no row is unshipped by definition, and a proof you cannot phrase as VISIBLE ("the API returns 200" is not visible) is under-specified. DG1 and the dropped-row tripwire parse EXACTLY this shape — the contract is `references/feature-manifest-format.md`, and a non-standard table is invisible to both. The org starter seeds it at clone time (`docs/feature-manifest.md`), alongside `docs/SPEC.md` — the in-repo requirement contract: ONE row per user ask, appended THE TURN it arrives (the user's words + turn ref · status asked→built→journey-green · evidence · source); the workspace PRD is the intake snapshot, `docs/SPEC.md` is the living contract the deploy gate reads.
- **Folders at create time:** the app's platform resources (workflows, tasks, agents, deployments) get/reuse the app's project folder AT CREATE TIME — one folder per project/role, every later resource assigned as it is created; a resource created "loose" and refiled later is the anti-pattern (mechanics: agent `folder`, `deployment folder`, skills/workflows via `/skill-folders` — `../nexus-skills-and-tasks/reference/skill-folders.md`).
- !! Before EVERY push of frontend code: run `skills/shared/scripts/precheck.py <file>` (CSS brace-balance · per-script node --check · i18n used⊆defined) — each sweep catches a whole-surface-killing class. Visual changes are verified from a RENDERED screenshot BEFORE the push, never after the user's. !!
- **The ENGINE is the default build path (ENTRY GATE at top) — P3 executes THROUGH it:** the FIRST unit of each surface is BUILT by the persistent `app-executor` under its iterate-loop and JUDGED personally by Cue against the bar (R#50(5) — judgment, never a relay of the executor's self-assessment); plumbing/verification lanes ride the lane pre-flight (`references/lane-contract.md`); craft concurrency = 1; a user's delegation ban binds the workstream. Solo building without the disclosed user go = off-doctrine (gate).
- **Watchable surface from wave 1:** the first served surface (walking skeleton on mock data) exists and its URL is SHARED by the end of wave 1, re-shared at each wave boundary; a long local-only phase (adapter/backend) posts a one-line status + offers a localhost preview PROACTIVELY — never wait for "show me on localhost" (R#9 build heartbeat). The serve-overdue nudge (hook `serve`) fires when build waves pass with no served URL.

### P4 — Deploy
Read `references/deploy-guide.md` for the platform mechanics (the app-vs-git-project model, the provision step, visibility-gated verification, rollback). ‼ `app create` does NOT provision the repo — `app provision-repo` does, and `deployability` is the field that proves it; run the guide's **pre-build deploy gate** on the EMPTY scaffold at P2 so no deploy risk survives into the build. The invariant sequence:
```
git pull --rebase                          # foreign-commit check (content-grep at HEAD if rejected/rebased)
<sync recipe if out-of-repo master> && git commit && git push
skills/shared/scripts/deploy_watch.sh <public-url> <sha-unique-marker> [timeout-s] [poll-s] [profile] [appId]
```
Pass `appId` so the audit poll is SCOPED to your app — an org-wide poll can be satisfied by a different app's deploy.
- A status/readiness event (HEALTHY) can PRECEDE the served-content swap — verify BOTH `servingDeployment.triggerSha` and the content marker; the skew runs in either direction (R#20). Build-succeeded-but-deploy-failed = a SWAP failure → retry with an empty commit (fresh sha, identical content), not a code change.
- ‼ **A marker miss on a PRIVATE app is an ACCESS state, not swap lag** — apps are created PRIVATE and answer 401 to any plain HTTP client, so a marker grep can never pass no matter the timeout. Read the HTTP status first (`DEPLOY_WATCH: ACCESS_BLOCKED`); verify via `servingDeployment` + `edgeReachability`, or make the app public / send the edge token.
- Track the LAST-KNOWN-GOOD sha at all times; rollback = explicit deploy of that sha (`nexus vibe deploy <appId> --sha <good>`). There is NO `--builder` flag; re-deploying an already-built sha is accepted and gets a fresh `versionNumber`.
- Run the watch in BACKGROUND (R#29 `until` loop) — never chained into one multi-minute foreground compound (commit+push+watch): a foreground timeout kills the chain and obscures WHICH step failed. And no in-memory async work (bulk backfills, queued jobs) scheduled across a swap window — the swap kills it (details + failure branches → `references/deploy-guide.md`).
- **The deploy is DRIVEN to verified-served and REPORTED with that state** — "marker confirmed at <url>", "HEALTHY, marker pending — still polling", or "HEALTHY but the app is PRIVATE so the URL 401s — verified via servingDeployment instead" — never an implicit done; the user noticing "nothing new on the url" or asking "can you try pushing again?" means the loop was under-driven (deploy-guide failure table).

### P5 — Review gate (before "done" on any surface) — journeys FIRST, renders second
P5 closes through the ENGINE's review wave + convergence (below) — reviewers/assessors → deterministic collate → ledger match → delta to the SAME executor → stop condition; a SOLO build (card-quoted go) substitutes Cue's own full pass against the same ledger. The journey lane below is the integration-side verdict either way.
- **Journeys are the PRIMARY verdict:** drive the manifest's journeys as the user — `npm run journeys` where the repo ships the harness (it stamps `journeys/.last-pass` + writes `docs/COVERAGE.md` verdicts; the deploy gate reads both) — LOCAL and HOSTED, asserting VISIBLE outcomes: an input's VALUE changed after an AI action · the tab's DOM switched · busy states appear AND clear · rendered text in the expected language · console errors == 0 at journey end. Verify the HARNESS before trusting results (hosted fetches may need a browser UA; wrong route slugs pass silently until screenshots are READ — individually, never "script printed ok"). Mechanical checks (console clean, screenshots taken, API 200s) never substitute for interaction assertions — render-green + journey-red is the "buttons are dead" class the user otherwise finds first. The `journey-verifier` agent MAY drive this lane (verification ≠ craft — R#50(5)); its verdicts land in COVERAGE.md, and YOU spot-check one journey yourself before relaying green.
- **Journey rows run LOCAL and HOSTED**; wave-close reconciliation counts hosted rows when the review contract names the hosted URL.
- **Per-archetype gate set (the card's Archetype row is the switch):** archetype 1/2 (no human surface) = light PRD + contract-tests-green against the RUNNING service + register-as-tool — a visual design lock and click-journeys are NOT demanded of an API; archetype 3 = the full set. The crew and council honour the same switch (`references/backend-crew.md` owns the 1/2 cycle).
- **Emergency-fix path:** app DOWN + a safe, typechecked, reviewed fix → the gate WARNS, never blocks, and the override is disclosed + logged; a precondition never satisfiable in this repo cannot hold a real fix hostage while the app is already broken (`references/gates-and-ledger.md` degrade rule).
- When the design lock names a MODE (light/dark), the capture set includes ONE opposite-mode shot — a suite that can only render the compliant path cannot fail on the violated axis.
- Coverage, not sampling (R#27 Deliverable Coverage Table): fullPage screenshot per surface pass (screenshot mechanics → `references/dev-loop.md`), ONE screenshot + verdict per unit, element-clip only for single controls; screenshots land in `<project>/.playwright-mcp/` (the review root; a lane's own scratch captures may sit in its worktree `_captures/`, but anything a reviewer or the user is asked to look at lands in the review root). Measurement can EXONERATE pre-existing behavior — measure before "fixing" it. The visual confirm on user-facing changes is the USER's (R#27). Coverage includes the ~390px viewport per surface (programmatic no-horizontal-scroll + screenshot) and, when the engagement carries a stated quality bar, a per-surface verdict against that bar (R#27 Coverage Table predicate) — the P0.5 design lock is that bar's concrete form. Reachability: the URL the USER opens is the tested surface — a passing check on your own endpoint proves nothing about theirs. A human-facing surface additionally carries an OWNER-RENDER-REVIEW before done: the owner saw it rendered at both viewports on real populated data (`references/design-round.md`; `feature-manifest-format.md` owner-render-review stamp) — a journey-green surface the owner never saw rendered is not done (β render-evidence).
- **Ship gate — the demo movie:** before "v1 accepted"/ship, ONE scripted journey through the whole core loop on HOSTED, with per-step evidence (screenshot/assertion per step). A core loop you cannot drive end-to-end on the hosted URL is not shipped.
- **The review wave and the bar-measurement are LOOP-scheduled, not user-ordered (γ).** Fire the council + the persona drives when a surface reaches a wave boundary — the USER asking "launch the review agents" means the loop already missed it (measured: the council existed only because the user ordered it twice, and it immediately "found more than the whole night's automated checking did", including a silent stock-corrupting double-withdrawal). The stated quality bar is MEASURED from the first surface, never left "asked" — an unmeasured "award-winning" bar is an aspiration nobody scored (measured: the bar sat "asked" from turn 1 to hour 15, then scored 4.66/9 the moment it was measured).
- **The step-back fires on the LOOP's own trigger, not the user's "Wait" (γ, R#49).** When the loop states its own re-assessment signal — "the easy win is spent, the rest is real database round-trips", a 2nd same-class rejection, a bar it never measured, a flat done-count while churn climbs — it emits the step-back SLATE then, not after the user forces it (measured: the read-path floor was stated at 08:09 and the option slate produced only at the user's 09:58 "Wait — explain the risk first"; the architecture was then chosen BY the user, not proposed TO them). The user forcing the re-assessment = the trigger was already on the table and skipped.

## The crew ENGINE — plan → contracts → build → review → converge (runs inside P3↔P5)

!! ENTRY GATE — at the top of this file; the card contract → `references/build-mode-card.md`. !!

**Two tracks, in PARALLEL.** The ENGINE owns the APP-SURFACE track; the PLATFORM-PRIMITIVE track (PA prompt authoring, AI-task/agent/workflow creation, OAuth/credential flows, data seeding) runs CONCURRENTLY in the main loop (R#19) — creating the app's AI task while the architect plans or the executor builds is the intended shape, never a violation. The merge point is the feature-IS-its-primitive contract (P3): a surface lands only when its primitive exists (execId) or is labeled mock. The BLD1/BLD2 nudges key on app-SOURCE writes and pushes only — `docs/` artifacts and platform-primitive work never trip them.

Registered `app-*` agent types (`.claude/agents/`) are the roles; Cue is the ORCHESTRATOR. P1/P2 produce the engine's inputs (PRD, design lock, repo); P3 hosts its lanes; P5 is its convergence gate. **The BACKEND track runs the same pipeline with the contract-test verdict:** `app-backend` (domain/use-cases/adapters — persistent executor) · `app-migrations` (schema + reversal; MANDATORY human approval gate, relayed via Cue) · `app-release` (rollout proven LIVE, not merged) — cycle + service defaults → `references/backend-crew.md`; a backend build with no test runner, no release discipline, and a gate script that doesn't exist is the measured solo-improvised failure this track replaces.

### Pipeline
```
app-architect  → plan JSON (references/plan-format.md); taste_questions → Cue synthesizes → USER
                 validates; `inferred` interpretations get the one-line user confirm PRE-dispatch
app-contracts  → shared types land FIRST (the type is the handoff medium)
app-executor   → N PERSISTENT executors, ONE per DISJOINT lane (execution concurrency = N;
                 see "dependency DAG + scheduler" below), guard suite green at each commit
app-tests      → checks that CAN FAIL (mutation evidence per check) + the UNIT-TEST-LOG;
                 present in every topology down to the smallest (contracts → executor → tests)
app-tester     → CAST users drive a DISPOSABLE TWIN toward goals (not click-lists);
                 their before/after captures are the review wave's PRIMARY evidence
review wave    → app-reviewer × ALL 7 dimensions (visual · ux · interaction · mobile · functionality ·
                 consistency · code) live-drive read-only + app-assessor council × ALL 21 categories
                 (per-breakpoint) — each dispatch inlines its QA method / rubric verbatim.
                 The wave IS the full roster; partial seating only by the user's quotable
                 drop, recorded in BUILD-MODE Fates
collate        → references/scripts/collate.mjs — a SCRIPT, never an LLM summary (R#48 law).
                 Run it WITH `--ledger docs/ISSUE-LEDGER.md --round <rN>`: that is what mints the
                 round's STABLE ids and re-opens a `fixed` row found again as a REGRESSION
ledger match   → stable IDs; a reappeared `fixed` = REGRESSION, outranks new work
                 (references/gates-and-ledger.md)
delta          → back to the SAME lane's executor (re-awaken; a sibling on the SAME SLICE is
                 the anti-pattern — N executors on DISJOINT slices are the point, not a smell)
converge       → app-taste (ONCE, after convergence) → user verdict
```
- **The wave judges a TAGGED sha:** the executor tags at wave-open; every seat dispatch names it; a seat refuses findings it cannot reproduce on that sha; the executor's next round starts after collate.
- `app-design-director` fires ONLY AFTER the council is COLLATED — it CONSUMES the collated council (docs/ISSUE-LEDGER.md) as its diagnosis, so it can NEVER run concurrently with a still-running council (the stock build fired it mid-council; a director without the full verdict is guessing, hook `dirseq`). It fires only on a structural verdict (contract-clean but "assembled"), and its direction becomes a NEW arbitrated plan wave, never a silent rework.
  - **Director grain vs the per-surface round:** the director proposes ONE whole-app direction (the app feels assembled as a whole). A single surface the OWNER rejects goes to the per-surface REDESIGN round instead (`references/design-round.md`: 3 alternatives incl. a blind lane for THAT surface, owner picks) — not a whole-app direction. Route by scope: whole-app verdict → director; one rejected surface → the round.
  - **`app-redesigner` (per-surface redesign lane):** dispatched by the per-surface round (`references/design-round.md`), N per surface on the HIGHEST model — informed lanes (see the current screens) + a REQUIRED blind lane (never sees them). Each proposes rendered alternatives for ONE surface; the owner picks; the executor builds the pick. NOT the review wave (which polishes) and NOT the director (one whole-app direction).
- **`app-tester` runs BEFORE the review wave, one dispatch per CAST persona** (identity · domain knowledge · goals · patience — an uncast tester is a crawler and stops). It is given OUTCOMES in the user's nouns, never click paths: finding its own route IS the test. It drives a DISPOSABLE TWIN (same build, copied data) — never the owner-truth instance — and destructive controls (Accept All · Re-run · Delete · Reset · bulk) are off-limits unless a goal names that exact action: "read-only" describes a lane's TOOLS, not its CLICKS. Its felt verdicts (BROKEN-FOR-ME · CONFUSING · SLOW-ENOUGH-TO-QUIT · WORKS-BUT-WRONG · FINE · DELIGHTFUL) and give-up points enter the ledger as findings; it scores nothing and judges no craft. A crawler proves elements exist — a user with goals finds the paths nobody designed.
- **Convergence:** the code lens CLEAN of unrefuted blocker/major AND each visual lens ≥9/10; per-lens deltas, never an aggregate; a lens flat >2 rounds = a PLATEAU → surface to the user (mechanism hunt vs sign-off, their call); dedupe findings vs SEEN, not vs confirmed (else rejected findings resurface every round). **Round-closure debt: a below-bar round stays OPEN until re-scored above the bar or the user signs it off** — "scored once, quietly stopped" is a loop with no exit, and the user must never be the loop's forcing function; round N+1 rotates in ≥1 fresh-eye seat (round N's author re-reading their own work converges on itself).
- **LOOP COMPLETE only when:** every roster seat fired-or-Fates-dropped · collate ran · ISSUE-LEDGER updated · delta returned to the SAME executor · re-scored ≥ bar or user-signed. **FAILURE (restart the round):** any seat missing w/o a Fates row · scores below bar w/o sign-off · executor re-awakened before collate.
- **Round-closure is MACHINE-CHECKED:** the collate output's scores vs the bar recorded in BUILD-MODE (hook CLOSE1); a below-bar "closed" claim is refused by numbers, not memory.
- **Stop condition:** no in-scope critical/HIGH open, no unresolved contract-challenge row, + the full deterministic gate green with zero regressions on an independently re-run clean build; residual = adversarial-floor + by-design + resolved-challenge + out-of-scope rows = SIGN-OFF items, never loop work.

### The dependency DAG + scheduler (EXECUTION concurrency = N)
Craft **JUDGEMENT** = 1 (review/taste); **PRODUCTION concurrency = N** — building DISJOINT units to a FROZEN contract is what a real team parallelizes; the "one executor" reasons (prompt-drift, lost fix-context) bind a sibling on the SAME slice, not N lanes on DIFFERENT slices. **The split is INDEPENDENCE OF UNITS, never kind-of-work.** N alternatives and N surfaces are N lanes EVEN WHEN THE WORK IS VISUAL — design is not exempt from partitioning, it is exempt from having two judges. Measured: worded as "craft concurrency = 1" this was read three independent times as "never spawn a second design lane", and a request for six alternatives plus "several surfaces — build them properly" ran as ONE lane every time, including in a session that had this file loaded. The architect emits a **dependency DAG**, NOT a GANTT — lane durations are unknown and lanes auto-retry, so a fixed timeline is fiction; the DAG is the dependency STRUCTURE the scheduler runs DYNAMICALLY (a GANTT-style level view is at most a human rendering, never the contract). Machine-readable shape → `references/plan-format.md` `lane_dag`. **The width is capped by the TREE, and the tree is the root's to edit first:** lanes ≤ files one lane can own end-to-end, so when the unit count exceeds the file count the root SPLITS FILES and commits before fan-out — measured, the identical 8-lane cut merged broken over 4 files (7 conflicts, suite 18/64, seams 1/15) and clean over 8. Never a lane's job mid-wave. Procedure + the per-stack seam ladders → `references/plan-format.md` "HOW TO DECOMPOSE" Step 4b, "Raising the ceiling".
- **DAG:** nodes = lanes `{id · owns:[EXCLUSIVE globs] · depends_on:[ids] · builds_against:[roots] · acceptance:[passes ALONE] · model}`; edges = `depends_on` (a lane waits for its dependency's quiesced merge); topological levels are DERIVED (everything at a level runs concurrently). **Roots = the frozen shared-types lane AND the reactive-spine lane** (`references/frontend-architecture.md` §1a) — Part A is a DAG ROOT: without it frozen, each lane invents its own state (the measured incoherence class — N divergent mechanisms + a fragmented cache).
- **Invariants (hook PARTITION-VALID — ADVISORY: it warns, it never denies):** acyclic · pairwise-disjoint `owns` (LP1 is the guard) · closure (every `depends_on` is a root or a declared lane; `builds_against` is informational and read by no check) · only roots have `depends_on:[]`. Above 200 lanes the validator declines to run — a cost bound on the checker, never a cap on width.
- **Scheduler, three phases:** (1) **SERIAL ROOT PROLOGUE** — freeze the roots + a reactivity journey; nothing fans out until committed (hook FANOUT-ROOTS ADVISES this; it does NOT block — CHECK-REGISTRY: "ADVISORY, never a deny"). **NOT speed-neutral:** measured at 49.6 min of a 388-min wave, and the Honest-speed line below counts it as one of three terms bounding the wave. A cross-cutting root whose files collide with lane files is SCHEDULED INTO THE PREVIOUS WAVE'S TAIL, where owner-response latency already leaves the fleet idle (44.0 min measured) — worth 44.6 min off this wave's critical path. (2) **MAX-WIDTH FAN-OUT** — launch EVERY lane whose deps are merged, AS MANY AS POSSIBLE, capped only by machine health (`references/fleet-resources.md`), NEVER a number; the speed lever is a WIDER DAG (finest clean disjoint slices); quality held regardless of width by the invariants. (3) **TOPO-ORDER MERGE TAIL** — merge only after a lane's deps are merged, at its quiescent point, through the existing granular rules (`references/fleet-resources.md`: worktrees · one-writer/LP1 · quiesced merges · fork-base protection · unique port+binary · self-scoped kills · tripwires · preview excluded); a whole-app reactivity journey runs after each merge.
- **Lane failure = ISOLATE + AUTO-RETRY:** only the failed lane's DIRECT dependents block; independents keep running; the failed lane auto-relaunches with the failure noted (the Heartbeat rule below); escalate after N retries. Whole-halt / re-partition are escalations, not defaults.
- **Execution lanes are NOT governed deliveries:** an execution worktree carries a `.lane-execution` marker; the delivery-governance gates (ROSTER1 · SPEC1 · CLOSE1) SKIP it — the council/journeys gate ONCE on the INTEGRATION repo, never per lane. Honest speed: bounded by the SLOWEST lane + the serial prologue + review. **The floor is max(lanes), so treating or splitting ONE lane is worthless past the point where another becomes the floor** — measured: splitting a 247.7-min lane 4 ways left the wave at 213.2, the second lane's own length. Treat and split EVERY lane: 4 ways each across 3 lanes = 12 lanes modelled a 3.00x wave against a measured 388.1-min baseline. Lane COUNT is a wall-clock factor once every lane is split; it is not one when only the biggest is.

### Orchestrator card (Cue)
- **The build-go turn DISCLOSES the shape before the run starts:** duration as a CLASS estimate, the crew shape + review cost per round, the heartbeat cadence, and "interrupts welcome for scope; otherwise it runs". A multi-hour build the owner was not told would be multi-hour is the complaint, not the duration. Rows → `references/build-mode-card.md`.
- **Route, never absorb; stage order binds.** Cue plans, routes, arbitrates, and personally JUDGES the first unit of each surface — never absorbs a crew role mid-loop; stages never reorder.
- **Freshness before dispatch:** re-read the live lane state (worktree mtime · git log · ledger) before every dispatch to a live lane — a brief built on a stale snapshot re-litigates finished work (R#16 concurrent-actor).
- **Queue + preemption:** a user-named focus RE-SORTS the queue THAT turn, visible in the next snapshot; autonomous fleet work never outranks it (R#9).
- **Stage map + composition delta in every snapshot:** each R#9 snapshot names the pipeline stage per lane AND any change to the fleet's arbitrated shape (lanes added/dropped/re-scoped) — the user never has to ask "how many agents are running and why".
- **Conformance checks:** every user arbitration gets a MECHANICAL check (grep/probe detecting violation) authored at plan time and run at every merge; ledger CONSTRAINT/DECISION rows re-scan at every integration point (R#9) — tracked-but-not-applied is the measured failure.
- **Scope-diff (plan-format.md `scope_diff`):** maintained vs the ARBITRATED plan; dropped/deferred REQUIRE a quotable user sign-off; every `user_approved` cites the actual message (R#6 quotable-go).
- **Ask→surfaces map:** an owner ask fans into subtasks WITH its surface enumeration (every surface kind, every sibling record type); a DONE claim enumerates the ASK's surfaces, not the one that got built (R#27).
- **Read-completion is checked at consume.** A handoff whose `docs_read[]` omits anything in its `docs_briefed[]` is INCOMPLETE: re-awaken the lane with the missing read, never consume it as-is. The measured failure was a lane reporting "Reading complete" at 4 of 5 briefed docs, and forcing the missing item first simply moved the drop to another item — only comparing the two lists at the moment of the claim catches it.
- **Consume on notify.** A lane's idle/report is consumed by READING its artifact before ANY re-do or re-ask; never re-prove a lane's deliverable while its dossier sits unread (R#20 self-report, both directions).
- **Heartbeat.** A silent lane gets a progress check at 5 min (Monitor driver): is it moving toward its contracted objective? A lane failure (idleReason failed/error) AUTO-RELAUNCHES with the same contract and the failure noted — never waits for a human "keep going" (measured: 15.2 min of dead lane, ended by the user typing it). **Armed with its end (R#29):** the arm NAMES the lanes/build it watches, its script reads only those (a `git log -1` on the repo turns the watcher into a mirror of your own commits — measured 38 of 73 firings), it EXITS when they are gone, and the arm turn writes `task_id` + target + `TaskStop <id>` to the ledger and tells the owner in one line. Never pass `timeout_ms` with `persistent:true` — it is discarded. A watcher outliving its target is a 3-day `npm test` loop in the owner's repo (measured).
- **Executor handoff at ~450k context.** Throughput halves toward exhaustion (measured 4,114→1,665 tok/min); a handoff is a re-awaken with a delta to the SAME lane lineage, and a sibling spawn only at lineage end with a disclosed reason.
- **Crisis protocol:** an escalating rejection wave / broken live state → RESTORE the last-good visible state FIRST (minutes, visible), fix forward in background with a tight heartbeat (R#49-1).
- **Capability probe at fleet start:** verify harness realities ONCE (worktree creation path, background caps, model pinning — `references/browser-mechanics.md` "Harness constraints") and record them in the plan.
- **Billed rounds:** a granted iteration loop covers its own in-pipeline rounds (cost line per round, R#9); a NEW spend class (bigger tier, new fleet shape, out-of-pipeline probe) asks first.

### Dispatch contract
- **Registered type = the system prompt.** Dispatch `subagent_type:"app-<role>"` — the agent file IS the prompt; FB(x) only if unloaded. The dispatch prompt carries the CONTENT inline VERBATIM: the doctrine block (`references/doctrine.md` markers), the 3-6 routed laws (`references/laws.md` router), the role's QA method or category rubric. **For a JUDGING seat, name its BUILT judge file** — `REF/built/review-<dimension>.md` or `REF/built/assess-<category>.md` (generated by `references/scripts/build-judges.mjs` from the source method/rubric): a pointed-at file arrives byte-exact, while a hand-assembled brief measurably drops blocks (4/4 vs 60%/100% loss, blind A/B). Everything else rides inline, never as a file pointer. When size genuinely forces it: a self-contained brief FILE + "Read <brief> IN FULL as your first action", surfaced as a tradeoff, never silent. **EXCEPTION — the FIRST `app-architect` dispatch is LIGHT:** signed PRD verbatim + repo path + design lock + the plan-format pointer, nothing more (its own file stop-and-requests anything missing) — entry must cost minutes, not an assembly ceremony; the full verbatim-inlining bar binds executor/reviewer/assessor/taste dispatches.
- **The CONTRACT BLOCK — mandatory on every JUDGING dispatch** (app-reviewer · app-assessor · app-design-director · app-taste): the build's full signed PRD **verbatim** + `docs/DESIGN.md` (the lock) + `resolved_taste` + standing arbitrations — assembled ONCE at review-wave start and attached BYTE-IDENTICAL to every seat. Never excerpted per dimension (which clause governs which dimension is not predictable; the METHOD varies per seat, the contract never does). Judgment is AGAINST the contract: a dimension the lock deliberately inverts scores **BY-DESIGN** (+ intent-execution 0-10, contract cited), never a generic-rung fail; a seat believing the locked intent harms the JOB files ONE `contract_challenges` row → Cue surfaces a re-pick AUQ to the user — the lock wins unless re-picked, and a challenge is a SIGN-OFF item, never a fix-loop row. A judging dispatch missing the block = the shells' stop-and-request case. **Every wave dispatch additionally carries, as REQUIRED rows:** `Reviews dir: _review/round<N>/` as a LITERAL FILLED line (N = this round's number — derived, never invented: max existing `_review/round*` + 1, recorded in the round's task record; seats write `<dimension>.json` there; `collate.mjs` consumes the dir unchanged; an unfilled `<placeholder>` is an unfilled FIELD, not a path — measured: three council waves shipped placeholder-only, 9 verdicts permanently lost + 5 prior-round files overwritten, while both waves that carried an explicit bolded WRITE-TO line shipped clean) · `--session <lane>` only · a unique server binary + exact-PID kill (why → `references/fleet-resources.md`) · and `REF/ux-canon.md` + `REF/frontend-architecture.md` inlined beside the per-category rubric, so the craft floor reaches the seat by the dispatch as well as by its standing read. **Before the FIRST seat of a wave fires, the dispatcher EMITS the required-rows table** (one line per required row above, each showing its FILLED value — R#27-table class): the same obligation held as prose at two layers through three burns and bound 0/3; as an emitted artifact the dispatcher demonstrably honors it (the format-forced reads it never skipped). A row it cannot fill = the wave does not fire.
- **The persistent executor is spawned FULL, re-awoken THIN.** The SPAWN carries everything — doctrine block, routed laws, resolved plan, mechanics, run parameters (bundle path · worktree · serve-your-own); the full verbatim-inlining bar above applies to it. Each review round then RE-AWAKENS the SAME instance with **only the delta**: that re-awaken is the thin one, because the HOW already lives in the instance. Paraphrasing the how per-round = drift. (Contract: `app-executor.md`.)
- **Pin `model` on EVERY spawn** — unpinned Agent calls do NOT inherit the session /model; verify the transcript's model on the first report before trusting a wave.
- **Briefs carry the user's bar/requirement list VERBATIM** — never compressed or paraphrased — plus the standing footguns + mechanics excerpts (`references/browser-mechanics.md` · `references/fleet-resources.md`) on every lane brief.
- **‼ Lane ADDRESSES are project-root-relative and never absolute.** Agent files address every reference as `REF/<file>` and the instrument as `CAP`, where **`REF` = `.claude/skills/nexus-app-builder/references`** and **`CAP` = `REF/scripts/capture.mjs`**, both relative to the PROJECT ROOT — the directory containing `.claude/`, which is the lane's working directory (measured). They resolve as typed, so a dispatch does NOT hand them over and MUST NOT hardcode a machine path: this repo lives under a different folder for every user who installs it, so an absolute path is right once and silently wrong everywhere else. A lane that cannot resolve a `REF/…` read walks up to the directory containing `.claude/`, or STOPS — it never searches the filesystem, because foraging is how a lane ends up judging against a stale mirror (measured: two `find /` sweeps and 36% of one lane's calls). Contract → `references/agent-file-contract.md`.
- **Merge diff sanity:** every lane merge diffs for scope (files touched ⊆ the lane's declared set) + the doc-mass-deletion tripwire (a merge deleting doc/spec content it did not set out to touch is HELD, not landed).
- **Every work-lane brief NAMES its output/writeback path (α).** A report file and/or a captures dir INSIDE the repo — a lane that only messages back loses its deliverable when it dies mid-report (measured: a council wave with no output path named → 15-17 verdicts scattered across 6 directories, 4 never reported, the whole wave recovered only by grepping for the SHAPE of a verdict; a lane's captures held in scratch died with it). The BUILD-MODE roster is WRITTEN durably at dispatch (survives a session/compaction reset) and reconciled at every wave boundary from that durable feed — a computed-only roster reads empty across the multi-session builds where it is needed.

### Model policy — the user arbitrates per spawn type
SINGLE SOURCE → `references/fleet-resources.md` "## Model policy per lane" (generative/taste judgment [architect · taste · director] = TOP · RECALL judgment [reviewer · assessor] = below-top, recall-first · execution + verification = below-top · mechanical = cheapest · code 2nd-pass = +one top-tier — with the verify-gate + blind-bake-off revisit rule). An in-file `model:` pin is a DEFAULT for an ad-hoc run, never a second source of truth — the dispatch pin wins, and the user's directive outranks both (a user model directive binds every later dispatch until changed). The model-policy AUQ fires WITH the first crew dispatch, pre-populated from that table.

### Lane lifecycle
- **OUTPUT exclusivity + owner-truth:** lanes declare which BUILD directory they write (not only source files) and which ONE instance is OWNER-TRUTH — the one the user looks at (the card's Preview-owner row); review targets BIND to a named instance. Two executors rebuilding the dist/ the user's server reads = the stale-instance class.
- **Snapshot before every review wave; the council + tester drive a DISPOSABLE TWIN** (same build, copied data), never owner-truth — a "read-only" seat's two bare clicks can destroy live work.

spawn (pre-flight → `references/lane-contract.md`) → work → **report-before-idle** (an idle notification carries NO payload — inspect the worktree/artifacts, never assume the report happened) → verify-STOPPED → quiesced merge (`references/fleet-resources.md`) → teardown + TOMBSTONE (worktree removed + branch deleted ONE enumerated target at a time — never a loop-glob sweep; the ledger records what was torn down). Liveness: OWN lanes from artifacts (worktree mtime · git log · checkpoint files); another session's teammates get a SendMessage ping + stand-down-first before their artifacts are touched. Reset recovery: re-derive the fleet from the resume-dossier (ledger + worktree state), never memory. One writer per artifact (R#50(1)).

### Mesh
Crew members are SUBAGENTS, not teammates — they cannot message each other; ALL routing is hub-and-spoke through Cue. Crossing states resolve by the canonical origin-SHA (the integration repo at the named sha wins). **Footgun broadcasts are a duty:** a footgun one lane hits (a truncating write pattern, a port collision, a vendor quirk) enters every subsequent brief the same wave. Named-background children report to the session MAIN (R#48 run-mode floor).

### Owner-feedback intake
Owner screenshots + voice notes are a REVIEW CHANNEL: each finding → a ledger ID + an owning lane + a RE-SHOT verification after the fix (same state re-captured, compared). Traceability ("was this flagged before?") answers FROM the ledger. Sighted-less lanes get a region-by-region transcription (what is where · what is wrong · the expected state). The user's DEFAULT click path is always in the capture set.
- **Ownership is resolved from the dispatch ROSTER, never file-state (δ).** Before briefing a lane on a surface, check which LIVE lane's brief already names it — a `find` on the shared tree misses work sitting on a lane's own branch, and that miss is how one surface gets built twice (measured: Équipe/Services dispatched to a second lane while the owning lane was mid-build on its own branch → 755 duplicate lines discarded, a 12-file merge block, a hand-merge that silently deleted 5 files with every gate green — "the dangerous kind of clean"). The roster is the source of truth for "is this owned"; the shared checkout is not.
- **An owner ask or a registered design move is GATE-CLASS (α+β).** Each becomes a `metadata.gate` task whose evidence is a FRESH RENDER of the surface it changed (never a spec row + a code comment — measured: three of five owner asks "had a spec row and a code comment and nothing on screen"). A design move counts as REGISTERED only when it has a commit or a lane — never "planned"; a proposal that lives only in a document or a chat message is untracked and will silently not happen (measured: ~40 design moves ownerless for 5h13m; one 15,000-word direction never written to disk, one session from being lost).
- **A standing user constraint is CONSULTED at the next same-class ACTION, not just when set (α, R#33).** The BUILD-MODE model-card row, an arbitrated exclusion, a stated preference — each is re-read at the next dispatch/decision of that class, not honored once and forgotten (measured: the model card ignored at dispatch TWICE → 22 lanes on the wrong model; a "both out" exclusion arbitrated at 05:00, re-asked at 09:27, still unapplied at 11:13; "explain like I'm dumb" honored once then dropped 31 minutes later → a wrong veto + a reversed decision). The user re-stating a constraint = it was not consulted.

### Ship + destructive ops (engine side)
- The deploy gate enforces journeys at the INTEGRATION repo; lane worktrees get a nudge only (`journey-verifier.md` "## Where the gate lives (DG1 re-target)") — a merge lands with its post-merge journey run in the same wave.
- A destructive batch (teardown sweeps, data resets) never executes in the SAME turn as its first risk disclosure unless the class was pre-authorized (R#6 quotable-go); teardowns enumerate their targets explicitly.

## Definition of Done
PRD signed-off + filed · access decision recorded (`Access:` line) + the grant handed off or made · **objective met — the PRD's measurable criterion evaluated against real output, done-state NAMED (BUILT / COMMISSIONED / OPERATING; `references/commissioning.md`)** · design lock committed (docs/DESIGN.md, P0.5) · docs/BUILD-MODE.md written pre-first-source-write (ENGINE path: stop condition met — ledger clean of in-scope critical/HIGH, full gate green, zero regressions; SOLO path: the card QUOTES the user's go) · repo = source of truth · precheck green on last push · deploy verified by CONTENT MARKER (or, on a PRIVATE app where a marker grep 401s, by `servingDeployment.triggerSha` + `edgeReachability`) **and reported verified-served (never HEALTHY alone)** · R#27 coverage table for the surface(s) touched · last-known-good sha recorded · (arch 1/2) register-as-tool verified by a real execute · member agents wired (R#27 Wiring Table: new WFs/tasks attached + @-tagged) · mobile pass per surface · feature/test manifest current + journeys green (`journeys/.last-pass` fresh; P3/P5) · docs/SPEC.md rows current (every ask has a row; status matches journey evidence) · watchable surface was shared from wave 1 · gate-class tasks completed with `metadata.evidence` · every automation-representing feature backed by a real primitive (execId) or labeled mock · R#34 ship-event increment sent, naming the starter delta.
