# Adoption audit — ingesting an existing codebase as a boilerplate

Gate: run BEFORE the first commit/render whenever an app starts from an EXISTING codebase (a donor app, a community boilerplate, a GitHub starter). The adopt DECISION itself is priced UPSTREAM at P1 via `references/base-decision.md` (fitness scorecard · LICENSE hard gate · timeboxed spike) — this audit assumes that decision is already made. Filing the RESULT to community is R#40's job (outbound anonymisation); this audit is the INBOUND twin — purge the donor, verify the model.
Technique for sweeps: ordered longest-first 1:1 find/replace (R#40) — never paraphrase code.

| # | Check | How | Pass bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Donor literals — 3 depths | case-insensitive grep of the donor's brand/org tokens across html/js/css/config: (a) display strings; (b) CODE data-tags (`==="<donor>"` source checks, class ternaries); (c) embedded DOMAIN SEMANTICS (taxonomies/enums/labels living in code) | 0 hits at all three depths |
| 2 | Palette + identity residue | grep the donor's brand hex FAMILY (all tints), favicon/logo data-URIs, font stacks | 0 donor hexes; icons/logos replaced |
| 3 | i18n residue | donor-specific strings in EVERY language dict (×N languages), incl. tooltips + microcopy | swept in all dicts |
| 4 | Code-vs-config enum diff | diff every enum/taxonomy DECLARED in config.example against what the CODE actually switches on | identical, or the code reads config |
| 5 | Config-actually-read litmus | flip each config value (brand label, dataset, taxonomy) → boot → does the UI change? | every config key is live (an ignored key = an instance-bound artifact, WORKFLOW_DESIGN_GUIDE litmus) |
| 6 | Relations on every surface | each first-order relation the PRD data section declares (e.g. entity↔competitors) exists in the DB AND renders on EVERY surface (cards, dashboards, analysis views) | no surface silently omits a declared relation |
| 7 | Derived data full-estate | derived/computed datasets (proximity pairs, aggregates) generated for the WHOLE estate at load time, not the analysed subset | counts match the estate, not the sample |

✗ "re-branding" = swapping display strings + the primary color → the donor's data-tags and embedded taxonomy surface one rejection at a time for days → ✓ the audit runs once, before iteration 1; a clean name-grep alone is NOT a clean adoption (structural tells leak — same insight as the community-KB hygiene generalisation check, opposite direction).

## The OUTBOUND twin — port-time de-brand/tokenize gate
The same discipline fires in the OTHER direction whenever code/styles/checks authored against one app are PORTED into another repo (a starter delta, a component graduation, a pattern reuse):
- **Branding/palette/provenance never merge:** the source app's brand tokens, palette values, and any provenance comments ("ported from <app>", session/wave markers) are stripped or re-tokenized BEFORE the merge — the receiving repo's tokens are the only skin.
- **Tests adapt to the design, never constrain it:** a ported check asserting the SOURCE app's look (its colors, its spacing values, its selectors) is rewritten against the RECEIVING app's tokens/ids — or dropped; a test that freezes the donor's design into the new repo is a defect, not coverage.
- Run checks 1-2 of the table above against the PORTED slice (donor literals · palette residue) with the SOURCE app as the "donor"; 0 hits before the merge lands.

# agent-browser — full reference for driving lanes > READ THIS BEFORE your first `agent-browser` command in a session. It is a fast, capable CLI with > three traps that have already produced a fabricated defect report in a measured evaluation. The > traps are first, because they are what makes an otherwise good tool dangerous unsupervised. A native Rust CLI (v0.33.x observed) that drives Chrome over CDP with no Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. The browser stays warm between commands, so a snapshot costs ~13ms against ~2.9s for a full `capture.mjs` run. It is the best tool we have for INTERACTIVE DRIVING. It is not a measurement instrument — see "What it cannot do". --- ## ‼ The three traps — measured, not theoretical ### 1. The snapshot's first node is a whole-page wrapper carrying every string, WITH a ref ``` - generic "BidNexTenders0Signals3159Proposals0Relevance rubric9Map⌘K Narrow…" [ref=e1] clickable [onclick] - button "Tenders 0" [ref=e3] - button "Relevance rubric 9" [ref=e6] ``` `@e1` is a container whose `name` is the concatenation of the entire page's text. **Any substring search over the snapshot output hits it before the control you wanted.** Measured: grepping for "Relevance rubric" returned `e1`, not `e6`. **Do:** resolve the handle from the control's OWN indented role line — the line that starts `- button "…" [ref=eN]` — never from a text match over the whole blob. ### 2. `click` returns `✓ Done` for a click that does nothing Clicking the wrapper ref above printed `✓ Done` and changed nothing. Clicking the real button ref navigated correctly. The CLI cannot tell you whether an action had an effect, only that it dispatched. **Consequence, measured:** a tester lane clicked wrapper/stale refs, saw `✓ Done` each time, found the page in an unexpected state later, and filed "reproducible silent revert to home, global" as its DOMINANT finding. It did not reproduce under three independent tests. The app was never at fault. **Do:** confirm every action by an OBSERVED change — `get url`, a re-`snapshot`, `diff snapshot`, console/network, or pixels. Never by the exit message. ### 3. `snapshot -i` omits real controls `-i` is what its own docs call "preferred", and on a real app it omitted **14 controls** — an entire map toolbar (zoom, rotate, fullscreen, layers, measure, draw) plus attribution links. All were present in the full `snapshot`. **Do:** use `-i` for token economy while acting. The moment your claim is about COMPLETENESS — how many controls exist, whether something is absent — read the full `snapshot`. ### Also: `get cdp-url` is not side-effect free With no session running it **launches a browser** and prints `[agent-browser] launched browser` before the url. Gate on `session list` (read-only, prints "No active sessions") if you need to know whether a browser is already up. `--max-output` truncates mid-string, which corrupts large JSON payloads — set it explicitly when asking for machine-readable output. --- ## The core loop ```bash agent-browser open # 1. navigate agent-browser snapshot -i # 2. see what is there, with @eN refs agent-browser click @e3 # 3. act on a ref from THAT snapshot agent-browser get url # 4. VERIFY the effect (never trust step 3's output) agent-browser snapshot -i # 5. re-snapshot: refs are regenerated every time ``` **Refs are per-snapshot and go stale the moment the page changes** — after a navigation, a form submit, a dynamic re-render, a dialog opening. Re-snapshot before every ref interaction. Its own guide is `agent-browser skills get core --full`, which ships version-matched with the binary. --- ## Command reference **Core** — `open ` · `read [url]` · `click ` · `dblclick` · `type ` · `fill ` · `press ` · `keyboard type|inserttext ` · `hover` · `focus` · `check` / `uncheck` · `select ` · `drag ` · `upload ` · `download ` · `scroll [px]` · `scrollintoview` · `wait ` · `screenshot [path]` · `pdf ` · `snapshot` · `eval ` · `connect ` · `close [--all]` **Navigation** — `back` · `forward` · `reload` **Getters** — `get text|html|value|attr |title|url|count|box|styles|cdp-url` · `is visible|enabled|checked` **Finders** (an ACTION verb is required: `click`, `fill`, `check`, `hover`, `text`) — `find role|text|label|placeholder|alt|title|testid|first|last|nth [--name ] [--exact]` **Mouse** — `mouse move ` · `down [btn]` · `up [btn]` · `wheel [dx]` **Emulation** — `viewport ` · `device ` · `geo ` · `offline [on|off]` · `headers ` · `credentials ` · `media [dark|light] [reduced-motion]` **Network** — `route [--abort|--body ] [--resource-type ]` · `unroute [url]` · `requests [--clear] [--filter

]` · `har [path]` **State** — `cookies [get|set|clear]` · `storage ` · `tab [new|list|close|]` **Diff** — `diff snapshot` (current vs last) · `diff screenshot --baseline` · `diff url ` **Debug** — `trace start|stop [path]` · `profiler start|stop [path]` · `record start [url]` / `record stop` (WebM video) · `console [--clear]` · `errors [--clear]` · `highlight ` · `inspect` · `clipboard [text]` **Analysis** — `vitals [url] [--json]` (LCP/CLS/TTFB/FCP/INP + React hydration) · `a11y [url] [--tags ] [--selector ] [--json]` (axe-core audit, WCAG violations with selectors and fix guidance) · `react tree` · `react inspect ` **SPA** — `pushstate ` (auto-detects the Next.js router; falls back to history.pushState) **Batch** — `batch [--bail] "cmd" ...` (sequential; `--bail` stops on first error) **Auth vault** — `auth save|login|list|show|delete ` (`--url`, `--username`, `--password-stdin`, `--credential-provider`, selector overrides) **Sessions** — `session` · `session list` · `--session ` to isolate **Snapshot options** — `-i` interactive only · `-c` compact · `-d ` depth cap · `-s ` scope **Setup** — `install [--with-deps]` · `upgrade` · `doctor [--fix]` · `profiles` · `mcp` (stdio server) --- ## Sessions and parallelism The daemon is SHARED STATE. Concurrent lanes driving one browser contaminate each other, which is the one-writer collision class this fleet has already paid for. Give each lane its own `--session `, or accept that you are sharing. `session list` is read-only and tells you what is already running; `close --all` closes every session, not just yours. An idle daemon shuts down on a timeout (`--idle-timeout`, `AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`) and the next command restarts it — so "the browser is warm" is an assumption to check, not a guarantee. --- ## Interop with `capture.mjs` `capture.mjs --attach` connects our instrument to an ALREADY-RUNNING agent-browser browser via `connectOverCDP`, so the thing we measure is the thing your lane is driving. Opt-in only. It is gated on `session list` and falls back to launching its own browser when no session exists. Honest sizing: `chromium.launch()` costs ~87ms of a ~2900ms capture, so attaching saves ~3%. Its value is shared-browser fidelity, not speed. Note that an attached page ignores Playwright's viewport option, so `capture.mjs` forces and asserts the metrics over CDP. --- ## What it cannot do No geometry, no occlusion, no reachability, no design measurement — its output carries none of it (we grepped for it). It therefore cannot find: - a control that renders and reads as present but whose click lands on something else (a panel overlapping it); - a control that changes nothing anywhere when clicked; - contrast, spacing-grid, target-size or column-void defects. Those are `capture.mjs`'s job. **Use agent-browser to DRIVE, capture.mjs to MEASURE and to PROVE.**

# The agent-file contract

> LOAD WHEN: writing or editing any `app-*` lane file, or adding a new lane. Enforced deterministically
> by `skills/shared/scripts/conformance.mjs` — run it before you commit an agent-file change.

An agent file IS a lane's system prompt. It is the only tier in this repo that had no contract of its
own, and every defect the W25 audit found is a consequence: three incompatible pointer conventions
none of which resolved, five lanes that could not refuse an under-specified dispatch, two lanes with
no completion predicate, and one lane shipping with no tools at all.

The rule that generates all of it: **a cross-artifact claim is a contract, and a contract nobody
executes is a wish.** Everything below is a claim an agent file makes about something else — where a
file is, what a dispatch owes it, what its output means — so everything below is checkable.

---

## Addresses: `REF` and `CAP`

**An agent file has no base directory.** A relative path inside one resolves to nothing. This is not
theoretical: a lane handed a `!!`-gated read it could not open ran two filesystem-wide `find /` sweeps,
burned 36% of its tool calls foraging, and resolved to the mirror copy of the doctrine rather than the
primary — so it judged against whatever was last pushed.

So a lane addresses everything through two tokens with ONE fixed meaning:

| Token | Expands to | Relative to |
|---|---|---|
| `REF` | `.claude/skills/nexus-app-builder/references` | the PROJECT ROOT |
| `CAP` | `REF/scripts/capture.mjs` | the PROJECT ROOT |

**The project root is the directory that contains `.claude/`, and it is the lane's working directory** —
measured: a subagent's `pwd` is the project root and `.claude/skills/nexus-app-builder/references/agent-browser.md`
resolves for it as typed. So nothing has to hand a lane its addresses; they already work.

- In an agent file, write `` `REF/agent-browser.md` `` and `` `CAP` ``.
- **Never an absolute path — not in the file, and not in the dispatch either.** This repo is installed
  under a different folder, by a different user, on every machine that runs it. `/Users/<someone>/…` is
  correct exactly once and wrong everywhere else, and the wrongness is silent: the read just fails and
  the lane goes foraging, which is the failure this convention exists to end.
- If a `REF/…` read fails, you are not at the project root. Walk up to the directory containing
  `.claude/` and retry, or say so and STOP. Do not search the filesystem for a copy — that is how a lane
  ends up reading a stale mirror of the doctrine instead of the live one.

---

## Required sections

Every lane carries all of these. The kit template this descends from put it plainly: *every field is
load-bearing; delete none of them.* Ours adds the addresses row and the STOP rule, because those are
what the audit proved were missing.

### `## Your dispatch carries (demand what is missing)`
What the orchestrator owes this lane, and the refusal. **The first row is always the addresses row:**

```
- **`REF`** — the absolute path of this skill's `references/` dir; **`CAP`** — the absolute path of
  `REF/scripts/capture.mjs`. Every `REF/…` and `CAP` below resolves through them. Absent → STOP and
  request them; do not guess a path, do not skip a gated read, do not go looking.
```

Then the lane's own inputs. Then the refusal, explicitly: *"→ STOP and request them."* A lane that
cannot refuse an under-specified brief will improvise one, and an improvised brief is the drift the
whole engine exists to prevent.

### `## You own`
2-5 bullets. Concrete artifacts, not responsibilities — "the shared type files" beats "type quality".

### `## You never touch`
Name the adjacent lanes' territory explicitly. An unnamed boundary is not a boundary.

### `## Tools`
The real granted toolset, and it must agree with the frontmatter. See below — this is where the
worst single defect of the audit lived.

### `## Method`
Ordered. **Starts with a read step. Ends with a verification step that names what evidence counts.**
A method whose last step is "implement" produces a lane whose last step is "implement".

### `## Role-specific traps`
The 2-4 mistakes this lane actually makes, grown from real incidents. A trap section invented up front
lists what you already feared; the valuable entries arrive after a failure.

### `## Handoff out`
`to:` and `must include:` — always covering `verified` (with a *how* per claim) and `unverified`.

### `## Done when`
Observable completion. Not "the work is finished" — the artifact exists and you saw it work, and for a
lane that produces evidence, that its evidence files exist on disk.

---

## Frontmatter `tools:` — the boundary is the toolset, not the prose

Two rules, both learned the expensive way.

**1. `tools: All tools` grants NOTHING.** It is parsed as the two-name list `["All","tools"]`; neither
is a tool, so the lane falls through to the always-injected defaults. Measured live: a backend
executor with that line held no Write, no Edit, no Bash — not even Read. To grant everything, **omit
the key**. To grant a subset, enumerate real names.

**2. The prose and the key are two declarations of one fact, so they must agree.**

| The file says | The frontmatter must |
|---|---|
| "Write access to X" / "your only writes are …" / "write `<file>.json`" | grant `Write` (or `Edit`) |
| "You edit NOTHING" | not grant `Write`/`Edit` |
| a boundary that `Bash` can trivially cross ("the migration directory **only**") | either tighten the toolset, or say plainly that the boundary is prose-enforced and name the check that backs it |

Where a boundary is prose-enforced, say so in the file rather than implying a guarantee the toolset
does not provide — the orchestrator's merge diff (`SKILL.md` "Dispatch contract") is the real check,
and a lane should know that is what it is trusting.

---

## Typed final message

A lane whose output is machine-consumed ends with one object and nothing after it. The doctrine
handoff schema binds it: `verified` and `unverified` are **required** — empty is allowed, absent is
not, and `not_verified` is not the field name. A prose obligation the object cannot express is an
obligation nobody can check: if the file says "run the harness falsification probe", the object needs
a slot that says whether it ran.

---

## Shared blocks

Some conduct is genuinely identical across lanes (the browser conduct block is 39 lines carried by
five). Copies are fine — the dispatch carries content, not pointers, and that is deliberate. What is
not fine is silent divergence, so the conformance checker asserts every carrier is byte-identical.
Edit one, edit all, in the same pass.

---

## Before you commit an agent-file change

```bash
node skills/shared/scripts/conformance.mjs --self-test   # every check proves it can fail
node skills/shared/scripts/conformance.mjs               # then the real tree
node skills/nexus-app-builder/references/scripts/build-judges.mjs --check   # built judges current
```

The self-test comes first on purpose: a check that has never been seen failing proves nothing about
the green it just gave you.

**You do not have to remember any of this.** The `CF1` arm (`hooks/nexus-conformance.py`, PostToolUse
on Write/Edit) runs the checker automatically after any write to an `app-*` lane, `journey-verifier`,
or anything under `skills/nexus-app-builder/`, and surfaces what broke. That is deliberate: the first
version of this document ended here, relying on a human reading it — which is the exact decay class
this whole contract exists to prevent. A gate whose only trigger is someone's memory is not a gate.
Rollout state: while `hooks/.conformance-observe` exists the arm records to the session decision log
and surfaces nothing; delete the marker to enforce, re-create it to revert.

# API surface contract

!! Before the first line of a middleware or API app: fill this in and put it in the PRD. !!

Four lines. If you cannot fill them in, the design is not yet decided — and deciding it in code is how a
dispatcher ends up with a spec that describes the dispatcher instead of the API.

    ROUTES:      one path per capability the caller invokes — list them
    AUTH:        the scheme, declared ONCE and applied globally — never a per-operation parameter
    SPEC SOURCE: what generates the document — the route table, or nothing
    SCHEMAS:     the objects the server validates against ARE the objects the spec publishes

This is a CONTRACT, not a guide. It is four fillable lines because a page that takes ten minutes to read
will not be read at the moment it matters — the moment the design is committed, before any code exists.

## The four failures this prevents

**One endpoint with a selector.** `POST /call` with a route name in the body collapses every capability into
one operation. The consumer sees one action; the spec describes the dispatcher, not the API. If the domain
has N operations, the surface has N paths.

**Auth as a parameter.** An API key declared per-operation is wrong in OpenAPI: it is a security scheme,
declared once and applied globally. Per-operation makes every generated client carry it as a business
argument.

**A spec that can drift.** A hand-written document diverges from the code on the first change after it is
written. Generate it by walking the route table, and assert in a test that served routes and documented
routes are the same set **in both directions**.

**A spec you need a key to read.** A contract exists to be consumed before the caller has credentials.
Behind the auth check it cannot do its job. Health and spec are unauthenticated.

## Two traps that pass every test

**Version keyword drift.** Declaring `openapi: 3.1.0` while using `nullable: true` is silent: JSON Schema
ignores unknown keywords, nothing errors, and every nullable field generates as **non-nullable** in client
code. In 3.1 nullability is a union type — `type: ["integer","null"]`, or `anyOf` for a nullable reference.

**Registration is idempotent.** Re-running registration does not refresh an already-registered tool: it keeps
advertising the old actions until the tool is explicitly updated. Changing the spec is not shipping it.

## Two engineering defaults worth stating

**Bodies are not downloaded to prove a resource exists.** A service that fetches caller-supplied URLs and
reads the whole response to confirm a 200 is a denial-of-service tool aimed at your own network. Destroy the
socket at header time; the timing you report is time-to-headers, and say so.

**A service that fetches caller-supplied URLs needs an SSRF guard, on by default.** Loopback, link-local
(including the cloud metadata address), private, CGNAT and reserved ranges — for v4 and v6, including
IPv4-mapped forms. The DNS-rebinding window between validation and connection is real; either pin the
connection to the validated address or state the gap plainly rather than implying it is closed.

## Failing the contract

Any line you cannot fill is a design decision you have not made. Make it — in one exchange with the owner if
it is theirs — before the first line of code.

Archetypes and boundary notes → `archetypes.md`. The PRD this is filed into → `prd-template.md`.
The build-mode record that governs whether a crew runs at all → `build-mode-card.md`.

# The 3 app archetypes — pick by consumer

| # | Archetype | Consumer | Shape | Closes with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MIDDLEWARE / backend | Nexus itself (agents/workflows need logic no single OpenAPI spec covers) | hosted service; polling, multi-step vendor flows, stateful logic | `register-as-tool` → the middleware becomes a CUSTOM_MANIFEST tool agents/WFs call |
| 2 | EXPOSED MODALITY | the outside world (a partner/system calls Nexus) | thin app wrapping an agent/workflow/tool behind the app's edge-auth token | publish the endpoint contract; key rotation story |
| 3 | FULL front+back | humans in a browser | UI + backend wired to Nexus data/modalities (BQ, agents, workflows) | P5 review gate + rollout per PRD |

Decision test: "who consumes the output?" Another SYSTEM → 1 or 2 (2 if the caller is external to Nexus). HUMANS on a URL → 3. Mixed (a UI **and** callers) → 3 + a `register-as-tool` slice of its backend.

Boundary notes:
- Archetype 2 ≠ a channel Deployment: a Deployment is a Nexus conversation channel for an AGENT; archetype 2 is an HTTP contract for machines.
- An app can EMBED an agent (a chat widget on archetype 3) — the agent stays a channel Deployment owned by `nexus-deployments`, and the integration is a LADDER (widget iframe → restyled deployment → API-mode native chat): `../nexus-deployments/channels/embed.md` "## Embedding the agent in your app".
- A workflow that only needs a nightly run is NOT an app — apps earn their runtime by being CALLED or OPENED.
- **A DESKTOP app is a DELIVERY FORM of archetype 3, never a fourth archetype.** The hosted app stays the single source; the desktop build is a thin SHELL that opens one window on its origin and adds what a tab cannot (persistent session, save-dialog exports, Dock icon + badge, OS notifications, an offline screen). It holds no server and no credential. Shape, feature floor, macOS packaging without a Developer ID, and copy-ready templates → `desktop-shell.md`.
- **Access is a first-class decision for EVERY archetype (recorded at the PRD, gated at deploy).** `visibility` is `PRIVATE|PUBLIC`; apps are created PRIVATE and `nexus vibe app visibility <appId> private|public` flips it (going private mints a FRESH edge token → re-register any linked tool). PRIVATE = a person signs in with Nexus and is admitted only if the app's ACCESS LIST allows them; an API client with neither identity nor token gets 401, never a silent 404. The access list is a permission tuple — resourceType `vibe_app` × subjectType `user|group|organization|api_key` × relation `owner|editor|viewer` — so "this GROUP may open this app" is native. LADDER: (1) DEFAULT — every person gets an identity, joins a GROUP, the GROUP is granted `viewer`; (2) FALLBACK, only on the owner's recorded decline — the app goes PUBLIC **and carries its own authentication**; public NEVER means unauthenticated. ‼ Granting is a DASHBOARD action (`/app/invitations`, `/app/settings/user-groups`): an org API key gets 403 on the permission + user-group routes, so Cue hands the step off with the exact grant to make and NEVER claims to have made it. Org-wide lever: setting resource-type `vibe_app` to `closed` makes every app permission-gated by default. **This is the POLICY half — who may open the app. The RUNTIME half (what the app reads to know WHO is calling: `X-Vibe-User-Id` · `X-Vibe-User-Email` · `X-Vibe-Auth-Via`, what they carry on each path, and why only the middleware makes them trustworthy) → `edge-identity.md`, before the first server route.**

Data-layer defaults (all archetypes; WF-node twins — SQL-in-a-node mechanics + MERGE upserts — live in `../nexus-workflow-builder/reference/workflow-patterns/patterns/db-check-branch.md`, don't restate them): warehouse-first (own store over live third-party reads once data lands); big/volatile payloads behind a TTL-cached endpoint + relative-path fetch; loaders tri-state (a failed load must NOT cache as success — reset the latch, bounded self-heal); an aggregate that refreshes at batch boundaries treats EMPTY as a miss → raw-layer fallback; static export twins re-exported after each data refresh. Pipeline/funnel stores carry PROVENANCE from v1: a `discovered_via`-class column (how each row entered) and a machine-readable `reason` on every dropped/excluded row — every row lands SOMEWHERE with a why, because the user must see work being done and these columns are the fastest diagnosis instrument you will own (forensics.md prior 7).

# The backend build discipline

A backend or middleware build is the SAME convergence loop as a UI build with ONE substitution: the visual verdict becomes a CONTRACT-TEST verdict. Almost no new machinery — a different judge.

## The cycle

```
contracts (schema FIRST, type derived from it)
    → tests generated FROM requirements
    → executor builds
    → tests run against the RUNNING service
    → read the failures
    → delta back to the SAME executor
    → repeat until green AND every FIX row evidenced
```

The executor is PERSISTENT — one instance per build, re-awoken with each round's delta, never re-spawned (CLAUDE.md R#48: craft concurrency = 1). The shared type is the handoff medium: contracts land before any consumer lane starts.

## The backend seam ladder — where a unit becomes a FILE somebody can own

A service fans out on exactly the same law as a UI: **lanes ≤ independently-ownable artifacts, and
the artifact count is a property of the TREE, which the root can edit before dispatch**
(`REF/plan-format.md`, Step 4b, "Raising the ceiling"). What differs is where the seams fall. Descend IN ORDER, stop when
ownable-artifacts ≥ units, and note that two rungs are NOT free to split at any width.

| # | Split at | Lives at | Crew owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **the contract** — schema first, type derived from it | `contracts/` | `app-contracts` |
| 2 | **the domain entity** — its type and its invariants | `domain/<entity>/` | `app-backend` |
| 3 | **the use case** — ONE file per use case | `usecases/<verb>-<entity>.*` | `app-backend` |
| 4 | **the port/adapter** — one per external system | `adapters/<system>/` | `app-backend` |
| 5 | **the route/controller** — one per resource, THIN | `routes/<resource>.*` | `app-backend` |
| 6 | **the migration** — see below, this rung does not fan out | `migrations/` | `app-migrations`, exclusively |
| 7 | **the test suite** — additive, globbed by a root-owned runner | `tests/<lane>.spec.*` | the owning lane |

**Rung 3 is the ceiling-raiser.** A `<Entity>Service` file holding twelve use cases passes every code
review as cohesive and is a hard ceiling of ONE lane, because twelve lanes cannot own one file. One
file per use case turns twelve units into twelve artifacts, and each one carries its own contract test.
This is the backend twin of splitting a screen into components, and it is skipped for the same reason:
nothing about the fat file looks wrong until dispatch.

**Rung 1 is a ROOT, never a lane's own file.** Every consumer compiles against the contract, so two
lanes editing it is the same defect as two lanes editing one screen — except worse, because the
failure surfaces as a type error in a THIRD lane that changed nothing. The contract lands, is
committed, and only then does anything fan out.

**Rung 6 has a ceiling of ONE by nature, not by tree shape.** Migration ORDER is global state: two
lanes writing migrations produce two timelines that are individually valid and jointly wrong, and the
damage is to data rather than to a build. `app-migrations` owns the directory alone, holds its human
approval gate, and no build lane owns a path inside it — no `unsplittable_reason` unlocks this one.

**The seam row is a CONTRACT-CONSISTENCY lane** (`plan-format.md`, Step 6 — verification must not be
cut along the same seam as the work). Its acceptance is cross-endpoint: the same entity serialised
identically by every route that returns it, one error vocabulary, one pagination grammar, one date
format. Per-endpoint tests pass while the API disagrees with itself, and no per-lane green can say so.

**Written from the contract, never from the running service** (Step 6b). A test derived from the
service's actual response passes because it was written to pass, and dies with that version.

## Four service defaults

| Default | Rule | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Queryable | the service can be ASKED what it holds, not only fed | if nobody can query it, nobody can tell BUILT from COMMISSIONED |
| Self-describing route | one endpoint reports version, health, and the objective's live measure | makes the commissioning measure readable without a console |
| Meaning-bearing OpenAPI | field names and descriptions carry domain meaning | `data: object` documents nothing and blocks every consumer |
| Auth answered at the PRD | decided at P0, never discovered at deploy — the DEFAULT answer is PRIVATE + a granted user GROUP (ladder + endpoints → `archetypes.md` "Boundary notes") | auth found late rewrites the client contract |

## Method

- **Checkpoint per file.** Commit each completed file. A limit death then costs one file, not a wave.
- **Disk-coverage recompute.** Coverage is recomputed FROM DISK, never accumulated in memory or carried across a restart — recall drops exactly the items you do not happen to remember.
- **Verifier silence = FAILURE.** A verification lane that returns nothing has not passed; it has not reported. Red until its artifact exists.
- **Unskippable gates.** A gate waivable by assertion is not a gate. A waiver is a logged override with a named reason.

## The tier ladder

Start at the cheapest model tier that could plausibly work. PROMOTE on a MEASURED trigger, never a hunch — state the number that promotes it ("65% zero-mapped → next tier"). Own harness bugs before blaming the model: a wrong prompt and a weak model look identical from the outside, and the prompt is the cheaper hypothesis to test.

## The self-test tool (a REQUIRED dispatch slot)

Every judgment-producing lane gets a DETERMINISTIC CHECKER that applies its output to real data and reports OK or PHANTOM per claim, with the actual keys observed. The lane iterates to zero phantom and stamps `verified_by_tool`.

**Self-reported confidence WITHOUT a tool stamp is unverified** (R#20 Self-report).

Prove the checker itself: plant a defect, watch it go red on that exact case, restore. A checker that has never failed has never been tested — a dead check passes every silent test.

This is the backend twin of the UI executor's build → screenshot → read-pixels loop: **propose → apply to reality → read the result → fix.**

## Boot resilience

A service BOOTS without a successful external call — degrade, retry with backoff, serve a health route reporting degraded. Never gate startup on an upstream 200: a container that cannot start until a third party answers is a crash-loop waiting for that third party's worst day, and the platform will roll it back before anyone sees the cause. Errors the service logs carry the REAL body, never the generic status (R#20).

## Where the rest lives

- Done-states + their evidence → `commissioning.md`
- Gate suite, ledger, enforcement ladder, gate-authoring meta-rules → `gates-and-ledger.md`
- Archetype 1/2 gate artifact sets → the P5 Review-gate section of `SKILL.md`, under **Per-archetype gate set** (the switch is the BUILD-MODE card's Archetype row): light PRD + contract-tests-green against the RUNNING service + register-as-tool; a visual design lock and click-journeys are NOT demanded of an API. `archetypes.md` picks the archetype; it does not carry the gate set.
- Lane pre-flight, output exclusivity, owner-truth → `lane-contract.md`

# Base-decision gate — price the foundation before building on it

!! Run at the adopt-vs-fresh moment (SKILL P1), BEFORE the first commit/render, for ANY base: a donor repo · a community boilerplate · a GitHub starter · an existing org SYSTEM to extend · a donor deck/template. The P2 `adoption-audit.md` is the POST-decision purge; this gate decides whether the base is worth carrying at all. The base is the furthest-fanning, hardest-reversed commit in a build — every later decision inherits its stack, license, de-brand surface, and design malleability, so disqualifiers found AFTER commit surface one rejection at a time for hours. !!

## 1. Fitness scorecard — STRUCTURAL ARTIFACT (R#27-class; emit before the arbitration AUQ)

One column per candidate, ALWAYS including "build fresh" and "org starter" (`apps-starter` — when it fits, the brownfield question rarely arises):

| Dimension | <base A> | Build fresh | Org starter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stack vs goal (language · rendering model: SPA/SSR · runtime) | | | |
| License (→ §2 hard gate) | | | |
| De-brand / strip surface (brand strings · palette · enums · icons · i18n) | | | |
| Build weight (files · deps · monorepo tax · build minutes) | | | |
| Design malleability (tokens vs identity baked into components) | | | |
| **Components shipped** — which complex controls come WITH this base (data table · filter/search · kanban · record page · wizard), enumerated from its resolved inventory root (installed catalog OR vendored tree), never recalled | | | |
| Nexus-wiring fit (data spine · chat bridge · register-as-tool) | | | |
| Client-state / reactivity architecture (a real data layer, or a per-page fetch pattern that fans out?) | | | |
| Est. strip-cost vs build-fresh cost | | | |

Verdict per column: adopt / reject / **spike first** (§3). Every cell is a FACT gathered in minutes (a LICENSE file read, a `package.json` glance, a grep of the brand token) — the gate exists because these facts are knowable upfront and historically went unpriced. A donor's ABSENCE of a client data layer is itself a decision INHERITED silently — its per-page fetch pattern fans out into every surface that copies it; state, per reused pattern, whether it is inherited or replaced.

## 2. License gate (HARD)

Read the base's LICENSE file — never assume from the README. Copyleft (AGPL/GPL) or non-commercial terms on a base for a proprietary/client deliverable is a DISQUALIFIER surfaced to the user for EXPLICIT accept, never silently carried; renaming identifiers or editing heavily does NOT change a derivative's license — only clean-room reauthoring from specs does. No license file found = unknown = blocking until resolved. AGPL's network clause binds even unpublished code the moment users interact with a served derivative.

## 3. Timeboxed proof spike (R#24 family)

Any ⚠/uncertain disqualifier ("will it boot against our stub?" · "does it hold our data model?" · "does the record UI strip cleanly?") → prove the RISKIEST assumption against a stub in a bounded spike (hours, not days), THEN decide. Never commit on paper to an uncertain base; never build fully to discover the answer. The spike is throwaway by contract — its output is one scorecard cell, not code to keep.

## 4. The arbitration AUQ carries the scorecard AS its decision surface

The adopt-vs-build question presents the PRICED columns (never a bare "fork or fresh?"), the recommendation, and the runner-up in one line each. Its outcome lands in the PRD **Foundation / base** row (the sign-off artifact) — and for a foreign repo, as `docs/BASE_DECISION.md` in the repo itself (the BAS1 hook checks for it at first mutation).

✗ user names a base → clone → build → wrong-stack, copyleft, and a de-brand war surface serially over hours; three foundations burned in a day. → ✓ scorecard at the decision: stack + license visible in rows 1-2 before any commit; the uncertain "holds our data model?" gets a bounded stub spike; the user picks a priced column ONCE.

# BROWSER + SERVE MECHANICS — hard-won; don't rediscover

> LOAD WHEN: assembling an executor or driving-reviewer dispatch (inject the relevant
> sections), or debugging a stalled/blank/wrong-size capture. These are tooling facts an
> agent otherwise burns real cycles rediscovering. Follow them from the first shot.

---

## ‼ FIRST CHOICE — the pre-built `capture.mjs` (fast, stall-proof, validated)

For measurement, screenshots, and no-scroll/mobile checks, DO NOT hand-roll Playwright and
NEVER use the interactive MCP browser tools. Call the hardened probe
(`references/scripts/capture.mjs` — copy it into the build's tooling or call it in place)
via Bash (`timeout: 90000`; `600000` when sweeping). It self-exits, always closes the browser,
never waits on canvas/networkidle, and returns JSON — so it cannot stall.

### `capture` — the consolidated run. Start here.

One command produces a run folder that answers all four review questions at once: what is on
this screen, does every control actually work, what does each control DO, and is it well made.

**Dependencies resolve themselves — do NOT pass `PW=` unless you have a reason.** The script
searches, in order: `$PW` · `~/.nexus-tools/node_modules/playwright` (the durable home) · beside
the script · the caller's project · node resolution. A session scratchpad is NOT a durable home;
pointing `PW` at one is how the instrument breaks for everyone when that temp dir is cleaned.

`node <scripts>/capture.mjs doctor` answers "can this machine run me, and if not, what exactly do
I run" in one call — it reports the resolved Playwright path, the browser cache, a real launch
test, and whether agent-browser is present (optional; it only unlocks the warm-attach path).
Missing dependency errors name their own fix command instead of dumping a stack trace.

```
node <scripts>/capture.mjs "http://localhost:$PORT/#/<route>" <outdir> 1512x900 [flags]
  # (a URL as the first argument means `capture`; the narrow modes below stay explicit by name)

  outdir/manifest.json        index + FINDINGS: unreachable controls, NO-OP controls, console errors
  outdir/state-NNN.json       every addressable control — stable `hash` (survives re-render) + `@eN` ref,
                              `rect` (document space) + `viewportRect` (screen space), `why` it counts as
                              interactive, `reachable`, plus the FULL design measurement under `measure`
  outdir/state-NNN.tree.txt   indented view; ref-bearing lines and their ancestors only
  outdir/state-NNN.png        clean shot
  outdir/state-NNN.annotated.png   the same shot with numbered @eN badges (RED = unreachable)
  outdir/<state>-tNN.transition.json   per action: identity diff (appeared/gone/changed) + content
                              delta + pixel diff (with a diff image) + network calls + focus/scroll +
                              a NO-OP verdict
```

Flags: `--click=@e5|<sel>|<text>` one action · `--sweep [--sweep-max=N]` exercise every control from a
fresh page each time · `--viewports=1920x1080,390x844` · `--themes=light,dark` · `--root=<sel>` ·
`--no-measure` · `--no-annotate` · `--pixel-threshold=0.1`.

**Two findings only `capture` can give you.** `unreachable` = a control the DOM says is there and a
screenshot shows, but a click at its centre lands on something else (a panel overlapping it). `NO-OP` =
a control that, when clicked, changes nothing anywhere — no DOM, no content, no pixels beyond its own
focus ring, no request, no focus move, no scroll. Neither is visible to a screenshot review, and
`--sweep` turns finding them from a lottery into an enumeration.

### Single-answer shortcuts

Still available when you want one number and not a folder:

```
node capture.mjs measure "<url>" 1512x900 [--dark] [--touch] [--root=<sel>]
  # → {distinctFontSizes[], distinctSpacings[], spacingsOffGrid[], distinctColors, distinctRadii[],
  #    worstContrasts[], contrastFailCount, undersizedTargets[], listDensity[], columnVoids[],
  #    scrollH,innerH,fits, scrollW,innerW,noHScroll, mustsee:[{sel,inView,hittable}]}
node capture.mjs shot  "<url>" /tmp/x.png 390x844 --touch     # a screenshot
node capture.mjs shots "<url>" <outdir> [--tabs=a,b]          # clean multi-viewport×theme set
node capture.mjs state "<url>" "<sel>"                        # idle/hover/active/focus pliancy diff
node capture.mjs hit   "<url>" "<sel>"                        # elementFromPoint at the centre
node capture.mjs eval  "<url>" "(()=>{ ...return JSON... })()" 1512x900
```

Use `--dark` for the dark theme, `--touch` + a phone WxH for mobile, and `--root=<selector>`
to scope to the screen under test (exclude the app shell).

### Porting from a reference implementation — calibrate, never inherit

A constant, unit or coordinate convention copied from someone else's browser code is a CLAIM about
THEIR runtime, not ours, and it fans out silently into every number derived from it. Measured, all three
in one port and all three silent:

| Inherited assumption | What our runtime actually does |
|---|---|
| "CDP bounds are device pixels, divide by devicePixelRatio" | Under a Playwright `deviceScaleFactor` context they are ALREADY CSS pixels — raw `[12, 104.296875, 207, 31.5]` matched `getBoundingClientRect` exactly at dpr=2. Dividing halved every rect and mis-located every hit test. |
| "bounds are viewport-relative" | They are DOCUMENT-relative: bounds y=900 at scrollY=500 while the DOM rect read 400. |
| "`cursor: pointer` marks a control" | It INHERITS, so every descendant of a pointer-styled button matches: 87 of 126 detected "controls" were a `::before`, an 8x8 `svg`, a 4x2 `path`. |

So: **derive the value from the live runtime rather than adopting the source's constant.** Measure one
known element against `getBoundingClientRect` and compute the scale per run; read the scroll offset
rather than assuming a space; test whether a CSS signal inherits before treating it as per-element.
The reference implementation is right about ITS setup — the reason it differs is usually a setup
difference (theirs applies `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`; ours does not), not a bug in either.

**AUTHORITATIVE vs candidate:** the probe's COUNTS + GEOMETRY are authoritative — distinct
font-sizes, spacings, off-grid list, radii, undersized targets, `fits`/`noHScroll`/`mustsee`.
**Its CONTRAST numbers are now authoritative too, including oklab()/oklch() accent tokens** — the
script resolves those in-page via Ottosson math rather than canvas alone, which is what used to
produce a false ~1:1 on accent elements (`capture.mjs` header + the resolver comment). *Superseded
2026-07: the older rule here said an accent-element contrast fail was only a CANDIDATE needing a
shot-confirm. It no longer is — discounting those was discounting the real failures.* The one
remaining exclusion is `color-mix()` with unresolved custom properties, which is skipped, not
guessed. Only drop to a hand-written script for behaviour the probe modes don't cover —
then follow the anti-stall rules below.

## Never the shared MCP browser for proof

The shared/interactive MCP browser has two silent traps:
- **Custom-filename screenshots silently no-op** — `screenshot({path:'x.png'})` reports
  success and writes nothing; only default filenames save (into `.playwright-mcp/`).
- **It floors the viewport** (~1125h / ~487w) — it will NOT honor 1512×900 or a 390-wide
  phone. Any dimension-sensitive verdict (no-scroll, mobile, density) taken on it is
  verified at the WRONG size — the exact hole that lets clipping through.

It is fine for a quick ad-hoc human-style look — never for spec-sized proof or the record.

## Self-launched chromium (when you drive beyond the probe)

```js
import pkg from '<worktree>/node_modules/playwright/index.js'; const { chromium } = pkg;
const b = await chromium.launch();
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1512, height: 900 }, deviceScaleFactor: 2 });
await p.goto(`http://localhost:${PORT}/#/<route>`);
await p.waitForSelector('<a real element on the screen>', { timeout: 15000 }); // readiness, not a blind sleep
await p.waitForTimeout(600);                                                    // settle for canvas/anim
await p.screenshot({ path: '_captures/<name>.png' });                           // honored: real file, exact size
```

**Wait on a readiness SIGNAL, not a race.** Shooting before the bundle/canvas renders
yields a blank page that reads as a real render — a blank/placeholder screenshot is a build
failure caught by reading pixels, never captured as a pass.

**Viewport discipline:** judge at the owner's REAL scale — calibrate against the viewport
the user actually works at, and sweep the fold sizes (1920×1080 · 1512×900 · **1512×768**
laptop fold · 390×844 · 844×390 landscape). A defect fixed at 900 height routinely
survives at 768.

**Drags:** `locator.dragTo(target)` dispatches real pointer events; components needing
intermediate moves take explicit `mouse.move` steps. Confirm the drop by `elementFromPoint`
+ the asserted state change — a drag that "looks done" in a screenshot is not a drag that
fired. Test the FAST variant too (single quick move→up): listeners attached in an effect
race a fast down→up and silently no-op.

## ‼ ANTI-STALL — bounded `.mjs` via Bash, never interactive waits

The harness kills a subagent after ~600s of NO OUTPUT (the stream watchdog). Driving the
browser through interactive MCP tools blocks the agent's output stream while a call waits —
and a WebGL canvas never fires `load`/`networkidle`, so an open-ended wait runs to the
watchdog and the agent dies. So:

- **Run browser work as a self-contained `.mjs` via the Bash tool** (pass `timeout: 90000`
  — a hung script dies in Bash and RETURNS; the agent never reaches the watchdog).
- Inside the script: a **global self-timeout** so it ALWAYS returns
  (`setTimeout(()=>{console.log(JSON.stringify(partial));process.exit(0)},60000)`),
  `browser.close()` in a `finally`, an explicit short timeout on EVERY op.
- **Never wait on `networkidle` or a canvas.** `goto(url,{timeout:20000,waitUntil:
  'domcontentloaded'})` then a FIXED short settle, then measure. Collect all numbers for a
  state in ONE `page.evaluate`.
- **Checkpoint** results to a file after each state, so a kill loses little.
- Few, short-lived chromium instances (launch → measure → close); many long-lived headless
  browsers contend and hang.

## Serve the BUILT bundle

After the production build, the served bundle is what ships (L08) — the dev server proves
nothing about it. Copy runtime assets the route needs into the build output (models,
photos, fonts) or they 404 and overlays render over nothing. An in-memory demo store
re-seeds on server restart — restart to re-seed rather than persisting reviewer mutations.

## Harness constraints (environmental — work around, never fight)

- **~600s stream watchdog** (above) — bounded scripts via Bash are the workaround.
- **Background Bash tasks are capped (~10 min)** — long serves/watches go in a detached
  process or the Monitor tool, not a background Bash that will be reaped.
- **Reaped processes (exit 144):** a server started in one step can be gone by the next —
  re-check `lsof -i :$PORT` before driving; restart from the recorded command if reaped.
- **Unpinned-model trap:** an Agent spawn without an explicit `model` does NOT inherit the
  session's /model choice — pin `model` on EVERY crew spawn and verify the transcript's
  model line on first report (SKILL dispatch contract).
- **Worktree unavailable to a copy-dispatch:** where a real worktree cannot be created for
  a lane, use the rsync-copy + `node_modules` symlink pattern (fleet-resources.md).
- **Compaction orphans:** a compaction can orphan running children — after one, re-derive
  the fleet from artifacts (worktree mtimes, ports, transcripts), never from memory.
- **A space in the path breaks `file://`:** a repo under a directory whose name contains a
  space yields an address the browser silently truncates — build it with `pathToFileURL`,
  never by concatenating, and never assume the failure is the page's.
- **Dual-rendered pages hide a second copy:** a responsive surface can keep BOTH the phone
  and desktop trees in the DOM with one hidden, so a bare `querySelector` matches the hidden
  one and every measurement reads zero — filter for visibility, and treat a zero measurement
  on a visibly-present element as an instrument fault until proven otherwise.

## The modes the FIRST CHOICE block does not list

`scroll` (scroll-position states) · `menu` (open a menu/overlay and capture it) · `bootstrap` — **the
repair `doctor` prescribes**: it installs a durable Playwright + a matching Chromium under
`~/.nexus-tools/` so the instrument resolves its own dependency from any cwd. Flags: `--attach`
(connect to an already-running agent-browser browser over CDP — `agent-browser.md` "## Interop with `capture.mjs`")
and `--max=<n>` (cap the element set). `doctor` reports what is missing and the exact command that fixes
it; a tooling error is a diagnosable state, not a blocker.

## Vendor quirks (verified; save the cycle)

- **oklab()/oklch() contrast** — RESOLVED (2026-07). The instrument resolves these tokens in-page,
  so accent-element contrast fails are real findings, not candidates. Only `color-mix()` with
  unresolved custom properties is still skipped.
- **Radix popovers under React 18:** popper can land offscreen after `npm install` peer
  conflicts — the `--force` install path is the known-good route; verify the popover
  on-screen by `hit` probe after upgrading.
- **FullCalendar v7 restructured packages** — imports/plugins from v6 guides don't resolve;
  read the installed package's exports before wiring.
- **maplibre markers:** the marker element is a WRAPPER — style/measure the inner element;
  hit-tests on the wrapper lie about the visual pin.
- **vite `emptyOutDir`:** an out-of-root `outDir` is NOT emptied by default — stale chunks
  serve beside new ones; set `emptyOutDir: true` explicitly.
- **npm shared-cache EACCES** under parallel installs — give lanes separate caches
  (`npm_config_cache=<lane-tmp>`) or serialize installs.
- **macOS has no `timeout` binary** — use Bash tool timeouts or a self-timeout in the
  script, never `timeout 60 node …` in a portable command.

## A watcher that cannot report a TRUE state is not evidence

`for f in $FILES` does NOT word-split in zsh: the loop runs ONCE over the whole string, every
`wc -c` fails, and every size reads 0. A monitor built that way emitted `STALL — no dossier
growth` while all five lanes it watched were writing normally (real sizes 518–759 B and
climbing). Use `while IFS= read -r f; do` — as `scripts/guard.sh:50` already does — or an
explicit array.

**The general rule, which outlives the shell detail:** before you rely on a watcher, make it
report one KNOWN-TRUE value through the same code path. A watcher that has only ever printed
the alarming state has not been shown to distinguish the two states at all. This is the
mutation-proof requirement — break it on purpose, watch the right case go red — applied to
ad-hoc monitors, where today it does not reach. It is the same defect as a probe reading the
hidden half of a dual-rendered page: the instrument measured something real that was not the
thing you were asking about.

### The capture harness measures the happy path, and its green is strongest where defects are least likely

A shoot script visits default routes in default states. Every defect that lives elsewhere is
invisible to it, and the automated probes stay green while the pixels are wrong. Measured three
times, by three different lanes, in two waves, on one app:

- an email address clipping its column — only reachable in the roster's SELECTED state, and the
  shoot only captures the default/empty state;
- prev/next buttons overflowing 23px at 390px on a long name — only on ROUTES the shoot never
  visits, one route per page;
- a title column crushed into mid-word line wraps at 1440px — a defect the overflow probe
  **cannot express at all**, since nothing overflows the viewport.

All three were found the same way: a lane drove the state itself, captured it, and READ the
image. None was found by the harness.

**The rule that follows: capture the states your FEATURE can reach, not the states the TOOL
offers.** Before shipping a surface, list its reachable states — selected, empty, error, long
content, every route class — and capture the ones your change can affect. A green overflow
number on an unvisited route is not evidence about that route.

# BUILD-MODE card — the engine-entry record (docs/BUILD-MODE.md)

The entry decision for an app build (engine or solo) is a DECISION — the card is its
RECORD. The decision must be made and RECORDED before the first app-source write (the
first non-`.md`, non-`docs/` Write/Edit): in a repo build the record is `docs/BUILD-MODE.md`
(the BLD gates stat it exactly as DG1 stats its four artifacts); where no repo file can
exist, the record is a ledger DECISION row. An app build with source writes and no
recorded decision is off-doctrine — not because a file is missing, but because the
decision was never visibly made.

Why a FILE where possible: the measured engine misses happened because "P1 closes by
dispatching" names no observable emission — a dispatch that never happens is
indistinguishable from a phase that never closed. The card gives the moment a checkable
trace (the Workstream Ledger precedent: a file at a known path survives compaction and
is hook-stat-able).

## The card (write it verbatim, fill every row)

    # BUILD-MODE — <app-slug>
    | Row | Value |
    |---|---|
    | Archetype | 1 / 2 / 3 |
    | Path | ENGINE / SOLO |
    | Authority | ENGINE: first `app-architect` dispatch (this session) · SOLO: the user's go, QUOTED verbatim ("<their message>") |
    | Lanes + models | TWO MACHINE-READABLE lines. `lanes: architect=1 · contracts=1 · executor=1 · tests=1 · tester=1 · reviewer=7 · assessor=20 · taste=1` — the roster the reconciliation reads (hook ROSTER1); a class you do not intend to run is DROPPED here with the user's quoted words, never silently omitted. # Action Model & Affordances

What looks interactive, what each control promises, how actions are ranked and reached. Covers view-vs-edit, context menus, primary/secondary, honest affordances. Pillars: 2, 3, 4.
