# Starter guide — the org app starter + component library lifecycle

!! Read at P1 whenever an app build starts FROM the org starter (the default base for archetype-3 apps) or hardens a delta back into it (P6 ship event). !!

Two org-owned repos carry the app-building capital. Both are **PRIVATE** (NexusGPT org). The component library is consumed as a **private npm package**, never vendored:

| Repo | Is | Consumed as |
|---|---|---|
| `github.com/NexusGPT/apps-starter` → **`@agent-nexus/apps-starter`** | the runnable, journey-verified app skeleton for record-system classes (CRM/ATS/ticketing/…): `starter.config.json` IS the app (objects · fields · views · relations · permissions · demo rows — `CONFIG_PATH=<file>` boots the same build as a different product); a zero-dep node server carries the data spine (command-log replay; warehouse driver) plus the platform wiring; `.nexus-starter` marker arms the deploy gate. Its CURRENT capability set is deliberately not listed here — read `docs/feature-manifest.md` in the extracted template at build time (one row per shipped feature, with the exact click path and the visible outcome that proves it; `Last verified` is stamped by the journey runner) | **`npm pack @agent-nexus/apps-starter`** → extract → config-instantiate per app. A PRIVATE package, same as the library: one registry credential reaches both, and no git access is needed to start an app |
| `github.com/NexusGPT/apps-ui` → **`@agent-nexus/apps-ui`** | the org component library for ANY product: shadcn/ui (new-york-v4) bridged to the Nexus token canvas (`tokens.css` = the single restyle surface, light+dark first-class) + the config-driven record-core (table · kanban · chart · record page). Its CURRENT component/prop surface lives in the docs shipped INSIDE the package — never in this file | **`npm install @agent-nexus/apps-ui`** — a built, versioned, PRIVATE package. NOT vendored: there is no `sync-ui`, no `src/ui`, no copy to own. Upgrades are a version bump |

## Import surface

The package's subpaths mirror its source tree, so an import reads as the path it lives at — and the `exports` map in the installed `package.json` is the truth: an import path is valid iff it matches an export entry (raw shadcn under `src/components/ui/` is NOT exported — reach it through the `primitives/` wrappers):

```ts
import { DataTable } from "@agent-nexus/apps-ui/record-core/DataTable";
import { Button }    from "@agent-nexus/apps-ui/primitives/Button";
import { Wizard }    from "@agent-nexus/apps-ui/blocks/wizard";
import { applySkin } from "@agent-nexus/apps-ui/skins/skin";  // brand-as-data skins
```

CSS is three imports, in this order, once, at the app entry:

```ts
import "@agent-nexus/apps-ui/tokens.css";   // the token canvas — the restyle surface
import "@agent-nexus/apps-ui/shadcn.css";   // tailwind + shadcn base layer
import "@agent-nexus/apps-ui/styles";       // the library's bundled component CSS
```

Restyling means overriding the tokens, never editing the library — you no longer own a copy to edit. A control the library lacks is proposed as a LIBRARY addition (ux-canon component-inventory rule), built once in `apps-ui`, released, consumed by version bump.

## Navigation contract (drift-proof — BINDING)

Both move fast and are SELF-DESCRIBING; any inventory written outside them (including this file) is stale on arrival. The contract: **capability questions are answered by reading the repo's / the installed package's own truth surfaces at build time, never from memory or skill docs.** Read order per need:

| Need | Read (at build time) |
|---|---|
| entry point + invariants | starter `AGENTS.md`, library `node_modules/@agent-nexus/apps-ui/AGENTS.md` (the agent-facing front door: what it is, binding rules, command table) |
| what EXISTS right now + how it's proven | starter `docs/feature-manifest.md` — one row per feature: exact click path · VISIBLE outcome · runner-stamped `Last verified`. The manifest row's `feature` string names its journey in `journeys/run.mjs` (the executable spec — read the journey when a row is ambiguous) |
| how to USE a capability (config knobs, env flags, recipes) | starter `docs/RECIPES.md` (task-shaped how-tos) + `starter.config.json` itself (the live example of every config axis) |
| file map / server shape | starter `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` + `docs/DATA-MODEL.md` |
| component/prop surface of the library | **`node_modules/@agent-nexus/apps-ui/docs/`** — `INDEX.md` + `catalog.json` (GENERATED — grep the JSON) + `CHOOSING.md` (task-first selection: need → candidates → the deciding question) + `MOTION.md` (the motion/interaction canon — BINDING for any component work) + `record-core.md` (ObjectConfig axes, component contracts, testid conventions) + `THEMING.md`. These ship inside the package, so they describe EXACTLY the version installed — no checkout-at-a-different-sha drift. The typed surface (`dist/**/*.d.ts`) is the second source of truth. **VENDORED fallback:** when npm auth is unavailable the library often arrives inside an adopted base as a source tree (`src/ui/` + a provenance marker such as `.ui-version`). Resolution order is installed → vendored; the vendored tree IS the library — it ships NO `docs/`, so its catalog twin in a starter-born app is `src/app/gallery.catalog.json` (a hand-restamped projection; trust its `uiVersion`), and absent that its folders (`record-core/` · `primitives/` · `blocks/`) ARE the catalog. Neither resolving = STOP and say so, never proceed as if no library exists |
| contribution rules when MODIFYING either repo (invariants, journey/manifest discipline, multi-agent lane protocol, port bands, suite lock) | starter `CONTRIBUTING-AGENTS.md` — binding for any agent lane touching the repos, including parallel-lane builds |
| which version is running / pinning | starter `VERSION` · `GET /api/healthz` (`{version, app}`) · git tags; the library version is whatever `package.json` pins (`node_modules/@agent-nexus/apps-ui/package.json` → `version`) |

Two hard rules: (1) NEVER assert "the starter/library has or lacks X" from recall — the manifest/catalog read is the check (absence = not proven, treat as absent); (2) when the repos and this guide disagree, the repos win — and this guide gets a correction in the same session (flag it).

## Cold start (any machine, no prior state)

Both the starter and the library are PRIVATE npm packages under `@agent-nexus`. The `NPM_TOKEN` already present in the build environment (read-only, `@agent-nexus`-scoped) reaches BOTH — starting an app needs no GitHub access at all.

```bash
npm pack @agent-nexus/apps-starter      # → agent-nexus-apps-starter-<v>.tgz
tar -xzf agent-nexus-apps-starter-*.tgz # npm tarballs extract to ./package
mv package <app-name> && cd <app-name>
npm install                             # pulls @agent-nexus/apps-ui from the private registry
npm run build && npm run serve          # zero-dep server: API + built UI
npm run journeys                        # the acceptance surface — green = the manifest's claims hold HERE
CONFIG_PATH=journeys/fixtures/<x>.config.json npm run serve   # same build, different product
```

If either package 404s, the token is missing or unscoped — that is an auth failure, never a reason to vendor the library's source, substitute a public component library, or hand-roll a skeleton.

## Lifecycle

1. **Pack → instantiate by CONFIG.** `npm pack` the starter → extract → **rename `package.json`'s `name` to the app and add `"private": true`** (the template ships publishable so it can BE a package; an instantiated app must never be publishable) → fill `starter.config` (app name, entities, palette seed) → boot. The `.nexus-starter` marker file stays — it is what arms the deploy gate's DENY tier (DG1: a starter-born repo shipping with red gate artifacts is 100%-sure unverified) and exempts the repo from BAS1. Never fork-and-drift: an app records the starter VERSION it was born from in `PROVENANCE.md`.
2. **Design lock rides the starter.** P0.5 direction boards scaffold from `boards/` (three static token-variant boards pre-wired to the app's nouns); the pick commits `docs/DESIGN.md`.
3. **Build on the record-core.** Tables/kanban/record pages come from `@agent-nexus/apps-ui` — installed OR vendored (resolution order above) — and a missing control is proposed as a LIBRARY addition (ux-canon component-inventory rule), built once, reused everywhere. **Dropping the library is a decision, not cleanup:** removing its imports or stylesheets ("this app renders none of those components") is an inventory verdict that belongs in the plan with its reason, and "a route back to the donor's look" is the misread that costs a rebuild — an org asset carried in by a donor lift is still an org asset.
4. **Journeys from feature 1.** Every feature lands with a manifest row + a journey; `npm run journeys` is the canonical Bash-visible runner (the hooks read its artifacts — no MCP-only verification).
5. **Ship-delta (P6).** At ship/accept, the hardened reusable delta (a new wiring module, a component fix, a template improvement) lands as a provenance-tagged commit/PR back to the starter/library — the NEXT build inherits it. A library delta ships as a version bump consumers pick up. The community KB receives the anonymised METHOD entry ONLY — the repos are private, so a KB pointer never carries a URL a reader cannot open. Repo DOCS written on a ship-delta serve the USING agent: functional content only (what exists, how to exercise it) — no build-process narrative, no wave/swarm provenance prose, no internal doctrine vocabulary; `docs/SPEC.md` in the TEMPLATE ships empty.
6. **Library upgrades.** Bump `@agent-nexus/apps-ui` and re-run journeys — the acceptance surface is what proves an upgrade safe. There is no vendor-sync and no re-vendor step; upstream shadcn tracking happens INSIDE `apps-ui`, not in consuming apps.

## Provenance + license posture (BINDING)

- `PROVENANCE.md` at each repo root records the per-file origin tags and the carry-scan results. The code is MIT-licensed but distribution is PRIVATE (org repos + a restricted-access npm package) — private distribution does not relax any origin rule below.
- EVERY file carries an origin tag in `PROVENANCE.md`: **`ours`** (authored from scratch — carried/de-branded freely) · **`rebuilt`** (clean-room reauthored from written specs/ideas — ideas are not copyrightable; the spec is cited) · **`derived`** (traces to third-party source). MIT/ISC-derived (shadcn/Radix patterns) is fine WITH notices kept in-repo. Copyleft-derived (AGPL/GPL) may exist ONLY as a temporary, tagged scaffold and MUST be replaced by `rebuilt` before ANY client delivery — identifier-stripping does not change a derivative's license.
- A carry from a prior fork workstream runs the CARRY SCAN first: `git log --diff-filter=A --author` to list files WE created; grep each against the donor's source for pasted fragments; only clean `ours` files cross, de-branded. The scan output is committed to `PROVENANCE.md`.

✗ "strip the donor's identifiers and repackage" → structural similarity is trivially detectable against public donor source, and a repo being private is not a defence once code ships to a client. → ✓ ideas + layouts carry as SPECS, our own files carry after the scan, the UI rebuilds on MIT primitives — ~90% of the value, zero legal surface.

# UX canon — information architecture + surface craft for hosted apps

Gate: read before the FIRST user-facing unit of EACH surface (SKILL P3; a compaction voids this read — R#13). The P0.5 design lock (`docs/DESIGN.md`) is the surface's visual AUTHORITY — read it WITH this file; this canon is the floor under whichever direction was picked.
`frontend-craft.md` owns rendering MECHANICS (does it work); this file owns DESIGN QUALITY (is it right).
Every rule below shipped as a user rejection once.

## The spine — glance → zoom → act

A management surface answers three questions in order, and its layout IS that order:

1. **GLANCE** — priority legible in one screen: a ranked/triaged board (compute the urgency score explicitly), status visible per row WITHOUT expanding (colored dot, count chip, progress bar).
2. **ZOOM** — one interaction to detail: accordion row or side drawer; NEVER a tab-jump for contextual detail (the jump survives as a secondary action INSIDE the drawer).
3. **ACT** — actions live where the reader already is: in-row/in-panel, persisted immediately, state reflected in place (checkbox → progress → counter).

✗ a flat fully-expanded list, everything the same weight, actions elsewhere → "layout is not readable, needs full overhaul" → ✓ scored triage board → one-line rows w/ verdict dots → accordion detail → in-place actions. Density is MEASURED: an open detail ≈ one screen (a 3-screen detail = restructure; two-column w/ a sticky context rail is the usual fix).

## Surface checklist (run per NEW surface, before first render)

| Item | Why (each shipped as a rejection once) |
|---|---|
| Explicit TYPE SCALE — every text element styled (title ~13.5/700 · body ~12.5/400 · meta 12 · micro-labels 10/800 caps); measure ≤~82ch | unstyled elements inherit the 16px browser default next to 13px neighbors = "font size inconsistency" |
| ONE nav pattern app-wide (sub-tabs: same component, same position on every tab) | two nav grammars = "inconsistent between tabs" |
| COMPONENT INVENTORY before any new control — the app's best existing component (filter bar, card, chips) is GENERALISED + tweaked, never re-invented per surface; org-wide the inventory ROOT is `@agent-nexus/apps-ui`, **RESOLVED against this repo's real shape**: INSTALLED (`node_modules/@agent-nexus/apps-ui/docs/catalog.json`) **or VENDORED** (a component tree carrying a provenance marker — e.g. `src/ui/.ui-version`; a library that arrived with a donor lift is still THE LIBRARY, never "the donor's look"). Read the resolved root, never recall. **A root that does not resolve is a STOP, not a pass** — a check that cannot execute reports green while every control is re-authored beside a superior one. The rule binds SUBTRACTION too: dropping a library import or stylesheet is an inventory decision, not cleanup. A control missing from the resolved root is proposed as a LIBRARY addition, not built as a one-off | two bespoke filter systems next to a superior existing one = "reuse components instead of reinventing the wheel"; a vendored library imported 8 times out of 20,688 LOC while its equivalents are hand-written |
| Stat chips that look clickable ARE clickable (they write into the same filter model) | count-styled-as-button that does nothing reads as broken |
| Long enumerations (>12 options) get typeahead; active filters surface ONE clear-all chip | a 400-option dropdown is unusable |
| AI results land ON the originating artifact (closed loop) and AI output is EDITABLE in place (stable anchors so structural edits never desync human feedback; armed 2-click delete) | send-side-only features + read-only AI output = "we need to see the result clearly on the plan" |
| Micro-interactions per the LIBRARY MOTION CANON — read `docs/MOTION.md` in the resolved `@agent-nexus/apps-ui` root (installed or vendored) before the first unit of each surface: the closed keyframe vocabulary (`nx-rise-in`/`nx-pop-in`/`nx-fade-in`/`nx-stream-in` + `--i` stagger), every interactive element acknowledges (hover step + `.nx-tap-scale`), expansion = grid-rows on the settle ease, working states = `.nx-shimmer` label + mono elapsed timer, streamed text = word-by-word (`StreamText`), `:focus-visible` ring (inset inside clipped containers), reduced-motion automatic. AI surfaces (traces, tool runs, approvals, streaming) use the `blocks/ai` components, never hand-rolled equivalents. A motion need outside the vocabulary is a LIBRARY addition, not a local `@keyframes` | static surfaces read as unfinished ("there were much more micro animation and interaction" is a measured rejection of a vocabulary-only surface); default focus rings read as broken; per-feature keyframes drift |
| Bounded internal scroll for long user content inside cards (max-height + overflow, thin scrollbar) | one long review stretching a card breaks the board |
| i18n: the language switch re-renders the ACTIVE view; every new string born in ALL dicts (count defs × languages); DATA stays in its own language | chrome switches, content doesn't = "page doesn't change language" |
| MOBILE (~≤760px) before ship: stacked cards, 2-line list rows, scrollable chip rails, full-width CTAs, no horizontal scroll (guard it), tap targets ≥40px; the @media block lives at stylesheet END (later same-specificity base rules win) + verify at 390px programmatically | desktop-only ships = "doesn't feel like an app on mobile" |
| Banner rhythm: balanced padding, centered search, nav underline offset from the edge | "margin in top banner is bad" |
| Irreversible or outward actions (send, delete, book, pay, bulk mutate) get a REVIEW surface before the fire: exactly what will happen (target, content, scope) shown + editable/redirectable + cancellable, and a verifiable result state after | a one-click real send with no preview or recipient control = "no confirmation, no message, unclear what is sent" |
| Icons from an ESTABLISHED library (e.g. Lucide, MIT), vendored as SVGs for self-containment; hand-drawn only for the brand's own marks | a hand-built icon set reads as amateur and swapping late touches every surface |
| Config/control surfaces speak the USER'S domain language — qualitative levels + concrete factors whose inputs the user can discover/supply; raw internal weights/thresholds/enums exposed as "settings" read as fake precision | decimal-weight sliders over abstract dimensions = "fake accuracy", unusable |

An org with its OWN design canon (brand/design-system files in its workspace) supersedes these defaults — read it FIRST when it exists (R#47); this checklist is the floor, not the ceiling.

## Uncertain hypothesis → ask, don't ship

When the IA hypothesis is not obviously forced (which grouping, which default view, fixed vs composable), state it as a one-line hypothesis to the user BEFORE building — a 30-second contrast question beats a rebuilt surface (Dim 8; design-conversation-canon "Surface-shape probe").

## Irreversible-action surfaces (canonical for CLAUDE.md G#9 builder's mirror)

The tool-execution tier discipline (READ / REVERSIBLE / SOFT-REVERSIBLE / IRREVERSIBLE) governs any UI Cue BUILDS: a user-triggered action that is irreversible or leaves the product (send/write/booking/payment/delete/bulk mutation) ships WITH a review surface — exactly what will happen: target, content, scope; edit/redirect/cancel — plus a verifiable result state after. A bare fire-button is the ✗ form, whatever the action.

nexus-cloud-imports.description: Import docs from cloud providers into Nexus KB. Setup/envelope → CLAUDE.md.

files.content:
---
name: nexus-cloud-imports
description: Imports documents from Google Drive, SharePoint, and Notion into the Nexus knowledge base via OAuth flows and the Public API v1.
---

# Nexus Cloud Imports

Import docs from cloud providers into Nexus KB. Setup/envelope → CLAUDE.md.

## OAuth + Import Flow (all providers)

All providers follow the same 4-step pattern:

1. **Exchange OAuth code** for tokens
2. **(Optional) Refresh** access token when expired
3. **List/search** files, pages, or sites
4. **Import** selected resources

```bash
# Step 1 — exchange code (all providers)
nexus api POST /documents/<provider>/auth --body '{"code":"..."}' --json

# Step 2 — refresh token (Google Drive, SharePoint only)
nexus api POST /documents/<provider>/refresh --body '{"connectionId":"..."}' --json

# Step 3 + 4 — see provider-specific endpoints below
```

## Provider-Specific Endpoints

| Provider | List endpoint | List param(s) | Import endpoint | Import body |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google Drive | `GET /documents/google-drive/files` | `accessToken=...&folderId=...` | `POST /documents/google-drive/import` | `{"fileIds":["..."]}` |
| SharePoint (sites) | `GET /documents/sharepoint/sites` | `connectionId=...` | – | – |
| SharePoint (files) | `GET /documents/sharepoint/files` | `connectionId=...&siteId=...` | `POST /documents/sharepoint/import` | `{"fileIds":["..."]}` |
| Notion (search) | `GET /documents/notion/search` | `connectionId=...&query=...` | `POST /documents/notion/import` | `{"pageIds":["..."]}` |

## Pre-import verification (per R#5)

Before bulk import, test-fetch one file w/ `nexus external-tool execute` against the Google Drive/SharePoint/Notion Pipedream tool — confirms credential can read target folder. Faster feedback than running full import + watching for `PROCESSING → ERROR`.

E.g., `nexus external-tool execute <googleDriveId> --action google_drive-find-file --input '{"q":"name contains '\''onboarding'\''"}' --credential <credId> --json`. Full → `nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`.

## Public web acquisition (NO OAuth, NO connectionId)

Distinct from private cloud (Drive/SharePoint/Notion). For public docs named by URL or well-known title (regulations, RFCs, manuals, specs, public API docs) — no provider auth required.

| Path | Command | When |
|---|---|---|
| Live (always current) | `nexus document add-website --url <URL>` | Source updates over time + agent should reflect changes (regulations, evolving docs) |
| Frozen (point-in-time PDF/HTML) | `WebFetch <URL>` → save → `nexus document upload <path>` | Source is a specific version / cited release / paywalled-but-user-supplied |

Decision: live `add-website` is default for public regulatory/spec docs; frozen `upload` when version-pinning matters or `add-website` can't access the source.

Full named-but-absent acquisition fork → `nexus-knowledge-base/SKILL.md` Q0.

## General-context integration

Workspace at `${GENERAL_CONTEXT_PATH}`.

### READ before import

| Need to know | Path | Read mode |
|---|---|---|
| Topic already imported? | `/knowledge/<topic>.md` | Whole-file |
| Provider OAuth quirks (Drive scopes, SharePoint tenant gotchas, Notion access) | `/tools/<provider>.md` "## Gotchas" | Grep |
| KB source-acquisition pattern decisions | `/knowledge/patterns/kb-source-decisions.md` | Whole-file |

### WRITE PULSE (during work, per CLAUDE.md R#34 — dispatch the background consolidation subagent on discovery)

| Trigger event | Workspace target | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| Provider OAuth quirk (scope drift / refresh TTL / tenant resolution) (org-specific config) | `/tools/<provider>.md` "## Gotchas" | Append H3 |
| Source-acquisition decision (live `add-website` vs frozen `WebFetch+upload`) (org-specific instance) | `/knowledge/patterns/kb-source-decisions.md` | Append H2 |
| Import format edge case (encoding / pagination / nested-object handling) (org-specific) | `/knowledge/learnings/cloud-import-<topic>.md` | New-file or Append H2 |
| **Cross-org** provider OAuth quirk (vendor-side) | `$TOOLS_PATH/<provider>/gotchas.md` | Append H3 |
| **Cross-org** import format edge case (vendor-side) | `$TOOLS_PATH/<provider>/gotchas.md` | Append H3 |

(Universal PULSE triggers from R#34 also apply: tool gotcha, CLI quirk, glossary term — see CLAUDE.md.)

### WRITE FINAL (end-of-build, import + indexing complete)

| Milestone | Content | Path | Mode | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Topic imported | Source URL + collection ID + verified date | `/knowledge/<topic>.md` | New-file or Append H2 | `templates/knowledge.md` |
| Provider quirk discovered (new OAuth issue / rate limit / format edge case) | Quirk | `/tools/<provider>.md` "## Gotchas" | Append H3 | (inline) |
| Source-acquisition lesson (live `add-website` vs frozen `WebFetch+upload`) | Decision | `/knowledge/patterns/kb-source-decisions.md` | Append H2 | (inline) |

### WRONG / RIGHT

✗ Notion HR-handbook import filed ONLY at `/systems/<active-system>/learnings.md` → no cross-pointer → ✓ `/knowledge/hr-handbook.md` (cross-system meta-doc w/ Notion source + collection ID); provider quirk → `/tools/notion.md "## Gotchas"`.

## Notes

- OAuth endpoints require valid auth code from provider's consent screen (R#G10 — present URL + poll for completion).
- Import endpoints create docs ASYNC → check status via `nexus document get <id> --json`.
- Imported docs auto-processed + embedded for KB search.
- Fallback for untyped ops → `nexus api <METHOD> <path>` per R#1.

nexus-deployments.description: Deploy agents to comm channels + manage lifecycle. Setup/envelope/dashboard URLs → CLAUDE.md.

files.content:
---
name: nexus-deployments
description: Deploys agents to channels (web widget, WhatsApp, Telegram, email, Slack, Teams, SMS, phone), manages deployment settings, embed widget configuration, deployment folders, and monitors deployment statistics via the Public API v1.
---

# Nexus Deployments

Deploy agents to comm channels + manage lifecycle. Setup/envelope/dashboard URLs → CLAUDE.md.

‼ A channel Deployment ≠ an app "deploy" (git-push→build→host): building/hosting an APP → `nexus-app-builder`; putting an AGENT on a channel → here.

**A deployment is a bidirectional channel, not just inbound agent delivery.** A workflow can SEND through any deployment channel via the native `sendMessage` node (`selectedDeployment`) — this is the path for outbound WhatsApp/Slack/SMS/etc. from a workflow, NOT a messaging plugin. Detail → `nexus-workflow-builder/node-types/output/send-message/GUIDE.md`.

## CLI (most-common cmds)

```bash
nexus deployment list [--type] [--active] [--json]
nexus deployment create --name X --type <T> --agent-id <id> [--body <json>] [--json]
nexus deployment embed-config <id> --json
nexus deployment embed-config-update <id> --body '<json>' --json
nexus html-template create|update|delete|get|list|render|fill   # embed HTML cards — channels/embed.md
nexus deployment stats <id> --json
nexus deployment folder list|create|update|delete|assign
nexus phone-number search|buy|list|get|release
nexus channel setup --type <T> [--auto] [--json]
nexus channel connection list|create
nexus channel whatsapp-sender list|create|get
```

Run `nexus <cmd> --help` per R#11 before first use.

## Deployment Types

| Type | Channel | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| EMBED | Web widget | None |
| WHATSAPP | WhatsApp Business | API key conn |
| TELEGRAM | Telegram bot | API key conn |
| GMAIL / OUTLOOK | Email | OAuth conn |
| SLACK / TEAMS | Workspace | OAuth conn |
| SMS / TWILIO_VOICE | Twilio | API key conn |
| API | Programmatic | None |

Channel creds (OAuth + API key) can use access cards to scope permissions → `nexus-tool-connection` skill.

## Channel Setup — Read FIRST per channel (R#2)

| Channel | Guide | Prerequisites |
|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp | `channels/whatsapp.md` | Connection + phone + sender |
| SMS | `channels/twilio-sms.md` | Connection + phone |
| Voice | `channels/twilio-voice.md` | Connection + phone |
| Telegram | `channels/telegram.md` | Bot token |
| Slack | `channels/slack.md` | Slack app + bot token |
| Gmail | `channels/gmail.md` | Google OAuth |
| Outlook | `channels/outlook.md` | Microsoft OAuth |
| Teams | `channels/teams.md` | Microsoft OAuth |
| Web Widget | `channels/embed.md` (+ HTML message templates) | None |
| API | `channels/api.md` | None |

**Orchestrator** before manual setup: `nexus channel setup --type <T> [--auto] --json` returns step-by-step checklist.

!! Card/template work on an embed deployment (design, create, or edit an HTML message template): Read `channels/embed.md` "## HTML Message Templates" FIRST — it holds the constraint matrix + the design-canon gate (`reference/html-cards-design.md`). !!

!! Embedding an agent chat INTO an app/site UI (iframe the widget, restyle it, or integrate natively): Read `channels/embed.md` "## Embedding the agent in your app" FIRST — the canonical ladder (widget iframe → interface restyle → API-mode session bridge, rung 3 recipe in `channels/api.md`). Building the host app itself → `nexus-app-builder`. !!

**Pre-deployment verification** (per R#5): verify the outbound credential w/ `nexus external-tool execute` before creating deployment. "Connected" badge ≠ "token can send." E.g., `nexus external-tool execute <slackId> --action slack-send-message --input '{"channel":"#bot-test","text":"preflight"}' --credential <credId> --json`. Full procedure → `nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`.

## General-context integration

Workspace at `${GENERAL_CONTEXT_PATH}`. Boundary-Read at conv start handled by CLAUDE.md Approach boundary check. This skill's specific READ-before / WRITE-after:

### READ before deployment

| Need to know | Path | Read mode |
|---|---|---|
| Target system architecture | `/systems/<system>/architecture.md` | Whole-file |
| Channel-specific prior gotchas (WhatsApp template approvals, voice quirks, embed cookie issues) | `/knowledge/patterns/deployments/<channel>.md` | Whole-file |
| Deployment owner / approver | `/people/<role>.md` | Grep "deployment" |

### WRITE PULSE (during work, per CLAUDE.md R#34 — dispatch the background consolidation subagent on discovery)

| Trigger event | Workspace target | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| Channel approval flow lesson (WhatsApp template / Twilio voice / Teams admin) (org-specific instance) | `/knowledge/patterns/deployments/<channel>.md` | New-file or Append H2 |
| Embed config / settings gotcha (cookie scope / CSP / postMessage origin) (org-specific) | `/tools/<channel>.md` "## Gotchas" | Append H3 |
| OAuth scope discovery (per-channel minimal scopes) (org-specific config) | `/tools/<channel>.md` "## Access scopes" | Append section |
| **Cross-org** channel approval flow (Meta brand validation, Twilio number provisioning) | `$TOOLS_PATH/<channel>/getting-started.md` | Append section + INDEX row update |
| **Cross-org** embed / channel gotcha (vendor-side, not org config) | `$TOOLS_PATH/<channel>/gotchas.md` | Append H3 |
| **Cross-org** FDE blind-spot in deployment (e.g., Meta validation lead-time) | `$USE_CASES_PATH/<domain>/<problem>/README.md "## Common pitfalls"` | Append H2 |

(Universal PULSE triggers from R#34 also apply: tool gotcha, CLI quirk, glossary term — see CLAUDE.md.)

### WRITE FINAL (end-of-build, deployment ACTIVE)

| Milestone | Content | Path | Mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deployment live | Deployment entry (channel, agent, deployment ID, dashboard URL) | `/systems/<system>/architecture.md` "## Architecture" — Deployments bullet | Replace-section (update manifest) |
| Channel quirk discovered (new) | Quirk + workaround | `/knowledge/patterns/deployments/<channel>.md` | New-file or Append H2 |
| Embed config / settings worth keeping | Config snippet | `/systems/<system>/runbook.md` "## Recovery — redeploy" | Append section |

### WRONG / RIGHT

✗ WhatsApp template-approval flow noted only as a chat TODO → lost between convs → ✓ after first approval, file `/knowledge/patterns/deployments/whatsapp.md` "## Template approval flow"; next deployment Reads + skips re-discovery.

## Endpoints / fallback

For untyped operations → `nexus api <METHOD> <path>` (R#1). Full endpoint list → `reference/endpoints.md`.

## User-facing questions (R#3, R#4)

Pre-populate from:

| Q category | Source |
|---|---|
| Channel type | Domain-fixed list above |
| Phone for SMS/Voice | `nexus phone-number list --json` |
| WhatsApp sender | `nexus channel whatsapp-sender list --json` |
| Existing deployment | `nexus deployment list --json` |
| Card design inputs (CTA model, fixed-vs-variable, brand refs) | `reference/html-cards-design.md` intake ladder |

Design → `nexus-getting-started/reference/clarification-guide.md`.

# API Deployment Setup

## Prerequisites

None. API deployments provide programmatic access to an agent — the channel for machines AND for a custom in-app chat UI (rung 3 of the embedding ladder → `embed.md` "## Embedding the agent in your app").

## Setup Flow

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "API Access" --type API --agent-id <agent-uuid> --json
```

## Native-chat session bridge (verified)

An app renders its OWN chat UI over an API deployment through the session endpoints. These are a PRODUCTION bridge, not a test-only surface (the emulator shares them).

Verify the chain with the CLI first:

```bash
nexus emulator session create <deploymentId> --json      # → sessionId
nexus emulator send <deploymentId> <sessionId> --text "hello" --json
```

The app backend calls the same surface (public API, `api-key` header):

1. `POST /emulator/<deploymentId>/sessions` → create the session.
2. `POST /emulator/<deploymentId>/sessions/<sessionId>/messages` → send the user's message.
3. Read the reply from the session's CONVERSATION — the send call is NOT synchronous: poll the conversation's messages with a bounded retry until the new ASSISTANT turn lands (anchor on the last message id, not a fixed sleep).
4. Message lists interleave tool-invocation rows with conversational turns — render conversational turns only.

Current-state (2026-07): API-mode conversations lack the EMBED widget's streaming/thinking/tool-status surface — design the native UI around full request→response turns (a typing indicator, not token streaming); supersede this note on retest after platform updates.

## CLI

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "API Access" --type API --agent-id X
```

# Web Widget (Embed) Deployment Setup ## Prerequisites None. Embed deployments are the simplest — no connections or phone numbers needed. ## Setup Flow ```bash # IMPORTANT: EMBED create validates a FULLY-specified settings object (a 400 lists what's missing) nexus deployment create --name "Website Chat" --type EMBED --agent-id --body embed-settings.json --json ``` **Note:** EMBED creation requires all five settings blocks fully specified — `embedSettings` (~30 required fields incl. `displayName`, `welcomeMessages`, `suggestedMessages`, `format`, bubble/ui colors + radii, `headerMessage`, `footerMessage`, `chatInputPlaceholder`, landing-screen fields), `securitySettings`, `leadsSettings` (+ `nameEnabled`/`emailEnabled`/`phoneEnabled`), `assistantSettings: {}`, `advancedSettings: {}`. The validation error enumerates every missing field — build the body from it. A complete working body → `### Full EMBED settings example` below. After creation, customize the widget appearance: ```bash nexus deployment embed-config-update --body '{"primaryColor":"#4F46E5","headerTitle":"Support Chat","position":"right","initialMessage":"Hi! How can I help you?","suggestedMessages":["Track my order","Return policy","Contact support"]}' ``` ## Widget Settings Beyond the embed-config appearance settings, embed deployments support additional configuration in the `settings` object. These are set via `nexus deployment create` or `nexus deployment update`, not via `embed-config-update`. ### Update semantics — always send the FULL object (measured) - Settings updates REPLACE the targeted settings object wholesale — a partial body (e.g. colors only) WIPES every field it does not carry (welcome messages, branding copy, labels). Always: fetch current (`deployment get` / `embed-config`) → modify in place → re-send the FULL object. Verify by re-fetch + diff (R#20 SILENT ACCEPTANCE), not by the 200. - `localized*` variants take PRECEDENCE for browsers matching that locale: override them ALONGSIDE the base fields — a base-only rebrand leaves the stale localized copy rendering for those users (a cloned deployment keeps silently showing its donor's copy in every localized language). - Undocumented/complex settings shape → clone a WORKING donor deployment's full settings, rebrand EVERY field including all `localized*` variants, send the full object — then text-diff the RENDERED widget against the intended copy, per language. ### Security Path: `settings.securitySettings` | Field | Type | Default | Description | |-------|------|---------|-------------| | `visibility` | `"public"` \| `"private"` | `"public"` | Widget visibility mode | | `allowOnlyOnSpecificDomains` | boolean | `false` | Restrict to allowed domains | | `allowedDomains` | string[] | `[]` | Domains where widget can load | | `rateLimiting` | boolean | `true` | Enable rate limiting | | `rateLimitingLimit` | number | `50` | Max messages per interval | | `rateLimitingInterval` | number (seconds) | `60` | Rate limit window | ### Leads Capture Path: `settings.leadsSettings` | Field | Type | Default | Description | |-------|------|---------|-------------| | `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Enable lead capture form | | `title` | string | — | Form title | | `nameEnabled` | boolean | `false` | Show name field | | `name` | string | — | Name field label | | `emailEnabled` | boolean | `false` | Show email field | | `email` | string | — | Email field label | | `phoneEnabled` | boolean | `false` | Show phone field | | `phone` | string | — | Phone field label | ### Display Customization Path: `settings.embedSettings` | Field | Type | Default | Description | |-------|------|---------|-------------| | `format` | `"bubble"` \| `"classic"` | `"bubble"` | Widget format | | `bubblePosition` | `"bottom-right"` \| `"bottom-left"` \| `"top-right"` \| `"top-left"` | `"bottom-right"` | Bubble position | | `bubbleSize` | `"small"` \| `"medium"` \| `"large"` | `"medium"` | Bubble size | | `bubbleBorderRadius` | `"none"` \| `"sm"` \| `"md"` \| `"lg"` \| `"full"` | `"lg"` | Bubble corner rounding | | `uiAppearance` | `"system"` \| `"light"` \| `"dark"` | `"light"` | Color scheme | | `uiPrimaryColor` | string (hex) | `"#000000"` | Primary color | | `uiAgentMessageColor` | string (hex) | `"#f3f4f6"` | Agent message background | | `uiUserMessageColor` | string (hex) | `"#3b82f6"` | User message background | | `showHeader` | boolean | `true` | Show widget header | | `showFooter` | boolean | `false` | Show widget footer | | `footerLinks` | array | `[]` | Footer links: `{ id, label, url }` | | `autoShowInitialMessagePopup` | boolean | `false` | Auto-show greeting popup | | `autoShowInitialMessagePopupDelay` | number | `3` | Seconds before popup | ### Landing Screen Bubble format only. Path: `settings.embedSettings` | Field | Type | Default | Description | |-------|------|---------|-------------| | `landingScreenEnabled` | boolean | `false` | Enable landing screen | | `landingScreenWelcomeMessage` | string | `"How can we help you?"` | Welcome text | | `landingScreenNewConversationLabel` | string | `"New Conversation"` | New chat button label | | `landingScreenShowPastConversations` | boolean | `true` | Show conversation history | | `landingScreenActionButtons` | array | `[]` | Action buttons: `{ id, label, description, icon, url }` | ### Localization Path: `settings.embedSettings` | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `defaultLanguage` | string | Default locale | | `localizedWelcomeMessages` | object | Welcome messages keyed by locale | | `localizedFooterMessage` | object | Footer text keyed by locale | | `localizedChatInputPlaceholder` | object | Input placeholder keyed by locale | ### Examples Restrict widget to specific domains: ```bash nexus deployment update \ --body '{"settings":{"securitySettings":{"visibility":"private","allowOnlyOnSpecificDomains":true,"allowedDomains":["example.com","app.example.com"]}}}' --json ``` Enable leads capture with name and email: ```bash nexus deployment update \ --body '{"settings":{"leadsSettings":{"enabled":true,"title":"Before we start...","nameEnabled":true,"name":"Your name","emailEnabled":true,"email":"Work email"}}}' --json ``` Configure landing screen with action buttons: ```bash nexus deployment update \ --body '{"settings":{"embedSettings":{"landingScreenEnabled":true,"landingScreenWelcomeMessage":"Welcome! How can we help?","landingScreenActionButtons":[{"id":"1","label":"Track Order","description":"Check your order status","icon":"package","url":""}]}}}' --json ``` Set rate limiting to 20 messages per 30 seconds: ```bash nexus deployment update \ --body '{"settings":{"securitySettings":{"rateLimiting":true,"rateLimitingLimit":20,"rateLimitingInterval":30}}}' --json ``` > **Tip:** For production deployments, use `visibility: "private"` with `allowedDomains` to prevent the widget from being loaded on unauthorized sites. ### Full EMBED settings example A complete create body that passes validation (adjust values; # Gmail Deployment Setup

## Prerequisites

1. **Google OAuth Connection** — Requires user to complete OAuth flow in browser

## Setup Flow

1. Create Gmail OAuth connection via tool-connection skill (triggers browser OAuth flow)
2. Create deployment:

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "Gmail Support" --type GMAIL --agent-id <agent-uuid> \
  --body '{"oauthConnectionId":"<gmail-oauth-connection-id>"}' --json
```

Gmail Pub/Sub watch is auto-configured during deployment creation for real-time email notifications.

The `oauthConnectionId` (which connected mailbox powers the deployment — the SENDER identity) is USER-ONLY knowledge: present the connected candidates from `credential list` and AUQ which; never infer it from an adjacent deployment's config (sender identity is irreversible-tier, G#9).

## Email Settings

All email-specific settings are passed inside the `settings` object on create or update.

### Settings Reference

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `draft` | boolean | `false` | Create draft replies instead of auto-sending |
| `signatureType` | `"DEFAULT"` \| `"CUSTOM"` \| `"NONE"` | `"DEFAULT"` | Signature mode |
| `signature` | string | — | Raw signature text (legacy). Max 5000 chars |
| `signatureInfos` | object | — | Structured signature: `{ image, name, title, phone, email, company, address }` |
| `whitelistEmails` | string[] | `[]` | Only these addresses can interact (takes priority over blacklist) |
| `whitelistDomains` | string[] | `[]` | Only these domains can interact |
| `blacklistEmails` | string[] | `[]` | Block specific addresses |
| `blacklistDomains` | string[] | `[]` | Block specific domains |
| `initialMessage` | string | `""` | First message sent when a conversation starts |

**Whitelist vs blacklist:** If a whitelist is set, ONLY those addresses/domains can interact — blacklist is secondary. Empty lists = no restrictions.

### Examples

Create deployment in draft mode (recommended for initial testing):

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "Gmail Support" --type GMAIL --agent-id <agent-uuid> \
  --body '{"oauthConnectionId":"<gmail-oauth-id>","settings":{"draft":true}}' --json
```

Enable draft mode on an existing deployment:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"draft":true}}' --json
```

Restrict to a single domain:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"whitelistDomains":["company.com"]}}' --json
```

> **Tip:** Start with `"draft": true` during testing — the agent creates draft replies you can review before anything is sent.

# Slack Deployment Setup

## Prerequisites

1. **Slack App** — Create a Slack app with bot token in the Slack API dashboard
2. **API Key Connection** — Create a SLACK_BOT API key connection with the bot token

## Setup Flow

1. Create Slack app at api.slack.com (user must do this manually)
2. Create API key connection via tool-connection skill (service: SLACK_BOT)
3. Create deployment:

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "Slack Bot" --type SLACK --agent-id <agent-uuid> \
  --body '{"apiKeyConnectionId":"<slack-connection-id>"}' --json
```

## Slack Settings

All Slack-specific settings are passed inside the `settings` object on create or update.

### Channel Filtering

Controls which channels and conversations the bot responds in.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `channelMode` | `"all"` \| `"dm_only"` \| `"specific_channels"` \| `"pattern"` | `"all"` | Which channels the bot responds in |
| `allowedChannels` | string[] | `[]` | Slack channel IDs (when mode is `specific_channels`) |
| `blockedChannels` | string[] | `[]` | Channel exclusion list — ignored channels even if otherwise allowed |
| `channelPattern` | string | — | Regex pattern for channel name matching (when mode is `pattern`) |

### Thread Behavior

Controls how the bot handles threads and conversation context.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `respondInThreadReplies` | boolean | `false` | Reply in thread when @mentioned in a channel |
| `dmRespondInThread` | boolean | `false` | Reply in thread for DM conversations |
| `threadInheritHistory` | boolean | `false` | Inherit the root channel message history when responding in threads |

### Notifications & UX

Visual feedback and notification settings during message processing.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `thinkingReaction` | boolean | `true` | Show :eyes: reaction while the agent is processing |
| `showWorkflowNotifications` | boolean | `false` | Notify in channel when a workflow is triggered |
| `showPluginNotifications` | boolean | `false` | Notify in channel when a skill/plugin is activated |
| `showWorkflowRunLink` | boolean | `false` | Include a link to the workflow run detail page |
| `unfurlLinks` | boolean | `false` | Show rich previews for URLs in responses |
| `unfurlMedia` | boolean | `false` | Unfurl media content (images, videos) in responses |

### Messages

Customize greeting and loading messages.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `firstMessage` | string \| null | `null` | Greeting sent before the first response in a new conversation |
| `loadingMessages` | string[] | `["Processing your request..."]` | Custom loading messages shown while processing (max 5) |

### Examples

Restrict to DMs only (recommended for initial testing):

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "Slack Bot" --type SLACK --agent-id <agent-uuid> \
  --body '{"apiKeyConnectionId":"<slack-connection-id>","settings":{"channelMode":"dm_only"}}' --json
```

Allow specific channels only:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"channelMode":"specific_channels","allowedChannels":["C01ABCDEF","C02GHIJKL"]}}' --json
```

Configure thread behavior and disable the thinking reaction:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"respondInThreadReplies":true,"dmRespondInThread":true,"thinkingReaction":false}}' --json
```

Customize loading messages:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"loadingMessages":["On it...","Thinking...","One moment please..."]}}' --json
```

> **Tip:** Start with `"channelMode": "dm_only"` during testing — the bot only responds in direct messages, so you can verify behavior before exposing it to channels.

> **Note:** User-visible rendering is confirmed by the USER, not by `osErr:0` (CLAUDE.md R#27). Slack uses mrkdwn, not standard Markdown — `**bold**` and triple-backtick code fences can render literally; after a real send, ask the user how it actually displayed.

## Voice Settings

All voice-specific settings are passed inside the `settings` object on create or update. Twilio Voice has the most extensive settings of any deployment type — covering provider selection, turn detection, call flow, transfers, and more.

### Core Settings

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `provider` | `"openai"` \| `"gemini"` | `"openai"` | Voice AI provider |
| `model` | string | `"gpt-realtime-1.5"` | AI model name |
| `language` | string | — | Primary language |
| `ttsProvider` | `"openai"` \| `"elevenlabs"` \| `"cartesia"` \| `"playht"` \| `"rime"` | — | Text-to-speech provider |
| `voiceId` | string | — | Voice identifier (provider-specific, see Available Voices below) |
| `hostRegion` | SupportedTwilioRegion | — | Twilio region |
| `initialMessage` | string | — | Greeting message spoken at call start |
| `initialMessageUrl` | string | — | URL to greeting audio file (alternative to text greeting) |

### Turn Detection

Controls how the system detects when the caller has finished speaking.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `turn_detection.type` | `"server_vad"` \| `"semantic_vad"` | `"server_vad"` | Detection mode |
| `turn_detection.threshold` | number (0.0-1.0) | `0.8` | Voice detection sensitivity |
| `turn_detection.prefix_padding_ms` | number (0-2000) | `300` | Milliseconds of audio captured before speech starts |
| `turn_detection.silence_duration_ms` | number (100-5000) | `500` | Milliseconds of silence before a turn ends |
| `turn_detection.eagerness` | `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"` | `"medium"` | How eager the agent is to take its turn |
| `turn_detection.interrupt_response` | boolean | `true` | Allow caller to interrupt the agent mid-response |
| `turn_detection.noise_reduction` | `"near_field"` \| `"far_field"` \| `null` | `"far_field"` | Noise reduction mode (`near_field` for headset, `far_field` for speakerphone) |
| `vad_threshold` | number | — | Voice activity detection threshold (top-level override) |

### Call Flow

Controls conversation pacing and filler responses.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `flow.user_start_first` | boolean | — | Whether the user speaks first (skip agent greeting) |
| `flow.interruption.allowed` | boolean | — | Allow caller interruptions |
| `flow.interruption.keep_interruption_message` | boolean | — | Keep the interrupted message in context |
| `flow.response_delay` | number | — | Delay in milliseconds before responding |
| `flow.auto_fill_responses.messages` | string[] | — | Filler messages during processing (e.g., `["One moment..."]`) |
| `flow.auto_fill_responses.response_gap_threshold` | number | — | Gap in milliseconds before filler kicks in |

### Transfers & SMS

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `transfers` | array | Transfer destinations. Each: `{ name: string, description: string, to: string, summaryDescription: string }` |
| `enableSms` | boolean | Enable in-call SMS sending capability |
| `sendSms` | array | SMS configurations for automated messages during calls |

### Filtering & Languages

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `whitelist` | string[] | Allowed caller phone numbers (E.164 format). Empty = allow all |
| `switch_languages` | string[] | Languages the agent can switch to mid-call |
| `keywords` | string[] | Keywords for call routing |
| `session_timeout` | object | Call timeout configuration |
| `geminiThinkingLevel` | `"minimal"` \| `"low"` \| `"medium"` \| `"high"` | Gemini reasoning depth (Gemini provider only) |

### Available Voices

**OpenAI Realtime:** alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse

**Gemini Live:** Puck, Charon, Kore, Fenrir, Aoede, Leda, Orus, Zephyr

### Examples

Create a voice deployment with a specific provider and voice:

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "Phone Support" --type TWILIO_VOICE --agent-id <agent-uuid> \
  --body '{"phoneNumberId":"<phone-number-id>","apiKeyConnectionId":"<connection-id>","settings":{"provider":"openai","voiceId":"coral","initialMessage":"Hi, thanks for calling! How can I help?"}}' --json
```

Configure turn detection for a noisy environment:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"turn_detection":{"type":"server_vad","threshold":0.9,"silence_duration_ms":800,"noise_reduction":"far_field"}}}' --json
```

Add a call transfer destination:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"transfers":[{"name":"Sales","description":"Transfer to sales team for pricing questions","to":"+15551234567","summaryDescription":"Caller asked about pricing"}]}}' --json
```

Enable SMS sending during calls:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"enableSms":true}}' --json
```

> **Tip:** Start with default turn detection settings and adjust after real calls. Lowering `silence_duration_ms` makes the agent respond faster but may cut off slow speakers. Raising `threshold` reduces false triggers from background noise.

To auto-provision what's possible (e.g., create the connection automatically):

```bash
nexus channel setup --type WHATSAPP --auto --json
```

## Full Setup Flow

### Step 1: Create Messaging Connection

```bash
nexus channel connection create --region us1 --json
```

Returns: `{ id, name, accountSid, region, status }`

Only one connection is allowed per organization. If one already exists, this step is skipped.

### Step 2: Connect WhatsApp Business Account (browser required)

This step **requires a browser** — it cannot be done via API or CLI.

**CLI:** `nexus channel connect-waba` (opens the dashboard in your browser)

Or manually open: `{NEXUS_DASHBOARD_URL}/app/connect-waba`

1. Click **"Connect with Meta"** (single button on the page)
2. Sign into your Meta Business account in the popup
3. Select or create a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA)
4. Authorize sharing with Nexus
5. The WABA ID is automatically stored in your connection

**Verify:** `nexus channel setup --type WHATSAPP` — the "WhatsApp Business Account" step should show `completed`.

### Step 3: Buy Phone Number

First, search for available numbers:

```bash
nexus phone-number search --country US --sms --json
```

Then purchase one:

```bash
nexus phone-number buy --phone-number +12025551234 --country US --price 1.15 --connection-id <connection-id-from-step-1> --json
```

Returns: `{ id, number, friendlyName, countryCode }`

### Step 4: Create WhatsApp Sender

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-sender create --connection-id <connection-id> --phone-number-id <phone-number-id> --sender-name "My Business" --json
```

Returns: `{ id, senderId, name, wabaId, phoneNumberId }`

This registers the phone number with Meta's WhatsApp Business Account. The sender status starts as `OFFLINE` and transitions to `ONLINE` once Meta approves (usually within minutes).

Check sender status:

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-sender list --json
```

### Step 5: Verify Readiness

```bash
nexus channel setup --type WHATSAPP --json
```

All steps should show `completed` (except `deployment` which is always `action_needed`).

### Step 6: Create Deployment

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "WhatsApp Support" --type WHATSAPP --agent-id <agent-uuid> --body '{"phoneNumberId":"<phone-number-id>","apiKeyConnectionId":"<connection-id>"}' --json
```

Or use the convenience field `whatsappSenderId` which auto-resolves phoneNumberId and apiKeyConnectionId:

```bash
nexus deployment create --name "WhatsApp Support" --type WHATSAPP --agent-id <agent-uuid> --body '{"whatsappSenderId":"<sender-id>"}' --json
```

## WhatsApp Settings

Additional settings passed inside the `settings` object on create or update.

### Voice Responses

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `enableVoiceResponses` | boolean | `false` | Enable voice message responses |
| `voiceProvider` | `"openai"` \| `"elevenlabs"` | — | TTS provider for voice messages |
| `voiceModel` | string | — | OpenAI model name or ElevenLabs voice ID |
| `voiceInstructions` | string | — | Custom instructions for voice generation |

### Multi-Message Handling

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `multiMessageHandling.concurrencyStrategy` | `"parallel"` \| `"ignore"` \| `"cancel_retrigger"` \| `"sequential"` | `"sequential"` | How to handle messages while agent is processing |
| `multiMessageHandling.debounceMs` | number (1000-60000) | `3000` | Debounce window in milliseconds |

### Upfront Actions

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `upfrontActions` | array | `[]` | Actions executed when deployment starts: `{ name: string, input: any }` |

### Examples

Enable voice responses with OpenAI:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"enableVoiceResponses":true,"voiceProvider":"openai","voiceModel":"alloy"}}' --json
```

Configure debounce for rapid messages:

```bash
nexus deployment update <deployment-id> \
  --body '{"settings":{"multiMessageHandling":{"concurrencyStrategy":"sequential","debounceMs":5000}}}' --json
```

> **Tip:** Use `"sequential"` concurrency strategy (the default) to avoid race conditions when users send multiple messages in quick succession. The agent processes each message in order, preventing duplicate or out-of-sequence replies.

## Common Errors

| Error                         | Cause                             | Fix                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `MISSING_PHONE_NUMBER`        | No phoneNumberId provided         | Buy a phone number first (Step 2)                    |
| `WHATSAPP_SENDER_NOT_FOUND`   | No WhatsApp sender for this phone | Create a WhatsApp sender first (Step 3)              |
| `MISSING_CONNECTION`          | No apiKeyConnectionId provided    | Create a messaging connection first (Step 1)         |
| `CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`        | Invalid connection ID             | Check connection exists: `nexus channel connection list --json` |
| `LIMIT_REACHED`               | Connection already exists         | Use existing connection (only 1 per org)             |
| Sender status stuck `OFFLINE` | Meta approval pending             | Wait a few minutes, then check status again          |

## Sender Status Lifecycle

```
OFFLINE (initial) → ONLINE (Meta approved, ready to send)
                  → OFFLINE with offline_reasons (Meta rejected, check reasons)
```

## WhatsApp Templates

WhatsApp templates are pre-approved message formats required by Meta for initiating outbound conversations. Templates must be created and approved by Meta before they can be used. Any conversation initiated by the business (not the user) requires a template.

> Template `{{1}}`/`{{2}}` are positional OUTBOUND-content params (below) — distinct from channel-injected RUNTIME sender vars (`{{customerPhone}}`, `{{wa_id}}`) the agent/workflow reads at message time → `../../nexus-agent-management/reference/conversation-context.md "## Channel-injected runtime variables"`.

### Template Lifecycle

```
Create template ──► Submit for Meta approval ──► Pending ──► Approved (ready to use)
                                                          ──► Rejected (fix & resubmit)
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                        Attach to deployment
                                        (configure variables)
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                        Agent/workflow uses template
                                        for outbound messages
```

### Template Types (Twilio Content API format)

| Type           | Key                     | Description                                         |
| -------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Text           | `twilio/text`           | Simple text body with optional variables            |
| Media          | `twilio/media`          | Text + media attachments (images, PDFs)             |
| Quick Reply    | `twilio/quick-reply`    | Text + up to 3 quick reply buttons                  |
| Call to Action | `twilio/call-to-action` | Text + up to 2 URL/phone buttons                    |
| Card           | `twilio/card`           | Rich card with title, subtitle, media, actions      |
| Carousel       | `twilio/carousel`       | Swipeable multi-card message (2-10 cards) with body |

### Step 1: Create Template

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-template create \
  --connection-id <id> \
  --friendly-name order_confirmation \
  --language en \
  --body "Hi {{1}}, your order #{{2}} has been confirmed." \
  --variables '{"1":"Customer","2":"12345"}'
```

Returns: `{ id, friendly_name, language, types, created_at }`

For complex templates (media, quick-reply, card), use `--body-file`:

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-template create \
  --connection-id <id> \
  --friendly-name promo \
  --language en \
  --body-file template.json
```

**Create + submit in one step:**

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-template create \
  --connection-id <id> \
  --friendly-name order_confirmation \
  --language en \
  --body "Order {{1}} confirmed" \
  --submit --category UTILITY
```

### Step 2: Submit for Meta Approval

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-template submit-approval \
  --connection-id <id> \
  --template-id <template-sid> \
  --name order_confirmation \
  --category UTILITY \
  --wait  # polls until approved/rejected (up to 2 min)
```

Approval categories:

- **UTILITY** — Transactional messages (receipts, confirmations). Faster approval.
- **MARKETING** — Promotional messages. Stricter review.
- **AUTHENTICATION** — OTP/2FA messages. Special approval process.

### Step 3: Check Approval Status

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-template approvals
```

Statuses: `unsubmitted`, `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`

### Step 3.5: Test-Send Template (Recommended)

Before attaching to a deployment, verify the template sends correctly through the real Twilio/Meta pipeline:

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-template test-send \
  --connection-id <uuid> \
  --template-id <template-sid> \
  --to +1234567890 \
  --variables '{"1": "Jane Doe", "2": "ORD-12345"}' \
  --wait  # polls delivery status (up to 2 min)
```

Returns: `{ messageSid, status, to, from, sentAt }`

Terminal statuses: `delivered`, `read` (success) or `failed`, `undelivered` (failure with error details).

This catches issues that only surface during actual sending: media URL resolution failures, variable formatting errors, Meta-side rendering issues, and account-level restrictions.

### Step 4: Attach Template to Deployment

Once approved and verified, attach the template to a WhatsApp deployment so the agent can use it:

```bash
nexus deployment template attach <deploymentId> \
  --template-id <template-sid> \
  --name order_confirmation \
  --description "Sends order confirmation" \
  --variables '{"1":{"description":"Customer name","isBodyVariable":true},"2":{"description":"Order number","isBodyVariable":true}}'
```

### Manage Deployment Templates

```bash
# List templates on a deployment
nexus deployment template list <deploymentId>

# Update template config
nexus deployment template update <deploymentId> <templateId> --name "Updated Name"

# Detach template from deployment
nexus deployment template detach <deploymentId> <templateId> --yes

# Enable/disable dynamic template creation by agent
nexus deployment template settings <deploymentId> --allow-dynamic-templates true
```

### Other Template Operations

```bash
# List all templates
nexus channel whatsapp-template list

# Get template details
nexus channel whatsapp-template get <templateId>

# Delete template
nexus channel whatsapp-template delete <templateId> --yes
```

### Template Settings on Deployment

- **`allowAgentToCreateAndSendTemplates`** — When enabled (`true`), the AI agent can dynamically create card-type templates during conversations. Default: `false`.

### Multi-Language Templates

For deployments serving multiple languages, create separate Twilio templates per language (same content, different language code), then attach with a template group that maps languages to template IDs.

**Naming convention:** Templates follow the pattern `base_name_<lang>` (e.g., `order_confirm_en`, `order_confirm_es`, `order_confirm_fr`). The system uses the base name to group related templates.

**Step 1: Create templates for each language**

```bash
# English version
nexus channel whatsapp-template create \
  --connection-id <id> --friendly-name order_confirm_en --language en \
  --body "Hi {{1}}, your order #{{2}} is confirmed." --submit --category UTILITY

# Spanish version
nexus channel whatsapp-template create \
  --connection-id <id> --friendly-name order_confirm_es --language es \
  --body "Hola {{1}}, tu pedido #{{2}} está confirmado." --submit --category UTILITY
```

**Step 2: Attach with template group**

```bash
nexus deployment template attach <deploymentId> \
  --template-id <english-template-sid> \
  --name order_confirm \
  --description "Order confirmation in multiple languages" \
  --enable-multi-language \
  --variables '{"1":{"description":"Customer name","isBodyVariable":true},"2":{"description":"Order number","isBodyVariable":true}}'
```

Then update with the template group mapping:

```bash
nexus deployment template update <deploymentId> <templateId> \
  --body '{"enableMultiLanguage":true,"templateGroup":{"baseName":"order_confirm","availableLanguages":[{"language":"en","templateId":"<english-template-sid>"},{"language":"es","templateId":"<spanish-template-sid>"}],"defaultLanguage":"en"}}'
```

The agent selects the correct language template at runtime based on the user's language preference.

### Carousel Templates

Carousels are swipeable multi-card messages — ideal for product catalogs, listings, or options. Each carousel has a shared body (text above the cards) and 2-10 individual cards with title, body, media image, and action buttons.

**Creating a carousel template:**

For complex templates (carousel, card, media), save the template body to a JSON file and use `--body-file`:

```bash
nexus channel whatsapp-template create \
  --connection-id <id> \
  --friendly-name product_catalog_3_en \
  --language en \
  --body-file carousel-template.json \
  --submit --category MARKETING
```

Example `carousel-template.json` content:

```json
{
  "types": {
    "twilio/carousel": {
      "body": "Here are our top picks for you:",
      "cards": [
        {
          "body": "{{1}} - ${{2}}",
          "media": "https://cdn.example.com/products/{{3}}",
          "actions": [{ "type": "URL", "title": "View", "url": "https://example.com/p/{{4}}" }]
        },
        {
          "body": "{{5}} - ${{6}}",
          "media": "https://cdn.example.com/products/{{7}}",
          "actions": [{ "type": "URL", "title": "View", "url": "https://example.com/p/{{8}}" }]
        },
        {
          "body": "{{9}} - ${{10}}",
          "media": "https://cdn.example.com/products/{{11}}",
          "actions": [{ "type": "URL", "title": "View", "url": "https://example.com/p/{{12}}" }]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "variables": {"1":"Sneakers","2":"29.99","3":"sneakers.png","4":"sneakers","5":"Backpack","6":"39.99","7":"backpack.png","8":"backpack","9":"Watch","10":"49.99","11":"watch.png","12":"watch"}
}
```

**Carousel card constraints:**

- `body`: Required, max 160 chars. Supports variables like `{{1}}`.
- `media`: Required image URL. **Must start with `https://` and a valid domain.** Variables may only appear in the URL path/query, NOT as the entire URL. The resolved URL must end with a file extension (`.png`, `.jpg`, etc.) and point to a publicly hosted image.
  - Valid: `https://cdn.example.com/products/{{3}}` (variable resolves to `sneakers.png`)
  - Valid: `https://cdn.example.com/{{3}}/thumbnail.jpg` (variable in path segment)
  - Invalid: `{{3}}` (no static base URL — Twilio/WhatsApp will reject this)
  - Invalid: `http://example.com/{{3}}` (must be `https://`)
- `title`: Optional, max 160 chars.
- Actions: 1-2 buttons per card. **Unlike standalone templates, carousel card actions require an explicit `type` field:**
  - `{ "type": "QUICK_REPLY", "title": "Select", "id": "select_1" }` — sends a predefined response
  - `{ "type": "URL", "title": "View", "url": "https://example.com/p/{{4}}" }` — opens a URL (variables allowed in path)
  - `{ "type": "PHONE_NUMBER", "title": "Call", "phone": "+1234567890" }` — initiates a call
- The carousel itself requires 2-10 cards.

**Media URL variable rule applies to all template types** (media, card, carousel) — always provide a static `https://` base URL and append variables to the path. Twilio rejects templates where a variable IS the entire media URL.

#### Variable-to-Text Ratio (Meta Rejection Gotcha)

Meta silently rejects templates where variables dominate the text content. The template creation API returns `status: received`, but the approval is immediately rejected with: _"This template has too many variables for its length."_

**Rule of thumb:** Every text field (body, title, subtitle) must have enough static/descriptive text around the variables. The static (non-variable) portion should be at least 3 characters per variable.

**Examples:**

| Body text               | Result   | Why                                 |
| ----------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `{{1}}`                 | REJECTED | No static text at all               |
| `{{1}} - ${{2}}`        | REJECTED | Only 4 static chars for 2 variables |
| `Price: ${{1}}`         | OK       | 9 static chars for 1 variable       |
| `{{1}} — Free shipping` | OK       | 17 static chars for 1 variable      |

**This applies to:** All text fields in all template types — `twilio/text` body, `twilio/carousel` card bodies and titles, `twilio/card` title and subtitle, etc.

**The backend validates this automatically** and will reject templates that are too variable-heavy before they reach Meta. The CLI also prints a warning before submission.

**Attaching a carousel to a deployment:**

```bash
nexus deployment template attach <deploymentId> \
  --template-id <carousel-template-sid> \
  --name product_catalog \
  --description "Shows product recommendations as a carousel" \
  --type carousel \
  --variables '{"1":{"description":"Product 1 name","cardIndex":0},"2":{"description":"Product 1 price","cardIndex":0},"3":{"description":"Product 1 slug","cardIndex":0},"4":{"description":"Product 2 name","cardIndex":1},"5":{"description":"Product 2 price","cardIndex":1},"6":{"description":"Product 2 slug","cardIndex":1},"7":{"description":"Product 3 name","cardIndex":2},"8":{"description":"Product 3 price","cardIndex":2},"9":{"description":"Product 3 slug","cardIndex":2}}'
```

Note: For carousel variables, use `cardIndex` to indicate which card each variable belongs to. Variables in the carousel body (above the cards) should use `isBodyVariable: true` instead.

#### Dynamic Carousel Size

When the number of items to display varies at runtime (e.g., search results may return 2, 3, or 5 products), you need **dynamic carousel size**. This requires creating multiple carousel templates — one per size — and grouping them.

**Naming convention for carousel size variants:** `base_name_<size>_<lang>` (e.g., `products_2_en`, `products_3_en`, `products_5_en`).

**Step 1: Create size variants**

```bash
# 2-item carousel
nexus channel whatsapp-template create --connection-id <id> \
  --friendly-name products_2_en --language en --body-file carousel-2.json --submit --category MARKETING

# 3-item carousel
nexus channel whatsapp-template create --connection-id <id> \
  --friendly-name products_3_en --language en --body-file carousel-3.json --submit --category MARKETING

# 5-item carousel
nexus channel whatsapp-template create --connection-id <id> \
  --friendly-name products_5_en --language en --body-file carousel-5.json --submit --category MARKETING
```

**Step 2: Attach with dynamic size enabled**

```bash
nexus deployment template attach <deploymentId> \
  --template-id <2-item-template-sid> \
  --name products \
  --description "Dynamic product carousel" \
  --type carousel \
  --enable-dynamic-size \
  --carousel-template-group '{"baseName":"products","availableTemplates":[{"language":"en","carouselSize":2,"templateId":"<2-item-sid>"},{"language":"en","carouselSize":3,"templateId":"<3-item-sid>"},{"language":"en","carouselSize":5,"templateId":"<5-item-sid>"}],"defaultLanguage":"en","minCarouselSize":2,"maxCarouselSize":5}'
```

Or equivalently via `nexus api`:

```bash
nexus api POST /deployments/<deploymentId>/whatsapp-templates --body '{
  "templateId": "<2-item-template-sid>",
  "name": "products",
  "description": "Dynamic product carousel",
  "type": "carousel",
  "enableDynamicSize": true,
  "carouselTemplateGroup": {
    "baseName": "products",
    "availableTemplates": [
      { "language": "en", "carouselSize": 2, "templateId": "<2-item-sid>" },
      { "language": "en", "carouselSize": 3, "templateId": "<3-item-sid>" },
      { "language": "en", "carouselSize": 5, "templateId": "<5-item-sid>" }
    ],
    "defaultLanguage": "en",
    "minCarouselSize": 2,
    "maxCarouselSize": 5
  },
  "variables": { }
}'
```

At runtime, the agent picks the template whose `carouselSize` matches the number of items. If no exact match exists, the closest larger size is used.

#### Single-Item Card Fallback

WhatsApp requires carousels to have at least 2 cards. When there's only 1 item to show, the system falls back to a **card template** instead. Configure this fallback when using dynamic size:

```bash
nexus deployment template attach <deploymentId> \
  --template-id <2-item-template-sid> \
  --name products \
  --description "Dynamic product carousel with single-item fallback" \
  --type carousel \
  --enable-dynamic-size \
  --single-item-card-template-id <card-fallback-sid> \
  --carousel-template-group '{"baseName":"products","availableTemplates":[...],"minCarouselSize":2,"maxCarouselSize":5}'
```

For multi-language deployments, use `--single-item-card-template-group` to map fallback card templates per language:

```bash
--single-item-card-template-group '{"availableTemplates":[{"language":"en","templateId":"<en-card-sid>"},{"language":"es","templateId":"<es-card-sid>"}]}'
```

#### Multi-Language Carousel

For carousels serving multiple languages, the template group contains entries with **both** language and carousel size dimensions. The naming convention is `base_name_<size>_<lang>`.

```bash
# Create all language + size combinations
nexus channel whatsapp-template create --connection-id <id> --friendly-name products_3_en --language en --body-file carousel-3-en.json --submit --category MARKETING
nexus channel whatsapp-template create --connection-id <id> --friendly-name products_3_es --language es --body-file carousel-3-es.json --submit --category MARKETING
nexus channel whatsapp-template create --connection-id <id> --friendly-name products_5_en --language en --body-file carousel-5-en.json --submit --category MARKETING
nexus channel whatsapp-template create --connection-id <id> --friendly-name products_5_es --language es --body-file carousel-5-es.json --submit --category MARKETING
```

Attach with the full matrix:

```bash
nexus api POST /deployments/<deploymentId>/whatsapp-templates --body '{
  "templateId": "<products_3_en-sid>",
  "name": "products",
  "description": "Multi-language dynamic product carousel",
  "type": "carousel",
  "enableMultiLanguage": true,
  "enableDynamicSize": true,
  "carouselTemplateGroup": {
    "baseName": "products",
    "availableTemplates": [
      { "language": "en", "carouselSize": 3, "templateId": "<3-en-sid>" },
      { "language": "en", "carouselSize": 5, "templateId": "<5-en-sid>" },
      { "language": "es", "carouselSize": 3, "templateId": "<3-es-sid>" },
      { "language": "es", "carouselSize": 5, "templateId": "<5-es-sid>" }
    ],
    "defaultLanguage": "en",
    "minCarouselSize": 3,
    "maxCarouselSize": 5
  },
  "singleItemCardTemplateGroup": {
    "availableTemplates": [
      { "language": "en", "templateId": "<card-en-sid>" },
      { "language": "es", "templateId": "<card-es-sid>" }
    ]
  },
  "variables": { }
}'
```

### Common Template Errors

| Error                                                   | Cause                                     | Fix                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_ERROR`                               | Invalid template body or Twilio rejection | Check types structure matches Twilio Content API format             |
| `NOT_FOUND`                                             | Template ID doesn't exist                 | Verify template was created: `nexus channel whatsapp-template list` |
| `WHATSAPP_TEMPLATE_APPROVAL_ERROR`                      | Approval submission failed                | Check connection ID is valid and template exists                    |
| `Templates can only be managed on WhatsApp deployments` | Wrong deployment type                     | Use a WHATSAPP deployment, not EMBED/SLACK/etc.                     |
| `Template already attached`                             | Duplicate templateId on deployment        | Template is already attached, use `update` to modify config         |
| Approval status `rejected`                              | Meta rejected the template                | Check `rejection_reason` and fix template content, then resubmit    |
| `too many variables for its length`                     | Card body/title is mostly variables       | Add more descriptive static text around `{{N}}` placeholders        |

# Deployment Endpoints

## Deployments CRUD

### List Deployments

`GET /deployments?page=1&limit=20&search=&type=EMBED&isActive=true`

Response: `{ success: true, data: DeploymentSummary[], meta: { total, page, hasMore } }`

### Create Deployment

`POST /deployments`
Body: `{ name: string, type: DeploymentType, agentId?: uuid, description?: string, settings?: object, phoneNumberId?: uuid, oauthConnectionId?: uuid, apiKeyConnectionId?: uuid, whatsappSenderId?: string }`

Note: Channel deployments (WhatsApp, SMS, Voice, etc.) require connection and phone fields. Use `GET /channels/setup?type=X` to check prerequisites.

Email settings (GMAIL, OUTLOOK): Pass email-specific fields inside `settings`: `draft` (boolean — draft replies instead of auto-sending), `signatureType` (`"DEFAULT"` | `"CUSTOM"` | `"NONE"`), `signatureInfos` (structured signature object), `whitelistEmails`/`whitelistDomains`/`blacklistEmails`/`blacklistDomains` (email filtering), `initialMessage`. Outlook also supports `sharedMailboxEmail` for shared mailboxes. See channel guides for full reference.

Voice settings (TWILIO_VOICE): Pass voice-specific fields inside `settings`: `provider`, `voiceId`, `turn_detection` (VAD config), `flow` (call flow and filler responses), `transfers` (call transfer destinations), `enableSms`, `whitelist`, and more. See `channels/twilio-voice.md` for the full settings reference.

### Get Deployment

`GET /deployments/:deploymentId`

### Update Deployment

`PATCH /deployments/:deploymentId`
Body: `{ name?, description?, agentId?, settings?, isActive? }`

For email deployments, use `settings` to toggle draft mode, update signatures, or change filtering rules — e.g., `{"settings":{"draft":true}}`.

### Delete Deployment

`DELETE /deployments/:deploymentId`

### Get Statistics

`GET /deployments/:deploymentId/statistics`
Response: `{ totalSessions, totalMessages, sessions: [...] }`

### Get Embed Config

`GET /deployments/:deploymentId/embed-config`
Response: `{ theme, primaryColor, position, initialMessage, suggestedMessages, logoUrl, avatarUrl, headerTitle }`

### Update Embed Config

`PATCH /deployments/:deploymentId/embed-config`
Body: any subset of embed config fields
