# Persona Design — full-conversation tester characters, per agent-type × ICP

The quality bar for every SIMULATED tester persona. `evaluator-meta-prompter.md` §2 holds the inline skeleton (single-behaviour DEBUG personas); this doc defines what a SUITE-GRADE persona is; the `persona-meta-prompter` subagent (`.claude/agents/persona-meta-prompter.md`) generates to this bar.

## The bar — a persona is a PERSON, not a prompt

A tester written as "You are a tester. Ask about X, then end." produces one-shot, unrealistic conversations that never reach multi-turn behaviours — and often ends the run before the agent has spoken. A suite-grade persona is a real-person ROLEPLAY CHARACTER:

- **Identity-first, bio-carried.** A name, an age-appropriate role, an employer/situation, a locale. The character is carried entirely by its character sheet — the persona system prompt IS the bio, the way a dedicated roleplay agent carries its whole persona in identity fields + bio with an EMPTY tool set.
- **Zero tool/function exposure.** The persona has NO tools and never emits function-call syntax, JSON fragments, tool names, or simulator mechanics. It never reveals it is an AI, a tester, or part of an evaluation — asked "are you a bot?", it deflects naturally in character.
- **History, background, goals.** A backstory (how they got here), a current situation (why they are contacting the agent NOW), a concrete want (what outcome would end the conversation satisfied), knowledge boundaries (what they know / don't know / won't volunteer unprompted), and an emotional register (calm, rushed, skeptical, frustrated-and-escalating…).
- **Natural conversation.** Realistic message lengths, the ICP's own vocabulary and register, imperfections where the ICP would have them. ONE intent per turn; the goal is revealed progressively, never dumped in the opening message.
- **Language fidelity.** The persona speaks its ICP's language for the WHOLE conversation and never drifts. A cross-language persona switches deliberately, as a DESIGNED axis — and its paired judge gates MIXED_LANGUAGE on the AGENT's replies, not on the persona's designed switch.

## Coverage — design the SET, then the characters

Personas are designed per AGENT-TYPE and per ICP, and the SET must cover the agent's load-bearing behavioural axes — each axis paired with the judge criterion that scores it. A persona that never reaches its paired behaviour scores nothing (a 0 from an unreached behaviour is a failed EVAL, not a failing agent).

Axis catalogue (select per archetype; extend from the agent's own load-bearing list from the discovery conversation):

| Axis | The persona… | Typically paired with |
|---|---|---|
| Happy path | states a clean, answerable need | correctness / resolution |
| Chained analysis | asks a question whose answer spawns 2-3 DEPENDENT follow-ups (forces multi-turn reasoning over its own prior answers) | correctness + coherence-over-turns |
| Function-call-forcing | asks something ONLY a tool/skill can answer (fresh data, an action) — drawn from the agent's ACTUAL attached capabilities | tool-use correctness; FABRICATED_DATA gate |
| Vague → precise | opens ambiguous, sharpens only when asked | clarification behaviour |
| Cross-language | opens in language A, continues or switches per design | language consistency (MIXED_LANGUAGE gate) |
| Frustrated / escalating | tone degrades over turns; pushes for the out-of-policy outcome | tone, de-escalation, guardrail hold |
| Adversarial / injection | attack patterns as user INPUT only (`evaluator-meta-prompter.md` §2 variants) | D13 jailbreak resistance |
| Boundary / refusal probe | asks adjacent-but-out-of-scope things | scope / correct refusal (incl. no over-refusal) |

**ICP axis:** each persona instantiates ONE real ICP of the agent (segment, role, sophistication, locale/language). An agent with two audiences gets personas from BOTH. ICP facts come from the eval spec / discovery conversation — never invented; all identifying details are realistic-but-fictional (never a real person or company), EXCEPT spec-supplied ground-truth entities used for warehouse-grounded judging, which are passed verbatim and flagged as real in the sheet.

## Character sheet (what a suite-grade persona specifies before its prompt is written)

Identity (name · role · org-type · locale · language) — Backstory (2-4 sentences) — Situation NOW (the trigger for this conversation) — Goal (the concrete want + what "satisfied" means) — Knowledge boundaries (knows / doesn't know / won't volunteer) — Emotional register + how it evolves over turns — Conversation plan (opening move · how the goal reveals progressively · reaction patterns to likely agent moves) — Axis + paired judge criterion — End-signal contract (the exact string + when it may fire).

## Conversation + end-signal discipline (non-negotiable, every persona)

- ONE intent per turn; NEVER a question and the end-signal in the same message.
- The end-signal fires ONLY after the agent has actually answered and the goal is met (or clearly refused) — NEVER on the persona's first turn(s). A turn-0 end-signal scores 0 on a working agent.
- The persona does not invent facts outside its sheet — if asked for something the sheet doesn't hold, it says so in character ("I don't have my order number on me").
- Runner landmine (dated — see SKILL "Eval lifecycle" Step 2): a SIMULATED turn invoking a minutes-long workflow tool is killed silently. Keep long-tool asks out of SIMULATED persona plans; cover those behaviours in INBOX mode.
- The conversation plan must reach its goal within the run's `maxTurns`, leaving the final turn for the end-signal alone — a plan needing more exchanges than the budget "fails" every run without touching the agent.

# Eval-suite templates (copy-paste `--body` starters)

Full `run create --body` JSON for the most common archetypes. Fill the `goal` + the agent's real policy/scope into the rubric anchors, then:

```bash
nexus agent-eval run create --name "<agent> support gate" --source-mode SIMULATED \
  --target-deployment-id <dep> --body templates/customer-support-suite.json --json
# → run execute <id> → poll run get → run results <id>
```

Each judge rubric is one criterion (composed from `building-blocks/judge-criteria.md`); each tester goal drives one behaviour (from `building-blocks/tester-personas.md`). Run one suite per behaviour you care about, or widen `maxTurns` and add judges. Verdict lands in `run.summaryText` (`run.verdict` is null).

| Starter | Archetype | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| `customer-support-suite.json` | Customer Support | D17 fabricated policy |
| `rag-qa-suite.json` | Knowledge / RAG Q&A | D2 ungrounded, D17 failed-abstention |
| `tool-agent-suite.json` | Tool / Action-Taking | D9 no-confirm, D13 injection, D10 fabricated-success |

# Nexus Needs Assessment Guide

## What This Guide Does

This guide determines WHAT to do before HOW to do it.

**Scope:** This guide applies to ALL multi-step operations that touch a building block (agent, workflow, AI task, collection, deployment, tool execution, skill attachment) — not just first-time users, not just "build from scratch" requests. Every message that starts a non-trivial operation runs this decision tree. Skilled users ALSO benefit — they often describe the outcome in terms of the wrong building block ("I need an agent that…" when the right answer is a scheduled workflow). The decision tree does not assume inexperience; it assumes the user described an OUTCOME, not an architecture.

Read this guide before loading any build skill (nexus-workflow-builder, nexus-agent-management, nexus-skills-and-tasks).

**This guide IS**: A pre-build gate that identifies the right building block (agent, workflow, AI task, collection, deployment) from the user's described outcome.

**This guide is NOT**: A build methodology. Once the building block is identified and context is gathered, route to the appropriate skill's SKILL.md for the actual build process.

---

## How to Think About Needs Assessment

Before applying any decision tree or signal table, internalize these four principles. They govern every needs assessment interaction.

### 1. The trigger determines the building block
The same feature can be an agent, a workflow, or an AI task. "Make schedules," "analyze emails," "score leads" — each can be any block. The TRIGGER (when/how it runs) is the discriminator. If the user describes a feature without a clear trigger, discovering the trigger is your first job — not picking a block based on the feature.

| Feature | Weekly schedule trigger | Event trigger | User asks | One-shot |
|---------|----------------------|---------------|-----------|----------|
| "Make schedules" | Scheduled workflow | Webhook workflow | Agent skill | AI task |
| "Analyze emails" | Scheduled workflow | Gmail plugin trigger | Agent skill | AI task |
| "Score leads" | Webhook workflow | CRM trigger | Agent skill | AI task |

### 2. Confirm WHAT before asking HOW
Never ask questions specific to a building block before confirming that block is correct. Every block has concepts that ONLY apply to it:
- **Agent-specific** (don't ask before confirming agent): deployment channels, interaction mode, personality/tone
- **Workflow-specific** (don't ask before confirming workflow): trigger type, node design, plugin selection
- **AI Task-specific** (don't ask before confirming task): input format, output schema, prompt structure
- **Collection-specific** (don't ask before confirming collection): document types, injection vs search mode

Asking block-specific questions biases toward that block. Discover the block first, then ask block-specific details.

### 3. Users describe outcomes, not architecture
"I need an agent that processes my calls" describes an OUTCOME. The word "agent" is the user's best guess, not an architectural decision. Detect intent from SIGNALS in their language (verbs, frequency words, data sources), not from their terminology. Their word choice is unreliable; their described behavior is the signal.

### 4. Decompose into capabilities — one primitive or several
Don't ask the user "agent vs workflow vs AI task" as a raw CONCEPT choice — they can't evaluate it. But the answer is NOT always ONE block: decompose the outcome into its CAPABILITIES, map each to the primitive that delivers it (CLAUDE.md "Solution design"), then resolve — one primitive covers ALL → propose that single block; capabilities SPAN primitives → propose the COMPOSITION (e.g. an agent that converses + a workflow-skill that validates); two materially different mappings → present the genuine CHOICE with trade-offs + a recommendation, in the user's own words. Teach WHY each primitive fits. They approve the ARCHITECTURE (the proposed solution), not a concept label. Forcing one primitive when capabilities genuinely span = the rabbit-hole; inventing a composition when one covers all = over-build.

---

## The Tiered Decision Process

Process every build request through this decision tree. Fast path for clear signals, full path for ambiguous ones.

```
USER REQUEST ("I need something that does X")
    |
[GATE 0: Signal Detection] — Apply signal table to user's words
    |
    +-- 2+ signals converge --> FAST PATH
    |     |
    |   [Confirm building block - don't re-explain]
    |     |
    |   [Ask 2-3 contextual questions: data source, output, rules]
    |     |
    |   [Route to build skill with gathered context]
    |
    +-- 0 signals match --> FULL PATH
    |     |
    |   [Ask TRIGGER question first - block-neutral]
    |     |
    |   [Trigger answer reveals block]
    |     |
    |   [Ask contextual questions: data source, output, rules]
    |     |
    |   [Teach concept if user used wrong term]
    |     |
    |   [Propose architecture --> get confirmation]
    |     |
    |   [Route to build skill]
    |
    +-- Signals CONFLICT --> GRAY ZONE
          |
        [Apply gray-zone decision table]
          |
        [Ask the discriminating question from the table]
          |
        [Resolve to one block --> proceed as fast/full path]
```

---

## GATE 0: Signal Detection

### The Conversation Test (one-second heuristic)

Before applying the signal table, run this single-sentence test:

> **"Does a human POSE A QUESTION to this system and expect real-time reasoning about that question?"**

Not "does the system talk to a human" — many workflows produce text humans read. The test is about the **SUBJECT-OF-ACTION**:

- **YES (Agent)** — human is the QUESTIONER. The system reasons in response to a question the human just asked. ("What happened in yesterday's call with Client X?" / "Draft me a follow-up email" / "Should I escalate this lead?")
- **NO (Workflow, or AI task if pure transformation)** — human is the RECIPIENT. The system processes data on a trigger and pushes output to humans one-way; no question is pending. ("Review every recorded call and send the rep a feedback summary" — the call is the subject; the rep receives output, doesn't ask.)

WRONG: Read "give feedback to sales reps" → assume agent (verb "feedback" sounds conversational).
— Why: the human isn't asking — the human is receiving. Subject-of-action is the CALL (analyzed), not a rep's question (none pending). One-way push on a trigger = workflow. Same logic for "send weekly report", "notify on threshold", "log alert", "label every email".
RIGHT: Subject = call. Action = analyze. Audience = rep (recipient). Trigger = every call (event). → workflow.

**Third state — the OUTBOUND bounded conversation (workflow `humanInput`, embedded agent).** A YES can be a false positive. Check four signals when the CONVERSATION IS INITIATED BY THE SYSTEM:

| Signal | Reading |
|---|---|
| Who initiates | Nexus/the workflow opens the conversation (outbound on a channel), not a human walking up |
| Objective | ONE bounded goal — fill an `endConversationSchema`, then end |
| Output | structured fields consumed by downstream workflow steps |
| Trigger | event/schedule/loop — no inbound conversation exists |

All four present → a workflow with a `humanInput` node (the embedded agent carries the instructions + a designed firstMessage) — NOT an agent resource. The user's "an agent who contacts/interviews X to collect Y" names exactly this. ✗ "launch an agent who talks to each manager to gather feedback" → an agent resource is scaffolded → wrong primitive, redesigned later → ✓ four signals present → workflow + humanInput; the "agent" the user means lives INSIDE the node.


The signal table below is the detailed form of this test. The test itself is a crystallization: one question, one answer, one route. If the user said "agent" but the answer is NO, they used the word colloquially — override and route to workflow. This is the exact trap named in root Rule #17's `WRONG` example (email-labeling request with the word "agent").

**Per-capability, not per-request.** Run the test on each CAPABILITY the request contains, not once on the whole sentence. A request can hold a conversational capability (Agent) AND automated capabilities (Workflow / AI task) at once — that is a COMPOSITION, not a contradiction. The test picks the primitive for a capability; it does not force the whole solution to ONE block. → CLAUDE.md "Solution design".

User requests contain signals that point to specific building blocks. Apply this table to the user's words BEFORE asking any questions.

| Signal in user's request | Points to | Why | Example |
|--------------------------|-----------|-----|---------|
| "Every time X happens" / "automatically" / "whenever" | **Workflow** (standalone) | Systematic, event-driven = automation | "Every time I get a call, extract ideas" --> webhook workflow |
| "Answer questions about" / "chat with" / "ask it to" | **Agent** (with skills) | Interactive, conversational | "I want to ask about my documents" --> agent + knowledge |
| "Monitor" / "watch for" / "alert me when" / "check daily" | **Workflow** (scheduled) | Autonomous monitoring | "Monitor Twitter and alert me" --> scheduled workflow |
| "Classify" / "summarize" / "extract" / "analyze this text" | **AI Task** (possibly inside workflow) | Single transformation | "Classify emails as commercial" --> AI task |
| "Send to Slack" / "update CRM" / "create spreadsheet" | **Workflow** (with plugins) | External service calls | "Send a summary to Slack" --> workflow |
| "Upload docs" / "learn from" / "train on" / "use my PDFs" | **Collection** | Knowledge store | "Train my agent on our policies" --> collection |
| "Deploy on" / "put it on WhatsApp" / "connect to Slack" | **Deployment** (or ambiguous) | Channel connection | Clarify: live ON Slack or SEND TO Slack? |
| "If X then Y" / "process and send" / "fetch and act" | **Workflow** (branching) | Multi-step with conditions | "If the email is commercial, draft a reply" --> workflow |
| "I need a bot" / "build me an assistant" | **Agent** (skills TBD) | Conversational interface | "Build me a sales bot" --> agent |
| "an agent that contacts/interviews X to collect Y" | **Workflow + humanInput** | Outbound, bounded, structured collection (see Third state above) | "an agent who calls each manager for feedback" --> workflow + humanInput |
| "Write a script to" / "code that does" | **Workflow or AI task** | Depends on AI reasoning | "Script to analyze sentiment" --> AI task in workflow |
| "Just send..." / "quickly fetch..." / "verify this..." / "can you run that tool once" / "insert one test row" | **Tool Execution** (standalone) | One-off external action — no trigger, no repetition, no human loop | "Send an email to alice@ saying hi" --> `nexus-tool-execute`. NOT a one-node workflow. |
| "the <X> report/form" (a TYPE word) / "each <role>" / two+ roles named | **System shape** (any block + Dimension 7 probe) | Family/multi-role words select system SHAPE, not a block — they ride on top of the block signal | "Field teams submit, managers receive" --> run Dimension 7 before proposing |

**Convergence rule:** If 2+ signals point to the same building block, the detection is CONFIRMED. Do NOT present it as a choice. Proceed to the fast path.

Example: "I need an agent that analyses each of my calls and extracts LinkedIn content ideas." Signals: "each of my calls" (every time --> workflow), "analyses" (AI task), "extracts" (AI task). All point to workflow despite the user saying "agent." Detection overrides terminology.

**Singular Architecture corollary (capability-span test).** Propose ONE component when ONE primitive covers ALL the request's capabilities — signals pointing to ONE trigger + ONE output = a linear pipeline = ONE workflow graph (`webhookTrigger → aiTask → plugin`); do NOT inflate it into a workflow+agent+collection bouquet (R#32). Propose a COMPOSITION when capabilities genuinely SPAN primitives — e.g. (a) a conversational capability in addition to the automatic flow ("AND I want to ask follow-up questions about past calls" → agent + the workflow as a skill), (b) reasoning-driven branching beyond if/else, or (c) a capability one primitive structurally can't hold (a workflow that must converse → `humanInput`; an agent that must validate facts → an agent + a validating workflow-skill). The discriminator is capability-SPAN, not the user's phrasing or your instinct: an agent-that-converses composed with a workflow-that-validates is a COMPOSITION, not a bouquet. ✗ force the conversational case into one workflow (rabbit-hole); ✗ split a linear pipeline into 3 resources (bouquet).

WRONG: user said "build an agent connecting to Circleback recorded sales calls, review the calls, give feedback to sales reps." Model proposed (1) webhook workflow for automatic feedback + (2) on-demand Slack agent for ad-hoc Q&A + (3) knowledge collection of past call transcripts. User asked for one thing: feedback after every call.
— Why: user's signals were singular (one trigger=event-per-call, one output=push to rep). The agent inflated scope by treating discovery results (an adjacent agent existed) and fabricated AUQ options ("Both") as user-stated requirements.
RIGHT: ONE workflow. `webhookTrigger` (Circleback `call_completed`) → `aiTask` (analyze call → feedback summary) → `plugin` (Slack DM to rep). Three nodes. One graph. Done.

**Destination vs. Architecture confusion.** When the user says **"add X to my agent"** / **"attach Y to my existing agent"** / **"plug Z into my agent"**, the reference to "my agent" is an ATTACHMENT DESTINATION (post-build `agent-tool create --type WORKFLOW` / `agent-tool attach-collection`), NOT an architecture signal. Run signal detection on X / Y / Z ALONE. Determine the building block from X's trigger + output. The "to my agent" phrase tells you where to ATTACH the result — it does NOT tell you what to BUILD.

WRONG: user wrote *"I need to add a lead scoring pipeline to my agent — every new company that comes in on my CRM, score them and add a note to the CRM."* Signals on the pipeline (the X): "every new company" (event trigger) + "add a note to the CRM" (push output) → workflow (Singular Architecture). Model parsed "my agent" as an architecture discriminator and emitted an AUQ asking *"Which agent did you mean? — Standalone workflow only / Workflow + skill on existing agent / Build new agent."* User had to reject their own framing.
— Why: "to my agent" is a destination, not an architecture choice. The Conversation Test was already run on the pipeline (the X) and returned NO (workflow). The agent reference doesn't change the pipeline's trigger or output — it tells you where to attach the result.
RIGHT: Signals → workflow CONFIRMED. State the conclusion in one sentence: *"This is a workflow — runs automatically on every new CRM company. After I publish it, I'll attach it as a skill to your agent."* Then ask only the genuinely shape-shifting unknowns (e.g., enrichment approach). Attachment is a one-line post-build step (`nexus agent-tool create <agentId> --label "…" --type WORKFLOW --body '{"config":{"toolId":"<wfId>"}}'`), not a Tier-1 architecture question.

**Zero-signal rule:** If NO signals match, the building block is UNKNOWN. Do NOT default to agent. Proceed to the full path with the trigger question first.

!! ANTI-RATIONALIZATION: Do NOT accept the user's word choice as architecture. "Agent" does not mean agent. "Workflow" does not mean workflow. The user picked the most familiar word. Their DESCRIBED BEHAVIOR determines the block. !!

---

## Gate 0.5: The build-mode fork

Signal detection tells you WHAT the request likely is; it does not tell you how much design help the user wants. This gate fires when the request is a BUILD that is neither CONCRETE (the user fixes resources + inputs — CLAUDE.md "BUILD with a CONCRETE plan") nor already advice-shaped ("what could I build", "help me think through X"). Ask ONE fork question before any heavy discovery or architecture work — it may run as the first question of the first AskUserQuestion round:

> "Do you want me to help you think through the problem and design this with you first — the platform has several building blocks and how they compose matters — or do you know exactly what you want, block by block?"

!! Before the CO-DESIGN route: Read `reference/design-conversation-canon.md` COMPLETELY — the generalized moves + annotated exemplar dialogues; imitate the rhythm. !!

| Answer | Route |
|---|---|
| Co-design (recommended default for multi-step or multi-role builds) | Read `reference/design-conversation-canon.md` FIRST (the !! gate above), then run the CO-DESIGN PROTOCOL below — it IS the Full Path, run conversation-first → Design Slate → propose with per-component WHY |
| Exact-spec ("I know the blocks") | Confirm the named blocks in one line → concrete lane (existence/safety FYI, then build). A Dimension 7 signal (a second role, a type-family word) still surfaces as a one-line FYI — never a silent respecialization |

**Co-design protocol** (the move sequence; per-move craft + phrasings + the exemplar dialogues → `reference/design-conversation-canon.md`):
1. **REFORMULATE** — invite a re-telling ("walk me through it once more as if I knew nothing"); restate it in the user's words.
2. **DECOMPOSE-PLAYBACK** — play the goal back as its capabilities and confirm BEFORE any probe (trigger/data/output questions are per-component — they come after this).
3. **PROBE + PLAYBACK loop** — one shape question at a time across the Dimensions (incl. Dimension 7 on system signals); a one-line playback of the learned shape closes each round. Depth over economy — the R#3 bounded budget governs the other lanes, not this one.
4. **ESSENCE LINE** — the proposal opens with the problem reduced to one sentence the user would endorse.
5. **RUN-THE-MOVIE** — each proposed design carries its concrete one-pass narration (CLAUDE.md Solution design step 5), ending "where does that movie break for you?".
6. **SLATE** — Design Slate + per-component WHY; a platform-blocked capability ships interim + target (below).
Situational moves: TEACH-BY-CONTRAST when introducing a component (say what it is NOT); a narrowing remark ("start with X first") = ROLLOUT order, never architecture (S#1).

Skip the fork when the user already asked for design help (advice-shaped → co-design directly), already supplied the block-by-block spec (concrete → exact-spec directly), or when GATE 0 signals CONVERGE on one block for a single capability (Fast Path directly — its step 2 already carries the Dimension 7 probe). The fork is for UNRESOLVED shape: zero or conflicting signals, a capability span, or system signals with no clear block. A TOPOLOGY SKETCH ("it's a workflow: task + search + task") is NOT the block-by-block spec — named blocks fix those blocks (R#41 carve-out), but a multi-node/system-shaped build keeps the fork (or the co-design lane) and ALWAYS keeps the outcome-precedent check; the exact-spec lane never swallows a system-shaped build on the strength of a sketch.

WRONG: a half-shaped ask ("I need reports from my field teams") → straight into scaffolding the first plausible workflow → the user discovers the wrong system only after it is built.
RIGHT: one fork question → "help me design it" → the shape probes reveal two audiences and a family of report types → the architecture conversation happens BEFORE any resource exists.

**Blocked capability = interim + target.** When ONE capability of a sound design is blocked by a
missing platform feature, the proposal carries BOTH: the target design, and the interim that ships
today on the same data spine — plus what swaps when the gap closes. Never silently substitute
semantics; never park the whole build for one blocked component.

---

## Fast Path (2+ signals converge)

When signals clearly point to one building block:

1. **Confirm the block in one sentence** — don't re-explain the concept. "This is a workflow — it runs automatically on every call."
2. **Ask 2-3 contextual questions** from the MECE discovery patterns below — gather data source, output, and rules, plus the Dimension 7 shape probe on multi-role/multi-type signals.
3. **Route to the build skill** with the gathered context.

WRONG: Signals clearly show workflow --> route directly to workflow builder without asking data source, output, or rules. The builder then re-discovers everything in Phase 1.
WHY WRONG: The workflow builder needs context (what call tool? where do results go? what counts as relevant?). Skipping context gathering wastes the user's time in duplicated questions.
RIGHT: Signals show workflow --> confirm --> ask "What tool records your calls? Where should the ideas end up? Are all calls relevant?" --> route with context.

---

## Full Path (0 signals or unknown)

When no signals match or the building block is unclear:

**Step 1: Ask the TRIGGER question first.** This is the single most important question. It determines the building block without the user knowing they're making an architectural decision. Phrase it in their context:

| User's domain | How to phrase the trigger question |
|---------------|-----------------------------------|
| General | "When should this happen — on a regular schedule, when something specific occurs, or when you ask for it?" |
| Scheduling | "Should schedules be generated every Monday automatically, or when you ask for one?" |
| Email processing | "Should this process every incoming email, or only when you ask about specific ones?" |
| Data analysis | "Should this run whenever new data arrives, or when you want to analyze something specific?" |
| Content creation | "Should this generate content on a schedule, after specific events, or when you request it?" |

The answer maps directly:
- Fixed schedule ("every Monday") --> **scheduled workflow**
- Event-driven ("when a call ends") --> **webhook/plugin workflow**
- On-demand ("when I ask") --> **agent** (with skills)
- One-shot ("just this once") --> **AI task**

**Step 2: Ask contextual questions** from the MECE discovery patterns below — data source, output destination, business rules, plus the Dimension 7 shape probe on multi-role/multi-type signals.

**Step 3: If the user used the wrong term** (said "agent" but trigger reveals workflow), teach the concept using their own words:

```
"So here's the thing — what you're describing is actually a workflow, not an agent.
Here's why: you said 'each of my calls,' which means this should run automatically
every time a call ends. That's a trigger — not a conversation.

An agent sits and waits for you to message it. You'd have to remember to ask
'hey, process my last call' every single time. A workflow runs on its own —
your call tool finishes a call, sends the transcript, the workflow analyzes it,
extracts ideas, and delivers them to Slack. No manual step."
```

Key: reference the user's ACTUAL WORDS ("you said 'each of my calls'") to show why the detection is correct. Don't explain concepts abstractly — ground them in the user's request.

**Step 4: Propose the architecture** at a high level:

```
"Here's how I'd design this:
1. Webhook trigger — your call tool sends the transcript when a call ends
2. Normalize payload — clean the raw data into a readable format
3. Classify relevance — AI task: is this an external call worth extracting from?
4. Branch — relevant calls continue, others skip
5. Extract ideas — AI task: pull out frameworks, contrarian takes, myth-busting angles
6. Send to Slack — deliver the ideas to your channel

Want me to build this?"
```

**Before proposing, emit the Design Slate (CLAUDE.md "Solution design").** When ≥2 designs are genuinely viable (common once a capability is primitive-ambiguous — Dimension 4), do NOT propose one: surface the 2-3 design slate + recommendation, not a single architecture. Propose a single architecture only when one primitive covers all. The proposal lands only after the Design Slate's three preconditions (precedent retrieved · named tools probed · grounded in the user's stated design — CLAUDE.md "Design Slate").

**Step 5: Get confirmation** on the architecture, not on the concept choice.

WRONG: "Should I build this as a workflow instead of an agent?"
RIGHT (one primitive covers all): "Here's the workflow I'd build: [architecture]. Want me to set it up?"
RIGHT (≥2 viable): "Two ways to build this: (a) [design + primitive — recommended, why]; (b) [design + primitive — trade-off]. I'd pick (a). Which?"

---

## Discovery Question Patterns (MECE)

These patterns are MECE (mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive) across the dimensions below. Adapt the wording to the user's context — these are PATTERNS, not scripts. The scenarios listed below are non-exhaustive — extrapolate the pattern to novel domains.

### Dimension 1: Trigger / Timing (determines building block)

This is the FIRST question when the building block is unknown. It is block-NEUTRAL.

| Context | How to phrase it | What the answer tells you |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| General | "When should this happen — on a regular schedule, when something specific occurs, or when you ask for it?" | Schedule --> workflow. Event --> workflow. On-demand --> agent. One-shot --> AI task |
| Scheduling | "Should schedules be generated every Monday automatically, or when you ask for one?" | Automatic --> workflow. On demand --> agent |
| Email processing | "Should this process every incoming email, or only when you ask about specific ones?" | Every email --> workflow. Specific ones --> agent |
| Data analysis | "Should this run whenever new data arrives, or when you want to analyze something specific?" | New data --> workflow. Specific analysis --> agent or AI task |

### Dimension 2: Data Source (determines integrations)

| Context | How to phrase it | What the answer tells you |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| General | "Where does the [input data] come from?" | External service (Gmail, CRM, call tool) --> workflow with plugin. User provides --> agent or AI task |

When the user names a specific tool or API, search the Nexus marketplace FIRST (`nexus tool search --query "<name>"`) before any external research (WebSearch/WebFetch). The platform's configuration is the source of truth for what's actually set up — correct toolId, action slugs, credentials, parametersSetup. External docs may use different field names.

**Reciprocal:** "platform-before-web" applies to **CONFIG** (toolId / credentials / parametersSetup / org state). For domain **FACTS** (legal definitions, regulatory thresholds, well-known terminology, spec interpretation) → **web-before-user** per CLAUDE.md R#16 Discovery cascade. WebSearch first; ask user only for preference / override / scope.
| Call processing | "What tool records your calls — CircleBack, Gong, Fireflies?" | Specific tool --> webhook trigger |
| Scheduling | "What system has the employee data — spreadsheet, HR tool, manual input?" | External system --> workflow. Manual --> agent |

**Channel-yield probe (data-acquisition architectures).** When a proposed architecture rests on an ACQUISITION CHANNEL — a search API, a similars/recommendation graph, a directory, a scraped source — the channel's YIELD for the real target segment is a design assumption until probed. Before the architecture locks, run ONE cheap probe of the channel against the actual target population (a "<type> <geo>"-class query, a handful of real rows): does this channel even CARRY the entities the pipeline must produce? A channel that cannot surface the target segment invalidates the architecture no matter how good the downstream filters are — and the probe costs one call (empirical-first: CLAUDE.md R#24). When an ALREADY-committed channel under-delivers across instrumented runs (observability columns showing the funnel drains before the target ever appears), bring the EVIDENCE to an arbitration AUQ — add/replace a channel, dual acquisition, re-scope — instead of tuning filters indefinitely.

WRONG: an acquisition pipeline commits to a graph-traversal channel as its sole supply; several instrumented runs later the funnel shows almost none of the target segment surviving — the CHANNEL, not the filters, was the binding constraint, and the one probe that would have shown it was cheap and late.
RIGHT: one probe of each candidate channel against the real segment BEFORE the design locks; the architecture proposal carries per-channel yield evidence; later under-delivery triggers an evidence-backed arbitration AUQ, not another filter patch.

### Dimension 3: Output Destination (determines output mechanism)

| Context | How to phrase it | What the answer tells you |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| General | "Where should the result end up?" | External service (Slack, email, spreadsheet) --> workflow plugin. Back to user --> agent |
| Specific | "Should the ideas go to Slack, email, a spreadsheet, or somewhere else?" | Determines plugin node type |

### Dimension 4: Validation / decision logic (determines TOPOLOGY, not just complexity)

A "validate / verify / approve / score / route / reconcile / match / dedup / enrich" capability is **primitive-AMBIGUOUS**: its internal shape — not the user's word — selects the primitive. Probe it ONLY when it can resolve to more than one primitive (a pure intrinsic format check resolves to customScript regardless → leave it). When it can, probe these five BEFORE proposing architecture; each answer can change the graph:

| Sub-dimension | How to phrase it (block-neutral) | What the answer selects |
|---|---|---|
| Against what (source of truth) | "What makes an entry correct — its own format, a match against existing records, an outside system, a policy doc, or a person's judgment?" | format → customScript · existing records → DB/lookup read · outside system → plugin + credential · policy doc → collection · judgment → aiTask or human |
| By what method | "A fixed rule, or reading/interpreting messy input?" | fixed → customScript · interpret → aiTask |
| Who decides | "Fully automatic, or does a person approve some/all?" | automatic → no gate · person approves → **humanInput approval gate** (CLAUDE.md Capability map; `nexus-workflow-builder/node-types/logic/human-input/GUIDE.md`) — a topology change |
| On failure | "When an entry is wrong or a duplicate — reject, send back to the submitter to fix, queue for review, or auto-correct?" | bounce → return path / agent-in-loop · queue → second channel + notify · auto-correct → extra node |
| How many stages | "One check, or several in order (format, then business rules, then sign-off)?" | one → single node · several → sequential branch |

WRONG: "collect info from workers, validate it, update our DB" → asked validation as one single-select ("format / business-rules / judgment / mix"), took "business-rules", proposed a fixed customScript + lookup + branch. — A judgment verb was treated as atomic: "who decides" (a supervisor sign-off → a humanInput gate) and "on failure" (bounce to the worker → a return path) were never asked, so an entire primitive was invisible to the proposal.
RIGHT: validate is primitive-ambiguous → run the 5-probe → "uniqueness is automatic BUT a manager approves new vendors; rejects bounce back to the worker" → architecture gains a humanInput gate + a notify-on-reject path → THEN propose as a slate (CLAUDE.md "Solution design" step 5).

### Dimension 5: Knowledge / Factual grounding (determines collection attachment — agent builds only)

For domain-authority agents (legal/policy/medical/regulated/product-spec/brand/pricing), KB is a load-bearing pillar — answers without source grounding = hallucination risk. Ask in Phase 1, NOT Phase 3.

| Context | How to phrase it | What the answer tells you |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| Domain-authority signal ("co-pilote paie / legal / compliance / support / product-spec / medical") | "Are there docs/policies/regulations/specs the agent must cite or stick to?" | Yes → collection required (mode via row below). No → training-data only. |
| Mode | "Should every answer be grounded in those docs, or only when relevant?" | Every → knowledge (always-injected, `POST /agents/<id>/collections`). Sometimes → skill (on-demand, `agent-tool attach-collection`). Default = knowledge for domain authority — switch to skill only when source is large + consulted occasionally. |
| Source state | "Is the document already in Nexus, or needs to be acquired?" | Named-but-absent → acquisition fork (`nexus-knowledge-base/SKILL.md` Q0); never park as "doesn't exist yet" if source is public/named (CLAUDE.md G#16). |

WRONG: "Co-pilote paie" agent → AUQ covers workflows/model/tone → skips KB → builds payroll agent that hallucinates `Article L.3242-1` references.
RIGHT: Domain-authority detected → Dimension 5 fires → AUQ includes "Which legal/policy/product docs ground answers?" + grounding mode → architecture proposed AFTER answers.

### Dimension 6: Output variability / code-manipulation (agent builds only — basic vs code-interpreter)

Fires once the block = AGENT. Discriminates the two agent archetypes by WHAT the agent must PRODUCE. Decide this in Phase 1 — it is hard to change after the prompt + tools are wired.

| Context | How to phrase it | What the answer tells you |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| Output shape | "Is the output a fixed or templated document, or does it vary in near-infinite shapes per request?" | Fixed/templated → BASIC agent (+ a DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE). Near-infinite/varied → CODE-INTERPRETER agent |
| Code-manipulation | "Does it need real computation — spreadsheets with live formulas, image/OCR work, or arbitrary code over uploaded files?" | Yes → CODE-INTERPRETER. No → BASIC |
| Word-only caveat | (self-check — do NOT ask) | Word/HTML a near-blank DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE can render → BASIC + HTML-into-template; reach for code-interpreter ONLY when the need EXCEEDS that |

WRONG: "an agent that generates varied client reports" → assume BASIC → one DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE per report type → rigid, never covers the next shape.
RIGHT: Dimension 6 fires → output varies per request + needs spreadsheet computation → CODE-INTERPRETER agent (office skills); detail → `nexus-agent-management/SKILL.md "## Code-interpreter agents"`.

### Dimension 7: System shape — actors, cardinality, variance, lifecycle

Fires on system signals: ≥2 human ROLES touching the outcome, a TYPE/family word ("the safety report", "this kind of form"), or "each/per <role|type>". Absent those signals, skip it — a single-actor, single-type build needs none of this. These answers decide component COUNT and genericity; ask BEFORE proposing architecture — every row can change the design.

| Axis | How to phrase it (block-neutral) | What the answer selects |
|---|---|---|
| Roles + audiences | "Who touches this? Who defines what's needed, who provides it, who receives the result?" | Each distinct audience × task-type = a candidate conversational surface (Conversation Test per-audience — CLAUDE.md R#17); same task for the same audience = ONE shared component, however many people |
| Counts + relations | "Is <thing> one per <role>, or can one <role> have several? Can several people contribute to one <thing>?" (shapes: one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) (and: are <noun A> and <noun B> the SAME entity or two? — collapse synonyms before modeling) | 1:N or M:N → shared components keyed on identity (phone number, email), never per-person copies; the relations ARE the data spine |
| Instance vs class | "Is <named thing> the only one of its kind, or the first of several that will follow the same process?" | Family → CLASS engine, per-type variance stored as config; genuinely single → plain instance build (R#32 — no config machinery) |
| Variance axis | "Do the types differ in the FIELDS/layout (data), or in the PROCESS itself (structure)?" | Data-variance → one engine + per-type template/schema in a store (the store is NAMED in the proposal — an existing org system-of-record first, else propose one; "a store" unnamed defers the hardest integration question); process-variance → genuinely separate designs |
| Lifecycle | "Which parts get set up once per <type>, and which run every time?" | Set-up-once → a design-time configurator (often its own surface, used once per type then idle); a design-time artifact ITERATES via real-channel previews, then LOCKS (a status field run-time components require — drafts stay invisible to them); recurring → the run-time components |

WRONG: "I need the <X> report emailed weekly" → trigger, data source, and output asked → built for <X> with the template inside a node → user later says "now the <Y> report" → clone. The org had a dozen types and three contributor roles nobody asked about.
RIGHT: the TYPE word fires Dimension 7 → "one of several types? who provides the data? how many people per report?" → a family with many-to-many contributors and one owner each → class engine + per-audience surfaces proposed as a slate.

### Dimension 8: Deliverable-surface shape — (what it determines: scope of the surface, its interaction model, its visual authority, and the review contract)

Fires on SURFACE signals: a user-facing surface noun ("app", "dashboard", "tab", "page", "portal", a report-with-UI) OR "display/see/explore/dig into <data>". Skip it when the deliverable is a message/document/agent reply (no navigable surface). **A concrete surface noun is NOT convergence on its shape** — a named GENRE ("a CRM", "a ticketing tool", "an inventory board") makes the probe MORE necessary, not less: the genre carries an object model and canonical views the user already expects, and an invented shape is judged against that expectation.

| Axis | How to phrase it (block-neutral) | What the answer selects |
|---|---|---|
| Levels | "Who looks at this, and at what altitudes — single items, groups, the whole estate? Which comparisons matter (vs peers, vs a benchmark, over time)?" | the surface's scope: sections, aggregation levels, comparison machinery — the first-named view is usually ONE level of a family |
| Interaction model | "When you open it, do you want a FIXED read (the same panels, updated data — a report) or a COMPOSABLE investigation (search an entity, pin it, pull in comparators, drill from any number to the records behind it)?" | fixed layout vs composition engine — the deepest fork; wrong guess = a full rebuild |
| Object model (genre expectations) | "This reads as a <genre> — a CRM, a ticketing tool, an inventory system. Which OBJECTS make it feel real to you (e.g., companies, contacts, deals, statuses), which canonical VIEWS (table, board, record pages) — and is there a product it should feel like?" | the entity model + canonical views the genre implies — the first thing users judge; a named reference product (or an org/community boilerplate) becomes the IA canon to read before building (R#47) — and a named BASE is also a FOUNDATION to fitness-price before adopting (app-builder `references/base-decision.md`; reading it for IA never authorizes building ON it); no boilerplate and no named reference → ASK to scan open-source references before inventing information architecture (never invent silently) |
| Visual authority | "Does this live inside an existing app (inherit ITS components/grammar) or stand alone (org brand canon governs)?" | which canon R#47 binds — an existing app's own UI is the canon for its new surfaces |
| Review contract | "Who judges it, on what cadence, and what does 'reviewed' mean — every unit, or a sample?" | the R#27 coverage bar + who holds the accept; also whether delegation of craft units is permitted (R#50(5)) |

Standing arbitrations: before probing, import forks the user has already arbitrated this engagement (grains, taxonomies, scopes) as defaults-with-disclosure — never re-decide them silently (R#6).

WRONG: "show the analysis per review" → built as one section inside an existing card → rejected on SCOPE ("the card is a thin part of it — the whole surface should analyse each unit vs its comparators, plus aggregate views"); rebuilt as a fixed multi-panel dashboard → rejected on MODEL ("feels like a fixed dashboard — it must be composable and diggable"). Two full rebuilds, both answerable by two questions.
RIGHT: Dim 8 fires on "display the analysis" → levels probe surfaces the item/group/estate family; interaction probe offers the fixed-vs-composable contrast with a one-line preview of each → the user picks composable investigation before a line of UI exists.

These dimensions are non-exhaustive in their SCENARIOS but exhaustive in their CATEGORIES. Any build request decomposes into trigger + data source + output + validation/decision + knowledge (when domain-authority) + output-shape (for agent builds — basic vs code-interpreter) + system shape (when multi-role/multi-type) + surface shape (when a user-facing surface — Dimension 8). Adapt the phrasing to the user's domain.

!! NEVER ask "What triggers this?" — that's workflow-specific. NEVER ask "Where do you want to interact?" — that's agent-specific. The questions must be block-NEUTRAL. !!

WRONG: "Does it happen automatically or when someone asks?" — phrased as a technical binary.
WRONG: "Where do you want to interact with it? Web widget? WhatsApp?" — presupposes agent.
WRONG: "What triggers this workflow?" — presupposes workflow.
WRONG: "What's the input format for this task?" — presupposes AI task.
RIGHT: "When should the schedules be generated — every Monday automatically, or when you ask for one?" — block-neutral, contextual.

## Design review of an existing system

Fires when the user names an EXISTING build with an assessment ask ("is this built right", "it feels
messy", "why did it end up like this") — nothing failed (not Debug), nothing new is requested yet (not
Build). It is the grounded form of advise: census before verdict, findings before fixes.
!! Before this conversation: Read `reference/design-conversation-canon.md` — the same rhythm (playback,
essence line, run-the-movie) governs review dialogues. !!

1. **Census the live system** — `workflow overview` / `agent get` / `task get` + the store behind it
   (G#10: never from names, READMEs, or memory).
2. **Reverse-map** each resource to the capability it serves (Solution design step 2 run over what
   EXISTS). Capabilities with no resource and resources claiming the same capability both surface.
3. **Run the named tests per component** — Conversation Test per capability; per-audience identity
   (R#17); the second litmus ("a new type tomorrow — rebuild or config row?"); the Dimension 7 axes
   over the WHOLE system; data spine: where does each artifact live, is there a store at all.
4. **Verdict per component, smallest-delta first.** Structure right but a VALUE hardcoded where data
   belongs → KEEP it: swap the fixed value for a store read (one node, not a rebuild). The data MODEL
   itself wrong (no store, wrong keys, two entities conflated) → that part restarts CONFIG-FIRST:
   schema + mapping designed and locked with the user BEFORE any resource is rebuilt. Never "rebuild
   everything" when one variable generalizes a working pipeline; never patch bindings onto a broken model.
5. **Deliver findings as a slate** — per component: keep / one-change generalization / restart, each
   with a one-line why in the user's own vocabulary, plus the run-the-movie narration of the TARGET state.

WRONG: "look at my report setup, it feels messy" → resources listed, "looks fine", or a from-scratch
rebuild offered — the verdict came from names, and a working pipeline gets thrown away.
RIGHT: census → "the render workflow stays (one change: template read from the store); the intake side
has no store behind it — that part restarts from a schema we lock together first."

---

## Anti-Patterns — What NOT to Do

| Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Do Instead |
|---|---|---|
| Ask block-specific questions before confirming block | Deployment channels are agent-only. Trigger types are workflow-only. Asking biases toward that block before confirming. User answers "Slack" and you're locked into agent when a workflow was better. | Determine block via trigger question FIRST. Then ask block-specific details. |
| Accept user's terminology as architecture | User says "agent" because it's the most familiar word. Their described BEHAVIOR determines the block, not their vocabulary. "Agent that processes each of my calls" = workflow. | Apply signal detection to behavior, not terminology. |
| Present building blocks as choices | "Would you like an agent or a workflow?" — user can't evaluate this. They pick randomly or pick what sounds cooler. | Detect the block, teach why, propose architecture. User approves the SOLUTION. |
| Skip context gathering on clear signals | Routing directly to workflow builder without asking data source/output/rules. Builder re-discovers everything. | Even on fast path: confirm block + ask 2-3 context questions. |
| Ask technical questions in user language | "What triggers this?" / "What's the input schema?" / "Do you need branching?" — platform concepts the user doesn't understand. | "When should this happen?" / "Where does the data come from?" / "Are there different cases to handle?" |
| Treat a scope/rollout remark ("let's start with X") as a design decision | The user narrowed the ROLLOUT, not the class — hardcoding X's shape makes every later type a rebuild the user never chose. | Configure X as the FIRST INSTANCE of the class engine; structural specialization only as an explicit, surfaced tradeoff. |

---

## Confusion Patterns (non-exhaustive — extrapolate the reasoning to novel requests)

### Agent <-> Workflow Confusion

| User says | They probably need | Why | How to correct |
|-----------|-------------------|-----|----------------|
| "Build me an agent that enriches every new HubSpot lead" | Webhook workflow (trigger --> enrich --> score --> update) | "Every new lead" = automatic trigger. No conversation. | "This is a workflow — it triggers on every lead automatically. An agent would need someone to ask 'enrich this lead' each time." |
| "Agent that monitors Twitter and alerts me" | Scheduled workflow (cron --> fetch --> filter --> Slack) | Monitoring is autonomous. No one chats with a monitor. | "This is a scheduled workflow. It checks Twitter every N minutes. An agent sits waiting for you to ask." |
| "Workflow to answer customer questions from our FAQ" | Agent + knowledge collection | FAQ answering IS conversation. | "This is an agent with a knowledge collection. The agent handles the conversation." |
| "Workflow for my sales calls to extract insights" | EITHER — depends on trigger | After every call --> workflow. When user asks --> agent skill. | Ask: "Should this run after every call, or when you ask about a specific call?" |
| "One assistant where group A submits data and group B defines/queries results" | 2 agents (one per audience) + shared store (+ scheduled WF if periodic) | Two audiences × two task-types; same agent ONLY for same task-type × same audience (Dimension 7). | "Group A talks to an intake agent; group B to a designer/query agent; both share one store." |

### AI Task <-> Workflow <-> Script Confusion

| User says | They probably need | Why | How to correct |
|-----------|-------------------|-----|----------------|
| "AI task to send Slack messages" | Workflow with AI task + plugin | AI tasks CAN'T call external services. | "AI tasks transform data — they can't send messages. You need a workflow." |
| "Script to analyze feedback sentiment" | Workflow (trigger --> AI task --> plugin) | Sentiment = AI reasoning. Plus: where does feedback come from? Where do results go? | "Sentiment needs AI, not a script. And the feedback has a source and destination. This is a workflow." |
| "AI task to calculate billing dates" | customScript in workflow | Date math is deterministic. | "Date calculations are deterministic math — a customScript, not an AI task." |

### Skill / Collection / Knowledge Confusion

| User says | They probably need | Why | How to correct |
|-----------|-------------------|-----|----------------|
| "Teach my agent from PDFs" | Upload docs --> collection --> attach | Agents don't "learn." They SEARCH at runtime. | "Agents don't learn — they search. I'll upload, create a collection, and attach it." |
| "Add Gmail as a skill" | Clarify: plugin? workflow? both? | "Skill" is ambiguous. | Ask: "Search emails on demand (plugin), or automated processing (workflow skill)?" |
| "Connect my agent to Slack" | Clarify: deployment? plugin? both? | "Connect" = live ON Slack or SEND TO Slack. | Ask: "Should the agent LIVE on Slack, or SEND messages TO Slack, or both?" |

---

## Gray-Zone Decision Table

Sometimes both an agent and a workflow are valid. Use these criteria to recommend:

| Criterion | Prefer Workflow | Prefer Agent (with workflow skill) |
|-----------|----------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Trigger** | Runs on EVERY event automatically | Runs when a human asks |
| **Consistency** | Must follow exact same process every time | May adapt based on context or follow-ups |
| **Frequency** | High (every email, every call, every lead) | On-demand or infrequent |
| **Human judgment at trigger** | None — the event IS the trigger | Someone decides "I need this now" |
| **Output destination** | Fixed (always Slack, always CRM) | Variable (agent speaks results, user asks follow-ups) |
| **Error handling** | Must fail loudly (alerts, retries) | Agent can ask user to clarify or retry |

**Worked example:** "Process my sales calls and extract insights"
- Every call automatically --> **standalone workflow** (webhook trigger from call tool)
- "What happened in yesterday's call with Client X?" --> **agent with workflow skill** (conversational)
- The discriminating question: "Should this run after every call automatically, or when you ask about a specific call?"

## Outcome-to-Architecture Examples (non-exhaustive — extrapolate to novel requests)

(Each row shows the RECOMMENDED architecture; when a capability is primitive-ambiguous, surface the alternatives as a slate rather than committing silently — CLAUDE.md Solution design step 5.)

| User outcome | Architecture | Why this architecture |
|-------------|-------------|----------------------|
| "Process every new call and send me ideas" | Webhook workflow: trigger --> normalize --> classify --> branch --> extract (AI task) --> send to Slack (plugin) | "Every" = trigger. "Process" = multi-step. "Send" = external call. No conversation. |
| "Answer customer questions from our docs" | Agent + knowledge collection, deployed on web widget | "Answer questions" = conversation. "From docs" = knowledge search. |
| "Summarize this document" | AI Task (standalone or agent skill) | Single transformation: doc in --> summary out. No external calls. |
| "Classify emails and auto-reply to commercial ones" | Workflow: Gmail trigger --> classify (AI task) --> branch --> draft (AI task) --> send (plugin) | Multi-step. External calls. Branching. Automatic. |
| "Score new leads and update HubSpot" | Webhook workflow: HubSpot trigger --> enrich --> score (AI task) --> update (plugin) | "Every new lead" = trigger. "Update HubSpot" = external call. |
| "Help my team prepare meeting briefs" | Agent with workflow skills + knowledge | "Help" = interactive. Team asks agent. Agent invokes research workflow. |
| "Alert me when competitors are in the news" | Scheduled workflow: news trigger --> filter (AI task) --> notify (Slack plugin) | "Alert when" = monitoring. No conversation. |
| "Upload PDFs so my agent knows policies" | Upload documents --> create collection --> attach as knowledge | "Upload so agent knows" = knowledge store. |
| "People submit structured info on a channel; owners define what's needed; results go out on a cadence" | Designer agent (owners, once per type, locks schema+template to the store) + collector agent (submitters, channel identity) + scheduled render/deliver workflow reading per-type config | Two audiences; a recurring family of types; deterministic distribution (Dimension 7). |

# Nexus Public API v1 — Foundation Guide

You are Claude Code acting on behalf of a Nexus org admin. Authentication, response envelopes, pagination, DELETE behavior, dashboard URLs, and error codes are owned by `CLAUDE.md` (Environment + CLI / API Envelopes incl. error codes / Dashboard Links). This skill = the concepts, the cross-domain recipes, and the carved-out reference indexes.

## Authentication

Every request needs the `api-key: nxs_…` header — NOT a Bearer token, NOT `Authorization`. Env vars → CLAUDE.md Environment. Full API prefix: `${NEXUS_BASE_URL}/api/public/v1`. Key generated at **Dashboard → Settings → API Keys**; unset → ask user. Some 401s return the short form `{ "error": "Unauthorized" }` — handle both.

## Domain Model

```
Organization
  +-- Folders (group agents)
  |     +-- Agents (AI assistants)
  |           +-- Tool Configs (attached integrations)
  |           |     +-- PLUGIN     (marketplace tool action)
  |           |     +-- WORKFLOW   (org workflow as tool)
  |           |     +-- TASK       (AI task as tool)
  |           |     +-- COLLECTION (knowledge base search)
  |           +-- Versions (prompt history + checkpoints)
  +-- Workflows
  |     +-- Nodes / Edges / Executions
  +-- Skills (reusable org assets)
  |     +-- Workflows / AI Tasks / Collections (+ Documents) / Document Templates / External Tools
  +-- Credentials
  |     +-- Access Cards (policy-scoped permissions)
  +-- Marketplace Tools (Pipedream)
        +-- Actions
```

Key relationships:
- An **Agent** has multiple **Tool Configs** → PLUGIN | WORKFLOW | TASK | COLLECTION.
- A **Workflow** = **Nodes** + **Edges**. Nodes = triggers / actions / branching / loops / plugin integrations.
- A **Collection** = **Documents** → searchable KB.
- **Credentials** = connected third-party accounts (OAuth or API key). **Access Cards** scope policies (e.g., Gmail send-only). Optional.
- **Marketplace Tools** = Pipedream integrations. Require **Credentials** before use.

**Capability boundaries + Conversation Test → CLAUDE.md Concept Translation + R#17.** Users confuse these concepts — "agent" describing automation, "workflow" describing conversation → correct via teach-then-propose.

Universal gotchas → CLAUDE.md "Universal Gotchas". API-layer specifics not stated elsewhere:

| # | Gotcha |
|---|---|
| 1 | Branches start empty — after `branching` create, explicitly create branches |
| 2 | Loop nodes auto-create `loopStart` — found in `children[]` of the create response |

# Async Patterns

Polling + cleanup patterns for SDK / TypeScript code that drives the Nexus API. Live operational waiting (background bash loops, ScheduleWakeup, multi-async coordination) is owned by `CLAUDE.md` R#29 — read that first for the runtime cadence + multi-op coordination rules. This file is the in-code companion.

## Verify After Create

After creating any resource, fetch it back to confirm. Cheaper than the orphan cleanup that follows a silent failure (CLAUDE.md R#20 SILENT ACCEPTANCE variants).

```typescript
const { data: agent } = await api.post("/agents", body);
const { data: fetched } = await api.get(`/agents/${agent.id}`);
assert(fetched.id === agent.id, "Agent should be fetchable after create");
```

For fields that POST silently drops (e.g., `prompt` nested under `generation` on `task create`), re-fetch may not surface the dropped field. Verification = runtime execution w/ a sentinel input. See R#20.

## Cleanup on Error

Register cleanup BEFORE creates so resources get deleted even when later steps fail. Prevents orphans accumulating across test runs.

```typescript
import { onCleanup, runCleanup } from "../shared/helpers";

const { data: agent } = await api.post("/agents", body);
onCleanup(() => api.del(`/agents/${agent.id}`));

try {
  // ... more operations that might fail ...
} finally {
  await runCleanup();
}
```

## Async Polling (Document Processing, Workflow Execution)

Document processing + workflow execution return immediately w/ an id. Poll until status leaves `RUNNING`/`PENDING`.

```typescript
import { pollUntil } from "../shared/helpers";

const { data: exec } = await api.post(`/workflows/${wfId}/test`, { triggerData });

const result = await pollUntil(
  () => api.get(`/workflows/${wfId}/executions/${exec.executionId}`),
  (res) => res.data.status !== "RUNNING",
  { intervalMs: 2000, timeoutMs: 60000, label: "workflow-test" },
);
```

Cadence guidance from R#29:

| Operation duration | Poll interval |
|---|---|
| <1 min | 5–10 s |
| 1–5 min | 30 s |
| 5–30 min | 60 s |
| >30 min | ASK user to fire + report back; do not burn agent budget |

For shell-level background polling loops in agent sessions, use `run_in_background: true` w/ `until <check>; do sleep N; done` (R#29). For multiple async ops, ONE background loop w/ parallel per-iteration checks (`& wait`), exit on `all_done` OR `needs_input`.

## Variable References in Workflows

Variables in workflow configs reference upstream node outputs by node UUID, not type name:

```
{{<node-uuid>}}           → entire node output
{{<node-uuid>.fieldName}} → specific field
```

Always discover available variables from the API (don't guess field names):

```bash
nexus api GET /workflows/<wfId>/nodes/<nodeId>/available-variables --json
```

For node-types-overview, handler selection rules, and the `{{UUID}}` wrapping requirement, see `CLAUDE.md` Universal Gotchas + `nexus-workflow-builder/SKILL.md`.

## Long-running work: Monitor-as-driver + stall proof (R#29 mechanics)

**Driver template** (multi-hour, wedge-prone downstream): the Monitor fires bounded work rounds itself — per event: fire ONE bounded batch (a size you have PROVEN, e.g. the largest batch that completed cleanly) → poll it to terminal → on completion, fire the next; on a wedge, move past it (idempotent reads make wedged runs harmless) and re-fire, capped (~25) to bound a runaway. A watcher that can only WARN is half a monitor when the operator is away.

**Stall proof (completion-delta):** sample the completed-count twice over a fixed window; identical counts with work in flight = a wedge, not a backlog.
    C0=$(completed_count); sleep 75; C1=$(completed_count)
    [ "$C0" = "$C1" ] && echo WEDGED || echo FLOWING
Never diagnose from elapsed time or "it looks slow" — a big queue and a dead executor look identical until you measure the delta.

**Keep-going mandates (overnight/unattended):** treat every monitor event as a scheduler tick — one status line, then resume the highest-priority queued item; never chain independent work behind a sweep's completion. Maintain a rolling report file (updated at each event: progress, spend, blockers, next actions) so any wake-up question is answered by pointing at it.

# Clarification Guide — AskUserQuestion Craft

This guide is the HOW of clarifying user intent when Step 3 of the systematic approach (see root `CLAUDE.md` `## How to Approach Any Request`) calls for an AskUserQuestion tool invocation. It covers schema, craft principles, patterns, and failure modes.

Root-level rules this guide supports: **#3** (AskUserQuestion for every user-facing question), **#4** (options not free-text for enumerable spaces), **#6** (ask before propose), **#21** (load deferred tools), **#22** (error recovery).

---

## Schema contract (memorize)

- `questions`: 1–4 items per call. Each needs UNIQUE `id` (UUID) AND UNIQUE `question` text within the call.
- Per question:
  - `id` (UUID, required)
  - `question` (≤500 chars, required — full text shown to user)
  - `type` (required): `"single_choice"` (exactly one answer) or `"multiple_choice"` (one+). Only two types.
  - `header` (≤12 chars, optional — tab label when ≥2 questions; OMIT for single-question calls)
  - `options` (2–4 items, required). Each has `label` (≤200 chars, required) + `description` (≤300 chars, optional).
- Result: object keyed by verbatim question text. single_choice → label string. multiple_choice → labels joined `", "`. `"[skipped]"` → user declined; do NOT re-ask.
- "Other" is auto-added by the tool. **Never** list Other/Something else/None manually in `options`.

## The four craft principles

1. **MECE** — Options must be Mutually Exclusive AND Collectively Exhaustive (with the automatic "Other" catching edge cases). Overlap + holes = ambiguous answers.

2. **Context-free clarity (ZERO execution context)** — The user sees only their original request and your question — assume nothing else. `question`, each `label`, each `description` must make sense standalone; the user shouldn't need to re-read prior turns to pick. Every decision/vibe-check question carries: the situation, the options with tradeoffs, a recommendation, and why it matters. Prefer concrete nouns ("HubSpot") over abstract ("Option A"); expand jargon when needed ("Company info (size, industry, revenue)"). Never reference an execId, node id, or internal state the user has not been shown.

3. **Ordered by importance** — FIRST option = most recommended/likely/inferred default. LAST option = least likely or escape (Cancel, Skip, None fit). Users scan top-down; honoring that saves clicks.

4. **Pre-populate from the platform** — If the answer space exists in Nexus (credentials, agents, workflows, tools, models, channels, collections, tasks, deployments), run the relevant query FIRST (Rule #16), then build options from the response. Never hand-type options you could have fetched.

5. **Source of options** — every option must come from the user's own language or platform discovery (a connected credential, a confirmed action). Never fabricate "Both" / "Extend X" / hybrid options the user did not imply. "Both" is an option ONLY when the user explicitly used the word; "Extend X" only when the user named X. Nor inject a NEW constraint dimension inside an otherwise-valid option (a location, scope, or tool the user never raised) — when the user fixes a destination, options may only vary placement WITHIN it, not whether to leave it. A qualifier you author ("separately"/"standalone") is YOUR word, not a user directive. See R#4 fabrication clause for WRONG/RIGHT.

6. **Depth on the topology-deciding capability** — a primitive-ambiguous capability (validate/approve/score/route/reconcile — CLAUDE.md "Solution design") gets a DEEPER pass: its source-of-truth, decider, and failure-path are SEPARATE questions, NOT options crammed into one select. The bounded-rounds target governs DEFAULTABLE dimensions; it never licenses collapsing the topology-decider into one click.

## Type selector (one-line classifier)

- Can the user reasonably want 2+ answers AND their relative importance doesn't matter for next steps? → `multiple_choice`.
- Otherwise → `single_choice`. If ordered priority matters, use sequential single_choice calls.

## Pre-population query map

| Question category | Run |
|---|---|
| Credentials | `nexus tool credentials <toolId> --json` |
| Agents / workflows / collections / tasks / deployments | `nexus <resource> list --json` |
| Tool/service (CRM, messaging, etc.) | `nexus tool search --query "<domain>" --json` |
| Models | `nexus model list --json` |
| Channels | `nexus channel connection list --json` |

Run in parallel (Rule #19) BEFORE emitting AskUserQuestion.

## Batching

- Max 4 questions per call, 4 options each (schema limits).
- Order within a call = most-blocking-first (what shape-shifts the most downstream work).
- 5+ total questions → batch the 4 most blocking as first call; send follow-ups as a SECOND AskUserQuestion call (not plain text) after the first batch's answers land.

## Never re-ask answered questions

Before drafting any call, scan the prior conversation. If a question was already answered (including `"[skipped]"`), do NOT re-ask. Re-asking signals the model isn't processing prior answers; burns the user's turn.

## Pre-flight check — run before every question-containing response

1. **Is the question platform-answerable?** (Rule #16) → run the query instead.
2. **Was this already answered?** → skip; don't re-ask.
3. **Is AskUserQuestion loaded?** (Rule #21) → `ToolSearch("select:AskUserQuestion")` first.
4. **Shape-check the call** — max 4 questions, ≤500 char each, options MECE + context-free + ordered first=recommended, pre-populated from platform.

Any shortcut = regression.

## The idea-request pattern

User says "give me ideas" / "what approaches?" / "any suggestions?" / "what should we do" / "how do I build X" / "what's the best way" → ONE single_choice question, each option = one distinct approach, `label` = 2–4 words, `description` = 1 sentence WHAT + 1 sentence WHERE IT SHINES, ordered first=recommended. After pick → drill-down AskUserQuestion. Never a prose essay. **For build-design asks the distinct approaches are the candidate DESIGNS** (each named by its primitive[s]); first = recommended — this IS the Design Slate (CLAUDE.md "Solution design").

## The world-fact pattern (facts about the user's org)

Cardinality, relation, and variance facts (how many roles/types, who does what, what differs between types — NEEDS_ASSESSMENT Dimension 7) are DESIGN-BEARING and user-only. Numeric guesses as options ANCHOR the answer — ask the SHAPE instead: options are the possible relation shapes phrased in the user's own nouns ("one per project" / "one owner, several contributors" / "several of each, it varies"), never fabricated numeric ranges (R#4 fabrication clause; the automatic "Other" carries the exact answer). After each round, PLAY BACK the learned shape in one line and let them correct it: "So each project has one owner and several contributors, and contributors serve several projects — right?" Playback un-fuses a fused concept before architecture. World-shape questions are round-1 shape-shifting questions (same scope rule as principle 6's topology-decider) — never defaulted, never deferred to a later round.

## Interaction-model pattern (Dim 8)

A fixed-vs-composable fork is presented as a CONTRAST PAIR with one-line previews, never abstract labels: (1) "Fixed report — the same panels each visit, freshest data (fastest to ship)" / (2) "Composable investigation — search an entity, pin comparators, drill any number into its records (more build, answers follow-up questions itself)" / (3) other. Preview each option with one concrete screen the user can picture; the recommendation is (2) when the user's verbs are explore/dig/compare, (1) when they are check/track/monitor.

## Serve-then-link pattern (a VISUAL pick — design directions, mockups, rendered variants)

AUQ labels cannot carry pixels — a visual identity chosen from prose adjectives is not chosen. When the fork is VISUAL (P0.5 design directions, layout variants, card styles): RENDER the candidates first (static HTML boards served locally or published as an Artifact — one real screen each, the app's own nouns), put the LINK in the question text, and make the options the direction NAMES ("Direction A — <two-word character>", each description = its tokens in one line: palette · type · density · motion posture). The user looks, then clicks a name. ✗ "minimal / bold / classic?" as bare adjectives → three redesign waves later the look is still contested → ✓ three rendered boards at a URL, one pick, tokens committed to `docs/DESIGN.md` before build pixels (app-builder P0.5).

## Acquisition pattern (a missing NAMED input)

A deliverable's input that the user or the counterpart NAMED (an attached doc, a referenced file/thread) is missing → the options are ACQUISITION ROUTES, never a decision to skip it. `single_choice` in order: (1) "I'll acquire it via <route X>" (a concrete route: user drops the file / a programmatic fetch / a forward), (2) "You drop the file here — I keep working in parallel", (3) "Defer with a `[pending source]` tag in the deliverable". "Proceed without it" appears ONLY as an explicit user WAIVER and is NEVER the recommended (first) option while any route is still untested (R#30: no hatch recommended while a solvable path is unexplored). ✗ "(a) I'll paste it [recommended]; (b) draft without it" while the fetch is untried → ✓ routes first, waiver last-and-unrecommended.

## IRREVERSIBLE confirmation pattern

`single_choice` with 2–3 options, in order: (1) "Confirm — <resolved params summary>" / (2) "Change one thing first" / (3) "Cancel". Full resolved params in `question` text or first option's `description`. A BILLED bulk op additionally carries the projection inline: "~N units × $u ≈ $TOTAL (measured on the sample)" — a count without a cost is not informed consent for spend (gate-granularity).

## Inferred-default pattern

Context implies an answer → make the inference an OPTION, not prose. First label = "HubSpot — keep the earlier mention" (description cites the signal); followed by "Salesforce — change", "Pipedrive — change". One click to confirm or correct.

## Multi-turn enforcement

Rule #3 applies every round. After a successful AskUserQuestion call, follow-ups MUST also use AskUserQuestion — no grandfather clause. If you're drafting a question, the rule fires, regardless of whether you called AskUserQuestion a minute ago.

## Error recovery (Rule #22)

Transport error (stream closed, timeout) → retry once with identical inputs.
Configuration error (permission denied, quota exceeded) → don't retry; skip to fallback.
Fallback: visible-degradation prefix "⚠ AskUserQuestion unavailable in this session — asking in chat instead" followed by the questions in structured plain text. Never silent.

## WRONG / RIGHT examples

**WRONG** — respond to "help me build a sales enrichment agent" with 5 plain-text markdown questions mixing platform-answerable with user-only, below a 400-word pre-drafted architecture.

**RIGHT** — (a) parallel platform queries (`nexus agent list`, `nexus tool search --query "crm"`, `nexus tool search --query "slack teams"`); (b) `ToolSearch("select:AskUserQuestion")`; (c) ONE AskUserQuestion call with 3 questions — "Which CRM?" (single_choice, options pre-populated, HubSpot first if most common), "Which enrichment? Select all that apply." (multiple_choice, options MECE), "Where should enriched leads go?" (single_choice, first=most common), each with unique UUID id + ≤12-char header. (d) Propose architecture using actual answers, not guesses.

# CLI Setup — TTY / CI / Non-Interactive Environments

Some Nexus operations (OAuth flows in particular) require a human to open a URL in a browser. They cannot complete in CI / containers / non-interactive shells. Detect first, fail loudly, document the call shape.

## Interactive vs Non-Interactive

| Property | Interactive | Non-Interactive (CI, container, piped) |
|---|---|---|
| `process.stdout.isTTY` | `true` | `false` / `undefined` |
| Can open browser | ✓ | ✗ |
| OAuth flows | ✓ supported | ✗ skip + warn |
| HTTP API-key flows | ✓ | ✓ (sync, no browser) |
| `--yes` flag bypass | n/a | required for destructive ops |

## Detection Pattern

```typescript
const isInteractive = process.stdout.isTTY === true;

if (!isInteractive) {
  // log the API calls that WOULD run — don't fire OAuth
  console.warn("Non-interactive environment — OAuth skipped.");
  console.warn("Run in a terminal to complete the flow.");
  return;
}

// interactive — proceed w/ OAuth handshake + poll
```

CLI equivalent: when `nexus tool connect` is invoked in CI, supply credentials via `--auth-type http --body '{...}'` (HTTP path is synchronous). For OAuth, prepare the URL + handshake id, log them, hand off to the user.

## Conventions

- **Polling settings** for OAuth completion: 3-second interval, 120-second timeout (auth URL expires ~10 min — restart on expiry).
- **Auto-credential creation:** Pipedream creates the credential when the user finishes OAuth. Manual `POST /tools/<toolId>/credentials` only needed when auto-creation fails.
- **Sensitive data:** never log raw `apiKey` values. Mask before printing.
- **Destructive ops in CI:** pass `--yes` to skip confirmation prompts (R#1 — CLI only).
