## Environment quirks (harness shell)

- Non-login shells can drop PATH entries mid-session (`python3`/`curl` "not found" while the binary exists) → use absolute paths (`/usr/bin/python3`, `/usr/bin/curl`) in scripted blocks.
- `grep` may alias to `ugrep`: long alternations hit "exceeds complexity limits", empty alternates (`(a|)`) are rejected → simpler patterns, or python `re`.
- `lsof -ti` is multiline → `kill $(lsof -ti tcp:PORT | tr '\n' ' ')`, never `kill $PID` with an unsplit multiline var.
- macOS `find`/`bfs` `-newermt` wants ISO dates (`2026-01-01T00:00:00`), not relative strings.

# Design-conversation canon — the moves, generalized, then demonstrated

The craft guide for the co-design protocol (NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE Gate 0.5). The RULES live in
NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md and CLAUDE.md "Solution design" — this file teaches HOW each move is
executed: what it is, when it fires, why it works, how it sounds, and what failure looks like
without it. Two annotated dialogues then show the moves composing. Both dialogues are generic
composites (the domain is an example class, not a client).

## The sequence — six moves, in order

### 1. Reformulate *(Gate 0.5 opening)*
**What:** invite the user to re-explain from zero, then restate what you heard in their own words.
**Why it works:** comprehension gets TESTED, not assumed — a restatement gives the user something
concrete to falsify, and their re-telling surfaces what the first telling compressed.
**How it sounds:** "Before I propose anything — walk me through it once more as if I knew nothing.
Who does what, and who is waiting for the result?"
✗ jump from the first message straight to platform questions — a misreading compounds silently for
the whole conversation. ✓ one reformulation round; the user corrects one word ("not summaries — raw
entries") that would have bent the entire design.

### 2. Decompose-playback *(Solution design step 2)*
**What:** play the goal back as its distinct CAPABILITIES and get confirmation BEFORE probing any
of them.
**Why:** the trigger/data/output questions are PER-COMPONENT — asked before the decomposition, one
answer silently binds every component.
**How it sounds:** "So I hear three parts: someone DEFINES the format, people SUBMIT the data,
someone RECEIVES results on a schedule — did I get the parts right?"
✗ "when should this happen?" answered for delivery ("weekly"), silently inherited by the collection
and design components — nobody chose that. ✓ parts confirmed first, then per-part triggers.

### 3. Probe + playback loop *(the Dimensions, incl. Dimension 7; world-fact pattern)*
**What:** one shape question at a time — roles, relations (and entity equivalence: are two of the
user's nouns the SAME thing?), instance-vs-class, variance, lifecycle — each round closed with a
one-line PLAYBACK of the learned shape, inviting correction.
**Why:** depth over economy — batched questions collect answers without testing understanding; the
playback IS the comprehension test. (The R#3 bounded budget governs the other lanes, not a chosen
design dialogue.)
**How it sounds:** "So leads and reporters are many-to-many across projects, and one lead owns each
project's format — right?"
✗ 3 batched questions × 3 rounds, comprehension never tested — at round 3 the user repeats
themselves (the failure signal). ✓ fewer questions, playback each round, corrections land the
moment they are cheap.

### 4. Essence line *(Gate 0.5 co-design protocol)*
**What:** open the proposal with the problem reduced to ONE sentence the user would endorse.
**Why:** it proves the reduction happened — if you cannot write the essence line, you do not yet
understand the problem; and it anchors every proposed component to one center.
**How it sounds:** "Fundamentally this is one thing: you're storing per-project structured data
against a per-kind schema and rendering it to the owner on a schedule."
✗ components proposed with no unifying statement — the user evaluates pieces, not a system. ✓ the
essence line first; each component becomes an obviously-necessary surface around it.

### 5. Run-the-movie *(Solution design step 5)*
**What:** narrate ONE concrete pass of each proposed design in the user's own nouns — who triggers,
what is read/written where, what reaches whom — and end by asking where the movie breaks.
**Why:** design-time simulation is the cheapest gap-detector (a missing identity key or store
column becomes VISIBLE in the narration) and the user's best validation surface — they can see a
movie; they cannot see an architecture diagram.
**How it sounds:** "Monday 08:00 the schedule fires: it reads the store, sees reporter A owes two
entries, messages them on the channel… Where does that movie break for you?"
✗ an abstract component list gets approved; the missing identity key surfaces mid-build. ✓ the
narration exposes it at proposal time, when it costs one question.

### 6. Slate *(Design Slate; "Blocked capability = interim + target")*
**What:** the Design Slate with per-component WHY in the user's words; a capability blocked by a
missing platform feature ships as INTERIM + TARGET on the same data spine.
**Why:** the user approves reasoning they can follow, not labels; the interim keeps one blocked
component from parking the build or silently changing its semantics.

## Situational moves — fire when their trigger appears

**Teach-by-contrast** *(Concept Translation)* — when introducing a component, say what it is NOT:
"the designer is NOT the collector — one audience configures once per kind and then it sits idle;
the other converses every week." Contrast is how a concept lands for a non-platform user.

**Rollout-not-structure** *(S#1 SYSTEM SHAPE)* — a narrowing remark ("start with X first") scopes
ORDER, never architecture: acknowledge X as the first CONFIGURED instance and keep the engine
class-wide. ✗ hardcode X's shape because the user said "first" → every later type becomes a rebuild
nobody chose. ✓ "noted — X is the first configured kind; a new kind stays a config row."

### Situational: Route-the-capability *(fires on APP builds — Solution design steps 3-4, app-builder P0)*

**What:** before the PRD is written, play back the feature list as a ROUTING TABLE — every capability tagged app-view / workflow / agent / AI-task (incl. an in-app "generate with AI" button backed by a task) / native-Nexus — and let the user arbitrate the table, not discover it later. DEFAULT = the native primitive: "does Nexus already do this?" precedes "should the app do this?". Cue PROPOSES the AI-opportunity map from the job analysis — the user reacts to a slate, they don't have to invent it.

**Why it works:** an app request bundles capabilities that do NOT all belong in the app; unrouted, they all silently become app features and the user must hand-route them after the build ("this shouldn't be on the app, this is typically a workflow" — the correction this move pre-empts).

**How it sounds:** "Before I write the spec — of these six capabilities, I'd put the recurring digest and the bulk classification in WORKFLOWS (they run without anyone watching), the reply-drafting behind an in-app validate-and-edit view with an AI task under a button, and only the map + triage board as app surfaces. The app is the surface; the workflows are the engine. Want to move any line?"

✗ every requested feature lands in the app; the user later re-routes them one by one. ✓ the routing table is the FIRST thing the user approves; the PRD records it.


### Situational: Surface-shape probe *(fires on a Dim 8 signal — a user-facing surface noun)*

**What**: before sketching any screen, fix the surface's two load-bearing unknowns — its LEVELS (which entities/aggregations must be explorable) and its INTERACTION MODEL (fixed read vs composable investigation) — with a concrete contrast pair, then name the VISUAL AUTHORITY and the REVIEW contract.

**Why it works**: surface rejections are almost never pixel complaints — they are scope ("this is a thin part of it") or paradigm ("it feels like a fixed dashboard") verdicts. Both are one question each BEFORE building; both are a full rebuild after.

**How it sounds**: "Two shaping questions before I design anything. When you open this, do you want the same panels every time with fresh data — a report you read — or a surface you interrogate: search a shop, pin its competitors, drill from any number into the reviews behind it? And which altitudes matter — single shop, city, region, the whole network?"

✗ the surface noun is treated as converged → a fixed dashboard ships → "not what I want, it must be diggable" → rebuild. ✓ the contrast pair takes 30 seconds; the user says "composable, all four levels"; the first build is the right paradigm.

## Exemplar A — a multi-role, multi-type system (the full rhythm)

USER: We need a bot for our field reports. People keep sending them in chat and everything gets lost.

CUE [reformulate]: Before I propose anything — walk me through it once more as if I knew nothing.
Who writes a report, and who is waiting for it?

USER: Field staff send updates on their projects. Each project lead needs a weekly summary of theirs.

CUE [decompose-playback]: So I hear three parts: someone DEFINES what a report looks like, field
staff SUBMIT the data, and leads RECEIVE a summary on a schedule. Did I get the parts right?

USER: Yes — though today nobody really "defines" anything, that's the problem.

CUE [probe — roles]: Who should own the format — each lead for their own projects, or one central
person for everyone?

USER: Each lead. Projects differ too much.

CUE [probe — relations]: Can one lead run several projects? Can one field person report on several?

USER: Both, all the time.

CUE [playback]: So leads and reporters are many-to-many across projects, and one lead owns each
project's format — right?

USER: Right.

CUE [probe — instance vs class]: Is the weekly summary one KIND of report, or the first of several
kinds that should follow the same pipeline?

USER: There will be more kinds. Start with the weekly one.

CUE [rollout-not-structure]: Noted — weekly is the first CONFIGURED kind, and the pipeline stays
generic so a new kind is a config row, not a rebuild. [probe — variance] Do the kinds differ in the
FIELDS they collect, or in the PROCESS itself?

USER: Just the fields, really.

CUE [probe — entity equivalence]: One more — you say "project" and "report" almost interchangeably.
Is a project exactly one report stream, or can a project have several?

USER: One project, one report stream. Same thing for us.

CUE [essence line]: Then fundamentally this is one thing: you're storing per-project structured
data against a per-kind schema, and rendering it to the owner on a schedule. Everything else is
surfaces around that store.

CUE [run-the-movie]: Here's one week of it running. Monday 08:00, the schedule fires: the workflow
reads the store, sees reporter A owes entries on two projects, and messages them on the channel —
it knows who they are by their channel identity. A replies in chat; the collector agent checks the
entries against that project's schema and writes rows. Wednesday, a lead adjusts their format with
the designer agent — previews arrive on their own channel until they approve, and only then does
the new schema go live for run-time. [teach-by-contrast] The designer is NOT the collector — one
audience configures once per kind and then it sits idle; the other converses every week. Two
agents, one store. Friday 17:00, the render workflow reads only LOCKED schemas, fills each
template, and mails each owner. Where does that movie break for you?

USER: It doesn't — but half our leads won't open a new tool to define formats.

CUE [interim+target]: Then the interim: I seed their schemas from one example report each — same
store, same shape — and the designer agent joins later without redesign. The slate you'll see next
carries both.

## Exemplar B — the boundary: a converged simple build (the rhythm correctly NOT used)

USER: Auto-label my incoming emails by urgency.

CUE: This is a workflow — it runs on every incoming email, no conversation involved. Two things
and I'll build it: which mailbox, and what counts as urgent for you — sender, keywords, or should
the AI judge from content?

USER: Main inbox; AI judges.

CUE: Building it — three nodes, live shortly.

[Margin: 2+ signals converged on one block, single capability → Fast Path. No fork question, no
decomposition ceremony, no slate — the depth machinery exists for unresolved shape, and using it
here would cost the user two turns for nothing. Restraint is half the craft.]

# TypeScript SDK Guide

The `@agent-nexus/sdk` package provides a typed client over the Public API v1. Reads `NEXUS_API_KEY` + `NEXUS_BASE_URL` from env (same vars as the CLI — see `CLAUDE.md` Environment).

```typescript
import { NexusClient } from "@agent-nexus/sdk";

const client = new NexusClient(); // reads NEXUS_API_KEY + NEXUS_BASE_URL

const { data: agents, meta } = await client.agents.list({ page: 1, limit: 5 });
const agent = await client.agents.create({
  firstName: "Test", lastName: "Bot", role: "Assistant",
});
const tools = await client.agents.tools.list(agent.id);
await client.agents.delete(agent.id);
```

## Resource Mapping

| SDK Path | API Domain |
|---|---|
| `client.agents.*` | Agents CRUD |
| `client.agents.tools.*` | Agent tool configs |
| `client.agents.versions.*` | Prompt versions |
| `client.folders.*` | Agent folders |
| `client.documents.*` | Document creation |
| `client.tools.*` | Tool discovery |
| `client.toolConnection.*` | Tool connection (OAuth + HTTP) |
| `client.skills.*` | Skills browsing |
| `client.workflows.*` | Workflow builder |

## Conventions

- Same response envelope as the API — `{ success, data, meta? }`. SDK methods return `data` directly (no manual unwrap).
- Pagination: most use `page`/`limit`; skills use `offset`/`limit` (R#9 in CLAUDE.md API Envelopes).
- Errors throw — wrap in try/catch + read `error.code` per `CLAUDE.md` Error Handling.

## Back-refs

- Foundation concepts → `../SKILL.md` (Domain Model, Tool Config Types)
- CLI vs SDK rule of thumb: CLI for ops + scripts; SDK for typed app code. CLAUDE.md R#1 mandates `nexus` CLI for ops — SDK is for application code only.

# Model Thinking Dialects — Reference

Every model declares a `thinkingDialect`. The dialect determines the VALID `thinkingLevel` vocabulary. Hardcoding levels = 400 invalid-level errors when the model changes.

## Dialects + valid levels + defaults

| Dialect | Provider family | Valid levels | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic-legacy` | Anthropic 4.x (Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.x / Haiku 4.5 / …) | `fast` / `detailed` / `extended` | `fast` |
| `anthropic-adaptive` | Anthropic 4.7+ family | `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max` | `high` |
| `openai-reasoning` | OpenAI o-series + GPT-5 reasoning (`o3`, `o4-mini`, `gpt-5-pro`, `gpt-5.4`, …) | `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` (gated by `supportedReasoningLevels`) | `medium` |
| `gemini-budget` | Gemini reasoning models (budget API) | `dynamic` / `low` / `medium` / `high` | `low` |
| `gemini-level` | Gemini 3+ family | `minimal` / `low` / `medium` / `high` | `low` |

`thinkingDialect: null` → model does not support thinking levels. Setting `thinkingLevel` is silently ignored.

## Canonical branch pattern

```bash
DIALECT=$(nexus model list --json | jq -r ".data[] | select(.modelId==\"$MODEL_ID\") | .thinkingDialect")
case "$DIALECT" in
  anthropic-legacy)   LEVEL="fast"     ;;
  anthropic-adaptive) LEVEL="high"     ;;
  openai-reasoning)   LEVEL="medium"   ;;
  gemini-budget)      LEVEL="low"      ;;
  gemini-level)       LEVEL="low"      ;;
  "")                 LEVEL=""         ;;
esac
```

## Deprecated booleans

`supportsThinking`, `supportsReasoning`, `supportsGeminiThinking`, `useAdaptiveThinking` — shims for backward compat. New code: check `thinkingDialect != null`.

## Back-refs

- CLAUDE.md R#8, G#17
- `nexus-agent-management/SKILL.md` model section
- `nexus-skills-and-tasks/SKILL.md` model selection

files.content:
---
name: nexus-inbox-management
description: Lists, searches, and manages inbox conversations — view messages, send agent replies, manage statuses and assignments, add comments, send WhatsApp templates, and close conversations via the Nexus CLI. Use when the user asks to manage inbox chats, reply to customers, assign conversations, update ticket statuses, or interact with WhatsApp channels.
domain_paths:
  - "apps/backend/src/public/v1/v1-conversations.*"
  - "apps/backend/src/public/v1/domain/use-cases/conversations/*"
  - "packages/sdk/src/resources/conversations.ts"
  - "packages/cli/src/commands/conversation.ts"
---

# Inbox Management

Manage inbox conversations programmatically: list, search, reply as agent, update statuses, assign users, add internal comments, send WhatsApp templates, and close conversations.

## Setup

```bash
# Authenticate
export NEXUS_API_KEY=nxs_u_...
export NEXUS_BASE_URL=https://api.nexusgpt.io  # or your self-hosted URL

# Verify access
nexus conversation list --limit 1
```

## Dashboard URLs

Conversations created or modified via the CLI/SDK appear in the Nexus dashboard:

- Inbox: `https://app.nexusgpt.io/inbox`
- Specific conversation: `https://app.nexusgpt.io/inbox/{conversationId}`

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. List open conversations assigned to you
nexus conversation list --status OPEN --assigned-to me

# 2. Get conversation details
nexus conversation get <conversation-id>

# 3. Read the messages
nexus conversation messages <conversation-id>

# 4. Send a reply as the agent
nexus conversation send-message <conversation-id> --body "Your issue has been resolved."

# 5. Update the ticket status to resolved
nexus conversation update-status <conversation-id> --ticket-status RESOLVED

# 6. Close the conversation
nexus conversation close <conversation-id>
```

## Features

### List Conversations

List inbox conversations with filtering and pagination.

```bash
# All conversations (paginated)
nexus conversation list

# Filter by status
nexus conversation list --status OPEN
nexus conversation list --status ARCHIVED

# Filter by ticket status
nexus conversation list --ticket-status IN_PROGRESS
nexus conversation list --ticket-status WAITING_ON_CUSTOMER

# Filter by response handling mode
nexus conversation list --response-handling MANUAL

# Filter by deployment
nexus conversation list --deployment-id <deployment-uuid>

# Filter by assignment
nexus conversation list --assigned-to me
nexus conversation list --assigned-to none

# Search by topic or message content
nexus conversation list --search "payment issue"

# Combine filters
nexus conversation list --status OPEN --assigned-to me --ticket-status SUBMITTED --limit 10

# JSON output
nexus conversation list --json
```

**Available statuses:** `OPEN`, `RUNNING`, `ARCHIVED`
**Ticket statuses:** `SUBMITTED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `WAITING_ON_CUSTOMER`, `RESOLVED`
**Response handling:** `AUTO`, `ON_APPROVAL`, `MANUAL`

### Advanced Filtering

These filters target activity windows and content — useful for follow-up scans, idle-detection workflows, and audit queries. All filters compose; server-side validation rejects nonsensical combinations (e.g. `--ticket-status` and `--ticket-status-in` together).

```bash
# Last-message activity window (ISO 8601 — compute the date at call time)
nexus conversation list --last-message-before <iso-24h-ago>
nexus conversation list --last-message-after <iso-window-start>

# Multi-value ticket status (comma-separated)
nexus conversation list --ticket-status-in SUBMITTED,IN_PROGRESS

# Exclude a ticket status
nexus conversation list --ticket-status-not RESOLVED

# Filter by last message role (USER = customer, AGENT = AI/human, SYSTEM = events)
nexus conversation list --last-message-type-in USER
nexus conversation list --last-message-type-in USER,AGENT

# Comment content matching (case-sensitive substring on internal comments)
nexus conversation list --comment-contains "tier 2"
nexus conversation list --comment-not-contains END_CONV_FIRED_AT:
```

**Combined: 24h customer abandonment scan**

The canonical use case — find OPEN conversations where the customer (`USER` role) sent the last message more than 24h ago, the ticket isn't already resolved, and no end-of-conversation marker comment has been written:

```bash
# Compute the 24h-ago ISO timestamp at call time, e.g. (macOS):
#   date -u -v-24H +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ
# Linux:
#   date -u -d '24 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ
nexus conversation list \
  --status OPEN \
  --last-message-before <iso-24h-ago> \
  --last-message-type-in USER \
  --ticket-status-not RESOLVED \
  --comment-not-contains END_CONV_FIRED_AT:
```

**Filter reference:**

| Flag                              | Type                 | Notes                                                               |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--last-message-before <iso>`     | ISO 8601 date        | last message strictly older than                                    |
| `--last-message-after <iso>`      | ISO 8601 date        | last message strictly newer than                                    |
| `--ticket-status-in <a,b,c>`      | comma-separated enum | any-of match; conflicts with `--ticket-status`                      |
| `--ticket-status-not <status>`    | enum                 | excludes; conflicts with `--ticket-status` and `--ticket-status-in` |
| `--last-message-type-in <a,b,c>`  | comma-separated enum | values: `USER`, `AGENT`, `SYSTEM`                                   |
| `--comment-contains <substr>`     | substring            | matches any internal comment                                        |
| `--comment-not-contains <substr>` | substring            | excludes conversations with a matching comment                      |

### Get Conversation Details

```bash
nexus conversation get <conversation-id>
nexus conversation get <conversation-id> --json
```

Returns: id, topic, status, ticketStatus, responseHandling, deploymentId, deploymentName, channelType, memberCount, assignedUserIds, unread, createdAt, updatedAt.

### Get Messages

Retrieve messages with cursor-based pagination (newest first by default).

```bash
# Default: last 50 messages
nexus conversation messages <conversation-id>

# Limit results
nexus conversation messages <conversation-id> --limit 10

# Cursor pagination: get messages before a specific date
nexus conversation messages <conversation-id> --before "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z"

# JSON output (for programmatic processing)
nexus conversation messages <conversation-id> --json
```

Message roles: `USER` (customer), `AGENT` (AI or human agent), `SYSTEM` (system events).

### Search Conversations

Full-text search across conversation topics and message content.

```bash
nexus conversation search --query "refund request"
nexus conversation search --query "login" --deployment-id <id>
nexus conversation search --query "billing" --json
```

### Send Agent Message

Send a message as the agent/support representative. This is the same as a human answer in the inbox UI — the message is delivered to the customer through the active channel (web widget, WhatsApp, etc.).

```bash
# Inline message
nexus conversation send-message <id> --body "We've processed your refund."

# From stdin (useful for longer messages)
echo "Your account has been updated..." | nexus conversation send-message <id> --body -
```

### Update Statuses

Update conversation status, ticket status, or response handling mode. All fields are optional — only provided fields are updated.

```bash
# Archive a conversation
nexus conversation update-status <id> --status ARCHIVED

# Mark ticket as resolved
nexus conversation update-status <id> --ticket-status RESOLVED

# Switch to manual response handling
nexus conversation update-status <id> --response-handling MANUAL

# Update multiple fields at once
nexus conversation update-status <id> --status OPEN --ticket-status IN_PROGRESS

# Via JSON body
nexus conversation update-status <id> --body '{"ticketStatus":"RESOLVED","responseHandling":"AUTO"}'
```

### Assign Users

Replace the full list of assigned users on a conversation.

```bash
# Assign users
nexus conversation assign <id> --user-ids user-uuid-1 user-uuid-2

# Unassign all (empty array via JSON body)
nexus conversation update-status <id> --body '{"userIds":[]}'
```

### Comments (Internal Notes)

Add or view internal comments on a conversation. Comments are not visible to the customer.

```bash
# Add a comment
nexus conversation comment <id> --body "Escalated to tier 2 support"

# From stdin
echo "Detailed investigation notes..." | nexus conversation comment <id> --body -

# List comments
nexus conversation comments <id>
nexus conversation comments <id> --json
```

### Send WhatsApp Template

Send a WhatsApp content template message (required for initiating new WhatsApp conversations or re-engaging after 24h).

```bash
nexus conversation send-template <id> --body '{
  "template": {
    "id": "HXxxxxxxxxx",
    "language": "en",
    "types": {
      "twilio/text": {
        "body": "Hello {{1}}, your order {{2}} has been shipped."
      }
    }
  },
  "templateData": {
    "1": "John",
    "2": "#12345"
  }
}'
```

### Close Conversation

Soft-delete (close) a conversation. It can still be viewed in the DELETED filter but is removed from the active inbox.

```bash
nexus conversation close <id>
```

### Mark as Read

Mark all messages in a conversation as read (via SDK only).

```typescript
await client.conversations.markAsRead(conversationId);
```

## SDK Usage

```typescript
import { NexusClient } from "@agent-nexus/sdk";

const client = new NexusClient({ apiKey: "nxs_u_..." });

// List conversations
const { data, meta } = await client.conversations.list({
  status: "OPEN",
  assignedTo: "me",
  page: 1,
  limit: 20
});

// 24h abandonment scan — same shape as the CLI example above.
// Compute the cutoff at call time so the window stays "24h ago" forever.
const twentyFourHoursAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
const abandoned = await client.conversations.list({
  status: "OPEN",
  lastMessageBefore: twentyFourHoursAgo,
  lastMessageTypeIn: ["USER"],
  ticketStatusNot: "RESOLVED",
  commentNotContains: "END_CONV_FIRED_AT:"
});

// Get details + messages
const conv = await client.conversations.get(conversationId);
const { messages, hasMore } = await client.conversations.getMessages(conversationId, { limit: 50 });

// Reply as agent
await client.conversations.sendAgentMessage(conversationId, {
  content: "Your issue has been resolved."
});

// Update statuses
await client.conversations.updateStatuses(conversationId, {
  ticketStatus: "RESOLVED",
  responseHandling: "AUTO"
});

// Assign users
await client.conversations.setAssignedUsers(conversationId, {
  userIds: ["user-1", "user-2"]
});

// Add internal comment
await client.conversations.addComment(conversationId, {
  content: "Escalated to engineering"
});

// Close
await client.conversations.close(conversationId);
```

## API Scopes

This skill requires the following API key scopes:

| Scope                  | Operations                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `conversations:read`   | List, get, search, messages, comments, assigned users                              |
| `conversations:write`  | Update statuses, assign users, add comments, send messages/templates, mark as read |
| `conversations:delete` | Close (soft-delete) conversations                                                  |

## Important Gotchas

1. **Conversation vs Chat**: The public API uses "conversation" terminology. Internally these are "chatrooms" — the mapping is automatic.
2. **Soft delete**: `close` sets status to DELETED — it doesn't permanently remove data.
3. **Agent message delivery**: `send-message` delivers through the active channel (WhatsApp, web widget, etc.) — not just a database record.
4. **WhatsApp 24h window**: After 24h of inactivity, you must use `send-template` (not `send-message`) to re-engage on WhatsApp.
5. **Cursor pagination for messages**: Use `--before` with an ISO date, not page numbers. The response includes `hasMore`.
6. **Page pagination for conversations**: Uses standard `--page` / `--limit` (1-based pages).
7. **Assignment replaces**: `assign` replaces the entire assignment list. To add a user, include all existing user IDs plus the new one.
8. **Response handling modes**: `AUTO` = AI responds automatically, `ON_APPROVAL` = AI drafts for human approval, `MANUAL` = humans only.
9. **Comments are internal**: Comments added via `comment` are team notes — customers never see them.
10. **DELETE returns `{ id, deleted: true }`**: Not 204 No Content.

## Related Skills

| Skill                    | Use case                                                 |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nexus-agent-management` | Create/configure the AI agent that handles conversations |
| `nexus-knowledge-base`   | Manage knowledge collections the agent uses to answer    |
| `nexus-getting-started`  | Authentication setup, API basics, error handling         |

## Fallback

For operations not covered by the CLI, use the raw API command:

```bash
nexus api GET /conversations
nexus api POST /conversations/{id}/agent-message --body '{"content":"Hello"}'
nexus api PATCH /conversations/{id}/statuses --body '{"ticketStatus":"RESOLVED"}'
```

files.content:
---
name: nexus-knowledge-base
description: Manages documents, knowledge collections, and data imports in Nexus via the Nexus CLI. Handles file uploads, text documents, website crawling, Google Sheets imports, and collection management. Use when the user asks to upload files, create knowledge bases, import websites, or manage document collections.
---

# Nexus Knowledge Base

User asks to upload docs / create KB / import websites / manage collections → translate plain language → `nexus` CLI. Setup, envelopes, dashboard URLs → CLAUDE.md.

## Pre-Flight Questions (MANDATORY)

Before any KB operation, ask via AUQ (R#3):

**Q0 — Source presence check.** Is the named source already in Nexus, or does it need acquisition?

| State | Path |
|---|---|
| Already a doc/collection in Nexus | Continue Q1–Q5 |
| User has file locally | `document upload` |
| Named but absent — public regulation/RFC/manual/spec | **Acquisition fork (canonical):** WebSearch canonical URL → `document add-website` (live, always current) OR WebFetch + `document upload` (frozen) → confirm version w/ user before ingest. |
| "Find it for me" | Same acquisition fork — proactively propose 2–3 candidate sources |

WRONG: User: "add Code du travail as knowledge." `collection list` → 0 → "doesn't exist yet, please provide the file" → wait.
RIGHT: WebSearch "Code du travail Legifrance" → propose "(a) Legifrance HTML via `add-website` — live; (b) PDF from <URL> via WebFetch+upload — frozen; (c) your own copy." → user picks → ingest.

1. **Knowledge type?**

| Type | Signal | Approach |
|---|---|---|
| FAQ | help/support pages, Q&A, support agent | [`reference/faq-import-guide.md`](reference/faq-import-guide.md) |
| Website pages | product/marketing/docs | `nexus document add-website` |
| Documents | PDFs, Word, spreadsheets user has | `nexus document upload` |
| Google Sheet | existing sheet w/ structured data | `nexus document create-google-sheet` |

2. **FAQ or website → which languages?** Each lang = separate crawl + doc + collection.
3. **Naming?** Doc name, collection `name` (machine key), `displayName` (human). Never auto-generate w/o confirmation.
4. **Google Sheets → which credential?** Present all w/ dates, user picks (R#16).
5. **Target agent for attachment?**

✗ Start crawl/upload without asking type, or auto-name collection + doc → ✓ ask type → langs → naming → credential → agent → execute.

## Document Creation — 4 Methods

| Method | Command | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Text | `nexus document create-text` | Inline (policies, FAQs, guides) |
| File | `nexus document upload <path>` | PDF, DOCX, TXT, CSV (manifest paths from CLAUDE.md "Attached files" pass through directly — no `cp` / `mv`) |
| Website | `nexus document add-website` | Crawl / sitemap |
| Sheet | `nexus document create-google-sheet` | Spreadsheet (OAuth required) |

### Text (instant — `READY` on create)

```bash
nexus document create-text --name "Return Policy" --content "All refunds within 30 days..." --description "Refund policy" --json
nexus document create-text --name "FAQ" --content - --json < faq.txt   # long content from file
```

Required: `--name`, `--content` (both min 1 char).

### File Upload (async — `PENDING` → `PROCESSING` → `READY`/`ERROR`)

```bash
nexus document upload ./handbook.docx --description "Employee handbook" --json
nexus document get <docId> --json   # poll status, processingProgress
```

### Website Import (async — folder doc + child per page)

```bash
nexus document add-website --url "https://docs.example.com" --mode sitemap --body '{"description":"Product docs"}' --json
```

Modes: `sitemap` / `single`. Advanced `--body` config keys: `urls` / `max_depth` / `max_pages`. Folder doc `isFolder: true`; track `totalChildren`, `readyChildren`, `processingProgress`. ✗ declare "website imported" on add-website 200 → ✓ poll `document get <folderId>` until `processingProgress: 100` AND `errorChildren: 0` (R#5).

### Google Sheets (OAuth required)

```bash
nexus document create-google-sheet --name "Customer Data" \
  --url "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/SPREADSHEET_ID/edit" \
  --body '{ "metadata": { "hasHeaderRow": true } }' --json
```

No Google credential → 400. Connect via `nexus-tool-connection` first. Multiple creds → ask which (R#16). Response: `folder` doc + `sheets` array (one doc per tab).

### Tool-Execute Bridge (non-native sources: Airtable / Notion / HubSpot KB / custom API)

```bash
nexus external-tool execute <airtableId> --action airtable-list-records \
  --input '{"baseId":"app123","tableId":"tbl456"}' --credential <credId> --json \
  | jq -r '.result.records[] | "\(.fields.question)\n\(.fields.answer)\n"' > faq.txt
nexus document create-text --name "Support FAQ" --content - --json < faq.txt
```

Fit: small/medium snapshots, weekly refresh. Continuous sync → scheduled workflow. Procedure: [`../nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`](../nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md).

# FAQ Import Guide

When a user needs to add FAQ knowledge from a website for a customer support agent, follow this end-to-end pipeline. The output is separate knowledge collections per language, each searchable by the agent.

## Pre-Flight Questions (MANDATORY — ask ALL before starting)

Before starting ANY FAQ import, ask the user ALL of these:

1. **What type of knowledge?** FAQ, website pages, documents, or documentation?
   - If FAQ (website with Q&A structure, customer support use case) → follow this guide
   - If website pages → use `nexus document add-website`
   - If documents (PDF, DOCX) → use `nexus document upload`

2. **What languages are available on the site?** (FR, NL, EN, DE, etc.)
   - Check the website for language switcher
   - Each language gets its own crawl, sheet tab, document, and collection

3. **What's the FAQ URL structure?** Visit the help/support page to understand:
   - Are there category pages that link to individual Q&A pages? (most common — two-level crawl)
   - Or are all Q&As on a single page? (single-page extraction)

4. **What should the knowledge be called?**
   - Google Sheet name (e.g., "hey! Telecom FAQ")
   - Document names per language (e.g., "hey! Telecom FAQ - FR", "hey! Telecom FAQ - NL")
   - Collection names per language — machine name + display name (e.g., name: "hey-faq-fr", displayName: "hey! Telecom FAQ - FR")
   - NEVER auto-generate names — always confirm with user

5. **Which Google Sheets credential should be used?** Present all available with dates, let user pick.

6. **Which agent will use this knowledge?** Needed for attaching collections as skills.

## Pipeline Overview

```
STEP 1: CRAWL — Discover and extract all FAQ Q&As per language
    ↓
STEP 2: GOOGLE SHEET — Create spreadsheet with one tab per language
    ↓
STEP 3: PERMISSIONS — User sets sharing to public edit
    ↓
STEP 4: IMPORT — Import Google Sheet as knowledge documents
    ↓
STEP 5: TEST DOCUMENTS — Search raw documents to verify content is indexed
    ↓ (only proceed if document search returns results)
STEP 6: COLLECTIONS — Create one collection per language, attach documents
    ↓
STEP 7: TEST COLLECTIONS — Search each collection to verify RAG works
    ↓ (only proceed if collection search returns results)
STEP 8: ATTACH — Connect collections to agent as skills
```

## Step 1: Crawl FAQ Pages

Launch a background agent per language. Each agent:
1. Fetches each category index page
2. Extracts links to individual FAQ pages
3. Fetches each individual page for the FULL answer
4. Writes results to `/tmp/hey_faq_<lang>.json`

**Output format per entry:**
```json
{"category": "Internet", "question": "...", "answer": "... (all [links](url) as markdown)", "url": "https://..."}
```

**Answer MUST preserve:** All hyperlinks as markdown, all image URLs, all referenced URLs. Nothing stripped.

### ETA Reporting & Progress Monitoring (MANDATORY)

When launching a background crawl agent, you MUST actively monitor it. The user should NEVER have to ask "where is it?" — you report proactively.

**On launch — report initial ETA:**
```
"Crawling ~50 FAQ pages in French at ~6 pages/min.
ETA: ~8 minutes. I'll check progress at 3 min, 6 min, and completion."
```

**Monitoring protocol — use a scheduled sleep loop:**
After launching the background agent, immediately set up a monitoring cadence:

1. `sleep 180` (3 min) → check output file size + check if JSON written → report progress
2. `sleep 180` (6 min) → check again → report updated ETA
3. `sleep 120` (8 min) → check for completion → if done, report. If not, check every 60s.

**How to check progress:**
```bash
# Check output file size (growing = active, stalled = stuck)
wc -c <output_file>

# Check if result JSON exists
ls -la /tmp/hey_faq_<lang>.json

# Count tool calls completed (rough progress indicator)
grep -c "tool_result" <output_file>
```

**Progress report format:**
```
"Progress: output file 45KB (growing). ~35 tool calls completed out of ~59 expected.
Estimated: 60% done. Updated ETA: ~3 more minutes."
```

**Stall detection — output file size unchanged for 2 consecutive checks (4+ min):**
1. Report to user: "Crawl agent appears stalled — output unchanged for 4 minutes."
2. Launch a FRESH agent immediately — do not wait longer
3. Report: "Relaunched. New ETA: ~8 minutes from now."

**NEVER:**
- Let the user ask "where is it?" or "check status" — YOU report first
- Wait until completion notification — actively monitor with sleep intervals
- Ignore a stalled agent — detect and relaunch within 4 minutes

| Metric | Typical value |
|---|---|
| Pages per minute | ~6 (including category index fetches) |
| Tool calls per FAQ entry | ~1.2 (some entries share pages) |
| Total time for ~50 FAQs | ~8-10 minutes |
| Stall threshold | Output unchanged for 4+ minutes |
| Check interval | Every 3 minutes for first 2 checks, then every 60 seconds |

## Step 2: Create Google Sheet via Pipedream

Create a temporary Nexus workflow to interact with Google Sheets using Pipedream actions. Delete the workflow after.

**ALWAYS use Pipedream actions** (`create-spreadsheet`, `create-worksheet`, `update-multiple-rows`, `delete-worksheet`) — NEVER use custom script nodes when Pipedream actions exist for the operation. This applies to ALL Google Sheets operations.

**Correct flow (avoids manual renaming):**

```
1. create-spreadsheet → get spreadsheet ID
     ↓
2. FOR EACH language:
   create-worksheet (name: "FR - FAQ") → get numeric sheetId from replies[0].addSheet.properties.sheetId
     ↓
3. FOR EACH language:
   update-multiple-rows using the NAMED worksheet's numeric sheetId
     ↓
4. delete-worksheet (sheetId: 0) → removes the auto-created default sheet
     ↓
5. Delete the temp workflow
```

**Critical: Credential selection.** Present ALL Google Sheets credentials to the user with dates. Let them pick. Never auto-select.

**Critical: `rows` parameter format.** The `update-multiple-rows` action requires:
- `type: "array"` (NOT `"string"`)
- `value`: actual JSON array of arrays (NOT a stringified JSON string)

| Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Do Instead |
|---|---|---|
| Using custom script node for Google Sheets | Pipedream actions exist for all needed operations | ALWAYS use `create-spreadsheet`, `create-worksheet`, `update-multiple-rows`, `delete-worksheet` |
| Writing to worksheetId 0 (default sheet) | Requires manual rename after | Create named worksheets first, write to them |
| `rows` as stringified JSON string | Fails: "Rows data is not an array of arrays" | Set type to `"array"`, value to actual array |
| Searching for a sharing/permission action | Doesn't exist in Pipedream | Ask user to set permissions manually |
| Not deleting the default sheet | Leaves a "Feuille 1" / "Sheet1" tab | Delete worksheetId 0 after writing named tabs |
| Auto-naming documents and collections | Names are user-facing, user should decide | Ask user for all names in pre-flight questions |

## Step 3: Permissions

Give the user the Google Sheet URL and ask them to set sharing:

```
"Please set sharing to 'Anyone with the link can edit' on this sheet:
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<ID>/edit

Let me know when done and I'll import it as knowledge."
```

Wait for user confirmation before proceeding.

**For repeat use:** Suggest creating a shared Google Drive folder with open permissions. Use `folderId` in `create-spreadsheet` so new sheets inherit permissions automatically.

## Step 4: Import as Knowledge

```bash
nexus api POST /documents/google-sheet --body '{
  "name": "<FAQ Name>",
  "url": "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<ID>/edit",
  "metadata": { "hasHeaderRow": true }
}' --json
```

This creates:
- A folder document (parent)
- One document per sheet tab (FR - FAQ, NL - FAQ, etc.)

Poll documents until status is READY:
```bash
nexus document get <docId> --json
```

## Step 5: Test Documents (MANDATORY — before creating collections)

After documents reach READY status, verify the content is actually indexed by searching:

```bash
# Use the document search/preview to verify content
nexus document get <frDocId> --json
# Verify: status is READY, type is correct
```

If documents are not READY after 2 minutes, something went wrong with the import. Check the Google Sheet permissions and retry.

Only proceed to creating collections AFTER documents are confirmed READY.

## Step 6: Create Collections

Create ONE collection per language:

```bash
nexus collection create --name "<project>-faq-fr" --display-name "<Project> FAQ - FR" --description "French FAQ" --k 10 --json
nexus collection create --name "<project>-faq-nl" --display-name "<Project> FAQ - NL" --description "Dutch FAQ" --k 10 --json
```

Attach each language document to its corresponding collection:

```bash
nexus collection attach-documents <frCollId> --document-ids "<frDocId>"
nexus collection attach-documents <nlCollId> --document-ids "<nlDocId>"
```

**Why separate collections per language:** Mixing languages causes cross-language noise in RAG retrieval. The agent needs to search the right language based on the user's language.

## Step 7: Test Collections (MANDATORY — before attaching to agent)

Search each collection to verify knowledge is indexed and retrievable:

```bash
nexus collection search <frCollId> --query "<question in French>" --limit 3 --json
nexus collection search <nlCollId> --query "<question in Dutch>" --limit 3 --json
```

If results are empty:
1. Wait 30 seconds and retry (indexing may still be in progress)
2. If still empty after 2 retries, check document status — documents need both `status=READY` and completed indexing before they appear in search
3. If still empty after several retries, file a ticket with the collection ID and document IDs

## Step 8: Attach to Agent

```bash
nexus agent-tool attach-collection <agentId> --collection-id "<frCollId>" --label "FAQ FR" --instructions "Search this when user asks questions in French about hey! Telecom services" --json

nexus agent-tool attach-collection <agentId> --collection-id "<nlCollId>" --label "FAQ NL" --instructions "Search this when user asks questions in Dutch about hey! Telecom services" --json
```
