# Sub-agent monitoring contract

When delegating a PA conversation to a sub-agent, the sub-agent prompt MUST include this contract. Without it, sub-agents fail silently — parent discovers gap only when downstream task missing or user spots it in dashboard.

## Required clauses (all nine)

| # | Clause | Why | Sub-agent emits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Thread ID emit-immediately | Recoverable if sub-agent dies mid-conv | `echo "<threadId>" > /tmp/pa_thread_<task-name>.txt` AND `[milestone] thread_created <threadId>` as FIRST line of final report |
| 2 | Milestone log per state transition | Parent reconstructs progress w/o full transcript re-read | `[milestone] PA_question <N>` / `generation_started` / `generation_complete` / `task_created <id>` / `test_<n>_passed` |
| 3 | No probe/test tasks for debugging | Probe tasks are recoverable via `nexus task delete <id>` but still avoid them; create the FINAL task once | `nexus task create` exactly once, for FINAL task. Diagnose via `nexus task execute` on that task only |
| 4 | 20-min generation warn-out | Distinguishes generation from hang | `[warn] PA generation exceeding 20 min, threadId=<id>` then KEEP polling |
| 5 | Loud failure on any non-success exit | Parent has clear recovery path | `[failure] reason=<reason> threadId=<id> last_step=<step>` as LAST line of final report |
| 6 | Canonical CLI sequence w/ `--mode` on every chat call | Platform silently no-ops continuation msgs w/o `--mode` | `chat --mode ai-task --message <spec>` (initial) → `get-thread <id>` (poll) → `chat --mode ai-task --thread-id <id> --message <reply>` (continue) → `task create` (once, final) |
| 7 | Client-side chat timeouts = PARTIAL successes; verify thread state before retry | If `chat` returns `Timed out waiting for assistant response`, user msg ALREADY landed server-side. Resending = duplicate user msg. | Do NOT resend; `get-thread <id>` + confirm last user msg timestamp matches your send. Then wait for `status === "completed"` + assistant reply at tail. `[warn] chat timed out, verifying thread state via get-thread before any retry` |
| 8 | Async waits use bg until-loop, NEVER foreground polling | Foreground `get-thread` polls cost a tool call each. PA generations 5–20 min → fg polling burns 100–400 tool calls per sub-agent → most common cause of #9 firing. Runtime auto-notifies on bg-loop exit. | Waiting for PA reply (last_role=user) → ONE `run_in_background:true` shell w/ `until [ "$(check)" = "done" ]; do sleep 45; done`. Cadence: 30–45s (1–5 min ops), 60s (5–30 min). Per R#29. |
| 9 | Budget cap w/ state handoff on exhaustion | Sub-agents exiting mid-poll w/o surfacing state force parent to discover failure via thread inspection. Clean handoff = parent resumes directly. | Tool-use count >70% budget w/o `[milestone] task_created` → write latest thread state to `/tmp/pa_state_<label>.json` (last user msg + PA reply + status + promptResult-if-any) AND emit `[failure] reason=budget_exhausted threadId=<id> last_step=<step>` as LAST line. Never silent exit. |

## Template snippet to paste into every PA sub-agent prompt

```
## Monitoring contract (mandatory)

1. After FIRST `nexus prompt-assistant chat --mode ai-task --message "<spec>"` returns:
   - Run: echo "<threadId>" > /tmp/pa_thread_<task-name>.txt
   - Emit: `[milestone] thread_created <threadId>` (FIRST line of final report)

2. Per state transition, emit one of:
   - `[milestone] PA_question N` / `generation_started` / `generation_complete`
   - `[milestone] task_created <taskId>` / `test_N_passed`

3. NEVER create probe/minimal-test tasks for debugging. Probe tasks are recoverable via `nexus task delete <id>` but still avoid them; create the FINAL task once.
   Run `nexus task create` exactly once, for the FINAL task. Diagnose via `nexus task execute` on the final task or raw API probes that don't persist.

4. If PA generation >20 min: `[warn] PA generation exceeding 20 min, threadId=<id>` and KEEP polling.

5. On any exit without `[milestone] task_created`: LAST line MUST be `[failure] reason=<reason> threadId=<id> last_step=<step>`. Never silent exit.

6. Continuation messages MUST include `--mode ai-task --thread-id <id>`. Without `--mode`, platform silently no-ops even though CLI returns `{status: null, msgs: 0}`.

7. If `chat` returns timeout error: user msg HAS landed server-side. Do NOT resend (would duplicate). Verify via `get-thread <id>`, then poll for assistant reply.

8. Async waits: ONE bg loop w/ `until <done>; do sleep 45; done` (run_in_background: true). Never foreground polling. (R#29)
```

WRONG: 3 PA sub-agents launched w/o contract. Two exited silently — no thread IDs, no failure signals. Parent discovers gap only when user notices 2 of 3 expected tasks missing from dashboard. ~30 min wasted before diagnosis.
RIGHT: Every PA sub-agent prompt includes the snippet. If sub-agent dies, parent recovers via `cat /tmp/pa_thread_<task-name>.txt` + continues directly.

## Brief discipline

Sub-agent brief = LEAN. Point at canonical spec, do NOT inline 200 lines. Inline material loads into sub-agent context PER TURN, competes w/ conversation for budget. Bloated brief = most common cause of clauses 8 + 9 firing.

**Brief template — the 5 essentials:**
1. **Goal** — one sentence ("generate prompt for task X via PA, create task, sentinel-verify, return task ID").
2. **Spec file path** — canonical doc, NOT inlined. Sub-agent reads on first turn via Read.
3. **Per-task scope** — LABEL or specific scope this sub-agent owns (e.g., "FIN_C2 only"). 1 paragraph.
4. **Sentinel input** — verbatim JSON payload for `nexus task execute <id> --input <sentinel>` (small + load-bearing for clause 5).
5. **Contract** — 9 clauses BY REFERENCE: `see SKILL.md Sub-Agent Monitoring Contract`.

WRONG: 200-line brief inline w/ full taxonomy + 8 anti-rationalization rules + 9 worked examples + voice matrix + sentinel + clauses 1–9. Sub-agent loads per turn × 10 = 2000 lines context cost atop the actual PA conversation. Budget exhausts mid-conv → silent exit w/o `[milestone] task_created`.
RIGHT: 30-line brief = spec path + per-task scope + sentinel + contract reference. Sub-agent reads spec on turn 1 (one Read), then engages PA. Spec in context once, not per-turn.

nexus-skills-and-tasks.description: Browse skills, create AI tasks, generate from doc templates, operate existing external tools. Env/auth/envelopes/dash...

files.content:
---
name: nexus-skills-and-tasks
description: Browses and manages Nexus skills (workflows, AI tasks, collections, document templates, external tools) via the Nexus CLI. Creates AI tasks, executes them, manages document templates, and operates already-created external OpenAPI tools (list, get, upload-icon, execute). For NEW custom-API integration, route to `nexus-tool-connection` (lifecycle owner). Use when the user asks to create AI tasks, generate documents from templates, list available skills, or operate existing external tools.
---

# Nexus Skills and Tasks

Browse skills, create AI tasks, generate from doc templates, operate existing external tools. Env/auth/envelopes/dashboard → CLAUDE.md.

## Boundary check — Is this actually an AI task?

AI tasks = single-purpose transformations: data in → processed data out. CAN'T call external services, hold conversations, run autonomously.

| User signal | Actually needs | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "AI task that sends to Slack/email/CRM" | Workflow w/ aiTask node + plugin node | AI tasks CAN'T call external services |
| "AI task that runs every day / every event" | Workflow w/ trigger + aiTask node | AI tasks have no triggers |
| "AI task that looks up from Gmail/HubSpot" | Workflow w/ plugin node + aiTask node | AI tasks CAN'T fetch external data |
| "Script to analyze sentiment/tone/intent" | AI task (NOT script) | Language understanding → AI reasoning |
| "Classify/summarize/extract from text I provide" | ✓ AI task | Pure transformation, no external calls |

External connection needed → teach in user's words ("AI tasks transform data; you need a workflow w/ the AI task inside") → switch to `nexus-workflow-builder`.

**Output language:** explicitly specify in prompt. Default = user's language (R#15). User writes French but task feeds English channel → ask explicitly. Include language as PA field.

Full classification → CLAUDE.md §Concept Translation + `nexus-getting-started/NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md`.

## Creating AI Tasks — PA Gate + reuse check

**Pre-PA reuse check (R#38 read-before-build):** before invoking PA, `grep -l 'category:' $TOOLS_PATH/ai-tasks/*/*.md` for existing cross-org reusable definitions. Match → propose user adapt existing (anonymised prompt + I/O schema at `$TOOLS_PATH/ai-tasks/<category>/<slug>.md`); no match → proceed to PA.

Per R#31 every new AI task routes through `nexus-prompt-assistant` BEFORE manual creation. Load that skill first.

## Canonical body shape — read BEFORE first `task create` per session

`task create` — `prompt` at TOP-LEVEL (NOT nested under `generation:{}` / `body:{}` / `config:{}` — silent CREATE drop per R#20 SILENT ACCEPTANCE; 200 create, empty execute).

```bash
nexus task create --name "task_name" --model-name "<frontier>" --model-provider "OPEN_AI" --body '{
  "prompt": "The full system prompt goes HERE at root level",
  "description": "Task description",
  "inputFormat": "json",
  "outputFormat": "json",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "generation": {
    "expectedInput":  "Description of what the task receives",
    "expectedOutput": "Description of what the task produces",
    "jsonInputSchema":  { "field_name":   { "type":"string", "description":"…" } },
    "jsonOutputSchema": { "result":       { "type":"string", "description":"…" },
                          "score":        { "type":"number", "description":"…" } }
  }
}' --json
```

**6-check pre-flight:** (1) casing — `inputFormat`/`outputFormat` lowercase only (`"text"`/`"json"`/`"template"`, NOT `"JSON"`). (2) `generation` object present w/ correct subfields per matrix below. (3) `prompt` at ROOT (NOT inside `generation`). (4) **Schema shape** — `jsonInputSchema`/`jsonOutputSchema` are a flat field-MAP (`{"field": <def>, …}`, no outer `{type:object,properties}` wrapper). Each `<def>` is a FULL JSON-Schema node that MAY nest arbitrarily — `{type:object,properties:{…}}` · `{type:array,items:{…}}` · `{type:string,enum:[…]}`. Nesting IS supported and round-trips create→get at arbitrary depth; deep structure is how you enforce "exact JSON" — NEVER collapse a field to a `{x:{type:object}}` stub. (5) Model not deprecated (`nexus model list`). (6) **PA output conversion** — PA wraps the whole schema in `{type:object,properties:{…}}`. Strip ONLY that OUTER wrapper (take `.properties`) → top-level field-map; PRESERVE every nested `properties`/`items`/`enum`. PA stubs structure — keep the depth, never re-flatten it.

WRONG (nested-prompt orphan): `{name, model, generation:{prompt:"…"}}` → 200 → `task execute` "Prompt is required" → orphan.
RIGHT: `{name, model, prompt:"…", generation:{schemas + descriptions}}` flat → 200 → expected output.

✗ Collapsing a field to a stub: `{report:{type:object,properties:{score:{type:integer},items:{type:array,items:{…}}}}}` → `{report:{type:object}}` — loses all structure, can't enforce exact JSON. ✓ Strip PA's OUTER `{type:object,properties}` wrapper only; keep `report`'s nested `properties`/`items`/`enum`.

**Recovery on `task execute` 500 / wrong output / timeout, cost order:** (0) SLOW/TIMEOUT ("Could not reach the Nexus API" on a long generation = the CLI's client-side HTTP timeout, not network): vary the MODEL first — `task update --model-name` to a sibling frontier model + ONE timed execute (structured-JSON latencies differ sharply across providers); REST w/ a long `--max-time` is the fallback, and a confirmed non-configurable CLI timeout is a same-session ticket; (1) inspect error, fix input if validation; (2) **`nexus task update <id>`** — fixes model/prompt/name/temperature AND the full (nested) `jsonOutputSchema` in place, free, no orphan, no dashboard; (3) recreate only if the task is fundamentally wrong, then delete the bad one via `nexus api DELETE /skills/tasks/<id>`. **Probe body shape on a `zz_probe` throwaway BEFORE the real create (R#5 — iterate locally, fire once).**

| Field | Where | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `--name` | yes | Min 1 char |
| `modelName` / `modelProvider` | `--model-name` / `--model-provider` | yes | `OPEN_AI` / `ANTHROPIC` / `GOOGLE_AI`; `model list` first |
| `prompt` | body ROOT | yes for real use | returned by `task get` at top level (with the schemas) |
| `inputFormat` / `outputFormat` | body | no | Lowercase enum, default `text` |
| `temperature` | body | no | 0–2, default 0.7 |
| `generation` | body | yes | Subfields per matrix |

## Model Selection

Always `nexus model list --json` FIRST — landscape changes. Filter `deprecated: false`, default to frontier per provider (R#8).

| Tier | When | OPEN_AI | ANTHROPIC | GOOGLE_AI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Frontier** (default) | Best quality, no cost constraint | latest `gpt-5.x` | latest `claude-opus-4.x` | latest `gemini-3.x-pro` |
| **Balanced** | Good quality, moderate cost | `gpt-5` / `gpt-4.1` | `claude-sonnet-4.x` | `gemini-3-flash` |
| **Efficient** | High volume, cost-sensitive | `gpt-5-mini` / `gpt-4.1-mini` | `claude-haiku-4.x` | `gemini-3-flash` |

Downgrade ONLY when user signals cost/latency concern. A frontier model that TIMES OUT on structured output → LATERAL swap within the frontier tier (different provider/variant), not a downgrade. **Thinking level:** dialect-locked per R#8 — branch on `model.thinkingDialect` before setting `thinkingLevel`. Reference: `nexus-getting-started/reference/thinking-dialects.md`.

## I/O format matrix

| inputFormat | outputFormat | generation fields needed |
|---|---|---|
| text | text | `expectedInput`, `expectedOutput` |
| text | json | `expectedInput`, `jsonOutputSchema` |
| json | text | `jsonInputSchema`, `expectedOutput` |
| json | json | `jsonInputSchema`, `jsonOutputSchema` |
| text | template | `expectedInput`, `documentTemplateId` |
| json | template | `jsonInputSchema`, `documentTemplateId` |

Missing fields → 400.

## Multimodal input (image / PDF / video)

Native media ingestion needs BOTH halves or it silently no-ops:
1. **`multimodal: true` at body ROOT** on `task create` — defaults `false`, NOT auto-derived from declaring a media field in the schema. Settable later via `task update` (it's a scalar).
2. A **multimodal-capable model** (`nexus model list`; e.g. a Gemini vision model).

Declare the media field in `jsonInputSchema`. Without the root flag, even a capable model ignores the media — confirmable only via `task get` (`multimodal:false`) or a no-op execution.

## Task execute / get

```bash
**Volume check (BEFORE scripting a loop):** WHEN the same task/action will run ≥~15-20× (or any billed unit at volume) → STOP and AUQ: (a) a Nexus WORKFLOW [recommended — persistent, org-owned, re-runnable, visible, demoable; bulk default = the self-serving work-queue pattern] vs (b) a throwaway local script [one-shot seeding only, disclosed as such]. A bash/python loop shelling `task execute` is NOT exempt — it is the same billed bulk with none of the platform's value. The user building on Nexus is the point; scripts build on you.

```bash
nexus task execute <taskId> --input "..." --json                # text input
cat document.txt | nexus task execute <taskId> --input - --json # long text via stdin
nexus task execute <taskId> --input '{"field":"value"}' --json  # json input
nexus task get <taskId> --json                                  # detail — returns prompt + schemas at TOP level (generation: null)
```

Response: `{"output": <text|object>, "outputType": "text|json"}`. Execution synchronous.

## Modifying an existing task prompt

Editing a LIVE AI task's prompt (or its I/O schema) is scan-heavy + trap-laden → **dispatch the `task-prompt-modifier` agent (R#46), FOREGROUND**, passing ONLY `{taskId, change_request, prior_qa?, approved_plan?}`. It runs the Cue task-modification doctrine (task-boundary feasibility · full-prompt scan · region-consolidation · exact-match edits on a local copy · update · verify-via-execute) and returns ONE of: `done` · `needs_clarification` · `plan_for_approval` · `infeasible` · `blocked`.
- Non-`done` → AUQ the user with the returned questions/plan, then re-dispatch with `prior_qa`/`approved_plan` (the modifier has no AskUserQuestion — it asks THROUGH you).
- **No draft/publish:** `task update` is immediately LIVE. The modifier edits + verifies via a `task execute` sentinel and returns; **YOU own the post-edit eval** — `Skill(nexus-evaluations)` TASK-eval; revert = re-`task update` with the prior prompt.
- Do NOT edit a live task prompt inline yourself — you will miss the output-contract line / enum / examples the scan catches. CREATION of a new task routes to PA (R#31), never the modifier.
- Fallback if the named agent isn't loaded: `general-purpose` + "Read `.claude/agents/task-prompt-modifier.md` COMPLETELY and follow it".

Verified CLI shape: `task get <id> --json` → prompt + schemas at TOP level (`generation` null on GET). Edit a local copy; PROMPT-ONLY → `task update <id> --prompt <file>` (avoids the outputFormat trap); PROMPT+SCHEMA → `--body` with `prompt` at ROOT + `outputFormat` LOWERCASE `"json"` at ROOT (GET returns `"JSON"` — echoing it 400s) + schemas under `generation:{}` (flat field-maps). VERIFY: re-`task get` (prompt changed, `jsonOutputSchema` not `{}`) + `task execute <id> --input <sentinel>` (update returns a thin `{success,id}` — re-GET + execute are load-bearing).

## Document Templates

| Op | Command |
|---|---|
| Create (metadata) | `nexus template create --name "Sales Proposal" --body '{"description":"…","type":"WORD_TEMPLATE"}' --json` |
| Upload file | `nexus template upload <templateId> --file ./proposal.docx` |
| Generate | `nexus template generate <templateId> --body '{"variables":{"customerName":"Acme","items":["A","B"]}}' --json` |
| List / get | `nexus template list --search "…" --limit 20 --json` ; `nexus template get <templateId> --json` |
| Folders (organize + assign) | `nexus template folder list/create/update/delete/assign` → [`reference/template-folders.md`](reference/template-folders.md) — SKILL folders (tasks/workflows) are a separate namespace: `/skill-folders` → [`reference/skill-folders.md`](reference/skill-folders.md) |

Types: `WORD_FORMAT` / `WORD_TEMPLATE` / `WORD_CONTENT` / `POWERPOINT_TEMPLATE` / `EXCEL_TEMPLATE`. `generate` → `{"url":"…"}` = TEMPORARY link. ✗ generate then save URL for later → expires → ✓ generate → download immediately → re-generate when needed.

## External tools — operate existing

> NEW tool from OpenAPI spec? → `nexus-tool-connection/reference/custom-tool-integration-guide.md`.

| Op | Command |
|---|---|
| List | `nexus external-tool list --search "weather" --limit 20 --json` |
| Get detail | `nexus external-tool get <externalToolId> --json` |
| Upload icon | `nexus external-tool upload-icon <externalToolId> --file <path.png> --json` |
| Execute action | `nexus external-tool execute <externalToolId> --action <operationId> --input '{…}' [--credential <credId>] --json` |
| Create | `nexus external-tool create --body <file.json> --json` (file form always — large-body trap) |

Execute response: `{"status":"success","output":{…},"executionTimeMs":342}` OR `{"status":"error","error":"…","output":null}`. **Envelope `status: success` only means Nexus endpoint returned 200** — parse `result.os[].k === "error"` for upstream failures (R#20 + G#9). Full procedure → `nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`.

**Auth types — mechanism reference. Decision rubric → integration guide Step 4e.**

| Type | Required fields |
|---|---|
| `none` | — |
| `service_http` | `apiKey`, `authorization_type` |
| `user_http` | `authorization_type` |
| `oauth` | `grant_type`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `client_url`, `authorization_url` |
| `user_oauth` | `grant_type` |
| `keys` | — |

`authorization_type` (HTTP): `basic`/`bearer`/`custom`. `custom` → `custom_header_name` (+ optional `custom_header_prefix`). Permission scoping → `nexus-tool-connection` Access Cards. Pass `--credential` for `user_http`/`oauth`; omit for `service_http`.

## Collections (brief)

Browse + create only. Document management → `nexus-knowledge-base`.

```bash
nexus collection list --search "support" --limit 20 --json
nexus collection create --name "support-kb" --display-name "Support KB" --k 10 --json
nexus collection attach-documents <collectionId> --document-ids "doc-1,doc-2"
```

## Workflows (read-only via skills)

```bash
nexus api GET /skills/workflows --query search=order --query limit=10 --query offset=0 --json
nexus api GET /skills/workflows/<workflowId> --json
```

Detail includes `agentInputSchema` (JSON schema agent passes when invoking). Build/modify → `nexus-workflow-builder`.

## Browse + pagination

Skills list commands → `--offset` / `--limit` (NOT `--page` / `--limit`, per CLAUDE.md §API Envelopes). `--search "…"` accepted by any list. Example: `nexus task list --search "summary" --limit 20 --json`.

## Attaching skills to agents

| Skill | Agent tool type | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow | `WORKFLOW` | `nexus agent-tool create <agentId> --label "…" --type WORKFLOW --body '…'` |
| AI Task | `TASK` | `nexus agent-tool create <agentId> --label "…" --type TASK --body '…'` |
| Collection | `COLLECTION` | `nexus agent-tool attach-collection <agentId> --collection-id <id>` |
| External Tool | `PLUGIN` | Tool config (→ `nexus-agent-management`) |

Full attachment patterns → `nexus-agent-management`.

## General-context integration

Surface/mounts/multi-writer/path-resolution → `nexus-workspaces`; FUSE → R#39. Env/auth/envelopes/dashboard → CLAUDE.md.

| Trigger | Mode | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Existing tasks in target system / cross-system patterns / domain glossary | read | `/systems/<sys>/tasks/*.md` (grep) · `/knowledge/patterns/ai-tasks/*.md` · `/knowledge/glossary.md` |
| Body-shape failure mode (silent prompt drop / nested-array crash / schema subset surprise) | pulse | `/knowledge/learnings/ai-task-creation.md` (append H2) |
| Sentinel-input pattern (small load-bearing test payload that surfaces shape bugs) | pulse | `/knowledge/patterns/ai-tasks/sentinel-inputs.md` (append H2) |
| Model-tier selection lesson (Sonnet vs Haiku per task complexity) | pulse | `/knowledge/patterns/model-tier-selection.md` (append H2) |
| **Cross-org** AI task body-shape pattern | pulse | `$SYSTEMS_PATH/workflows/<pattern>/lessons.md` (append H2) |
| **Cross-org** task attachment pattern (per archetype) | pulse | `$SYSTEMS_PATH/agents/<archetype>/tools.md` (append H2) |
| Task created (system-bound) | final | `/systems/<sys>/tasks/<task-name>.md` (lazy-create `tasks/`, `templates/prompt-rule.md`) |
| Task created (cross-system / generic) | final | `/knowledge/patterns/ai-tasks/<task-name>.md` (new-file) |
| Failure mode discovered (silent schema-drop / model-mismatch silent fail) | final | `/knowledge/learnings/ai-task-<topic>.md` (append H2, `templates/learning.md`) |

✗ Task spec only in dashboard, no workspace doc → next conv rebuilds from `task get` → ✓ doc at `/systems/<sys>/tasks/<task>.md` w/ `task_id` frontmatter; next conv Reads first.

## Gotchas

1. **Task execution is synchronous** — response = output directly.
2. **`generation` object required** when creating tasks, even if subfields optional.
3. **Workflows read-only via skills commands** → `nexus-workflow-builder` to modify.
4. **`modelProvider` must match `modelName`** (e.g., `gpt-4o` w/ `OPEN_AI`).
5. **`service_http` stores key server-side**; `user_http` requires per-user keys.
6. **`operationId` for external tool testing** comes from OpenAPI spec operations.
7. **`task get` returns the full `prompt` + `jsonInputSchema`/`jsonOutputSchema` at TOP level** — `generation` is null in GET. `task create` nests the schemas under `generation:{}`; GET flattens them out, so parse GET at the top level, never under `.generation`.
8. ‼ **`jsonOutputSchema` silently drops to `{}` unless `outputFormat:"json"` is at the body ROOT** — put `outputFormat` under `generation`, omit it, or miscase it (`"JSON"`) and `task create`/`task update` return `success:true` with NO error but an EMPTY schema (R#20 SILENT ACCEPTANCE). Always re-GET after create/update to confirm the schema persisted.

## User-facing questions

Every Q → AUQ (R#3). Design → `nexus-getting-started/reference/clarification-guide.md`.

| Question category | Pre-populate from |
|---|---|
| Task input format (text / json / image) | Domain-fixed short list. Image/PDF inputs → manifest paths from CLAUDE.md "Attached files" via `PIL.Image.open` / `pdfplumber.open` per MIME table. |
| Task output format (text / json / template) | Domain-fixed short list |
| Existing task to reuse | `nexus task list --json` |
| Model tier (frontier / balanced / efficient) | `nexus model list --json` filtered by tier |
| Template type | Domain-fixed enum |

# Skills and Tasks CLI Reference

All commands require authentication via `nexus auth login` or the `NEXUS_API_KEY` environment variable.
Add `--json` to any command to get machine-readable JSON output.
All list commands use `offset`/`limit` pagination (not `page`/`limit`).

---

## 1. Workflows (2 commands -- via fallback)

### List Workflows

```bash
nexus api GET /skills/workflows --query search=keyword --query limit=20 --query offset=0 --json
```

| Param  | Type   | Required | Notes               |
| ------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------- |
| search | string | no       | Search by name      |
| limit  | number | no       | Default 20, max 100 |
| offset | number | no       | Default 0           |

**Response:**

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "Order Processor",
      "description": "Processes incoming orders",
      "status": "PUBLISHED",
      "triggerType": "AGENT_INPUT",
      "iconUrl": null,
      "agentInputSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "orderId": { "type": "string" },
          "action": { "type": "string" }
        }
      },
      "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "total": 5
}
```

Only returns published workflows visible as skills.

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized

---

### Get Workflow

```bash
nexus api GET /skills/workflows/<workflowId> --json
```

**Response:** Full workflow summary with `agentInputSchema`.

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not found

---

## 2. AI Tasks (4 commands)

### List Tasks

```bash
nexus task list [--search <query>] [--limit <N>] --json
```

| Flag     | Type   | Required | Notes               |
| -------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------- |
| --search | string | no       | Search by name      |
| --limit  | number | no       | Default 20, max 100 |

**Response:**

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "Email Classifier",
      "description": "Classifies emails by urgency",
      "category": "GENERATION",
      "inputFormat": "text",
      "outputFormat": "json",
      "modelProvider": "OPEN_AI",
      "modelName": "gpt-4o",
      "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",

# Skills + Tasks — Gotchas

Domain-specific gotchas for AI tasks, document templates, and external-tool ops via `nexus-skills-and-tasks`. Cross-skill rules → CLAUDE.md Operating Rules + Universal Gotchas. PA-related gotchas → `nexus-prompt-assistant/SKILL.md`.

## 1. Task `prompt` field placement (CREATE silent-drop — R#20)

`nexus task create` accepts `prompt` ONLY at body ROOT. Nested under `generation` → silently dropped. POST returns 200 + new `id`, but `task execute` fails at runtime w/ `"Prompt is required"`. GET doesn't expose `prompt` (re-fetch is a no-op). Validator only enforces REQUIRED fields under `generation`; it does NOT report fields ACCEPTED-and-IGNORED elsewhere. Permanent orphan if missed (no PATCH or DELETE on public API).

WRONG: `nexus task create --body '{"name":"X", ..., "generation":{"prompt":"...","jsonInputSchema":{...},"jsonOutputSchema":{...}}}'`.
RIGHT: `nexus task create --body '{"name":"X","prompt":"...","modelName":"...","inputFormat":"json","outputFormat":"json","generation":{"jsonInputSchema":{...},"jsonOutputSchema":{...}}}'`.

**Verification:** immediately after create returns id, `nexus task execute <new-id> --input <sentinel>` — verify response contains structured output. Only then wire the task into agents/WFs.

## 2. JSON schema format — flat field definitions, NOT JSON Schema wrapper

Task `jsonInputSchema` / `jsonOutputSchema` expect FLAT field definitions, NOT JSON Schema `{"type":"object","properties":{...}}` wrapper.

WRONG: `"jsonInputSchema": {"type":"object","properties":{"email":{"type":"string"}}}`
RIGHT: `"jsonInputSchema": {"email":{"type":"string"}}`

### 2b. Restricted JSON-Schema subset on `jsonOutputSchema`

`aiTask.jsonOutputSchema` accepts a **restricted** subset of JSON-Schema. Empirically:

| Shape | Status |
|---|---|
| `{type:"string"}` / `{type:"number"}` / `{type:"boolean"}` | ✓ |
| `{type:"object", properties:{...}}` w/ scalar leaf types | ✓ |
| `{type:"array", items:{type:"string"}}` | ✓ |
| `{type:"array", items:{type:"object", properties:{...}}}` | ✗ **500 at execute** |
| `{type:"object", properties:{...}}` w/o `properties` declared | ✗ (CLAUDE.md G#13) |

Workaround for unsupported nested array-of-objects: declare as `{type:"string", description:"JSON-encoded array of {f1,f2,...} objects"}` — downstream consumer `JSON.parse`s.

WRONG: `{availability:{type:"array",items:{type:"object",properties:{...}}}}` → 500 at execute → orphan.
RIGHT: `{availability:{type:"string",description:"JSON array of {date, slots}"}}` → string carrying parseable JSON → downstream parse.

Cross-skill suspect (verify before relying): `parallelai` schemas, `customScript` outputFormat.

## 3. `inputFormat`/`outputFormat` — case-sensitive lowercase

Accepted: `text`, `json`. NOT `JSON`, `Text`, `String`.

## 4. Task `prompt` not returned by GET

`nexus task get <id>` returns metadata only — does NOT expose the `prompt` field even when set correctly. The CONTRACT for verification is RUNTIME EXECUTION (per R#20 SILENT ACCEPTANCE CREATE variant).

## 5. Task format matrix — combinations + required `generation` fields

| Input → Output | Required in `generation` |
|---|---|
| text → text | (none — prompt at root) |
| text → json | `jsonOutputSchema` |
| json → text | `jsonInputSchema` |
| json → json | `jsonInputSchema` + `jsonOutputSchema` |
| text → template | `templateId` |
| json → template | `jsonInputSchema` + `templateId` |

## 6. Task execution failure recovery (migrated from nexus-prompt-assistant/SKILL.md)

When `nexus task execute <task-id>` returns 500 or unexpected output on a task you JUST created via PA:

| Step | Action | Cost | Recoverable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Inspect the error | Read response. Validation error → fix input. 500 → next step. | Free | Yes |
| 2. Swap the model | Open task in dashboard, change `modelName`, save. Retry SAME task ID. | Free (no new task) | Yes |
| 3. Re-test | `nexus task execute <same-id>` with same input. | Free | — |
| 4. ONLY IF prompt or schema is wrong | Recreate via PA + `nexus task create`. Accept the orphan. | Permanent orphan | NO undo until DELETE endpoint ships |

WRONG: `nexus task execute <task-id>` returns 500 on a frontier model. First instinct: kick off PA sub-agent to recreate w/ different model. Sub-agent creates 6 probe/minimal-test tasks while debugging. All become permanent orphans (no DELETE API).
RIGHT: 500 on execute → tell user "swap the model on this task to <newer-model> in dashboard, retry same task ID". Recovery in 30s, zero orphans. Only escalate to recreation if model swap doesn't help.

WRONG (sub-agent driven): PA sub-agent hits model-specific 500. Creates `task_v2_shortprompt`, then `task_minimal`, then `task_gpt41` ×2, then `task_opus`, then `task_v3`. 7 orphans, dashboard cluttered, user cleans up via UI.
RIGHT: PA sub-agent prompt MUST forbid probe tasks (Sub-Agent Contract clause 3 — `nexus-prompt-assistant/SKILL.md`). Sub-agent diagnoses via `nexus task execute` on FINAL task only. If 500 → emit `[failure] reason=execution_500 model=<name>` + stop. Parent (or user) handles model swap; sub-agent does not retry by creating new tasks.

## 7. PA Gate — all NEW AI tasks via Prompt Assistant

Every new AI task routes through `nexus-prompt-assistant` BEFORE `nexus task create`. Per R#31 in CLAUDE.md.

## 8. Document Templates — generation requires structured input

`nexus template generate` expects structured `--input` matching template variables. Free-text input → empty/garbled output. See `template list` to find templates and `template get <id>` for the variable schema.

## 9. External tool ops in this skill = OPERATE existing tools

This skill is for operating tools ALREADY in your org. For NEW custom-API integration → `nexus-tool-connection` skill.

---

Back-refs:
- `nexus-skills-and-tasks/SKILL.md`
- CLAUDE.md Reference File Index
- `nexus-prompt-assistant/SKILL.md` (Sub-Agent Contract clause 3 cross-refs gotcha #6)

### Structured-output 500: bisect the SCHEMA on throwaway twins before blaming model or prompt
A per-provider 500 at execute with a JSON output schema is a SCHEMA-SHAPE bug until proven otherwise. Bisect on `zz_` throwaway tasks (delete after): (1) trivial prompt + full schema — 500? it's the schema, not the prompt; (2) drop the array-of-objects — passes? the array is the break; (3) drop/shrink the enum — passes? the enum size is. A nested array-of-objects whose property carries a large enum is the highest-risk shape. The identical schema often runs on another provider — a provider swap (`task update` model) is a legitimate escape, not a workaround smell.

### Task creation dedups on IDENTICAL prompt text
`task create` with a system prompt byte-identical to an existing task returns `Conflict: An AI task with this exact system prompt already exists`. Probe/twin tasks need a nonce line (a comment) varied per probe — or update the existing task instead of re-creating.

# Skill Folders

Organize skills (workflows and AI tasks) into folders. These operations use the fallback `nexus api` command since there are no dedicated CLI commands for skill folders.

Assignment happens AT CREATE TIME — a project's first platform resource creates/reuses the project folder, and every subsequent resource is assigned as it lands (the app-builder P3 rule); bulk refiling later is the recovery path, not the norm.

## List Folders

```bash
nexus api GET /skill-folders --json
```

Response includes all folders and all skill-folder assignments:

```json
{
  "folders": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "name": "Production",
      "iconUrl": null,
      "parentId": null,
      "createdAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": null
    }
  ],
  "assignments": [
    { "skillId": "skill-uuid", "folderId": "uuid" }
  ]
}
```

## Create Folder

```bash
nexus api POST /skill-folders --body '{ "name": "My Folder", "parentId": "uuid-or-null" }' --json
```

| Field    | Type   | Required | Notes                        |
| -------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------- |
| name     | string | yes      | Min 1 character              |
| parentId | uuid   | no       | Parent folder ID for nesting |

## Update Folder

```bash
nexus api PATCH /skill-folders/<folderId> --body '{ "name": "Renamed", "parentId": null }' --json
```

| Field    | Type        | Required | Notes                              |
| -------- | ----------- | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
| name     | string      | no       | Min 1 character if provided        |
| parentId | uuid / null | no       | Set parent or null to move to root |

## Delete Folder

```bash
nexus api DELETE /skill-folders/<folderId> --json
```

Skills assigned to the deleted folder are unassigned (not deleted).

Response: `{ "id": "uuid", "deleted": true }`

## Assign Skill to Folder

```bash
nexus api POST /skill-folders/assign --body '{ "skillId": "uuid", "folderId": "uuid-or-null" }' --json
```

| Field    | Type        | Required | Notes                                          |
| -------- | ----------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| skillId  | uuid        | yes      | Workflow or AI task ID                         |
| folderId | uuid / null | yes      | Target folder ID, or `null` to unassign        |

Response: `{ "skillId": "...", "folderId": "...", "assigned": true }`

To move a skill, call assign again with the new folder ID. To unassign, pass `"folderId": null`.

# Document Template Folders

Organize document templates into folders via the typed `nexus template folder` group (R#1: typed first; the raw `/document-template-folders` routes remain a fallback and return a composite `{folders, assignments}` shape, unlike the typed list).

## List

```bash
nexus template folder list --json      # → { "data": [ ...folders ] }
```

## Create

```bash
nexus template folder create --name "Proposals" [--parent-id <folderId>] --json
# → { "success": true, "id": "<folderId>" }
```

## Update

```bash
nexus template folder update <folderId> [--name "Renamed"] [--parent-id <id|null>] --json
```

`--parent-id null` moves the folder to root.

## Delete

```bash
nexus template folder delete <folderId>
```

## Assign a template

```bash
nexus template folder assign --template-id <templateId> --folder-id <folderId> --json
```

`--folder-id null` unassigns the template from any folder.

nexus-tickets.description: Translate user-described problems into structured `nexus ticket` calls.

files.content:
---
name: nexus-tickets
description: Reports bugs, requests features, and tracks issues on the Nexus platform. Tickets are created on Linear and can be managed via the CLI, API, SDK, or MCP tools. Use when the user encounters errors, wants to report bugs, request features, or manage existing tickets.
---

# Nexus Tickets — Bug Reports & Feature Requests

Translate user-described problems into structured `nexus ticket` calls.

## Before Filing (MANDATORY)

**Step 0 — Dedup search** (per CLAUDE.md R#10). Before filing, suggesting, OR investigating/building around a suspected platform-capability gap: `nexus ticket list --search '<keyword>' --json` (or broader: `nexus ticket list --limit 100 --json \| jq '.data[] \| select((.title // "") + " " + (.description // "") \| test("<re>"; "i"))'`). Related ticket exists → `nexus ticket comment <id> --body "..."`, do NOT file duplicate.

**Self-diagnosis gate (root R#10):** tool/API returned correct response + you misused it (didn't reference, ran twice, ignored answer) → DO NOT file. Behavioral bug, not platform. Acknowledge + fix your behavior.

Then verify root cause — many "bugs" are config errors.

| Signal | Action |
|---|---|
| HTTP 500 from any endpoint | File immediately — always server bug |
| HTTP 400 w/ clear validation msg | Fix your request, never file |
| HTTP 401 | Check API key, never file |
| HTTP 429 | Wait + retry, never file |
| HTTP 404 on resource you didn't create | Expected, never file |
| Runtime "Action not found"/"Task not found"/"Connection failed" | VERIFY FIRST |
| Node execution failure (possible misconfig) | VERIFY FIRST |
| Unexpected empty response | VERIFY FIRST |
| Integration / webhook not firing | NO bug filed without self-reproduction: `reproductionSteps` MUST carry (a) Cue's OWN endpoint hit / standalone `external-tool execute` AND (b) user-confirmed external setup ("did you paste the URL, on which calendar?"). Missing either → don't file. |

**Verification steps for ambiguous cases:**
1. Check input values — action ID, task ID, credential ID correct?
2. Try alternative values — known-good ID to isolate.
3. Ask user — they may know correct value (e.g., `operationId` for CUSTOM_MANIFEST tool).
4. File only after confirming issue persists w/ correct inputs.

✗ "Action not found" → immediately file ticket (root cause was wrong `operationId`: `chatCompletion` instead of `search`) → ✓ verify `operationId` via `external-tool test` or ask user → no ticket.

✗ 0 executions → "wrong calendar / platform bug" → file → ✓ ask user + POST the endpoint → real 410 surfaced → file w/ both in reproductionSteps.

**Standalone tool isolation.** Before filing a plugin/tool bug, repro w/ `nexus external-tool execute <toolId> --action <key> --input '<same input>' --credential <credId> --json`. Standalone fails identically → clean repro, attach to ticket. Standalone works → bug is in WF/agent wiring (variable refs, access-card scope), not the tool. Full procedure: `../nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`.

## Ticket Types + Priority

| Type | Use |
|---|---|
| `BUG` | Broken — API wrong status, UI crash, data loss |
| `FEATURE_REQUEST` | New capability needed |
| `IMPROVEMENT` | Enhance existing — better error msg, more fields, etc. |

| Priority | Use |
|---|---|
| `URGENT` | System down, blocking all work |
| `HIGH` | Blocks current task, no workaround |
| `MEDIUM` | Important but workaround exists |
| `LOW` | Cosmetic / minor |
| `NONE` | Default |

## Ticket CRUD

**Flag distinction (silent failures when wrong):** `--data` = JSON body on `ticket create`/`update`. `--body` = comment TEXT only (on `ticket comment`). Swapping → either rejected or comment text appears as malformed JSON.

**Every ticket Cue files carries the "CUE" label.** As of 2026-07 the public ticket API exposes NO labels surface (a `labels` array in `--data` is silently dropped; PATCH ignores it; GET returns none — probed): the interim mechanism is a FIRST comment `[CUE] — Cue-filed ticket` on every create (a labels-API feature request is tracked; retest + supersede this note when labels land, then set the real label). A Cue-filed ticket without the marker is mis-filed.

**Post-create identifier extraction.** `identifier` may be `null` immediately after `ticket create` (Linear short-code is populated async, ~5s). `ticket create` and `ticket get` both print a BARE object — no `data` wrapper — so read the field directly. Extract from URL: `IDENT=$(... --json \| jq -r '.url \| split("/") \| last')`. Or re-fetch after a brief delay: `nexus ticket get <id> --json \| jq '.identifier'`.

```bash
# Create — only --title required; type/priority/context highly encouraged
nexus ticket create --title "PATCH /agents/:id returns 500 for valid modelConfig" \
  --type BUG --priority HIGH \
  --data '{"context":{"endpoint":"/agents/abc-123","method":"PATCH","statusCode":500,
    "errorCode":"INTERNAL_ERROR","requestBody":"{...}","responseBody":"{...}",
    "reproductionSteps":"1. Create agent\n2. PATCH modelConfig\n3. Observe 500",
    "expectedBehavior":"200 w/ updated agent","actualBehavior":"500 PrismaClientValidationError"}}' --json

# List / search / filter
nexus ticket list --json
nexus ticket list --type BUG --priority HIGH --json
nexus ticket list --search "modelConfig" --json
nexus ticket list --status "In Progress" --json   # Linear state name, case-sensitive

# Get / update
nexus ticket get <ticketId> --json
nexus ticket update <ticketId> --priority URGENT --title "Updated title" --json

# Comments — --body is comment TEXT
nexus ticket comment <ticketId> --body "Root cause: enum validation rejects underscores."
echo "Long analysis..." | nexus ticket comment <ticketId> --body -
nexus ticket comments <ticketId> --json
```

**Status filter** uses Linear state names (case-sensitive): `Triage`, `Backlog`, `Todo`, `In Progress`, `In Review`, `Done`, `Canceled`, `Current Sprint`. CLI returns all unless `--status` set.

## Context Object

Always include as much context as possible. `context` is a JSON OBJECT nested inside `--data`, NOT a string.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| endpoint | string | API endpoint that triggered the issue |
| method | string | HTTP method (GET, POST, PATCH, etc.) |
| statusCode | number | HTTP status received |
| errorCode | string | Nexus error code from response |
| requestBody | string | Request body sent (secrets auto-stripped) |
| responseBody | string | Error response received |
| reproductionSteps | string | Step-by-step instructions |
| expectedBehavior | string | What should have happened |
| actualBehavior | string | What actually happened |
| environment | string | production / staging / etc. |
| sdkVersion | string | SDK or client version |
| agentId | string | Related agent UUID |

Request/response bodies are STRINGS — `JSON.stringify()` before including.

**Security auto-redaction:** fields matching `password`, `secret`, `token`, `apiKey`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `credential` are redacted before Linear. Still avoid raw creds in descriptions.

## Attachments

Visual evidence, recordings, logs, any file. Manifest paths from CLAUDE.md "Attached files" pass to `--file` directly — no `cp` / `mv`.

```bash
# Upload — typed command ONLY (`nexus api` has NO --file option)
nexus ticket attach <ticketId> --file screenshot-error.png --json
# → { success, id, filename, url, contentType, size, createdAt }

# List
nexus api GET /tickets/<ticketId>/attachments --json
# → { attachments: [...] }
```

For UI/dashboard bugs (white screen, broken layout, click doesn't work) → Playwright capture flow: `reference/visual-bug-reporting.md`.

## After Filing — Retest, Supersede, Evidence

Tickets are the PRIMARY artifact for specific platform defects; skill docs and KB rows carry only the GENERALIZED check/workaround doctrine, written as dated current-state. That split has a lifecycle:

- **Retest on request — and on next use.** When the user asks whether a bug is fixed (or the feature is next exercised after a fix window), re-run the ticket's own repro — ideally two independent ways (the original failing call + a variant). Confirmed FIXED → comment the evidence on the ticket, then SUPERSEDE the stale guidance the SAME session: every doc/KB row carrying the workaround gets a dated supersede note (append-style per root R#35 #1, never silent deletion) — a fixed bug's stale workaround guidance is itself a doc defect. Still broken → comment the fresh repro + date.
- **Priority follows the user.** "Set it as important" → `nexus ticket update <id> --priority HIGH` (or `URGENT`) same turn, + a comment saying why it was raised.
- **Minimal repro + control experiment.** The strongest ticket carries BOTH the failing call AND the adjacent call that SUCCEEDS (the control — e.g. the same config completing under a different execution path, a scratch-clone probe result). It localizes the defect for triage and proves the reporter's config is sound.
- **Failed artifacts as living evidence.** A failed run/resource that demonstrates the bug MAY be deliberately kept — with a stated reason to the user and the artifact ID on the ticket. Otherwise clean up test residue the user can see: their dashboard is part of the deliverable, and an unexplained FAILED artifact left visible is a defect of its own.
- **Where defect knowledge lands (routing).** Vendor/plugin quirks → the community tools KB under the vendor's REAL connector home (resolved via a live `tool search`), read before first use. Platform defects → the ticket carries the specifics (IDs, payloads, stack text); the owning skill doc carries only the generalized "what to test / what to check" doctrine, dated, superseded on retest. Never bake a ticket's specifics into a skill doc as permanent truth (root R#36 doc-completion gate).

✗ a bug verified FIXED on request → ticket commented, but three doc rows still teach the workaround → the next session pays the workaround tax on a healthy platform. ✓ verified-fixed two ways → ticket comment + the same session sweeps every row carrying the workaround with a dated supersede note.

## Reference

- Endpoint catalog → `reference/endpoints.md`
- Visual bug capture (Playwright) → `reference/visual-bug-reporting.md`

## Error Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `LINEAR_RATE_LIMITED` | Too many requests — wait 30s + retry |
| `LINEAR_UNAVAILABLE` | Linear API temporarily down |
| `TICKET_NOT_FOUND` | Doesn't exist / belongs to another org |
| `LINEAR_VALIDATION_ERROR` | Invalid data sent to Linear |

## Fallback

For ops not in typed CLI: `nexus api <METHOD> <PATH> --body '<json>'` (JSON body only — `nexus api` has no `--file`; file uploads go through the typed `nexus ticket attach <id> --file <path>`).

# Visual Bug Reporting w/ Playwright

Capture visual evidence for Nexus dashboard / frontend UI bugs where API context alone can't describe the problem. Use Playwright (via `web-browser` agent / MCP tools) to navigate, screenshot, extract console + network errors, then attach to a ticket.

Back-ref: `../SKILL.md` (Attachments section). Index: CLAUDE.md → Reference File Index.
Reviewing/iterating your OWN app build (not filing a bug) → `../../nexus-app-builder/references/dev-loop.md`.

## When to use

- UI rendering issues — layout broken, elements overlapping, wrong colors/styles
- Interaction bugs — click doesn't work, form doesn't submit, modal doesn't close
- State bugs — stale data after action, wrong page shown after nav
- Dashboard crashes — white screen, error boundary, frozen UI
- Any bug the user describes by what they SEE — screenshots prove the issue

## Step 1 — Navigate + capture

```
browser_navigate         → {dashboardUrl}/app/my-agents/{id}/tabs/prompt
browser_take_screenshot  → .playwright-mcp/bug-screenshot-{timestamp}.png

# Multi-step interactions: capture sequence
#   .playwright-mcp/screenshot-01-initial-state.png
#   .playwright-mcp/screenshot-02-after-action.png
#   .playwright-mcp/screenshot-03-error-state.png

browser_console_messages → extract JS errors (often reveals root cause)
browser_network_requests → extract 4xx / 5xx API calls from browser
```

Landing dir (probed 2026-07): a bare relative filename lands in the PROJECT ROOT (the MCP's cwd) — it does not vanish, but it litters the repo; the MCP's own artifacts (snapshots, defaults) land in `<project>/.playwright-mcp/`. Convention: prefix every filename with `.playwright-mcp/` so evidence lands with the MCP's artifacts, then `ticket attach` from that path. Browser-automation gotchas (profile lock, UA needs, landing dirs) live in the tools KB under the browser-automation vendor home — INDEX-resolved; read before first browser use (R#12).

## Step 2 — Create the ticket

```bash
nexus ticket create \
  --title "Dashboard crashes when saving agent with long prompt" \
  --type BUG --priority HIGH \
  --description "Agent prompt editor white-screens when saving prompt > 10,000 chars." \
  --data '{"context":{
    "endpoint":"/app/my-agents/{id}/tabs/prompt",
    "reproductionSteps":"1. Open prompt editor\n2. Paste 15,000 char prompt\n3. Click Save\n4. White screen",
    "expectedBehavior":"Prompt saves successfully",
    "actualBehavior":"White screen, console: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined",
    "environment":"production"}}' --json
```

## Step 3 — Attach the screenshots

```bash
nexus ticket attach <ticketId> --file screenshot-01-initial.png --json
nexus ticket attach <ticketId> --file screenshot-02-error.png --json
```

## Step 4 — Add console / network evidence as comment

```bash
nexus ticket comment <ticketId> --body "## Console Errors
\`\`\`
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'slice')
  at PromptEditor.tsx:142
\`\`\`

## Failed Network Requests
- POST /api/agents/abc-123 → 413 Payload Too Large"
```

## Agent-behavior bugs (not UI) → emulator

When the bug is in agent RESPONSES (wrong answers, tool invocation failures, unexpected convo flow), use the emulator — not Playwright. See `../../nexus-emulator/SKILL.md`.

```bash
nexus emulator session create <deploymentId> --json
nexus emulator send <deploymentId> <sessionId> --text "msg that triggers bug" --json
# Response includes debug: { modelUsed, tokensUsed, toolsInvoked, latencyMs } — paste into ticket context
nexus emulator scenario save --name "Bug repro: wrong tool invoked" \
  --session-id <sessionId> --deployment-id <deploymentId> --json
```

---
name: nexus-tool-connection
description: Discovers marketplace tools, connects OAuth and HTTP credentials, resolves dynamic dropdown options, manages org-wide credentials, and configures access cards (policy-based permission scoping) via the Nexus Public API v1. Use when the user asks to find tools, connect accounts (Google Sheets, Gmail, Slack, etc.), manage API keys, configure Pipedream integrations, manage credentials, or create access cards.

# Nexus Tool Connection

User describes plain-language need → translate to `nexus` CLI. Auth + envelope shape → CLAUDE.md.

## CLI Commands

```bash
# Discovery + connection
nexus tool search [--query] [--category] [--type] [--limit] [--json]   # no positional, no --offset
nexus tool get <toolId> [--json]
nexus tool credentials <toolId> [--json]
nexus tool connect <toolId> [--auth-type oauth|http] [--api-key-value <k>] [--body <json>] [--json]

# Direct action (no WF)
nexus external-tool execute <toolId> --action <key> [--input '{...}'] [--credential <id>] [--json]

# Org-wide credentials
nexus credential list [--source oauth_connection|http] [--status CONNECTED|EXPIRED] [--json]
nexus credential get|update|delete <id> [--name "X"] [--json]

# Access cards
nexus access-card list|get|create|update|delete [<id>] [--credential-id <id>] [--data <json>] [--json]
nexus access-card available-actions --credential-id <id> [--json]
```

Passthrough (no typed CLI): OAuth status polling, resolve-options, manual credential create → `nexus api`.

## Quick Start — OAuth Connect

7-step walkthrough w/ concrete commands → [`reference/oauth-flow-example.md`](reference/oauth-flow-example.md).

## Custom API Integration (OpenAPI Tools)

Tool not in marketplace OR marketplace tool missing required action → lifecycle owner = [`reference/custom-tool-integration-guide.md`](reference/custom-tool-integration-guide.md). Canonical 6-step procedure (source spec → marketplace check → gap analysis → build → test → attach). Read BEFORE `nexus external-tool create`. **Fixing/updating an existing tool** (not in marketplace, or a misconfigured action) → same guide, "## Updating an existing custom tool" (`external-tool update`, in place, no re-attach).

**No marketplace tile?** Prefer the vendor's API → MCP → CLI (that order) before any browser automation (CLAUDE.md Universal Gotcha "external-system access ladder"). A rung is left only when its capability space is EMPIRICALLY exhausted (a filed limitation is an R#24 probe trigger, not an exit pass); interactive auth (device-code/OAuth-consent) is UI-class, same opt-in bar as the browser rung.

## Tool Discovery

| Operation | Command | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| Search marketplace | `nexus tool search --query "gmail" --limit 20 --json` | `tools[]`, `facets[]`, `total` |
| Get tool detail | `nexus tool get <toolId> --json` | `id`, `authType` (`oauth`/`http`/null), `actions[]` w/ `key`/`parameters[]` |
| List tool credentials | `nexus tool credentials <toolId> --json` | `credentials[{id,name,type,createdAt}]` |
| List org skills | `nexus api GET /tools/skills --query type=WORKFLOW --query search=X --query limit=20 --json` | WFs / AI tasks / collections |

`parameters[]` w/ `remoteOptions:true` → resolve dynamically (see below). Multi-credential → AUQ per R#3/R#4, never auto-select.

## Direct Tool Execution

Verify action works before attaching to agent — no throwaway WF (~3s vs full WF cycle).

```bash
# Pipedream — action by key | CUSTOM_MANIFEST — action by operationId
nexus external-tool execute google_sheets --action add-single-row --input '{"spreadsheetId":"...","sheetName":"Sheet1","values":{"name":"Alice"}}' [--credential cred-uuid] --json
nexus external-tool execute my-custom-api --action listUsers --input '{"limit":10}' --json
```

`--credential` omitted → auto-resolves first (use AUQ if multiple, per R#3). Test attached agent tool: `nexus api POST /agents/<agentId>/tools/<toolConfigId>/test --body '{"input":{...}}' --json`.

## Tool Connection Flows

!! Before any connect: Read `reference/auth-flows.md` (3 patterns + full flow diagrams). !!

Secret handling: the key VALUE never rides argv (persists in shell history + transcript) — put it in a chmod-600 temp file and `--body`/stdin it, or export an env var for the single call; delete after connect.

Keys: **Pipedream OAuth** → `tool connect <toolId> --auth-type oauth --body '{"service":"<pipedream-id>"}'` → present `authorizationUrl` to user → poll status every 3–5s until `COMPLETED` (credential auto-created) / `FAILED` (inspect `errorMessage`) / `EXPIRED` (~10min). **HTTP API key** → `--auth-type http --api-key-value "sk-…"` — created immediately, no browser flow, no polling. **Built-in OAuth** (Gmail, Notion, …) → same shape as Pipedream OAuth. `service` must match the Pipedream identifier exactly (`"google_sheets"` ≠ `"Google Sheets"`).

## Resolve Dynamic Options

Params w/ `remoteOptions: true` need runtime resolution (e.g., spreadsheet picker). No typed CLI → API passthrough.

```bash
nexus api POST /tools/<toolId>/resolve-options --body '{
  "componentId": "action-key",
  "propName": "spreadsheetId",
  "credentialId": "cred-uuid",
  "configuredProps": { /* prior selections — for cascading deps */ }
}' --json
# => { options: [{ label: "My Sheet", value: "sheet-id-123" }, ...] }
```

`configuredProps` carries already-selected parent values. Resolve parent BEFORE child.

For cascading dropdown resolution inside workflow plugin nodes → `nexus-workflow-builder/node-types/processing/plugin/GUIDE.md`.

## Credential + access-card lifecycle

`tool credentials <toolId>` = ONE tool's view; `credential list` = ALL org-wide. Same data, IDs interoperable.

```bash
# Manual credential create (after OAuth completes, if auto-creation didn't fire)
nexus api POST /tools/<toolId>/credentials --body '{"accountId":"pipedream-account-id","name":"My Google Account"}' --json
nexus api DELETE /tools/<toolId>/credentials/<credentialId> --json     # returns {deleted:true}, NOT 204

# Org-wide views
nexus credential list --status CONNECTED --json                        # all connected accounts
nexus credential list --source oauth_connection --json                 # filter source; --status EXPIRED for stale
nexus credential get|update|delete <id> [--name "Production Gmail"] --json

# Access cards — optional policy layer limiting what a credential can do (no card → full access)
nexus access-card available-actions --credential-id <credId> --json    # REQUIRED first step — don't guess actions
# policies is a MAP action id -> { parameters: { <param>: { enabled } } }, NOT a list of names.
# Unlisted action = denied. Unlisted parameter = STRIPPED from the call, so list every one you need.
nexus access-card create --credential-id <credId> --name "Send Only" \
  --data '{"policies":{"gmail-send-email":{"parameters":{"to":{"enabled":true},"subject":{"enabled":true},"body":{"enabled":true}}}}}' --json
nexus access-card list --credential-id <credId> --json   # --credential-id is REQUIRED
nexus access-card get|update|delete <cardId> --json
```

⚠ **`{"policies":{"allowedActions":[...]}}` is not a shape this API has.** It
validates — `allowedActions` is read as an action id — and the card then denies
every real action it was created to permit. Keys are action ids from
`available-actions` (`actionId`, verbatim), values are `{ "parameters": { … } }`.
`{}` is the master card (everything); `{"<actionId>":{}}` allows that action and
calls it with NO parameters. `"enabled": false` with a `"value"` pins a
parameter the caller cannot override.

⚠ **Delete blast radius:** deleting a credential removes it from all agents/WFs/deployments referencing it + deletes its attached access cards. Check `nexus access-card list --credential-id <id>` first.

E2E scoped setup: connect → `tool credentials` → `available-actions` → create card → attach to agent (→ `nexus-agent-management`).

## Gotchas

1. **`service` must match exactly** — `"google_sheets"` ≠ `"Google Sheets"`.
2. **Poll cadence 3–5s.** Auth URLs expire ~10min — check `expiresAt`.
3. **HTTP credentials create immediately** — no polling. **Delete returns 200 + `{deleted:true}`** (not 204).
4. **`remoteOptions:true` → resolve-options** — don't hardcode dynamic field values. Parent BEFORE child via `configuredProps`.
5. **Agent tool config field = `toolCredentialId`** — NOT `credentialId`.
6. **Pagination `offset`/`limit`** for tool search + skills (not `page`/`limit`).
7. **Access cards optional** — no card → full access. Always `available-actions` BEFORE create. Delete credential → deletes its cards.
8. **Per-tool + org views = same data** — IDs interoperable; `credential list` ID works as `toolCredentialId`.
