```bash
      },
      \"website\": {
        \"id\": \"ps-website\", \"type\": \"string\", \"handler\": \"variable\",
        \"variable\": \"{{$TRIGGER_ID.website}}\", \"value\": \"\", \"prompt\": \"\"
      }
    }
  }
}"

# 5. Create output node — pass through full parallelai output (content + citations)
OUT_ID=$(nexus workflow node create "$WF_ID" --type outputNode --json | jq -r '.id')

# IMPORTANT: Use outputType "previous" with "instructions" (NOT "output").
# "custom" mode invokes an LLM that will corrupt your structured JSON.
# See node-types/output/output-node/GUIDE.md for all three modes.
nexus workflow node update "$WF_ID" "$OUT_ID" --body "{
  \"data\": {\"outputType\": \"previous\", \"instructions\": \"{{$PAR_ID}}\", \"label\": \"enrichment_result\"}
}"

### Output Node Mode Selection (for parallelai workflows)

| You want to... | Use this mode | `instructions` value | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pass through full JSON (content + citations) | `"previous"` | `"{{parallelaiNodeId}}"` | No AI processing. Fastest. Use for agent-triggered workflows. |
| Return only the content fields | `"text"` | `"{{parallelaiNodeId.content}}"` | Template interpolation. No AI. Drops citations/basis. |
| Have AI summarize/reformat the research | `"custom"` | `"Summarize {{parallelaiNodeId.content}} into..."` | Adds 5-15s latency. Risk: AI may produce generic responses if instructions are vague. |

WRONG: `"outputType": "custom", "output": "{{nodeId.content}}"` — two bugs: field is `instructions` not `output`, and `"custom"` invokes AI.
RIGHT: `"outputType": "previous", "instructions": "{{nodeId}}"` — passthrough, correct field.

# 6. Wire edges
nexus workflow edge create "$WF_ID" --source "$TRIGGER_ID" --target "$PAR_ID"
nexus workflow edge create "$WF_ID" --source "$PAR_ID" --target "$OUT_ID"

# 7. Validate
nexus workflow validate "$WF_ID"

# 8. Test node
nexus workflow node test "$WF_ID" "$PAR_ID"
# NOTE: Node test returns an executionId, but it may NOT match the actual execution ID.
# Use `nexus execution poll` to wait for results, or list recent executions:
nexus execution list --json | jq '.data[0]'
# Then get the specific node result:
nexus execution node-result "<executionId>" "$PAR_ID" --json
```

## Action Types

### Task (most common)
Structured research: JSON input → JSON output matching `outputSchema`.
Best for: Company enrichment, person research, market intelligence.
You KNOW what entity you're researching — you provide name/website/linkedin and get structured data back.

### Search
Web search with objective + search queries. Returns `results[]` with `{url, title, excerpts, publish_date}`.
Params: `objective`, `searchQueries[]`, `mode` (e.g. "agentic"), `maxResults`, `includeDomains[]`, `excludeDomains[]`, `maxCharsPerResult`.
Cost: $5/1K. Best for: targeted queries, domain-specific searches, finding articles/sources.

### Task Groups
Batch: process an array of inputs with the same schema.
Cost: processor × batch size. CRITICAL: each array item must match exact input schema.
Best for: enriching a LIST of known entities (e.g., 50 companies to research).

### Extract
Content extraction from specific URLs. Returns `{results[], errors[], warnings[]}`.
Params: `urls[]`, `objective`, `searchQueries[]`. Options: `extractExcerpts`, `extractFullContent`.
Cost: $1/1K. Best for: scraping known pages — you have the URLs and want specific content.

### Find All
DISCOVERY engine — finds entities you DON'T already know about.
Params: `objective`, `entityType`, `matchConditions[]` (each with `{name, description}`), `matchLimit`.
Returns `{candidates[], run, last_event_id}`. Options: `findAllGenerator` tier, `enrichmentProcessor` tier.
Cost: Varies by generator tier ($0.10-$10/query + per-match cost).
Best for: "Find all AI startups in YC F25 batch", "Discover all PE funds in Belgium with healthcare focus", "List all companies using Salesforce in the Nordics".

**Key distinction**: Task/Search/Extract work on entities you ALREADY KNOW. Find All DISCOVERS new entities matching criteria.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Why Wrong | Do Instead |
|---------|----------|------------|
| Using JSON Schema format for outputSchema | parallelai uses flat `{fieldName: {id, type, description}}` not `{type: "object", properties: {...}}` | Use flat per-field format with id, type, description |
| Using `selectedAction` | That's for plugin nodes | Use `action: "task"` |
| Generic field descriptions | "The revenue" produces shallow results | Use 6-component structure with SEARCH, INFERENCE, FORMAT directives |
| No reasoning fields | Can't verify where data came from | Add `{field}_reasoning` companion for every value field |
| Defaulting to `pro` or `ultra` | 10-30x more expensive than needed | Start with `base` for ≤5 fields, `core` for ≤10 |
| Text input mode for structured data | Less precise, harder to map fields | Use `inputMode: "json"` with structured inputSchema |
| Not configuring output node | Workflow returns nothing useful | Set `outputType: "previous"` and `instructions: "{{parallelaiNodeId}}"` (NOT `output`, NOT `"custom"`) |
| Using `outputType: "custom"` on output node | "custom" invokes an LLM that corrupts structured JSON — you get generic AI responses instead of your research data | Use `outputType: "previous"` with `instructions: "{{parallelaiNodeId}}"` for passthrough |
| Using `parametersSchema` for trigger | Fields don't show in dashboard | Use `parameters` (not `parametersSchema`) for agent input trigger |

# Plugin (Integration Node)

## Node Type Identifier

`plugin`

## What It Does

Executes an action from an external tool integration (Pipedream or custom). This is the primary node for connecting workflows to third-party services like Google Sheets, Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot, and thousands of other integrations. Requires selecting a tool, an action, credentials, and configuring parameters.

## Required Fields in `data`

| Field            | Type     | Description                                                                             |
| ---------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toolId`         | `string` | The ID of the tool to use. Obtained from `nexus tool search --query "..." --json`.                 |
| `selectedAction` | `string` | The operation ID of the action to execute. Obtained from the tool's `userActions` list. |

## Optional Fields

| Field              | Type             | Description                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `toolCredentialId` | `string`         | Credential ID for authentication. Obtained from `nexus tool credentials <toolId> --json`.                                  |
| `instructions`     | `string`         | Natural language prompt for parameters using the `prompt` handler. Supports `{{nodeId.path}}` variable references. |
| `label`            | `string`         | Display label. Auto-populated from tool name.                                                                      |
| `parametersSetup`  | `ParameterSetup` | Auto-populated when `toolId` + `selectedAction` are both set.                                                      |
| `masked`           | `boolean`        | When `true`, node is skipped during execution (pass-through).                                                      |

## Default Data (set automatically on creation)

```json
{
  "additionalParameters": {},
  "parametersSetup": {},
  "label": "Plugin",
  "toolId": "",
  "instructions": "",
  "selectedAction": "",
  "toolCredentialId": ""
}
```

Read-only fields (set by backend): `appName`, `dynamicPropsId`, `additionalParameters`, `currentTab`, `selectTool`, `imageUrl`, `runOutput`, `testExecutionId`, `outputFormat`.

## Connection Rules

- Can be placed inside a loop: Yes
- Can be masked (skipped): Yes

## Pre-flight — Probe Action Standalone (MANDATORY before configuration)

Per `WORKFLOW_DESIGN_GUIDE.md` Failure-Mode Anticipation, every plugin action gets probe-tested via `nexus external-tool execute` BEFORE the node is configured. Catches three classes of failure: (1) Pipedream component has missing/wrong fields (e.g., a `*-create-note` action's `configurableProps` exposes only association fields, no body); (2) credential mismatch (credential exists but lacks scope for this specific action); (3) param-shape assumptions wrong (top-level vs nested).

```bash
RESULT=$(nexus external-tool execute "$TOOL_ID" --action "$ACTION_KEY" --credential "$CRED_ID" --input '<minimal probe>' --json 2>&1)
echo "$RESULT" | jq '{success: (.result.ret != null), errs: ([.result.os[]? | select(.k=="error")] | length)}'
```

If standalone probe fails: per R#14, ESCALATE with three options — (a) propose alternative action with WRONG/RIGHT side-by-side, (b) ask user to test from their side, (c) accept as documented debt. Do NOT silently swap actions.

**If the probe is inconclusive** (success: true but no useful response, empty `result.os`, or generic acknowledgement) — DO NOT skip. Treat inconclusive as "pre-flight failed." Re-probe with realistic parameters (look up required fields via `nexus tool get <toolId> --json | jq '.actions[] | select(.key=="<action>") | .parameters'` and fill in throwaway test values), OR ask the user to confirm parameter shape before proceeding.

**Credential scope verification** (after multi-credential selection). When the user picks a credential from a multi-credential list, verify the credential has the SCOPES needed for the planned action: `nexus tool credentials <toolId> --json | jq '.[] | select(.id=="<chosen>") | {scopes: (.scopes // .meta.scopes // null)}'`. If scopes are listed and don't include what the action needs (e.g., `chat:write:bot` for sending Slack DMs) → ask the user to either re-OAuth with broader scopes or pick a different credential.

WRONG: model configures plugin node with `selectedAction: <X>-create-note`, sets the body params at top-level. Workflow validation passes. At test time the action returns 400 — required field not set. Model iterates 5 turns inside the node config trying different shapes before realising the action is broken. Eventually swaps to a different engagement-type action silently.
RIGHT: BEFORE configuring the node, probe `nexus external-tool execute <X>-create-note --input '<minimal body>' --json`. Probe returns 400 with the exact missing-field error. Model fires AskUserQuestion: "`<X>-create-note` Pipedream component is broken (no body field exposed in `configurableProps`). Three options: (a) swap to `<X>-create-engagement` with `engagementType=notes` (verified working — slight semantic difference); (b) you set up a custom HTTP plugin from your side; (c) accept as debt and revisit. Which?"

## Configuration Steps

1. **Create the node** with `nexus workflow node create`.
2. **Connect it** to an upstream node.
3. **Search for a tool** with `nexus tool search --query "<query>" --json`.
4. **Set `toolId`** via `nexus workflow node update`.
5. **Get tool details** with `nexus tool get "<toolId>" --json` to find available actions.
6. **Set `selectedAction`** via `nexus workflow node update`. The backend auto-populates `parametersSetup` and sets `appName`.

> **CRITICAL: Steps 4, 6, and 8 must be SEPARATE `nexus workflow node update` calls, in order.**
> The backend auto-populates `parametersSetup` ONLY when `selectedAction` is set on a node that already has `toolId` from a prior update.
>
> WRONG (one update with everything — `parametersSetup` stays empty):
> ```json
> { "data": { "toolId": "...", "selectedAction": "...", "toolCredentialId": "..." } }
> ```
> RIGHT (sequential updates — auto-population fires):
> ```
> Update 1: nexus workflow node update "$WF_ID" "$NODE_ID" --body '{"data":{"toolId":"..."}}'
> Update 2: nexus workflow node update "$WF_ID" "$NODE_ID" --body '{"data":{"selectedAction":"..."}}'  ← triggers auto-population
> Verify:   nexus workflow node get "$WF_ID" "$NODE_ID" --json  ← confirm parametersSetup populated
> Update 3: nexus workflow node update "$WF_ID" "$NODE_ID" --body '{"data":{"toolCredentialId":"..."}}'
> ```
7. **Get or create credentials** with `nexus tool credentials "<toolId>" --json` or the tool connection flow.
8. **Set `toolCredentialId`** via `nexus workflow node update`.
9. **Reload dynamic props** (if needed) with `nexus workflow node reload-props`.
10. **Configure each parameter** in `parametersSetup`.
11. **Resolve remote options** (for dropdown-type parameters) with `nexus tool resolve-options`.
12. **Test the node** with `nexus workflow node test`.

## Example API Calls

### Step 1: Create the plugin node

```bash
nexus workflow node create "$WORKFLOW_ID" --type plugin --json
```

### Step 2: Connect to upstream node

```bash
nexus workflow edge create "$WORKFLOW_ID" --source "$UPSTREAM_NODE_ID" --target "$PLUGIN_NODE_ID"
```

### Step 3: Search for a tool

```bash
nexus tool search --query "google sheets" --json
```

### Step 4: Set the tool ID

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$PLUGIN_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "toolId": "tool_google_sheets_abc123"
  }
}'
```

### Step 5: Get tool details and find available actions

```bash
nexus tool get "tool_google_sheets_abc123" --json
```

The response includes a `userActions` array. Each action has an `operationId` to use as `selectedAction`.

### Step 6: Set the selected action (triggers auto-population)

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$PLUGIN_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "selectedAction": "add-single-row"
  }
}'
```

CRITICAL: After this update, the backend auto-sets `appName` and populates `parametersSetup`. Fetch the node to see the updated data:

```bash
nexus workflow node get "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$PLUGIN_NODE_ID" --json
```

### Step 7: Set credentials

First, check for existing credentials:

```bash
nexus tool credentials "tool_google_sheets_abc123" --json
```

If no credentials exist, start the connection flow:

```bash
nexus tool connect "tool_google_sheets_abc123" --json
```

Then set the credential on the node:

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$PLUGIN_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "toolCredentialId": "cred_xyz789"
  }
}'
```

**If multiple credentials exist for this tool:** ALWAYS present the list and ask the user which to use. Never auto-select — different credentials may be connected to different workspaces, accounts, or team members.

```bash
nexus tool credentials "$TOOL_ID" --json
# Returns: [
#   { "id": "cred-1", "name": "Slack (Assem)", "createdAt": "2026-02-27" },
#   { "id": "cred-2", "name": "Slack (Marketing)", "createdAt": "2025-11-18" },
#   { "id": "cred-3", "name": "Slack (Legacy)", "createdAt": "2025-11-11" }
# ]
# → Ask: "You have 3 Slack credentials. Which one should I use?"
# → User picks → set toolCredentialId with their choice
```

WRONG: Multiple credentials exist → silently pick the most recent → it's connected to the wrong Slack workspace → messages go to the wrong team.
RIGHT: Present the list with dates → user says "use the Marketing one" → set `cred-2`.

### Step 8: Reload dynamic props (for parameters that depend on other parameters)

For parameters whose options depend on previously configured values (e.g., selecting a specific spreadsheet before choosing a sheet tab):

```bash
nexus workflow node reload-props "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$PLUGIN_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "configuredProps": {
    "googleSheets": "'"$CREDENTIAL_ACCOUNT_ID"'",
    "drive": "My Drive",
    "sheetId": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms"
  }
}'
```

This returns updated `parametersSetup` with new dynamic fields revealed (e.g., specific sheet tabs, column names).

> **When is reload-props needed?**
> Only for actions with **cascading dynamic parameters** — selecting one parameter reveals others. After setting `selectedAction` and fetching the node, check if `dynamicPropsId` is present in the response:
> - `dynamicPropsId` present → call reload-props with `configuredProps`
> - `dynamicPropsId` null/absent → skip reload-props, configure parameters directly
>
> Typical dynamic: Google Sheets (drive→spreadsheet→tab), Slack (workspace→channel), HubSpot (object→fields).
> Typical static: Gmail Find Email, Gmail Create Draft, simple single-parameter actions.
>
> **"additionalProps not a function" error** = the action has no dynamic props. Not a bug — skip reload-props and proceed to configure parameters directly.

### Step 9: Configure parameters

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$PLUGIN_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "parametersSetup": {
      "drive": {
        "id": "param-uuid-1",
        "type": "string",
        "handler": "manual",
        "value": "My Drive",
        "prompt": "",
        "variable": ""
      },
      "sheetId": {
        "id": "param-uuid-2",
        "type": "string",
        "handler": "manual",
        "value": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms",
        "prompt": "",
        "variable": ""
      },
      "sheetName": {
        "id": "param-uuid-3",
        "type": "string",
        "handler": "manual",
        "value": "Sheet1",
        "prompt": "",
        "variable": ""
      },
      "row_values": {
        "id": "param-uuid-4",
        "type": "object",
        "handler": "variable",
        "value": "",
        "prompt": "",
        "variable": "{{UPSTREAM_NODE_UUID.body}}"
      }
    }
  }
}'
```

### parametersSetup Key Names — Discover From Platform, Never Guess

parametersSetup key names MUST match the Pipedream component's internal prop names. These often differ from the external service's API naming:
- Google Sheets API: `spreadsheetId` → Pipedream: `sheetId`

**How to discover correct key names:**
1. **Auto-populated parametersSetup** — after setting `selectedAction`, fetch the node. Keys appear even with empty values.
2. **reload-props response** — `configurableProps[].name` gives the exact prop names.
3. **Sibling action on the same tool** — e.g., `update-multiple-rows` shows `sheetId` → `create-worksheet` likely uses the same.

WRONG: Guess from API docs: `{"spreadsheetId": {"id": "p-1", "type": "string", "handler": "manual", "value": "1hFe5P..."}}` → Pipedream ignores unknown keys. Silent failure or "Missing required parameters."
RIGHT: Discover from platform: `{"sheetId": {"id": "p-1", "type": "string", "handler": "manual", "value": "1hFe5P..."}}`.

### Step 10: Resolve remote options (for dropdown parameters)

For parameters with `constraints.remoteOptions: true`, fetch allowed values dynamically:

```bash
nexus tool resolve-options "tool_google_sheets_abc123" --body '{
  "propName": "sheetName",
  "configuredProps": {
    "googleSheets": "'"$CREDENTIAL_ACCOUNT_ID"'",
    "drive": "My Drive",
    "sheetId": "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgVE2upms"
  },
  "credentialId": "'"$TOOL_CREDENTIAL_ID"'"
}' --json
```

### Step 11: Test the node

```bash
nexus workflow node test "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$PLUGIN_NODE_ID" --json
```

## Common Patterns / Tips

- **CRITICAL: `appName` must be camelCase** derived from the tool's `configurableProps`, not the action slug. For example, `"googleSheets"` not `"google_sheets"`. The backend auto-sets `appName` when `selectedAction` is updated via `nexus workflow node update` -- do NOT set it manually. It is a read-only field.
- **`toolCredentialId` is the correct field name**, not `credentialId`. The frontend reads `toolCredentialId`.
- **The full lifecycle is: select tool -> select action -> auto-populate params -> set credentials -> reload-props -> configure params -> test.** Skipping steps (especially reload-props) can leave parameters in an invalid state.
- **`reload-props` may need to be called multiple times.** Each call with new `configuredProps` may reveal additional dynamic fields. For example: first call with `drive` reveals `sheetId` options, second call with `sheetId` reveals `sheetName` options.
- **Every `parametersSetup` entry MUST include `id` as a non-empty string.** Omitting it causes publish to fail:
  ```
  Invalid parametersSetup in node "...", parameter "...": "id" is required and must be a non-empty string.
  ```
  All fields must be present: `id` (non-empty string), `type` (string/number/boolean/object/array), `handler` ("manual"/"prompt"/"variable"), `value` (for manual), `prompt` (for prompt), `variable` (for variable).
  WRONG: `{ "title": { "handler": "manual", "value": "My Sheet" } }` — missing `id`, `type`, `prompt`, `variable`.
  RIGHT: `{ "title": { "id": "p-title", "type": "string", "handler": "manual", "value": "My Sheet", "prompt": "", "variable": "" } }`
  Best practice: after `reload-props` returns parametersSetup entries, PRESERVE the returned `id` and `constraints`. Only change `handler` + the corresponding value field.
- **Parameters with `constraints.remoteOptions: true`** must have their values fetched via `nexus tool resolve-options`. These are typically dropdown selects (spreadsheet names, channel names, etc.).
- **Integer `0` is a valid value.** When checking parameter values, use `!= null` not `||` -- otherwise `0` is treated as empty.
- **`manual` handler `{{ref}}` interpolation depends on upstream `outputFormat`.** If the referenced upstream node has never been tested successfully (or its last test produced an error), `{{UUID.field}}` in `manual` handler values resolves as a LITERAL STRING — the platform sends the raw `{{uuid.field}}` text as-is to the external service (e.g., Slack receives `{{518f021a-8387-4d90-850b-1eb88bda9fa2.text}}` as the message body, email sends with template variables visible to the recipient). No error is raised anywhere. The debugging path is deceptive: switching to `variable` handler may produce type errors (the target expects a string, variable passes the whole object), leading you to think `manual` is the wrong handler — but the real issue is the upstream node's `outputFormat` being empty. Fix: always test upstream nodes individually and verify `outputFormat` is populated BEFORE configuring downstream manual handler references.

## CUSTOM_MANIFEST Tools (Non-Pipedream)

CUSTOM_MANIFEST tools are custom API integrations defined by OpenAPI specs. They work in plugin nodes but differ from Pipedream plugins in important ways.

### Action Discovery

CUSTOM_MANIFEST tools may return an empty `actions` array from `nexus tool get <toolId> --json` even when `totalActions > 0`. When this happens:

1. **Ask the user for the operationId.** They can find it in the Nexus dashboard under the tool's configuration, or they know it from setting up the tool.
2. **Try `nexus external-tool test <toolId> --operation-id <guess>` to verify** — if the operationId is wrong, the test will fail.

WRONG: Guessing the operationId and assuming it's correct because the `nexus workflow node update` to set `selectedAction` succeeded. The backend accepts any string — it only validates at execution time.
RIGHT: Asking the user for the correct operationId, or testing with `nexus external-tool test` before wiring it into the workflow.

### Configuration Differences

| Aspect | Pipedream Plugin | CUSTOM_MANIFEST Tool |
|--------|-----------------|---------------------|
| Action discovery | `nexus tool get` returns `actions[]` | May return empty — ask user |
| `reload-props` | Works — reveals dynamic parameters | Does NOT work — returns 404/500 |
| `resolve-options` | Works for dropdown parameters | Does NOT work |
| Credentials | `toolCredentialId` required | Often `authType: "none"` — no credential needed |
| Parameters | Auto-populated after `reload-props` | Must be configured manually — ask the user for parameter names and types |

### Configuration Steps for CUSTOM_MANIFEST Tools

1. Set `toolId` via `nexus workflow node update`.
2. **Ask the user** for the action operationId and parameter names/types.
3. Set `selectedAction` via `nexus workflow node update`.
4. Manually configure `parametersSetup` with the user-provided parameter names.
5. Test the node to verify it works.

## Variable References

The `instructions` field supports inline variable references:

```
Add the following data to the spreadsheet: {{UPSTREAM_NODE_UUID.body}}
```

Each `parametersSetup` entry supports variable references:

- **`handler: "variable"`** -- put the reference in the `variable` field: `"{{nodeUUID.path}}"`
- **`handler: "prompt"`** -- put a natural language prompt in the `prompt` field (can contain `{{...}}` references)

### Choosing the Right Handler Per Parameter

Every parameter in `parametersSetup` needs a handler. The handler determines HOW the value is resolved at runtime.

- **`manual`** — Hardcoded value. **Strings CAN include `{{references}}` inline** — the platform interpolates them. Use for ALL string fields, even when they contain dynamic upstream references. Also use for arrays of hardcoded entries.
- **`variable`** — Full passthrough of an object, array, number, or boolean from upstream. No interpolation — the entire value is passed as-is. Use for complex-type fields.
- **`prompt`** — Lightweight AI task. The agent decides ALL prompt-mode parameters at once at runtime using the node's `instructions` field. Each parameter has its own `description`. Use ONLY when genuine AI judgment is needed.

**Handler choice is NODE-TYPE-SPECIFIC** — the rule below applies to `plugin` nodes (this file's scope). **`aiTask` nodes follow a different rule: ALL upstream-referenced fields, including strings, use `variable`** (see `ai-node/GUIDE.md`). The reason they differ: aiTask uses a unified resolver (variable-fetch-then-prompt-construction); plugin nodes use Pipedream's prop-interpolation engine, which expects strings as `manual` with inline `{{}}` references.

**For `plugin` nodes:**

| Field type | Handler |
|---|---|
| String, no upstream reference | `manual` with literal value |
| String, with upstream reference (`{{nodeUUID.field}}`) | `manual` with the reference inline (Pipedream interpolates) |
| Object / array / number / boolean from upstream | `variable` with the reference in `variable` field |
| AI judgment needed | `prompt` |

**Special case — boolean/number LITERALS (not from upstream):** Use `handler: "manual"` with `value: true` (boolean) or `value: 42` (number). The `manual` handler passes the `value` field as-is — it supports any JSON type, not just strings. Only use `variable` when the boolean/number comes FROM an upstream node's output.

WRONG: `{ "mrkdwn": { "handler": "variable", "variable": "true" } }` — passes the STRING "true", not the boolean `true`.
RIGHT: `{ "mrkdwn": { "handler": "manual", "value": true } }` — passes the boolean `true`.

WRONG: Using `handler: "prompt"` for a `worksheetId` from upstream. Prompt is a lightweight AI task — the agent hallucinates IDs instead of passing real values.
RIGHT: `worksheetId` is a number → use `handler: "variable"` with the exact field path from `nexus execution node-result`.

WRONG: Using `handler: "variable"` for a string field like `sheetId` that contains an upstream spreadsheet ID.
RIGHT: String fields use `handler: "manual"`. The `value` field supports inline `{{references}}`: `value: "{{create_spreadsheet.spreadsheetId}}"`.

See `reference/pipedream-plugins.md` → "Handler Types — When to Use Each" for the complete decision framework, field discovery flow, and prompt mode mechanics.

### Prompt Mode Does NOT Guarantee Exact Values

When `handler: "prompt"` is used, an AI agent decides the parameter value at runtime based on the `instructions` field. This means:
- The AI may rephrase, modify, or ignore your intended value
- Search queries and filter expressions will NOT be passed verbatim
- Results vary between runs (non-deterministic)

For ANY parameter where the value must be EXACT (search queries, filter strings, API parameters, IDs):
→ Use `handler: "manual"` with the exact value
→ NEVER use `handler: "prompt"`

WRONG: `instructions: "Use this exact Gmail query: in:sent from:me older_than:3d"`
=> AI backend may rephrase or apply a different query.

RIGHT: `parametersSetup.q = { handler: "manual", value: "in:sent from:me older_than:3d" }`
=> Value passed verbatim. No AI interpretation.

**Rule:** If you can write the value as a literal string → `manual`. If you need the AI to compose it from context → `prompt`. If in doubt → `manual`.

### Variable References Don't Support Array Indexing

`{{UUID.field.nested}}` works (dot notation). `{{UUID.array[0].field}}` does NOT — resolves to null.

Plugin outputs from external services often have deeply nested structures. Example — Google Sheets create-worksheet returns:
```json
{"replies": [{"addSheet": {"properties": {"sheetId": 2114432973, "title": "Bilan Mars 2026"}}}]}
```

WRONG: `{{UUID.sheetId}}` → null (not at root level).
WRONG: `{{UUID.replies[0].addSheet.properties.sheetId}}` → null (array indexing not supported).
RIGHT: Add a customScript bridge to extract and flatten:
```js
function func(input) { return { sheetId: input.replies[0].addSheet.properties.sheetId }; }
```
Then reference `{{scriptUUID.sheetId}}`. Plan these bridges during Phase 1.

**Output:** Downstream nodes reference the plugin's execution result:

```
{{PLUGIN_NODE_UUID}}
{{PLUGIN_NODE_UUID.response.id}}
{{PLUGIN_NODE_UUID.response.values}}
```

The output structure depends on the specific tool action's response format.

## Cascading Resolution — Dependent Dropdown Props

> Moved here from `nexus-tool-connection/SKILL.md` — this is workflow-builder territory (configuring plugin node parametersSetup at design time).

Some plugin action props depend on previously selected values. The "sheet tab" dropdown needs the spreadsheet ID first; the "channel" dropdown for a specific Slack workspace needs the workspace; etc. The API resolves these via `resolve-options` with a `configuredProps` object carrying the upstream selections.

**Pattern:** after selecting parent prop value → call `resolve-options` for child prop, passing parent value in `configuredProps`.

**Example — Google Sheets "sheet name" depends on selected spreadsheet:**

```bash
nexus api POST /tools/<toolId>/resolve-options --body '{
  "componentId": "action-key",
  "propName": "sheetName",
  "credentialId": "cred-uuid",
  "configuredProps": {
    "spreadsheetId": "sheet-id-123"
  }
}' --json
# => { options: [{ label: "Sheet1", value: "Sheet1" }, { label: "Sheet2", value: "Sheet2" }] }
```

**Without `configuredProps`** the resolver has no context — returns empty options or errors. Always pass the parent prop value(s).

**At design time** (configuring the plugin node in the dashboard), the UI does this automatically. **At CLI build time** (you constructing `parametersSetup` programmatically), you must call `resolve-options` per dependent prop in order. Persist the chosen `value` (not `label`) into the node's `parametersSetup`.

# Search Collection

## Node Type Identifier

`searchCollection`

## What It Does

Searches a Nexus knowledge collection by semantic similarity. Provide a collection ID and a search query, and the node returns matching documents from the collection's knowledge base. Useful for RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) patterns where workflows need to find relevant context from uploaded documents, websites, or text entries.

## Required Fields in `data`

| Field                  | Type     | Description                                                           |
| ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `selectedCollectionId` | `string` | The collection ID to search. Obtained from `nexus collection list --json`. |

## Optional Fields

| Field             | Type             | Description                                                        |
| ----------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `parametersSetup` | `ParameterSetup` | Search parameters. Auto-populated by the backend when `selectedCollectionId` is set. |
| `instructions`    | `string`         | Search query text. Supports `{{nodeId.path}}` variable references. |
| `label`           | `string`         | Display label for the node.                                        |

## Default Data (set automatically on creation)

```json
{
  "selectedCollectionId": "",
  "parametersSetup": {},
  "label": "Search Collection",
  "instructions": ""
}
```

## Connection Rules

- Can be placed inside a loop: Yes
- Can be masked (skipped): Yes

## Configuration Steps

1. **Create the node** with `nexus workflow node create`.
2. **Connect it** to an upstream node with `nexus workflow edge create`.
3. **List available collections** with `nexus collection list --json`.
4. **Select a collection** by updating `selectedCollectionId` with `nexus workflow node update`.
5. **Set the search query** in the `instructions` field (can use variable references) via `nexus workflow node update`.
6. **Configure additional parameters** (optional) via `parametersSetup`.

## Example API Calls

### Step 1: Create the search collection node

```bash
nexus workflow node create "$WORKFLOW_ID" --type searchCollection --json
```

### Step 2: Connect to upstream node

```bash
nexus workflow edge create "$WORKFLOW_ID" --source "$UPSTREAM_NODE_ID" --target "$SEARCH_NODE_ID"
```

### Step 3: List available collections

```bash
nexus collection list --json
```

### Step 4: Set the collection

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$SEARCH_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "selectedCollectionId": "collection_abc123"
  }
}'
```

### Step 5: Set the search query (static)

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$SEARCH_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "instructions": "Find documentation about API authentication methods"
  }
}'
```

### Step 5 (alternative): Set a dynamic search query using variables

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$SEARCH_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "instructions": "{{TRIGGER_NODE_UUID.body.question}}"
  }
}'
```

### Step 6: Test the node

```bash
nexus workflow node test "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$SEARCH_NODE_ID" --json
```

## Common Patterns / Tips

- **The collection must exist and have documents** before this node can return useful results. Use the documents API to upload files, add websites, or create text entries in the collection first.
- **Use variable references in `instructions`** to make the search query dynamic. For example, pass the user's question from a webhook trigger directly as the search query.
- **Combine with an AI task node** for a RAG pattern: Search Collection -> AI Task. The search results provide context, and the AI task generates a response based on that context.
- **Config status requires only `selectedCollectionId`** to be non-empty. The `instructions` field is optional for config status, but the search will be empty without a query.
- **The `parametersSetup` field is auto-populated by the backend** when `selectedCollectionId` is set, similar to how plugin nodes auto-populate when `selectedAction` is set. Configure handler types for any additional parameters.

## Variable References

The `instructions` field supports inline variable references:

```
{{TRIGGER_NODE_UUID.body.search_query}}
Find information about {{UPSTREAM_NODE_UUID.topic}}
```

The `parametersSetup` entries support variable references in the `variable` and `prompt` fields, following the same pattern as plugin and AI task nodes.

**Output:** Downstream nodes reference the search results:

```
{{SEARCH_NODE_UUID}}
{{SEARCH_NODE_UUID.results}}
{{SEARCH_NODE_UUID.results[0].content}}
{{SEARCH_NODE_UUID.results[0].score}}
```

The output typically includes an array of matching document chunks with content and relevance scores.

# Text Formatter

## Node Type Identifier

`textFormatter`

## What It Does

Formats and templates text with variable interpolation. Takes a text template containing `{{nodeUUID.path}}` references and produces a resolved string by substituting those references with actual values from upstream nodes at runtime.

**NOT for markup payloads (HTML, XML).** It resolves `{{refs}}` into human-readable text — not a verbatim passthrough; markup routed through it can be rendered/flattened. To carry a markup payload to a downstream send node, build it in a `customScript` that returns the string verbatim → `../custom-script/GUIDE.md`. ✗ HTML email body → textFormatter → send node → arrives as flattened text. ✓ customScript returns the HTML string verbatim w/ recipient name injected → send node `contentType: html`.

## Required Fields in `data`

| Field  | Type     | Description                                                                                                                          |
| ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `text` | `string` | The text template. Use `{{nodeId.path}}` syntax for variable references. Must be non-empty for the node to be considered "complete". |

## Optional Fields

| Field   | Type     | Description                 |
| ------- | -------- | --------------------------- |
| `label` | `string` | Display label for the node. |

## Default Data (set automatically on creation)

```json
{
  "label": "Text formatter",
  "text": "",
  "instructions": ""
}
```

## Connection Rules

- Can be placed inside a loop: Yes
- Can be masked (skipped): Yes

## Configuration Steps

1. **Create the node** with `nexus workflow node create`.
2. **Connect it** to an upstream node with `nexus workflow edge create`.
3. **Check available variables** by inspecting upstream node outputs with `nexus workflow node get` (check `outputFormat`).
4. **Set the text template** with variable references via `nexus workflow node update`.

## Example API Calls

### Step 1: Create the text formatter node

```bash
nexus workflow node create "$WORKFLOW_ID" --type textFormatter --json
```

Capture the `nodeId` from the response.

### Step 2: Connect to upstream node

```bash
nexus workflow edge create "$WORKFLOW_ID" --source "$UPSTREAM_NODE_ID" --target "$TEXT_FORMATTER_ID"
```

### Step 3: Discover available variables

```bash
nexus workflow node get "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TEXT_FORMATTER_ID" --json
```

Inspect `outputFormat` on upstream nodes to see which variables can be referenced in the template.

### Step 4: Set the text template

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TEXT_FORMATTER_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "text": "Hello {{TRIGGER_NODE_UUID.body.customer_name}}, your order {{TRIGGER_NODE_UUID.body.order_id}} has been processed. Total: ${{TRIGGER_NODE_UUID.body.amount}}"
  }
}'
```

### Step 5: Verify configuration status

```bash
nexus workflow node get "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TEXT_FORMATTER_ID" --json
```

Returns `configStatus: "complete"` when `text` is non-empty, or `configStatus: "incomplete"` with `missingFields: ["text"]` when empty.

### Step 6: Test the node

```bash
nexus workflow node test "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TEXT_FORMATTER_ID" --json
```

## Common Patterns / Tips

- **Variable syntax: `{{nodeUUID.propertyKey}}`** -- you MUST use the actual node UUID, not the node type name. For example, `{{abc123-def4-5678.body.name}}`, NOT `{{webhookTrigger.body.name}}`.
- **Nested paths are supported.** Use dot notation for nested objects: `{{nodeUUID.body.user.email}}`.
- **The node's config status is "complete" when `text` is non-empty.** Even a single character is sufficient.
- **Use `nexus workflow node get "$WF_ID" "$NODE_ID" --json`** and inspect upstream nodes' `outputFormat` to discover exactly which variables are reachable from this node. This avoids referencing variables that are not upstream.
- **Validate variable references** by testing the node with `nexus workflow node test` to verify that all `{{...}}` references in the text resolve to valid upstream variables.
- **The output is a single string.** Downstream nodes that receive this node's output get the fully interpolated text as a string value.

## Variable References

The `text` field supports inline variable references:

```
{{nodeUUID.propertyKey}}
{{nodeUUID.nested.deep.path}}
```

The API automatically translates these references to the internal format on write and back to `{{...}}` format on read. You always work with the `{{...}}` syntax.

**Output:** The text formatter outputs its resolved string. Downstream nodes reference it as:

```
{{TEXT_FORMATTER_NODE_UUID}}
```

There is no nested path on the output -- the entire output is the resolved text string.

# Timer

## Node Type Identifier

`timer`

## What It Does

Pauses workflow execution for a specified number of seconds. Useful for rate limiting, waiting for external processes to complete, or adding delays between API calls to avoid throttling.

## Required Fields in `data`

| Field     | Type     | Description                                                                               |
| --------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `seconds` | `number` | Number of seconds to wait. Must be a positive integer (> 0) for config status "complete". |

## Optional Fields

| Field          | Type     | Description                                  |
| -------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `label`        | `string` | Display label for the node.                  |
| `instructions` | `string` | Optional notes about why this timer is used. |

## Default Data (set automatically on creation)

```json
{
  "label": "Timer",
  "seconds": 0,
  "instructions": ""
}
```

Note: With `seconds: 0`, the node starts as "incomplete" (`missingFields: ["seconds"]`).

## Connection Rules

- Can be placed inside a loop: Yes
- Can be masked (skipped): Yes

## Configuration Steps

1. **Create the node** with `nexus workflow node create`.
2. **Connect it** to an upstream node with `nexus workflow edge create`.
3. **Set the duration** with `nexus workflow node update`, setting `seconds` to a positive integer.

## Example API Calls

### Step 1: Create the timer node

```bash
nexus workflow node create "$WORKFLOW_ID" --type timer --json
```

### Step 2: Connect to upstream node

```bash
nexus workflow edge create "$WORKFLOW_ID" --source "$UPSTREAM_NODE_ID" --target "$TIMER_NODE_ID"
```

### Step 3: Set the delay duration

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TIMER_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "seconds": 30
  }
}'
```

### Example: Short delay between API calls (5 seconds)

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TIMER_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "seconds": 5,
    "label": "Rate limit delay"
  }
}'
```

### Step 4: Verify configuration

```bash
nexus workflow node get "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TIMER_NODE_ID" --json
```

Returns `configStatus: "complete"` when `seconds` > 0. Returns `configStatus: "incomplete"` with `missingFields: ["seconds"]` when `seconds` is 0 or missing.

## Common Patterns / Tips

- **The timer does not produce output data.** It simply delays execution. Downstream nodes do not receive any new data from the timer -- they reference variables from nodes upstream of the timer.
- **Use timers inside loops** to add delays between iterations when calling rate-limited APIs.
- **`seconds` must be a positive integer.** Setting `seconds: 0` leaves the node incomplete. Fractional values (e.g., `2.5`) may be rounded or cause unexpected behavior.
- **Be mindful of total execution time.** Long timer values (e.g., 300 seconds) combined with loops can cause workflow execution to time out.
- **The `instructions` field is for documentation only** -- it has no effect on execution. Use it to note why the delay exists (e.g., "Wait for webhook processing to complete").

## Variable References

The timer node does not use `{{...}}` variable references in its configuration. The `instructions` field technically supports them, but since instructions are for documentation only, it has no practical effect.

**Output:** The timer node passes through data from the upstream node unchanged. Downstream nodes should reference the upstream node's UUID, not the timer node's UUID, when accessing data.

```
{{UPSTREAM_NODE_UUID.someField}}
```

The timer itself does not add any data to the workflow context.

# Agent Input Trigger

> Object-typed `parameters[]` (when `type: "object"`) must declare `properties` — see CLAUDE.md G#13.

## Node Type Identifier

`agentInputTrigger`

## What It Does

Triggers a workflow when an AI agent invokes it as a tool. The trigger defines a typed parameter schema that the agent fills in at runtime, making the workflow callable like a function with named inputs.

## Required Fields in `data`

None. The agent input trigger is considered "complete" immediately after creation, even without parameters defined.

## Optional Fields

| Field        | Type                             | Description                                                                                                        |
| ------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `parameters` | `Record<string, DataSchemaType>` | Input parameter schema. Each key defines a named parameter with its type (string, number, boolean, object, array). |
| `label`      | `string`                         | Display label for the node.                                                                                        |

## Default Data (set automatically on creation)

```json
{
  "parameters": {},
  "label": "Agent input trigger",
  "instructions": ""
}
```

## Connection Rules

- Can be placed inside a loop: No
- Can be masked (skipped): No

## Configuration Steps

1. **Replace the placeholder trigger** with `agentInputTrigger` using `nexus workflow trigger`.
2. **Define input parameters** by patching the node's `parameters` field. Each parameter specifies a name, type, and optionally a description and whether it is required.

## Example API Calls

### Step 1: Replace the placeholder trigger

```bash
nexus workflow trigger "$WORKFLOW_ID" --type agentInputTrigger --json
```

### Step 2: Define the input parameter schema

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TRIGGER_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "parameters": {
      "customer_email": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "The email address of the customer to look up",
        "required": true
      },
      "include_history": {
        "type": "boolean",
        "description": "Whether to include order history",
        "required": false
      },
      "max_results": {
        "type": "number",
        "description": "Maximum number of results to return",
        "required": false
      }
    }
  }
}' --json
```

### Step 3: Set test data (`runOutput`)

Configure realistic sample values that will be used when testing the workflow. These values feed into sequential node tests and enable one-click testing from the dashboard.

```bash
nexus workflow node update "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TRIGGER_NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "runOutput": {
      "customer_email": "jane@example.com",
      "include_history": true,
      "max_results": 10
    }
  }
}' --json
```

The `runOutput` keys MUST match the `parameters` keys exactly. Use realistic values that exercise the full workflow — avoid placeholder strings like "test" or "foo".

WRONG: Passing per-run test data with `workflow test --input '{...}'` (or a flat `--body '{...}'`). For an agentInputTrigger BOTH are silently ignored — the trigger's stored `runOutput` is used instead, so you keep testing the same data without noticing.
RIGHT: Set `runOutput` once for one-click node/dashboard tests; to vary data per run, pass `workflow test --body '{"triggerData":{...}}'` (the `triggerData` wrapper is required). Keys must match the `parameters` schema either way.

### Step 4: Verify the trigger configuration

```bash
nexus workflow node get "$WORKFLOW_ID" "$TRIGGER_NODE_ID" --json
```

The response will show `configStatus: "complete"` since agent input triggers have no required fields.

### Step 5: Test the workflow with sample input

```bash
nexus workflow test "$WORKFLOW_ID" --body '{
  "triggerData": {
    "customer_email": "jane@example.com",
    "include_history": true,
    "max_results": 10
  }
}' --json
```

## Common Patterns / Tips

- **Use this trigger when the workflow will be attached to an agent as a tool.** The agent sees the parameter schema and fills in the values at runtime based on the conversation context.
- **Parameter types should match what the agent will produce.** Use `string` for freeform text, `number` for numeric values, `boolean` for yes/no flags, `object` for structured data, and `array` for lists.
- **Include clear descriptions for each parameter.** The agent reads these descriptions to decide what values to provide, so the more descriptive they are, the better the agent's output.
- **Always set `runOutput` after defining parameters.** This enables sequential node testing from trigger downward and one-click testing from the dashboard. The `runOutput` object should contain realistic sample values for every parameter.
- **The `parameters` object keys become the variable paths.** Downstream nodes reference them as `{{triggerNodeUUID.customer_email}}`, not as `{{triggerNodeUUID.parameters.customer_email}}`.

## Variable References

Downstream nodes reference the trigger parameters using the trigger node's UUID:

```
{{TRIGGER_NODE_UUID.customer_email}}
{{TRIGGER_NODE_UUID.include_history}}
{{TRIGGER_NODE_UUID.max_results}}
```

IMPORTANT: Always use the actual node UUID (from the API response), not the type name.

The output schema corresponds directly to the `parameters` object you defined:

```json
{
  "parameters": {
    "customer_email": "string",
    "include_history": "boolean",
    "max_results": "number"
  }
}
```

# Platform Listener Trigger

## Node Type Identifier

`platformListenerTrigger`

> Object-typed `filters` + `idleConfig` fields must declare `properties` — see CLAUDE.md G#13.

## What It Does

Fires the workflow on a Nexus platform event (conversation lifecycle, calls, emails, customer changes, knowledge events, workflow events, agent events). ONE trigger type — pick the event via `platformEventType`. Idle events fire ONCE per silence stretch on OPEN/RUNNING conversations and re-arm on the next inbound message.

## Discover events + filter schemas

```bash
nexus workflow platform-listener-events --json \
  | jq '.data[] | {eventType, label, category, description, filterFields, samplePayload}'
```

32 events live across categories: Agents, Calls, Conversations, Customers, Email, Knowledge, Workflows. Each event publishes its own `filterFields` schema (keys + operators + enum options). Inspect `samplePayload` for the downstream variable shape.

## Required Fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `platformEventType` | string | Event key from the registry above. |

## Optional Fields

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `filters` | object | Per-event filter config. Keys = `filterFields[].key` of the chosen event; values match the field's `fieldType` + `operators`. Empty `{}` = no filtering. **G#13:** declare `properties` if you author this object as a schema. |
| `idleConfig` | object | **Required when `platformEventType = conversation.idle`.** Shape: `{ thresholdMinutes: number (≥ 1), lastMessageBy?: "USER"|"AGENT"|"SYSTEM" }`. |
| `label` | string | Display label. |

## Idle event — payload + filter schema

Payload (downstream nodes consume via `{{trigger.X}}`):

```json
{
  "conversation": { "id": "...", "status": "OPEN", "ticketStatus": "IN_PROGRESS", "lastMessageUpdatedAt": "..." },
  "idle":         { "thresholdMinutes": 1200, "lastMessageBy": "USER", "firedAt": "..." },
  "channel": "WHATSAPP",
  "agentId": "...",
  "deploymentId": "..."
}
```

Filter schema (`filterFields` for `conversation.idle`):

| Key | Field type | Operators |
|---|---|---|
| `deploymentId` | deployment-select | eq, neq |
| `agentId` | agent-select | eq, neq, in, nin |
| `channel` | enum-select (EMBED / WHATSAPP / SLACK / TEAMS / TELEGRAM / FB_MESSENGER / TWILIO_SMS / TWILIO_VOICE / GMAIL / OUTLOOK / IMAP / SMTP / API) | eq, neq, in, nin |

Per-event filter sets differ — always query the registry for the chosen event.

## Connection Rules

- Inputs: 0 (trigger)
- Outputs: 0–1
- Inside loop: No
- Maskable: No

## Test Mechanism

Behaves like `webhookTrigger`: `workflow test` returns `AWAITING_TRIGGER` + 0-node execution stub (per CLAUDE.md G#14 + workflow-builder SKILL.md Phase 4). Chain only fires on a real platform event after publish.

## Creation — two paths

**Path A — Two-step typed CLI** (recommended for typed flow; the typed `workflow trigger --body` currently drops the body for this trigger type):

```bash
NODE_ID=$(nexus workflow trigger "$WF" --type platformListenerTrigger --json | jq -r '.node.id')
nexus workflow node update "$WF" "$NODE_ID" --body '{
  "data": {
    "platformEventType": "conversation.idle",
    "idleConfig": {"thresholdMinutes": 30, "lastMessageBy": "USER"},
    "filters": {}
  }
}' --json
```

**Path B — One-step raw API** (single call):

```bash
nexus api POST "/workflows/$WF/nodes" --body '{
  "type": "platformListenerTrigger",
  "data": {
    "platformEventType": "conversation.idle",
    "idleConfig": {"thresholdMinutes": 30, "lastMessageBy": "USER"},
    "filters": {}
  }
}' --json
```
