## Node Type Rationale

| Node | Type | Why This Type |
|------|------|---------------|
| Parallel research branches | `parallelai` | Internet research requiring different depth tiers per dimension. Each branch gets its own processor level (base/core/pro). |
| Parallel evaluation branches | `aiTask` | Scoring against criteria requires judgment, but input is already structured (from pre-compute). No internet research needed. |
| Consolidation (merge) | `customScript` | Spread-merge (`{...a, ...b, ...c}`) is pure object manipulation. Deterministic, no AI needed. |
| Pre-compute | `customScript` | Building dimension-specific input bundles is deterministic data routing. Reduces token cost by giving each AI task only the data it needs. |
| Post-compute | `customScript` | Weighted score calculation (`score * weight`) is arithmetic. Must be exact, not AI-approximated. |
| Synthesis assessment | `aiTask` | Narrative assessment requires understanding all dimensions holistically. AI judgment is the point. |

## Handler Configuration

### parallelai node parameters

```json
{
  "name": {"handler": "manual", "value": "{{trigger.name}}"},
  "website": {"handler": "manual", "value": "{{trigger.website}}"},
  "linkedin": {"handler": "manual", "value": "{{trigger.linkedin}}"}
}
```

All parallelai input fields use `manual` handler with inline `{{references}}` in HTML data-mention format. This is the correct pattern for string parameters referencing upstream data.

### aiTask parameters from pre-compute (evaluation variant)

```json
{
  "candidate": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{pre-computation.dimA.candidate}}"},
  "hard_criteria": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{pre-computation.dimA.hard_criteria}}"},
  "client_company_name": {"handler": "manual", "value": "{{pre-computation.dimA.client_company_name}}"}
}
```

Complex objects (candidate, criteria arrays) use `variable` handler. String values (company name) use `manual` handler. This follows the handler rule: `variable` for objects/arrays, `manual` for strings.

### customScript consolidation

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {"name": "firmographics", "node": "{{FIRMOGRAPHICS_UUID}}"},
    {"name": "automation", "node": "{{AUTOMATION_UUID}}"},
    {"name": "hiring", "node": "{{HIRING_UUID}}"}
  ],
  "code": "function func(firmographics, automation, hiring) {\n  return {...(firmographics?.content || {}), ...(automation?.content || {}), ...(hiring?.content || {})};\n}"
}
```

Each input `node` field MUST wrap the UUID in `{{}}`. Without the wrapping, the function parameter receives `null`.

## WRONG / RIGHT

### Mistake 1: Using a loop instead of explicit parallel nodes

```
WRONG:
agentInputTrigger -> loop [dimensions]
  parallelai:research -> outputNode

All dimensions use the same parallelai node with the same processor tier.
You cannot tune depth per dimension. A "decision makers" search needs
pro-level research; "firmographics" only needs base.
```

```
RIGHT:
agentInputTrigger
  +---> parallelai:Firmographics (base)
  +---> parallelai:DecisionMakers (pro)
  +---> parallelai:Hiring (core)

Each dimension gets its own node with its own processor tier, instructions,
and output schema. Independent tuning per dimension.
```

### Mistake 2: Sending all data to every evaluation task

```
WRONG:
pre_compute outputs the full candidate + client + position to every aiTask.
Each task gets 15K tokens of context, most irrelevant.
The hard-criteria evaluator sees soft-skills data, which cross-contaminates its judgment.
```

```
RIGHT:
pre_compute builds dimension-specific bundles:
- dimA gets ONLY hard_criteria + disqualifiers + candidate basics
- dimC gets ONLY client_culture + cultural_criteria + candidate basics

Each task sees only its relevant data. Reduces tokens, improves focus,
prevents cross-contamination.
```

### Mistake 3: Using aiTask for the merge step

```
WRONG:
parallelai:A + parallelai:B + parallelai:C -> aiTask:merge

The AI "summarizes" the merge, losing fields, renaming keys, and
adding hallucinated interpretations.
```

```
RIGHT:
parallelai:A + parallelai:B + parallelai:C -> customScript:merge

Deterministic spread-merge: {...a, ...b, ...c}. Every field preserved
exactly. No interpretation, no data loss.
```

### Mistake 4: Skipping pre-compute for the evaluation variant

```
WRONG:
agentInputTrigger
  +---> aiTask:dimA (receives full trigger)
  +---> aiTask:dimB (receives full trigger)

Each AI task independently extracts what it needs from the full input.
Derived metrics (years of experience, career velocity) are calculated
independently by each task -- possibly with different results.
```

```
RIGHT:
agentInputTrigger -> customScript:pre_compute
  +---> aiTask:dimA (receives curated dimA bundle with pre-computed metrics)
  +---> aiTask:dimB (receives curated dimB bundle with same pre-computed metrics)

Metrics calculated ONCE in JavaScript, then distributed. Consistent
across all dimensions. Cheaper (smaller prompts).
```

# Human-in-the-Loop

## When to Use

Use when the workflow requires human judgment, approval, or refinement at a critical decision point before expensive downstream processing. The human gate should sit between cheap preparation (research, planning) and expensive execution (generation, API calls, document creation). Common triggers: creative direction approval, research plan validation, insight review before publication, content approval before posting.

## Architecture

### Approval gate with branching

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
plugin:research (cheap)
    |
aiTask:generate_plan_or_draft
    |
humanInput:validation
    |
branching:decision (logic mode)
    |
    +--- "approved" branch: proceed to generation
    |
    +--- "needs_changes" branch: extra research -> generation
```

### Insight review before document generation

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
[N parallel data loops] (fetch + transform)
    |
customScript:aggregate
    |
aiTask:generate_insights
    |
humanInput:review_insights
    |
aiTask:format_for_document
    |
generateDocument
    |
outputNode
```

```json
// aiTask:Insights generates analytical commentary:
"Camden gained 0.5pp volume share in off-trade, driven by strong promotional
activity (+2.1pp promo pressure). However, PTC index declined 3 points,
suggesting price erosion offsetting volume gains..."

// humanInput:review presents insights for business validation
// Human refines: "Add context that promotional investment was a deliberate
// Q1 strategy to defend shelf space against new competitor launch"

// Validated insights flow into document generation
```

## Node Type Rationale

| Node | Type | Why This Type |
|------|------|---------------|
| Human gate | `humanInput` | Pauses workflow execution, presents data via an embedded agent, captures structured output through `endConversationSchema`. The only node type that enables mid-workflow human interaction. |
| Branching after human | `branching` (logic mode) | Human output is structured (arrays, booleans). `array_is_empty` or `equals` conditions are deterministic checks. Prompt mode would waste tokens on what is a simple boolean question. |
| Plan/draft generation | `aiTask` | Creating a storyline, research plan, or insight summary requires language understanding and creative judgment. |
| Extra search execution | `plugin` inside loop | When the human requests additional research, each search query is an API call. Deterministic execution of the human's explicit requests. |

## Handler Configuration

### humanInput node

```json
{
  "parametersSetup": {
    "firstMessage": {
      "type": "string",
      "handler": "prompt",
      "value": "",
      "prompt": "Present the storyline to the user in a clear, organized way and ask for their feedback.",
      "variable": ""
    }
  },
  "instructions": "Present the storyline to the user. Ask for validation. Capture their exact storyline and any additional search queries they request.",
  "endConversationSchema": {
    "storyline": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "List of storyline elements validated by the user"},
    "extra_searches": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "description": "Additional search queries requested by the user"}
  }
}
```

`firstMessage` uses `prompt` handler via `parametersSetup` -- one of the few legitimate uses. The embedded agent needs AI judgment to present the storyline conversationally. `endConversationSchema` uses flat Nexus format (NOT standard JSON Schema — standard format silently corrupts `outputFormat`). Each key becomes a field in the node's output.

### Branching after humanInput (logic mode)

```json
{
  "mode": "logic",
  "branches": [
    {
      "name": "No Extra Searches",
      "conditions": [{"field": "{{humanInput}}.extra_searches", "operator": "array_is_empty"}]
    },
    {
      "name": "Extra Search",
      "isDefault": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Logic mode with `array_is_empty` operator. The default branch handles the case where extra searches exist.

### Search loop from human output

```json
{
  "iterationsSetup": {"variable": "{{humanInput.extra_searches}}"},
  "iteratorName": "search"
}
```

The loop iterates over the human-provided search queries. Each iteration passes the query string to a Perplexity plugin call.

## WRONG / RIGHT

### Mistake 1: Placing the human gate too early

```
WRONG:
agentInputTrigger -> humanInput:confirm_topic -> plugin:research -> aiTask:generate

The human confirms the topic before ANY research is done.
They have no context to make a meaningful decision.
The gate adds latency without adding value.
```

```
RIGHT:
agentInputTrigger -> plugin:research -> aiTask:generate_storyline
    -> humanInput:validate_storyline -> branching -> generation

The human sees the AI's work product (storyline with research backing).
They can make an informed decision: approve, refine, or request more research.
```

### Mistake 2: Using prompt mode branching after structured human output

```
WRONG:
humanInput (outputs {storyline[], extra_searches[]})
    |
branching (prompt mode): "Did the user request any extra searches?"

An LLM evaluates a boolean question. Costs tokens, adds latency,
and introduces non-determinism (the LLM might misinterpret).
```

```
RIGHT:
humanInput (outputs {storyline[], extra_searches[]})
    |
branching (logic mode): extra_searches array_is_empty

Deterministic array check. Zero token cost. Always correct.
```

### Mistake 3: Free-form human output instead of structured schema

```
WRONG:
humanInput with no endConversationSchema
Human types: "Looks good but also search for Gartner data and McKinsey report"

The downstream nodes receive a free-form string.
Parsing "Gartner data" and "McKinsey report" into separate search queries
requires another aiTask just to extract the intent.
```

```
RIGHT:
humanInput with endConversationSchema:
{
  "storyline": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
  "extra_searches": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
}

Human output: {"storyline": [...], "extra_searches": ["Gartner 2026 AI adoption", "McKinsey AI ROI study"]}
Downstream loop iterates directly over the typed array. No parsing needed.
```

### Mistake 4: Duplicating post-human branches instead of converging

```
NOTE: This is a design tradeoff, not always wrong.

PATTERN A (duplicated branches, as in LinkedIn Post Human #15):
branching
  +--- "approved": Write -> ImagePrompt -> Generate -> Output
  +--- "extra searches": Loop -> Write -> ImagePrompt -> Generate -> Output

Pros: Each branch is self-contained. No merge complexity.
Cons: 5 nodes duplicated across branches. Changes must be applied twice.

PATTERN B (convergent branches):
branching
  +--- "approved": customScript:pass_through
  +--- "extra searches": loop:extra_research
       |
       v (both converge)
Write -> ImagePrompt -> Generate -> Output

Pros: Single downstream pipeline. DRY.
Cons: More complex edge wiring. The convergence node must handle both shapes.
```

Use Pattern A when branches produce different data shapes. Use Pattern B when the only difference is a prepended step.

| Workflow | ID | Nodes | Gate Position |
|----------|-----|-------|---------------|
| LinkedIn Post Human | `ba9f5de1-650c-4125-9560-c12f1964ac6c` | 32 | After storyline generation, before writing + image generation. Logic-mode branching on `extra_searches array_is_empty`. Duplicated post-branches. |
| Deep Research | `d65d9ecb-2627-4756-bdaf-dd2bcb7e1765` | 33 | After research plan generation, before 3-level nested search execution. Human validates plan structure to prevent runaway costs. |

# Linear Pipeline

## When to Use

Use when each step depends on the previous step's output, there is no branching or parallelism, and the workflow has fewer than 8 nodes. Ideal for simple enrichment, transformation, or generate-research-structure flows where the data moves in a straight line from trigger to output.

## Architecture

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
aiTask (query generation)
    |
plugin (external search/API)
    |
aiTask (structuring)
    |
outputNode (previous)
```

Or the loop variant:

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
loop [items]
  |-- loopStart
  |     |
  |   plugin (fetch per item)
  |     |
  |   jsonata/customScript (transform)
  |     |
  |   outputNode
    |
outputNode (loop results)
```

## Scaffold

### Simple variant

```bash
nexus api POST /workflows/$WF_ID/batch --body '{
  "nodes": [
    { "ref": "query", "type": "aiTask", "label": "generate_query" },
    { "ref": "search", "type": "plugin", "label": "external_search" },
    { "ref": "structure", "type": "aiTask", "label": "structure_result" },
    { "ref": "out", "type": "outputNode", "label": "output",
      "data": { "outputType": "previous" } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "source": "@trigger", "target": "@query" },
    { "source": "@query", "target": "@search" },
    { "source": "@search", "target": "@structure" },
    { "source": "@structure", "target": "@out" }
  ]
}' --json
```

### Loop variant

```bash
nexus api POST /workflows/$WF_ID/batch --body '{
  "nodes": [
    { "ref": "loop", "type": "loop", "label": "loop_items",
      "data": { "iteratorName": "candidate", "executionMode": "parallel" } },
    { "ref": "fetch", "type": "plugin", "label": "fetch_details", "parentId": "@loop" },
    { "ref": "transform", "type": "jsonata", "label": "parse_profile", "parentId": "@loop" },
    { "ref": "inner_out", "type": "outputNode", "label": "item_result", "parentId": "@loop",
      "data": { "outputType": "previous" } },
    { "ref": "out", "type": "outputNode", "label": "output",
      "data": { "outputType": "previous" } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "source": "@trigger", "target": "@loop" },
    { "source": "@loopStart", "target": "@fetch" },
    { "source": "@fetch", "target": "@transform" },
    { "source": "@transform", "target": "@inner_out" },
    { "source": "@loop", "target": "@out" }
  ]
}' --json
```

### Simple 3-step (Person Enrichment #10)

```json

{"first_name": "Assem", "last_name": "Chammah", "email": "assem@gpt.nexus"}

// After aiTask:query_generation
"Find professional background for Assem Chammah, founder at gpt.nexus domain..."

// After plugin:Perplexity (sonar-deep-research)
{"message": {"content": "Assem Chammah is the co-founder of Nexus..."}, "citations": [...]}

// After aiTask:structuring
{
  "full_name": "Assem Chammah",
  "current_title": "Co-Founder & CEO",
  "current_company": "Nexus",
  "linkedin_url": "https://linkedin.com/in/assem-chammah",
  "confidence": "high"
}
```

### Loop variant (SESR Enrich #19)

```json
// Trigger input
{"candidates": [{"full_name": "Jane Doe", "linkedin_url": "https://linkedin.com/in/jane-doe"}]}

// After plugin:getPersonProfile (per iteration)
{"status": 200, "message": {"firstName": "Jane", "headline": "VP Engineering at..."}}

// After jsonata:parse (per iteration)
{
  "identity": {"full_name": "Jane Doe", "headline": "VP Engineering"},
  "current_role": {"title": "VP Engineering", "company": "Acme Corp"},
  "career": {"total_experience_years": 12, "positions": [...]},
  "behavioral_signals": {"tenure_patterns": "stable", "job_hopping_risk": "low"}
}

// Loop output: array of enriched profiles
```

## Node Type Rationale

| Node | Type | Why This Type |
|------|------|---------------|
| Query generation | `aiTask` | Crafting an optimized search query requires understanding name disambiguation, email domain analysis, and search strategy. Deterministic string templates would miss these nuances. |
| External search | `plugin` | API call to Perplexity/LinkedIn/Exa. No AI judgment -- just executing the query. |
| Structuring | `aiTask` | Raw research output is unstructured text. Extracting 12+ typed fields from prose requires language understanding. |
| Data transformation | `jsonata` | Pure data mapping (field extraction, date parsing, country code lookup). Declarative syntax is more concise than customScript for nested data access. |
| Data transformation (alt) | `customScript` | When you need procedural logic (conditionals, helper functions, loops). Use when jsonata's functional style becomes unwieldy. |

## Handler Configuration

### aiTask parameters (simple passthrough)

```json
{
  "first_name": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{trigger.first_name}}"},
  "last_name": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{trigger.last_name}}"},
  "email": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{trigger.email}}"}
}
```

Use `variable` handler for single-value passthrough of any type. Use `manual` when you need to compose strings with inline references.

### Plugin parameters inside a loop

```json
{
  "url": {"handler": "manual", "value": "{{candidate.linkedin_url}}"},
  "lang": {"handler": "manual", "value": "en"},
  "use_cache": {"handler": "manual", "value": "if-present"}
}
```

Note: `{{candidate.linkedin_url}}` uses the loop's `iteratorName`, not the loop node UUID. String params use `manual` handler even with `{{ref}}` references.

### outputNode

```json
{"outputType": "previous"}
```

Always use `"previous"` for structured data passthrough. `"custom"` invokes an LLM that will produce generic text instead of your JSON.

## WRONG / RIGHT

### Mistake 1: Using customScript for data that requires language understanding

```
WRONG:
agentInputTrigger -> customScript (parse email to extract company) -> plugin:search -> outputNode

The customScript tries to extract company from email domain with regex.
For "assem@gpt.nexus" it might work, but for "jane@gmail.com" it fails silently.
```

```
RIGHT:
agentInputTrigger -> aiTask (generate search query) -> plugin:search -> aiTask (structure) -> outputNode

The aiTask uses the email domain as one signal among many, handles gmail/outlook
gracefully, and crafts a disambiguation-aware query.
```

### Mistake 2: Skipping the structuring step

```
WRONG:
agentInputTrigger -> plugin:Perplexity -> outputNode

Raw Perplexity output is unstructured prose with citations mixed in.
Downstream consumers get inconsistent data shapes.
```

```
RIGHT:
agentInputTrigger -> aiTask:query -> plugin:Perplexity -> aiTask:structure -> outputNode

The structuring aiTask extracts typed fields (strings, arrays, confidence level)
from the prose, producing a clean contract for downstream consumers.
```

### Mistake 3: Using aiTask inside a loop for deterministic transformation

```
WRONG:
loop [candidates]
  plugin:getProfile -> aiTask:parseProfile -> outputNode

An aiTask to parse structured JSON API responses wastes tokens and adds latency.
```

```
RIGHT:
loop [candidates]
  plugin:getProfile -> jsonata:parse -> outputNode

JSONata handles nested data extraction, date parsing, and field mapping
without an LLM call. Faster, cheaper, deterministic.
```

# Loop Per-Item AI

## When to Use

Use when you have an array of items and each item needs independent AI processing (scoring, classification, enrichment, summarization). The AI task inside the loop operates on ONE item per iteration. This is the correct pattern when the AI verb is "analyze", "classify", "score", or "extract" and the input is an array. Never pass the entire array to a single aiTask -- use a loop.

## Architecture

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
customScript:prepare (optional -- normalize/filter array)
    |
loop [items] (parallel)
  |-- loopStart
  |     |
  |   aiTask:process_one_item
  |     |
  |   outputNode (previous)
    |
customScript:post_process (optional -- sort, deduplicate, aggregate)
    |
outputNode
```

With plugin fetch + AI:

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
plugin:fetch_list (or customScript:build_array)
    |
loop [items] (parallel)
  |-- loopStart
  |     |
  |   plugin:fetch_details (API call per item)
  |     |
  |   customScript:transform (normalize API response)
  |     |
  |   aiTask:evaluate (score/classify per item)
  |     |
  |   outputNode (previous)
    |
customScript:aggregate
    |
outputNode
```

## Scaffold

### Simple loop with AI

```bash
nexus api POST /workflows/$WF_ID/batch --body '{

      "data": { "outputType": "previous" } },
    { "ref": "post", "type": "customScript", "label": "post_process" },
    { "ref": "out", "type": "outputNode", "label": "output",
      "data": { "outputType": "previous" } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "source": "@trigger", "target": "@prep" },
    { "source": "@prep", "target": "@loop" },
    { "source": "@loopStart", "target": "@process" },
    { "source": "@process", "target": "@inner_out" },
```

```json
// Loop input: array of LinkedIn URLs
["https://linkedin.com/company/acme-corp", "https://linkedin.com/company/beta-inc"]

// Per iteration -- after plugin:fetchInfo
{"status": 200, "message": {"companyName": "Acme Corp", "industry": "Technology", "employeeCount": 500}}
```

## Node Type Rationale

| Node | Type | Why This Type |
|------|------|---------------|
| Per-item scoring | `aiTask` | Relevance scoring requires understanding article content, matching against themes, producing reasoned judgment. Pure keyword matching would miss semantic relevance. |
| Per-item classification | `aiTask` | Classifying by category (pillar, urgency, sentiment) requires language understanding. |
| Array normalization | `customScript` | Filtering by active status, sorting, field extraction from API responses -- all deterministic operations on structured data. |
| Deduplication | `customScript` | URL-based dedup via hashmap is O(n) exact matching. No AI judgment needed. |
| Deterministic scoring | `customScript` | Rule-based scoring against country/industry/size lists is deterministic. AI would produce inconsistent scores across runs. |
| AI enrichment on top of rules | `aiTask` | After deterministic scoring, AI adds nuance the rules miss (edge cases, contextual signals). Hybrid scoring. |

## Handler Configuration

### aiTask parameters from loop iterator

```json
{
  "article_title": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{article_loop.article_title}}"},
  "article_description": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{article_loop.article_description}}"},
  "theme": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{article_loop.theme}}"}
}
```

Inside loops, reference the iterator using `{{iteratorName.field}}` -- not the loop node UUID. The `iteratorName` is set on the loop node (e.g., `"article"` produces references like `{{article.field}}`). Note: some production workflows use the loop UUID, but `iteratorName` references are cleaner and preferred.

### Plugin parameters from loop iterator

```json
{
  "url": {"handler": "manual", "value": "{{linkedin_urls}}"},
  "lang": {"handler": "manual", "value": "en"},
  "use_cache": {"handler": "manual", "value": "never"}
}
```

String params always use `manual` handler, even when the value is a `{{ref}}`. The iterator reference `{{linkedin_urls}}` refers to the current item (the loop iterates over a flat string array, so the iterator IS the URL string).

### Loop output node

```json
{"outputType": "previous"}
```

Always `"previous"` inside loops. The loop auto-collects each iteration's output into an array.

## WRONG / RIGHT

### Mistake 1: Passing the entire array to one aiTask

```
WRONG:
agentInputTrigger -> aiTask:score_all_articles -> outputNode

The aiTask receives 30 articles at once.
It loses focus, truncates low-ranked items, produces inconsistent scores,
and the prompt grows with O(N) token cost.
```

```
RIGHT:
agentInputTrigger
    |
loop [articles] (parallel)
  aiTask:score_one_article -> outputNode
    |
customScript:sort_by_score -> outputNode

Each article gets focused, consistent evaluation.
Parallel execution means latency = max(single article), not sum.
```

### Mistake 2: Using aiTask for deterministic post-processing

```
WRONG:
loop [articles]
  aiTask:score -> outputNode
    |
aiTask:deduplicate_and_sort

The AI "deduplicates" by summarizing similar articles together,
losing individual scores and URLs.
```

```
RIGHT:
loop [articles]
  aiTask:score -> outputNode
    |
customScript:deduplicate_and_sort

URL-based dedup via hashmap is exact. Sort by score is arithmetic.
Zero AI cost, deterministic output.
```

### Mistake 3: Sequential loop for independent items

```
WRONG:
loop [articles] (executionMode: "sequential")
  aiTask:score -> outputNode

Articles are scored one at a time. 30 articles x 3s per aiTask = 90s total.
```

```
RIGHT:
loop [articles] (executionMode: "parallel")
  aiTask:score -> outputNode

All 30 articles scored simultaneously. Total latency = ~3s.
Use sequential only when: (a) a rate-limited API requires pacing,
or (b) each iteration depends on the previous iteration's output.
```

### Mistake 4: Mixing deterministic scoring with AI in one node

```
WRONG:
loop [companies]
  aiTask:full_assessment (combines rule-based criteria + AI judgment)

The aiTask sometimes applies the country/industry rules, sometimes ignores them.
Inconsistent results across runs.
```

```
RIGHT:
loop [companies]
  customScript:deterministic_score (rules: country, industry, size)
    |
  aiTask:verdict (adds nuance the rules miss)
    |
  customScript:merge_scores (combines both)

Deterministic rules are always consistent. AI adds value on top.
The customScript merge gives AI reasoning priority but falls back to rules.
```

# Nested Loops

## When to Use

Use when your data has a hierarchical structure where one level produces an array that must be iterated at the next level. Common shapes: tabs containing rows, queries returning articles, sub-topics containing questions containing search queries. The nesting depth maps to the data hierarchy depth. Two levels is common; three levels is the practical maximum before the workflow becomes unmanageable.

## Architecture

### Two-level nesting (config -> query -> process)

```
scheduleTrigger
    |
plugin:fetch_config
    |
loop:outer [config_items] (parallel)
  |-- loopStart
  |     |
  |   plugin:fetch_data (per config item)
  |     |
  |   customScript:transform
  |     |
  |   loop:inner [data_items] (parallel)
  |     |-- loopStart
  |     |     |
  |     |   aiTask:process_one
  |     |     |
  |     |   outputNode
  |     |
  |   outputNode (inner loop results)
    |
customScript:aggregate
    |
outputNode
```

### Three-level nesting (plan -> subtopic -> question -> query)

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
aiTask:generate_plan
    |
humanInput:validate_plan
    |
loop:subtopics [subtopic]
  |-- loopStart
  |     |
  |   loop:questions [question]
  |     |-- loopStart
  |     |     |
  |     |   loop:queries [query]
  |     |     |-- loopStart
  |     |     |     |
  |     |     |   plugin:search
  |     |     |     |
  |     |     |   aiTask:evaluate_quality
  |     |     |     |
  |     |     |   branching:satisfactory?
  |     |     |     |
  |     |     |   outputNode
  |     |     |
  |     |   aiTask:compile_answer
  |     |     |
  |     |   outputNode
```

## Node Type Rationale

| Node | Type | Why This Type |
|------|------|---------------|
| Config reading | `plugin` | Google Sheets API calls are deterministic data fetching. |
| Query construction | `customScript` | Combinatorial query building from keyword arrays is deterministic string manipulation. AI would hallucinate query syntax. |
| Date arithmetic | `customScript` | Computing "30 days ago" or "yesterday" is `new Date()` arithmetic. No AI needed. |
| Per-item scoring | `aiTask` | Relevance scoring requires semantic understanding of article vs. theme. |
| Quality evaluation | `aiTask` | Deciding if a search result is "satisfactory" requires judgment. |
| Deduplication | `customScript` | URL-based hashmap dedup is exact matching, O(n). |
| String interpolation | `textFormatter` | Constructing `"SheetTitle!A2:F500"` from a loop variable. More concise than customScript for simple concatenation. |

## Handler Configuration

### Plugin parameters from nested loop iterator

```json
// Level 2 loop (query_loop), referencing Level 2 iterator fields
{
  "q": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{query_loop.q}}"},
  "from": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{query_loop.fromDate}}"},
  "size": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{query_loop.size}}"}
}
```

All parameters use `variable` handler because they pass structured values (strings, numbers) from the loop iterator directly. This is correct for single-field passthrough from iterators.

### aiTask parameters from innermost loop iterator

```json
{
  "article_title": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{article_loop.article_title}}"},
  "article_url": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{article_loop.article_url}}"},
```

### Loop node iterationsSetup

```json

// Inner loop: iterates over outer loop iterator's sub-array
{"iterationsSetup": {"variable": "{{query_loop.articles}}"}}
```

The `iterationsSetup.variable` MUST use `{{UUID.path}}` or `{{iteratorName.path}}` to reference the array to iterate over.

## WRONG / RIGHT

### Mistake 1: Flattening a hierarchical structure into one loop

```
WRONG:
customScript:flatten_all -> loop [flat_items]
  aiTask:process -> outputNode

Loses the hierarchical context. An article from the "AI" theme query
is processed identically to one from the "IoT" theme query.
Theme-specific scoring criteria cannot be applied per-query.
```

```
RIGHT:
loop:query_loop [query]
  plugin:fetch_news
  loop:article_loop [article]
    aiTask:score (has access to query.theme via outer loop)
    outputNode

Each article retains its query context. The aiTask can use the theme
from the outer loop to tailor scoring.
```

### Mistake 2: Sequential execution for independent iterations

```
WRONG:
loop:outer [tabs] (sequential)
  loop:inner [articles] (sequential)
    aiTask:score

Tabs are independent. Articles within a tab are independent.
Sequential execution wastes time.
```

```
RIGHT:
loop:outer [tabs] (parallel)
  loop:inner [articles] (parallel)
    aiTask:score

All levels execute in parallel. Total latency = max(single article score),
not sum across all tabs x all articles.

Exception: use sequential when calling rate-limited APIs (e.g., LinkedIn profile
fetches that throttle at 5 req/s).
```

### Mistake 3: Deduplicating inside the loop instead of after

```
WRONG:
loop:query_loop [query]
  plugin:fetch_news
  customScript:deduplicate (dedup within this query only)
  loop:article_loop [article]
    aiTask:score

Only deduplicates within each query's results. The same article
appearing in two different queries is scored twice.
```

```
RIGHT:
loop:query_loop [query]
  plugin:fetch_news
  loop:article_loop [article]
    aiTask:score -> outputNode
  outputNode
    |
customScript:deduplicate (dedup across ALL queries)

Score everything in parallel, then deduplicate at the end.
Trade some redundant AI calls for simpler architecture and
guaranteed cross-query deduplication.
```

### Mistake 4: Three-level nesting without a validated plan

```
WRONG:
agentInputTrigger -> aiTask:generate_plan
  -> loop:subtopics -> loop:questions -> loop:queries
     plugin:search (expensive Perplexity calls)

If the plan is poorly structured, dozens of wasted API calls execute
before anyone notices. A 3x3x3 plan = 27 search calls.
```

```
RIGHT:
agentInputTrigger -> aiTask:generate_plan
  -> humanInput:validate_plan
  -> loop:subtopics -> loop:questions -> loop:queries
     plugin:search

Human validates the plan structure before expensive execution.
Prevents runaway costs on a misguided research plan.
```

# Self-Serving Work-Queue

## When to Use
Bulk processing of N entities where the run is EXPENSIVE (billed API calls, AI analysis) or LONG (hundreds+ of items): the child workflow claims its OWN next slice of work from a shared store instead of receiving it as parameters, marks every ATTEMPTED key in a marker table, and an orchestrator fires it in parameter-free rounds until nothing is pending. Essential when work must be resumable after any failure, when zero-output items must not recycle forever, and when parameters crossing a sub-workflow boundary are fragile. Also the shape to reach for when a parent-driven design keeps failing at the parameter boundary — invert instead of fighting the resolver.

Pair it with DECOUPLED STAGES: cheap acquisition (fetch) persists its results BEFORE the expensive stage (AI analysis) runs as a separate self-serving queue — a wedge in the expensive stage never loses acquired data.

## Architecture
```
CHILD (self-serving, published, agentInputTrigger — takes NO parameters)
agentInputTrigger
  → read_pending      (plugin: SELECT keys NOT IN (SELECT key FROM <marker>) LIMIT <N>)
  → shape_pending     (customScript: rows → work items; spread all fields)
  → guard_items       (branching, logic mode: array_is_not_empty)
      ├─ br_has → loop_work (parallel, iteratorName=item)
      │             └─ process_item (aiTask or plugin — ONE item)
      │                → build_row (customScript: attach key + stage fields)
      │          → collect (customScript: objects → JSON strings, write-once payload)
      │          → guard_rows (branching: array_is_not_empty)
      │               ├─ br_rows → write_results (plugin: insert-rows — ONE write per block)
      │               └─ br_none → out_none_rows (outputNode)
      │          → file_attempted (plugin: insert-rows → <marker> — EVERY processed key,
      │                            including zero-output ones, so empties never recycle)
      │          → out_done (outputNode: "processed {{collect.count}}")
      └─ br_none → out_empty (outputNode: "queue drained")

ORCHESTRATOR (fires rounds; passes NOTHING)
agentInputTrigger → count_pending → guard (0? done : fire) → run_child (sub-workflow, param-free)
  → loop back via re-trigger per round (or an external driver-monitor fires rounds — see Operate note)
```

## Scaffold
Batch-create the child's shell (nodes as empty shells first — R#18/G#5 scaffold-first), then configure top-to-bottom. The `read_pending` query and the `<marker>` table name are the only per-use bindings:
```
nexus api POST /workflows/$WF_ID/batch --body '{
  "nodes": [
    {"ref":"read_pending","type":"plugin","label":"read_pending"},
    {"ref":"shape_pending","type":"customScript","label":"shape_pending"},
    {"ref":"guard_items","type":"branching","label":"guard_items"},
    {"ref":"loop_work","type":"loop","label":"loop_work"},
    {"ref":"process_item","type":"aiTask","label":"process_item","parentId":"@loop_work"},
    {"ref":"build_row","type":"customScript","label":"build_row","parentId":"@loop_work"},
    {"ref":"collect","type":"customScript","label":"collect"},
    {"ref":"guard_rows","type":"branching","label":"guard_rows"},
    {"ref":"write_results","type":"plugin","label":"write_results"},
    {"ref":"file_attempted","type":"plugin","label":"file_attempted"},
    {"ref":"out_done","type":"outputNode","label":"out_done"},
    {"ref":"out_none_rows","type":"outputNode","label":"out_none_rows"},
    {"ref":"out_empty","type":"outputNode","label":"out_empty"}
  ],
  "edges": [ ... per the ASCII above; branch handles created explicitly (G#2) ... ]
}'
```
(Branch placement in the batch body: the `branches` array sits at the node's TOP LEVEL — nested under `data` the `@ref` sourceHandles do NOT resolve (probe-verified); see gotcha #56.)

## Data Flow
### review-analysis queue (production-verified shape)
Round 1, block of 40 keys:
```
read_pending  → {"rows":[{"key":"K1",...},{"key":"K2",...} ×40]}            # 40 unclaimed keys
loop_work     → 40 parallel process_item runs (ONE item each)
collect       → {"rows":["{\"key\":\"K1\",...}", ...], "count": 37}          # 3 items yielded nothing
write_results → 37 rows inserted, ONE insert-rows call                        # write-once per block
file_attempted→ 40 marker rows (K1..K40 — including the 3 zero-output keys)   # empties can't recycle
```
Round 2 reads the NEXT 40 (`NOT IN` excludes all 40 attempted). A wedged round leaves its keys unmarked → automatically retried next round; a re-run can at worst double-insert results, which the read-side dedup absorbs (below).

## Node Type Rationale
| Node | Type | Why This Type |
|---|---|---|
| read_pending | plugin (SQL) | deterministic claim: `NOT IN <marker> LIMIT <N>` — the LIMIT is the bounded fan-out |
| guard_items / guard_rows | branching (logic) | empty array would throw at insert-rows behind a lying success envelope (gotcha #56) |
| loop_work | loop (parallel) | N bounded by the CLAIM, not the loop — the proven-batch-size lives in the SQL LIMIT |
| collect | customScript | loop emits objects; insert-rows needs JSON strings; ONE write per block (quota + retention) |
| file_attempted | plugin (insert-rows) | ATTEMPTED ≠ produced-output: a marker per processed key is what makes empties terminal |

## Handler Configuration
`read_pending.query` = manual handler (fixed SQL, `<N>` literal); `loop_work.items` = variable → `{{shape_pending.items}}`; `process_item` params = variable → `{{item.<field>}}`; everything deterministic — no prompt handlers (G#1).

**Choosing `<N>` (the proven batch size):** start at the largest batch that has COMPLETED CLEANLY end-to-end (prove on a small block first); raise only after a clean larger run. An unproven jump to thousands of parallel AI calls is how executors wedge — and there is no cancel API; the halt lever is unpublishing the child.

**Read-side dedup (at-least-once):** every consumer of the results table dedups on the natural key at READ time — `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY key) = 1` — because a resumable, re-firing queue is at-least-once by construction. Do not chase write-side exactly-once.

## WRONG / RIGHT
### Mistake 1: parent passes the work as parameters
WRONG: orchestrator computes the block and passes `items` into the sub-workflow — one resolver fault at the boundary and every child processes null while guards convert it to green.
RIGHT: the child CLAIMS its own block from the store; the orchestrator passes nothing and cannot poison the run.
### Mistake 2: inferring "processed" from the results table
WRONG: `NOT IN (SELECT key FROM results)` — a key that produced zero output re-enters the queue forever.
RIGHT: a dedicated marker table records ATTEMPTED keys, written for every processed key including zero-output ones.
### Mistake 3: unbounded fan-out
WRONG: `LIMIT`-less claim → thousands of parallel AI calls in one execution → executor wedge, no cancel.
RIGHT: the claim's LIMIT is a PROVEN batch size; rounds, not one mega-run.
### Mistake 4: verifying the sweep against a dirty store
WRONG: "rows exist after the run" over a table that already held test rows — leftovers manufacture green (R#20 Green-but-unattributed).
RIGHT: truncate/tag a baseline before any row-count E2E; count only rows attributable to THIS run.

# Sub-Workflow Composition

## When to Use

Use when a workflow needs to invoke reusable processing that is (a) complex enough to warrant its own workflow (7+ nodes), (b) shared across multiple parent workflows, or (c) independently testable and versioned. Sub-workflows turn a large monolithic workflow into a tree of smaller, focused workflows. The parent (orchestrator) handles data routing and cross-cutting concerns (document generation, email delivery); the children handle domain-specific processing.

## Architecture

### Sequential orchestrator (pipeline)

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
workflow:Step_A (sub-workflow)
    |
workflow:Step_B (sub-workflow, receives Step_A output)
    |
workflow:Step_C (sub-workflow, receives Step_A + Step_B output)
    |
generateDocument
    |
plugin:email
    |
outputNode
```

### Micro-orchestrator (compose 2 sub-workflows)

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
workflow:Enrich (sub-workflow)
    |
workflow:Score (sub-workflow, receives Enrich output + trigger context)
    |
outputNode
```

### Loop-based composition (sub-workflow per item)

```
agentInputTrigger
    |
plugin:initial_search
    |
loop [items]
  |-- loopStart
  |     |
  |   workflow:process_one (sub-workflow per item)
  |     |
  |   outputNode
    |
customScript:consolidate
    |
outputNode
```

```json
// Data routing: client and position pass through UNCHANGED from trigger.
// candidate comes from Enrich output (dynamic data).
```

```json
// Per iteration:
//   workflow:Find_peers_flow receives: {"company_url": "https://acme.com", "company_name": "Acme"}
//   Returns: peer companies discovered via LinkedIn similar pages

// Loop:companies_infos -- one sub-workflow call per company

```

## Node Type Rationale

| Node | Type | Why This Type |
|------|------|---------------|
| Orchestrator routing | `workflow` node | Delegates to a published sub-workflow. The parent stays lean (8 nodes vs 50+ inline). Sub-workflows are independently testable, versioned, and reusable. |
| Data forwarding | `variable` handler | Sub-workflow parameters are entire objects passed through unchanged. `variable` handler is correct for object/array passthrough. |
| Cross-cutting concerns | `generateDocument`, `plugin:email` | Document generation and email delivery belong at the orchestrator level. Sub-workflows should not have side effects beyond returning data. |
| Consolidation between stages | `customScript` | Merging results from multiple sub-workflow calls is deterministic data manipulation (dedup, flatten, merge). |

## Handler Configuration

### Sub-workflow parameter passing (selective forwarding)

```json
// Search receives ONLY search_scope (not client, not position)
{
  "search_scope": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{trigger.search_scope}}"}
}

// Enrich receives ONLY candidates (from Search output)
{
  "candidates": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{Search}}"}
}

// Score receives static context from trigger + dynamic data from Enrich
{
  "client": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{trigger.client}}"},
  "position": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{trigger.position}}"},
  "candidate": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{Enrich}}"}
}
```

Key principle: **selective parameter forwarding**. Each sub-workflow receives only the data it needs. This is the principle of least privilege applied to data flow.

### Sub-workflow inside a loop

```json
// Loop iterator provides per-item data
{
  "company_url": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{companies.website_url}}"},
  "company_name": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{companies.name}}"}
}
```

### Email plugin (cross-cutting concern at orchestrator level)

```json
{
  "to": {"handler": "variable", "variable": "{{trigger.emails}}"},
  "subject": {"handler": "manual", "value": "[Candidate Report] {{trigger.client.company.name}}"},
  "body": {"handler": "manual", "value": "{{Prep Email}}"},
  "bodyType": {"handler": "manual", "value": "html"}
}
```

## WRONG / RIGHT

### Mistake 1: Putting delivery concerns inside sub-workflows

```
WRONG:
workflow:Search -> workflow:Enrich -> workflow:Score_and_Email

The Score sub-workflow also sends the email. Now you cannot reuse Score
without triggering an email. The Enrich-Score micro-orchestrator
would also send emails when it should just return data.
```

```
RIGHT:
workflow:Search -> workflow:Enrich -> workflow:Score
    |
generateDocument -> customScript:prep_email -> plugin:send_email

Cross-cutting concerns (document, email) live at the orchestrator level.
Sub-workflows are pure data transformations with no side effects.
Score can be reused from Enrich-Score without unwanted emails.
```

### Mistake 2: Forwarding the entire trigger to every sub-workflow

```
WRONG:
workflow:Search receives: trigger (all 50+ fields)
workflow:Enrich receives: trigger (all 50+ fields)
workflow:Score  receives: trigger (all 50+ fields)

Each sub-workflow gets data it does not need. Search sees scoring weights.
Enrich sees client culture. Coupling increases; changes to trigger
schema ripple through all sub-workflows.
```

```
RIGHT:
workflow:Search receives: {"search_scope": trigger.search_scope}
workflow:Enrich receives: {"candidates": Search.output}
workflow:Score  receives: {"client": trigger.client, "position": trigger.position, "candidate": Enrich.output}

Each sub-workflow has a minimal input contract. Changes to search_scope
do not affect Score. Changes to position do not affect Search.
```

### Mistake 3: Inlining complex processing instead of delegating

```
WRONG:
loop [companies]
  plugin:LinkedIn_lookup
  loop [similar_pages]
    plugin:LinkedIn_lookup (again)
    loop [level_2_pages]
      plugin:LinkedIn_lookup (again)
  customScript:URL_cleaning
  outputNode

37 nodes inline in the parent workflow. The parent is unreadable.
The peer discovery logic cannot be reused by other workflows.
```

```
RIGHT:
loop [companies]
  workflow:Find_peers (sub-workflow, 12 nodes)
  outputNode

The parent stays clean. Find_peers encapsulates the 2-level snowball
discovery. It can be called from Screen Industry, from a standalone
agent, or from any new workflow that needs peer discovery.
```

### Mistake 4: Creating a sub-workflow for 2-3 nodes

```
WRONG:
workflow:format_name (sub-workflow with: trigger -> customScript -> outputNode)

A 3-node sub-workflow for simple string formatting. The overhead of
sub-workflow invocation (trigger schema, publishing, version tracking)
exceeds the complexity of the operation.
```

```
RIGHT:
customScript:format_name (inline in parent)

Simple operations belong inline. Sub-workflows are for 7+ node
operations that warrant independent testing and reuse.
```

## Node-by-Node Configuration

### trigger (agentInputTrigger)

| Field | Variant A | Variant B |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| Schema | Entity + evaluation context + scoring weights | Entity + document references + emails |
| Key design | Scoring weights are INPUT, not hardcoded | Documents use `{{document_name}}` format for KB lookup |

### pre_compute (customScript -- Variant A)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Purpose | Build dimension-specific input bundles |
| Key logic | Compliance checks, metric computation (years of experience, career velocity), bundle construction |
| Why customScript | Deterministic operations that must be consistent across AI tasks. Pre-computed metrics avoid each AI independently calculating the same values. |

### dim_N_score (aiTask -- Variant A)

| Param | Handler | Value |
|-------|---------|-------|
| All fields | variable | `{{pre_compute.dimN.field_name}}` |

Each task receives ONLY its dimension-specific bundle. This reduces token usage and prevents cross-contamination between dimensions.

### post_compute (customScript -- Variant A)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Purpose | Extract scores, apply weights, compute composite |
| Formula | `composite = (dimA * weight_hard) + (dimB * weight_exp) + (dimC * weight_culture) + (dimD * weight_soft)` |
| Weights | From `trigger.position.scoring_weights` (configurable, not hardcoded) |

### write_section_N (aiTask -- Variant B, shared template)

All 10 writing tasks use the **same AI task ID**. Each receives different assessment data but produces the same output schema:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Output | `{ isLow: boolean, isMid: boolean, isHigh: boolean, rationale: string }` |
| Why booleans | Eliminates string comparison in document template. Each boolean controls section visibility/color. |

### generate_html (customScript -- Variant B)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Size | Up to 10K characters |
| Purpose | Full HTML email with conditional rendering based on boolean flags |
| Why customScript | HTML generation is deterministic string templating. Full control over conditional sections. |

## Customization Points

- **SWAP:DATA_GATHERING** -- Choose between loop+DB dedup (batch assessment), pre-compute+fan-out (dimensional scoring), or document extraction (document-based assessment).
- **SWAP:CRITERION** -- Define your evaluation criteria. Sales: AI readiness, timing, budget. Grants: compliance, impact, capacity. Hiring: hard criteria, experience, cultural fit.
- **SWAP:WRITER_TASK_ID** -- Create one AI task that converts any assessment into a narrative section. Reuse across all criteria for consistency.
- **SWAP:SOURCE_DOC** -- Replace document extraction with API data fetch, knowledge base lookup, or direct input.
- **SWAP:DATABASE** -- Replace BigQuery with any database for dedup/persistence. Replace the SQL generation customScript with appropriate dialect.
- **SWAP:SCORING_WEIGHTS** -- Make weights configurable via trigger input (not hardcoded). Different evaluation contexts can weight criteria differently.

## Testing Strategy

1. **Test data gathering first** -- Verify document extraction, API fetches, or DB dedup work correctly.
2. **Test one research dimension** -- Verify parallelai returns substantive research with citations.
3. **Test one criterion assessment** -- Verify the AI produces the expected rating schema.
4. **Test the shared writer task** -- Verify `{ isLow, isMid, isHigh, rationale }` output. Test with both high-score and low-score inputs to verify all branches.
5. **Test post_compute / summary** -- Verify composite score calculation is correct. Verify overall recommendation aligns with individual criteria.
6. **Test document generation** -- Verify template fills correctly. Check conditional sections render based on boolean flags.
7. **Test email** -- Verify HTML renders correctly in email client. Check download link works.
8. **End-to-end** -- Run with a known entity. Verify the email contains accurate ratings and the document is well-formatted.

## Key Design Principles

1. **Separate assessment from narrative.** Assessment AI tasks produce structured ratings. Separate writer tasks convert ratings into prose. This lets you change writing style without affecting evaluation logic.

2. **Pre-compute deterministic metrics.** Never ask multiple AI tasks to independently calculate the same values. Pre-compute in customScript, then distribute.

3. **Use boolean flags for conditional formatting.** `isLow/isMid/isHigh` is simpler than string comparison in templates and HTML generators.

4. **Share AI task templates.** One well-crafted writer task serves all criteria. Prompt improvements benefit every section simultaneously.

5. **Deterministic bookends around AI.** Pre-compute (deterministic) -> AI scoring (judgment) -> Post-compute (deterministic). This maximizes reliability and reproducibility.

## Node-by-Node Configuration

### trigger (agentInputTrigger)

| Field | Variant A | Variant B |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| Schema | `{ name, website, linkedin, company_id? }` | `{ entities: [{ name, website, linkedin }] }` |
| runOutput | Single entity test data | Array of 2-3 entities |

### dim_N (parallelai)

| Field | Variant A | Variant B |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| Action | `task` | `task_group` |
| Processor | Per-dimension: `base`, `core`, or `pro` | Same tiers |
| Input params | `manual` with `{{trigger.name}}`, etc. | Same references (parallelai handles the array internally) |
| Instructions | Empty or dimension-specific guidance | Same |
| outputSchema | Dimension-specific fields with sources | Same |

### consolidate (customScript)

**Variant A** -- Simple spread merge:
```javascript
function func(d1, d2, d3, d4, d5, d6, d7) {
  return Object.assign({}, ...[d1,d2,d3,d4,d5,d6,d7]
    .map(o => (o && typeof o === 'object' ? o : {})));
}
```

**Variant B** -- Index-aligned array merge:
```javascript
function func(d1, d2, d3, basic_info) {
  const maxLen = Math.max(d1?.length||0, d2?.length||0, d3?.length||0);
  const result = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < maxLen; i++) {
    result.push(Object.assign({},
      basic_info?.[i] || {},
      d1?.[i] || {}, d2?.[i] || {}, d3?.[i] || {}));
  }
  return result;
}
```

### assessment / assess (aiTask)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Type | `aiTask` |
| Task ID | **Same task for both variants** (DRY principle) |
| Input | `variable` handler for complex objects, `manual` for strings |
| Output | Structured scoring: `{ tier, total_score, dimension_scores, gate_results, buying_committee, outreach_sequence }` |

### sql_query (customScript -- Variant A only)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Purpose | Generate INSERT/UPDATE SQL deterministically |
| Inputs | `data` from assessment, `company_id` from trigger |
| Logic | If `company_id` exists: UPDATE. If absent: INSERT with `GENERATE_UUID()`. MERGE for people. |
| Why customScript | SQL syntax must be exact. AI-generated SQL risks syntax errors and injection. |

### synthesize (customScript -- Variant B only)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Purpose | Compress full assessments to ~460 tokens per entity |
| Input | Full assessment array from loop |
| Output | Compact text optimized for LLM context window consumption |

## Customization Points

- **SWAP:DIMENSION** -- Change the research dimensions. Sales qualification might use firmographics + automation + hiring + decision makers. Due diligence might use financials + legal + ESG + management.
- **SWAP:SAME_TASK** -- Share the assessment AI task between Variant A and Variant B. One prompt definition, two workflow topologies.
- **SWAP:DATABASE** -- Replace BigQuery with any database plugin. Replace the sql_query customScript with the appropriate SQL dialect.
- **SWAP:SCORING_MODEL** -- The assessment AI task defines the scoring rubric. Change the output schema to match your evaluation criteria (e.g., MEDDIC, BANT, custom rubric).
- **SWAP:OUTPUT** -- For Variant B, replace synthesize with a different compression strategy. Adjust tokens-per-entity based on downstream consumer needs.

## Testing Strategy

1. **Test one parallelai node first** -- Verify it returns substantive research with the correct processor tier. Inspect output via `nexus execution node-result`.
2. **Test consolidate** -- Verify the spread merge produces a single object with all dimension fields.
3. **Test assessment** -- Verify the AI task produces the expected scoring schema. Check that all gates, scores, and recommendations are populated.
4. **Test sql_query (Variant A)** -- Verify SQL is syntactically correct. Check INSERT vs UPDATE logic based on `company_id` presence.
5. **Test synthesize (Variant B)** -- Verify token count is in range. Check that key data points are preserved in compressed form.
6. **End-to-end** -- Run with a known entity. Verify scores are reasonable. For Variant A, verify database record was created.

## Customization Points

- **SWAP:IMAGE_GENERATION** -- Replace the sub-workflow call with a direct image API plugin, or remove image generation entirely for text-only content.
- **SWAP:DUPLICATE** -- In Variant B, the downstream pipeline (write + image + assemble) is duplicated across both branches. For simpler maintenance, converge the branches before write_content using a customScript that merges research data.
- **SWAP:PERPLEXITY_MODEL** -- Use `sonar-pro` for all searches (consistent quality, as in #14/#15) or tier models (sonar for follow-ups, sonar-pro for primary).
- **SWAP:CONTENT_TYPE** -- Replace the write_content AI task prompt for different formats: blog post, email newsletter, presentation script, social media thread.
- **SWAP:RESEARCH_DEPTH** -- Add more loops (e.g., a third research phase after gap-fill) or remove the gap-fill loop for simpler content that does not need exhaustive fact coverage.

## Testing Strategy

1. **Test initial_search** -- Verify Perplexity returns substantive content AND `related_questions` array.
2. **Test research_expansion loop** -- Run one iteration. Verify `{question, answer}` pairing works.
3. **Test storyline** -- Verify the AI produces `missing_facts[]` (not empty). If empty, adjust the prompt or topic to require more research.
4. **Test gap_fill loop** -- Verify missing facts are researched and paired correctly.
5. **Test write_content** -- Verify the output is publication-quality content, not a summary of research.
6. **Test image_generator** -- Verify the sub-workflow or API returns a valid image URL.
7. **Test assemble** -- Verify the JSONata expression produces `{ copy, image }`.
8. **For Variant B** -- Test the humanInput node. Verify structured output with `storyline[]` and `extra_searches[]`. Test both branches: empty extra_searches (no-extra path) and non-empty (extra-search path).

### deduplicate (customScript -- Variant A)

```javascript
function func(all_results) {
  const seen = {};
  const unique = [];
  for (const item of all_results.flat()) {
    if (!item?.url || seen[item.url]) continue;
    seen[item.url] = true;
    unique.push(item);
  }
  return { articles: unique.sort((a, b) => (b.relevance_score || 0) - (a.relevance_score || 0)) };
}
```

### deliver (plugin -- Slack)

| Param | Handler | Value |
|-------|---------|-------|
| `text` | variable | `{{generate_digest}}` |
| `mrkdwn` | manual | `true` |
| `users` or `conversation` | manual | Slack user ID or channel ID |

## Customization Points

- **SWAP:CONFIG_SOURCE** -- Replace Google Sheets with any config source: Notion database, Airtable, JSON file, API endpoint.
- **SWAP:CONTENT_SOURCE** -- Replace the news API with any content source: RSS feeds, social media APIs, web scraping, internal databases.
- **SWAP:DELIVERY_CHANNEL** -- Replace Slack with email (Gmail plugin), Microsoft Teams, webhook, or database write.
- **SWAP:DATE** -- Set startDate to tomorrow for daily, 1st of next month for monthly. Compute `fromDate` dynamically in customScript rather than hardcoding.
- **SWAP:BOUNDS** -- Add endDate for time-bounded monitoring campaigns (e.g., one calendar year).

## Testing Strategy

1. **Test config loading** -- Verify Google Sheets reads return expected keyword/dimension data.
2. **Test query construction** -- Verify boolean queries are syntactically correct and combinatorial coverage is complete.
3. **Test one fetch** -- Verify the content source API returns results for the constructed query.
4. **Test normalization** -- Verify raw API fields map correctly to standard schema.
5. **Test scoring/filtering** -- Verify the AI correctly identifies relevant vs irrelevant items. Check that chain-of-thought reasoning matches the assigned score.
6. **Test deduplication** -- Verify duplicate URLs are removed and sort order is correct.
7. **Test digest generation** -- Verify the AI produces a well-formatted, readable digest.
8. **Test delivery** -- Verify the message arrives in the correct Slack channel/DM with proper formatting (mrkdwn enabled).

# Template: Multi-Stage Pipeline (Orchestrator + Sub-Workflows)

## When to Use

**Objective:** Decompose a complex end-to-end process into independently testable sub-workflows, coordinated by a thin orchestrator that handles cross-cutting concerns (document generation, email delivery).

**Complexity:** High (65+ total nodes across all workflows). The orchestrator itself is simple (4-8 nodes), but the system involves multiple published workflows.

Use this template when:
- Total node count would exceed ~20 if built as a single workflow
- Stages have natural data transformation boundaries (discovery -> enrichment -> evaluation -> delivery)
- Sub-workflows need to be reusable in multiple contexts
- Different stages use different tools/credentials
- You need alternative entry points (full pipeline vs partial pipeline)

## Complete Node Graph

## Data Flow End-to-End

```
Input: {
  search_params: { title_variants, geography, source_companies, ... },
  evaluation_context: { client, position, scoring_weights },
  emails: ["client@example.com"]
}
  |
  [stage_1: Search] receives: search_params only
    -> discovers 50-200 entity skeletons: [{ name, identifier }]
  |
  [stage_2: Enrich] receives: stage_1 output (skeletons)
    -> enriches each to 8-sub-object profiles
  |
  [stage_3: Score] receives: stage_2 output + evaluation_context
    -> produces scored entities with dimensional breakdowns
  |
  [generate] -> formatted report document (URL)
  |
  [prep_email] -> branded HTML with summary table + download link
  |
  [send_email] -> email delivered
  |
  [output] -> { document_url, email_status }
```

### Data Contracts Between Stages

```
Stage 1 output -> Stage 2 input:
  { name: string, identifier: string }[]
  Minimal skeleton. Discovery produces only fields needed to locate the entity.

Stage 2 output -> Stage 3 input:
  { identity: {...}, career: {...}, education: {...}, skills: {...}, ... }
  Full structured profile. Enrichment guarantees this schema regardless of API response.

Stage 3 output -> Document generation:
  { assessment: string, dim_a_score: number, ..., composite_score: number }
  Flat structure suitable for template variables.
```

### Static Context (passed through, not transformed)

```
evaluation_context: { client, position, scoring_weights }
```

These objects flow from the orchestrator trigger to Stage 3 unchanged. They are never modified by intermediate stages. The orchestrator routes them directly.

## Node-by-Node Configuration

### trigger (agentInputTrigger -- Orchestrator)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Schema | Union of all sub-workflow inputs + `emails` for delivery |
| runOutput | Full test data covering all stages |

The orchestrator carries the complete input and selectively forwards subsets to each stage.

### stage_N (workflow nodes)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Type | `workflow` |
| Sub-workflow ID | The published workflow ID |
| Parameter passing | `variable` handler for all params |

**Selective forwarding -- each stage gets ONLY what it needs:**

| Stage | Receives | Does NOT receive |
|-------|----------|-----------------|
| stage_1 (Search) | `search_params` | evaluation_context, emails |
| stage_2 (Enrich) | `stage_1` output | search_params, evaluation_context, emails |
| stage_3 (Score) | `stage_2` output + `evaluation_context` | search_params, emails |

This is the **principle of least privilege** applied to data flow.

### generate (generateDocument)

| Param | Handler | Value |
|-------|---------|-------|
| `data` | variable | `{{stage_3}}` |

### prep_email (customScript)

| Input | Source |
|-------|--------|
| `document_url` | `{{generate.url}}` |
| `data` | `{{stage_3}}` |

Generates complete HTML with branding. Typically includes a summary table and download link.

| Param | Handler | Value |
|-------|---------|-------|
| `to` | variable | `{{trigger.emails}}` |
| `subject` | manual | `[Report] {{trigger.evaluation_context.client.name}}` |
| `body` | manual | `{{prep_email}}` |
| `bodyType` | manual | `html` |

## Customization Points

- **SWAP:STAGE_NAME** -- Name each stage for your domain: search/enrich/score, discover/analyze/report, ingest/process/deliver.
- **SWAP:WORKFLOW_ID** -- Point each workflow node to your published sub-workflow ID.
- **SWAP:EMAIL_PROVIDER** -- Replace Gmail with Outlook, SendGrid, or skip email entirely.
- **SWAP:STAGE_COUNT** -- Add or remove stages. The SESR system uses 3 stages. Simpler pipelines might use 2. More complex ones might use 4-5.
- **SWAP:MICRO_ORCHESTRATOR** -- Create additional micro-orchestrators for alternative entry points. If users sometimes have entities already discovered, create a 2-stage orchestrator (Enrich + Score) that skips Search.

## Testing Strategy

1. **Test each sub-workflow in isolation first.**
   - Stage 1: Provide search params, verify entity skeletons are returned.
   - Stage 2: Provide entity skeletons, verify enriched profiles.
   - Stage 3: Provide enriched profiles + context, verify scores.

2. **Test data contracts between stages.** Verify that Stage 1's output schema exactly matches Stage 2's input schema. A mismatch here causes silent failures.

3. **Test the orchestrator.** Run end-to-end with a small input (2-3 entities). Verify each sub-workflow completes and data flows correctly through the chain.

4. **Test document generation.** Verify the template fills correctly with Stage 3 output.

5. **Test email delivery.** Verify the email arrives with correct formatting, subject, and download link.

6. **Test the micro-orchestrator.** Provide entities directly (skip Stage 1). Verify Enrich + Score produce correct output.

## When NOT to Use This Pattern

- **Total nodes under ~20** -- Just build one workflow. The sub-workflow overhead adds complexity without benefit.
- **Stages are not reusable** -- If there is only one entry point and no stage will ever be called independently, decomposition adds indirection without gaining reusability.
- **Data contracts are unstable** -- If the schema between stages is changing frequently, ripple effects across workflows are painful. Stabilize contracts first.
- **Purely linear with no branching** -- A flat sequence of 5 nodes does not benefit from sub-workflow decomposition. The overhead exceeds the clarity gain.

```bash
    { "ref": "query", "type": "aiTask", "label": "query_builder" },
    { "ref": "research", "type": "plugin", "label": "research" },
    { "ref": "structure", "type": "aiTask", "label": "structurer" },
    { "ref": "out", "type": "outputNode", "label": "output",
      "data": { "outputType": "previous" } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "source": "@trigger", "target": "@query" },
    { "source": "@query", "target": "@research" },
    { "source": "@research", "target": "@structure" },
    { "source": "@structure", "target": "@out" }
  ]
}' --json
```

### Variant B: Deep Multi-Dimensional (12 nodes)

Based on #08 SearchCompany v2.

```
[agentInputTrigger] trigger
  label: trigger
  schema: { entity: { name, website_url, geography, context } }
     |
     v
SWAP:PREPROCESSING -- website scrape, context extraction, or skip
[plugin] scrape_website
  label: scrape_website
  tool: Exa API (getContents)
     |
     v
[customScript] extract_context
  label: extract_context
  purpose: pull summary/description from scrape result
     |
     +---> [parallelai] dimension_1 (SWAP:DIMENSION)
     +---> [parallelai] dimension_2 (SWAP:DIMENSION)
     +---> [parallelai] dimension_3 (SWAP:DIMENSION)
     |         |               |
     v         v               v
[aiTask] norm_1    [aiTask] norm_2    [aiTask] norm_3
  (SWAP:NORMALIZER)   ...              ...
     |         |               |
     +----+----+-------+-------+
          |
          v
[customScript] merge
  label: merge
  purpose: flat Object.assign merge of all normalizer outputs
     |
     v
[outputNode] output
  label: output
  outputType: previous
```

#### Scaffold

```bash
nexus api POST /workflows/$WF_ID/batch --body '{
  "nodes": [
    { "ref": "scrape", "type": "plugin", "label": "scrape_website" },
    { "ref": "extract", "type": "customScript", "label": "extract_context" },
    { "ref": "dim1", "type": "parallelai", "label": "dimension_1" },
    { "ref": "dim2", "type": "parallelai", "label": "dimension_2" },
    { "ref": "dim3", "type": "parallelai", "label": "dimension_3" },
    { "ref": "norm1", "type": "aiTask", "label": "normalize_1" },
    { "ref": "norm2", "type": "aiTask", "label": "normalize_2" },
    { "ref": "norm3", "type": "aiTask", "label": "normalize_3" },
    { "ref": "merge", "type": "customScript", "label": "merge" },
    { "ref": "out", "type": "outputNode", "label": "output",
      "data": { "outputType": "previous" } }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "source": "@trigger", "target": "@scrape" },
    { "source": "@scrape", "target": "@extract" },
    { "source": "@extract", "target": "@dim1" },
    { "source": "@extract", "target": "@dim2" },
    { "source": "@extract", "target": "@dim3" },
    { "source": "@dim1", "target": "@norm1" },
    { "source": "@dim2", "target": "@norm2" },
    { "source": "@dim3", "target": "@norm3" },
    { "source": "@norm1", "target": "@merge" },
    { "source": "@norm2", "target": "@merge" },
    { "source": "@norm3", "target": "@merge" },
    { "source": "@merge", "target": "@out" }
  ]
}' --json
```

## Data Flow End-to-End

### Variant A

```
Input: { first_name: "Jane", last_name: "Doe", email: "jane@acme.com" }
  |
  [query_builder] -> "Find professional background of Jane Doe, email domain
                      acme.com suggests she works at Acme Corp..."
  |
  [research] -> { message: { content: "Jane Doe is VP Engineering at Acme..." },
                  citations: [...] }
  |
  [structurer] -> { full_name: "Jane Doe", current_title: "VP Engineering",
                    current_company: "Acme Corp", industry: "Software",
                    linkedin_url: "...", confidence: "high" }
  |
  [output] -> passthrough
```

### Variant B

```
Input: { entity: { name: "Waterland", website_url: "waterlandpe.com",
                    geography: "Europe", context: "PE value chain..." } }
  |
  [scrape_website] -> { results: [{ summary: "European PE firm...", text: "..." }] }
  |
  [extract_context] -> "European private equity firm specializing in..."
  |
  [dimension_1: Profile] -> { legal_name, employee_count, geography, ... }
  [dimension_2: Financials] -> { revenue_history[], ebitda_history[], ... }
  [dimension_3: Leadership] -> { top_management[], ownership_structure, ... }
  |
  [norm_1] -> { company: "Waterland", country: "Netherlands", description: "..." }
  [norm_2] -> { revenue: "2.5B EUR", EBITDA: "...", number_FTE: 250 }
  [norm_3] -> { contact_first_name: "...", ownership_management_value: 85 }
  |
  [merge] -> { company, country, description, revenue, EBITDA, number_FTE,
               contact_first_name, ..., valuechain_step1_presence: true, ... }
  |
  [output] -> passthrough (flat ~35-field JSON)
```

## Node-by-Node Configuration

### trigger (agentInputTrigger)

| Field | Variant A | Variant B |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| Schema | `{ first_name, last_name, email }` | `{ entity: { name, website_url, geography, context } }` |
| runOutput | Realistic test data matching schema | Same |

### query_builder (aiTask -- Variant A only)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Type | `aiTask` |
| Purpose | Generate optimized search query |
| parametersSetup | All fields use `handler: "variable"`, each referencing a trigger field |
| Output | String (the search query) |

### research / scrape_website (plugin)

| Field | Variant A (Perplexity) | Variant B (Exa) |
|-------|------------------------|-----------------|
| Tool | Perplexity | Exa API |
| Action | search | getContents |
| Key params | `model: sonar-deep-research`, `content: variable`, `temperature: 0.1` | `ids: [website_url]`, `livecrawlTimeout: 10000` |

### dimension_N (parallelai -- Variant B)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Type | `parallelai` |
| Action | `task` |
| Processor | `base` / `core` / `pro` (per dimension) |
| Input params | `manual` handler with `{{trigger.entity.name}}`, `{{extract_context}}`, etc. |
| Instructions | Empty -- guided by `outputSchema` field descriptions |
| outputSchema | Dimension-specific fields with detailed descriptions including search strategies |

### norm_N (aiTask -- Variant B)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Type | `aiTask` |
| Purpose | Normalize parallelai output into flat database-ready fields |
| Input | `manual` handler composing entity info + parallelai dimension output |
| Output | Flat JSON with `_source` companion fields for provenance |

### merge (customScript -- Variant B)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Type | `customScript` |
| Inputs | One per normalizer: `{ name: "json_1", node: "{{norm_1_uuid}}" }` |
| Function | `Object.assign({}, ...inputs.map(o => o && typeof o === 'object' ? o : {}))` |

### output (outputNode)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Type | `outputNode` |
| outputType | `previous` -- structured data passthrough, no LLM invocation |

## Customization Points

- **SWAP:PREPROCESSING** -- Replace Exa website scrape with any context-gathering step. Skip entirely if no preprocessing needed (Variant A has none).
- **SWAP:DIMENSION** -- Add, remove, or reconfigure parallelai research dimensions. Each is independent. Adjust processor tiers based on research depth needed.
- **SWAP:NORMALIZER** -- Replace aiTask normalizers with customScript if the parallelai output is already structured enough. Use aiTask when raw research text needs interpretation to extract consistent field values.
- **SWAP:OUTPUT_SCHEMA** -- Define your domain's output fields in the structurer (Variant A) or normalizer tasks (Variant B).
- **SWAP:PERPLEXITY_MODEL** -- Use `sonar-deep-research` for maximum depth, `sonar-pro` for balanced quality/cost, `sonar` for cheap supplementary queries.

## Testing Strategy

1. **Test trigger first** -- Set realistic `runOutput` data. Verify trigger node produces expected output.
2. **Test query_builder / scrape_website** -- Verify it produces a usable query or successfully scrapes the website.
3. **Test research / parallelai nodes** -- Verify research returns substantive content with citations. Check processor tier produces appropriate depth.
4. **Test structurer / normalizers** -- Verify output matches expected schema. Check all fields are populated. Verify `_source` fields contain real citations.
5. **Test merge** -- Verify all normalizer outputs are merged without field collisions.
6. **End-to-end** -- Run full workflow with a known entity. Compare output against manually verified facts.

## Source Workflows

| Variant | Workflow | ID | Nodes |
|---------|----------|----|----|
| A (Simple) | Basic Person Enrichment | `3f0efc00` | 5 |
| B (Deep) | SearchCompany v2 | `4af08cae` | 12 |

---
name: nexus-workflow-executions
description: Views workflow execution history, debugs failed runs, inspects node-level results, retries failed nodes, and exports execution data via the Public API v1.
---

# Nexus Workflow Executions

Debug WF runs + inspect node-level results. Setup/envelope → CLAUDE.md.

!! **Used during WF building too**, not just post-hoc debugging. `nexus execution node-result` is essential during `nexus-workflow-builder` Phase 3 — when a tested node's `outputFormat` is empty, `node-result` is authoritative for discovering output field names (string fields → `manual` w/ `{{ref}}`, complex types → `variable`). !!

CLI ↔ Dashboard sync: node tests via CLI persist `testExecutionId` in API responses; dashboard updates in real-time.

## CLI

```bash
nexus execution list [--workflow-id] [--status] [--start-date] [--end-date] [--limit] --json
nexus execution get <id> --json                  # workflowId, status, startedAt, duration, nodeStatusCounts, triggerType, error
nexus execution diagnose <id> [--verbose] --json # all nodes w/ status, timing, errors
nexus execution poll [id] --json                  # poll until complete/timeout
nexus execution output <id> --json
nexus execution node-result <id> <nodeId> --json # input/output/logs/duration per node
nexus execution retry <id> <nodeId> --json
nexus execution export <id> --json                # returns { url } for full JSON download
```

## Node Result — discovery pattern (per R#20)

`node-result` returns the REAL output structure. Use it BEFORE configuring downstream references. Empty `outputFormat` ≠ "no data" — it means node hasn't run yet. Test top-to-bottom; inspect `node-result` per node; discover real field names; configure next.

As of 2026-07 the typed introspection commands (`diagnose`/`node-result`) can 500 on some executions — the raw `nexus api GET /workflows/<wfId>/executions/<execId>` (carrying `nodeResults`) is the fallback read; retest on next use + supersede this note when they hold.

**Poll a parent by execId, never by enumerating the list:** a parallel loop's children appear as their OWN executions and flood `execution list` — the parent run you are tracking may not appear at all (an orchestrator scanning the list concludes "never ran" and re-fires). Capture the execId at fire time → `execution poll <execId>` (workflow-builder gotcha 66).

## Retry — fresh-upstream-state pattern (per R#5)

Failed node needs fresh upstream state (original email archived, CRM record updated) before retry will succeed? Recreate it w/ `nexus external-tool execute` BEFORE calling retry. Otherwise retry replays against stale data and fails identically.

E.g., `nexus external-tool execute <gmailId> --action gmail-find-email --input '{"q":"from:alice@example.com newer_than:1d"}' --credential <credId> --json` to confirm trigger email exists. Full → `nexus-tool-execute/TOOL_EXECUTION_GUIDE.md`.

## Execution Statuses

| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| PENDING | Queued, not started |
| RUNNING | Currently executing |
| COMPLETED | Finished successfully |
| FAILED | Encountered an error |

## General-context integration

Workspace at `${GENERAL_CONTEXT_PATH}`.

### READ before debugging

| Need to know | Path | Read mode |
|---|---|---|
| System-specific runbook | `/systems/<system>/runbook.md` | Whole-file |
| Prior similar incidents (system-bound) | `/systems/<system>/learnings.md` | Grep H2 for keyword |
| Cross-system silent-acceptance / debugging patterns | `/knowledge/learnings/*.md` | Frontmatter scan |
| Tool-side gotchas implicated in failure | `/tools/<tool>.md` "## Gotchas" | Grep |

### WRITE PULSE (during work, per CLAUDE.md R#34 — dispatch the background consolidation subagent on discovery)

| Trigger event | Workspace target | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| New silent-acceptance variant beyond G#20 catalog (org-specific instance) | `/knowledge/learnings/silent-acceptance-variants.md` | Append H2 |
| Recovery procedure discovered (fresh-upstream-state trick / retry boundary) (org-specific) | `/systems/<system>/runbook.md` "## Recovery — <cause>" | Append section |
| Tool quirk surfaced via execution failure (org-specific) | `/tools/<tool>.md` "## Gotchas" | Append H3 |
| **Cross-org** silent-acceptance variant (vendor-side / platform-side, not org config) | `$SYSTEMS_PATH/workflows/<pattern>/lessons.md` | Append H2 |
| **Cross-org** tool quirk surfaced (vendor-side) | `$TOOLS_PATH/plugins/<tool>/gotchas.md` | Append H3 |

(Universal PULSE triggers from R#34 also apply: tool gotcha, CLI quirk, glossary term — see CLAUDE.md.)

### WRITE FINAL (end-of-build, postmortem complete)

| Milestone | Content | Path | Mode | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Incident postmortem (system-specific cause) | Postmortem | `/systems/<system>/learnings.md` | Append H2 | `templates/learning.md` |
| Cross-system pattern (debugging trick / silent-fail variant beyond known) | Lesson | `/knowledge/learnings/<topic>.md` | New-file or Append H2 | `templates/learning.md` |
| Recovery procedure (newly discovered) | Runbook update | `/systems/<system>/runbook.md` "## Recovery — <cause>" | Append section | (inline) |
| Tool quirk surfaced via execution failure | Quirk + workaround | `/tools/<tool>.md` "## Gotchas" | Append H3 | (inline) |

### WRONG / RIGHT

✗ Execution failed (`runOutput` PATCH silent-dropped on aiTask) → debug + fix + move on, lesson never filed → ✓ append to `/knowledge/learnings/silent-acceptance-variants.md` + cross-link from `/systems/<system>/learnings.md`.
