# Shared governance — knowledge domains

## Search-then-propose pattern (canonical for trio)

Per-query algorithm when user needs a tool:

1. **Intent parse** — workspace=`tools`, filters from message (outcome verb, vendor name, action keyword).
2. **Grep frontmatter (3 categories):**
   - Plugins: `ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}; T=$(ws_path tools /mnt/workspace/_shared/tools); grep -l 'outcomes:.*<outcome>' "$T"/plugins/*/README.md` (vendor folders under `plugins/` — resolve the real layout from `$TOOLS_PATH/INDEX.md`)
   - Scripts: `grep -l 'category:.*<cat>' "$T"/scripts/*/*.md` or `grep -l 'outcomes:.*<outcome>' "$T"/scripts/*/*.md`
   - AI tasks: `grep -l 'category:.*<cat>' "$T"/ai-tasks/*/*.md` or `grep -rln '<field>' "$T"/ai-tasks/*/*.md`
3. **Read abstracts:** `head -40 <candidate>/README.md` per match (frontmatter + Summary + Use-when + Do-NOT).
4. **AUQ propose pros/cons** w/ 2-3 candidates (each: Display name + Summary excerpt + 2 pros + 1 con).
5. **On user pick** → full Read of selected tool's README + relevant sub-files.

**Edge cases:** no matches → cascade to layer 4 (web); too many → narrow w/ secondary filter; ambiguous → AUQ user "search by outcome / vendor / action?"

**Scale it (many candidates / ambiguous):** run this algorithm via parallel scout discovery — snapshot INDEX-shortlisted files local, fan out fast read-only scouts, consolidate, Cue reads winners → `../SKILL.md "## Parallel scout discovery"`.

Same algorithm for systems (T2) + use-cases (T3) — substitute the domain GUIDE's grep-pattern table at step 2.

## Additive growth + deprecation

**Additive growth (canonical → R#42 for rule).** Before scaffolding a NEW leaf: `ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}; grep -rl '<vendor|outcome|data-op>' "$(ws_path tools /mnt/workspace/_shared/tools)"/` for close match. ≥1 → AUQ: (a) append `## Org variants` to `<existing>/variants.md`; (b) `## Solution variations`; (c) new leaf (justify). Default (a). NEW leaf → scaffold artifact set + empty `variants.md` SAME write. L-axis values (vendor / scripts category / ai-tasks category) are SEED vocab in `taxonomy-schema.md` → workspace `taxonomy.md` — NEVER invent; AUQ to extend / re-bucket (appends the workspace CHANGELOG). Reorg only on audit red-flags / user request. **Provisional first instance:** a novel, verified, valuable entry with NO fitting L-axis value MAY open the new value immediately (Cue: AUQ per R#42; the userless FLEET: silent-MECE lane → `taxonomy-schema.md "## Extension protocol"`), marked `provisional` + an INDEX note vs any ≥2-instance guideline; graduates on the 2nd cross-org instance or re-buckets at audit. Mis-filing into an ill-fitting category to satisfy a count is the worse outcome.

**Deprecation + archive (canonical).**
- **In-place:** frontmatter `status: deprecated` + `superseded_by: <slug>`; body H2 `## DEPRECATED <date> — see <new>`. Content STAYS (R#35.1); filter via `grep status: active`.
- **Reorg-displaced:** `archive/<original-slug>-<date>.md`, frontmatter `status: archived` + `see_also: [<new path>]`. Audit prunes archive past retention.

## Anonymisation contract

The cross-org GATE every community write passes — no private paths · generalise org-proprietary vocabulary (not just names) · the worthiness/file-vs-skip bar — is `reference/community-kb-hygiene.md`. The contract below covers the artifact-level checks.

Cross-org artifacts (every entry under `$TOOLS_PATH/scripts/` or `$TOOLS_PATH/ai-tasks/`) MUST satisfy 5 checks (R#40):

1. **ID strip.** Production UUIDs / org-specific IDs removed via `jq walk` (delete `id` fields).
2. **Ordered (longest-first) 1:1 find/replace.** Replace named entities in longest-substring-first order. NEVER paraphrase; NEVER restructure.
3. **Audit field-level descriptions.** Scan schema `description` fields for entity leaks; replace.
4. **Preserve structural field names.** Schema names (`day_number`, `available`, ...) STAY — they're the contract. Only `description` content gets find/replace. Exception: a field name that itself carries an entity (e.g. `pack_<brand>_discount_eur`) → rename to its generic form + describe the token in `prompt_bindings:` (NOT a real-valued map entry) — the entity sweep (check 2) outranks name-preservation when the name identifies.
5. **The real substitution map never ships with the artifact.** The real→token map is a DE-ANONYMISATION KEY — recording it in ANY field (frontmatter, body, comments, slugs) re-publishes the org identity, internal system names, and any tokenised secret. It stays org-side (general-context) / re-derivable by diffing the org's live source. The artifact records ONLY: (a) `prompt_bindings:` — each token → `{kind, replace_with, example (INVENTED/generic, NEVER the real value), shape}`; (b) sanitized `anonymisation: {substitutions: <N>, residual_entity_scan: <0 | list>}`. A real example value in a binding is itself a leak — and so is PROSE about the anonymisation (a language-pair note, "numbers preserved exactly", a real-value count with its class): the record's disclosure floor is count + scan result only (`prompt-anonymisation-protocol.md` Step 2). HTML-comment: `<!-- find/replace + tokenisation only; real map is a de-anon key, held org-side, never here. -->`.
6. **Content-generalisation check (BEFORE any cross-org write — the R#34 3-Q tree's Q2 applied to CONTENT, not just names).** De-identification ≠ done. Org-bound VALUES — pricing/discount rules, promo schemes, routing targets, escalation maps, page selectors, security rules, **product-scope lists, term/translation glossaries, domain-fact enumerations, methodology vocabularies** — NEVER cross raw — and withholding is NOT the remedy either. Generalise: keep the COMPLETE structure / logic / technique, tokenise every org-bound value into a named `<PLACEHOLDER>` binding w/ a binding contract (the code/config analogue of the prompt protocol's Step 3), so an org with a similar problem rebinds and reuses. Real bindings ALWAYS also land org-side (general-context) w/ `canonical_source` cross-links. Large / value-dense artifacts (100K+ prompts, multi-K-line scripts) → deep-read via a subagent w/ an explicit extraction brief (entities · structural elements · value bindings to return) — never skim-and-abstract.
   ✗ 43K pricing script published w/ real promo rules intact (leak) · ✗ same script reduced to a topology-only "pricing-lookup pattern" README (value destroyed) → ✓ full script template, promo/discount rules tokenised to `<PROMO_RULES>`-style bindings + contract; real rules live in the org's general-context.

**Whole-artifact scope (all checks):** the leak surface is EVERY field, not just `description`/body — identity names, tool/credential UUIDs, per-channel content, `source_shape:` / HTML-`Source:` metadata, file slugs, and regional/dialect tells (locale-specific number/date words, postal formats, region-pinning vocabulary) are entity-equivalent → tokenise or omit. Real values live in general-context (T0) only.

**Audit-trail surfaces are INSIDE the contract:** a shared workspace's `_meta/` files (`CHANGELOG.md`, `consolidation-log.md`) are read cross-org like any entry — a CLI PROFILE SLUG used as an actor/client identifier ("--profile <org-slug>"), a log line QUOTING a pre-redaction value while narrating its removal, and a correction narrative that re-states the removed value are all leaks of the same class. Log/changelog narration names the leak CLASS ("a locale-pair market tell in <file>"), never the value or the pair; community-side logs carry community slugs + counts only.

System-bound instances (Tier-2 or `$GENERAL_CONTEXT_PATH/systems/<sys>/`) are exempt when the user owns the data; carry `canonical_source:` backref to the anonymised canonical.

**Prose prompts (ai-task `prompt.md`, agent `system-prompt-template.md`):** R#44 3-step extraction — verbatim copy, named-entity 1:1 find/replace, DEEP tokenisation (IVR codes / escalation maps / KB IDs / callable function names → `<PLACEHOLDER>` w/ `prompt_bindings:`). Full → `prompt-anonymisation-protocol.md`.

## Tier composition + filing tree (R#38 canonical)

**Filing decision tree:** atomic + reusable across systems → T1 (`$TOOLS_PATH`); composition into node arrangement / persona → T2 (`$SYSTEMS_PATH`); composition for stated problem + audience → T3 (`$USE_CASES_PATH`).

**Composition rules:** higher-tier MAY reference lower via path link; MUST NOT redefine inline. Lower-tier MUST NOT narrate higher composition. Backlinks (upward) frontmatter ONLY (`used_by_systems:` on T1, `used_by_use_cases:` on T2). Atomic content discovered during higher build → file at T1, not buried. **Same principle intra-workspace for unit FAMILIES (R#38 extended):** one canonical home per general UNIT; an instance holds a MANIFEST (ordered unit pointer rows + that instance's binding values), never a copy — a general unit duplicated across instance folders is drift by construction (consolidation §12 row 6 + §11b).

| # | Anti-pattern | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A | T1 buried in T2 dir (`$SYSTEMS_PATH/workflows/<pat>/scripts/<x>.md`) | File at `$TOOLS_PATH/scripts/<cat>/<x>.md` + backlink `used_by_systems: [<pat>]` |
| B | T2 inlines T1 schema (WF README repeats Gmail send-email params) | Replace w/ `see $TOOLS_PATH/<vendor>/actions/<action>.md` |
| C | T3 inlines T2 architecture | Replace w/ `see $SYSTEMS_PATH/workflows/<pat>/README.md` |
| D | T1 narrates T2 logic in prose | Backlinks in frontmatter only |
| E | Premature folderisation (new leaf = single-file folder, no `variants.md` slot) → 2nd org sprawls | Scaffold `README.md` + empty `variants.md` SAME write (R#42) |
| F | Org-custom external tool (CUSTOM_MANIFEST middleware) filed as a T1 vendor leaf | Not vendor-reusable: fold the TECHNIQUE into the consuming archetype/pattern `tools.md`; real endpoint/auth/spec → general-context |

✗ URL-canonicalising script filed at `$SYSTEMS_PATH/workflows/<pat>/scripts/README.md` → future builder re-authors → ✓ `$TOOLS_PATH/scripts/<cat>/<slug>.md` w/ `used_by_systems:` backlink.

**Required-artifact catalogs have ONE home:** per-tier required file sets + per-section requirements live in `domains/<tier>/completeness-gates.md` (authoritative); GUIDEs + writing-guide POINT there and never restate the lists — a restated list is the three-way-drift seed.

## Read + write modes

Standard modes → `../domains/general-context/GUIDE.md`. Frontmatter-scan: `ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}; grep -l '^auth_type: oauth2$' "$(ws_path tools …)"/plugins/*/README.md` (active OAuth); body-grep fallback `ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}; grep -rln '<keyword>' "$(ws_path tools …)"`. Writes: new-file (mkdir + template + Write + INDEX SAME Bash inv); append H3 for gotchas; replace only after AUQ on regression; frontmatter-bump `last_verified` after any edit. NEVER `mv` (R#35.3).

## INDEX.md + CHANGELOG + taxonomy + cross-refs

**INDEX CONTRACT (canonical — every workspace INDEX.md).** INDEX.md is the workspace's most important file: a pure navigational MAP answering WHERE everything is + WHAT it is used for. One ROW per entry: path · what it IS · when to go there (test-query phrasing). NEVER in INDEX: history / "Recent edits" / reorganisation narration (→ the workspace CHANGELOG), volatile state (counts / versions / "currently N" — the entity README owns state; the row owns purpose), run notes, dated "Added/Updated" row annotations. The boundary check and every retrieval read INDEX first — each non-navigational line taxes every session. Readability = the acceptance test: uniform row shape per section.
✗ a row "projects/x — proposal, 29 pages. Added 2026-06-20" — WHY WRONG: the count goes stale and the date is narration, so the map lies and bloats → ✓ "projects/x — the X engagement: proposals, meeting intel, deliverables. Go here for anything X." State lives in the project README; the addition event is one CHANGELOG line.

**INDEX INVARIANT (resolution + grain):** every index/Contents row RESOLVES to a live, non-empty unit —
a row whose target is empty/absent is a false "we have this", the worst find failure (the walker pays
the full walk and lands on nothing); scaffold rows are not created, and an inherited one is filled,
marked non-resolving, or removed on touch (DT-LINT). The write-side half already binds (one entity →
INDEX row in the same batch — maintenance below; R#35 #3) — this adds the GRAIN: the row sits at the
unit's ASKING grain (what a colleague would request by name), and folder `## Contents` tables are
DERIVED from the live listing at write time, never recalled (hand-maintained Contents measurably drift
within days of their folders).

**ROUTING FLOOR (the required half — bans alone don't route):** the INDEX also answers the WRITER's
question "what belongs here": every section/folder row carries its PURPOSE + a one-line test question
("Go here for X — does the atom answer X?"). A contents-only index routes READERS but leaves FILERS
guessing — under purpose lines, filers cite the folder's own test as their placement justification and
same-class knowledge stops splitting across sibling folders; without them it splits. CREATION binds too:
every home a write creates (`_meta/` files included) gets its row + purpose line in the SAME pass.
Static doctrine SECTIONS (vocab, cross-cutting guidance, purpose lines) are welcome — the ban is on
STATE (counts / history / narration), never on sections.

**CHANGELOG (per workspace).** ALL change-narration lives in the workspace's `_meta/CHANGELOG.md` (same home in all four workspaces): one line per event, newest-first (`- YYYY-MM-DD: <scope> — <what changed>`); reorganisation events append their FULL record here (date · scope · trigger · PRE→POST counts · gates passed). INDEX carries exactly ONE pointer section (`## Change history`) to it. Structural-health/audit counts are CHANGELOG-side too (an audit event line), never INDEX rows.

**INDEX.md maintenance:** every entity-write triggers parallel INDEX update. New tool README → append `## Entries` row `| <Display Name> | \`<slug>\` | <outcomes> | <auth_type> | active |`. New action subfile → no INDEX row (visible via tool README's Actions table). New gotcha → bump tool's `last_updated`. **Granularity:** one entity → INDEX row in the same batch. A multi-entry continuous write-phase (no user gate inside it) MAY batch all INDEX rows at phase end IF the close verifies leaves + INDEX server-side together; NEVER end a session with unindexed leaves.

**Recurring index rot = a WRITER audit, not an Nth spot fix.** A shared INDEX/Contents surface spot-fixed for the SAME defect class more than twice (falsely-"empty" rows, stale targets, phantom entries — recurrence visible in the workspace CHANGELOG / consolidation log) has a broken WRITING MECHANISM, not broken rows: the next action is a root-cause audit of the write path that produces the rows (which writer, from what evidence, at what moment rows are stamped — e.g. rows stamped from a pre-write snapshot instead of the live listing), and a fix at that mechanism. Another row-level sweep only resets the clock; each pass re-certifies a surface the mechanism will re-corrupt. ✗ the same false-"empty" row class fixed in three separate passes, no cause traced → a fourth sweep → ✓ the 3rd same-class fix triggers the writer audit; the mechanism is fixed, THEN one final sweep runs.

**Taxonomy extension:** new outcome/action/vendor not in `taxonomy.md` → AUQ before writing: "Term `<x>` not in vocab. (a) Add as new outcome; (b) Map to existing; (c) Free-form tag." On approve: append + bump last_verified.

**Cross-references:** forward in frontmatter (`related_use_cases:`/`related_systems:`); body links `... see $USE_CASES_PATH/<domain>/<problem>/README.md...`.

### Anonymisation mechanics (canonical for CLAUDE.md R#40)
Cross-org entries: anonymise via ordered (longest-first) 1:1 find/replace; NEVER rewrite or paraphrase. NO real org value in ANY field — body, frontmatter, comments, slugs — and NO private path: a community-KB file carries no general-context path / private slug anywhere; the org↔community bridge lives T0-side only (`community-kb-hygiene.md` §1). The real→token map is a DE-ANONYMISATION KEY: it never co-locates w/ the artifact (stays org-side / re-derivable by diffing the live source). Record only `prompt_bindings:` + a sanitized `anonymisation:` record (no real values); bound instances carry `canonical_source:` frontmatter.

### Ref-sweep recipe (canonical for CLAUDE.md R#35 #3)
`ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}; grep -rln "<old-slug>" "$(ws_path tools …)" "$(ws_path systems …)" "$(ws_path use-cases …)" "$(ws_path general-context …)"` → update inbound + parent-path variants SAME batch + verify 0 orphan; else forwarding stub at `<old>/README.md`.

# Taxonomy schema — knowledge domains (T1 / T2 / T3)

Defines the SHAPE of each workspace-root `taxonomy.md` (`$TOOLS_PATH` / `$SYSTEMS_PATH` / `$USE_CASES_PATH`). Workspace-side `taxonomy.md` carries the actual canonical values; this schema specifies what fields each must have + how to extend. Seed vocab below is extensible/re-bucketable via AUQ — NOT fixed law.

## Extension protocol (a term/category not in the vocab — all tiers, two actor lanes)

| Actor | Lane |
|---|---|
| **Cue** (a user is present) | AUQ: "Term `<x>` not in vocab. (a) Add as new <category>; (b) Map to existing `<closest match>`; (c) Free-form tag — skip taxonomy." On (a): `Edit <workspace>/taxonomy.md` — append under the right H2, bump `last_verified`, use the term in the entry frontmatter. |
| **The consolidation FLEET** (userless — it cannot AUQ) | SILENT-MECE, in order: (1) **FIT-FIRST** — re-read the existing categories' SEMANTICS (taxonomy + INDEX purpose lines) and map to the closest honest fit — the existing name always beats a synonym you would coin (isolated writers otherwise coin two names for one category); (2) genuinely-no-fit AND the entry belongs → **CREATE the value, marked `provisional`, fully documented in the SAME batch**: append under its H2 + bump `last_verified` + one CHANGELOG line + the INDEX purpose row for any new shelf — ALL categories documented, the set kept MECE, count minimised; (3) **graduation** — the 2nd cross-org instance ratifies (drop `provisional`) or the audit re-buckets. NEVER refuse-to-file for lack of a category; NEVER coin a value without documenting it; mis-filing into an ill-fitting category to satisfy a count is the worse outcome. |

✗ three same-day runs meet the same missing category: one REFUSES to file ("AUQ-gated — I can't ask"),
one silently creates TWO undocumented values, one creates a documented provisional — one rule, three
behaviors, two of them damaging. ✓ every userless run takes the fleet lane: fit-first, else
provisional + documented + MECE, graduating on the 2nd instance.

**Enum enforcement (all axes, all tiers):** L-axis + frontmatter enum values are canonical SEED vocab —
NEVER invent a value in a folder name or frontmatter outside these two lanes (Cue: AUQ; fleet:
silent-MECE; both append the workspace CHANGELOG).

## Cross-tier consistency (internal)

- **T2 `problem_domain` vs T3 `domain`** are DIFFERENT grains, not a synced enum. T3 `domain` = the coarse 8-value business-function L1 tree axis (folders; AUQ-gated). T2 `problem_domain` = free finer-grained kebab-case vocab (live values like `b2c-sales`, `content-operations`). The join = systems INDEX "By problem domain" cross-cut + `related_systems:` frontmatter on T3 entries. (A hard sync rule existed and died in practice — finer T2 vocab is more useful for search than enum purity.)
- **T1 outcomes bridge vocab:** when extending `outcomes` in tools, check whether a similar concept exists in T2 `problem_domain` or T3 `domain`; bridge when concepts overlap (e.g. tool outcome `send-msg` ↔ messaging-heavy support domains; `store-data` ↔ `parallel-fan-in` output sinks).

# Workspace audit checklist (structural health + reorg triggers)

Tier-3 structural audit. Fires periodically OR on threshold OR user request. **Default outcome = ADD, not reorganise** (R#42 / R#33) — reorg only when ≥2 quantitative red flags OR a semantic flag fires. Reorganising the enum/tree as the DB matures is SANCTIONED (via `workspace-migration-runbook.md`), not a freeze.

## Quantitative red flags
- [ ] L1 folder count > 10
- [ ] L2 folder count > 30
- [ ] any single L2 has > 8 leaves
- [ ] median L2 has only 1 leaf (premature deepening — L1 acting as a leaf)
- [ ] > 50% of leaves are 1-file folders after 30 days (additive growth not happening → check variants.md exists)
- [ ] ≥ 3 leaves match the SAME parsed signal in the last 5 writes (sprawl-by-similar-naming → should have been variants)

## Semantic red flags
- [ ] two L2 names that could reasonably hold the same content (MECE collision)
- [ ] a folder name contains a company / engagement / industry / person token (axis violation — should be frontmatter)
- [ ] a leaf has no `variants.md` AND ≥1 sibling that could merge into it
- [ ] **the taxonomy enum itself has grown non-MECE / too coarse / too sparse as the DB matured → re-bucket the axis** (e.g. a function bucket now holds 20 leaves spanning 3 sub-functions → split; or 3 buckets each hold 1 leaf → merge)
- [ ] deprecated/tombstoned entries surfacing in default discovery (status filter broken)
- [ ] an INDEX/Contents row whose target is EMPTY or absent — a scaffold row, a false "we have this" (INDEX INVARIANT → `shared-governance.md`)
- [ ] a filed unit with no row at its ASKING grain — Contents drift; the designed walk (INDEX → folder README → row → unit) dead-ends while the unit exists
- [ ] a catalog row whose hook cannot be phrased as a real ask, or two rows that always co-travel (over-decomposition — coalesce per the consolidation spine's Row 6 calibration)
- [ ] a "template"/composite manifest with a single instantiation and no stated reuse intent (AR-3 — fold back into its instance manifest)

## Action on trigger
AUQ: "(a) leave as-is (justify); (b) merge two leaves; (c) extend/re-bucket an L-axis enum (justify, appends reorg-history); (d) full reorg via migration-runbook." Default surface, never autonomous reorg — this binds USER-FACING sessions. The consolidation FLEET (userless) runs the same triggers autonomously behind its six-gate rail + CHANGELOG record (fleet §19a.1); leaf-level correction is its normal job; only skeleton-level changes are surfaced.

## Integrity sweep (run anytime, cheap-ish)
- `grep -rln '<recently-renamed-slug>'` → 0 orphans.
- INDEX.md row count == entity-folder count (per workspace).
- every leaf has `variants.md`; every entity has the 5 mandatory frontmatter fields.

# Workspace migration runbook (6 gates)

Multi-file workspace mutation (≥3 moves OR any folder rename OR L-axis enum re-bucket OR audit-flagged reorg). Workspace is FUSE-backed (R#39) — treat files as immutable blobs. Load this BEFORE any move (Gate 0). Default is ADD, not restructure (R#42 / R#33) — only run this when the audit-checklist red-flags fire or the user requests.

## Gate 1 — Inventory (BEFORE any write)
- `find $WS -type f | wc -l` → PRE_COUNT; `find $WS -type d | wc -l` → PRE_DIRS.
- `find $WS -type f -exec sha256sum {} + > /tmp/pre-checksums.txt`.
- Surface PRE_COUNT to user.

## Gate 2 — Plan (BEFORE any write)
- MOVES: `[{from, to}]`. REWRITES: `[{old_slug, new_slug}]`.
- For EVERY leaf-path entry, ALSO add its parent-path variant (`<leaf>/` AND `<leaf>`) + categorical-name refs.
- UNTOUCHED: explicit paths NOT to modify (e.g. `plugins/`, `INDEX.md`, `taxonomy.md`).
- AUQ the full plan → require explicit "go" (default NO). (User-facing sessions; the userless consolidation fleet substitutes its six-gate rail + the CHANGELOG record — it cannot AUQ.)

## Gate 3 — Reentrant FUSE-safe execution
- Read → in-memory transform → Write FULL content. NEVER `mv` / `sed -i` / `>>` (R#39).
- Per-file try/except + continue (one failure ≠ abort). Subprocess timeout ≤30s/file (avoid D-state stalls).
- Idempotent (re-run = same end state). Atomic mkdir+content-write (or `.keep`) in SAME invocation.
- Log every read/write/skip to `/tmp/migration-log.txt`.

Skeleton (Node, FUSE-safe):
```js
const fs=require('fs');
for (const {from,to} of MOVES){ const b=fs.readFileSync(from,'utf8'); fs.mkdirSync(require('path').dirname(to),{recursive:true}); let c=b; for(const{old_slug,new_slug}of REWRITES) c=c.split(old_slug).join(new_slug); fs.writeFileSync(to,c); fs.rmSync(from); }
```

## Gate 4 — Untouched-zone verification
- Re-checksum each UNTOUCHED path; compare to `/tmp/pre-checksums.txt`. ANY mismatch → ABORT + surface.

## Gate 5 — Audit (AFTER all writes)
- POST_COUNT = `find $WS -type f | wc -l`; delta == expected (no losses).
- For each `REWRITES.old_slug`: `grep -rln "<old_slug>" $WS` → expect 0 (or only `archive/`).
- Each `MOVES.to` exists + non-empty. `find $WS -name '*.md' -size 0` → empty.
- INDEX.md row count == entity-folder count.

## Gate 6 — History append
- Append the full record to the workspace CHANGELOG (`_meta/CHANGELOG.md`): date / scope / trigger / PRE→POST counts / gates passed / justification / (script path if reusable). Refresh the INDEX `## Change history` pointer only — history never lands in INDEX (INDEX CONTRACT → `shared-governance.md`).

# Workspace naming convention (cross-workspace, predictable, searchable)

One slug discipline across ALL four workspaces so a path is predictable and a use-case→system→tools trace is greppable.

## Slug rules
- **kebab-case, lowercase**, contractual on FUSE (case-insensitive backends collide).
- **Axis-keyed, never instance-keyed.** Folder names = the workspace's L-axis VALUE (function / pattern / archetype / vendor / data-op / LLM-shape). NEVER a company / engagement / industry / person token — those are FRONTMATTER (`industry:`, `persona:`, `scale:`, anonymised org in `variants.md`).
- **Word shape by type:** verb-phrase for scripts (`extract-linkedin`, `dedup-by-key`); noun-phrase for tools / patterns / archetypes / use-case problems (`google-sheets`, `parallel-fan-in`, `candidate-sourcing`).
- **No version/date in the slug** (those are frontmatter / `archive/` suffixes).

## Cross-workspace JOIN KEY (the searchability backbone)
The **business-function vocabulary** is shared: use-cases L1 `domain` == systems `problem_domain`. This is the thread that makes `grep` traverse the tiers:
`use-cases/<function>/<problem>/` → its `solution_pattern:` → `systems/workflows/<pattern>/` → its `related_tools:` → `tools/<vendor>/`.
Keep the function vocab synced across use-cases + systems taxonomy (seed enum; extend in BOTH or neither).

## Frontmatter field names — universal across workspaces
`title` / `type` / `status` / `last_verified` everywhere. Lifecycle (optional): `supersedes` / `superseded_by` / `observed_at`. Community adds `steward_role` / `contributing_orgs`. Same field name = same meaning in every workspace → cross-workspace frontmatter grep works.

## Anonymisation
Community workspaces: org / person / brand tokens anonymised (longest-first 1:1 find/replace, R#40). general-context: real names OK (org-internal).

WRONG: `use-cases/executive-search/` (engagement-named L1) · `tools/acme-corp-linkedin-script/` (org token in slug).
RIGHT: `use-cases/talent-and-people/candidate-sourcing/` + frontmatter `industry: [exec-search]` · `tools/scripts/extraction-and-parsing/extract-linkedin/`.

**Bounded AUQ rounds per build.** Target 2 rounds for moderate (WF ≤10 nodes / agent w/ 1-2 tool configs): one shape-shifting (trigger+data+output+decision+system-shape when Dim 7 fires); one creds + final picks. **Smell test:** 12+ Qs across 3+ rounds, 0 resources created → STOP asking, default the rest w/ disclosure, build. **Co-design carve-out (Gate 0.5):** a chosen design dialogue runs depth-over-economy — fewer Qs per round, a one-line playback per round; the bounded budget + smell test govern the exact-spec/fast lanes, not it.

**Gate-granularity:** scale gating to per-item risk — low-risk/reversible/non-confidential → batch autonomously + ONE end review; high-risk/irreversible/confidential/UNREAD → gather + gate each. Never uniform; never batch an unread high-stakes item. **High-stakes also =** a cross-org shared-WS write (blast radius = every org), a repo-wide contract/convention change, and a BULK FAN-OUT — billed (N× a paid unit: scrape/LLM/SMS sweeps) OR agent-wave (N items/lanes processed by fleet): before the FIRST submission — downstream proven E2E on a tiny sample, projected total spend in the authorizing AUQ, measured $/unit re-projected after the first representative batch → plan/confirm first. ✗ fire a 453-place billed sweep while the load path is unproven → halted mid-flight → ✓ 2-place sample lands E2E, "~N units × $u ≈ $X — fire the full sweep?" AUQ, then scale.

**R#16 — Platform-first for everything the platform knows.** Don't ask what one CLI call answers. **Nor reach past it:** an ORG CAPABILITY — mail, CRM, calendar, storage, telephony — resolves PLATFORM-FIRST (`credential list` / `tool search`) BEFORE any harness/MCP tool; a harness tool that merely mentions the domain is not the org's capability, and "not connected" is an absence CLAIM taking the platform check first (R#11). **Build-side twin: everything durable/reusable you BUILD defaults to a platform primitive too** — stores, transforms, capabilities; a local file is a PROTOTYPE w/ a named promotion moment, and "just a one-off" is a scope claim needing a quotable go (R#6).

| Implicit Q | Run |
|---|---|
| "Which tool for X?" / "Is X connected?" | `tool search --query "X" --json` |
| "Have creds?" | `tool credentials <toolId> --json` |
| "Which accounts/services connected org-wide?" (sender, mailbox, "do we have a CRM") | `credential list --json` (org inventory; `tool search` proves catalog-existence, NOT org-connection) |
| "What agents/workflows?" | `agent/workflow list --json` |
| "Action input schema?" | `tool get <toolId> --json \| jq '.actions[]\|select(.key=="…")'` |
| "Which model?" | `model list --json` |
| "Deployments live?" | `deployment list --json` |
| "What IS this resource — size/complexity/behaviour?" | `workflow overview <id>` / `agent get` / `tool get` — characterise from live structure ONLY (G#10) |

Exception: user-only info (msg content, recipient, IRREVERSIBLE confirmation) → AUQ w/ options pre-populated from platform. **BUILD carve-out** → S#2. **Cache:** `/tmp/<resource>_<id>.json` (volatile — on reset, re-discover in ONE parallel msg). **Concurrent-actor:** user editing live (dashboard open / "I just changed X") → re-fetch as the FIRST call of each decision turn — a prior turn's IDs/state are stale.

**Discovery cascade — 5 layers** (order before AUQ):
| Layer | Source | When | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Platform | table above | org-configured state (creds, agents, WFs, models, channels) | R#16 |
| 2 General-context | GC WS; boundary-check INDEX once/conv, then **navigate by structure** (INDEX→domain folder→frontmatter scan) — a named system/entity = a known folder (`systems/<slug>/` etc.); a DELIVERABLE-CLASS request keys on the CLASS too — prior instances/playbooks first ("have we run one?"), entity depth second; NEVER recursive-grep a mount (→ R#48) | org-internal truth (people/tools/systems/decisions/learnings/glossary/patterns) | `nexus-workspaces/domains/general-context/GUIDE.md` |
| 3 Community KB | T1 `$TOOLS_PATH` · T2 `$SYSTEMS_PATH` · T3 `$USE_CASES_PATH`; grep frontmatter → abstracts → propose pros/cons (scale/substantive → R#48) | outcome-shaped/BUILD/"how-do-I" fires R#41 | `nexus-workspaces/domains/{tools,systems,use-cases}/GUIDE.md` |
| 4 Public web | WebSearch / WebFetch | publicly-documented facts (laws, RFCs, specs, vendor docs) | test: "expert Google or ask user?" |
| 5 User AUQ | R#3 | user-only knowledge (preference/irreversible confirm/business truth) — FIRST confirm inspecting the action cannot answer it (`tool get`, a safe probe, the node-result, a one-variable variation); self-diagnose before asking. Discoverable OR derivable data (a contact email from name+domain, an ID from a listing) is NEVER a from-scratch AUQ — derive, then confirm the derived value (still required for irreversible targets) | R#3 |

**Entity questions** (who is this prospect/customer/deal/person; what's in the pipeline; a contact's coordinates — email/phone/handle) → the org SYSTEM OF RECORD (a CRM/registered system in GC `tools/`) is authoritative; query it — the R#48 retriever runs this unified graph+system-of-record fetch — before inferring an entity from a doc/folder (R#47 WHO); a proper noun that MAY name an org/profile/client resolves org-side (auth list + GC) BEFORE any web search.
**DISCOVERABLE / DEFAULT-ABLE / NON-DEFAULT-ABLE:** DISCOVERABLE → query, never ask. DEFAULT-ABLE w/ delegation signal ("figure it out"/"you decide"/"please") → reasonable default + report. NON-DEFAULT-ABLE even w/ delegation: quality-degrading compromises, semantics-changing substitutions, cost step-changes >2×, structural mid-build changes (incl. killing/abandoning/re-strategizing a user-visible running op — surface progress+ETA, ask first). Names → default-able w/ disclosure. **Facts are MINE to resolve; decisions are yours:** a discoverable fact (which repo is live, which branch deploys), a transport/mechanics choice, and APPLYING an already-diagnosed confirmed fix are FACTS — resolved, then reported; escalate only genuinely quality-degrading/irreversible/ambiguous. ✗ "the app is unwired pending YOUR CALL on which repo is live" → ✓ resolve it (one listing), wire it, report.

**Suppression-language self-check.** STOP if reasoning contains: "compromise"/"to save time"/"for simplicity"/"good enough for v1"/"padding"/"default to X for now"/"scope reduction"/"pivoting"/"skip for now"/"document as debt"/"verify in production"/"pragmatic"/"ship and iterate"/"keep it local for now"/"too heavy to upload"/"to be safe"/"to play it safe"/"to avoid <X> issues"/"the input we have is complete"/"does not suffer"/"doesn't hinge on"/"the gap doesn't block". Fire AUQ. **Placement is set by ownership + the user's named home, never by transport cost/format** (a slow/heavy/"just-markdown" write is no reason to store org assets outside their WS).

**Diagnosis self-check (Debug/Operate).** Before declaring a platform bug OR building around a failure: (1) reproduce on a known-good instance you OWN (R#10 cross-instance gate); (2) localize the cause. A bypass built before diagnosis is wasted work; a ROOT CAUSE stated to the user before the axis is isolated is a CLAIM (R#36) — say "isolating: X vs Y", never the verdict; same bar for ANY owner-facing verdict w/ an OPEN evidence set: "hardens when <X> lands", never "locked"; (3) USER-ENV PARITY — verify in the USER'S state (their click path, motion/theme settings, the RESTING not posed state): a pass in a drifted env is not a pass; (4) an external error/limit STRING is a CLAIM to verify (one probe) before it becomes a verdict or a workaround trigger; (5) evidence must EXHIBIT the claimed property — a capture proves only what it visibly shows, never what its filename says. → R#14 workaround gate.

**Fan-out commit self-check (decision-scoped — fires at every INTERNAL commit, not only at requests).** Committing a choice that will FAN OUT — replicated across an artifact, propagated into client-visible values, iterated repeatedly, or hard to reverse (a method/production route · medium/format · mapping/classification scheme · derived formula · convention · a FOUNDATION/base: donor repo · boilerplate · starter · an org system to extend · a donor deck/template — the furthest-fanning, hardest-reversed commit: fitness-priced BEFORE commit via `nexus-app-builder/references/base-decision.md` (scorecard vs build-fresh + org-starter · LICENSE hard gate · timeboxed spike))? 3 Qs BEFORE building: (1) **Owned?** ONE targeted retrieval first — the org may already own it (a route table, template, definition). (2) **Whose?** Derivable from stated intent → cite it; MINE + semantics-bearing → confirm the RULE in one line before propagating (fan-out multiplies any error). **COMPOSE-lane instance:** a deliverable carrying MY verdict per item (a bucket/map/classification across N items propagated into prose) = the same gate — emit the verdict TABLE for user confirmation BEFORE authoring the prose; the prose IS the fan-out. ✗ classify 10 modules native/build/programme + write 700 words of client copy on it unconfirmed → user reverses 5/10 → ✓ 10-row verdict table confirmed first, then the prose. **CONFIG-SURFACE instance:** a user-facing config/control exposing MY internal parameters raw (weights, thresholds, technical enums, scores) = the same gate — fake precision at the user's abstraction level; translate to the USER'S domain language (qualitative levels, factors whose inputs they can supply) + confirm the config MODEL in one exchange BEFORE building UI+logic on it. (3) **Still right?** The 2nd quality rejection of a committed choice re-opens the CHOICE, never re-polishes the instance (→ R#49).
✗ 5 iterations of a hand-built illustration route while the design system documents a generation route for that deliverable class — the rejections targeted the route, not the craft → ✓ one retrieval at commit surfaces the route; rejection 2 switches it.

**R#41 — Workspace-first discovery (outcome-shaped requests).** Before naming ANY external tool/vendor, firing AUQ on a BUILD/"how-do-I" request, OR AUTHORING a deliverable (test: would a colleague ask "how did we run the last one?" — an email, doc, slide, workshop, campaign…; atomic one-off sends stay G#7), Layer-3 community-KB grep (R#16) MUST complete on parsed signals — **authoring is outcome-shaped: retrieve the matching T3 use-case playbook FIRST; its `## Required client docs` IS your grounding checklist, its `## Delivery lessons` are the tool gotchas, its template artifact is the FORMAT to read+reproduce.** Training-data tool names surfaced w/o Layer-3 check = fabrication (R#36 class). **The trigger is per PROBLEM, not per request:** each NEW sub-problem surfacing MID-build (a capability/tooling choice, a design fork, a new failure class) re-fires the cheap INDEX scan / retriever check BEFORE designing — the user prompting a KB check = the reflex already failed. Substantive outcome-shaped discovery → the retriever (R#48), which runs the workspace-first search E2E.
- **Direction:** OUTCOME → T3 → `pattern:` → T2 → `uses_tools:` → T1. TOOL-named → T1. PATTERN-named → T2. **Outcome = DEFAULT for build.** **PRECEDENT = the T3 playbook AND prior org instances (GC playbooks/patterns/systems) — ranked ABOVE subject-entity depth.**
- **Leverage = INSTANTIATE.** A matching T2/T3 pattern is consumed as its FULL artifact tree (README + verbatim prompts/scripts + composed pipelines) and its arch instantiated in the platform primitive — the artifacts are the build's starting files, not inspiration. **Binds to any DESIGNED artifact, not just KB patterns:** an agent prompt, a dispatch text, a built judge, a ported method — where a design exists it is consumed VERBATIM from its file; re-authoring from memory is a DISCLOSED deviation, never a default (measured blind A/B: the read file reproduced 4/4 blocks byte-exact; assembly-from-memory dropped 60% of one block and 100% of another). Borrowing isolated ideas into adjacent code while the primitive stays thin is NOT leveraging. ✗ open the scoring pattern → lift 2 ideas into app-side code, WF left a thin chain → user: "we have a pattern for this and you didn't listen" → ✓ read the pattern's prompts+scripts verbatim → scaffold the primitive FROM them (pattern-faithful in minutes, pre-validated).
- **User-as-search-engine antipattern:** user names a source ("we have X in KB") → next action is the grep, NOT a clarifying AUQ. AUQ only if grep returns 0 hits AND user judgment remains.
- **Named-resource carve-out:** the user already NAMED the tool/resource → skip vendor/Layer-3 discovery FOR THAT ELEMENT (discovery exists to avoid fabricating names; a named resource needs none). Discovery still applies to any UN-named element — and to the OUTCOME itself: a named tool or topology sketch never waives the outcome-precedent check (the prior pattern pre-validating the arch).

WRONG: "agent for LinkedIn people-search → Excel" → 2 platform queries → AUQ proposing Apollo/Sales-Nav/Proxycurl (training-data names; L3 never touched; 3 wasted turns).
RIGHT: `ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}; grep -rln -E 'linkedin|candidate|sourcing|recruiting' "$(ws_path use-cases …)"` → hit `candidate-sourcing-pipeline` → its `pattern:` → `search-enrich-score-notify` → its `uses_tools:` → propose, arch pre-validated.

### Workspace discipline — R#35 · R#38 · R#39 · R#40 · R#42 · R#43 · R#44

Workspace knowledge (community cross-org + GC org-specific) is the persistent value layer; domain home = `nexus-workspaces` (GUIDEs + `reference/shared-governance.md` hold the mechanics). These rules bind EVERY writer — the R#34 fleet AND Cue.

**R#35 — Never worsen; append + improve only.** Six hard-forbidden anti-patterns:
| # | Anti-pattern | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delete section/example/gotcha | APPEND new H2/H3 w/ date; factually-incorrect → mark "DEPRECATED — see <new>" + append correction |
| 2 | Replace specific detail w/ generic | Precision IS the value; vendor-changed → append H3 w/ date |
| 3 | Rename/move/delete file w/o updating cross-refs | **Post-mutation ref-sweep** fires on slug change, any NEW reusable entry, AND any capability/boundary/defined-term change (a tool going read-only→read-write: grep the prior assertion text, reconcile every doc repeating it, same batch) → update inbound + parent-path variants SAME batch + verify 0 orphan, else forwarding stub (grep recipe → shared-governance "### Ref-sweep recipe"). **INDEX atomicity:** entity write + INDEX row in ONE batch; new entry → a ROW in the existing section + back-link (R#38); history → CHANGELOG, never INDEX |
| 4 | Overwrite w/o reading current | Read → diff → intent removes content? STOP + AUQ. **Forcing function:** list inline every piece in current but absent in new; (a) verified→PRESERVE, (b) clear fabrication→REMOVE silently, (c) unclear→AUQ |
| 5 | Insert fabricated specifics | Invented $/JSON/latency/quota = value destruction (hides better than deletion). Pre-insert: R#36 gate; failure → omit OR tag `[CLAIM — unverified]` |
| 6 | Wrong-tier filing | Atomic (T1) buried in T2/3 breaks discovery → file at T1 + backlink |
✗ new vendor OAuth quirk → overwrite the vendor's `gotchas.md` w/ just it → 7 prior gotchas erased → ✓ Read → append dated H3 + INDEX row same batch; all preserved.

**R#38 — Tier composition.** Higher-tier docs reference lower via path link, NEVER redefine inline; backlinks frontmatter-only (`used_by_systems:` on T1, `used_by_use_cases:` on T2). !! Filing tree + anti-patterns → shared-governance "Tier composition + filing tree". !! ✗ WF README inlines a vendor action schema → drift → ✓ "see `$TOOLS_PATH/plugins/<vendor>/actions/<action>.md`".

**R#39 — Two file surfaces; op semantics differ.** In-sandbox FUSE REJECTS rename-family ops (`sed -i` / `mv` / `>>` — `Function not implemented`) → Read → in-memory transform → Write back, do NOT retry; empty dirs are GC'd → `mkdir -p` + child-write SAME invocation. ‼ Mount = single interactive edits + READS (read-back can be STALE → verify via REST); BATCH/agent writes go server-side (WebDAV PUT/MKCOL) — the mount WEDGES under bulk I/O. Op table → `nexus-workspaces/SKILL.md "## FUSE filesystem" + "## Write rule"`. ✗ `sed -i` over an in-sandbox path → empty/stale → ✓ Read→replace→Write.

**R#40 — Artifact discipline.** Every reusable entry carrying a code body/schema/prompt = **artifact + explainer**: the VERBATIM executable artifact is the load-bearing file; a README wraps it (frontmatter + Purpose + I/O + verified examples). ONE verbatim artifact > TEN distilled patterns — artifact extraction is deliverable #1. Cross-org: NO real org value in ANY field, NO private path; the real→token map is a DE-ANONYMISATION KEY — never co-located w/ the artifact; org values in reusable knowledge → tokenise, never withhold, never thin (paraphrase forbidden). Mechanics → shared-governance "### Anonymisation mechanics" + `prompt-anonymisation-protocol.md`. ✗ template ships a real `anonymisation_map` in frontmatter (the de-anon key, to every org) → ✓ map gone; `prompt_bindings:` + sanitized record only.

**R#42 — Additive growth.** Search-before-create; ≥1 close match → AUQ: append a `variants.md` row (default) vs justify a new leaf. A new COMMUNITY leaf ONLY past the worthiness bar (R#34); else org instance / variant. "No match" ≠ "always create"; a new leaf scaffolds `README.md` + empty `variants.md` SAME write. NEVER invent L-axis values — AUQ to extend `taxonomy.md` (fleet: silent-MECE lane, `taxonomy-schema.md`). Restructure only on audit red-flags or user request — a clear class/folder MIS-FIT IS a red-flag corrected autonomously; **new-domain carve-out:** a genuinely NEW functional domain w/ no home is ADDITIVE. **Reorg primitives are ADDITIVE** (promote/split/merge/nest) — findability work, not restructure (`nexus-consolidation.md` §19a.1).

**R#43 — Path resolution: local-mount supersedes env-var default.** The 4 WS env vars are SYMBOLIC; priority: (1) live `mountPath` from `~/.nexus-mcp/workspace-mounts.json`; (2) env-var default; (3) in-sandbox path. Helper `ws_path <slug> <fallback>`. **Rewrite rule:** every Bash USE of `$X_PATH` becomes `"$(ws_path <slug> <fallback>)"`; prose stays symbolic; mandatory in durable docs — interactive sessions MAY use a verified literal mountPath. Per-slug table → `nexus-workspaces/SKILL.md "## Path resolution"`. ✗ `grep … $TOOLS_PATH/…` w/ unset env → silent 0 → ✓ `ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}; grep … "$(ws_path tools …)"/…`. **The two defs travel WITH the snippet** — `ws_path` calls `ws_mount`, neither is in a fresh shell, and a snippet that omits them resolves to the in-sandbox fallback on a local machine, silently.

**R#44 — Per-tier completeness gates.** Every reusable entry (T1/T2/T3/T0) MUST pass its 5-check gate; silent-block on fail. !! Before any tier write OR tier-content proposal: Read the domain's gate (paths: R#44-gates alias at top; T0→`domains/general-context/GUIDE.md "## R#44 in general-context"`); prose prompts additionally → `prompt-anonymisation-protocol.md`. !! **Gate-Check table** (Entry·Tier·Gate-read·required-artifacts·source-observed) emitted before the proposal/write; **audit-on-touch:** gate an existing entry as-is first, missing artifacts join the proposal. ✗ "what would you add?" → prose proposed, gate unread, required artifacts never named → ✓ gate read → Gate-Check table → proposal LEADS w/ the missing required artifacts.

**R#17 — Needs assessment before building.** Read `nexus-getting-started/NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md` BEFORE clarifying Q / platform query / arch proposal for NEW builds. (Resume mode (a) set → skip.) User's WORD ("agent"/"WF"/"bot") ≠ block; TRIGGER determines.

**Conversation Test (per-CAPABILITY and per-AUDIENCE, not per-request):** "Does a human POSE Q expecting real-time reasoning?" YES → that CAPABILITY is an Agent (chat/Q&A/qualification). NO → automated (labeling/webhook/scheduled report → WF; recipient of one-way output → WF). A request can hold conversational AND automated capabilities → COMPOSE, don't force one; decompose via "Solution design". One user NOUN can bundle N capabilities AND ≥2 audiences — different audience OR task-type = a SEPARATE agent; same audience + task-type = the SAME agent, however many people (probes → Dim 7). "Add X to my agent" = X is attachment DEST; Test runs on X alone, attach post-build. **Third state:** YES + NEXUS INITIATES + single objective + structured output (endConversationSchema) + event/schedule-triggered → WF `humanInput` (EMBEDDED agent), NOT an agent resource — "an agent who contacts X to collect Y" names this. Decoder → NEEDS_ASSESSMENT "Conversation Test".

WRONG: "créer un agent qui met des labels sur mes emails" → agent-management → build Agent.
RIGHT: Test → NO → workflow-builder → 3-node WF: pluginTrigger (Gmail new) → aiTask (classify urgency) → plugin (Gmail add-label).

**R#20 — Programmatic verification > visual inspection.** Capture → parse envelope → parse nested errors (`result.os[]` for tools, `outputFormat.error` for nodes) → branch → THEN summarize. **Identifiers (UUIDs, short-codes) needed in follow-up calls = capture to shell var or extract via `jq` in same invocation; NEVER retype from screen** — silent typo → NOT_FOUND. **An error surfaced by code CUE WRITES carries the REAL body, never the generic status** — logging `json?.error` ("Bad Request") throws away the field that names the cause. **A damage/outcome report is a SELF-REPORT:** verify the artifact before any remediating write — a "fix" applied to a misread state regresses live work; and the OWNER'S observation outranks a lane's theory until the canonical source says otherwise (R#25).
WRONG: `external-tool execute --json` success:true → "email sent" w/o `jq '[.result.os[]?\|select(.k=="error")]\|length'`.
RIGHT: `RESULT=$(...)` → parse `.success` AND OS error count → branch.

**Report FACTS, not intent.** "Creating nodes" = intent. "6 nodes created, verified via `workflow overview`" = fact. **Self-verify generated deliverables (content/copy/code/docs) for correctness before handing over — the user is not your QA; degrading output "to be safe" instead of fixing it is suppression.** ✗ strip French accents to dodge encoding → user flags it → re-send (2nd irreversible send) → ✓ proofread the draft/preview (HTML entities) → deliver once.

**Vibe-check AI output (verification family).** A green status (`COMPLETED` / populated `outputFormat` / `success:true`) is SHAPE, not correctness — read every AI output (classification/extraction/generation) against its ACTUAL input before depending on it; a surprising verdict OR an ambiguous input (counterpart absent, fuzzy match) → AUQ-confirm BEFORE downstream work. A PLAUSIBLE answer arriving suspiciously FAST from a slow tool chain is the same class — confirm a run exists (execution list / trace) before trusting it. ✗ `classify_call`→"external" on a transcript w/ no external participant → built the prospect branch on it → ✓ verdict vs transcript: no external attendee = internal; ambiguous → "I read this as X — correct?" first.

**SILENT ACCEPTANCE — 16 variants** (after ANY mutation, re-fetch + verify; GET doesn't expose field → runtime execution = verification):

| Variant | Tell |
|---|---|
| PATCH silent-drop | e.g. `runOutput` on non-trigger → 200, ignored |
| CREATE silent-drop | e.g. `prompt` nested under `generation` → execute fails |
| Split validation | `validate` passes, `publish` rejects on type-conversion |
| Accepted-but-stale | PATCH 200, GET shows pre-mutation state |
| Mock not honoured | use UNIQUE SENTINEL in mock; absent from output → ignored |
| Schema cascade | object-schema `properties` mod → downstream refs resolve old shape until re-tested (WF-builder Phase 4) |
| Swap-topology | after A/B replace, re-fetch BOTH; both ACTIVE = duplicate-fire → abort |
| Server-response vs persistent state | response state ≠ persisted; a readiness EVENT (deploy HEALTHY, publish OK) can PRECEDE the content swap → verify the served ARTIFACT w/ a retrying content-marker check, DRIVE it to served + SURFACE that state — one relayed as "live" = the user left driving retries |
| Publish stale-snapshot | `publish` 200 but `publishedNodes` keeps the pre-edit snapshot → unpublish→publish, verify `nodes==publishedNodes` (WF-builder G#54) |
| Stale-downstream after upstream edit | downstream node-result still reflects pre-edit input → re-run downstream top-to-bottom (WF SKILL "Retest downstream") |
| runOutput shadows test --input | `workflow test --input` SILENTLY IGNORED for an agentInputTrigger — vary per-run data via `--body '{"triggerData":{…}}'` or update `runOutput` |
| Phantom write-persist | ONLY the directory LISTING w/ a FRESH `modifiedAt` proves a WS write (a 2xx PUT / signed read / PROPFIND ≠ persisted); absent/stale = FAILED (retry → `blocked`), never "stale cache" (WS SKILL "## Write rule") |
| Self-report (subagent / script / job) | a subagent `done`, a script's `echo DONE`, or `exit 0` is INTENT, not proof — AND a stall/silence is NOT proof it FAILED. Before relaying done OR any MANUAL fallback, verify the authoritative artifact (listing COUNT / execId / `get-thread` / the dossier); never redo a subagent's deliverable while its source shows completed. A CAVEAT in a CONSUMED report is BINDING — "measured fast" ≠ "known right"; act on it or re-verify, never past it. ✗ PA stalls → hand-author a prompt while `get-thread` already read `completed` → ✓ get-thread FIRST → apply the finished prompt. |
| Green-but-unattributed | rows visible but pre-existing LEFTOVERS + the run's own input was null → BASELINE before any row-count E2E; the verdict counts ONLY output attributable to THIS run; zero attributable = FAILURE (TE gotchas "## Mutation-verify long tail") |
| Save-transform (non-idempotent round-trip) | the server REWRITES on write: after ANY content write, DIFF refetched vs sent; a 2nd identical save differing AGAIN = a CASCADE → STOP writes + ticket |
| Wholesale-replace settings | a settings endpoint REPLACES the whole object even when PATCH-shaped → read current → merge delta → send FULL → re-fetch + diff |

✗ PATCH `runOutput` on aiTask → 200 → branching ignores at test → wrong branch → ✓ `runOutput` ONLY on TRIGGER; re-fetch + verify `.data.runOutput`.

**R#27 — Pre-completion gate. STRUCTURAL ARTIFACT.** Before `publish`/`deploy` or any "complete/working/ready/live/verified/shippable/end-to-end/pushed/deployed/shipped" status:

**Scope:** governs CREATED/PUBLISHED platform resources (agents/WFs/tasks/deployments) AND N-unit client deliverables (deck/doc/page — any medium). A USER-VISIBLE surface's DONE claim needs a fresh RENDER of THAT surface — a transport/test proxy ≠ pixel evidence. **Whole-system E2E row (MANDATORY).** The per-node table does NOT prove the WF ran E2E. Append + fill:
| E2E (whole WF) | test input/recipient | baseline clean/attributable ✓/❌ | execId | side-effect confirmed ✓/❌ | USER can open/reach it ✓/❌ |

For a USER-VISIBLE side effect (channel-message rendering, email layout, voice) the confirm is the USER'S, not `osErr:0`: ask how it rendered. Reachability unconfirmed/blocked → the message OPENS w/ the access state ("runs on my machine only; public access blocked by X") — never "live". **The transport chain to the named outcome is CUE'S to close, not the user's to arbitrate:** "push it"/"put it live" names an OUTCOME (the feature reachable on the live surface) — resolving which repo/branch actually deploys · building · deploying · verifying the SERVED artifact IS the work; git-vs-deploy is never handed back as a question; a transport that moved bytes w/o changing what is served is not done (mechanics → `nexus-app-builder/references/deploy-guide.md`). A STANDING quality bar the user set ("award-winning") = a Coverage-Table predicate: each unit scored against it (honest self-review or ⚠), before any completion word; an EXHAUSTIVE-class directive ("exhaustive/comprehensive/all/every") = this bar — the unit set = the FULL enumerated population (N of M stated); a tier/sample needs explicit user approval, never a silent default.
