def dsub(obj, key):
    """The value at `obj[key]` ONLY when it is a dict — otherwise an empty dict.

    W28/E09: nine sites wrote `dsub(x, "data").get(...)`, which checks the OUTER object
    and then assumes the NESTED one is a dict too. Every `*-list` command returns the flat-list
    envelope `{data: [...], meta: {...}}`, so `data` is a LIST and `.get` raises. That crashed
    the PostToolUse adapter on `nexus <resource> list --json` — the single most common command
    shape in the doctrine — and, because a PostToolUse crash is non-blocking, it lost every
    hint that adapter exists to inject, invisibly. CLAUDE.md's own envelope section warns about
    this exact crash; the guard layer was committing the error it exists to catch."""
    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {}
    v = obj.get(key)
    return v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers ----

# THE canonical heredoc pattern. Every stripper in the tree must use this one.
#
# W28/F01 — the previous pattern required the delimiter to be IMMEDIATELY followed by a
# newline, so any trailing token on the opener line meant the heredoc was not stripped AT ALL
# and its whole body was scanned as command text by the DENY tier. Measured on 5,675 real
# heredoc commands: **796 (14%) leaked their body**, and **716 of those 796 (90%) were the
# opener followed by `2>&1`.**
#
# That is the sharp edge. This layer's own standing rule is "never `2>/dev/null`; use `2>&1`",
# so appending `2>&1` is the PRESCRIBED form — and it was the form that disabled the
# mention-stripper. Writing a runbook, a postmortem or a test fixture that merely NAMES a
# dangerous command was then denied for documenting it. A lane's first tool call this cycle
# was denied through exactly this door.
#
# `<<-` (whose entire reason for existing is a tab-indented terminator) was 100% broken for
# the same reason, since the terminator never sat at column zero.
#
# `[^\n]*` after the tag admits the redirect, the pipe and the `&&`; `[ \t]*` before the
# closing tag admits the indented form. Not special-casing `2>&1`: the cause is that the
# pattern modelled a narrower grammar than the shell's, and 80 of the 796 leaks are not
# `2>&1`. Special-casing the observed token would be the substring-not-act mistake again.
_HEREDOC_RE = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*(['\"]?)(\w+)\1[^\n]*\n.*?\n[ \t]*\2\b", re.S)


# The payload an interpreter is told to RUN. `_strip` lifts it back into the act view:
# text inside quotes is normally a mention, but the argument of `-c`/`-e` is executed.
# W48/F1 — ONE DEFINITION, imported. This file used to carry its own copy and the two had
# DRIFTED: this one matched any number of preceding flags but required c/e LAST, while the
# guard's matched a SINGLE flag with c/e anywhere. Each missed spellings the other caught, so
# "is this an interpreter payload" had two different answers depending on which module asked —
# and a check keyed to one spelling of an act is a check an ordinary variation walks past.
#
# The canonical pattern (the union of both) lives in `destructive_guard.py`, not here, because
# that module is stdlib-only BY DESIGN: the firewall imports it lazily and fail-open, so giving
# it an estate dependency would add a new failure mode to a safety net. Importing this
# direction is acyclic — the guard imports nothing of ours.
#
# NO try/except FALLBACK, deliberately. A fallback copy is a SECOND definition that can drift
# — the exact defect being repaired, re-introduced one indirection deeper and harder to see.
#
# But the import must not depend on HOW WE WERE LOADED. The first version assumed every
# consumer had already put `lib/` on `sys.path`, and a verification lane found that assumption
# false within the hour: `tests/test_w28_wake.py` execs this file by LOCATION at its line 147
# and only inserts `lib/` at line 247, so it died mid-suite with ModuleNotFoundError. Worse
# than the crash was its shape — the traceback went to stderr, the summary line printed no
# FAIL token, and a runner that greps for FAIL scored the aborted suite CLEAN. That is the
# dead-harness-reads-as-a-pass class this cycle has now hit four times.
#
# So resolve our own directory. One definition, no fallback, and no dependence on the caller.
# DEPENDENCY DIRECTION, DECIDED BY FAULT INJECTION. The first version put the canonical
# pattern in `destructive_guard.py` and imported it HERE. Driving a copied tree with that
# module deleted showed what that costs: this file fails to import, and EVERY adapter —
# firewall, pretool, posttool, lifecycle, awareness — dies with it. That is not fail-open,
# it is a total hook-layer outage caused by one optional safety module going missing.
#
# So the arrow points the other way. The canonical lives HERE, in the module every adapter
# already cannot run without, and `destructive_guard` imports it. That module is loaded
# LAZILY and FAIL-OPEN by `_destructive_guard()`, so if this import ever breaks in that
# direction the guard simply does not run — one check absent, every other hook intact.
#
# Still ONE definition: `destructive_guard` carries no copy, so the two cannot drift.
_INTERP_PAYLOAD_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|[\s;&|(])(?:python3?|node|ruby|perl|sh|bash|zsh)\s+"
    # W37/H06: the flag may be COMBINED — `bash -lc`, `sh -ec`, `zsh -ic`, `python3 -Ic`.
    # W48/F8: `(?:[^-'\"\s]\S*\s+)?` steps over a flag's own ARGUMENT (`-X dev`), and the
    # trailing `\s*` allows `python3 -c"…"` with no space. Verified: 8 positives, 7 negative
    # controls (`git commit -m '…'`, `cat 'file with spaces.txt'`, `node server.js`).
    r"(?:-[A-Za-z]*\s+(?:[^-'\"\s]\S*\s+)?)*-[A-Za-z]*[ce][A-Za-z]*\s*"
    r"(?:'(?P<sq>[^']*)'|\"(?P<dq>[^\"]*)\")")


def _strip(cmd: str) -> str:
    """Quote- and heredoc-stripped view for keyword matching (no false hits
    on keywords that live inside string arguments or doc bodies).

    W28/F01 — this used a local `'[^']*'|"[^"]*"` regex, the exact non-escape-aware pattern
    that `strip_quoted_spans` was written to replace. The wave-3 class sweep that introduced
    the canonical helper searched the ADAPTERS and concluded "none remain"; this copy is in
    the LIBRARY and survived, while being the view every `classify_bash_reliability` check
    runs on plus 14 call sites in the pretool adapter. The two disagreed on 41 of 20,007 real
    commands. Measured example: `git commit -m "he said \\"use 2>/dev/null\\" once"` — a pure
    mention — denied under the local regex and is correctly ignored by the canonical one.

    W32/G02 — and the INVERSE leak, which is worse. Stripping quoted spans is right for a
    MENTION (`git commit -m "... 2>/dev/null ..."` is talk) and wrong for an INTERPRETER
    PAYLOAD (`bash -c 'nexus agent list 2>/dev/null'` is the act itself, merely spelled
    inside quotes). Driven: the bare command DENIED, the same command wrapped in `bash -c`
    emitted NOTHING AT ALL — the whole deny tier plus every advisory, invisible.

    So the payload of `-c`/`-e` is lifted back in at a COMMAND POSITION. `; ` and not a
    space: every verb test in this estate anchors on a command position, and appended with
    a space the verb sits after `-c` and no test matches — measured on the firewall's own
    copy of this fix before it was corrected.

    This lives HERE, not per adapter, because it is the twelfth instance of one defect class
    (a guard naming a substring rather than an act) and the firewall had already grown a
    private copy. One definition, every caller: `classify_bash_reliability`, the pretool call
    sites and the posttool feed writers inherit it at once."""
    _h = _HEREDOC_RE.sub(" ", cmd)
    out = strip_quoted_spans(_h)
    for _m in _INTERP_PAYLOAD_RE.finditer(_h):
        out += "; " + (_m.group("sq") or _m.group("dq") or "")
    return out


MUTATION_FEEDS = ("dispatch-log", "agent-lifecycle", "push-log-v3", "exec-log", "verify-log")


def untracked_evidence(lines_fn, since_ts):
    """Count MUTATION-class events recorded after `since_ts` — the last board operation.

    W41 — arm 2 of the turn-end wake fired on `tools_since_last_task_op > 0`, which reads "you
    did not touch the board this turn" rather than "work went untracked". Measured on one real
    session: **87 blocked turn ends**, one per wake key, because any turn with tool calls and no
    board write qualified — and most turns are that. A check that fires on nearly every turn is
    not a signal, and each firing costs a blocked turn whether or not its text is visible.

    The evidence has to be something that OUTLIVES the turn: a lane dispatched, a resource
    published or evaluated, a push, an execution, a verification. Reading a file, running a
    grep or thinking out loud are not untracked work — they leave nothing for the board to
    track. Epoch-stamped feeds only: a feed with no timestamp cannot answer "since when", and
    guessing would reintroduce the same always-true predicate in a new shape.

    `lines_fn` is passed in rather than importing the store here, so this stays a pure function
    over whatever the caller can read."""
    n = 0
    for feed in MUTATION_FEEDS:
        try:
            rows = lines_fn(feed) or []
        except Exception:
            continue          # a missing feed is no evidence, not an error
        for row in rows:
            # the epoch is whichever whitespace/tab-separated field parses as a plausible one
            for tok in str(row).replace("\t", " ").split():
                try:
                    ts = float(tok)
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                if ts > 1_000_000_000 and ts > (since_ts or 0):
                    n += 1
                    break
    return n


def ack_present(cmd, token):
    """True when a deliberate-override token is genuinely SET on this command.

    W40 — every ack was tested with `token in cmd` on the RAW command, so a token appearing
    anywhere disarmed the gate: an `echo`, a heredoc doc body, a commit message. Driven on the
    live tree: a real exclude-sweep DENIED by `RM1`, and the same command plus
    `; echo "override is NEXUS_RM_ACK=1"` returned **allow** — the verdict that also removes the
    native permission prompt. A `git commit -m "docs: … NEXUS_RM_ACK=1 …"` did the same.

    Two of the sites mixed the views in ONE expression — the ACT on the stripped view (correct)
    and the ACK on the raw command (wrong), with the right view already in scope one identifier
    away.

    The sharpest case was durable rather than per-command: `NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1` mentioned in a
    heredoc doc body wrote a session flag, retiring the engine-entry gate for the REST OF THE
    SESSION with no app operation performed at all. So a session that writes ABOUT this layer
    disarms this layer — and this cycle's own CHANGELOG and check registry name all four tokens
    in prose, which makes the failure self-inflicting for exactly the work that documents it.

    Tested on the act view: a genuine `NEXUS_RM_ACK=1 rm -rf …` env prefix is unquoted and
    survives stripping, while every quoted mention is removed. One definition, so the next
    override token cannot be added on the raw view by habit."""
    return token in _strip(cmd or "")


def _body_json(cmd: str):
    """Best-effort extract the JSON passed to --body/--input as an INLINE
    single/double-quoted literal. Returns (obj, raw) or (None, None).
    File/stdin bodies (`--body file.json` / `--body -`) are not inspectable
    here — those are handled by the adapter or simply deferred."""
    m = re.search(r"--(?:body|input)\s+('(\{.*?\})'|\"(\{.*?\})\")", cmd, re.S)
    if not m:
        return None, None
    raw = m.group(2) or m.group(3)
    try:
        return json.loads(raw), raw
    except Exception:
        return None, raw


def _decide(check_id, decision, reason):
    # CONVENTION: `reason` is injected as hook additionalContext, so write it as a
    # FACTUAL statement, never an imperative/out-of-band command. Command-framed
    # injections trip Claude's prompt-injection defense, which surfaces the text to
    # the user instead of using it as context (CC hooks docs). Standing rules live in
    # CLAUDE.md; reasons here state the situation as fact and let the rule act.
    return {"id": check_id, "decision": decision, "reason": reason}


def body_file_path(cmd):
    """Return the --body/--input FILE path (NOT inline JSON, NOT '-' stdin), or
    None. The adapter reads+parses it and passes `body` to
    classify_bash_reliability, so body-shape checks cover file bodies too
    (the common case — the docs recommend `--body <file>` for accent-safety)."""
    m = re.search(r"--(?:body|input)\s+(?!['\"-])(\S+)", cmd or "")
    if not m:
        return None
    return m.group(1)


# ------------------------------------------------ PreToolUse: Bash checks ----
# Each returns a Decision or None. classify_bash_reliability runs them in
# priority order (deny wins) and returns the first decisive result.

def _te6_wrong_namespace(cmd, s):
    # TE6 [F] `nexus tool execute` does not exist → external-tool execute.
    if re.search(r"(^|[\s;&|(])nexus\s+tool\s+execute(\s|$)", s):
        return _decide("TE6", "deny",
                       "`nexus tool execute` does not exist — use "
                       "`nexus external-tool execute`. The `tool` namespace is "
                       "read-only (search/get/credentials/connect).")
    return None


# C1 matched ONE literal spelling (`2>/dev/null`), so `2> /dev/null`, `&>/dev/null`,
# `2>>/dev/null` and `>/dev/null 2>&1` all walked past the FIRST row of the blocking
# tier. A gate with a whitespace-sized bypass is not a gate.
#
# Split by CERTAINTY, per the standing deny-only-when-sure rule:
#   DENY — stderr goes to null AS THE ACT: fd 2 redirected/appended, `&>` (which
#          includes fd 2), or `2>&-` (fd 2 closed outright). No intent to read.
#   WARN — `>/dev/null 2>&1`: the primary act discards STDOUT and stderr follows it.
#          That is also the standard capability-probe idiom (`command -v x …`), where
#          the exit code IS the signal, so it is advised rather than blocked.
#
# ORDER IS SEMANTIC and the patterns respect it: `2>&1 >/dev/null` leaves stderr on the
# ORIGINAL stdout and suppresses nothing, so matching it would be a false positive.
# `(?<!\d)` keeps `port22>/dev/null`-shaped tokens out of the fd-2 arm.
_C1_DENY_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\d)2>>?\s*/dev/null|&>>?\s*/dev/null|(?<!\d)2>&-")
_C1_WARN_RE = re.compile(r">\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1")


def _c1_devnull(cmd, s):
    # C1 [F] never suppress stderr (stripped view so it won't hit inside a string).
    if _C1_DENY_RE.search(s):
        return _decide("C1", "deny",
                       "This command sends stderr to /dev/null (R#23) — that swallows "
                       "diagnostics and turns a failure into apparent success. Every "
                       "spelling has the same effect: `2>/dev/null`, `2>> /dev/null`, "
                       "`&>/dev/null`, `2>&-`. Use `2>&1` and inspect the captured output.")
    if _C1_WARN_RE.search(s):
        return _decide("C1B", "warn",
                       "`>/dev/null 2>&1` discards stderr along with stdout (R#23), so a "
                       "failure here is indistinguishable from success. When the exit "
                       "code is the only signal wanted this is deliberate; when the "
                       "output matters, `2>&1` and inspecting it keeps the diagnostics.")
    return None


def _u1_limit(cmd, s):
    # U1 [warn] --limit > 100 silently caps.
    m = re.search(r"--limit\s+(\d+)", s)
    if m and int(m.group(1)) > 100:
        return _decide("U1", "warn",
                       f"--limit {m.group(1)} exceeds the server cap of 100 and "
                       "is silently capped; paginate with --offset/--limit 100.")
    return None


def _u2_inline_body_accents(cmd, s):
    # U2 [warn] inline-quoted --body/--input with non-ASCII / apostrophe / backtick
    # / nested quote → shell-quoting/substitution breakage; build via file or jq -n.
    # W18: both quote styles (the double-quoted form additionally invites $-expansion).
    m = re.search(r"--(?:body|input)\s+('(\{.*?\})'|\"(\{.*?\})\")", cmd, re.S)
    if m:
        frag = m.group(2) or m.group(3) or ""
        if any(ord(ch) > 127 for ch in frag) or "'" in frag[1:-1] or "`" in frag:
            return _decide("U2", "warn",
                           "Inline-quoted --body/--input contains non-ASCII, an "
                           "apostrophe, or a backtick — shell quoting/substitution "
                           "will break or rewrite it. Build the JSON in a file "
                           "(`--body f.json`) or with `jq -n --arg`.")
    return None


def _py1_fragile_inline_python(cmd, s):
    # PY1 [warn] python3 -c with an f-string backslash or escaped quotes → SyntaxError /
    # shell-quote collision. Robust carrier = a quoted heredoc (python3 << 'PY' … PY) or a .py file.
    m = re.search(r"python3?\s+-c\s+(['\"])(.*?)\1", cmd, re.S)
    if not m:
        # W18: a PYTHON heredoc whose stdout is redirected into a file = a fixture
        # written from print()s — whatever the script prints (or nothing, on any
        # error) lands in the file, so a corrupt/EMPTY fixture ships silently.
        # Scoped to python heredocs only (`cat > f <<EOF` is the standard safe form);
        # the intro line alone decides (the _HEREDOC_RE body-shape check requires the
        # word to end the line, which a trailing redirect legitimately breaks).
        _intro = cmd.split("\n", 1)[0]
        if re.search(r"python3?\s+(-\s+)?(<<|>)", _intro) \
                and re.search(r"<<-?\s*'?\w+'?", _intro) \
                and re.search(r">\s*[\w/.$~-]+", _intro):
            return _decide("PY1", "warn",
                           "Python heredoc with stdout redirected into a file — a "
                           "print-built fixture lands EMPTY/corrupt on any script "
                           "error. Write the file with an explicit open()/json.dump "
                           "inside the script, then verify non-empty + parseable "
                           "before use (test-snippets `fixture_check`).")
        return None
    lit = m.group(2)
    fragile = (re.search(r"f(['\"]).*?\{[^}]*\\[^}]*\}", lit, re.S)  # backslash inside f-string braces
               or '\\"' in lit or "\\'" in lit                       # escaped quote inside the -c literal
               or any(ord(ch) > 127 for ch in lit))                  # W18: non-ASCII through shell -c → mojibake/e.k.
    if fragile:
        return _decide("PY1", "warn",
                       "Fragile inline python: `python3 -c` with an f-string backslash or escaped "
                       "quotes breaks (f-string-backslash SyntaxError / shell quote collision). Use a "
                       "quoted heredoc (python3 << 'PY' … PY) or a .py file.")
    return None


def _stmts(text):
    """Split a shell command into STATEMENTS (;, newline, &&, ||) — pipe adjacency
    checks must never cross a statement boundary (W15: a `case … in http*)` literal
    in a LATER statement made a naive whole-command split read as pipe-upstream)."""
    return re.split(r"(?:;|\n|&&|\|\|)", text or "")


_TE5_PARSE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(jq\b|python3?\s+-c\b|python3?\s+-(\s|$))")


def _te5_missing_json(cmd, s):
    # TE5 [S] a nexus command piped DIRECTLY into jq/python without --json →
    # pretty text, parse fails. Warn (advisory). W15 precision: ADJACENCY — the
    # parse stage's immediate upstream pipe segment (same statement) must BE the
    # nexus invocation; `nexus api` is whitelisted (its output is already JSON);
    # a pipe into a python SCRIPT file is not JSON-parsing and must not trigger.
    for stmt in _stmts(s):
        segs = stmt.split("|")
        for i in range(1, len(segs)):
            if not _TE5_PARSE_RE.match(segs[i]):
                continue
            up = segs[i - 1]
            if (re.search(r"(^|[\s;&(])nexus\s+\w", up)
                    and not re.search(r"(^|[\s;&(])nexus\s+api\b", up)
                    and "--json" not in up):
                return _decide("TE5", "warn",
                               "piping a nexus command into jq/python WITHOUT --json — "
                               "it emits human pretty-text and the parse fails. Add "
                               "`--json` before the pipe.")
    return None


def _wf6_branch_field_string(cmd, s, body):
    # WF6 [F] branching condition `field` must be {id,label,type}, not a string.
    if not re.search(r"(workflow\s+(node\s+update|branch)|--type\s+branching)", s):
        return None
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        return None
    # Look for a condition.field that is a bare string anywhere in the body.
    def walk(o):
        if isinstance(o, dict):
            if "field" in o and isinstance(o["field"], str):
                return True
            return any(walk(v) for v in o.values())
        if isinstance(o, list):
            return any(walk(v) for v in o)
        return False
    if walk(body.get("data", body)):
        return _decide("WF6", "deny",
                       "Branching condition `field` must be an object "
                       "{id,label,type}, not a bare string — a string is "
                       "silently accepted but fails at execution with "
                       "'Unknown field type'.")
    return None


_OUTPUT_TYPE_OK = {"previous", "custom", "text"}


def _wf7_output_type(cmd, s, body):
    # WF7 [warn] outputNode outputType must be previous|custom|text. Any other
    # value (e.g. "all", "json", "passthrough") is silently accepted, passes
    # validate AND publish, and at run time falls back to a generic LLM reply
    # instead of your data — only a test execution reveals it.
    if not re.search(r"workflow\s+(node\s+(create|update)|batch)", s):
        return None
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        return None

    def find_output_type(o):
        if isinstance(o, dict):
            v = o.get("outputType")
            if isinstance(v, str):
                return v
            for x in o.values():
                r = find_output_type(x)
                if r is not None:
                    return r
        elif isinstance(o, list):
            for x in o:
                r = find_output_type(x)
                if r is not None:
                    return r
        return None

    v = find_output_type(body.get("data", body))
    if isinstance(v, str) and v not in _OUTPUT_TYPE_OK:
        return _decide("WF7", "warn",
                       f"outputNode outputType '{v}' is not one of "
                       f"{sorted(_OUTPUT_TYPE_OK)} — an invalid value is silently "
                       "accepted (validate/publish do NOT catch it) and the node "
                       "falls back to a generic LLM reply. Use 'previous' "
                       "(passthrough) / 'text' (template) / 'custom' (AI reformat); "
                       "confirm via `nexus workflow node-type outputNode`.")
    return None


def classify_bash_reliability(cmd, body=None):
    """All PreToolUse Bash reliability checks. Returns the highest-priority
    Decision (deny first), or None."""
    if not cmd:
        return None
    s = _strip(cmd)
    if body is None:                       # adapter may pass a file-resolved body
        body, _ = _body_json(cmd)

    results = [
        _te6_wrong_namespace(cmd, s),
        _c1_devnull(cmd, s),
        check_task_body(cmd, s, body),
        check_agent_body(cmd, s, body),
        check_agenttool_body(cmd, s, body),
        _wf6_branch_field_string(cmd, s, body),
        _wf7_output_type(cmd, s, body),
        _te5_missing_json(cmd, s),
        _u1_limit(cmd, s),
        _u2_inline_body_accents(cmd, s),
        _py1_fragile_inline_python(cmd, s),
    ]
    results = [d for d in results if d]
    # deny wins (priority), else the first warn.
    for d in results:
        if d["decision"] == "deny":
            return d
    return results[0] if results else None


# ------------------------------------------------ body-shape (task) ----------

_FMT_OK = {"text", "json", "template"}


def check_task_body(cmd, s=None, body=None):
    """ST1/ST2/ST4/ST3 — task create/update body shape. DENY for the
    would-fail-anyway cases; WARN for the 500-risk nested array."""
    s = s if s is not None else _strip(cmd)
    if not re.search(r"(^|[\s;&|(])nexus\s+task\s+(create|update)(\s|$)", s):
        return None
    if body is None:
        body, _ = _body_json(cmd)
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        return None
    gen = body.get("generation") or {}

    # ST1 [F]: prompt nested under generation with no root prompt → orphan.
    if isinstance(gen, dict) and "prompt" in gen and "prompt" not in body:
        return _decide("ST1", "deny",
                       "task `prompt` must be at body ROOT, not under "
                       "`generation` — nested → 200+id but execute fails "
                       "'Prompt is required'. Move it to the root. (A bad task "
                       "is recoverable: `nexus task delete <id>`.)")
    # ST4 [F]: inputFormat/outputFormat must be lowercase enum.
    for key in ("inputFormat", "outputFormat"):
        for src in (body, gen if isinstance(gen, dict) else {}):
            v = src.get(key)
            if isinstance(v, str) and v not in _FMT_OK:
                return _decide("ST4", "deny",
                               f"{key} must be lowercase one of "
                               f"{sorted(_FMT_OK)} — '{v}' miscased → schema "
                               "drop / validation failure.")
    # ST2 [F]: TASK schemas must be FLAT, not the {type:object,properties} wrapper.
    for skey in ("jsonInputSchema", "jsonOutputSchema"):
        sch = gen.get(skey) if isinstance(gen, dict) else None
        if isinstance(sch, dict) and sch.get("type") == "object" and "properties" in sch:
            return _decide("ST2", "deny",
                           f"TASK {skey} must be a FLAT field-map "
                           "(`{field:{type,...}}`), NOT the "
                           "`{type:'object',properties:{...}}` wrapper. (NB: "
                           "agent-tool `agentInputSchema` IS wrapped — this "
                           "check is task-scoped only.)")
    # ST3 [warn]: nested array-of-objects in jsonOutputSchema → 500 at execute.
    jos = gen.get("jsonOutputSchema") if isinstance(gen, dict) else None

    def has_array_of_objects(o):
        if isinstance(o, dict):
            if o.get("type") == "array" and isinstance(o.get("items"), dict) \
               and o["items"].get("type") == "object":
                return True
            return any(has_array_of_objects(v) for v in o.values())
        return False
    if isinstance(jos, dict) and has_array_of_objects(jos):
        return _decide("ST3", "warn",
                       "jsonOutputSchema has a nested array-of-objects → 500 at "
                       "execute. Declare it as {type:'string', description:'JSON "
                       "array of {...}'} and JSON.parse downstream.")
    return None


# ------------------------------------------------ body-shape (agent) ---------

def check_agent_body(cmd, s=None, body=None):
    """AM2 — agent create must not carry removed objective/tone fields."""
    s = s if s is not None else _strip(cmd)
    if not re.search(r"(^|[\s;&|(])nexus\s+agent\s+create(\s|$)", s):
        return None
    if body is None:
        body, _ = _body_json(cmd)
    # flags OR body keys
    if re.search(r"--(objective|tone)\b", s) or (
            isinstance(body, dict) and ("objective" in body or "tone" in body)):
        return _decide("AM2", "deny",
                       "`objective`/`tone` were REMOVED from the agent create "
                       "API (400). Set the system prompt via `--prompt <file>` "
                       "or `prompt` in the body instead.")
    return None


def check_agenttool_body(cmd, s=None, body=None):
    """AM1/AM4 — agent-tool create config field names/types.
    NOTE: agent-tool `agentInputSchema` is CORRECTLY the wrapped
    {type:object,properties} shape — do NOT flag it (scout-error guard)."""
    s = s if s is not None else _strip(cmd)
    if not re.search(r"(^|[\s;&|(])nexus\s+agent-tool\s+create(\s|$)", s):
        return None
    if body is None:
        body, _ = _body_json(cmd)
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        return None
    cfg = body.get("config") or {}
    # AM1 [F]: field is toolCredentialId, not credentialId (silent drop).
    if isinstance(cfg, dict) and "credentialId" in cfg and "toolCredentialId" not in cfg:
        return _decide("AM1", "deny",
                       "PLUGIN credential field is `toolCredentialId`, not "
                       "`credentialId` — `credentialId` is silently dropped and "
                       "the tool fails at runtime 'missing credential'.")
    # AM4 [warn]: invalid param types.
    params = cfg.get("parameters") if isinstance(cfg, dict) else None
    if isinstance(params, dict):
        for _, pdef in params.items():
            if isinstance(pdef, dict) and pdef.get("type") in ("integer", "string[]"):
                return _decide("AM4", "warn",
                               "param type must be string/number/boolean/object/"
                               "array — not 'integer'/'string[]'.")
    return None


# ------------------------------------------------ PostToolUse: execute -------

def classify_execute_result(cmd: str, response):
    """TE1/TE2/TE3 — parse an `external-tool execute` envelope for the hidden
    truth (os[] errors/warns, async PENDING). `response` is the parsed JSON
    object. Returns an annotate Decision or None. Surface-agnostic."""
    if cmd and "external-tool execute" not in _strip(cmd):
        return None
    if not isinstance(response, dict):
        return None
    result = response.get("result")
    # TE3 [A]: async PENDING.
    if isinstance(result, dict):
        status = result.get("status")
        if status == "PENDING" or result.get("jobId"):
            job = result.get("jobId", "")
            return _decide("TE3", "annotate",
                           f"Async job (status={status}, jobId={job}) — the "
                           "result is INCOMPLETE. Poll until status==COMPLETED "
                           "before using the output (R#29).")
        os_ = result.get("os")
        if isinstance(os_, list):
            errs = [e for e in os_ if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("k") == "error"]
            warns = [e for e in os_ if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("k") == "warn"]
            if errs:
                # TE1 [D]: envelope success:true but upstream error.
                detail = json.dumps([e.get("err", e) for e in errs])[:400]
                return _decide("TE1", "annotate",
                               f"ENVELOPE LIE: success may be true but "
                               f"result.os[] has {len(errs)} UPSTREAM ERROR(S) — "
                               f"the action FAILED. Do not report success. "
                               f"Errors: {detail}")
            if warns:
                # TE2 [A]: non-fatal warns (truncation / 429 retry).
                return _decide("TE2", "annotate",
                               f"result.os[] has {len(warns)} warning(s) "
                               "(truncation / rate-limit / deprecation) — "
                               "non-fatal but inspect before relying on output.")
    return None


# --------------------------- PostToolUse: command-pattern post-hints --------

def classify_command_posthints(cmd, response=None, dashboard_base="https://gpt.nexus"):
    """KB1/WF9/AM3/C5/C2 — reminders keyed on the MUTATION command (and, for the
    dashboard link, the created id). Returns one combined annotate Decision or
    None. Pure: dashboard base is a param, not an env read."""
    if not cmd:
        return None
    s = _strip(cmd)
    rid = None
    if isinstance(response, dict):
        rid = response.get("id") or dsub(response, "data").get("id")
    hints = []

    if re.search(r"document\s+add-website", s):
        hints.append(("KB1", "async import — poll `document get <id>` until "
                             "processingProgress==100 AND errorChildren==0 "
                             "before declaring it imported (R#5)."))
    if re.search(r"document\s+upload", s):
        hints.append(("KB2", "to attach this to a SERVER-SIDE action, get a "
                             "fetchable URL via `nexus document download <id>` "
                             "(local paths fail there); the uploaded file is an "
                             "org asset — keep it (R#47)."))
    if re.search(r"workflow\s+publish", s):
        hints.append(("WF9", "`publish` can keep a STALE snapshot after edits — "
                             "verify nodes==publishedNodes; if you edited, "
                             "unpublish→publish (R#20)."))
        hints.append(("WF1", "if this WF is webhook-triggered and "
                             "`data.webhookUrl` is EMPTY, that is the known API "
                             "gap: copy the URL from the dashboard (webhook "
                             "trigger node); the external test loop still works."))
        hints.append(("WF10", "before declaring done, run "
                              "`reference/test-snippets.md` `publish_integrity_sweep` "
                              "<wfId> and resolve every flag (topology / "
                              "cross-branch refs / configStatus / snapshot, R#27)."))
        if rid:
            hints.append(("C5", f"dashboard: {dashboard_base}/app/workflows/{rid}"))
    if re.search(r"agent\s+update|(^|[\s;&|(])version\s+(create|update|publish|restore)", s):
        hints.append(("AM3", "`agent update` returns no prompt echo — re-GET "
                             "`.prompt` to confirm the write persisted "
                             "(SILENT ACCEPTANCE)."))
    # C5 dashboard link on create (id from the response).
    if rid:
        for pat, path in (
            (r"agent\s+create", f"/app/my-agents/{rid}/tabs/prompt"),
            (r"workflow\s+create", f"/app/workflows/{rid}"),
            (r"task\s+create", f"/app/my-ai-tasks/{rid}"),
            (r"deployment\s+create", f"/app/deployments/{rid}"),
        ):
            if re.search(pat, s):
                hints.append(("C5", f"dashboard: {dashboard_base}{path}"))
    # C5 stale-downstream: a node edit invalidates every downstream node-result.
    # Placed BEFORE the generic C2 re-fetch so it wins for node updates.
    if re.search(r"workflow\s+node\s+update", s):
        hints.append(("WF11", "you changed an upstream node; downstream node "
                              "outputs are now STALE: re-run them top-to-bottom "
                              "before testing/trusting (WF SKILL Retest-downstream; "
                              "R#20 stale-downstream)."))
    # C2 generic re-fetch — only when no more-specific mutation hint already fired.
    if not hints and re.search(
            r"(task|agent|agent-tool|deployment)\s+update|workflow\s+node\s+update", s):
        hints.append(("C2", "mutation returned 200 — re-fetch (GET) to confirm "
                            "it persisted; a 200 can hide a silent drop (R#20)."))

    if not hints:
        return None
    # C8: these reminders ride a PRIVATE channel; Cue performs the nudged action
    # and shows only its result, never the reminder itself (leak #5).
    return _decide("+".join(h[0] for h in hints), "annotate",
                   " ".join(h[1] for h in hints))


# ------------------------------------------------ XREF workspace-sweep -----
# Match on the RAW cmd (not _strip): a WebDAV PUT's signed URL is usually quoted,
# and _strip would erase it. Fail-open: a missed nudge is fine; the once-per-
# session guard in the adapter prevents spam on a bulk PUT loop.
_WS_WRITE = re.compile(
    r"(curl[^\n]*-X\s*(PUT|POST)[^\n]*"
    r"(general-context|/tools/|/systems/|/use-cases/|/workspaces/))"
    r"|(nexus\s+api\s+(PUT|POST)[^\n]*/workspaces/)")
_CAP_HINT = re.compile(r"read-only|read[- ]write|deprecat|use .* for writes|"
                       r"now supports", re.I)


# W31/G01-B3: `-X PUT` was the ONLY upload spelling recognised. `curl` has three more that
# do exactly the same thing — `--request PUT`, and `-T` / `--upload-file`, which imply a
# PUT without naming one — and the slug class `[a-z0-9-]` excluded a legitimate slug
# carrying an underscore or a capital. A gate that watches one of four spellings of the
# same act is a gate on the spelling.
_DAV_PUT = re.compile(
    r"curl[^\n]*(?:-X\s*(?:PUT|MKCOL)|--request\s+(?:PUT|MKCOL)|(?:^|\s)(?:-T|--upload-file)\s)"
    r"[^\n]*/api/dav/([\w.-]+)", re.I)


def dav_slug_if_mounted(cmd, mounts, scope=None):
    """A raw curl PUT/MKCOL to /api/dav/<slug> while <slug> has a live mountPath in the registry
    (mounts dict) → the agent should be writing via the mount's file tools, not hand-rolling WebDAV
    (which phantom-fails + fumbles the host). Returns the slug or None. Pure (mounts + scope
    injected; `scope` is `acting_scope()`'s (orgId, profile) pair — see `mount_record`)."""
    m = _DAV_PUT.search(cmd or "")
    if not m:
        return None
    slug = m.group(1)
    return slug if mount_path(mounts, slug, scope) else None


# ------------------------------------------- workspace mount registry -------
#
# `~/.nexus-mcp/workspace-mounts.json` was a flat map keyed by BARE SLUG until CLI
# PR #2486 (NEX-2360 / NEX-2372) rekeyed it to `<kind>:<id>|<slug>` keys, where
# `<kind>:<id>` is the identity that was ACTING at mount time — `org:<orgId>`, else
# `profile:<name>`, else `url:<baseUrl>`.
#
# DESCRIBE, NEVER SPELL — the repo-wide convention for the broken reader, and it has no
# "but it was a warning" exemption. Everything under hooks/ and skills/ ships to users
# inside the CLI's skills bundle and is scanned there by the CLI's own
# `workspace-registry-skill-compat` tripwire, which matches LITERAL strings. A quoted
# example of the broken form is byte-identical to the broken form, so prose here names
# the old key shape and the old lookup in words instead of writing either one out. The
# rule is what makes the literal scan sound: any literal occurrence in the bundle is a
# reader, with no case to argue. It also closes the dodge — RESPELLING the construct just
# far enough to miss a needle (same characters, different punctuation, inside a NEVER
# warning) satisfies the tripwire while changing nothing, and a future editor can silence
# a real regression the same way.
#
# WHAT THE SCAN ACTUALLY ENFORCES — stated narrowly, because the wide version of this
# sentence has now been wrong twice. The needle list is a list of LITERAL SPELLINGS, not
# a detector for the construct, and no arrangement of literals is one. Counted against
# the list as it stands in NexusGPT/nexus#2668: for the jq path it carries the variable
# subscript, the quoted-string subscript, and the dot-quoted form — three spellings, not
# every way brackets can be arranged (a space inside the subscript already misses). For
# the Python path it carries five variants of the dict-METHOD lookup and NOT the plain
# subscript lookup at all. A bundle can therefore be green on every needle and still
# spell the construct.
#
# It was. Until this commit two shipped hook comments named the old lookup in plain
# subscript notation — one in `nexus-awareness.py`, one in `nexus-pretool.py` — and the
# tripwire read green over both, because no needle covers that spelling. The revision of
# this preamble that shipped in 0.18.1 asserted the broken form was spelled in exactly
# ONE place, the needle list, which does not ship. That was false when it was written,
# and those two comments are why. They describe now.
#
# The supportable claim is the measured one: as of this commit a scan of the whole tree
# is clean for the tripwire's needle list AND for the subscript spellings the list omits.
# Nothing here claims the construct cannot return in a spelling neither scan carries.
# The DESCRIBE rule is the guard; the scan is a backstop with known gaps, and treating it
# as a class detector is how the gap got shipped.
#
# A reader that indexed the registry by BARE SLUG resolved nothing for any slug mounted
# on the new CLI — not for the whole registry, because legacy rows are not rewritten in
# bulk (they migrate on first touch), so on a mid-upgrade machine the same reader still
# answered for un-remounted slugs and failed for re-mounted ones. That mix is worse than
# a clean break, and the failure mode is not an error either way: a dict lookup on a key
# that is no longer there returns None, so a live mount reads as "no workspace mounted"
# and a resolver hands back a fallback path or a null base URL. Silence, on the machines
# that had the feature working.
#
# Matching the record's OWN `slug` field is format-agnostic by construction: `slug` is
# a required field of `MountRecord` both before and after the rekey (verified against
# `packages/cli/src/workspace-mounts.ts` and its pre-rekey ancestor in
# `commands/workspace.ts`), so one value scan reads a legacy registry, a rekeyed one,
# and the mixed registry a mid-upgrade machine actually has.  The KEY is parsed only as
# a fallback, for a row hand-edited out of its `slug`.
#
# Disambiguation is the whole point of the rekey — two orgs may now hold one slug at
# once — so "first match wins" is not available: it would hand a caller another
# tenant's files, and every caller here turns the answer into a path it reads. Nor is
# "only one row, so it must be mine": a slug scan tells you a mount EXISTS, the record
# tells you WHOSE it is, and those are different questions. `mount_record` answers the
# second, and answers None when it cannot.


def mount_slug(key, record):
    """The slug a registry row is FOR, in EITHER registry format. Pure.

    The record's own `slug` is authoritative (present in both formats). The key is the
    fallback: `<kind>:<id>|<slug>` splits on the last `|` — slugs never contain one, and
    all three id sources are `|`-free by construction (org ids and profile names are
    alphanumeric/`-`/`_`; `|` is not a legal URL character) — and a legacy bare-slug key
    is its own slug."""
    if isinstance(record, dict):
        s = record.get("slug")
        if isinstance(s, str) and s:
            return s
    return key.split("|")[-1] if isinstance(key, str) else ""


# OWNER FIELDS ARE NOT NECESSARILY STRINGS, and the OWNED/OWNERLESS test is the hinge the
# whole cross-tenant refusal hangs from — so it is asked through these two predicates and
# never through a bare truth test on the raw field.
#
# A bare `not record.get("orgId")` calls a row OWNERLESS whenever the field is falsy in
# the host language, and the falsy sets differ per language: Python's includes `0`, `[]`
# and `{}`; jq's `//` default treats `false` as absent. Either way a row that NAMES an
# owner gets sorted into the ownerless tier and handed to a caller who cannot match it —
# the cross-tenant read re-entering through a type hole rather than a missing tier.
#
# `nexus` writes these fields as strings or omits them, so no CLI-written registry reaches
# this; a hand-edited or corrupted file does. The rule below is deliberately strict in the
# refusing direction: PRESENT-AND-NOT-EMPTY means OWNED, and only a STRING can ever match
# an acting identity (`acting_scope` returns a `(str, str)` pair), so a non-string owner
# names an owner that nobody can be — the row resolves for no caller at all.
def mount_names_owner(record, field):
    """Does this registry row NAME an owner in `field`? Pure.

    True for every present value except `null`/absent and the empty string — including
    non-strings (`0`, `false`, `[]`, `{}`), which are corrupt rather than ownerless."""
    v = record.get(field) if isinstance(record, dict) else None
    return v is not None and v != ""


def mount_owner_is(record, field, ident):
    """Does this row name EXACTLY `ident` in `field`? Pure.

    `ident` comes from `acting_scope()` and is always a `str`; an empty one is "no
    identity" and matches nothing. Requiring a STRING on the record side is what keeps
    `mount_names_owner`'s corrupt values unmatchable instead of coercible."""
    v = record.get(field) if isinstance(record, dict) else None
    return bool(ident) and isinstance(v, str) and v == ident


def acting_scope(home=None):
    """The `(orgId, profile)` a `nexus` call would act as right now — the identity a
    mount is keyed and owned by. Impure (env + `~/.nexus-mcp/config.json`); returns
    plain data so `mount_record` stays pure.

    Mirrors the CLI's own two-step resolution — `config.ts resolveProfile` picks the
    profile, `commands/workspace.ts actingScope` turns it into the mount scope:

      * `NEXUS_API_KEY` (resolveProfile STEP 3) BYPASSES profiles entirely. It returns a
        synthetic `{name:"override", source:"override"}` carrying only a key and a base
        URL — no `orgId` — and `actingScope` then drops the profile name (`source ===
        "override" ? undefined : name`). So the acting scope is `(NEXUS_ORGANIZATION_ID
        or "", "")` and the mount lands in the anonymous `url:<baseUrl>` bucket. Reading
        `config.activeProfile` here instead would resolve a DIFFERENT org's row than the
        CLI acts as — a cross-tenant read, which is the failure this ladder exists to
        prevent — so the config is not consulted at all on this branch. `NEXUS_PROFILE`
        loses to `NEXUS_API_KEY` for the same reason it does in the CLI: step 3 < step 4.
        (Only an explicit `--profile` FLAG outranks it, and a hook has no flags.)
      * otherwise the profile is `NEXUS_PROFILE`, else `config.activeProfile` when that
        profile exists, else a configured `default` (resolveProfile steps 4 and 6), and
        the org is `NEXUS_ORGANIZATION_ID`, else that profile's selected org (NEX-2474).

    `.nexusrc` directory pinning (step 5) is deliberately NOT walked — a hook's cwd is
    the harness's, not the directory the user ran `nexus` from, so honouring it would key
    on the wrong org exactly when the two differ.

    Missing or malformed config → `("", "")`, which degrades `mount_record` to its
    OWNERLESS tier alone rather than resolving to somebody else's org. That degradation
    is deliberately lossy: an unidentified caller sees legacy and `url:`-bucket rows and
    nothing else, so an unreadable config costs a mounted org its orientation instead of
    routing the session onto whichever row happened to be there."""
    cfg = {}
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(home or "~"), ".nexus-mcp", "config.json")) as fh:
            cfg = json.load(fh)
    except Exception:
        cfg = {}
    if not isinstance(cfg, dict):
        cfg = {}
    if os.environ.get("NEXUS_API_KEY"):
        org, prof = os.environ.get("NEXUS_ORGANIZATION_ID") or "", ""
    else:
        profiles = dsub(cfg, "profiles")
        prof = os.environ.get("NEXUS_PROFILE") or ""
        if not prof:
            active = cfg.get("activeProfile")
            if isinstance(active, str) and isinstance(profiles.get(active), dict):
                prof = active
            elif isinstance(profiles.get("default"), dict):
                prof = "default"
        org = os.environ.get("NEXUS_ORGANIZATION_ID") or dsub(profiles, prof).get("orgId") or ""
    return (str(org) if isinstance(org, str) else "",
            str(prof) if isinstance(prof, str) else "")


def mount_record(mounts, slug, scope=None):
    """The registry row for `slug` that belongs to the ACTING scope, or None. Pure —
    `scope` is injected (`acting_scope()`'s pair); `None` or `("", "")` means no
    identity is resolvable.

    The ladder is `ownerConflictsWithScope`'s three-way owner test, reordered into a
    resolution order. It is NOT a port of `findMount`: `findMount` walks CANDIDATE KEYS
    and then tests the record; this walks records only, because the key is not something a
    hook can trust (see `mount_slug`). Where the two differ is enumerated below.

      1. a row whose recorded `orgId` IS the acting org — the org decides, and a second
         profile on the same org must still resolve that org's mount;
      2. a row whose recorded `profile` is the acting profile and whose `orgId` does not
         name a DIFFERENT org — absorbs the orgId-vs-profile key drift a mount written
         before login filled in orgId leaves behind;
      3. an OWNERLESS row: a pre-rekey legacy bare-slug entry, or the anonymous
         `url:<baseUrl>` bucket a raw `--api-key`/`NEXUS_API_KEY` mount lands in. Naming
         no org, neither can be another tenant's, so an unidentified caller may have it.

    OWNERLESS is decided by `mount_names_owner`, not by a truth test on the raw field:
    only an absent/`null` or empty-string owner is ownerless, so a corrupt non-string
    owner (`0`, `false`, `[]`, `{}`) stays in tiers 1–2 where no acting identity can match
    it. Read the header on those two predicates for why the bare test was a type hole.

    THERE IS NO FOURTH TIER, and that is the whole point. A row that NAMES an `orgId` or
    a `profile` is never handed to a caller who cannot show the row is theirs — least of
    all to a caller with NO resolvable identity, which is reached by ordinary accidents:
    an absent or unreadable `~/.nexus-mcp/config.json`, a raw `NEXUS_API_KEY` with no
    `NEXUS_ORGANIZATION_ID`, a machine with no profile configured. UNIQUENESS IS NOT
    OWNERSHIP — a registry holding one row for the slug proves only that one mount
    exists, never that it is this caller's, and the row itself says whose it is.

    THIS IS STRICTER THAN THE SHIPPED CLI, in three places, all in the refusing
    direction. Read that as the design, not as a mirror — an earlier revision of this
    docstring claimed `findMount` already refuses at its slug-only last resort and quoted
    a line of TypeScript for it. That line is not in the shipped CLI. It is PROPOSED by
    NexusGPT/nexus#2668, which is open. Verified against `packages/cli/src/
    workspace-mounts.ts` on `origin/main`:

      * `findMount`'s slug-only last resort returns the unique slug match WITHOUT testing
        its owner (`if (matches.length === 1) return …`). That path is reached only when
        the caller passes no scope, and its caller is `unmount`. Here there is no such
        tier at all — see "NO FOURTH TIER" above.
      * `findMount` hands an unscoped caller a row stored under a LEGACY bare-slug key
        without testing its owner either — `!scope ||` short-circuits
        `ownerConflictsWithScope` on that branch — so an upgraded-then-hand-edited legacy
        row naming another org still reaches `unmount`. Here ownership is judged on the
        RECORD alone and the key is never a bypass.
      * `ownerConflictsWithScope` opens with `if (!record.orgId && !record.profile)
        return false`, and JS falsiness makes a `0` or `false` owner ownerless there.
        `mount_names_owner` calls it OWNED. See the header on that predicate.

    The asymmetry has to run this way: `unmount` can print "which org did you mean?" and
    stop, while every caller on this side silently READS the path it is handed, and some
    write under it. What is mirrored is `ownerConflictsWithScope`'s refusal — org decides
    when both name an org, profile when both name a profile, an ownerless record never
    conflicts. Nothing here mirrors `findMount`'s key walk or its last resort.

    A tier holding two rows that are not identical resolves to None — two orgs, one slug,
    and no way to tell the caller which one it got."""
    if not isinstance(mounts, dict):
        return None
    org, prof = (scope or ("", ""))
    cand = [v for k, v in mounts.items()
            if isinstance(v, dict) and mount_slug(k, v) == slug]
    tiers = [
        [v for v in cand if mount_owner_is(v, "orgId", org)],
        [v for v in cand if mount_owner_is(v, "profile", prof)
         and (not org or not mount_names_owner(v, "orgId")
              or mount_owner_is(v, "orgId", org))],
        # Tier 3 is the LAST tier. An unidentified caller falls off the end of this list
        # rather than into a bare-slug match: `cand` at that point holds only rows that
        # name an owner, and handing one back is the cross-tenant read (a hook then reads
        # AND writes under another org's mountPath). See the docstring's "NO FOURTH TIER".
        [v for v in cand if not mount_names_owner(v, "orgId")
         and not mount_names_owner(v, "profile")],
    ]
    for tier in tiers:
        if not tier:
            continue
        if any(v != tier[0] for v in tier[1:]):
            return None      # two orgs, one slug — report nothing rather than guess
        return tier[0]
    return None


def mount_path(mounts, slug, scope=None):
    """`mount_record`'s recorded mountPath, or None when unmounted/ambiguous. Pure."""
    rec = mount_record(mounts, slug, scope)
    mp = rec.get("mountPath") if isinstance(rec, dict) else None
    return mp if isinstance(mp, str) and mp else None

_LOCAL_SRC = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|[\s:\[\(\"'>])(?:~|/Users/|/private/tmp/|/home/daytona/|/tmp/|/var/folders/)")


# Scheme-OPTIONAL: filed entries write forge refs bare ("Repo: github.com/Org/x") as often
# as with https://; require an org segment so a prose mention of the host alone stays clean.
_PRIVATE_REPO_HOST = re.compile(
    r"(https?://)?(www\.)?(github|gitlab|bitbucket)\.[\w.]+/[\w][\w.-]*/", re.I)


def local_file_source_ref(value):
    """A grounding/source string pointing at a LOCAL/PRIVATE file path never uploaded
    to the workspace (self-containment failure). A public URL (http/https) is NOT
    flagged — EXCEPT a code-forge URL (github/gitlab/bitbucket): a repo is provenance,
    never the HOME of an org-produced artifact (pointer-only filings: the artifact
    itself gets uploaded — DT-2 / consolidation §12 preservation). Pure. Returns bool."""
    if not value or not isinstance(value, str):
        return False
    v = value.strip()
    if _PRIVATE_REPO_HOST.search(v):
        return True
    if re.match(r"https?://", v, re.I):          # other public URL → SOURCED, fine
        return False
    return bool(_LOCAL_SRC.search(v))


def tool_vendor_from_cmd(cmd):
    """The real vendor slug for `external-tool execute … --action <vendor>-<verb>`
    (UUID toolIds carry NO vendor; it lives in --action). `microsoft_outlook-…` →
    `microsoft-outlook`. None if not derivable. Pure."""
    s = _strip(cmd or "")
    m = re.search(r"--action\s+['\"]?([a-z0-9]+(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*)-", s)
    if m:
        return m.group(1).replace("_", "-")
    # W24: an MCP tool call is a VENDOR action too (`mcp__<server>__<Verb>`), and the
    # CLI-only shape above is why KB1 fired 0× across a 19k-line session that
    # integrated ~2,894 external sources — the vendor was simply invisible to it.
    m = re.search(r"^mcp__([a-z0-9_-]+)__", (cmd or "").strip(), re.I)
    return m.group(1).replace("_", "-").lower() if m else None


_BRIEF_DEST = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:file|place|put|store|save|create|add)\b[^.\n]{0,60}?"
    r"\b(?:companies|competition|competitors|knowledge|systems|use-cases|sales|deals|tools)/[a-z]",
    re.I)


def brief_pre_names_homes(subagent_type, prompt):
    """A nexus-consolidation dispatch whose brief PRE-NAMES a destination folder
    ('create companies/google/', 'file under knowledge/…') instead of stating FACTS
    (R#34). Source-doc paths to READ are not flagged (no filing verb). Pure → bool."""
    if (subagent_type or "") != "nexus-consolidation":

# ------------------------------------------------ Awareness: doc graph ------

def parse_doc_gates(text):
    """AW1/AW2 — extract a doc's dependency graph: `!! … Read `path` … !!` and
    `Skill(name)` HARD-GATES, plus `→ see `path`` pointers. Returns an ordered,
    de-duped list of (kind, target): kind ∈ {'read','skill','see'}. Pure —
    path-existence verification happens in the adapter."""
    if not text:
        return []
    out, seen = [], set()

    def add(kind, target):
        target = target.strip()
        key = (kind, target)
        if target and key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            out.append((kind, target))

    # Inside `!! … !!` hard-gate spans: Read `path` and Skill(name).
    for m in re.finditer(r"!!(.+?)!!", text, re.S):
        span = m.group(1)
        for p in re.findall(r"Read\s+`([^`]+)`", span):
            add("read", p)
        for p in re.findall(r"Skill\(`?([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)`?\)", span):
            add("skill", p)
    # `→ see `path`` / `→ `path.md`` pointers anywhere.
    for p in re.findall(r"→\s*(?:see\s+)?`([^`]+?\.md[^`]*)`", text):
        add("see", p)
    return out


# ------------------------------------------------ round-2 matchers ----------

def model_name_in_cmd(cmd):
    """Extract the --model-name value, or None. Pure helper so the adapter
    knows whether to bother warming the model-list cache (autoload-on-demand)."""
    # stripped view → a model-name inside a quoted string (commit msg, echo'd
    # payload) does not count, only a real --model-name flag.
    m = re.search(r"--model-name\s+([\w./:+-]+)", _strip(cmd or ""))
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def check_model_name(cmd, valid_names):
    """S2 [warn] — model-name not in the live NON-deprecated set. Exact match after
    normalization (casefold, strip a `models/` prefix); an alias/version RELATIVE of
    a valid name (either is the other + `-suffix`) is treated as valid — the check
    exists to catch DEPRECATED/renamed models, not naming-style drift (W18: false
    fires train blindness; the adapter also dedups once per session×name). If
    valid_names is None (not yet available) → no opinion."""
    if not valid_names:
        return None
    name = model_name_in_cmd(cmd)
    if not name:
        return None
    n = name.casefold()
    n = n[len("models/"):] if n.startswith("models/") else n
    vset = set()
    for v in valid_names:
        v = (v or "").casefold()
        vset.add(v[len("models/"):] if v.startswith("models/") else v)
    if n in vset or any(n.startswith(v + "-") or v.startswith(n + "-") for v in vset):
        return None
    return _decide("S2", "warn",
                   f"model '{name}' is not in the live non-deprecated model "
                   "list — it may be deprecated/renamed. Verify via "
                   "`nexus model list --json` (R#8: default frontier, never "
                   "hardcode).")


def check_execute_input_keys(input_keys, valid_params):
    """tool-get param validation [warn] — input keys not in the action's
    parameter set (catches Pipedream prop-name mismatch BEFORE the call).
    Pure set-diff; the adapter supplies both sides from the cached `tool get`."""
    if not valid_params or not input_keys:
        return None
    unknown = [k for k in input_keys if k not in valid_params]
    if unknown:
        return _decide("TG1", "warn",
                       f"--input has key(s) not in the action's parameters: "
                       f"{unknown}. Pipedream prop names differ from the external "
                       "API (e.g. sheetId not spreadsheetId) — confirm via "
                       "`nexus tool get <toolId>` (TE#17).")
    return None


def extract_prompt_markers(prompt_text):
    """Pure: return (set of %%collection%% names, set of @skill tags) in a prompt
    body, lowercased. Adapter supplies prompt_text (from --prompt file or --body)."""
    text = prompt_text or ""
    markers = set(m.strip().lower() for m in re.findall(r"%%([^%\n]+)%%", text))
    tags = set(t.lower() for t in re.findall(r"(?<![\w])@([A-Za-z0-9_]+)", text))
    return markers, tags


def _wir_slug(s):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", (s or "").lower()).strip("_")


def check_prompt_wiring(prompt_text, collection_names, tool_labels):
    """WIR1 [warn] — every ATTACHED knowledge collection must carry its
    `%%name%%` marker in the prompt, and every attached skill its `@label` tag.
    Pure set-diff: the adapter supplies the census (collection_names from
    GET /agents/<id>/collections, tool_labels from `agent-tool list`). Attaching
    only REGISTERS a capability; without its marker/tag it is invisible at runtime."""
    if prompt_text is None or (not collection_names and not tool_labels):
        return None
    markers, tags = extract_prompt_markers(prompt_text)
    mslugs = {_wir_slug(m) for m in markers}
    tslugs = {_wir_slug(t) for t in tags}
    missing_k = [c for c in (collection_names or []) if _wir_slug(c) not in mslugs]
    missing_s = [t for t in (tool_labels or []) if _wir_slug(t) not in tslugs]
    if not missing_k and not missing_s:
        return None
    bits = []
    if missing_k:
        bits.append("collection(s) with no `%%marker%%` in the prompt: "
                    + ", ".join(missing_k)
                    + " — YOU add `%%<name>%%` on its own line in the Knowledge section")
    if missing_s:
        bits.append("skill(s) with no `@tag` in the prompt: " + ", ".join(missing_s)
                    + " — ask the prompt editor to add the `@<skill>` reference")
    return _decide("WIR1", "warn",
                   "attached capability is NOT referenced in the prompt, so it will "
                   "not reach the agent at runtime (attaching only registers it). "
                   + "; ".join(bits) + ".")

_MODIFIER_AGENTS = {"agent-prompt-modifier", "task-prompt-modifier",
                    "pa-prompt-author"}
_STATUS_TOKENS = ("done", "needs_clarification", "plan_for_approval",
                  "infeasible", "blocked")
# Resource kinds R#27's E2E gate applies to. A `ticket`/`workspace`/`folder`/

# (W10: the STc completion-WORD scan was removed — it hoped for the right words in the
# outgoing message; hooks are purely logic. The state-based LC gate below carries R#27.)
E2E_ABLE_KINDS = frozenset({"agent", "workflow", "task", "deployment", "version"})

# Subagents that return a typed result OBJECT to Cue (the "return-contract" family). A NAMED
# background dispatch of one of these becomes a resumable teammate that idles without auto-
# delivering its final message; a NAMELESS background dispatch completes and returns it.
_RETURN_CONTRACT_AGENTS = {"knowledge-retriever", "pa-prompt-author",
                           "agent-prompt-modifier", "task-prompt-modifier"}
# A reference to a DELIVERED retrieval artifact: a dossier path, a REST signed-read path, or any
# `*.md` path. Deliberately does NOT match the bare word "dossier" — so prose like "could not write
# a dossier" is not mistaken for a delivered artifact and a needed block is not silenced.
_DOSSIER_RE = re.compile(r'(retrieval-dossier[\w./-]*|/file\?path=|[\w./-]+\.md\b)', re.I)


def _top_level_json_objects(source):
    """All top-level parseable JSON objects in source, in order: raw_decode at each
    candidate '{', skipping past successful parses (so nested objects stay whole and
    unbalanced prose braces cannot poison what follows)."""
    dec = json.JSONDecoder()
    out, i = [], 0
    while True:
        j = source.find("{", i)
        if j < 0:
            return out
        try:
            obj, end = dec.raw_decode(source, j)
        except Exception:
            i = j + 1
            continue
        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            out.append(obj)
            i = end
        else:
            i = j + 1


def _last_json(text):
    """Pull the LAST parseable JSON object out of a subagent's final message.

    W12.2 hardening (measured): the old first-{-to-last-} greedy grab returned None on
    prose reports containing stray braces (a `{{var}}` template fragment, a shell
    brace-expansion like `adv-{a,b}.json`), silently blinding every report check — 4/4
    live fleet reports parsed to {}. Now: a labeled ```json fence wins (last fence
    first — the declared result object beats a trailing prose example); else the raw
    text, last complete top-level object wins. Unlabeled fenced objects still resolve
    via the raw-text scan; only ```json is trusted as a declared block (a ```bash fence
    may embed heredoc JSON that is not the report). Pure parsing — no wording."""
    if not text:
        return None
    for fence in reversed(re.findall(r"```json\s*(.*?)```", text, re.S)):
        objs = _top_level_json_objects(fence)
        if objs:
            return objs[-1]
    objs = _top_level_json_objects(text)
    return objs[-1] if objs else None


def _questions_text(obj):
    qs = obj.get("questions") if isinstance(obj, dict) else None
    if isinstance(qs, list) and qs:
        out = []
        for q in qs:
            if isinstance(q, dict):
                opts = q.get("options")
                line = q.get("question", "")
                if opts:
                    line += " [" + " / ".join(map(str, opts)) + "]"
                out.append(line)
            else:
                out.append(str(q))
        return " | ".join(out)
    return ""


def subagent_stop_action(agent_type, last_message):
    """TYPE-SPECIFIC SubagentStop handling — each subagent type has its own
    contract + next-action. Uses the payload's agent_type + last_assistant_message.

    needs_clarification / plan_for_approval are an AUQ-FORCING mechanic: the
    injected directive imperatively tells Cue to relay via AskUserQuestion (and
    parses the structured `questions` so Cue has the exact options). The modifier
    prompts return those questions structured so this mechanic works.

    nexus-consolidation is handled in the adapter (SILENT, leak #7)."""
    if agent_type not in _MODIFIER_AGENTS:
        return None
    obj = _last_json(last_message) or {}
    status = (obj.get("status") or "").lower() if isinstance(obj, dict) else ""
    low = (last_message or "").lower()

    def is_(tok):
        return status == tok or (not status and tok in low)

    # 1. contract integrity.
    if not status and not any(t in low for t in _STATUS_TOKENS):
        return _decide("SA1", "annotate",
                       f"{agent_type} returned no recognizable status "
                       f"{_STATUS_TOKENS} — output contract may be malformed; "
                       "verify before acting on it (R#45/R#46).")
    # 2. AUQ-forcing: needs_clarification.
    if is_("needs_clarification"):
        qt = _questions_text(obj)
        return _decide("SA-AUQ", "annotate",
                       f"{agent_type} returned needs_clarification — you MUST "
                       "present these to the user via AskUserQuestion NOW and "
                       "must NOT answer them yourself; then re-dispatch the "
                       "modifier with prior_qa."
                       + (f" Questions: {qt}" if qt else ""))
    # 3. AUQ-forcing: plan_for_approval.
    if is_("plan_for_approval"):
        return _decide("SA-PLAN", "annotate",
                       f"{agent_type} returned a plan_for_approval — you MUST get "
                       "explicit user approval via AskUserQuestion before it "
                       "proceeds; then re-dispatch with approved_plan.")
    # 4. done → type-specific publish/eval path.
    if is_("done"):
        if agent_type == "pa-prompt-author":
            return _decide("SA-PA", "annotate",
                           "pa-prompt-author returned the finalized prompt/spec: "
                           "YOU now fire `task create`/`agent update` (R#31) and "
                           "run the post-create eval; it did NOT create the "
                           "resource.")
        if agent_type == "agent-prompt-modifier":
            return _decide("SA-APM", "annotate",
                           "agent-prompt-modifier edited the DRAFT only — before "
                           "publishing run a nexus-evaluations REGRESSION (R#45), "
                           "then `version publish` on PASS.")
        return _decide("SA-TPM", "annotate",
                       "task-prompt-modifier edit is LIVE (no draft) — run the "
                       "post-edit nexus-evaluations TASK-eval now (R#46); "
                       "revert = re-`task update` with the prior prompt.")
    # 5. infeasible / blocked.
    if is_("infeasible") or is_("blocked"):
        return _decide("SA-X", "annotate",
                       f"{agent_type} reported infeasible/blocked — surface the "
                       "workaround to the user; do not force the edit.")
    return None


def dispatch_named_bg_warn(subagent_type, tool_input):
    """A return-contract subagent dispatched in the BACKGROUND with a NAME becomes a resumable
    teammate that idles without auto-delivering its final result. Fire-and-consume should omit the
    name so the agent COMPLETES and returns its final message. Factual WARN. Returns (id, reason) |
    None. Fail-open (pure; the adapter applies the once-per-session dedup)."""
    ti = tool_input or {}
    if subagent_type not in _RETURN_CONTRACT_AGENTS:
        return None
    if not ti.get("run_in_background") or not ti.get("name"):
        return None
    return ("KR-NAME",
            "a return-contract subagent is dispatched in the background WITH a name, which makes it "
            "a resumable teammate that goes idle without auto-delivering its final result; a "
            "fire-and-consume retrieval completes and returns its final message when dispatched "
            "WITHOUT a name, and a named dispatch's result is read from its dossier file or "
            "transcript rather than by re-prompting an idle agent.")


def retriever_stop_action(agent_type, last_message):
    """knowledge-retriever SubagentStop: PROBE-VERIFIED (17-stop cascade on a trivial probe,
    2026-07-04) — an emitted additionalContext is delivered to the STOPPING CHILD as its next
    input and re-invokes it; an annotate written for Cue role-confuses the child (it starts
    acting as the consumer, hunting other sessions' dossiers). Therefore: (a) the text is
    addressed TO THE RETRIEVER itself; (b) it fires ONLY when the final message lacks the §12
    typed object / dossier path — a clean ending gets NO emission and hence NO re-invoke;
    (c) the caller once-guards per agent_id (max ONE corrective turn; after that the dossier
    artifact floor covers delivery). Cue-side consumption guidance lives in doctrine (R#48
    artifact-first), never here.
    Returns a _decide dict | None. Fail-open."""
    if agent_type != "knowledge-retriever":
        return None
    obj = _last_json(last_message) or {}
    has_obj = isinstance(obj, dict) and (
        obj.get("status") in ("done", "needs_clarification", "blocked") or obj.get("dossier"))
    has_path = bool(last_message and _DOSSIER_RE.search(last_message))
    if has_obj or has_path:
        return None
    return _decide("KR-JSON", "annotate",
                   "your final message must be the §12 typed object — emit it NOW and end the "
                   'turn: {"status":"done|needs_clarification|blocked","dossier":"<on-disk '
                   'path>",...} with NOTHING after it. Your findings already live in your '
                   "dossier file / transcript; do NOT re-run the search, do NOT consume other "
                   "dossiers, do NOT act as your caller — emit the object only.")


def partial_listing_warn(cmd):
    """A workspace `.../files` listing parsed via .folders-only or .files-only — the sibling axis
    (a flat `<x>.md` at a folder root, or a subfolder) is then invisible, so a present entity reads
    as absent (G#10). Heuristic WARN. Returns (id, reason) | None. Fail-open."""
    s = cmd or ""
    if not re.search(r"workspaces/[^\s\"']+/files", s):
        return None
    reads_folders = re.search(r"\.(data\.)?folders\b", s)
    reads_files = re.search(r"\.(data\.)?files\b", s)
    if bool(reads_folders) != bool(reads_files):
        return ("LISTING1",
                "this workspace listing reads only one of `.data.files` / `.data.folders`; an "
                "entity can be a flat `<x>.md` at a folder root OR a subfolder, so both axes are "
                "read before concluding anything is absent (G#10).")
    return None


def lifecycle_phase(cmd, response=None):
    """Capture the Nexus BUILD lifecycle phase of a command (deterministic — no
    model). Returns (phase, resource_id) or None. Phases: created/built/tested/
    validated/published/e2e. The Stop gate uses the per-id phase set to flag a
    publish that skipped test/E2E (R#27) — the build→test→validate→publish pain."""
    if not cmd:
        return None
    s = _strip(cmd)

    def wf_id():
        # Extract from the RAW command, never the quote-stripped view. (Bug caught
        # by a live test: _strip removed the quoted id, so the positional regex
        # grabbed `--type` instead of the workflow id.)
        # 1) A real UUID (quoted or not) is the most reliable signal.
        m = re.search(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-"
                      r"[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}", cmd)
        if m:
            return m.group(0)
        # 2) Fallback: positional id on the RAW command (handles short/non-UUID ids).
        for pat in (r"workflow\s+(?:publish|validate|unpublish|overview|get)\s+(\S+)",
                    r"workflow\s+node\s+\w+\s+(\S+)",
                    r"workflow\s+test\s+(\S+)",
                    r"workflow\s+(?:edge|branch)\s+\w+\s+(\S+)",
                    r"execution\s+(?:get|poll|node-result)\s+(\S+)"):
            m = re.search(pat, cmd)
            if m:
                return m.group(1).strip("'\"")
        return None

    if re.search(r"workflow\s+publish\b", s):
        return ("published", wf_id())
    if re.search(r"workflow\s+validate\b", s):
        return ("validated", wf_id())
    if re.search(r"workflow\s+test\b|workflow\s+node\s+test\b", s):
        return ("tested", wf_id())
    if re.search(r"task\s+execute|emulator\s+send|agent-eval\s+run|execution\s+(get|poll|node-result)\b", s):
        return ("e2e", wf_id() or "*")   # NOTE: `execution list` is NOT e2e (metadata read)
    if re.search(r"workflow\s+create\b", s):
        rid = None
        if isinstance(response, dict):
            rid = response.get("id") or dsub(response, "data").get("id")
        return ("created", rid)
    if re.search(r"workflow\s+(node\s+create|batch|node\s+update|edge\s+create)\b", s):
        return ("built", wf_id())
    return None


def lifecycle_gaps(phase_lines):
    """Given the lifecycle log (lines 'id phase'), return ids that were PUBLISHED
    but never reached a REAL run. A `workflow test` (AWAITING_TRIGGER) does NOT
    count as a real run for a webhook/plugin-triggered WF — those need a real
    fired event (an `e2e` phase). The `webhook` token is logged once by the
    adapter when it sees the published WF is webhook or plugin triggered."""
    by_id = {}
    global_e2e = False
    for ln in phase_lines:
        parts = ln.split(" ", 1)
        if len(parts) != 2:
            continue
        rid, ph = parts
        by_id.setdefault(rid, set()).add(ph)
        if ph == "e2e":
            global_e2e = True
    gaps = []
    for rid, phs in by_id.items():
        if "published" not in phs:
            continue
        real_run = ("e2e" in phs) or global_e2e
        # a webhook/plugin WF needs a REAL fired event; `workflow test`
        # (AWAITING_TRIGGER) does not count.
        if "webhook" in phs and "e2e" not in phs:
            gaps.append(rid + " (webhook: needs a real fired event, not "
                              "`workflow test`)")
        elif "tested" not in phs and not real_run:
            gaps.append(rid)
    return gaps
