# W28/F15 — a SHAPE, not a hand-maintained alphabet.
#
# This enumerated bracketed ids literally, and the list had not grown with the layer:
# measured, it covered 9 of ~100 live ids, and 13 of its 20 alternatives named ids that no
# adapter can emit any more — the decommissioned judge layer, never pruned when it went.
# Worse, it was blind to EVERY deny-class id, which are precisely the messages a model
# relays: a deny stops the turn, so the user is owed an explanation. `[STOP-WAKE]` was
# invisible, and that one is literally a block reason the model is being asked to answer.
# The check fired on the three ids a meta-session mentions and stayed silent on the ninety
# it exists for — which reads, from the log, as a working backstop.
#
# The anchor stays LINE-LEADING, which is what keeps the docstring's narrowness promise: an
# inline `R#47` in a doctrine discussion still does not match. Not "add the 91 missing ids":
# that re-creates the maintenance debt that produced this, and it has already failed once
# here and once in the registry. A list must be edited whenever a check is added; a shape
# is closed under new ids, which is the property that failed.
_LEAK_TOKENS = re.compile(
    r"(Conversation Test:|Locked in:|do not verbalize|\(internal nudge|"
    r"This is the FIRST user message of the conversation|previously summarized state|"
    r"read in full at session start per the boundary check|\(IDENTITY\.md continued|"
    r"^\s*\[[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:[-.][A-Z0-9]+)*\]|"
    r"^\s*\[R#?\d+[A-Z-]*\])",
    re.M)


# `(?:>[ \t]*)*` — a fence inside a BLOCKQUOTE is still a fence. Quoting a prior message is the
# most natural way to reproduce an instruction, and it was leaking.
_FENCE_RE = re.compile(r"^[ \t]*(?:>[ \t]*)*(?:```|~~~).*?"
                       r"(?:^[ \t]*(?:>[ \t]*)*(?:```|~~~)|\Z)", re.S | re.M)
# W28/F01 — `` `[^`\n]*` `` matches the FIRST PAIR of backticks, so in a CommonMark
# double-backtick span the first pair is the empty opening delimiter and the content between
# them survives as prose. That is the exact shape this module's own docstring uses to describe
# the danger — the literal `` `lane-owes:<task id>` `` is written in a double-backtick span —
# and it was the one span shape the code did not blank. Substituting a real id into that echo
# muted the very task the model was being asked about.
#
# CommonMark rule: the longest run of backticks opens, and the same run closes.
# Not "strip everything between the first and last backtick": that swallows genuine claims in
# any message containing two unrelated inline spans, which is most of them, and the failure
# direction there is muting a real handoff — worse than the leak.
_INLINE_CODE_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!`)(`+)(?:(?!\1)[^\n])+\1(?!`)")


def _strip_code(s):
    """Blank out fenced blocks AND inline backtick spans, preserving line structure.

    A hook that reads a CLAIM out of the model's own final message must not read it out of a
    QUOTATION. Measured: a fenced block explaining the `lane-owes:` exit — prefixed with "I
    have not actually delegated anything" — registered a real claim and muted a task for 90
    minutes. That makes the check self-disarming: any turn that discusses it, quotes its own
    block message back, or pastes an audit of it can silence itself.

    Inline spans matter as much as fences, and for a sharper reason: the block message ITSELF
    contains the literal `` `lane-owes:<task id>` ``. Echoing the instruction back is the most
    natural thing a model does when it cannot comply, and today that is safe only by accident
    — `<` happens not to be in `[\\w-]`. Substitute a real id into that echo and the model
    mutes the very task it was being asked about.

    What survives is prose, which is where a real claim lives: "the retriever owes me this.
    lane-owes:1" is a claim; the same token in backticks or a fence is a mention.

    An UNTERMINATED fence swallows the rest of the message deliberately (`\\Z`): a claim after
    an unclosed fence is inside it by every reasonable reading, and failing toward "no claim"
    is failing toward the check still firing. Newlines are preserved so any `re.M` anchor in
    the caller still lines up with the original text."""
    if not s:
        return ""
    out = _FENCE_RE.sub(lambda m: "\n" * m.group(0).count("\n"), s)
    return _INLINE_CODE_RE.sub(lambda m: " " * len(m.group(0)), out)


def scan_leak(last_message):
    """LEAK — deterministic, HIGH-PRECISION internal-leak backstop (Internal≠Surface).
    It scans for OUR OWN emitted codes/markers — literal identifiers, never natural-language
    wording (the wording-judging LI1 twin left with the judge layer, W10). Fires on a Stop message

    'Locked in:' tag, a literal '(internal nudge' / 'do not verbalize', a bracketed hook

    if not last_message or not _LEAK_TOKENS.search(last_message):

def _human_entry(content):
    """True only when a user entry carries HUMAN-typed text. Harness-injected
    entries (hook feedback, teammate/agent messages, task notifications, command
    echoes) are stored as type=user too; counting them is the measured every-
    message false-fire (84% of 402 fires, W21). Literal-identifier matching on
    OUR OWN wrappers — never wording interpretation. An entry mixing a wrapper
    block with a real typed block still counts (any non-wrapper text block
    qualifies)."""
    blocks = ([content] if isinstance(content, str) else
              [b.get("text") for b in (content or [])
               if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text"])
    return any(b and b.strip() and not b.lstrip().startswith(_INJECTED_PREFIXES)
               for b in blocks)


def read_tail_lines(path, n, window=4 << 20):
    """The last `n` lines of a file WITHOUT materialising it.

    W28/E09: seven sites did `open(path).readlines()[-n:]`. The `n` reads like a bound and is
    not one — the whole file loads first. Measured on this machine's REAL transcripts, at
    EVERY turn end: a 590 MB session cost 4.36 s and 731 MB RSS, a 204 MB one 2.68 s, and the
    cost grows with session length — worst exactly when a session matters most. Five
    transcripts on this box exceed 150 MB.

    BYTE-BOUNDED, not merely seek-based: an endless character device reports size 0, so a
    size-guarded seek still reads forever (`/dev/zero` never returned). Reading at most
    `window` bytes makes the cost O(window) for every input, including ones that never end.

    The first line of the window is discarded when the file is larger than the window, because
    seeking lands mid-line. Fail-open → [] : a tail that cannot be read is not an error worth
    breaking a hook over."""
    try:
        size = os.path.getsize(path)
    except OSError:
        return []
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as fh:
            partial = False
            if size > window:
                fh.seek(size - window)
                partial = True
            data = fh.read(window)
    except OSError:
        return []
    text = data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if partial and lines:
        lines = lines[1:]        # the seek landed mid-line; that fragment is not a line
    return lines[-n:] if n else []


# The prefix group is ONE repeated alternation rather than "wrapper, then its flags": a bare
# leading assignment (`D=/tmp rm -rf x`) has no wrapper word at all, and requiring one meant the
# position landed on the assignment instead of the verb. Where the prefix cannot be resolved
# (`sudo -u nobody rm`), the scan stops early and yields an EXTRA position — which errs toward
# treating something as a command, i.e. toward the guard firing. On a deny tier that is the
# correct direction to be wrong in.
# W44: the wrapper-absorbing alternation is QUADRATIC on a long command, measured through the
# real adapter — 5K chars 0.5s, 10K 1.7s, 20K 7.5s, 40K past a 25s timeout, on EVERY Bash call.
# Cause: `\w+=\S+` and `-\S+`. On a long run of word characters with no `=`, `\w+` matches to
# the end, fails to find `=`, then backtracks one character at a time — O(n) per start position,
# and `finditer` tries every position, so O(n^2). Bounding the two unbounded runs makes each
# failure O(1)-ish and the whole scan linear. The bounds are far above anything real: shell
# variable names and flag tokens are tens of characters, not thousands, so no command that
# previously matched stops matching.
_CMD_SEP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[;&|(){}\n]|&&|\|\||\bthen\b|\bdo\b|\belse\b)\s*"
                         r"(?:(?:sudo|command|env|nohup|time|exec|xargs|doas|builtin|eval)\s+"
                         r"|-\S{1,256}\s+|\w{1,128}=\S{1,1024}\s+)*")


def s(v, default=""):
    """A payload field that MUST be a string. Non-str -> default, never a crash.

    W28/F13. W28/E09 added `if not isinstance(data, dict): sys.exit(0)` to every adapter with
    the comment "shape is part of the contract, not just parseability" — and applied it at
    DEPTH 0 ONLY. Every nested read is `(data.get("tool_input") or {}).get("file_path", "")`,
    and `or {}` guards `None` and nothing else. A non-string one level down propagates into
    `os.path`, `str.startswith`, `str.replace` or a `set` lookup and kills the process.

    Measured: seven adapters, 15 of 17 targeted probes, exit **1**. That is not the deny code —
    these adapters signal deny with exit 2 — so exit 1 means the hook ERRORED and the guard did
    not run for that call. `nexus-fs-firewall.py` is among them, and it is the adapter holding
    `rm -rf` of a protected root, raw-disk writes, the fork bomb and the SIP guard: a payload
    shape that makes it exit 1 is a payload shape for which none of those denies exist.

    Reachability, stated honestly: across 33,430 real tool-use blocks there were ZERO non-string
    `file_path`/`command`/`content` and zero non-dict `tool_input`. This is a defensive gap, not
    an observed incident. It is worth closing anyway because the fields most at risk —
    `tool_input` for `mcp__*` tools — are shaped by third-party servers rather than by the
    harness's own schemas, and the layer's own contract already claims shape is part of it.

    NOT a top-level `try/except: sys.exit(0)`: that converts a crash into a SILENT skip, so the
    guard still does not run and now nothing says so. Coercion keeps the guard running on the
    fields that are well-formed, which is almost always all of them — and it is the only version
    that can be asserted, because you can test a deny on a coerced field and you cannot test
    anything about a swallowed exception."""
    return v if isinstance(v, str) else default


def d(v):
    """A payload field that MUST be a mapping. Non-dict -> {}. See `s()`."""
    return v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}


_CMD_POS_CACHE = {}   # W44: see `command_positions` — pure function, called ~82x per run


def command_positions(cmd):
    """Offsets in `cmd` where a shell would begin reading a COMMAND.

    W28/F20. The layer's single most repeated defect is a trigger that names a SUBSTRING rather
    than an ACT — eight instances by the time this was written, two of them at DENY tier, and
    the fixes kept being per-check. Three checks solved it independently (`aw5` by hand, then
    `DISKWRITE` and `G19` each with their own `CMDPOS` constant); four more never did, and
    those four produced the bulk of the measured false positives — 33 of 39 firewall denies in
    a 19,333-command corpus among them.

    The shared question every one of them needs is the same: **does my match START where a
    command starts?** Answering it once, here, is what stops instance #9. A check then reads
    its OPERANDS from the raw text, which is the other half — a stripped view protects against
    mentions but destroys quoted operands (it deleted the `''` that told a correct `sed -i ''`
    from a broken `sed -i`).

    Quoted spans are excluded, so a command name inside a string is never a command position —
    that is the mention case, and it reuses `strip_quoted_spans`'s own scanner rather than a
    fourth private quote regex. Wrapper words that TAKE a command (`sudo`, `env VAR=x`,
    `xargs`, `timeout`-style prefixes) are absorbed, so the position lands on the real verb.

    Returns a set of integer offsets. `pos in command_positions(cmd)` is the whole API.

    W44: MEMOISED. This is a pure function of `cmd`, and `at_command_position` calls it once per
    candidate match — measured at 82 scans of the same string in a single adapter run, each one
    re-running the separator regex AND `strip_quoted_spans` over the whole command. Caching by
    identity of the command text turns 82 scans into 1. Bounded to the last few commands seen so
    a long-lived process cannot grow the cache without limit."""
    if not cmd:
        return set()          # no command text, no command positions — not offset 0
    hit = _CMD_POS_CACHE.get(cmd)
    if hit is not None:
        return hit
    out = {m.end() for m in _CMD_SEP_RE.finditer(strip_quoted_spans(cmd))}
    if len(_CMD_POS_CACHE) >= 8:
        _CMD_POS_CACHE.clear()   # a hook process is short-lived; a plain bound beats an LRU
    _CMD_POS_CACHE[cmd] = out
    return out


def at_command_position(cmd, match):
    """True when `match` (a re.Match on the RAW command) starts where a command starts."""
    return match is not None and match.start() in command_positions(cmd)


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)
def strip_quoted_spans(s):
    """Replace quoted spans with whitespace, honouring backslash escapes — a scanner.

    W46-hookfix, cost: MEMOIZED. Profiled on a 200 KB hostile command, this scanner was
    rebuilt char-by-char SIXTEEN times for the same input in one adapter invocation
    (3.2 M list appends, ~10.4 s of a 34 s run). Hooks are one-shot processes and every
    caller passes the same one or two strings, so an 8-slot cache turns 16 builds into 1
    with identical output. Never key views by anything but the full string.

    THE CANONICAL implementation. Two adapters each carried their own
    `'[^']*'|"[^"]*"` regex, which is not shell-aware: an ESCAPED quote inside a
    double-quoted span ended it early and leaked the rest of the string into the view the
    keyword checks run on. Measured live and repeatedly during W28 on ordinary commands —
    `python3 -c "... \\" ..."` and `git commit -m "don't run \\"csrutil disable\\""` both
    tripped gates on text plainly inside quotes. A reader does not perceive a subtle quoting
    bug; they perceive a guard firing while they write a commit message, which is how a
    guard earns being ignored.

    It lives here because it had ALREADY diverged: fixing one copy and leaving the other is
    the whack-a-mole pattern the change log exists to prevent.

    Inside DOUBLE quotes a backslash escapes the next character. Inside SINGLE quotes it does
    not (POSIX) — so `'\\''` closes the span, which is the shell concatenation idiom and needs
    no special case."""
    s = s or ""
    out = []
    i, n, q, open_at = 0, len(s), None, -1
    while i < n:
        c = s[i]
        if q is None:
            if c in "'\"":
                q, open_at = c, i
                out.append(" ")
            else:
                out.append(c)
            i += 1
            continue
        if q == '"' and c == "\\" and i + 1 < n:
            i += 2                                  # escaped char stays INSIDE the span
            continue
        if c == q:
            # `'\''` is the shell idiom for a literal quote inside a single-quoted argument:
            # the span closes, a literal `'` is emitted, and a new span opens. It is ONE
            # logical argument, so treat it as a continuation — otherwise the middle of a
            # commit message leaks into the keyword view (measured: a message about
            # `csrutil disable` tripped the SIP deny).
            if q == "'" and s[i + 1:i + 3] == "\\'":
                # FOUR characters: the closing `'`, the `\`, the literal `'`, and the
                # RE-OPENING `'`. Skipping only three lands on the re-opening quote, which
                # then closes the span and leaks the rest of the argument — measured.
                i += 4 if s[i + 3:i + 4] == "'" else 3
                continue
            q = None
        i += 1
    if q is not None:
        # UNTERMINATED quote. Stripping to end-of-string would hide whatever follows, and a
        # guard must never become more permissive on malformed input. Emit the remainder
        # verbatim so the keyword checks still see it — fail CLOSED, not open.
        out.append(s[open_at:])
    return "".join(out)


def tools_since_last_task_op(transcript_path, last_task_op_ts, tail_lines=600):
    """W28 — assistant TOOL CALLS in the transcript tail after the last task-board op.

    The work signal for STOP-WAKE's second arm. The first arm gates on the board holding a
    PENDING and unblocked row, so a board that is empty or holds only in_progress rows
    could not wake the turn however much work was open (measured: a 3h06m dead stop with
    work open, inside a 4h07m uncoverable window).

    It counts WORK, deliberately, because the arm it feeds must re-arm on work happening —
    never on compliance. TASK1 keyed its once-flag on the last task-op epoch and therefore
    re-armed only when the model complied, so a loop that stopped tracking permanently
    silenced the check whose whole job was to notice that (reproduced at 20 untracked
    messages). Same timestamp convention as task_gap_state: with no task-op yet recorded,
    entries carrying no parseable timestamp count. Fail-open → 0 (no work seen, no wake)."""
    if not transcript_path:
        return 0
    try:
        lines = read_tail_lines(transcript_path, tail_lines)
    except Exception:
        return 0
    # W29: does this transcript carry parseable timestamps AT ALL? The per-row test below
    # counts an unparseable row only while no task-op has been recorded yet — so once the
    # board has been touched even once, every unparseable row is skipped in silence. If the
    # harness ever renames or reformats its timestamp field, `_entry_ts` returns None for
    # EVERY row, the count is 0 forever, and STOP-WAKE's second arm dies for the rest of
    # every session with no decision row and no trace. That is the silent-dependency class
    # this cycle keeps finding, on the one check the operator actually feels — the wake path
    # behind "why do I have to tell you to continue".
    #
    # So: if NOTHING in the tail parses, treat timestamps as unavailable and fall back to the
    # no-task-op behaviour (count the work). A guard must fail toward firing; the cost of
    # being wrong here is one extra nudge, and the cost of the current direction is the whole
    # arm. When timestamps DO parse this changes nothing.
    _any_ts = False
    for ln in lines:
        try:
            if _entry_ts(json.loads(ln)) is not None:
                _any_ts = True
                break
        except Exception:
            continue
    if not _any_ts:
        last_task_op_ts = 0.0
    n = 0
    for ln in lines:
        try:
            o = json.loads(ln)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if o.get("type") != "assistant" or o.get("isMeta"):
            continue
        c = (o.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if not isinstance(c, list):
            continue
        calls = [b for b in c if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "tool_use"]
        if not calls:
            continue
        # A board WRITE resets the counter: work done and then tracked is not untracked
        # work. Without this, the TaskUpdate that completes the last task is itself counted
        # as work, so finishing everything correctly WOKE THE TURN (caught by the W24
        # forward-reconciliation fixture). TaskList/TaskGet are READS and do not reset —
        # looking at the board tracks nothing.
        if any(str(b.get("name", "")) in ("TaskCreate", "TaskUpdate") for b in calls):
            n = 0
            continue
        ts = _entry_ts(o)
        if (ts is None and not last_task_op_ts) or (ts is not None and ts > last_task_op_ts):
            # W28/E02-F2: board READS are excluded from the COUNT, not merely from the reset.
            # They were already correctly barred from resetting the counter — looking at the
            # board tracks nothing — but they were still counted AS work, so three `TaskList`
            # calls against an empty board woke the turn to say something the operator did was
            # untracked, when all they had done was look at the board. A check that fires on
            # its own diagnostic is the fastest way to teach someone to ignore it.
            n += sum(1 for b in calls
                     if str(b.get("name", "")) not in ("TaskList", "TaskGet"))
    return n


# W28: how far the work counter must move before arm 2 re-arms. A bucket, not a cooldown —
# the key is the bucket index, so an unchanged situation asks once and continuing work asks
# again. Small enough that real work re-wakes the turn, large enough that one nudge does not
# become a per-tool-call nag.
WAKE_WORK_BUCKET = 10

# W46/I1: how many wakes on an UNCHANGED board signature whisper before one blocks.
# Slots 0..N-1 emit the dim `systemMessage` line and queue for the next prompt; slot N and
# beyond stop the turn. An open board is not a stuck board — measured, 281 of 282
# user-rendered blocking Stop records in one session carried [STOP-WAKE].
# PROVISIONAL. Calibrate from the decision log once `whisper` and `block` rows accumulate:
# whispers followed by real movement are correct suppressions; blocks at slot >= this are
# correct catches. Raise it if the board routinely un-sticks itself; lower it if a stuck
# board sits too long unwoken.
WAKE_WHISPER_UNTIL = 3

# W28: how long a `lane-owes` claim suppresses the task it names. Exit (c) has to be
# claimable or the block cannot be complied with — but a claim that never expires is a mute
# button, so a lane that goes quiet re-wakes the turn.
LANE_OWES_GRACE_S = 5400   # 90 min


def task_gap_state(transcript_path, last_task_op_ts, tail_lines=600):
    """TASK1 (W18) — (burst, gap_count, last_user_key) from the transcript tail.
    Genuine USER entry = type user, not isMeta, content a non-empty string or carrying
    a text block (the NARR1 boundary test — tool_result-only entries excluded).
    burst = ≥2 genuine USER entries ADJACENT (no assistant entry between them — the
    queued-messages signature) whose FIRST arrived after last_task_op_ts.
    gap_count = genuine USER entries after last_task_op_ts (entries with no parseable
    timestamp count only when last_task_op_ts == 0). Pure counting; fail-open →
    (False, 0, None)."""
    if not transcript_path:
        return (False, 0, None)
    try:
        lines = read_tail_lines(transcript_path, tail_lines)
    except Exception:
        return (False, 0, None)
    burst = False
    gap = 0
    last_key = None
    prev_kind = None       # "user" | "assistant" | None
    prev_user_ts = None
    for ln in lines:
        try:
            o = json.loads(ln)
        except Exception:
            continue
        t = o.get("type")
        if t == "assistant" and not o.get("isMeta"):
            prev_kind = "assistant"
            continue
        if t != "user" or o.get("isMeta"):
            continue
        c = (o.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if not _human_entry(c):
            continue
        ts = _entry_ts(o)
        after = (ts is None and not last_task_op_ts) or (ts is not None and ts > last_task_op_ts)
        if after:
            gap += 1
            last_key = str(int(ts)) if ts is not None else "n%d" % gap
            if prev_kind == "user" and (prev_user_ts is None or not last_task_op_ts
                                        or prev_user_ts > last_task_op_ts):
                burst = True
        prev_kind = "user"
        prev_user_ts = ts
    return (burst, gap, last_key)


def _real_id(tok):
    """[pure] True when a captured identifier is a LITERAL id, not an unexpanded
    shell fragment. Hooks read the raw command string BEFORE shell expansion, so
    `version publish $AGENT_ID` captures the placeholder text — recording it
    poisons the lifecycle log with a phantom obligation. Reject any token carrying
    shell-meta characters; a rejected event is simply not recorded (a re-run with
    the literal id records normally).

        W38/live: rejecting shell-meta alone was not enough. Two rows landed in the real
    lifecycle feed this session with the "agent ids" `for` and `v1',` — English text and a
    fragment of a quoted string, captured from a probe command and then nagged about by EV1 as
    agents that were "published this session". Nothing had been published. An obligation keyed
    on prose is unclosable: the id never appears again, so it can never be discharged.

    So the token must also LOOK like an id: platform ids here are UUIDs, and test ids are of the
    `agent-1` shape. Three cheap rules kill the junk without a UUID-only rule that would reject
    legitimate short-form ids — no stray punctuation, a minimum length, and not a bare
    lowercase word (which is what prose and shell keywords look like)."""
    if not tok or any(ch in tok for ch in "${}<>`\\"):
        return False
    if any(ch not in "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789._-"
           for ch in tok):
        return False                      # quotes, commas, brackets — a captured fragment
    if len(tok) < 4:
        # A floor, not a shape claim. The observed junk (`for`, `v1',`) is already caught by the
        # punctuation and bare-word rules, so this only has to exclude the very shortest
        # fragments. It was briefly set to 6, which rejected the legitimate short-form id `ag-9`
        # in this estate's own fixture — a security predicate must not be tightened past the
        # evidence that motivated it.
        return False
    return not tok.isalpha()              # a bare word is prose, never an identifier


def agent_publish_events(cmd):
    """EV1 feed (W18; hardened W19) [pure]. Classify a command as an agent-family
    lifecycle event: ("publish", <id>) for `version publish <id>` /
    `deployment create --agent-id <id>`; ("eval", None) for
    `agent-eval run create|execute` / `emulator send`. Else None. A captured id
    failing _real_id (unexpanded $VAR etc.) returns None — never recorded."""
    s = _strip(cmd or "")
    m = re.search(r"version\s+publish\s+(\S+)", s)
    if m:
        aid = m.group(1).strip("'\"")
        return ("publish", aid) if _real_id(aid) else None
    if re.search(r"deployment\s+create\b", s):
        am = re.search(r"--agent-id\s+(\S+)", cmd or "")
        if am:
            aid = am.group(1).strip("'\"")
            return ("publish", aid) if _real_id(aid) else None
        return None
    if re.search(r"agent-eval\s+run\s+(create|execute)\b|emulator\s+send\b", s):
        return ("eval", None)
    return None


def narration_count(transcript_path, tail_lines=400):
    """NARR1 (W11) — PURE COUNTING of inter-tool narration volume in the CURRENT turn.
    Reads the transcript tail, finds the last genuine user input (type=="user", not
    isMeta, content a string or carrying a text block — interrupts and teammate
    notifications count as turn boundaries), then counts assistant TEXT blocks that are
    followed by at least one later tool_use in the window (the final reply never counts
    — it is the legitimate deliverable, however long). Exclusions are FLAG-based only:
    thinking blocks by type, isApiErrorMessage entries, isMeta entries. Returns the
    count, or None when the path is absent/unreadable (fail-open). Zero wording
    interpretation — hooks are purely logic (W10 ruling); volume is the measurable."""
    if not transcript_path:
        return None
    try:
        lines = read_tail_lines(transcript_path, tail_lines)
    except Exception:
        return None
    entries = []
    for ln in lines:
        try:
            entries.append(json.loads(ln))
        except Exception:
            continue
    start = None
    for i in range(len(entries) - 1, -1, -1):
        o = entries[i]
        if o.get("type") != "user" or o.get("isMeta"):
            continue
        c = (o.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if (isinstance(c, str) and c.strip()) or (
                isinstance(c, list) and any(isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") == "text"
                                            for b in c)):
            start = i
            break
    if start is None:
        return None
    events = []
    for o in entries[start + 1:]:
        if o.get("type") != "assistant" or o.get("isMeta") or o.get("isApiErrorMessage"):
            continue
        for b in ((o.get("message") or {}).get("content") or []):
            if not isinstance(b, dict):
                continue
            if b.get("type") == "text" and (b.get("text") or "").strip():
                events.append("text")
            elif b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                events.append("tool")
    count, tools_after = 0, 0
    for ev in reversed(events):
        if ev == "tool":
            tools_after += 1
        elif tools_after:
            count += 1
    return count


def consolidation_verify_gap(last_message):
    """SC-* gate — now FLEET-aware. Checks the SPINE's own writes AND each tiers[] sub-result (a tier
    agent's slice carries its own retrieved + verify.writes). The nexus-consolidation fleet reports writes;
    a subagent self-report is INTENT, not proof (R#20: SILENT ACCEPTANCE → subagent self-report), so each
    write is reconciled against the authoritative listing. Internal to Cue (leak #7). Returns one annotate
    Decision or None."""
    obj = _last_json(last_message) or {}
    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        return None
    d = _verify_one(obj)
    if d:
        return d
    for t in (obj.get("tiers") or []):
        if isinstance(t, dict):
            dt = _verify_one(t)
            if dt:
                dt = dict(dt)
                dt["reason"] = f"(tier {t.get('tier', '?')}) " + dt["reason"]
                return dt
    return None


def _verify_one(obj):
    """The per-result SC-VERIFY/RETR/GROUND/PARENT/DOMAIN checks on ONE result dict (the spine's top-level
    object OR a single tiers[] slice). Returns one annotate Decision or None."""
    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        return None
    if not (obj.get("filed") or obj.get("updated") or obj.get("reorganised")):
        return None
    v = obj.get("verify")
    writes = v.get("writes") if isinstance(v, dict) else None
    # Each write must carry a status AND an evidence token (modifiedAt / listed_at /
    # evidence string). This catches the real failure (a bare `verify:"ok"` with NO
    # writes array) while tolerating a mixed ledger (persisted + blocked, each with
    # its evidence) and the agent's natural key choice (path|target, evidence string).
    # W18: a mount-read/stat/read-back claim is NOT persistence proof (R#20 phantom-write;
    # a mount can serve stale content right after a server-side write) — evidence strings
    # asserting mount/stat/read-back evidence do not satisfy the gate.
    def _ev_ok(w):
        if w.get("modifiedAt") or w.get("listed_at"):
            return True
        ev = w.get("evidence")
        return bool(ev) and not re.search(r"\bmount\b|\bstat\b|read.?back", str(ev), re.I)
    ok = (isinstance(writes, list) and writes
          and all(isinstance(w, dict) and w.get("status") and _ev_ok(w)
                  for w in writes))
    if not ok:
        return _decide("SC-VERIFY", "annotate",
                       "the consolidation agent reported writes without per-write "
                       "persistence evidence (listing path + fresh modifiedAt, "
                       "status=persisted); a subagent's success is intent, not proof "
                       "(R#20), and each write is confirmed via the directory listing, "
                       "since a 2xx PUT / signed read can phantom-succeed.")
    if not obj.get("retrieved"):
        return _decide("SC-RETR", "annotate",
                       "the consolidation agent filed without reporting a pre-write "
                       "retrieval (§14b); dedup/placement may be blind, so duplicates "
                       "are worth a spot-check.")
    # SC-GROUND — a grounding/source edge points at a LOCAL/PRIVATE file never uploaded
    # (self-containment, §10 / §1b inv 5). Public URLs + workspace-relative paths pass.
    _srcs = []
    for _e in (obj.get("edges") or []):
        if isinstance(_e, dict):
            _srcs += [_e.get("to"), _e.get("from")]
    for _k in ("filed", "updated"):
        for _it in (obj.get(_k) or []):
            if isinstance(_it, dict):
                _srcs.append(_it.get("path"))
    if any(local_file_source_ref(s) for s in _srcs if s):
        return _decide("SC-GROUND", "annotate",
                       "a learning grounds to a LOCAL/PRIVATE file path never uploaded to "
                       "the workspace; the workspace must be self-contained, so the source "
                       "is uploaded (DT-2) and re-grounded to the workspace copy.")
    # SC-PARENT — a NEW leaf whose parent folder README was not refreshed (DT-3 propagate-up):
    # the roll-up signature goes stale and signature-pruned retrieval can't see the child.
    import os as _os
    from collections import Counter as _C
    filed = obj.get("filed") or []
    updated_paths = [u.get("path", "") for u in (obj.get("updated") or []) if isinstance(u, dict)]
    for f in filed:
        p = f.get("path", "") if isinstance(f, dict) else ""
        # Only a NEW FOLDER (its README.md) needs its PARENT folder's signature rolled up.
        if not p.endswith("/README.md"):
            continue
        parent = _os.path.dirname(_os.path.dirname(p))   # the folder whose README should list this child
        if parent and not any(parent in up for up in updated_paths):
            return _decide("SC-PARENT", "annotate",
                           "a new entry was filed without refreshing its PARENT folder README "
                           "signature; the roll-up is stale (DT-3) until the parent README "
                           "lists the new child.")
    # SC-DOMAIN — >=3 new siblings under ONE parent → maybe a sub-domain (structural-fit gate).
    parents = _C(_os.path.dirname(f.get("path", "")) for f in filed if isinstance(f, dict))
    if any(n >= 3 for n in parents.values()):
        return _decide("SC-DOMAIN", "annotate",
                       "≥3 new sibling entries landed under one folder; the structural-fit "
                       "gate asks whether they form a sub-domain that deserves its own partition.")
    # SC-XORG — a COMMUNITY tier slice referenced a private (general-context/) path in a filed/updated
    # body, path, or edge. Community KB is cross-org; the org-community bridge lives on the T0 side only.
    if obj.get("tier") in ("tools", "systems", "use-cases"):
        _blob = []
        for _k in ("filed", "updated"):
            for _it in (obj.get(_k) or []):
                if isinstance(_it, dict):
                    _blob += [str(_it.get("path", "")), str(_it.get("what", ""))]
        for _e in (obj.get("edges") or []):
            if isinstance(_e, dict):
                _blob += [str(_e.get("to", "")), str(_e.get("from", ""))]
        if any("general-context/" in s for s in _blob):
            return _decide("SC-XORG", "annotate",
                           "a community write referenced a private path (general-context/...); community "
                           "KB is cross-org and the org-community bridge lives on the T0 side only.")
    return None


_MISFIT_RE = re.compile(r"mis-?fit|mis-?placement|mis-?filed", re.I)


def consolidation_report_checks(agent_type, last_message):
    """SC-MISFIT + SC-ADV + SC-DRYRUN (W12) + SC-CANON (W12.2) + SC-UNIT (W13) —
    deterministic structure checks on the consolidation SPINE's completion report. All
    measure FIELD/TYPE PRESENCE, never language quality.

    SC-MISFIT: a flagged mis-placement with no reorganised[] move and no deferred_because —
    detection-without-correction entrenches the mis-fit (DT-PROP row-gate; a flag alone was
    the measured failure mode: detected repeatedly, corrected never, then indexed as settled).

    SC-ADV: a tier slice carries community writes but no adversary verdict (spine §0 step
    6.5), or a fail/blocked verdict coexists with canonical_source edges when no passing
    tier could own them — value-instrument self-scans measured-miss semantic leaks; the
    adversary verdict is the gate canonical_source wiring waits on.

    Returns a LIST of annotate Decisions (0-5); [] for non-spine agents."""
    if agent_type != "nexus-consolidation":
        return []
    obj = _last_json(last_message) or {}
    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        return []
    out = []
    # --- SC-MISFIT ---
    flagged = [f for f in (obj.get("flagged") or []) if isinstance(f, dict)]
    misfits = [f for f in flagged if _MISFIT_RE.search(json.dumps(f))]
    if misfits and not (obj.get("reorganised") or []) \
            and not any("deferred_because" in f for f in misfits):
        out.append(_decide(
            "SC-MISFIT", "annotate",
            "the report flags a mis-placement with no matching reorganised[] move and no "
            "deferred_because — the DT-PROP row-gate corrects a detected mis-fit in the SAME "
            "run (§19a.1 #1 MOVE + ref-sweep + CHANGELOG) or defers it explicitly; a flag "
            "alone entrenches the mis-fit. Correct (or defer with a reason) and re-emit."))
    # --- SC-ADV ---
    tiers = [t for t in (obj.get("tiers") or []) if isinstance(t, dict)]
    cs_edges = [e for e in (obj.get("edges") or [])
                if isinstance(e, dict) and (e.get("type") or "") == "canonical_source"]
    passing_writers = 0
    for t in tiers:
        wrote = bool(t.get("filed") or t.get("updated"))
        adv = t.get("adversary") if isinstance(t.get("adversary"), dict) else {}
        verdict = (adv.get("verdict") or "").lower()
        if wrote and not verdict:
            out.append(_decide(
                "SC-ADV", "annotate",
                "tier %s carries community writes but no adversary verdict — canonical_source "
                "wiring waits on the §0 step-6.5 adversary PASS per slice; run the gate and "
                "re-emit the report with adversary:{verdict,leaks,artifact} on that slice."
                % (t.get("tier") or "?")))
            break
        if wrote and verdict == "pass":
            passing_writers += 1
    else:
        # Only attributable deterministically when NO passing tier could own the edges.
        failed = [t for t in tiers
                  if isinstance(t.get("adversary"), dict)
                  and (t["adversary"].get("verdict") or "").lower() in ("fail", "blocked")]
        if failed and cs_edges and passing_writers == 0:
            out.append(_decide(
                "SC-ADV", "annotate",
                "a tier slice's adversary verdict is fail/blocked yet canonical_source edges "
                "appear in the report with no passing slice to own them — a failed slice files "
                "NOTHING to community and gets no forward edge; unwire and re-emit."))
    # --- SC-DRYRUN (W12) --- field presence only: a composition run (composed[] carries a
    # family/deliverable sub-record) must emit the §0 7b blind-retrieval record. Both audited
    # deck runs would have passed prose-only completion wording; the emitted dry_run[] is the
    # deterministic surface. No family record → no fire (the common zero-community run).
    composed = [c for c in (obj.get("composed") or []) if isinstance(c, dict)]
    needs_dry = [c for c in composed if isinstance(c.get("family"), dict)
                 or (c.get("family") or "") not in ("", None)]
    if needs_dry and not (obj.get("dry_run") or []):
        out.append(_decide(
            "SC-DRYRUN", "annotate",
            "composed[] carries a family/deliverable record but dry_run[] is absent/empty — "
            "run the blind-retrieval gate (§0 7b: one zero-context retriever probe built from "
            "the §11b Next-Task probes; only the blind reader's found/not-found is evidence) "
            "and re-emit with dry_run:[{probe,request,blind,resolves_via,verdict}]."))
    # --- SC-CANON (W12.2) --- KEY MEMBERSHIP, not falsiness: `canon_deltas: []` is the
    # legal "considered, none" verdict (SILENT); only an ABSENT key fires. (SC-DRYRUN's
    # falsy test is intentionally different — an empty dry_run on a family run is itself
    # the defect there.) Same detection base as SC-DRYRUN; both may fire on one report.
    if needs_dry and "canon_deltas" not in obj:
        out.append(_decide(
            "SC-CANON", "annotate",
            "composed[] carries a deliverable/family record but the canon_deltas key is "
            "absent — run the §12 Row 7 canon-touch (which cross-cutting canons does this "
            "work refine: design · voice · recipes · org facts?) and re-emit with "
            "canon_deltas:[{canon,delta,provenance}] (an empty list = considered, none)."))
    # --- SC-UNIT (W13) --- TYPE + KEY MEMBERSHIP + declared-defect echo: fires when the
    # coverage record is absent, malformed (not a dict / no unmapped key — coverage never
    # computed), or carries a non-empty unmapped list (the agent's OWN declared gap).
    # Silent ONLY on a dict with an explicit empty `unmapped` (complete coverage) — the
    # doctrine's structural/blocked escapes move residuals OUT of unmapped before emitting.
    uc = obj.get("unit_coverage")
    if needs_dry and (not isinstance(uc, dict) or "unmapped" not in uc or uc.get("unmapped")):
        out.append(_decide(
            "SC-UNIT", "annotate",
            "composed[] carries a deliverable/family record but unit_coverage is "
            "absent/incomplete — run the §12 Row 6 enumeration (position table scripted "
            "from the assembly, count-asserted) and re-emit with "
            "unit_coverage:{positions,rows,unmapped} (empty unmapped = complete; residuals "
            "classed structural in the position table or blocked{coverage} with a reason)."))
    return out

_ERR_FIX = {
    "EDGE_INVALID_SOURCE_HANDLE": "the edge's source handle is wrong — for a "
        "branching node use the branch's handle id, not the node id.",
    "EDGE_SCOPE_VIOLATION": "edge crosses a scope (loop/branch) boundary — wire "
        "within the same parent scope.",
    "NODE_TYPE_INVALID": "check the --type value against `workflow node-types`.",
    "NODE_TRIGGER_DELETE_FORBIDDEN": "the trigger node can't be deleted; replace it instead.",
    "VALIDATION_ERROR": "a field is malformed — re-read the body shape; do NOT file a ticket.",
    "NOT_FOUND": "the id/key is wrong — re-resolve it (don't retype from screen, R#20).",
    "CONFLICT": "resource state conflict — re-fetch current state before retrying.",
    "INVALID_API_KEY": "auth issue — check the active profile / key (don't file a ticket).",
}


def classify_failure(cmd, error_text):
    """FH1-4 [S] — turn a tool failure into the next correct action.
    `error_text` = the captured stderr/stdout of the failed command."""
    e = error_text or ""
    if re.search(r"Cannot find module[^\n]*(cmux-claude-node-options|"
                 r"restore-node-options)", e):
        return _decide("FH5", "annotate",
                       "stale NODE_OPTIONS: a harness wrapper set `--require` to a "
                       "temp module that no longer exists. Prepend `unset "
                       "NODE_OPTIONS` to the command and retry. Environment glitch, "
                       "NOT a Nexus platform bug — do not file a ticket.")
    if re.search(r"unknown option|unknown command|usage:", e, re.I):
        # raw-read: pulls the SUBCOMMAND out for the message text; the caller
        # has already established the command is a `nexus` invocation.
        m = re.search(r"nexus\s+([a-z-]+(?:\s+[a-z-]+)?)", cmd or "")
        sub = m.group(1) if m else "<subcommand>"
        return _decide("FH1", "annotate",
                       f"Unknown option/command — run `nexus {sub} --help` to get "
                       "the correct flags before retrying (R#11 failure path).")
    if re.search(r"SANDBOX_READY_TIMEOUT|SANDBOX_PROVISIONING_FAILED", e):
        return _decide("FH2", "annotate",
                       "Transient sandbox provisioning — the server retries "
                       "(build-then-swap). Do NOT wrap in client-side retry; "
                       "surface only if it persists.")
    if re.search(r"Credential not found|does not belong to this tool", e, re.I):
        return _decide("FH6", "annotate",
                       "`external-tool execute --credential` needs the TOOL-SCOPED id "
                       "from `nexus tool credentials <toolId>`, NOT the org-level id "
                       "from `credential list`/`credential get` (R#16).")
    if (re.search(r"Operation timed out|\b423\b|Locked", e)
            and re.search(r"workspaces?[/_-]|general-context|/mnt/workspace", cmd or "", re.I)):
        return _decide("FH7", "annotate",
                       "Workspace mount wedged (read timeout / 423 Locked). RECOVER "
                       "via the REST signed URL (`nexus api GET /workspaces/<slug>/"
                       "file?path=`); verify writes via the directory listing, NOT the "
                       "signed read; a wedge on a plain op is a DEFECT → dedup-search + "
                       "file (R#7/R#10/R#30), do not silently route around.")
    m = re.search(r"\b(" + "|".join(_ERR_FIX) + r")\b", e)
    if m:
        return _decide("FH3", "annotate", f"{m.group(1)}: {_ERR_FIX[m.group(1)]}")
    if re.search(r"\b500\b|INTERNAL_ERROR|PrismaClient", e):
        return _decide("FH4", "annotate",
                       "500 = server bug → file a ticket via nexus-tickets with "
                       "endpoint + request + response + repro (R#7); dedup-search "
                       "`ticket list --search` first.")
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save-transform (R#20 "Save-transform" variant) — pure helpers for AM5/AM6/AM7.
# The server may REWRITE content on write (escape-on-save) and re-escape its own
# escapes on the next save (a cascade: backslash runs grow ~2x per round-trip).
# Deterministic, fail-open: any missing/None input -> no verdict.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_BSLASH_RUN = re.compile(r"\\{2,}")


def prompt_stats(text):
    """Length + longest backslash run of a prompt body. None on non-string."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return None
    longest = 0
    for m in _BSLASH_RUN.finditer(text):
        n = len(m.group(0))
        if n > longest:
            longest = n
    return {"length": len(text), "max_backslash_run": longest}


def prompt_precheck(stats):
    """Warns BEFORE `agent update --prompt <file>` fires. Returns [(id, reason)].
    AM5: file exceeds the server's 1,000,000-char `prompt` validation cap.
    AM6: file already contains a runaway backslash run (re-saving compounds it)."""
    out = []
    if not stats:
        return out
    if stats["length"] > 1_000_000:
        out.append(("AM5", "prompt is %s chars — the server rejects `prompt` "
                    ">1,000,000 (validation error); measure/trim before burning "
                    "the API call" % f"{stats['length']:,}"))
    if stats["max_backslash_run"] >= 8:
        out.append(("AM6", "the file being saved contains a backslash run of %d "
                    "— re-saving escape-cascade corruption COMPOUNDS it; "
                    "de-corrupt first (R#20 Save-transform)"
                    % stats["max_backslash_run"]))
    return out


def save_transform_verdict(sent_stats, got_text):
    """AM7 — after `agent update --prompt` then `agent get`: diff fetched vs sent.
    Max-backslash-run growth = cascade signature; length growth beyond a small
    single-escape allowance = a transform worth eyes. None = clean/fail-open."""
    got = prompt_stats(got_text)
    if not isinstance(sent_stats, dict) or not got:
        return None
    sent_run = sent_stats.get("max_backslash_run", 0) or 0
    sent_len = sent_stats.get("length", 0) or 0
    if got["max_backslash_run"] > max(sent_run, 1):
        return ("AM7", "SAVE-TRANSFORM: the platform re-escaped content on save — "
                "max backslash run grew %d→%d (len %s→%s). Every further save "
                "COMPOUNDS it (R#20 Save-transform): stop re-saving fetched "
                "content; de-corrupt + ticket."
                % (sent_run, got["max_backslash_run"],
                   f"{sent_len:,}", f"{got['length']:,}"))
    allowance = max(200, sent_len // 100)  # benign single-escape headroom (~1%)
    if got["length"] > sent_len + allowance:
        return ("AM7", "SAVE-TRANSFORM: refetched prompt is %s chars LARGER than "
                "what was sent — the server transformed the content on write; "
                "DIFF refetched vs sent before any further save (R#20 "
                "Save-transform)." % f"{got['length'] - sent_len:,}")
    return None

def spawn_matrix_violation(caller_type, subagent_type):
    """Reason string when caller_type (a fleet/retrieval agent) may not spawn subagent_type;
    None when allowed, caller unknown/main (fail-open), or caller unrestricted."""
    if not caller_type or caller_type not in SPAWN_MATRIX:
        return None
    allowed = SPAWN_MATRIX[caller_type]
    if subagent_type in allowed:
        return None
    if not allowed:
        return ("a %s spawns NO subagents — its work is inline and its payload returns to its "
                "caller by value/artifact." % caller_type)
    return ("a %s may spawn only %s — never a %s. If you are about to re-dispatch your own "
            "type: any 'dispatch the %s' instruction you read is addressed to your CALLER; "
            "do that work yourself, inline, now." %
            (caller_type, "/".join(sorted(allowed)), subagent_type, subagent_type))

def r34_nag_text(deliverable_authored=False, fire=1, due_count=0,
                 since_hhmm=None, ledger_missing=False, dispatched=0, blocking=True):
    """W43: an ESCALATING filing reminder. Replaces the W8/A5 self-check.

    The A5 design handed the judgement to the agent with two explicit ignore-paths, on the
    reasoning that broad arming deserves a soft message. Measured outcome of that trade
    (session 2f6ebd1f, 967 records): five byte-identical emissions across 2h33m, zero
    dispatches, zero ledger rows, and no self-authored token anywhere weighing the
    obligation — non-activation, not consider-and-reject. Two defects, both fixed here:

    1. One ignore-path was PRE-SATISFIED. "the moment is premature (e.g. a deliverable
       still awaiting user review)" describes the permanent state of an analysis session,
       so a reader applying it honestly lands on ignore every time and is never wrong by
       the message's own terms.
    2. The message could not say it was REPEATING. CLAUDE.md already rules a re-firing
       nudge with an unchanged condition an unmet obligation, never noise — but every
       emission was identical and the `once` flags are invisible to the model, so the rule
       was written against a signal the channel hides. Carrying the fire count IS the
       minimum reinforcement that makes the EXISTING rule reachable.

    Evidence for the shape: in the failing session one injected block carried both [TASK1]
    and [R34]; the imperative half naming a concrete tool call was acted on 2m35s later,
    the interrogative half never. Blind A/B before adoption, scoring fixed before any
    output was read: the old text produced 0/2 subjects naming a dispatch (one explicitly
    discarded the vendor gotchas as "des détails d'exécution de mon côté"), this text 2/2,
    both also creating the ledger, at positions 1-3 of their own plans instead of 9th and
    absent. Caveat kept with the claim: n=2 per arm, and this text is longer as well as
    more imperative, so length is an uncontrolled confound."""
    voice = (" Deliverable tone/format feedback is a voice/brand-home candidate (via the "
             "retriever)." if deliverable_authored else "")
    call = ('Agent(subagent_type="nexus-consolidation", run_in_background=true, '
            'name="<workstream>-consolidation")')
    since = (" and the condition has not changed since %s" % since_hhmm) if since_hhmm else ""
    ledger = ("\nNo ledger file exists for this session. R#34 makes it due at the FIRST "
              "filing-worthy event; you are at %d. Create it before you dispatch."
              % max(1, int(due_count))) if ledger_missing else ""

    if fire <= 1:
        return ("Filing is due: %d filing-worthy event(s) have accrued since the last "
                "consolidation ran, and this session has dispatched none. Dispatch the "
                "spine in the background at this turn's natural pause — %s — briefed with "
                "each verified learning, its source-document path and the ledger "
                "snapshot.%s If this is genuinely the wrong moment, log the deferral with "
                "its re-arm condition and open a durable board task for it; a silent skip "
                "is the one option that is not available.%s"
                % (max(1, int(due_count)), call, ledger, voice))

    if fire == 2:
        return ("Reminder 2 of this session%s. %d filing-worthy events have accrued and "
                "this session has dispatched nothing.\nACT THIS TURN — %s — briefed with "
                "every verified learning, its source-document path and the ledger "
                "snapshot.%s\nThe ONLY alternative is an EXPLICIT deferral: log its "
                "re-arm condition AND open a durable board task. Staying silent is not "
                "one of them, and this reminder fires again unchanged.%s"
                % (since, max(1, int(due_count)), call, ledger, voice))

    # W43-b: every clause below is CONDITIONAL on state actually checked. The first cut
    # asserted three things unconditionally and was measured lying about all three in one
    # live emission: an event count of 1786 (it counted the whole project's history, of
    # which 2 rows were this session's), "this session has dispatched nothing" while the
    # dispatched-log held a row for it, and "Turn blocked" while the observe marker was
    # present and nothing had been blocked. A reminder that misstates state is the exact
    # defect W43 exists to fix, rebuilt one layer up: the A/B proved the copy MOVES a
    # reader and never asked whether it was TRUE.
    head = ("Turn blocked — knowledge filing is overdue."
            if blocking else
            "Knowledge filing is overdue (escalated). This is NOT blocking your turn — the "
            "`.r34-observe` marker is set, so this is a record-only emission.")
    if int(dispatched) > 0:
        disp = ("this session HAS dispatched %d time(s), but filing-worthy events have "
                "landed since the last one" % int(dispatched))
        prior = ""
    else:
        disp = "this session has dispatched nothing"
        prior = (" No ledger exists either, and no deferral has been logged."
                 if ledger_missing else " No deferral has been logged.")
    exits = ("Two things clear this:" if blocking else "Two things clear the condition:")
    tail = (("This block is bounded to %d per session and then goes quiet on its own."
             % R34_BLOCK_BUDGET) if blocking else
            "Nothing is blocked; delete `.r34-observe` to make this enforce.")
    return ("%s This is reminder %d of this session%s, %d filing-worthy event(s) have "
            "accrued since the last consolidation ran, and %s.%s\n\n%s\n"
            "  1. Dispatch now — %s — with each verified learning, its source path and "
            "the ledger snapshot. This clears the condition immediately.\n"
            "  2. The owner turns filing off for this conversation by sending: "
            "consolidation off\n\n"
            "Logging an explicit deferral with a board task remains the right thing to do "
            "and is what R#34 asks for, but nothing reads it yet, so it does not by itself "
            "release this.%s\n%s%s"
            % (head, int(fire), since, max(1, int(due_count)), disp, prior, exits,
               call, ledger, tail, voice))

def pflag_age_s(project, key):
    """Seconds since a project flag was set, or None when it is not set.

    None, never 0: a missing flag must not read as "just set". The stores record no
    provenance at all — the nine-day hold's origin was unknowable — so the file's own mtime
    is the only age signal that exists, and this is the one place that reads it.

    `time` is imported HERE because this module has no module-level `time`; relying on one
    made the first cut raise NameError into the except below and return None for every
    flag, fresh or nine days old — a silent always-None that the caller could not tell from
    "no hold set". Caught by the fixture, not by review."""
    import time as _time
    try:
        import session_cache as _sc
        p = os.path.join(_sc._pdir(project, create=False), "flag_" + _sc._safe(key))
        return _time.time() - os.path.getmtime(p)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return None   # unset, unreadable, or no project — the caller treats it as "no hold age"


def r34_ledger_text(ledger_name, ledger_age_min):
