def r34_verify_text(age_min, dts=None):
    """W12 R34-VERIFY: a consolidation DISPATCH with no verified COMPLETION past the grace.
    Pure file-state (two project-log timestamps); the dispatch-time ran-credit masks a dead
    run from R34-DUE, so this is the only signal that a spine died mid-flight (measured: a
    connection-killed run sat unnoticed ~2 days until a manual resume). W15: the nudge names
    the dispatch epoch (the registry is PROJECT-scoped by design — a pending item can belong
    to an earlier session; the id makes it attributable) + the write CLASSES verification
    covers (a sampled check is self-report acceptance)."""
    stamp = (" (dispatch epoch %s)" % str(dts).strip()) if dts else ""
    return ("a consolidation dispatched ~%d min ago%s has no verified completion — read its "
            "report/transcript, confirm EVERY briefed write CLASS in the LISTING (entities · "
            "org docs · community twins per slug: tools/systems/use-cases · INDEX rows), then "
            "resume it or re-dispatch with its increments (R#34). If it completed without its "
            "final consolidation-log write, that write IS the missing completion evidence."
            % (max(1, int(age_min)), stamp))


RESIDENT_HINT_ROWS = 6  # ~6 ledger EVENTS (data rows) → the resident-mode hint (docs unit)


def ledger_data_rows(text):
    """Count DATA rows in a ledger, format-agnostic (pure structure, W11): ledgers in
    practice use either markdown TABLES (pipe rows, minus the header/separator) or
    top-level BULLETS (`- DECISION: …` lines). Count both — the W8 pipe-only counter
    silently returned 0 for bullet ledgers, so the resident hint and the ledger-armed
    due condition never fired on the common format (measured live)."""
    lines = (text or "").splitlines()
    pipe = [l for l in lines
            if l.lstrip().startswith("|") and set(l.strip()) - set("|-: ")]
    bullets = [l for l in lines if l.startswith("- ")]
    return max(0, len(pipe) - 1) + len(bullets)


_PUT_SRC_RE = re.compile(r'--data-binary\s+@([^\s"\';|&)]+)')
# W28/F01 — this REBOUND the module-level `_HEREDOC_RE` defined at the top of the file. Python
# binds module globals in file order, so the later definition won every call: `_strip()` — the
# view the whole DENY tier matches on — silently used THIS pattern, not the one documented
# beside it 2,000 lines up. A fix applied to the canonical copy had no effect at all until this
# was found. Renamed, because two different jobs were sharing one name: stripping a heredoc
# needs no groups, extracting its body needs the body captured. Same corrected grammar as the
# canonical pattern, plus a capture for the body.
_HEREDOC_BODY_RE = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*(['\"]?)(\w+)\1[^\n]*\n(.*?)\n[ \t]*\2\b", re.S)


def selfcontain_hits(text):
    """First local/tmp/code-forge reference in a workspace-bound BODY (pointer-only
    filings: org-produced artifacts referenced by repo/local/tmp paths instead of
    uploaded). Returns the matched token | None."""
    m = _PRIVATE_REPO_HOST.search(text or "")
    if m:
        return m.group(0)
    m = _LOCAL_SRC.search(text or "")
    return m.group(0).strip() if m else None


def heredoc_bodies(cmd):
    """The heredoc CONTENT segments of a compound Bash command — the only parts of a
    curl-PUT command that are BODY rather than transport (the @file args, key reads and
    URLs around them are infra and false-positive the body scan)."""
    return [m[2] for m in _HEREDOC_BODY_RE.findall(cmd or "")]


def put_body_selfcontain(cmd):
    """On a WebDAV PUT (`--data-binary @<file>` + `/api/dav/`), read each resolvable local
    source file (text, ≤300KB) and return the first self-containment hit as
    (source_path, token) | None. Variable paths (@"$f") and binaries are skipped
    (fail-open); the fleet STAGING Write/Edit scan is the catcher for loop-staged files."""
    if "/api/dav/" not in (cmd or "") or "--data-binary" not in (cmd or ""):
        return None
    for src in _PUT_SRC_RE.findall(cmd)[:8]:
        if "$" in src or "{" in src:
            continue
        try:
            p = os.path.expanduser(src)
            if not os.path.isfile(p) or os.path.getsize(p) > 300_000:
                continue
            if not p.endswith((".md", ".txt", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".html")):
                continue
            with open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
                tok = selfcontain_hits(fh.read())
            if tok:
                return (src, tok)
        except Exception:
            continue
    return None


_IX1_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"(^|\n)#{2,}[^\n]*(Recent edits|Reorganisation history|\b20\d\d\b)")
# W18: state-prose rows are the same INDEX-CONTRACT violation class — an INDEX row asserting
# emptiness/state ("empty scaffold", "no entry yet") instead of content (I55 writer-rot family).
_IX1_ROW_RE = re.compile(r"\bAdded 20\d\d-|empty scaffold|no entr(?:y|ies) yet", re.I)


def index_hygiene_check(content):
    """True when INDEX-bound content carries change-narration debris: a dated/history heading
    (`## Recent edits`, `## Reorganisation history`, `## <20xx …>`) or an `Added 20xx-` row
    annotation. Rows only in INDEX; history → the workspace CHANGELOG (INDEX CONTRACT,
    shared-governance)."""
    c = content or ""
    return bool(_IX1_HEADING_RE.search(c) or _IX1_ROW_RE.search(c))


# --------------------------------------------------- W19 build-gate helpers --

# The hook estate's own project root, computed once. This file is
# <root>/.claude/hooks/lib/hook_core.py, so FOUR dirname() hops land on <root>:
# lib/hook_core.py -> lib -> hooks -> .claude -> <root>. (Three hops stop at `.claude` and
# leave the project root itself detected as an app repo, which is the exact defect this
# exclusion exists for — caught by driving it rather than by reading it.)
# Used by `app_repo_ctx` to exclude the estate by IDENTITY rather than by a marker
# heuristic; see the note there for the two heuristics that were driven wrong first.
_ESTATE_ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))))


def ledger_paths(sid, lines_fn=None):
    """[file-state] Every path that could be this session's workstream ledger, from ALL the
    channels a ledger actually arrives on: the flat scratchpad glob, one level down (a cycle
    keeps its artifacts in a per-cycle subdirectory), and the `cycle-artifacts` feed the
    Write/Edit path registers.

    W44: this exists because THREE locators had drifted apart — `_latest_ledger` unioned the
    feed (hardened W27), `consol_ledger_checkpoint` globbed flat, and `consol_brief_lint`
    globbed flat. The first W44 pass fixed one of the two stragglers and missed the other,
    which is the wave's own "a fix at one call site is not landed" rule failing inside the
    wave that added it. One helper, three callers, so the next channel is added once.

    `lines_fn` takes the session_cache reader (`lambda f: sc.lines(sid, f)`) so this module
    stays free of a session_cache import."""
    import glob as _glob
    out = []
    try:
        out += _glob.glob("/private/tmp/claude-501/*/%s/scratchpad/ledger-*.md" % sid)
        out += _glob.glob("/private/tmp/claude-501/*/%s/scratchpad/*/ledger-*.md" % sid)
    except Exception:
        pass   # advisory: an unreadable scratchpad must not decide a ledger claim either way
    if lines_fn is not None:
        try:
            out += [p for p in lines_fn("cycle-artifacts")
                    if p and os.path.isfile(p)]
        except Exception:
            pass   # advisory: the feed is one channel of three; losing it is not fatal here
    return [p for p in out if not p.endswith(".closed.md")]


def app_repo_ctx(rdir):
    """[file-state] True when the CURRENT repo/cwd itself carries app-build markers
    (.nexus-app · .nexus-starter · docs/{PRD,DESIGN,BUILD-MODE,SPEC,feature-manifest}.md).
    W23 widened the set to P0/P0.5-time artifacts — the old trio was all P3 output,
    so every gate keyed on it post-dated the entry moment it policed. W21: the durable
    project-scoped app_build flag was retired as a gate trigger — one sprint's flag
    bled app gates (SPEC1/C2/H1/DL1/H2 + the R#34 sprint hold) into every later
    session in the project, including doc/meta sessions (Issue E). The repo the
    command actually touches is the only honest scope."""
    root = os.path.expanduser(rdir or "")
    if not root:
        return False
    # W44: the HOOK ESTATE is never an app build, whatever markers it carries. Measured:
    # a leftover `docs/PRD.md` (9,010 B, weeks old) made the estate repo permanent app
    # context, so every doc/meta session in it inherited SPEC1/C2/H1/DL1/H2 and the R#34
    # sprint hold — with ZERO app-source writes recorded. That is precisely the "Issue E"
    # bleed W21 retired the durable project flag to stop; the file-marker replacement
    # reproduced its permanence by another route.
    #
    # Fixed HERE and not at the 17 call sites (code twin: one helper, not seventeen
    # patches). Deliberately NOT fixed by additionally requiring recorded app-source
    # writes: `nexus-pretool.py:988` supports pre-`git init` app scaffolds, which
    # legitimately have a marker and no writes yet, so that test would fail them closed.
    # IDENTITY, not a heuristic. Two earlier attempts were both wrong and a verification lane
    # drove each of them:
    #   1. a test at `root` alone missed a call site passing `.claude/hooks/lib` as its cwd,
    #      which is a real working directory while the layer is being edited;
    #   2. the bounded walk UP that replaced it returned False for ANY repo with a
    #      `.claude/hooks` within 6 ancestors — and `~/.claude/hooks` is the STANDARD
    #      user-level config location. Driven: one `mkdir ~/.claude/hooks` silently disabled
    #      all 15 app gates for every repo within 5 levels of $HOME, i.e. every repo on the
    #      measured host, with no decision row. Strictly worse than the defect it fixed.
    # The estate's own root is computable exactly: lib/ -> hooks/ -> .claude/ -> project.
    # This excludes the estate and everything inside it, and nothing else, on any machine at
    # any nesting depth — where both heuristics had false positives that fail CLOSED.
    _abs = os.path.abspath(root.rstrip(os.sep))
    if _abs == _ESTATE_ROOT or _abs.startswith(_ESTATE_ROOT + os.sep):
        return False
    for cand in (".nexus-app", ".nexus-starter",
                 os.path.join("docs", "PRD.md"), os.path.join("docs", "DESIGN.md"),
                 os.path.join("docs", "BUILD-MODE.md"), os.path.join("docs", "SPEC.md"),
                 os.path.join("docs", "feature-manifest.md")):
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, cand)):
            return True
    return False


_CD_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[;&|\n])\s*cd\s+(?P<p>[^;&|\n]+)")


def repo_root_of(d):
    """[file-state] Walk UP from a directory to its repo root — `.git` (dir OR a
    worktree's `.git` file) or an app marker. Directory twin of the adapter's
    _repo_root, which takes a FILE path. Returns the root, or None.

    A filesystem walk, not `git rev-parse`: same answer for every shape this engine
    sees (including a pre-`git init` scaffold, where rev-parse returns nothing and an
    app scaffold is exactly the case the gates must still cover), with no subprocess
    on the PreToolUse path."""
    try:
        d = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(d or ""))
        for _ in range(12):
            g = os.path.join(d, ".git")
            if os.path.isdir(g) or os.path.isfile(g) or app_repo_ctx(d):
                return d
            nd = os.path.dirname(d)
            if nd == d:
                return None
            d = nd
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def resolve_repo(cmd, data, appid_map=None):
    """[file-state] Resolve the repo a deploy-path command ACTS ON.
    Returns (rdir, how) on success, or (None, reason) — always a REASONED outcome.

    Replaces the cd-prefix regex the deploy gates used to share, which was wrong three
    ways and measured FALSE-ALLOW 3/3 on real deploy commands: it read the RAW command
    (so a `cd` inside a heredoc or a quoted string won `), it took the FIRST cd rather
    than the effective one, and it required a trailing `;`/`&&`. When it missed it fell
    back to the session cwd — frequently the scratchpad — so the gates ran their file
    checks against a directory holding none of the artifacts and returned green.

    Resolution order:
      1. `nexus vibe deploy <appId>` carries no path at all → the appId→repo registry
         (`app-repos` session feed, written by posttool at `vibe app create`). A miss is
         `appid-unmapped:<id>`, never a silent fall-through to cwd.
      2. Otherwise the effective cwd = the LAST `cd <path>` in the STRIPPED command if
         any, else data['cwd'] — then walk up to the repo root.

    Callers MUST treat (None, reason) as "could not evaluate" and SAY SO, never as
    "not an app repo" — that conflation is what made the gates silent."""
    s = _strip(cmd or "")
    eff = None
    for cm in _CD_RE.finditer(s):
        cand = cm.group("p").strip().strip("'\"")
        if cand:
            eff = cand
    # An explicit `cd` OUTRANKS the appId registry: the command states the directory
    # outright, which is stronger evidence than a lookup, and `cd <repo> && nexus vibe
    # deploy <id>` is a normal shape. The registry exists for the shape that carries no
    # path at all — resolving THAT from cwd is the measured false-allow.
    if eff is None:
        m = re.search(r"nexus\s+vibe\s+deploy\s+(?P<id>[\w-]{6,})", s)
        if m:
            aid = m.group("id")
            hit = (appid_map or {}).get(aid)
            if hit and os.path.isdir(os.path.expanduser(hit)):
                return hit, "appid"
            return None, "appid-unmapped:%s" % aid
        eff = data.get("cwd") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    if not eff:
        return None, "no-cwd"
    if not os.path.isdir(os.path.expanduser(eff)):
        return None, "cwd-missing:%s" % eff
    root = repo_root_of(eff)
    if not root:
        return None, "no-repo-root:%s" % eff
    return root, "cwd" if eff == (data.get("cwd") if isinstance(data, dict) else None) else "cd"


# The row is written INSIDE a markdown table cell, inside backticks, after prose
# ("MACHINE-READABLE, one line: `lanes: architect=1 · …`"), so neither key is at line start.
# Anchoring on line start made this parser return {} against its OWN documented template — the
# reader and the writer disagreeing about format is the same class as a reader with no writer.
_LANE_ROW_RE = re.compile(r"lanes:\s*(?P<v>[^`|\n]+)", re.I)
_BAR_ROW_RE = re.compile(r"bar:\s*(?P<v>\d+(?:\.\d+)?)", re.I)
# Both spellings the template and the prose use: `reviewer=7` and `reviewer x7` / `reviewer ×7`.
_LANE_ITEM_RE = re.compile(r"(?P<name>[a-z][\w-]*)\s*(?:[=x×]\s*(?P<n>\d+))?", re.I)
# W28/model: the card's per-lane models, as a STRUCTURED row (models were prose before, so no
# parser could read them; a dispatch's model could not be checked against the card).
_MODELS_ROW_RE = re.compile(r"models:\s*(?P<v>[^`|\n]+)", re.I)
_MODEL_ITEM_RE = re.compile(r"(?P<name>[a-z][\w-]*)\s*=\s*(?P<m>[\w.\-]+)", re.I)
# W28/J: a Fates table row — `| lane | declared | fired | fate | drop-quote |`. A lane with
# Fired:0 and no quoted drop is an OPEN obligation (build-mode-card.md:59), which the roster
# parser never read, so ROSTER1's own advice ("record the drop in Fates") was never verified.
_FATES_ROW_RE = re.compile(
    r"^\|\s*(?P<lane>[a-z][\w-]*)\s*\|\s*(?P<decl>\d+)?\s*\|\s*(?P<fired>\d+)?\s*\|"
    r"[^|]*\|(?P<drop>[^|]*)\|", re.I | re.M)


def build_mode_roster(rdir):
    """[file-state] Parse docs/BUILD-MODE.md into {lanes: {lane: expected_count},
    bar: float|None, has_card: bool, has_lanes_row: bool}.

    The card IS the durable roster (CLAUDE.md Resume-mode: "from the durable roster,
    never recall"). Recall is exactly what failed — a wave shipped with reviewer 0/7,
    assessor 0/20 and taste 0/1 while the session believed the crew had run.

    A card with no machine-readable `lanes:` row reports has_lanes_row=False; callers
    must SAY that rather than substitute a default roster, or the check invents an
    expectation the owner never agreed to."""
    out = {"lanes": {}, "bar": None, "has_card": False, "has_lanes_row": False,
           "models": {}, "fates": {}}
    fp = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(rdir or ""), "docs", "BUILD-MODE.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(fp):
        return out
    out["has_card"] = True
    try:
        txt = open(fp, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return out
    m = _BAR_ROW_RE.search(txt)
    if m:
        try:
            out["bar"] = float(m.group("v"))
        except ValueError:
            pass
    lm = _LANE_ROW_RE.search(txt)
    if not lm:
        return out
    out["has_lanes_row"] = True
    for part in re.split(r"[·,|]", lm.group("v")):
        part = part.strip()
        if not part:
            continue
        im = _LANE_ITEM_RE.match(part)
        if im:
            name = im.group("name").lower()
            if not name.startswith("app-"):
                name = "app-" + name
            out["lanes"][name] = int(im.group("n") or 1)
    # W28/model: per-lane models (structured `models:` row).
    mm = _MODELS_ROW_RE.search(txt)
    if mm:
        for part in re.split(r"[·,|]", mm.group("v")):
            im2 = _MODEL_ITEM_RE.match(part.strip())
            if im2:
                nm = im2.group("name").lower()
                if not nm.startswith("app-"):
                    nm = "app-" + nm
                out["models"][nm] = im2.group("m").lower()
    # W28/J: Fates table — record open obligations (declared>0, fired 0, no drop quote).
    for fm in _FATES_ROW_RE.finditer(txt):
        lane = fm.group("lane").lower()
        if not lane.startswith("app-"):
            lane = "app-" + lane
        if lane not in out["lanes"] and fm.group("decl") is None:
            continue   # a header/rule row, not a lane row
        decl = int(fm.group("decl") or 0); fired = int(fm.group("fired") or 0)
        drop = (fm.group("drop") or "").strip()
        out["fates"][lane] = {"declared": decl, "fired": fired,
                              "open": decl > 0 and fired == 0 and not drop}
    return out


EXEC_LANES = ("app-executor", "app-contracts", "app-backend", "app-tests")
JUDGE_LANES = ("app-reviewer", "app-assessor", "app-taste", "app-design-director")


def review_round_due(rows, threshold=1):
    """[state] True when the build has run executing waves but no review round is keeping pace.

    W28/J: the CENTRAL fix. The skill tied review to self-judged convergence, so a 14h build
    deferred the whole council to the end. This makes review a WAVE-BOUNDARY obligation: after
    `threshold` executing-lane dispatches with NO judging-lane dispatch since (round 1 never
    opened, or the build moved on `threshold` waves since the last round), a review round is due.
    `rows` = [(lane, epoch)]. Convergence stays the EXIT; this is the ENTRY the doc never had."""
    last_judge = max([e for l, e in rows if l in JUDGE_LANES] or [0])
    exec_after = sum(1 for l, e in rows if l in EXEC_LANES and e > last_judge)
    return exec_after >= threshold


def council_collated(rdir):
    """[file-state] True when the council's verdicts have been collated (the round's ledger
    exists). W28/I: the design director CONSUMES the collated council as its diagnosis, so a
    director dispatch before collate (measured: it ran concurrently with still-running assessors)
    has nothing to read. Proxy for 'collate ran': docs/ISSUE-LEDGER.md exists."""
    root = os.path.expanduser(rdir or ".")
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, "docs", "ISSUE-LEDGER.md"))


def serve_overdue(rows, served, threshold=1):
    """[state] True when executing waves have run but no live surface was ever served.

    W28/serve: SKILL.md:84 wants a watchable URL by wave 1; the stock build served a 703-byte
    scaffold for 13h. `served` = the deploy-watch SERVED epochs. Overdue once `threshold`
    executing dispatches have happened with zero served events."""
    exec_count = sum(1 for l, e in rows if l in EXEC_LANES)
    return exec_count >= threshold and not served


def open_fates(rdir):
    """[lane] for every declared-but-unfired review seat with no quoted drop — an OPEN
    obligation (build-mode-card.md:59). W28/J+taste: this plugs into R#27's completion-block
    family so a 'done/shipped' claim with an unfired declared seat (measured: taste 0/1 at the
    stock build's session end) is a `❌` row, not a silent pass. Empty = no open seats."""
    return sorted(l for l, f in (build_mode_roster(rdir).get("fates") or {}).items()
                  if f.get("open"))


# The placeholder CONCEPT, not a casing (W42 verify OP-2: the first cut was lowercase-only
# `<[a-z]…>` with no re.I — <REVIEWS-DIR>, <OutDir>, $REVIEWS_DIR, %VAR%, [reviews-dir],
# `...` and TODO/ all bound; 9 measured bypasses through the live entrypoint).
_OUT_PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(
    r"<[^<>\n]{1,40}>|\{\{?[^}\n]{1,40}\}?\}|\[[^\]\n]{1,40}\]"
    r"|%[A-Za-z_]\w*%|\$\{?[A-Z_]{2,}\}?|\.\.\.|\bTODO\b|\b[A-Z_]{4,}_HERE\b", re.I)
# Read-context vocabulary inside a binding span = the path is being DESCRIBED, not written
# to (W42 verify OP-1: "return your typed JSON in the shape defined in `schema/verdict.json`"
# silenced the check on the real failing brief — the bare locative `in` reads formats,
# shapes and rubrics as destinations).
_OUT_READCTX = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:shape|format|style|described|defined|documented|specified|see|read|reading"
    r"|rubric|schema|example)\b", re.I)
_OUT_NEGATED = re.compile(r"\b(?:do\s+not|don'?t|never)\s*$", re.I)

_OUT_LABELS = re.compile(
    r"(?:output\s+(?:path|file)\s*:|reviews\s+dir\s*:|dossier\s+file\s*:|deliverable\s*:"
    r"|report\s+to|WRITE\s+TO)"
    r"[^\S\n]*\n?[^\n]{0,80}?[`\"']?((?:/|~/|[\w.-]+/)[\w./\-]+"
    r"|[\w-]+\.(?:json|jsonl|md|txt|csv|ndjson)\b)", re.I)
_OUT_VERBS = re.compile(
    r"(?:written\s+to|append\s+to"
    r"|(?:write|save|put|land|deliver|return)\s+(?:your\s+)?[\w ]{0,30}?(?:to|into|in)\b"
    r"|write\s+(?:your\s+)?(?:output|verdict|report|findings|results|handoff)\b)"
    r"[^\n]{0,80}?[`\"']?((?:/|~/|[\w.-]+/)[\w./\-]+"
    r"|[\w-]+\.(?:json|jsonl|md|txt|csv|ndjson)\b)", re.I)


def lane_output_bound(prompt):
    """[pure] True iff a judging-lane brief BINDS an output destination: a writing verb or
    output label introduces a concrete, placeholder-free path (absolute, relative-with-slash,
    or a bare data filename — the W30 FP census holds six real briefs of the form "Save your
    findings to reviews-visual.json" that MUST stay silent). W42: the unfilled `<reviews-dir>`
    template was the highest-scoring input to the old mentions-a-path regex (3 council waves
    shipped placeholder-only; prose prevention 0/3, measured). Hardened per the adversarial
    verify lane (OP-1/OP-2/OP-3/OP-7): placeholder veto is concept-wide + case-insensitive,
    the destination class admits no bracket characters, read-context spans ("in the shape
    defined in …") and negated writes ("do not write to …") do not bind, and a label may put
    its path on the next line (the common markdown layout). Destination chars exclude <>{}
    so a bracketed token can never BE the destination — belt to the veto's braces."""
    p = s(prompt)
    for pat in (_OUT_LABELS, _OUT_VERBS):
        for m in pat.finditer(p):
            if _OUT_PLACEHOLDER.search(m.group(0)):
                continue
            if _OUT_READCTX.search(m.group(0)):
                continue
            if _OUT_NEGATED.search(p[max(0, m.start() - 24):m.start()]):
                continue
            return True
    return False


def perf_budget_line(rdir):
    """[pure] The PRD's machine-readable perf budget row; "?" when docs/PRD.md exists but
    cannot be read (W42 verify PE-4: an unreadable PRD must not read as "no budget declared"
    — that is the silent-death class the lifecycle's own except-comment names); None when
    there is genuinely no digit-bearing row (PE-6: a budget row always carries numbers, so
    prose mentions and negations do not count). W42: a prose budget nothing reads went 5 user
    slow-complaints unenforced; the greppable `Perf-budget:` key (the Access: precedent) is
    what makes a deterministic reader possible."""
    p = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(rdir or "."), "docs", "PRD.md")
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        return None
    try:
        with open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
            for ln in fh:
                if "Perf-budget:" in ln and re.search(r"\d", ln):
                    return ln.strip()
    except OSError:
        return "?"
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None

def model_mismatches(rdir, dispatched):
    """[(lane, used, want)] where a dispatched lane's model disagrees with the card's models row.

    W28/model: the card records the arbitrated per-lane model; a dispatch that overrides it
    silently spent the wrong tier (measured: 22 judging lanes on Opus against a recorded Sonnet
    arbitration). `dispatched` is [(lane, model)] recorded per Agent dispatch. Checked at Stop,
    where the app repo (hence the card) is resolvable from app-src-writes — the dispatch-time
    cwd is the project root, not the app repo, so a dispatch-time check has nothing to read.
    A lane with no card model, or a dispatch with no recorded model, is skipped (not a mismatch —
    the absent-model case is MODEL1's separate nudge)."""
    card = build_mode_roster(rdir)
    want = card.get("models") or {}
    out = []
    for lane, used in dispatched:
        lane = lane if lane.startswith("app-") else "app-" + lane
        w = want.get(lane)
        if w and used and used.lower() != w.lower():
            out.append((lane, used.lower(), w))
    return out

def read_lane_dag(rdir):
    """[file-state] Parse <rdir>/docs/lane-dag.json into the DAG dict, or None if absent/unreadable.
    The COMMITTED DAG is W29's single source of truth for the roots-frozen + fan-out facts — no
    filename guessing. A malformed file reads as None (the adapter treats that as no committed DAG)."""
    root = os.path.expanduser(rdir or "")
    p = os.path.join(root, "docs", "lane-dag.json")
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        return None
    try:
        with open(p, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            d = json.load(fh)
    except Exception:
        return None
    return d if isinstance(d, dict) else None


def _norm_glob(g):
    """Normalise an owns glob for comparison: strip a leading ./, drop a trailing /."""
    g = str(g).strip()
    if g.startswith("./"):
        g = g[2:]
    if g.endswith("/") and len(g) > 1:
        g = g[:-1]
    return g


def _globs_overlap(a, b):
    """[pure] TOTAL (W29/G1): never raises → False. True when two repo-relative owns globs can match
    a common path, matched SEGMENT BY SEGMENT so a single `*` does NOT cross `/` (only `**` does)
    and a `[...]` is LITERAL not a character class (G10/G11). Covers a normalised exact match and
    directory-prefix subsumption (a bare dir or a `/**` suffix prefixing the other) — so `src/**`
    overlaps `src/pages/Foo.tsx`, `src/pages` overlaps `src/pages/`, `./x` overlaps `x`; while
    `src/a` vs `legacy/a`, `src/*` vs `src/pages/x`, and `src/pages/[id].tsx` vs `src/pages/i.tsx`
    do NOT."""
    import fnmatch
    try:
        a, b = _norm_glob(a), _norm_glob(b)
        if not a or not b:
            return False
        if a == b:
            return True

        # directory-prefix subsumption: a bare directory (no glob char, no dotted filename) or a
        # `/**` suffix subsumes everything beneath it.
        def _dir_prefix(x):
            if x.endswith("/**"):
                return x[:-3]
            seg = x.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
            if not any(c in x for c in "*?[") and "." not in seg:
                return x                       # x is itself a bare directory path
            return None
        for x, y in ((a, b), (b, a)):
            px = _dir_prefix(x)
            if px is not None and (y == px or y.startswith(px + "/")):
                return True

        # segment-by-segment: * matches within one segment, ** spans >=0 segments, [ is literal.
        def seg_ok(sx, sy):
            ex, ey = sx.replace("[", "[[]"), sy.replace("[", "[[]")
            return fnmatch.fnmatch(sy, ex) or fnmatch.fnmatch(sx, ey)

        def match(xs, ys):
            if not xs and not ys:
                return True
            if not xs or not ys:
                return all(s == "**" for s in (xs or ys))
            if xs[0] == "**" or ys[0] == "**":
                which, other = (xs, ys) if xs[0] == "**" else (ys, xs)
                return (match(which[1:], other) or match(which, other[1:])
                        or match(which[1:], other[1:]))
            if seg_ok(xs[0], ys[0]):
                return match(xs[1:], ys[1:])
            return False
        return match(a.split("/"), b.split("/"))
    except Exception:
        return False


def _dag_owns(lane):
    """The owns list of a lane row, coerced: a bare string is NOT a list (flagged elsewhere) but is
    read as a single glob here so file-existence checks still work."""
    o = lane.get("owns") or []
    if isinstance(o, str):
        return [o]
    return [x for x in o if isinstance(x, str)]


def roots_frozen(rdir):
    """[file-state] TOTAL wrapper (W29/G1): any unexpected DAG shape or recursion → NOT frozen. A
    hook predicate must never raise — a malformed committed lane-dag.json that crashed here took
    the whole PreToolUse adapter down (rc=1, no stdout = fail-open of every other check)."""
    try:
        return _roots_frozen_impl(rdir)
    except Exception:
        return False


def _roots_frozen_impl(rdir):
    """[file-state] True when the COMMITTED lane DAG proves the fan-out roots are frozen:
    docs/lane-dag.json exists, declares a non-empty `roots`, EVERY root id resolves to a real lane
    row (a root is a committed lane, not a bare reference), and every path in those root-lanes'
    `owns` EXISTS on disk (a concrete path must be present; a glob must match at least one file).
    No filename guessing — the architect commits the DAG plus the root artifacts and the gate checks
    they are actually there. Missing repo / no DAG / any root artifact absent → NOT frozen.
    W29/FANOUT-ROOTS reads this."""
    root = os.path.expanduser(rdir or "")
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        return False
    dag = read_lane_dag(root)
    if not dag:
        return False
    roots = dag.get("roots") or []
    if not roots:
        return False
    lanes = {l.get("id"): l for l in (dag.get("lanes") or []) if isinstance(l, dict)}
    for rid in roots:
        lane = lanes.get(rid)
        if not lane:
            return False                      # a root that is not a committed lane row is not frozen
        owns = _dag_owns(lane)
        if not owns:
            return False
        for g in owns:
            if not _owns_present(root, _norm_glob(g)):
                return False
    return True


def _owns_present(root, g):
    """[file-state] True when a root-lane owns glob resolves to a real file committed under `root`.
    Concrete paths are tested by EXISTENCE FIRST, so a literal `[seg]` App-Router segment is seen
    (G3). A degenerate/too-broad owns (`.`, `*`, `**`, a bare directory, a `..` escape, an absolute
    path) is NOT a frozen root (G6). A genuine glob (only `*`/`?`, never a literal `[`) is matched
    with node_modules/.git/dist pruned and every match required to stay under `root` (G6)."""
    import glob as _glob
    if not g or g in (".", "*", "**") or g.startswith("..") or os.path.isabs(g):
        return False
    full = os.path.join(root, g)
    rp_root = os.path.realpath(root) + os.sep
    if os.path.isfile(full):                          # exists-first (handles [id]/types.ts, G3)
        return os.path.realpath(full).startswith(rp_root)
    if os.path.isdir(full):
        return False                                  # a bare directory is not a committed file
    if any(ch in g for ch in "*?"):                   # a real glob; `[` stays literal (handled above)
        for m in _glob.glob(full, recursive=True):
            if not os.path.isfile(m):
                continue
            if any(p in ("node_modules", ".git", "dist", "_captures")
                   for p in os.path.relpath(m, root).split(os.sep)):
                continue
            if os.path.realpath(m).startswith(rp_root):
                return True
    return False


def fanout_blocked(rdir):
    """[state] TOTAL wrapper (W29/G1): any unexpected DAG shape → NOT blocked (never raises)."""
    try:
        return _fanout_blocked_impl(rdir)
    except Exception:
        return False


def _fanout_blocked_impl(rdir):
    """[state] True when the committed lane DAG DECLARES a fan-out — >=2 non-root lanes to build in
    parallel — while the roots are NOT yet frozen. Keyed entirely off docs/lane-dag.json: per-repo,
    no session-global count, no prose dependency. No DAG → False here (the adapter's no-DAG backstop
    covers a fan-out dispatched without a committed DAG). W29/FANOUT-ROOTS."""
    dag = read_lane_dag(rdir)
    if not dag:
        return False
    roots = set(str(r) for r in (dag.get("roots") or []) if isinstance(r, (str, int)))
    nonroot = set()                           # DISTINCT non-root ids (G12: dup rows must not inflate)
    for l in (dag.get("lanes") or []):
        if isinstance(l, dict):
            lid = l.get("id")
            if isinstance(lid, str) and lid not in roots:
                nonroot.add(lid)
    if len(nonroot) < 2:
        return False                          # not a fan-out
    return not roots_frozen(rdir)


def _unit_stems(owns, lane_id=""):
    """[pure] Collapse owned PATHS into owned UNITS. Never raises.

    A path count is not a unit count, and treating it as one made this check fire on the shape the
    decomposition doctrine PRESCRIBES. Descending the frontend seam ladder gives every correct lane
    three files — the component, its own stylesheet (rung 4) and its own journey file (rung 6) —
    so `js/views/index/search.js` + `styles/search.css` + `journeys/L1-search.py` is ONE unit
    wearing three extensions. Measured on a blind architect run whose partition was otherwise
    clean: TEN of its lanes flagged, every one of them correctly built. A check that fires on its
    own prescribed behaviour is one people learn to switch off — the same lesson `partition_shape`
    already paid for twice (the digest arm, the worktree arm).

    The collapse is pure string arithmetic on the basenames, no semantics: two stems are the same
    unit when one CONTAINS the other, which is exactly the naming law (`plan-format.md` Step 5b.3 —
    a lane's paths share their distinguishing token). `search`/`search`/`L1-search` collapse to one;
    `CONTRACT`/`DIGEST`/`lane-dag` stay three, because they genuinely are three artifacts."""
    try:
        # AN ENTRY-POINT BASENAME IS ITS DIRECTORY'S UNIT, NEVER ITS OWN. `index`, `main`, `app`
        # and `mod` are positional names — every ecosystem uses them for "the thing this folder
        # IS" — so they can never share a token with their lane id, and the naming law would
        # report every one of them as a separate unit. Measured on a 27-lane plan: a `server-boot`
        # lane owning `src/server/index.ts` plus its own journey read as two units when it is one.
        # Substituting the PARENT DIRECTORY is what a reader does anyway when they see `index.ts`.
        _ENTRY = {"index", "main", "app", "mod", "__init__"}
        stems = []
        for o in owns:
            _raw = str(o or "").strip().rstrip("/")
            b = os.path.basename(_raw)
            b = re.split(r"\.", b)[0].strip().lower()
            if b in _ENTRY:
                _parent = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(_raw))
                b = re.split(r"\.", _parent)[0].strip().lower() or b
            b = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", b).strip("-")
            if b:
                stems.append(b)
        # SEPARATORS ARE NOT MEANING. `WeekGrid.tsx` and `week-grid.css` are one unit spelled two
        # ways, and comparing them with their hyphens intact makes "weekgrid" and "week-grid" two
        # different things — a casing convention split a lane in half. Compare on the letters.
        def _flat(x):
            return x.replace("-", "")

        keep = []
        for s in stems:
            # STRICTLY shorter, or two spellings of one name annihilate each other: `weekgrid` and
            # `week-grid` are each "inside" the other once separators are ignored, so a non-strict
            # test skipped BOTH, emptied `keep`, and the fallback restored the pair it had just
            # collapsed. The equal case is a duplicate, handled by the dedup below.
            if any(_flat(s) != _flat(t) and _flat(s) in _flat(t) for t in stems):
                continue                     # a shorter stem inside a longer one is the same unit
            if _flat(s) in {_flat(k) for k in keep}:
                continue                     # same letters, different separators
            keep.append(s)
        if not keep:
            keep = list(dict.fromkeys(stems))
        # SECOND PASS — the naming law, applied. Containment alone still splits a lane whose files
        # are named for the same thing without one name nesting in the other: `responsive-index.css`
        # and `L9-index-mobile.py` are the mobile layer and its own journey, one unit, and neither
        # string contains the other. Step 5b.3 says a lane's paths share their DISTINGUISHING TOKEN
        # with the lane id, so every survivor sharing a token with the id folds into ONE bucket —
        # the lane's own unit — while survivors sharing nothing with it stay separate and countable.
        # Tokens under 3 chars are dropped: `L9`, `js`, `v2` are position markers, not subjects.
        idt = {t for t in re.split(r"[^a-z0-9]+", str(lane_id or "").lower()) if len(t) >= 3}
        if idt:
            mine, theirs = [], []
            for s in keep:
                st = {t for t in re.split(r"[^a-z0-9]+", s) if len(t) >= 3}
                (mine if (st & idt) else theirs).append(s)
            if mine:
                keep = [mine[0]] + theirs
        return keep
    except Exception:                                        # pragma: no cover
        return list(owns or [])


def lane_granularity(dag):
    """[pure] TOTAL. Is the partition DECOMPOSED, or is it one fat lane wearing a schema?

    Returns (ok, [problems]). SCHEDULE RISK, not correctness — deliberately separate from
    `partition_valid`, which answers "will these lanes merge cleanly". A fat lane is a slow
    plan, not an invalid one, and conflating them would block a dispatch on a judgement call.

    WHY IT EXISTS. `partition_valid` passes a ONE-ROW partition: acyclic, disjoint, closed and
    rooted are all trivially true when there is nothing to conflict with. So a partition can
    be written, validated, and still describe exactly the serial build the whole mechanism was
    built to prevent. Measured on the first two real partitions the estate ever produced: one
    declared 5 lanes but gave a single row THREE owned files, and the other declared 3 lanes
    for work that had at least twice that many separable units.

    THREE ARITHMETIC RULES. No wording is inspected, nothing is inferred from a name:
      1. a lane with NO `surfaces` key, or an empty one, is UNDECLARED — the field exists so
         decomposition is countable, and an absent count is not a small count;
      2. `len(surfaces) > 1` with no `unsplittable_reason` — more than one user-facing surface
         in one lane is the exact defect the field was added to make visible;
      3. `len(owns) > 1` with no `unsplittable_reason` — several owned paths are several units;
         a shared-foundation row owning three files is three lanes' worth of work with one
         lane's schedule, and it is where a partition quietly re-serialises.
    Every rule has the SAME escape: say why in `unsplittable_reason`. The check never argues
    for a particular width — it argues that a decision to keep units together is WRITTEN.
    """
    try:
        lanes = (dag or {}).get("lanes")
        if not isinstance(lanes, list):
            return (False, ["lane_dag has no readable `lanes` list"])
        probs = []
        for l in lanes:
            if not isinstance(l, dict):
                probs.append("a lane row is not an object")
                continue
            lid = str(l.get("id") or "<unnamed>")
            why = str(l.get("unsplittable_reason") or "").strip()
            surf = l.get("surfaces")
            # W48: AN EMPTY LIST IS A DECLARATION; A MISSING KEY IS SILENCE. This arm was written
            # when every lane was a UI surface, and it treated `[]` and absent alike. The backend
            # seam ladder then made no-surface lanes the NORMAL case — a store, a route, a boot
            # entry, a seed and a contract have no user-facing surface and saying so is honest.
            # Measured on the first plan to use both ladders: 29 rows fired, and 26 of them were
            # lanes that had correctly declared `"surfaces": []`. Same shape as the digest and the
            # units count — the author declares, the check reads, and it never guesses.
            if not isinstance(surf, list):
                probs.append("lane `%s` declares no `surfaces` key — decomposition is not "
                             "countable, so nothing can tell one screen from six. A lane with no "
                             "user-facing surface declares `[]`; absent is silence, not zero" % lid)
            elif len(surf) > 1 and not why:
                probs.append("lane `%s` carries %d surfaces with no `unsplittable_reason` "
                             "— one user-facing surface per lane (desktop and mobile of one "
                             "screen are TWO)" % (lid, len(surf)))
            owns = l.get("owns")
            if isinstance(owns, list) and len(owns) > 1 and not why:
                stems = _unit_stems(owns, lid)
                if len(stems) > 1:
                    probs.append("lane `%s` owns %d units with no `unsplittable_reason` — several "
                                 "owned units are several pieces of work sharing one lane's "
                                 "schedule (%s)" % (lid, len(stems),
                                                    ", ".join(sorted(stems))[:70]))
        return (not probs, probs)
    except Exception as e:                                   # pragma: no cover
        return (False, ["lane_granularity could not read the DAG: %s" % e])


def _lane_list(dag):
    """[pure] The lane rows, whichever spelling the DAG uses. Never raises."""
    if not isinstance(dag, dict):
        return []
    ls = dag.get("lanes")
    if not isinstance(ls, list):
        ls = ((dag.get("lane_dag") or {}) if isinstance(dag.get("lane_dag"), dict) else {}).get("lanes")
    return [l for l in (ls or []) if isinstance(l, dict)]


def _looks_like_path(tok):
    """[pure] A builds_against entry naming a FILE rather than a sibling LANE.

    The distinction is the whole point of the shared-consumption check below: `builds_against:
    ["spine"]` is a DEPENDENCY on another lane and costs nothing, while `builds_against:
    ["shell.js contract block", "docs/PRD.md S1"]` is a declaration that this lane will go READ
    those files itself. Three lanes declaring the same file is three lanes reading it."""
    t = str(tok or "").strip()
    return ("/" in t) or bool(re.search(r"\.\w{1,5}\b", t))


def partition_shape(dag, dispatched=None, repo=None):
    """[pure + file-state] DECOMPOSITION-QUALITY checks. Returns (ok, [problem strings]).

    WHY THIS EXISTS, and why it is not `lane_granularity` or `partition_valid`.

    Those two ask whether the partition is WELL-FORMED — acyclic, disjoint, closed, not too
    coarse. A partition can pass all of that and still be a bad CUT. Measured, on two rollouts
    of one build, neither seeing the other:

      · One declared four lanes, validated them, then DISPATCHED NONE and built solo. Every
        existing partition gate fires AT dispatch, so a partition that is declared and then
        bypassed passes all of them by never reaching them.
      · The other dispatched its lanes correctly and still lost: all three re-read the same
        ten root files, all three independently rediscovered the SAME six harness traps, and
        two of three had to create their own worktree because none existed at dispatch. The
        fan-out measured SLOWER than the solo build (49min vs 32min) — not because parallelism
        is slow, but because one shared prologue ran three times, serially, inside the lanes.
      · Its lanes then diverged exactly where the contract was SILENT: three escaping policies
        (one of them none, shipping live XSS), two different numbers for the same audience
        count one click apart, and a re-invented copy of a shared component. A reviewer put the
        cause precisely: not one journey compared a value on surface A with the same value on
        surface B, because verification was partitioned along the same cut as the work.

    So the arithmetic here is about the SHAPE of the cut, never its formal validity. All six arms
    are counts over JSON and the filesystem — no wording is read, nothing is judged. Arms 5 and 6
    enforce two procedure steps that were written and never checked: a merge with no reason, and an
    additive store with no runner to glob it.

    `dispatched` = agent dispatches observed since the DAG was written (caller supplies it;
    None skips that arm). `repo` = repo root for the worktree arm (None skips it)."""
    if not isinstance(dag, dict):
        return True, []
    lanes = _lane_list(dag)
    roots = {str(r) for r in (dag.get("roots") or []) if r}
    work = [l for l in lanes if str(l.get("id")) not in roots]
    probs = []

    # ARM 5 RUNS FIRST, AND IT RUNS ON A ONE-ROW DAG. The early return below skips arms 1-4 when
    # nothing was partitioned, which is right for them — they all ask about the shape of a cut, and
    # there is no cut. Arm 5 asks the opposite question: was there SUPPOSED to be one? Measured, by
    # driving a real build: a lane wrote `units: 8` and ONE root row owning all six files, and
    # `partition_shape` returned CLEAN — the loudest possible under-decomposition signal, silenced
    # by a guard written before this arm existed. The escape is unchanged and still applies: a
    # written reason silences it, and in that measured case the reason was a good one. The point is
    # that a good reason and a fig leaf must not be indistinguishable to the check.
    try:
        _u = int(dag.get("units"))
    except Exception:
        _u = None
    _denom = len(work) or len(lanes)
    if _u and _u > 0 and _denom and _u > _denom:
        if not [l for l in lanes if str(l.get("unsplittable_reason") or "").strip()]:
            probs.append(
                "%d units declared against %d lane(s), and NOT ONE row carries an "
                "`unsplittable_reason` — %d unit(s) were merged and that decision exists nowhere a "
                "reader can find it. The width is not the complaint; the silence is "
                "(`REF/plan-format.md`, Step 5)" % (_u, _denom, _u - _denom))

    if len(lanes) < 2:
        return (not probs), probs   # no cut to judge — but arm 5 above has already spoken

    # 1 — DECLARED vs DISPATCHED. The partition that was written and then bypassed.
    if dispatched is not None and work:
        try:
            d = int(dispatched)
        except Exception:
            d = None
        if d is not None and d < len(work):
            probs.append(
                "%d work lanes declared, %d agent dispatch(es) since the DAG was written — "
                "a partition that is declared and then built solo passes every dispatch-time "
                "check by never reaching one; either dispatch the lanes or delete the rows"
                % (len(work), d))

    # 2 — SHARED CONSUMPTION. A file every lane declares it will read is a prologue that was
    # never hoisted into the root, and it is paid once PER LANE, serially, inside each lane.
    # THE DIGEST IS DECLARED, AND DECLARED ENTRIES ARE EXEMPT. This arm exists to catch lanes
    # each re-reading the same RAW SOURCES; a purpose-built digest being read by every lane is
    # the doctrine working, not failing. The two cases are indistinguishable by path alone —
    # `docs/DESIGN.md` can be either — and a hook must not guess semantics. So the partition
    # DECLARES `digest`: the artifacts the root wrote specifically to be consumed. Caught by
    # driving this check against the first partition built under the new doctrine, where it
    # flagged `docs/CONTRACT.md` and `docs/DIGEST.md` — the exact artifacts the doctrine
    # requires every lane to read. A check that fires on its own prescribed behaviour trains
    # people to ignore it. Declaring 10 raw sources as `digest` is still visible and reviewable
    # in the artifact; guessing would not have been.
    _digest = {_norm_glob(x) for x in (dag.get("digest") or []) if x}
    seen = {}
    for l in work:
        for b in (l.get("builds_against") or []):
            if _looks_like_path(b) and _norm_glob(b) not in _digest:
                seen.setdefault(str(b).strip(), set()).add(str(l.get("id")))
    shared = sorted((k, v) for k, v in seen.items() if len(v) > 1)
    if shared:
        probs.append(
            "%d input(s) declared by more than one lane (%s) — each lane pays that reading "
            "again; hoist the shared prologue into the root and hand lanes the RESULT, not "
            "the source" % (len(shared), ", ".join(k for k, _ in shared[:3])))

    # 3 — FROZEN BUT UNOWNED. A file asserted untouched that no lane owns is the
    # 'asserted-frozen while being edited' pattern; it also means nobody is accountable for it.
    frozen = [str(f) for f in (dag.get("root_files") or dag.get("roots_frozen") or []) if f]
    if frozen:
        owned = set()
        for l in lanes:
            for o in (l.get("owns") or []):
                owned.add(_norm_glob(o))
        orphan = [f for f in frozen if _norm_glob(f) not in owned]
        if orphan:
            probs.append(
                "%d frozen root file(s) owned by NO lane (%s) — frozen is a claim about who "
                "may write; with no owner the claim has nobody to hold. TREAT AS BLOCKING for "
                "anything a lane must WRITE to pass its own gate: measured, five of nine lanes "
                "independently appended to one unowned acceptance harness (+192/+185/+106/+87/"
                "+74 lines) off a formally valid disjoint partition, and the merge conflict was "
                "guaranteed before any of them started. Make the shared store ADDITIVE — a "
                "directory the runner globs, one file per lane — or have the root write it "
                "complete up front (`REF/plan-format.md`, Step 5b)"
                % (len(orphan), ", ".join(orphan[:3])))

    # 3b — THE SAME QUESTION, ASKED OF THE REPO INSTEAD OF THE DECLARATION. Arm 3 above reads
    # `root_files`, which means a partition can silence it by not declaring one — the declaration
    # is the check's own off switch. Found by a build that fixed arm 3's complaint by REMOVING the
    # key, then asked the better question itself: not "are the files I declared frozen owned" but
    # "which tracked files have no owning lane at all". Its answer was 25 unowned where arm 3 had
    # named 3, and the dangerous one was never in the declared list — a shared component FOUR lanes
    # build against, which is guaranteed conflict rather than possible conflict.
    # Scoped to files a lane plausibly WRITES, by extension, because a README or a lockfile is
    # legitimately unowned and a check that demands an owner for every tracked byte is noise.
    if repo and len(work) >= 2:
        try:
            import subprocess as _sp
            _o = _sp.run(["git", "-C", os.path.expanduser(repo), "ls-files"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
            if _o.returncode == 0:
                _globs = [str(o) for l in lanes for o in (l.get("owns") or []) if o]
                _src = tuple(".js .mjs .cjs .ts .tsx .jsx .py .css .scss .sql .vue .svelte".split())
                _orph = []
                for f in _o.stdout.splitlines():
                    f = f.strip()
                    if not f or not f.endswith(_src):
                        continue
                    if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(f, g) or f == g or f.startswith(g.rstrip("/") + "/")
                           for g in _globs):
                        continue
                    _orph.append(f)
                if _orph:
                    probs.append(
                        "%d tracked SOURCE file(s) owned by no lane (%s) — asked of the repo, not "
                        "of the declaration, because a partition can silence the frozen-files arm "
                        "by declaring nothing. An unowned file two lanes both need is guaranteed "
                        "conflict, not possible conflict (`REF/plan-format.md`, Step 5b)"
                        % (len(_orph), ", ".join(_orph[:3])))
        except Exception:
            pass                          # no git / no repo -> decline, never guess

    # 4 — WORKTREES NOT PRE-PROVISIONED. Provisioning is the SPAWNER's job; a lane that has to
    # create its own worktree pays setup the fan-out was supposed to have already paid.
    if repo and work:
        # ASK GIT, never a path. The first build of this arm counted directories under
        # `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/` and fired on 3 of 3 real fixtures — including one that
        # HAD a worktree per lane, sited as repo siblings instead. A check that flags correct
        # work is one people learn to ignore, so the question is put to the only component
        # that actually knows: `git worktree list` reports every registered worktree wherever
        # it lives. Absent git, or a non-repo, the arm declines to judge rather than guess.
        have = None
        try:
            import subprocess as _sp
            _o = _sp.run(["git", "-C", os.path.expanduser(repo), "worktree", "list"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
            if _o.returncode == 0:
                have = max(0, len([x for x in _o.stdout.splitlines() if x.strip()]) - 1)
        except Exception:
            have = None
        if have is not None and have < len(work):
            probs.append(
                "%d work lanes declared, %d worktree(s) provisioned — a lane that creates its "
                "own worktree pays setup the spawner should have paid before dispatch"
                % (len(work), have))

    # 5 — UNITS MERGED WITH NO WRITTEN REASON. The decomposition procedure's Step 5 says: count the
    # units, and where the DAG carries fewer rows than that count, every merge names its
    # `unsplittable_reason`. Nothing has ever checked it, and nothing COULD: every other field
    # describes the lanes that exist, so a partition that quietly folded eight units into four rows
    # is indistinguishable from one that only ever had four units. Hence the DECLARED `units` count
    # (`plan-format.md` "HOW TO DECOMPOSE") — this arm reads it and DECLINES when it is absent
    # rather than inferring a unit count from row shapes, which would be guessing at the one number
    # the plan exists to record. The escape is the doctrine's own: one reason silences the arm,
    # because the rule asks for the decision to be written, never for a particular width.
    # 6 — AN ADDITIVE STORE WITH NO AGGREGATOR. Step 5b removes the shared-file collision by making
    # the store a DIRECTORY the root's runner globs, one file per lane. Measured, and reported by a
    # lane that hit it: a wave was told to write `journeys/<lane>.py` while the runner still knew
    # only the single pre-existing suite file, so "the suite is green" became two separate commands
    # and stopped being ONE checkable predicate — which is the exact property the additive rule
    # exists to protect. An additive store with no aggregator is not additive, it is scattered.
    #
    # ASK GIT, never walk the tree (arm 4's lesson). A directory IS an additive store when two or
    # more work lanes own paths under it — that is arithmetic over `owns`, not a guess about intent.
    # It HAS an aggregator when some tracked file outside it names it. Tracked is the right test,
    # not merely present: Step 5b requires the runner in the same COMMIT that creates the directory,
    # so an untracked runner is the defect rather than a false positive. No repo, no git, or a git
    # error → the arm declines and says nothing.
    if repo and len(work) > 1:
        _dirs = {}
        for l in work:
            for o in (l.get("owns") or []):
                s = str(o or "").strip().lstrip("./")
                if "/" in s:
                    _dirs.setdefault(s.rsplit("/", 1)[0] + "/", set()).add(str(l.get("id")))
        _orphan = []
        for d in sorted(k for k, v in _dirs.items() if len(v) > 1):
            try:
                import subprocess as _sp
                _o = _sp.run(["git", "-C", os.path.expanduser(repo), "grep", "-l",
                              "--fixed-strings", d],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
                if _o.returncode not in (0, 1):
                    continue                      # git error -> decline on THIS dir, never guess
                # THE PARTITION FILE IS NEVER ITS OWN AGGREGATOR. `docs/lane-dag.json` lists every
                # owned path by construction, so once it is committed it names every additive store
                # and the arm can never fire again. Found by DRIVING the check against a real repo
                # with a real committed DAG — the unit fixture passed because it held the partition
                # in memory and never wrote it to the tree, which is precisely the difference
                # between testing a predicate and testing the system.
                # LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: any other tracked file that merely MENTIONS the
                # directory still satisfies this arm — a plan doc listing the paths would. That errs
                # toward silence, which is the safe direction for an advisory.
                if not [x for x in _o.stdout.splitlines()
                        if x.strip() and not x.strip().startswith(d)
                        and os.path.basename(x.strip()) != "lane-dag.json"]:
                    _orphan.append(d)
            except Exception:
                continue                          # no git -> decline, never guess
        if _orphan:
            probs.append(
                "%d shared store(s) (%s) are written one-file-per-lane, and NO tracked file "
                "outside them names the directory — so nothing globs it and the suite stops being "
                "one command. The root builds the globbing runner in the SAME commit that creates "
                "the directory (`REF/plan-format.md`, Step 5b)"
                % (len(_orphan), ", ".join(_orphan[:3])))

    return (not probs), probs


def partition_valid(dag):
    """[pure] TOTAL wrapper (W29/G1+G15): any unexpected shape or a RecursionError on a pathological
    depth → (False, [...]), never a raise."""
    try:
        return _partition_valid_impl(dag)
    except RecursionError:
        return (False, ["lane DAG dependency graph is too deep to validate"])
    except Exception:
        return (False, ["lane DAG could not be validated (malformed shape)"])


def _partition_valid_impl(dag):
    """[pure] dag = {"roots":[ids], "lanes":[{id, owns:[globs], depends_on:[ids]}]}. Returns
    (ok, problems). ok iff acyclic (incl. cycles through a root-lane) + pairwise glob-disjoint owns
    + closure + roots carry no depends_on + no duplicate ids + well-formed shape. NEVER raises — a
    malformed shape returns (False, [...]), because the adapter reads this straight off disk and a
    raise there silently passes an unvalidated partition. W29/PARTITION-VALID."""
    if not isinstance(dag, dict):
        return (False, ["lane DAG is not an object"])
    raw = dag.get("lanes")
    if raw is None:
        raw = []
    # W29/G15 + cost bound (law 5): a real fan-out is dozens of lanes; the pairwise owns-overlap is
    # O(n²) and the dependency walk recurses per lane. Refuse to grind on a pathological DAG.
    if isinstance(raw, list) and len(raw) > 200:
        return (False, ["lane DAG has too many lanes (%d) to validate — partition into sub-DAGs"
                        % len(raw)])
    roots = set(dag.get("roots") or [])
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        return (False, ["`lanes` is not a list"])
    problems = []
    lanes = {}
    for l in raw:
        if not isinstance(l, dict) or "id" not in l:
            problems.append("a lane row has no `id`")
            continue
        lid = l["id"]
        if lid in lanes:
            problems.append("duplicate lane id '%s'" % lid)
            continue
        lanes[lid] = l

    def owns_of(l):
        o = l.get("owns") or []
        if isinstance(o, str):
            problems.append("lane %s `owns` is a string, must be a list of globs" % l.get("id"))
            return []
        return [x for x in o if isinstance(x, str)]

    for lid, l in lanes.items():
        for dep in (l.get("depends_on") or []):
            if dep not in roots and dep not in lanes:
                problems.append("lane %s depends on unknown '%s'" % (lid, dep))
    for lid, l in lanes.items():
        deps = l.get("depends_on") or []
        if lid in roots and deps:
            problems.append("root lane %s must have no depends_on (a root is the floor)" % lid)
        elif not deps and lid not in roots:
            problems.append("non-root lane %s has no depends_on (roots must be its floor)" % lid)
    ids = list(lanes)
    owns_cache = {lid: owns_of(lanes[lid]) for lid in ids}
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(ids)):
            ov = sorted({x for x in owns_cache[ids[i]] for y in owns_cache[ids[j]]
                         if _globs_overlap(x, y)}
                        | {y for x in owns_cache[ids[i]] for y in owns_cache[ids[j]]
                           if _globs_overlap(x, y)})
            if ov:
                problems.append("lanes %s and %s own overlapping paths %s" % (ids[i], ids[j], ov))
    WHITE, GREY, BLACK = 0, 1, 2
    color = {lid: WHITE for lid in lanes}

    def visit(n, stack):
        if n not in lanes:
            return
        color[n] = GREY
        for dep in (lanes[n].get("depends_on") or []):
            if dep in roots and dep not in lanes:
                continue                      # a bare-reference root has nothing to traverse
            if color.get(dep) == GREY:
                problems.append("cycle: %s" % " → ".join(stack + [dep]))
                return
            if color.get(dep) == WHITE:
                visit(dep, stack + [dep])
        color[n] = BLACK
    for lid in lanes:
        if color[lid] == WHITE:
            visit(lid, [lid])
    seen, uniq = set(), []
    for p in problems:
        if p not in seen:
            seen.add(p)
            uniq.append(p)
    return (not uniq, uniq)


def exec_slice_collision(new_owns, live_owns_sets):
    """[state] True when new_owns GLOB-overlaps any live lane's owns (a SAME-slice re-spawn). Empty
    new_owns → no opinion (False). Glob/path-form aware, so `src/pages/X` and `legacy/pages/X` do
    NOT collide while `src/**` and `src/pages/X` do. W29/EXEC1 reads this — disjoint siblings are
    expected."""
    if not new_owns:
        return False
    for s in live_owns_sets:
        for a in new_owns:
            for b in s:
                if _globs_overlap(a, b):
                    return True
    return False


def is_execution_lane(rdir):
    """[file-state] True when the repo is an execution-lane worktree (carries `.lane-execution`),
    which the delivery-governance gates (ROSTER1/SPEC1/CLOSE1) must SKIP. W29/exec-lane marker."""
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(rdir or ""), ".lane-execution"))


def unmerged_done_worktrees(rdir, min_age_min=20):
    """[git-state] TOTAL (never raises → []). Returns [(branch, ahead, age_min)] for each git
    worktree of `rdir` that is DONE but UNMERGED: journeys/.last-pass present (gate-green) · a clean
    status (quiesced) · commits on its branch not on `main` · the branch HEAD older than
    min_age_min. This is the W30/MERGEWATCH signal — the merge-ABSENCE detector: a done lane waits
    invisibly and a dead lane's branch is GC-eligible, and NO existing gate fires on 'green +
    committed + quiesced + unmerged for N' (every merge gate fires at merge-time or Stop, none on
    the absence). Git is inherently live state; no feed needed. Bounded (5s per git call, ≤~40
    worktrees scanned)."""
    import time as _t
    out = []
    root = os.path.expanduser(rdir or "")
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        return out
    try:
        # W30/verify: detect the default branch (main/master/trunk) instead of hardcoding `main`
        # — a repo on `master` otherwise makes `main..br` fail and silently skips every lane.
        _default = None
        for _cand in ("main", "master", "trunk"):
            _rp = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", _cand],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
            if _rp.returncode == 0:
                _default = _cand
                break
        if not _default:
            return out
        wt = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "worktree", "list", "--porcelain"],
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        if wt.returncode != 0:
            return out
        blocks, cur = [], {}
        for line in wt.stdout.splitlines():
            if line.startswith("worktree "):
                if cur:
                    blocks.append(cur)
                cur = {"path": line[9:]}
            elif line.startswith("branch "):
                cur["branch"] = line[7:].replace("refs/heads/", "")
        if cur:
            blocks.append(cur)
        for b in blocks[:40]:
            p, br = b.get("path", ""), b.get("branch", "")
            if not p or not br or os.path.realpath(p) == os.path.realpath(root):
                continue                       # skip the main worktree itself
            if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(p, "journeys", ".last-pass")):
                continue                       # not gate-green → not a "done" lane
            st = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", p, "status", "--porcelain"],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
            if st.returncode != 0 or st.stdout.strip():
                continue                       # not quiesced (dirty tree)
            lg = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "log", "--oneline", "%s..%s" % (_default, br)],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
            if lg.returncode != 0:
                continue
            ahead = len([x for x in lg.stdout.splitlines() if x.strip()])
            if ahead < 1:
                continue                       # already merged (nothing on the branch past main)
            ct = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", root, "log", "-1", "--format=%ct", br],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
            try:
                age_min = int((_t.time() - int(ct.stdout.strip())) / 60)
            except Exception:
                age_min = min_age_min          # unknown age → treat as due (conservative)
            if age_min >= min_age_min:
                out.append((br, ahead, age_min))
    except Exception:
        return out
    return out


def roster_gap(rdir, rows, since=0):
    """[(lane, fired, expected)] for every card lane under-fired since `since`.
    `rows` is [(agent_type, epoch)] from the dispatch-log. Empty list = roster met
    (or no card lanes to compare, which the caller distinguishes via
    build_mode_roster(...)['has_lanes_row'])."""
    card = build_mode_roster(rdir)
    gaps = []
    for lane, want in sorted(card["lanes"].items()):
        got = sum(1 for t, e in rows if t == lane and e >= since)
        if got < want:
            gaps.append((lane, got, want))
    return gaps


def gate_artifacts(rdir):
    """[pure] File-state read of the four deploy-gate artifacts in a repo. Returns a
    list of (artifact, problem) for everything missing/red — empty list = gate green.
    Manifest logic = the W18 MAN1 row scan (a row whose Primitive cell is empty/?/TBD
    and not marked mock is an unwired feature — R#27 blind-spot class)."""
    root = os.path.expanduser(rdir or ".")
    out = []
    man = None
    for cand in (os.path.join("docs", "feature-manifest.md"), "feature-manifest.md"):
        p = os.path.join(root, cand)
        if os.path.isfile(p):
            man = p
            break
    if man is None:
        out.append(("feature-manifest", "docs/feature-manifest.md absent — no feature/test "
                                        "coverage list exists for this repo"))
    else:
        bad = []
        try:
            with open(man, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
                for ln in fh:
                    if not ln.strip().startswith("|"):
                        continue
                    cells = [c.strip() for c in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
                    if len(cells) >= 2 and cells[1].lower() in ("", "?", "tbd") \
                            and "mock" not in ln.lower() and cells[0] \
                            and not set(cells[0]) <= {"-", " "} and cells[0].lower() != "feature":
                        bad.append(cells[0])
        except Exception:
            bad = []
        if bad:
            out.append(("feature-manifest", "rows with no primitive id and not marked mock: "
                                            + ", ".join(bad[:3])))
    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, "docs", "DESIGN.md")):
        out.append(("DESIGN.md", "no design lock on file (docs/DESIGN.md, P0.5) — visual "
                                 "direction was never committed"))
    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(root, "docs", "SPEC.md")):
        out.append(("SPEC.md", "no in-repo requirement contract (docs/SPEC.md) — asks have "
                               "no durable home the gate can read"))
    lp = os.path.join(root, "journeys", ".last-pass")
    if not os.path.isfile(lp):
        out.append(("journeys", "journeys/.last-pass absent — the journey suite has never "
                                "gone green in this repo (`npm run journeys`)"))
    # W27 5th row: the ISSUE-LEDGER. A review round produces per-lane JSON verdicts, and
    # without a single collated ledger the round's findings live only in scattered files
    # nobody re-reads at ship time — which is how a category scoring 2.14 against a bar of
    # 9 was treated as closed. A repo that has not run a review round yet is reasoned-GREEN
    # (there is nothing to collate), so absence only counts once lane outputs exist.
    led = os.path.join(root, "docs", "ISSUE-LEDGER.md")
    revs = []
    for d in ("reviews", os.path.join("docs", "reviews")):
        rd = os.path.join(root, d)
        if os.path.isdir(rd):
            revs += [f for f in os.listdir(rd) if f.endswith(".json")]
    if revs:
        if not os.path.isfile(led):
            out.append(("ISSUE-LEDGER", "%d lane verdict file(s) exist but docs/ISSUE-LEDGER.md "
                                        "is absent — the round's findings were never collated, "
                                        "so nothing re-reads them at ship time" % len(revs)))
        else:
            try:
                rows = [ln for ln in open(led, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
                        if ln.strip().startswith("|") and not set(ln.strip()) <= set("|- ")]
            except OSError:
                rows = []
            # header row alone is not a ledger
            if len(rows) < 2:
                out.append(("ISSUE-LEDGER", "docs/ISSUE-LEDGER.md carries no findings rows "
                                            "while %d lane verdict file(s) exist" % len(revs)))
    return out


def manifest_rows(text):
    """Feature-key cells of a standard docs/feature-manifest.md (first column of
    each data row: Feature | Primitive | How to exercise | VISIBLE outcome |
    Last verified — the starter's existing convention), lowercased. A row whose
    PRIMITIVE cell carries `removed` is a deliberate retirement, not a drop.
    Returns (keys_set, removed_set). Pure text parsing; the format contract lives
    in nexus-app-builder/references/feature-manifest-format.md."""
    keys, removed = set(), set()
    for ln in (text or "").splitlines():
        if not ln.strip().startswith("|"):
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in ln.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
        if len(cells) < 2 or not cells[0] or set(cells[0]) <= {"-", " "} \
                or cells[0].lower() == "feature":
            continue
        k = cells[0].lower()
        (removed if "removed" in cells[1].lower() else keys).add(k)
    return keys, removed


def manifest_dropped(old_text, new_text):
    """Feature keys present in the previously pushed manifest, absent from the
    current one, and not marked `removed` — the silently-dropped-features class
    (a rebuild shipped minus views the user had accepted, W21 S6). Pure set
    difference; both sides parse via manifest_rows."""
    old_keys, _ = manifest_rows(old_text)
    new_keys, new_removed = manifest_rows(new_text)
    return sorted(old_keys - new_keys - new_removed)


def user_msgs_since(transcript_path, since_epoch, tail_lines=600):
    """Count GENUINE user entries (type=="user", not isMeta, content carries text)
    in the transcript tail whose timestamp is later than `since_epoch`. Returns an
    int (0 on any failure — fail-open). Powers SPEC1: asks landing after the spec
    contract's mtime without a matching append."""
    if not transcript_path:
        return 0
    n = 0
    try:
        lines = read_tail_lines(transcript_path, tail_lines)
        for raw in lines:
            try:
                e = json.loads(raw)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if e.get("type") != "user" or e.get("isMeta"):
                continue
            if not _human_entry((e.get("message") or {}).get("content")):
                continue
            ep = _entry_ts(e)
            if ep is not None and ep > since_epoch:
                n += 1
    except Exception:
        return 0
    return n



# ── W24: board + turn helpers (D1 STOP-WAKE, board-entry, ORD1) ───────────────
def board_state(transcript_path, tail_lines=1200):
    """W24 [pure]. The task board as the HARNESS sees it, read from the most recent
    `task_reminder` attachment in the transcript (rows carry id · subject · status ·
    blockedBy · blocks). No new feed is needed: at PreToolUse a TaskCreate carries no
    id (the id only exists in the result), so a payload feed could never build the
    board — the injected reminder is the authoritative source and it also carries
    blockedBy, making "pending AND unblocked" computable rather than guessed.
    Returns {"pending":[…], "unblocked":[…], "in_progress":[…], "all":[…]} of row
    dicts, or None when no reminder is present (caller FAILS OPEN — never block on
    a board we cannot see)."""
    try:
        lines = read_tail_lines(transcript_path, tail_lines)
    except Exception:
        return None
    rows, at = None, len(lines)
    for i in range(len(lines) - 1, -1, -1):
        if '"task_reminder"' not in lines[i]:
            continue
        try:
            att = (json.loads(lines[i]).get("attachment") or {})
            if att.get("type") == "task_reminder" and isinstance(att.get("content"), list):
                rows, at = att["content"], i
                break
        except Exception:
            continue
    if rows is None:
        return None
    # W27: the attachment is a SNAPSHOT and it is not re-emitted after every task update, so
    # completions made after it are invisible to this read. Measured at a cycle close: the newest
    # attachment still listed two tasks as pending 62 transcript lines after both were completed,
    # and the end-of-turn check kept waking on work that no longer existed — a check firing on
    # stale input is indistinguishable from a check firing wrongly, and it teaches the reader to
    # ignore it. Reconcile forward: any TaskUpdate to completed/deleted AFTER the snapshot wins.
    _closed = set()
    for ln in lines[at + 1:]:
        if '"TaskUpdate"' not in ln:
            continue
        try:
            obj = json.loads(ln)
        except Exception:
            continue
        stack = [obj]
        while stack:
            cur = stack.pop()
            if isinstance(cur, dict):
                if cur.get("name") == "TaskUpdate" and isinstance(cur.get("input"), dict):
                    inp = cur["input"]
                    if str(inp.get("status", "")).lower() in ("completed", "deleted"):
                        _closed.add(str(inp.get("taskId")))
                stack.extend(cur.values())
            elif isinstance(cur, list):
                stack.extend(cur)
    if _closed:
        rows = [dict(r, status="completed") if str(r.get("id")) in _closed else r for r in rows]
    return board_from_rows(rows)


def board_from_rows(rows):
    """W28/F02. The row list -> board verdict, split out of `board_state` UNCHANGED so the
    store path (`board_live`) runs the same normalisation, ghost/cycle handling and
    unblocked-ness rule. A second implementation would drift from this one in silence — and
    nearly did: the first patch drafted for the store path re-derived the unblocked rule and
    would have silently dropped the stuck/ghost-cycle work added the same morning."""
    # W28/E02-S4/S5: NORMALISE before comparing. `status` was matched exactly, so any casing or
    # whitespace drift in the harness's row shape ("Pending") retired arm 1 in silence; and
    # `blockedBy` was iterated directly, so a bare STRING was walked character by character
    # ("12" -> blockers "1" and "2"), which either accidentally blocks a row or accidentally
    # unblocks it, with no error either way.
    def _st(r):
        return str(r.get("status") or "").strip().lower()

    def _bb(r):
        b = r.get("blockedBy") or []
        return [str(x) for x in (b if isinstance(b, list) else [b])]

    ids = {str(r.get("id")) for r in rows}
    done = {str(r.get("id")) for r in rows if _st(r) == "completed"}
    pend = [r for r in rows if _st(r) == "pending"]

    # W28/E02-S2/S3: a blocker that CANNOT EVER BE SATISFIED must not hold a row down forever.
    # Two shapes, both measured silent: a GHOST blocker (an id that is not on the board at all
