            # degrade and delivering them twice is the failure this primitive exists to
            # prevent.
            if _lk.timed_out:
                return default
            cur = get(sid, name)
            if cur is not None:
                put(sid, name, None)
            return default if cur is None else cur
    except Exception:
        try:
            cur = get(sid, name)
        except Exception:
            return default
        return default if cur is None else cur


def is_set(sid, key):
    """Non-mutating check of a once()-flag (does NOT create it)."""
    try:
        return os.path.exists(os.path.join(_dir(sid, create=False), "flag_" + _safe(key)))
    except Exception:
        return False


try:
    import fcntl as _fcntl
except Exception:
    _fcntl = None      # non-POSIX: degrade to the unlocked behaviour, never fail


# W48/MECH-3/L3 — the bound is PER ACQUIRE; the budget that matters is PER HOOK RUN.
#
# A hook takes MANY locks in one run: `nexus-posttool.py` has 36 lock-taking call sites
# in `main`, and `nexus-awareness.py`'s `handle_user_prompt` takes two — so a per-acquire
# bound alone makes a run's worst case (bound x acquires), and it grows every time an
# adapter gains a feed. That is the actual budget defect: the UserPromptSubmit path
# declares `timeout: 20` in settings.json and its two `take`s alone could wait 16 s.
#
# Once ONE acquire has timed out, something is wedged, and every later acquire in the
# same process is overwhelmingly likely to wait the full bound and time out too — so
# waiting again buys nothing and spends the run's budget again. After the first timeout
# this process stops waiting: later acquires refuse immediately, and the worst case for
# any run is ONE bound whatever the acquire count. Legitimate contention never trips it,
# because legitimate contention SUCCEEDS: measured at 16 writers x 25 updates, the worst
# single wait is ~2.4 s against an 8 s bound.
_gave_up = False


class _flock:
    """Advisory exclusive lock around a feed, for the read-modify-REWRITE paths.

    W28/E12: `drop`/`pdrop` read a whole feed into memory and reopen it `"w"`, so every append
    landing between the read and the rewrite was DESTROYED. Measured: **33–43% of concurrent
    appends lost** (626/1600, 1361/3200, 2106/6400 at 8/16/32 appenders against 2 droppers).

    `pdrop`'s blast radius is the reason this matters: it operates on PROJECT-scoped feeds
    (`id-cache`, `lifecycle`, `agent-lifecycle`) that every session and every subagent lane
    shares by construction, so one `nexus agent delete` while lanes are running silently ate
    other lanes' rows.

    An `O_APPEND` write is already atomic against other appenders, so `log` only needs the
    lock to be EXCLUDED BY a rewrite in progress — both sides must participate or the lock
    buys nothing. Fails open in every direction: no fcntl, or an unlockable file, and the
    operation proceeds exactly as it did before."""

    def __init__(self, path, mode, wait=8.0):
        self.path, self.mode, self.fh = path, mode, None
        # W48/V3 — the acquire now reports its own VERDICT. Before this, a timed-out acquire
        # returned byte-for-byte what a successful one returned, so a caller could not tell
        # whether it held the lock. `update()` could not, and did an unlocked read-modify-write.
        self.wait, self.timed_out = wait, False

    def __enter__(self):
        self.fh = open(self.path, self.mode)
        if _fcntl is not None:
            # W28/F01 — a BOUNDED acquire. A plain blocking `LOCK_EX` made `log()` wait as long
            # as any other process held the lock; measured, one holder stalled a logger for
            # 2.60 s. Hooks are synchronous and sit on the tool-call critical path, so a `drop`
            # that stalls (a slow filesystem, a mount going away, a stopped process) would stall
            # every hook logging to that feed, up to the harness timeout. Before the lock landed,
            # the append path could not block at all — that liveness change was unrecorded.
            #
            # Not `LOCK_NB` alone: that reopens the write-destroying race under any contention,
            # which is what the lock exists to close. Real contention costs ~0.1 ms, so a 2 s
            # bound keeps the correctness win and caps the pathological case below the hook
            # timeout — the only case that ever reaches a person. On timeout we proceed
            # UNLOCKED, which is exactly the pre-lock behaviour: degraded, never stuck.
            # W48/V3 — TWO CHANGES, both measured. (1) The backoff is JITTERED. The bound was
            # being exceeded by STARVATION, not by slow holders: the critical section is
            # sub-millisecond (median wait 0.0000 s over 1,200 instrumented acquires) yet 5-8%
            # of acquires waited over a second, because `LOCK_NB` + a fixed 5 ms sleep is an
            # unfair lottery with no queue — waiters sleep in lockstep and a releaser
            # re-acquires ahead of them. (2) The bound is a PARAMETER, and the default rose
            # 2.0 → 8.0 s. Measured on the append paths: at 2.0 s the `no append is lost
            # against concurrent drops` assertion was green 4/10 runs; at 8.0 s, 10/10, with
            # zero FAIL lines across ten consecutive suite runs.
            #
            # W48/MECH-3 — TWO EARLIER CLAIMS HERE WERE WRONG, both corrected on measurement.
            #
            # (1) "the harness timeout is 10 s" — it is not. A `command` hook with no `timeout`
            # field gets the documented 600 s default; `UserPromptSubmit` gets 30 s. The only
            # tight budget in this layer is the one the estate sets itself: `timeout: 20` on the
            # four `nexus-awareness.py` wirings. So 8 s never risked a kill on the paths that
            # were worried about, and the real exposure was the path nobody costed — two `take`s
            # in one UserPromptSubmit run, 16 s against a self-declared 20 s.
            #
            # (2) "the measured cause is starvation, not slowness, so the durable fix is a FAIR
            # acquire" — driven, a fair acquire does NOT fix it. The tail is the CRITICAL
            # SECTION, not the queue order: with 17 processes on 12 cores the median section is
            # under 1 ms but its MAXIMUM reaches 137-201 ms, so any queue of 15 waiters is
            # seconds long however fairly it is served. Measured at 16 writers x 25 updates over
            # 5 trials of 400 acquires each: plain blocking `LOCK_EX` still waited 2.576 s at
            # worst, and a real FIFO ticket queue still reached 2.325 s while costing 4-7x the
            # wall time, moving the MEDIAN wait from 0.0000 s to 0.4-0.7 s, and giving up the one
            # property flock has for free — release on process death. A `LOCK_NB` fast path in
            # front of a blocking acquire is actively harmful: it barges past everyone already
            # queued, and dropped 159 of 400 entries.
            #
            # The bound therefore stays 8 s, and what is fixed instead is the MULTIPLICATION.
            global _gave_up
            if _gave_up:
                # This run already spent its budget on a wedge, so it will not WAIT again.
                # It still TRIES: one non-blocking attempt costs a single syscall and takes
                # the lock whenever the contention has cleared, so giving up on waiting
                # never means giving up on the lock. Without it, one timeout would refuse
                # every later acquire in the run, including ones that would have succeeded
                # in a millisecond.
                try:
                    _fcntl.flock(self.fh.fileno(), _fcntl.LOCK_EX | _fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                except Exception:
                    self.timed_out = True
                return self.fh
            _deadline = time.time() + self.wait
            while True:
                try:
                    _fcntl.flock(self.fh.fileno(), _fcntl.LOCK_EX | _fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                    break
                except BlockingIOError:
                    if time.time() > _deadline:
                        self.timed_out = _gave_up = True
                        break
                    time.sleep(0.002 + _random.random() * 0.008)
                except Exception:
                    # fail-open: an unlockable filesystem must not break the write. `timed_out`
                    # stays False here deliberately — this path is the non-POSIX / unlockable
                    # degrade, which is intended, not a contended miss a caller should refuse on.
                    break
        return self.fh

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        try:
            self.fh.flush()
            if _fcntl is not None:
                try:
                    _fcntl.flock(self.fh.fileno(), _fcntl.LOCK_UN)
                except Exception:
                    pass   # fail-open: the close below releases the lock anyway
        finally:
            self.fh.close()
        return False


def log(sid, name, line):
    """Append a line to a per-session log file (read-log, mutation-log)."""
    try:
        # W28/F14: the lock is the SIDECAR, and the data file is opened separately.
        # Every participant must contend on the SAME object. When `drop` moved to a
        # write-temp-and-rename (so a dead writer cannot leave a half-rewritten feed),
        # locking the data file here stopped excluding it: the appender held the OLD
        # inode while the rename landed, and 124 of 640 appends vanished. A lock on a
        # file that gets replaced is not a lock. Caught by this cycle's new concurrency
        # fixture on its first run, which is exactly why that fixture exists.
        _p = os.path.join(_dir(sid), _safe(name))
        with _flock(_p + ".lock", "a"):
            with open(_p, "a") as fh:
                fh.write(line.rstrip("\n") + "\n")
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: the cache is best-effort — a hook must never fail because a log did


# The marker naming convention already exists on disk (`.lp1-observe`, `.stopwake-observe`);
# making it the contract costs nothing and is exhaustive, where "is a dotfile" is not.
_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"^\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,40}-observe$")


def _field(v):
    """One TSV field: never a tab, never a newline, never None.

    The decision log is positional TSV with no escaping whatsoever, so an embedded newline
    does not corrupt a field — it FORGES A WHOLE ROW, and one that parses perfectly and is
    attributed to a hook that never ran. A tab silently shifts every later column, so a
    strict reader takes the wrong value for `decision` and `epoch` without erroring."""
    return str(v).replace("\t", " ").replace("\n", " ").replace("\r", " ")


def log_decision(sid, hook, dec_id, decision):
    """Observe-mode telemetry — record every hook decision so warns can later be
    promoted to denies on data (zero would-have-denied false hits).

    Column 4 is the EPOCH of the decision. Without it the file answers "how often" but
    never "since when", so a check that has been noisy since day one and one that started
    misfiring last week are indistinguishable — and promoting a warn to a deny on that
    basis is guesswork. Every temporal question had to be answered through file mtimes,
    a proxy that degrades exactly where it matters, at a re-touched directory.

    APPENDED, never prepended: existing readers index hook/id/decision at 0/1/2, and a
    legacy 3-column row stays valid. Marker flips are NOT written here — they are 4
    free-text columns and would squat this one; they live in `markers` (see flip_marker).

    W28/E06: `int()`, not `%.0f`. `"%.0f" % t` ROUNDS, so roughly half of all rows carried a
    stamp up to 0.5 s in the FUTURE of the write (1785300000.600 -> …001). Any check of the
    form "this row's epoch <= that artifact's mtime" is then flaky by construction — the
    shape of a gate flake that cost a release. Truncation cannot produce a future stamp.

    W28/E06: fields are SANITISED. The format has no escaping, so a newline in any of the
    three forged a syntactically perfect extra row attributed to a hook that never ran, and
    a tab broke arity (measured: 11 calls produced 14 rows, 7 of them not 4 columns). Every
    call site passes a literal today, so this is one careless f-string from live — and no
    test could catch it, because the tests write their own clean ids."""
    log(sid, "decisions",
        "%s\t%s\t%s\t%d" % (_field(hook), _field(dec_id), _field(decision), int(time.time())))


def drop(sid, name, substr):
    """Remove every line of the named log that contains substr (rewrite-in-place).
    Used when a resource is deleted so the lifecycle/id-cache obligation clears —
    otherwise the completion gate nags forever about a resource that no longer
    exists. Failure-silent."""
    try:
        # W28/E12: read and rewrite under ONE exclusive lock. Unlocked, every append that
        # landed in the window between them was destroyed — a third to nearly half of all
        # concurrent writes.
        # W28/F06: `create=False`. `drop` is a rewrite path that is a NO-OP when the feed
        # does not exist, so calling it on a session that never wrote one manufactured the
        # directory — the exact "looking at state must not manufacture it" rule the earlier
        # sweep established for the seven read paths and missed here, because these two
        # look like writes while behaving like reads. Measured live: 188 of 1081 store
        # directories (17%) are empty. It got WORSE in W28/F14: the sidecar lock meant the
        # no-op also left a `.lock` file behind, so the empty-directory count stopped
        # detecting it. A missing directory now raises inside the existing try and degrades
        # to the documented answer — a missing feed reads as empty.
        path = os.path.join(_dir(sid, create=False), _safe(name))
        # W28/F14: CRASH-ATOMIC. The in-place rewrite (seek/writelines/truncate) leaves the
        # file as `kept rows + stale tail` for the window between the last two steps — and
        # if the writer dies there the flock is released by process death and the feed STAYS
        # corrupt, with no recovery path. Driven with the window widened: 33,029 rows the
        # drop was meant to remove survived, 3,669 were duplicated, one was a sliced
        # fragment. Write a sibling and rename: a reader either sees the whole old file or
        # the whole new one, and a dead writer leaves only a temp file behind.
        with _flock(path + ".lock", "a"):
            with open(path) as fh:
                kept = [ln for ln in fh if substr not in ln]
            tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (path, os.getpid())
            with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
                fh.writelines(kept)
            os.replace(tmp, path)
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: a missing feed reads as empty, which is the correct answer


def _read_shared(path):
    """Read a feed under a SHARED lock.

    W28/F14: the lock had only two participants — appenders and rewriters. READERS were
    never enrolled, and `drop` rewrites in place: seek(0) -> writelines(kept) -> truncate().
    Between the writelines and the truncate the file is `kept rows + stale tail`, so a
    reader landing there sees duplicated rows and a line sliced mid-token. Measured at
    natural timing: 1 corrupt snapshot in 12,000 reads, three readers against one drop.
    Widened deliberately, a single snapshot showed 3,669 duplicated rows and the fragment
    `ETEME\trow00003301`.

    That matters because `has`/`lines` are the completion gate's and AW5's inputs: a short
    read makes `has` answer False for a row that IS present, so AW5 fires on a skill that
    was read, or the completion gate forgets an obligation — the layer's two worst failure
    classes, produced by an ordinary delete while lanes run."""
    # W32/G05 — the lock goes on the SIDECAR, like every writer's. This took LOCK_SH on the
    # DATA file while `log`, `drop`, `plog`, `pdrop` and `update` all lock `<path>.lock`, so
    # the reader was enrolled in a lock nobody else holds — measured, a `drop` ran straight
    # through a held shared lock in 0.000 s. It is the same wrong-object mistake the earlier
    # wave found and fixed for the WRITERS, reintroduced on the reader in the same change,
    # and the suite's own "every writer contends on the same object" invariant missed it
    # because its function list names only writers.
    #
    # The lock is advisory and best-effort in both directions: no fcntl, or an unlockable
    # sidecar, and the read proceeds exactly as before. A reader that refuses to read is
    # worse than one that races.
    _lk = None
    if _fcntl is not None:
        try:
            _lk = open(path + ".lock", "a")
            _fcntl.flock(_lk.fileno(), _fcntl.LOCK_SH)
        except Exception:
            if _lk is not None:
                try:
                    _lk.close()
                except Exception:
                    pass   # best-effort: a close failure must not break a read
            _lk = None
    try:
        with open(path) as fh:
            return fh.readlines()
    finally:
        if _lk is not None:
            try:
                _lk.close()
            except Exception:
                pass   # best-effort: the lock releases when the fd is dropped either
                       # way, so a close failure changes nothing observable


def take_lines(sid, name, default=None):
    """Atomic read-and-CLEAR of a LINE feed — the queue counterpart of `take`.

    W35 — `take` is the object API (`get` then `put(None)`); a feed written with `log` needs
    its own. Without it the obvious call is `drop(sid, name)`, which takes THREE arguments
    (`substr`), so it raises `TypeError`, the caller's broad `except` swallows it, and the
    queue is never cleared — measured: the advisory repeated on every drain. Reading and
    clearing under ONE lock also closes the race two separate calls leave open, where two
    concurrent drains both read the rows and both deliver them.

    A failure to clear degrades to a REPEATED advisory rather than a lost one, which is the
    right direction for a queue whose contents are obligations."""
    try:
        path = os.path.join(_dir(sid, create=False), _safe(name))
        _lk = _flock(path + ".lock", "a")
        with _lk:
            # W48/MECH-3/L2 — the LINE-feed read-and-clear, same refusal as `take()` and
            # the same reason: unlocked it either loses the clear (the queue re-delivers)
            # or races a second drain into a double delivery.
            if _lk.timed_out:
                return [] if default is None else default
            try:
                with open(path) as fh:
                    rows = [ln.rstrip("\n") for ln in fh if ln.strip()]
            except Exception:
                return [] if default is None else default
            if rows:
                tmp = path + ".tmp"
                with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
                    pass
                os.replace(tmp, path)
            return rows
    except Exception:
        return [] if default is None else default


def has(sid, name, substr):
    """True if any line of the named log contains substr."""
    try:
        return any(substr in ln
                   for ln in _read_shared(os.path.join(_dir(sid, create=False), _safe(name))))
    except Exception:
        return False


def lines(sid, name):
    try:
        return [ln.rstrip("\n")
                for ln in _read_shared(os.path.join(_dir(sid, create=False), _safe(name)))]
    except Exception:
        return []


def put(sid, name, obj):
    """Write a JSON cache value ATOMICALLY.

    W28/E12: this was `open(path, "w")` + `json.dump`. The `"w"` truncates before the new
    bytes land, so a concurrent `get()` read a half-written file, `json.load` raised, and the
    bare except turned it into a cache MISS. Measured under fan-out: **~50% of concurrent
    reads missed** (240/480, 453/960, 929/1920 at 8/16/32 writers).

    It fails safe — no caller ever sees corrupt data — but the consequences were real. The
    TTL caches this exists to serve (`model list`, credentials, collections) were half
    ineffective exactly when the most lanes were running, so the hook re-shelled the
    expensive discovery command the cache was there to avoid. Worse, `stop-pending` is a
    read-modify-write: a torn read made `_pend` empty and SILENTLY DROPPED queued Stop
    advisories.

    `os.replace` is atomic on POSIX, so a reader sees either the old file or the new one.
    The temp name carries the pid so two writers cannot collide on it."""
    try:
        d = _dir(sid)
        path = os.path.join(d, _safe(name) + ".json")
        tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (path, os.getpid())
        with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
            json.dump({"t": time.time(), "v": obj}, fh)
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except Exception:
        try:
            os.remove(tmp)      # never leave a partial temp behind
        except Exception:
            pass   # fail-open: the temp may not exist yet; a stray one is harmless either way
        # fail-open: best-effort cache write — a hook must never fail because a cache did


def get(sid, name, ttl=None):
    """Return cached value, or None if missing/expired (ttl seconds)."""
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(_dir(sid, create=False), _safe(name) + ".json")) as fh:
            rec = json.load(fh)
        if ttl is not None and (time.time() - rec.get("t", 0)) > ttl:
            return None
        return rec.get("v")
    except Exception:
        return None


# ----------------------------------------------- project-scoped state --------
# State the build needs for its WHOLE lifetime — not just one session_id. Keyed
# on the project (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR / cwd), so a completion or consolidation
# fact survives a new session_id AND a sandbox reset (where a session-keyed flag
# is invisible to the next session). Mirrors the session API above; same _safe,
# same shapes, failure-silent. Lives under:
#
#     ~/.nexus-mcp/cue-project/<project-basename>/
#
def _proot():
    """Resolved per CALL, never at import — see `_root()`."""
    return os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".nexus-mcp", "cue-project")


def _pdir(project, create=True):
    """create=False for READ paths — see `_dir()`."""
    d = os.path.join(_proot(), _safe(os.path.basename(str(project or "default"))))
    if create:
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def plog(project, name, line):
    try:
        # sidecar lock, same reason as `log` — and project feeds are the shared ones.
        _p = os.path.join(_pdir(project), _safe(name))
        with _flock(_p + ".lock", "a"):
            with open(_p, "a") as fh:
                fh.write(line.rstrip("\n") + "\n")
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: best-effort project-feed write


def plines(project, name):
    try:
        # shared lock, same reason as `lines` — and project feeds are the ones every lane
        # reads, so an unlocked read here races with every other lane's `pdrop`.
        return [ln.rstrip("\n")
                for ln in _read_shared(os.path.join(_pdir(project, create=False), _safe(name)))]
    except Exception:
        return []


# W34/F1 — the prefix for the per-slug "this workspace was listed" project flag.
# It is written by `nexus-posttool` and read by `nexus-fs-firewall`, in different
# adapters on different events, and it is the prerequisite of the ENFORCING `WSW-RET`
# deny. Held as two bare string literals it could drift on a one-line rename that reads
# as a no-op: driven, renaming it in the writer only left the deny standing after five
# genuine listing reads, with the flag on disk under the other name — and BOTH the
# feed-contract suite and the 22-assertion WSW suite stayed green, because one resolves
# feed names only for string constants and the other hand-writes the flag file instead
# of driving the producer. A deny whose remedy cannot clear it is the worst shape a deny
# takes. One definition makes the pair structurally unable to drift — the same argument
# `hook_core._strip` settled in W32 when the firewall had grown a private copy.
WSREAD_FLAG = "wsread_"


def pset(project, key):
    try:
        open(os.path.join(_pdir(project), "flag_" + _safe(key)), "w").close()
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def pis_set(project, key):
    try:
        return os.path.exists(os.path.join(_pdir(project, create=False), "flag_" + _safe(key)))
    except Exception:
        return False


def pclear(project, key):
    """Remove a project flag — the missing half of `pset`/`pis_set`.

    A durable flag with no removal path IN CODE is how a nine-day silence happens:
    `consolidation_hold` could be set and never cleared, so 1,094 suppressions accumulated
    with zero emissions and no record of who set it or when. W21 retired the durable
    `app_build` flag for the same class ("one sprint's flag bled … into every later
    session"); this one was left standing.

    Idempotent: clearing an absent flag returns True, because the caller asks "is it clear
    now?" — treating an absent flag as failure makes callers retry forever."""
    try:
        os.remove(os.path.join(_pdir(project, create=False), "flag_" + _safe(key)))
        return True
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return True    # already clear — that IS the desired end state
    except Exception:
        return False


def pdrop(project, name, substr):
    # W28/E12: the HIGHEST-blast-radius instance of the rewrite race. Project feeds are shared
    # by every session and every subagent lane in the project BY CONSTRUCTION, so an unlocked
    # read-then-rewrite here ate other lanes' rows on any concurrent append. Same lock as
    # `drop`; both sides of the race now participate.
    try:
        # W28/F06: `create=False`, same reason as `drop`.
        p = os.path.join(_pdir(project, create=False), _safe(name))
        # W28/F14: crash-atomic, same reasoning as `drop` — and it matters MORE here,
        # because a project feed is shared by every session and every lane, so a corrupt
        # tail outlives the process that produced it and is read as truth by all of them.
        with _flock(p + ".lock", "a"):
            with open(p) as fh:
                kept = [ln for ln in fh if substr not in ln]
            tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (p, os.getpid())
            with open(tmp, "w") as fh:
                fh.writelines(kept)
            os.replace(tmp, p)
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: a missing project feed reads as empty


def pc_epoch(sid):
    """Number of compaction snapshots this session (read-log.pc* files). Lets a
    once-per-session warn re-arm per epoch instead of dying after one firing
    (the LEAK warn fired once while 164 leak turns followed, W21)."""
    try:
        import glob as _g
        return len(_g.glob(os.path.join(_dir(sid, create=False), "read-log.pc*")))
    except Exception:
        return 0


def flip_marker(name, on, why, sid=None, hooks_dir=None):
    """Create or delete an observe-rollout marker AND record the flip. Returns the row.

    Why this exists: an observe marker is how a verdict-bearing check is rolled out
    (present = record only, absent = enforce). One was cleared with no record at all, so
    a later audit found a check emitting warns with no marker on disk and could not tell
    whether the rollout had been deliberately completed or the marker had been lost. A
    flip is a DECISION; it belongs in the decision log next to the verdicts it changes.

    A flip made by hand (touch/rm) still works and cannot be prevented — the rule is that
    a flip with no `MARKER` row is a defect, and this function is the way not to create one.
    """
    hooks_dir = hooks_dir or os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    # W28/E06-2b: `name` went straight into os.path.join with no validation at all, and the
    # `on` branch opens it "w" — which TRUNCATES. Measured: flip_marker("../outside.txt", True)
    # zeroed a file outside the tree; ("nexus-pretool.py", True) zeroed a LIVE HOOK; False
    # deleted either outright. `name` comes from argv[2] of the CLI below, so a typo or an
    # unset shell variable was one keystroke from destroying a hook. A marker is a dotfile
    # directly inside the hooks dir and nothing else — anything else is a caller bug, and the
    # right answer to a caller bug is a refusal, not a truncated file.
    # W28/F01 — "a dotfile in the hooks dir" was too weak a contract. `.gitignore` and
    # `.DS_Store` satisfy that sentence and are not markers; measured, `flip_marker(".gitignore",
    # True)` zeroed a tracked repo file, and a dotfile SYMLINK was followed straight out of the
    # tree. Name the ACT instead: every real marker is `.<slug>-observe`. A positive pattern is
    # exhaustive by construction, where a denylist of known dotfiles leaves the next dotfile
    # added to the repo unprotected — the same substring-not-act mistake one level up.
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not _MARKER_RE.match(name):
        return "MARKER\t%s\tERROR\tinvalid marker name (must match .<slug>-observe)" % _field(name)
    path = os.path.join(hooks_dir, name)
    if os.path.islink(path):
        return "MARKER\t%s\tERROR\trefusing to write through a symlink" % _field(name)
    try:
        if on:
            open(path, "w").close()
        elif os.path.exists(path):
            os.remove(path)
    except OSError as e:
        return "MARKER\t%s\tERROR\t%s" % (_field(name), _field(e))
    # BOTH free-text fields go through `_field`. W28 sanitised `why` (argv[4]) and left `name`
    # (argv[2]) raw — half the row a property and half a promise. A name carrying a newline
    # passed validation and still forged a row, and the suite pinned only the `why` half, so it
    # was invisible to the battery. The row format must be self-defending regardless of who
    # validates upstream; that is the same argument this file makes for `log_decision`.
    row = "MARKER\t%s\t%s\t%s" % (_field(name), "on" if on else "off", _field(why))
    if sid:
        # Its OWN file. `decisions` is a strict TSV whose 3-column contract
        # nexus-conformance.py documents 20 lines from here, and W28 added a 4th column
        # for the decision epoch. A marker row is 4 FREE-TEXT columns, so co-locating them
        # both corrupts any strict-arity parser (measured: 7 such rows, two written by the
        # session that found them) and squats the timestamp column. A flip is still a
        # logged decision; it is a different SHAPE, and shapes do not share a file.
        log(sid, "markers", row)
    return row


if __name__ == "__main__":   # tiny CLI so a flip is one command that always logs
    import sys as _s
    if len(_s.argv) >= 5 and _s.argv[1] == "flip-marker":
        _name, _state, _why = _s.argv[2], _s.argv[3], _s.argv[4]
        _sid = _s.argv[5] if len(_s.argv) > 5 else os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID")
        print(flip_marker(_name, _state == "on", _why, _sid))
    else:
        print("usage: session_cache.py flip-marker <.marker-name> <on|off> <why> [sid]")
        _s.exit(2)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Claude Code awareness adapter — makes Cue aware without recall.

Registered on three event/matcher pairs, branches on hook_event_name:
  • PreToolUse  / Read  → AW3: warn on a PARTIAL read of a governing doc
        (incl. a workspace INDEX.md) + log mount content-reads (KR2 feed).
  • PostToolUse / Read  → AW1/AW2: parse the doc's `!! Read … !!` / `Skill(…)`
        / `→ see` graph and inject the required/related paths (existence-verified).
  • UserPromptSubmit    → AW4: once per session, the general-context orientation —
        mounted variant, or the unmounted/wedged variant naming the REST read path.

W10 posture: every trigger here is PURE LOGIC (an event, a file/dir state, a path
identifier). The former prompt-wording triggers (R41 pre-grep on build-shaped text,
plan-FYI framing, the ARCH archetype inject) were removed — hooks never interpret
request language; that judgment is Cue's, via doctrine.

Failure-silent: any error → exit 0 (never break a turn).
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "lib"))
import hook_core as hc       # noqa: E402
import session_cache as sc   # noqa: E402

GOV_RE = ("SKILL.md", "GUIDE.md", "NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md",
          "CLAUDE.md", "WORKFLOW_DESIGN_GUIDE.md", "AGENT_BUILDER_LIFECYCLE.md",
          "INDEX.md")  # W10: a workspace INDEX is a map — partial reads hide whole domains


def _is_governing(path):
    return bool(path) and any(path.endswith(suf) or path.rstrip("/").endswith(suf)
                              for suf in GOV_RE)


def _mtime(path):
    """[file-state] mtime at millisecond resolution, 0 when unreadable. The re-arm dimension
    for the AW1/AW3 once-keys: a CHANGED governing doc re-arms the warning, while re-reading
    the same one — including page by page — does not.

    Milliseconds, not seconds: at integer-second resolution an edit followed by a read inside
    the same wall-clock second did not re-arm, which a fast agent loop hits."""
    try:
        return int(os.path.getmtime(path) * 1000)
    except Exception:
        return 0   # fail-open: an unreadable mtime must not suppress the warning forever


def _dockey(path):
    """[file-state] The once-key identity for a governing doc: a short digest of its ABSOLUTE
    path, never its basename.

    Measured on the real tree: keying on `basename` collided on files that share a name AND a
    timestamp, and bulk-created files routinely share a timestamp. `nexus-workflow-builder/
    SKILL.md` — the largest gate-bearing doc in the estate — was silenced for the whole
    session by `nexus-skills-and-tasks/SKILL.md`, and 7 of 24 `GUIDE.md` docs were silenced by
    a sibling. The guard that exists to catch a partial read of exactly that file was the one
    suppressed.

    sha1 of the abspath rather than the abspath itself because the session store collapses
    `/` in key names, which would trade one collision class for another. NOT the builtin
    `hash()`: PYTHONHASHSEED is randomised per process and the two Reads run in separate
    subprocesses, so the key would never match itself and the de-duplication would vanish."""
    try:
        return hashlib.sha1(os.path.abspath(path).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
    except Exception:
        return "unknown"   # fail-open: an unkeyable path warns every time rather than never


def _project_dir(data):
    return (os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR")
            or data.get("cwd") or os.getcwd())


_SID = None   # set by main(); _emit()'s telemetry reads it (no data param there)


def _emit(event, ctx):
    # W49 — telemetry. This emitter never wrote a decision row, so AW1/AW3/PC-CANON (and
    # every other id leaving through here) were structurally unmeasurable. Unlike the
    # lifecycle twin this logs on EVERY event: nothing else in this adapter logs these
    # ids, so there is no double-count to avoid (R34-HOLD and AW-ENGINE log at their own
    # sites and do not pass through _emit). Ids parsed from the emitted "[ID]" prefixes.
    # Log-only; output byte-identical; a telemetry failure must never cost the emission.
    try:
        if _SID:
            for _cid in dict.fromkeys(
                    re.findall(r"\[([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_+-]{1,24})\]", ctx or "")):
                sc.log_decision(_SID, event, _cid, "annotate")
    except Exception:
        pass
    print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
        "hookEventName": event, "additionalContext": ctx}}))
    sys.exit(0)


def _resolve(kind, target, doc_path, proj):
    """Best-effort resolve a gate target to an existing absolute path."""
    cands = []
    if kind == "skill":
        cands += [os.path.join(proj, ".claude", "skills", target, "SKILL.md"),
                  os.path.join(proj, ".claude", "skills", target)]
    else:
        docdir = os.path.dirname(doc_path) if doc_path else proj
        cands += [os.path.join(docdir, target),
                  os.path.join(proj, ".claude", target),
                  os.path.join(proj, target)]
    for c in cands:
        if os.path.exists(c):
            return os.path.normpath(c)
    return None


def handle_read_pre(data):
    ti = hc.d(data.get("tool_input"))
    # W39/H12: coerced at the READ. A non-string `file_path` reached a path call and
    # exited 1 with a traceback — and a crashed adapter is an ABSENT adapter: every check
    # in it skipped for that tool call, no decision row, a non-blocking exit, the call
    # proceeds. W28/F13 fixed this class "at the READ rather than a str() at the use";
    # this read was missed by that sweep. Driven: `file_path: [1]` and `{"a":1}` both
    # took this adapter down on PreToolUse AND PostToolUse Read.
    path = hc.s(ti.get("file_path"))
    limit = ti.get("limit")
    # KR2 feed (W10, pure path logic): a Read of workspace CONTENT via a live mount —
    # boundary trio (INDEX.md + _meta/*) excluded — joins the serial-reads count.
    # BND1 feed (W11): a mount Read OF the boundary trio is logged as the boundary read.
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    if sid and path:
        _is_boundary = os.path.basename(path) == "INDEX.md" or "/_meta/" in path
        for mp in (v.get("mountPath") for v in _mounts().values() if v):
            if mp and path.startswith(os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(mp)) + "/"):
                sc.log(sid, "boundary-read" if _is_boundary else "ws-file-reads",
                       "mount:" + path)
                break
    # W28/F19: `isinstance(limit, int)` went silent on `"100"` and on `100.0` — the float
    # is one JSON round-trip away — and `True` passed as an int, reporting "1/608 lines".
    if not _is_governing(path):
        sys.exit(0)
    if isinstance(limit, bool):
        sys.exit(0)
    try:
        limit = int(limit)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        sys.exit(0)
    try:
        with open(path) as fh:
            total = sum(1 for _ in fh)
    except Exception:
        sys.exit(0)
    # W44: AW3 was PAGINATION-BLIND — it compared `limit < total` and never inspected
    # `offset`, so the paginated reading R#2 explicitly licenses ("paginate w/ offset for
    # larger") tripped it once per page. Measured: reading CLAUDE.md across four pages
    # emitted AW3 3× and AW1 4×, byte-identical each time. A read with an offset is a
    # CONTINUATION, not a partial first read.
    try:
        offset = int(ti.get("offset") or 0)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        offset = 0
    if limit < total and offset <= 0 \
            and sc.once(data.get("session_id"),
                        "aw3_%s_%d" % (_dockey(path), _mtime(path))):
        _emit("PreToolUse",
              f"⚠ [AW3] Partial read ({limit}/{total} lines) of a GOVERNING doc "
              f"({os.path.basename(path)}). Read it FULLY (R#2) — gotchas past the "
              "limit are how builds silently break.")
    sys.exit(0)


def handle_read_post(data):
    ti = hc.d(data.get("tool_input"))
    # W39/H12: coerced at the READ. A non-string `file_path` reached a path call and
    # exited 1 with a traceback — and a crashed adapter is an ABSENT adapter: every check
    # in it skipped for that tool call, no decision row, a non-blocking exit, the call
    # proceeds. W28/F13 fixed this class "at the READ rather than a str() at the use";
    # this read was missed by that sweep. Driven: `file_path: [1]` and `{"a":1}` both
    # took this adapter down on PreToolUse AND PostToolUse Read.
    path = hc.s(ti.get("file_path"))
    sc.log(data.get("session_id"), "read-log", path)  # powers AW5 first-mutation gate
    if not _is_governing(path):
        sys.exit(0)
    try:
        with open(path) as fh:
            text = fh.read()
    except Exception:
        sys.exit(0)
    gates = hc.parse_doc_gates(text)
    if not gates:
        sys.exit(0)
    proj = _project_dir(data)
    lines = []
    for kind, target in gates[:10]:
        resolved = _resolve(kind, target, path, proj)
        tag = {"read": "MUST READ", "skill": "Skill", "see": "related"}[kind]
        if resolved:
            lines.append(f"  • {tag}: {resolved}")
        else:
            lines.append(f"  • {tag}: {target} (unresolved)")
    # W44: same repetition class as AW3 — the dependency list is byte-identical on every
    # read of the same file, so a paginated read re-emitted it once per page. Keyed on
    # (file, mtime): a genuinely CHANGED doc re-arms it, re-reading the same one does not.
    if not sc.once(data.get("session_id"),
                   "aw1_%s_%d" % (_dockey(path), _mtime(path))):
        sys.exit(0)
    _emit("PostToolUse",
          f"[AW1] `{os.path.basename(path)}` declares dependencies — surface them "
          f"before acting:\n" + "\n".join(lines))


def _mounts():
    """The mounts map — ALWAYS a dict of dicts, whatever the file actually contains.

    W28/E09: the READ was guarded by try/except but the SHAPE was not, so a file parsing to
    a LIST (or to a dict whose values are strings) sailed through and crashed the caller at
    `v.get("mountPath")` — on EVERY Read, EVERY Skill load and EVERY prompt. This file is
    written by external mount tooling and is the piece of state most likely to drift across
    versions; it was the only crash in 84 state-corruption cases. A guard that dies on its
    own optional config is not optional."""
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".nexus-mcp",
                               "workspace-mounts.json")) as fh:
            raw = json.load(fh)
    except Exception:
        return {}
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        return {}
    return {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if isinstance(v, dict)}


_SCOPE = None


def _scope():
    """The acting (orgId, profile), resolved ONCE per process.

    The registry is keyed by the org/profile that was acting at mount time (CLI #2486 /
    NEX-2360), so a slug alone no longer identifies a row: two orgs may hold
    `general-context` at once, and the one this session must read is the one the CLI
    would act as. Resolution is `hc.acting_scope()`; every registry read below goes
    through `hc.mount_record`/`hc.mount_path` with this scope, which also keeps a legacy
    bare-slug registry resolving. One process = one prompt/tool event, so caching costs
    nothing and cannot go stale mid-run."""
    global _SCOPE
    if _SCOPE is None:
        _SCOPE = hc.acting_scope()
    return _SCOPE


def _probe_mount(mounts, slug, timeout=2):
    """Liveness probe: mountPath recorded AND the dir lists non-empty; an EMPTY listing
    counts as not-live (the read-side wedge signature: the server may hold content the
    mount does not show). Pure state logic.

    W46-hookfix: the probe runs in a DETACHED child polled to a deadline and ABANDONED on
    miss. The prior SIGALRM guard could not actually bound a wedged WebDAV mount: a
    filesystem call stuck in uninterruptible I/O (D state) does not receive the alarm
    until the syscall returns — the "timeout-guarded" probe hung for the harness's whole
    budget, which is one of the mechanisms behind "UserPromptSubmit hook timed out after
    10s". Never `wait()` on the child past the deadline: a D-state child ignores even
    SIGKILL until its I/O returns, and waiting on it re-creates the hang."""
    mp = hc.mount_path(mounts, slug, _scope())
    if not mp:
        return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.Popen(["/bin/ls", os.path.expanduser(mp)],
                             stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                             start_new_session=True)
        deadline = time.time() + timeout
        while time.time() < deadline:
            if p.poll() is not None:
                if p.returncode != 0:
                    return None
                out = p.stdout.read() if p.stdout else b""
                return mp if out.strip() else None
            time.sleep(0.02)
        try:
            p.kill()
        except Exception:
            pass   # fail-open: best-effort kill; a D-state child is abandoned, never waited on
        return None
    except Exception:
        return None

# (W10: _mount_path/_r41_matches/_agent_build_prompt removed — the R41 pre-grep and
# the ARCH inject triggered on prompt WORDING; hooks are purely logic. The KB-first
# discovery obligation lives in doctrine (R#41/R#47/R#48); the AW4 orientation below
# is event-keyed and carries the precedent framing factually.)


# W46-hookfix: the INDEX cache. The prompt path only ever READS this file; the fetch
# chain (node-CLI start + API + signed-URL download, seconds each) runs in a DETACHED
# refresher. Resolved at module import — every hook invocation is a fresh process, so
# a redirected HOME in a test subprocess resolves correctly.
_GC_CACHE_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".nexus-mcp", "gc-index-cache")
_GC_CACHE = os.path.join(_GC_CACHE_DIR, "general-context.md")
_GC_CACHE_TTL = 24 * 3600          # a stale org map still orients; refresh in background


def _gc_ident(mounts):
    """The IDENTITY of the mounted general-context: workspaceId, else mountPath, else the
    bare slug. Never empty when general-context is present — an empty identity would collapse
    every org onto one key. The org-switch procedure is "unmount + remount every slug", which
    changes BOTH workspaceId and mountPath (the org folder is part of the path), so either
    field discriminates; workspaceId is preferred because it is the server's own id."""
    gc = hc.mount_record(mounts, "general-context", _scope())
    if not isinstance(gc, dict):
        return ""
    return str(gc.get("workspaceId") or gc.get("mountPath") or "general-context")


def _gc_cache_path(mounts):
    """The INDEX cache file for THIS org. Org-scoped, with NO fallback to the legacy
    single-file name: after a switch the legacy file holds the PREVIOUS org's map, and
    injecting it verbatim as the new org's map is worse than injecting nothing. A miss costs
    one turn — the detached refresher writes the org's own file and the next prompt injects."""
    ident = _gc_ident(mounts)
    if not ident:
        return _GC_CACHE
    return os.path.join(_GC_CACHE_DIR,
                        "general-context-%s.md"
                        % hashlib.sha1(ident.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10])

_GC_REFRESH_DEBOUNCE = 300         # one refresh request per 5 min, however many prompts


def _spawn_gc_refresh():
    """Request an INDEX refresh: stamp the request (the test observable + the debounce),
    then fire `--refresh-gc-index` DETACHED and return immediately (~10 ms).

    W46-hookfix: the fetch used to run inline on the boundary prompt — 6-8s legitimate
    worst case against a 10s harness budget, and a run killed mid-fetch left the once-flag
    unwritten, so every subsequent prompt retried the whole chain: the timeout storm the
    owner reported as constant. Off-path, its cost is invisible and a failure costs one
    missing org map, never a dead hook."""
    try:
        os.makedirs(_GC_CACHE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
        stamp = os.path.join(_GC_CACHE_DIR, ".refresh-requested")
        try:
            if time.time() - os.path.getmtime(stamp) < _GC_REFRESH_DEBOUNCE:
                return
        except OSError:
            pass
        with open(stamp, "w") as fh:
            fh.write(str(int(time.time())))
        if os.environ.get("NEXUS_AWARENESS_NO_SPAWN"):
            return   # tests assert the REQUEST stamp; the exec itself is suppressed
        subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, os.path.abspath(__file__), "--refresh-gc-index"],
                         stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                         stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: no refresher means no INDEX this round, never a dead hook


def _refresh_gc_index_cli():
    """The detached refresher body (`--refresh-gc-index`): fetch INDEX.md and write the
    cache ATOMICALLY (tmp + rename) so a prompt-path read never sees a torn file. Latency
    here costs nothing — nothing waits on this process."""
    _m = _mounts()
    txt = _fetch_gc_index(_m, timeout=45)
    if txt:
        os.makedirs(_GC_CACHE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
        dest = _gc_cache_path(_m)
        tmp = dest + ".tmp.%d" % os.getpid()
        with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(txt)
        os.replace(tmp, dest)


def _fetch_gc_index(mounts, timeout=4):
    """AW4b (W15.2): best-effort fetch of the general-context INDEX.md — VERBATIM, in FULL,
    STRUCTURE-AGNOSTIC (never parse or trim: a workspace's INDEX shape varies per org, so only
    the whole file generalises). Mount read if the mount is live; else REST (ambient active
    profile — the same authority the conv-start boundary read trusts). Bounded by an alarm; any
    failure → None (AW4 degrades to orientation-only, never crashes). general-context ONLY —
    community KBs stay on-demand (fastpack / the retriever fetch them when a build-shaped ask
    fires)."""
    def _alarm(_s, _f):
        raise TimeoutError()
    old = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, _alarm)
    signal.alarm(timeout)
    try:
        mp = hc.mount_path(mounts, "general-context", _scope())
        if mp:
            p = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(mp), "INDEX.md")
            if os.path.isfile(p):
                with open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
                    txt = fh.read()
                if txt.strip():
                    return txt
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["nexus", "api", "GET",
             "/workspaces/general-context/file?path=INDEX.md", "--json"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        out = r.stdout or ""
        i = out.find("{")
        if i < 0:
            return None
        url = hc.dsub(json.loads(out[i:]), "data").get("url", "")
        if not url.startswith("http"):
            return None
        # W28/F06: imported HERE, not at module scope. This adapter is wired to four
        # events (PreToolUse Read, PreToolUse Skill, PostToolUse Read, UserPromptSubmit),
        # so it is the layer's most-invoked program — and `urllib.request` costs about as
        # much as the whole bare interpreter (measured interleaved: 29.3 ms baseline vs
        # 58.1 ms with the import). It is reachable at most ONCE per session, inside the
        # boundary-inject branch, and the mount path is tried first so it often never runs
        # at all. Every file the assistant reads was paying for it twice. Measured
        # end-to-end: the adapter halves, and a realistic 26-invocation turn drops by
        # ~0.9 s of hook wall-time, with outputs identical.
        import urllib.request
        body = urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=timeout).read()
        if b"NoSuchKey" in body[:300] or body[:100].lstrip().startswith(b"<?xml"):
            return None
        txt = body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        return txt if txt.strip() else None
    except Exception:
        return None
    finally:
        signal.alarm(0)
        signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old)


def handle_user_prompt(data):
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    mounts = _mounts()
    parts = []

    # W43 — the OFF switch for knowledge filing.
    #
    # R#34 documents a per-conversation hold ("a scoped 'not now' = a SESSION hold (sid
    # flag)") and `nexus-lifecycle.py` READS `consolidation_hold` in four places, but
    # nothing in the estate ever WROTE it. The read side was fully built, so the control
    # looked implemented while an instruction to stop filing changed no state anywhere.
    #
    # The estate previously declared that no predicate may set it, on the ground that "a
    # hold is a language event and hooks do not read wording". That ban is kept for
    # INFERENCE and lifted here for one narrow case, with the owner's explicit decision
    # (W43): this is equality against a RESERVED CONTROL TOKEN that must be the entire
    # message — the same class as a slash command — so nothing is being interpreted. The
    # alternative left the switch depending on the agent noticing and acting, which is the
    # exact dependency that produced the failure this cycle exists to fix.
    #
    # Deliberately narrow: this function inspects the prompt for nothing else, and the
    # tokens are fixed strings, never patterns.
    try:
        _tok = hc.s(data.get("prompt", "")).strip().lower().strip(".!")
        if _tok in ("consolidation off", "off consolidation"):
            sc.set_flag(sid, "consolidation_hold")
            sc.log_decision(sid, "UserPromptSubmit", "R34-HOLD", "set-by-user")
            parts.append("[R34-HOLD] State change: knowledge filing is now OFF for this "
                         "conversation (session flag set). It stays off until the owner "
                         "sends 'consolidation on'. It binds this conversation only and "
                         "never carries to another.")
        elif _tok in ("consolidation on", "on consolidation"):
            sc.clear(sid, "consolidation_hold")
            sc.log_decision(sid, "UserPromptSubmit", "R34-HOLD", "cleared-by-user")
            parts.append("[R34-HOLD] State change: knowledge filing is back ON for this "
                         "conversation (session flag cleared).")
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: an advisory state token must never take the whole adapter down

    # AW4 — org-context orientation, once per session (EVENT-keyed: first prompt).
    # Factual project info (NOT an imperative/out-of-band command — command-framing
    # trips the prompt-injection defense and gets surfaced to the user; see hooks
    # docs). The behavioural rules live in CLAUDE.md, not here. Two variants by
    # mount STATE — pure logic, no prompt inspection.
    _PRECEDENT = (
        " Prior deliverables and playbooks for recurring activity classes (workshops, "
        "decks, campaigns, reports) live there too: a request to produce one has "
        "same-class precedent in the workspace as well as subject-entity context.")
    # W28/F19: the once-flag used to be consumed HERE, before any variant was chosen, so
    # a session that started with no `workspace-mounts.json` emitted nothing AND could
    # never emit again — mounting a workspace mid-session bought silence. That is the
    # state of every FRESH INSTALL: the mounts file is created by `nexus workspace mount`,
    # so a user who has not yet mounted gets no boundary orientation and no INDEX at all.
    # The flag now guards only the EMISSION (consumed inside `if parts:` below). Not
    # "drop the once-guard": AW4b injects the whole INDEX verbatim and must not repeat
    # per turn.
    # W46-hookfix: the once-flag is written FIRST, before any probe or I/O — via
    # `once_strict`, which is an atomic test-and-set. The old order (flag consumed after
    # the work) meant a run killed at the harness timeout retried the whole boundary
    # chain on every later prompt: the measured storm behind "timed out after 10s —
    # output discarded" recurring for a session's whole life. The `mounts` precondition
    # preserves W28/F19: with no mounts file the flag stays unconsumed, so mounting
    # mid-session still gets its orientation on the next prompt.
    # W48/V3 — THE FLAG IS KEYED ON THE MOUNT SET, not on "any mounts file exists".
    # The `mounts` precondition above preserved W28/F19 only for a session with NO mounts
    # file at all. Driven across three trees: with `{"tools": …}` mounted at turn 1 the flag
    # was consumed, general-context mounted mid-session, and the session then got NO org
    # orientation and no INDEX for its ENTIRE life. That is the W28/F19 defect narrowed from
    # "fresh install" to "any non-gc mount present" — a state `test_awareness_boundary.py`
    # never covered, because its fixture only ever writes `{"general-context": …}` or `{}`.
    #
    # Keying on the sorted slug set preserves BOTH properties at once: a run killed at the
    # harness timeout retries nothing (same mount set → same key → still consumed, so the
    # storm fix stands), while MOUNTING SOMETHING NEW mints a fresh key and the orientation
    # lands on the next prompt. It reads only the already-parsed map — no probe, no I/O —
    # so it runs before the work exactly as the storm fix requires.
    # W48/D6 — THE KEY IS THE IDENTITY OF general-context, NOT THE MOUNT SET.
    # A slug-set hash is both wider and narrower than the intent: an ORG SWITCH is
    # "unmount + remount every slug", which leaves the slug set IDENTICAL, so the new org's
    # orientation and INDEX were suppressed for the session's whole life; and unmounting any
    # UNRELATED slug shrinks the set, minting a fresh key and re-emitting the whole block.
    # Keying on the gc workspaceId (mountPath as the fallback for older mount tooling) makes
    # B4 and B5 stop competing: only a DIFFERENT general-context mints a new key.
    # The guard is the gc ENTRY, not `mounts`: a state that CANNOT emit (no gc mounted) must
    # not consume a flag — that is W28/F19's rule, applied to the new key.
    # Still pure dict reads, no probe, no I/O, so the storm fix's ordering stands (B3).
    # CLI #2486 / NEX-2360: the general-context row is no longer under a top-level key
    # that is just the slug — the registry keys on `<kind>:<id>|<slug>`, so indexing the
    # map by the bare slug resolved None on every post-rekey machine and this whole block
    # went silent while a workspace WAS mounted.
    # `hc.mount_record` scans the rows' own `slug` (present in both formats) and picks the
    # ACTING org's, so it reads a legacy, a rekeyed and a mixed registry alike.
    _gc = hc.mount_record(mounts, "general-context", _scope())
    _gc = _gc if isinstance(_gc, dict) else None
    _gcid = _gc_ident(mounts)
    _mkey = "boundary_inject_%s" % hashlib.sha1(_gcid.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10]
    if _gc is not None and sc.once_strict(sid, _mkey):
        if os.environ.get("NEXUS_AWARENESS_TEST_HOLD"):
            # T3b fault-injection point: the kill window between the flag write and the
            # boundary work is unreachable by any payload — the storm contract test
            # SIGKILLs inside this hold and asserts the flag survived. No-op in production.
            time.sleep(float(os.environ["NEXUS_AWARENESS_TEST_HOLD"]))
        if _probe_mount(mounts, "general-context"):
            parts.append(
                "An organisation workspace (general-context) is active for this session. "
                "The organisation's canonical context (positioning, customers, commercial "
                "terms, people) lives there and is retrieved via the knowledge-retriever "
                "rather than recalled from memory (the conv-start boundary read — INDEX.md "
                "+ _meta/IDENTITY.md — is still the session's OWN full read; the retriever "
                "supplements it, never substitutes); its folder structure varies per "
                "organisation. Questions about the Nexus product are answered from built-in "
                "product knowledge; questions about the organisation are grounded in "
                "retrieved general-context." + _PRECEDENT)
        elif _gc is not None:
            parts.append(
                "An organisation workspace (general-context) is registered for this session, "
                "but its local mount is not readable right now (unmounted, wedged, or listing "
                "empty). The canonical context — positioning, customers, commercial terms, "
                "people — is still live server-side and is read via REST (`nexus api GET "
                "\"/workspaces/<slug>/files?path=<dir>\"` for listings, `…/file?path=<p>` for "
                "content); zero-hit scans over the unreadable mount are not evidence of "
                "absence. The conv-start boundary read (INDEX.md + _meta/IDENTITY.md, read "
                "FULLY) still runs — over these REST paths — before any org entity is acted "
                "on; the retriever supplements it, never substitutes." + _PRECEDENT)

    # AW4b (W46-hookfix, was W15.2) — inject the general-context INDEX.md VERBATIM as the
    # org map, from the LOCAL CACHE only, on the first prompt where the cache exists (its
    # own once-flag, decoupled from the boundary turn: a session whose cache arrives on
    # prompt 2 still gets its map). Structure-agnostic (whole file, never trimmed).
    # Failure-silent: no cache → orientation-only + a detached refresh request. The fetch
    # NEVER runs on the prompt path. `once_strict` (fail-closed), not `once`: this injects
    # the whole file verbatim, and repeating it per turn on an unwritable store would
    # flood the context (W28/F14's argued exception, preserved).
    # W48/D6: the flag AND the cache file are ORG-SCOPED. A single `general-context.md`
    # cache with a fixed flag meant that after an org switch the session injected the
    # PREVIOUS org's INDEX, labelled as the new one's — worse than injecting nothing.
    _ipath = _gc_cache_path(mounts)
    if _gc is not None and not sc.is_set(sid, "boundary_index_" + _mkey[-10:]):
        idx = None
        try:
            if os.path.isfile(_ipath):
                with open(_ipath, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
                    idx = fh.read()
        except Exception:
            idx = None
        if idx and idx.strip():
            if sc.once_strict(sid, "boundary_index_" + _mkey[-10:]):
                parts.append(
                    "The general-context INDEX.md follows verbatim (from the local cache; "
                    "a background refresher keeps it current, so a very recent edit may "
                    "not show yet) — the org's own map (its structure varies per org; "
                    "navigate the org's context FROM it). It orients; it is not the source "
                    "you answer org claims from (an org claim → the knowledge-retriever). "
                    "Community KBs (tools/systems/use-cases) are NOT loaded here — "
                    "fastpack / the retriever pull them on demand when a build-shaped ask "
                    "fires.\n\n===== general-context/INDEX.md =====\n" + idx)
            try:
                if time.time() - os.path.getmtime(_ipath) > _GC_CACHE_TTL:
                    _spawn_gc_refresh()
            except Exception:
                pass   # fail-open: a stat/refresh miss costs one stale map, never a dead hook
        else:
            _spawn_gc_refresh()

    # PC-CANON resume re-emit (W18): a compaction stores the re-read obligation
    # (lifecycle PreCompact); the first prompt AFTER the seam re-emits it ONCE as
    # live context, then clears. Pure state — no prompt inspection.
    try:
        # W32/G05: read-and-clear ATOMICALLY — an unlocked get/put pair raced the
        # producer and resurrected advisories that had already been delivered.
        pend = sc.take(sid, "pc-canon-pending")
    except Exception:
        pend = None
    # W28/F19: keyed per COMPACTION EPOCH, not per session. `pc_epoch` exists for exactly
    # this and is already used that way for the LEAK warn. Once-per-session meant that in
    # a long session — the sessions that compact most — the R#13 re-read obligation was
    # GUARANTEED absent after the first compaction. Measured live: one session held a
    # 669-character obligation that could never be delivered.
    if pend and sc.once(sid, "pc_canon_reemit_%d" % sc.pc_epoch(sid)):
        parts.append("[PC-CANON] A compaction occurred; prior reads are VOID (R#13). "
                     "Re-read before resuming their task-type:\n" + str(pend))
        try:
            pass   # already cleared by `take` under the lock
        except Exception:
            pass   # fail-open: clearing a consumed flag; a stale one re-emits once, harmless

    # W21 stop-pending delivery: turn-end nudges queued by the lifecycle hook
    # (the Stop channel renders user-visibly; this one does not — AW4-proven).
    try:
        spend = sc.take(sid, "stop-pending")
    except Exception:
        spend = None
    if spend:
        # W28/E13-Q5: this join sat outside any `try`, so ONE non-string element raised
        # TypeError out of main() — rc=1, and the whole UserPromptSubmit hook died: the AW4
        # org orientation, the verbatim general-context INDEX injection and the PC-CANON
        # re-read obligation all lost with it. Worse, the clear below never ran, so it
        # recurred every turn for the life of the session. `map(str, …)` inside the guard.
        #
        # And ONE NUDGE PER LINE, not two spaces. Measured on an armed fixture: a realistic
        # busy turn delivers 11 advisories / 3,157 characters as a single unbroken paragraph
        # with zero newlines — no header, no severity, no ordering. An item that genuinely
        # matters starts at character 621 of a grey wall, formatted identically to ten
        # default-quiet self-checks, seven of which carry their own "ignore if…" clause. The
        # separator is the cheapest available fix and it is one character.
        try:
            _lines = [str(x) for x in (spend if isinstance(spend, list) else [spend])]
            parts.append("\n".join(_lines))
        except Exception:
            pass   # fail-open: an undeliverable queue must not take the whole hook with it
        try:
            pass   # already cleared by `take` under the lock
        except Exception:
            pass   # fail-open: same as above — an uncleared queue repeats a nudge, never blocks

    if parts:
        _emit("UserPromptSubmit", "\n\n".join(parts))
    sys.exit(0)


def handle_skill_pre(data):
    # W15 (AW5 root cause): the Skill tool had NO matcher, so a skill LOADED via
    # Skill(name) was invisible to the read-log and AW5 fired on the very skill in
    # use. A Skill invocation IS the governing-doc read — log the slug. Pure event.
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    slug = ((hc.d(data.get("tool_input"))).get("skill") or "").strip()
    if sid and slug:
        sc.log(sid, "read-log", "skill:" + slug.split(":")[-1])

        # entry gate once per session at the moment the skill enters context (the
        # measured miss: engine in context, never entered). Pure event, no wording.
        if slug.split(":")[-1] == "nexus-app-builder" and sc.once(sid, "aw_engine_gate"):
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PreToolUse", "AW-ENGINE", "nudge")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",

                    "[AW-ENGINE] app-builder loaded — ENTRY GATE: the crew ENGINE is the "
                    "DEFAULT for any human-facing (archetype-3) build — P1 closes by "
                    "dispatching app-architect; the platform-primitive track (PA, AI "
                    "tasks, workflows, OAuth) runs in PARALLEL beside it. Solo building "
                    "needs the user's disclosed go (mark it: NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1)."}}))
