                 "list. Enumerate what TO delete instead: match an explicit "
                 "pattern (e.g. `for d in ~/path/wt-*`), echo the matched list "
                 "first, then delete exactly that. A deliberate everything-except "
                 "sweep re-issues the SAME command with NEXUS_RM_ACK=1.", "RM1")

    # RM1B (W22): the same everything-except inversion, worktree/branch family —
    # `git worktree remove --force` or `git branch -D` driven by a loop (glob OR
    # command-substitution list) plus an exclude/keep-list signal. One omission on
    # the keep-list force-removes a live lane's worktree or deletes its branch
    # (probe-proven gap: the RM1 arm sees only `rm -rf`). ALL THREE signals must
    # be present; a plain single remove or an allowlist loop never fires. A
    # deliberate sweep re-issues with NEXUS_RM_ACK=1. Observe-gated by
    # .rm1b-observe (log-only) until the W22 battery + one live fire clear it.
    _WTBR_RE = re.compile(
        r"\bgit\s+worktree\s+remove\s+(?:[^\n;|&]*\s)?(?:--force|-f)\b"
        r"|\bgit\s+branch\s+-D\b")
    if (_WTBR_RE.search(kw) and not hc.ack_present(cmd, "NEXUS_RM_ACK=1")   # W40: act view
            and re.search(r"\bfor\s+\w+\s+in\b[^\n;]*(\*|\$\()", kw)
            and _EXCL_RE.search(kw)):
        _rm1b_obs = os.path.exists(os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".rm1b-observe"))
        # W28/F05: the OBSERVE path logs here; the ENFORCE path lets `emit` do it.
        # Logging in both places wrote TWO rows per enforce event against ONE per
        # observe event, so any raw count comparison across the two modes was 2x
        # wrong IN FAVOUR OF ENFORCE — and a promotion decision reads exactly that
        # comparison. One event, one row, whichever mode is on.
        if _rm1b_obs:
            sc.log_decision(data.get("session_id"), "fs-firewall", "RM1B",
                            "would-deny")
        if not _rm1b_obs:
            emit("deny", "[RM1B] Worktree/branch teardown written as everything-"
                 "except-a-keep-list. Enumerate what TO delete: list the exact "
                 "worktrees/branches first (echo them), then remove each named "
                 "target — one enumerated teardown at a time, never a keep-list "
                 "sweep. A deliberate sweep re-issues the SAME command with "
                 "NEXUS_RM_ACK=1.", "RM1B")

    # WSW — a mutating Bash op (cp/mv/sed -i/>>/tee/mkdir/rm…) targeting a workspace
    # MOUNT path: deny + redirect to server-side WebDAV (mount writes wedge). Reads
    # (cat/ls/grep — not MUT/REDIR) are unaffected; `nexus api`/curl to /api/dav
    # carry the slug, not the mount path, so they are not caught here.
    # W10 precision: (a) network verbs (curl/wget/fetch) write ONLY via their output
    # flags — URLs and `@file` upload sources are read args, and every-token scanning
    # denied pure reads; (b) redirect DETECTION runs on a position-preserving MASK of
    # quoted strings + heredoc bodies (an in-quote `->` in a jq format string or a
    # `len(x)>3000` in an inline script is content, not a redirect), with the TARGET
    # extracted from the raw command at the matched offset so quoted targets still count.
    _mroots = _mount_roots()
    # W28/F09 — ONE target-based check replaces three token scans (the MUT_NONNET_RE loop, the
    # NET_RE output-flag loop and the standalone redirect scan). `write_targets` returns None for
    # any shape it cannot resolve, and None routes to `norms` — the broad every-token set, i.e.
    # exactly today's behaviour — so this can only be QUIETER, never weaker.
    #
    # The gate is now just "are there mounts", not "does a mutating verb appear": a pure read
    # returns [] instead of being token-scanned, and per-verb destination semantics let
    # `unzip -d`, `tar -xC` and `git clone <dir>` be covered at all. Widening the OLD scan to
    # those verbs was declined precisely because it would have worsened the false positives.
    if _mroots:
        try:
            _wt = write_targets(HEREDOC_RE.sub(" ", cmd), cwd)
        except Exception:
            _wt = None         # unparseable quoting -> broad set, i.e. fail toward denying
        for t in (norms if _wt is None else [norm(c, cwd) for c in _wt]):
            if any(under(t, r) for r in _mroots):
                emit("deny", WSW_MSG, "WSW")

    # W48/MECH-2 — THE DESTRUCTIVE-ACT GUARD. Position has been wrong twice, in opposite
    # directions, and both failures were silent.
    #
    # TOO DEEP (first draft): the call sat inside `if is_recursive_force_rm(kw) or
    # is_recursive_rm(kw):`, so the guard chosen precisely because it catches
    # `python3 -c shutil.rmtree`, `perl rmtree`, `tar -xC`, `dd of=`, `mv` and `ln -sf`
    # never saw a single one of them. Driven from that position it scored 3/8 while the
    # module scored 18/18 — the corpus tests the MODULE, not the CALL SITE.
    #
    # TOO SHALLOW (second draft): moved to the top of the Bash path, above everything.
    # `emit()` terminates the adapter, so the guard's `ask` PRE-EMPTED the WSW arm's
    # `deny`, and four mount-write shapes that had always been blocked started passing:
    # `cp INTO mount`, `mkdir INTO mount`, `> mount/f`, `>> mount/f`. Driven on the WSW
    # suite's own fixture, all four returned `[DESTROY-BACKSTOP]` and no deny. A call site
    # is not only a COVERAGE knob; it is a PRECEDENCE declaration.
    #
    # HERE is the resolution: below WSW, so a mounted path is judged by the arm that owns
    # it, and still at main()'s top level, so the guard keeps full coverage of every other
    # Bash command. It parses INDEPENDENTLY of the segmenter above, so RM1/RM1B are
    # untouched — this file warns that changing that segmenter "silences three guards at
    # once".
    #
    # `None` means DEFER: exit silently, emit NO permissionDecision, leave the host's own
    # prompt alone. Wiring None to `allow` would suppress that prompt and void D9.
    if cmd:
        _dg = _destructive_guard()
        if _dg is not None:
            try:
                _d = _dg.hook_decision(
                    cmd, cwd=cwd, home=home,
                    project=os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or cwd,
                    mounts=_dg.live_mount_paths(home))
            except Exception:
                _d = None      # a guard that raises is a guard that is not running
            if _d:
                # W48/L18 — AN UNQUOTED PROTECTED ROOT CONTAINING A SPACE, named honestly.
                # The VERDICT here is right and is deliberately not changed: unquoted, a path
                # with a space really is several arguments, so the command does NOT target the
                # estate and `ask` is the correct answer. The MESSAGE was the defect. Measured:
                # `rm -rf <estate with a space>/.claude/hooks` produced "rm -r on
                # /Users/assem/Code/nexus/.claude — a config tree named `.claude` that is NOT
                # this estate". That path does not exist; the fragment after the space was
                # resolved against cwd, and the reader was told the target was something safe
                # somewhere else. A reason that invents a path and then reassures about it is
                # worse than no reason. Say what actually happened instead.
                _reason = _d[1]
                if _d[0] == "ask":
                    for _pr in ((home, "your home directory"),
                                (os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or "", "the project root"),
                                (cwd, "the working directory")):
                        _p0 = (_pr[0] or "").rstrip("/")
                        # W48/F2 — MEASURE the quoting, never assume it. The first version
                        # fired on `" " in cmd` (a space ANYWHERE) plus a bare substring test,
                        # so it told the reader a fully-QUOTED root was "NOT QUOTED" and to
                        # quote it — advice that cannot be followed, because the re-issued
                        # command is byte-identical and asks again. Inventing a quoting state
                        # is the same defect as the invented PATH this message replaced.
                        # `_unq` ALONE, never `_named`: the advisory's headline case is
                        # `rm -rf <root>/.claude/hooks`, where the root is a PREFIX, so the
                        # target test fails by design. What the message claims is only that
                        # the root appears unquoted and contains a space — exactly `_unq`.
                        _unq = _root_as_word(cmd or "", _p0)[1]
                        if _p0 and " " in _p0 and _unq:
                            _reason = (
                                "[DESTROY] This command names %s (`%s`), whose path CONTAINS A "
                                "SPACE, and it is NOT QUOTED — so the shell splits it into "
                                "several arguments and the delete will not do what you intended. "
                                "Quote the path and re-issue, then this guard can judge the real "
                                "target. (Any path the guard reports below was reconstructed "
                                "from the fragment after the space and may not exist.)\n\n"
                                % (_pr[1], _p0)) + _d[1]
                            break
                emit(_d[0], _reason, "PROT-ROOT", recoverable=(_d[0] == "ask"))

    # ---- DEFER to native permissions for sensitive operations ----
    if (SUDO_RE.search(kw) or CHOWNMOD_ROOT_RE.search(kw)
            or PIPE_SHELL_RE.search(kw) or SENSITIVE_RE.search(kw)):
        sys.exit(0)
    for t in norms:
        if any(under(t, s) for s in secret_dirs) or t in secret_files:
            sys.exit(0)
        if t in persist or any(under(t, p) for p in persist):
            sys.exit(0)

    # ---- scope: ALLOW clearly in-scope Nexus work; DEFER the rest ----
    if not (MUT_RE.search(kw) or REDIR_RE.search(kw)):
        sys.exit(0)
    if not norms:
        # W28/E01 — an EMPTY candidate set means "I could not tell what this touches", and
        # that inference must never become `allow`. It did: the loop below simply never ran
        # and the hook auto-approved, SUPPRESSING the native prompt for `bash -c 'rm -rf /'`,
        # `rm -rf "$(pwd)"`, `T=/; rm -rf "$T"` and a heredoc'd `csrutil disable`. Deferring
        # hands those to the native permission flow instead of green-lighting them.
        sys.exit(0)
    for t in norms:
        if t in SAFE_DEV or t.startswith("/dev/fd/"):
            continue
        if not any(under(t, w) for w in work):
            sys.exit(0)   # out-of-scope -> native acceptEdits prompt
    # W48/CONTAINMENT — a PROTECTED ROOT is never "in-scope work", whatever the verb.
    #
    # Measured, driven twice: `python3 -c "import shutil; shutil.rmtree('$HOME')"` and four
    # sibling spellings (`os.system('rm -rf $HOME')`, `perl rmtree`, `dd of=`, `ln -sf`)
    # reached THIS line and were auto-approved. `allow` SUPPRESSES the host's own permission
    # prompt, so the act proceeded with no human in the loop. The literal `rm -rf $HOME`
    # family is denied upstream at every spelling tried; the interpreter-wrapped family is
    # not, because the destructive guard's predicate returns None (defer) for it and defer
    # falls through to here.
    #
    # The file already states the principle, 24 lines above the guard call: "Wiring None to
    # `allow` would suppress that prompt and void D9." It is not wired that way — it happens
    # one arm later, which is why guarding only the direct path missed it.
    #
    # This is CONTAINMENT, not the fix. The predicate gap is a separate, larger piece of work
    # (a call-site corpus, not a module one). Here we only refuse to convert an abstention
    # into an approval when the target is a root whose loss is unrecoverable. Deferring hands
    # it to the native permission flow, which is what an abstaining guard is for.
    _local_src = [p for p in
                  ([home, os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or "", cwd]) if p]
    _mounts_resolved = _resolved_mount_roots()   # W49: cached — see _resolved_mount_roots
    _prot_src = _local_src + sorted(_mounts_resolved)
    _prot = ({os.path.realpath(p) for p in _local_src}
             | set(_mounts_resolved.values()))
    # W48 — the raw-text test needs the UNRESOLVED spellings too. First attempt compared only
    # `realpath` forms against the command text and matched NOTHING on a spaced path: on macOS
    # `/tmp` is a symlink to `/private/tmp`, so every realpath'd root differs from the string
    # the user actually typed. Driven proof of the miss: four wrapped deletes of a spaced
    # project root all returned `allow` under the realpath-only version. Both spellings, both
    # tested.
    _prot_txt = {p for p in _prot_src} | _prot \
        | {os.path.expanduser(p) for p in _prot_src}
    # W48/L18 — the RAW-TEXT test, and it is NOT redundant with the `norms` loop below.
    # `norms` derives from `candidates()`, whose ABS_RE character class `[\w.+@/-]` has NO
    # SPACE, so a path truncates at the first one and the guard then REASSEMBLES a plausible
    # path from the fragment: the real estate under ".../Claude Code/nexus/.claude" was
    # reported to the reader as "/Users/assem/Code/nexus/.claude — a config tree that is NOT
    # this estate", and downgraded from deny to ask. An invented path inside a user-facing
    # reason is worse than a miss: it actively tells the reader the target is safe. Measured:
    # 1 of 7 protected roots reachable; six live under a directory named "Claude Code".
    #
    # NOT fixed by widening ABS_RE: it feeds every other check in this adapter, and a space
    # is also an argument separator, so widening it swallows the next token on ordinary
    # commands — a wide blast radius for a narrow problem.
    #
    # The roots are KNOWN STRINGS. So ask "does the command NAME one", which needs no
    # extractor and cannot be truncated. Both loops run: this one catches spaced literals,
    # the `norms` loop below catches the `~` and `$HOME` spellings this one cannot see.
    # W48 — MATCH THE ROOT AS A TARGET, NOT AS A PREFIX. A bare substring test matched the
    # project root inside every path BENEATH it, so `echo hi > <project>/src/note.txt` — the
    # most ordinary edit there is — stopped being approved. Driven proof of the over-block:
    # three controls (a file write, `npm run build`, a `cat`) all fell to defer. The root
    # counts only when the path ENDS there: the next character must not continue the path.
    _raw = cmd or ""
    for _p in _prot_txt:
        if _root_as_word(_raw, _p)[0]:
            sys.exit(0)   # protected root NAMED AS A WORD -> native prompt, never a silent allow
    for t in norms:
        if os.path.realpath(t) in _prot:
            sys.exit(0)   # protected root -> native prompt, never a silent allow
    emit("allow", "In-scope Nexus filesystem operation.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Nexus ladder-gate ENGINE (plan Section 3).

ONE table-driven PreToolUse decision function: the gate matrix G1-G19 is DATA.
Reused by nexus-pretool.py (engine mode) as the SINGLE nudge emitter — stacked
hooks drop later additionalContext (proven live this session), so ALL nudge-class
logic (the new gates + the existing pretool CVE/kb/design/cred nudges) resolves
here and emits ONE merged nudge; fs-firewall stays separate (denies compose).

Properties (each maps to a measured finding in synthesis/test-results.md):
- single emitter: one deny (highest-priority) OR one merged nudge OR allow.
- re-fire-until-satisfied: every unsatisfied matching gate fires EVERY call (no once-flag).
- quote/heredoc strip: a command that merely MENTIONS a trigger is not gated.
- session-lineage read-log: subagents share the main read-log (correct).
- observe-mode: log_decision records would-block for new DENYs before enforce.
- fail-silent: any exception -> exit 0.

This module has NO side effects on import and is NOT wired into settings.json here;
it is unit-tested via subprocess (test_ladder_engine.py) first, then wired in
observe-mode per Section 8.4.
"""
import functools
import os
import re

# ---- prereq kinds (deterministic; never wording) -------------------------
# read(<substr>)     : sc.has(sid,"read-log", substr)         (awareness logs every Read)
# skill(<slug>)      : sc.has(sid,"read-log","skill:"+slug)   (awareness logs Skill loads)
# dispatch(<agent>)  : sc.has(sid,"dispatch-log", agent)
# exec(<marker>)     : sc.has(sid,"exec-log", marker)         (a node-test/execId this session)
# file(<abspath>)    : os.path.exists(path)                   (a receipt/SPEC/register file)
# register_clear()   : the standing-directive register has no unchecked "- [ ]" rows

DENY, NUDGE = "deny", "nudge"

# Each gate: (id, tier, trigger_regex, prereq_tuple, message)
# prereq_tuple = (kind, value) or ("any", [prereq, prereq]) — satisfied if ANY holds.
B = r"(^|[\s;&|(])"  # TOKEN-boundary prefix — NOT a command position (see CMDPOS)

# W28: `B` is a token boundary despite reading like a command boundary — it matches any
# whitespace-preceded word, so `grep -rn vite src/` and `grep -rn serve src/` were both
# DENIED for merely naming the thing. CMDPOS is the real anchor: start of command, after a
# shell separator, after a package runner, or the local bin path. Bare-word ARGUMENTS never
# match it, which is the whole point — a deny fires only when we are 100% sure, and someone
# searching for a word is not starting a dev server.
# W28/F11 — three shapes were not command positions, so every DENY gate simply missed them:
#   PORT=3000 npm run dev     a BARE env-assignment prefix (no `env` word in front of it)
#   ( npm run dev )           a subshell
#   { npm run dev; }          a group
# Measured: all three returned `-` while the bare form denied. A gate that a leading
# `PORT=3000` walks past is not a gate — and that prefix is the single most common way a dev
# server is actually started. Shell keywords are here for the same reason `_RM_PREFIX` needs
# them: `for f in …; do npm run dev; done` puts the gated command after `do`.
# W44: every unbounded `\S+`/`\w+` run inside a repeated group is BOUNDED. Measured through the
# real adapter: this pattern cost 7.2s of a 7.4s run on a 20,000-char command, and 40,000 chars
# passed a 30s timeout — on every Bash call, not just a hostile one. `\w+=\S+` on a long run of
# word characters with no `=` matches to the end, fails, and backtracks one character at a time;
# with the outer `+` and a scan from every start position that is O(n^2). The bounds sit far
# above anything real (shell variable names and flags are tens of characters), so nothing that
# matched before stops matching. Same class fixed in the same pass in `hook_core._CMD_SEP_RE`
# and `nexus-fs-firewall._WRITE_PREFIX` — three siblings, one defect.
CMDPOS = (r"(?:^|[;&|(){}]\s*|\n\s*|"
          r"(?:\bthen\b|\bdo\b|\belse\b|\belif\b)\s*|"
          r"(?:\w{1,128}=\S{1,1024}\s+)+|"
          r"(?:npx|bunx|pnpm|yarn|npm)\s+(?:dlx\s+|exec\s+|run\s+)?|"
          r"(?:nohup|sudo|command|env|timeout|doas|stdbuf|setsid)\s+"
          r"(?:\S{1,256}=\S{1,1024}\s+|-\S{1,256}\s+|\d{1,12}\s+)*|"
          r"node_modules/\.bin/)")

# Literal prefilters for expensive gate patterns (see evaluate() for the invariant:
# every branch of the gate's rx contains at least one of these literals verbatim).
_RX_PREFILTER = {
    "G19": ("npm", "pnpm", "yarn", "next", "vite", "http.server", "http-server", "serve"),
}

GATES = [
    # --- DENY (100%-sure would fail/orphan/ship-broken) ---
    ("G2", DENY, B + r"nexus\s+workflow\s+(create|publish)\b", ("read", "WORKFLOW_DESIGN_GUIDE"),
     "[G2] Workflow build blocked: read nexus-workflow-builder/WORKFLOW_DESIGN_GUIDE.md before creating or publishing a workflow — it defines the node types, handler rules, and branch model this build needs. Building blind ships a shell that passes `publish` and fails at runtime. Read it, then re-issue. A deliberate override re-issues the SAME command with NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1 (visible, logged)."),
    ("G3", DENY, B + r"nexus\s+workflow\s+publish\b", ("exec", "tested:"),
     "[G3] Untested publish blocked: no node-test or execution recorded for this workflow this session. A publish without a real run ships a thin shell. Run workflow test / node test, capture an execId, then publish. A deliberate override re-issues the SAME command with NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1 (visible, logged)."),
    ("G9", DENY, B + r"(nexus\s+)?vibe\s+app\s+create\b", ("file", "docs/PRD.md"),
     "[G9] App build blocked: an app starts at the PRD, not the scaffold. Load Skill(nexus-app-builder), write + sign off the PRD (pivotal loop, surfaces, base-decision), then scaffold. A surface whose backing primitive does not exist yet looks finished and does nothing. A deliberate override re-issues the SAME command with NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1 (visible, logged)."),
    ("G14", DENY, B + r"nexus\s+version\s+publish\b", ("exec", "eval:run"),
     "[G14] Publishing a behavioural change without an eval: run the nexus-evaluations regression (baseline->fix->postfix) and publish only on PASS — publish-stale runs the OLD nodes while a draft test passes. Eval, then publish. A deliberate override re-issues the SAME command with NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1 (visible, logged)."),
    # W28/F20 — G19 read the BINARY, not the SUBCOMMAND. `vite` at a command position denied
    # regardless of what vite was asked to DO, so `vite build` — how an app actually ships —
    # `vite --version` and `vite -v` were all blocked as "local dev-server". Measured live:
    # **55 of 115 G19 denies (48%) are `vite build`**. The message names a localhost server
    # that does not exist, on a DENY with no per-call override, which is the fastest way to
    # teach a reader that the gate is noise.
    #
    # `vite` now denies only on the SERVING subcommands (bare / dev / serve / preview), and the
    # npm arm's boundary tightens from `(dev|start)\b` to `(dev|start)(?![\w:.-])` so script
    # names that merely BEGIN with them — `dev:types`, `start:prod` — fall out. `\b` matched
    # before `:`, which is the same substring-not-act shape as `mkfs-report`.
    #
    # Not "require a --port signal": that fails open on `npm run dev`, where the port comes from
    # vite.config and never appears in the command — and that is the gate's primary case. The
    # subcommand is in the text; the port is not.
    ("G19", DENY, CMDPOS + r"(npm|pnpm|yarn)\s+(run\s+)?(dev|start)(?![\w:.-])|" + CMDPOS + r"next\s+dev\b|" + CMDPOS + r"vite(?:\s+(?:dev|serve|preview))?\s*(?:--(?:port|host|open)\b[^\n]*)?$|" + CMDPOS + r"vite\s+(?:dev|serve|preview)\b|" + CMDPOS + r"python3?\s+-m\s+http\.server\b|" + CMDPOS + r"http-server\b|" + CMDPOS + r"serve\b", ("skill", "nexus-app-builder"),
     "[G19] Local dev-server without the app-builder skill: load Skill(nexus-app-builder) + read its dev-loop, and clear the PRD gate, before starting a localhost server — an app build starts at the PRD, not `npm run dev` — built blind, the buttons do nothing and the environment is lost on restart. Load + PRD, then re-issue. A deliberate override re-issues the SAME command with NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1 (visible, logged)."),
    # --- NUDGE (re-fire-until-satisfied) ---
    ("G1", NUDGE, B + r"nexus\s+(workflow|agent(-tool)?|task)\s+(create|update)\b", ("skill_for_cmd", None),
     "[G1] About to mutate a resource whose governing skill is not loaded this session. Load the matching Skill first — it holds the body-shape, the typed CLI, and the gotchas this mutation needs; CRUD muscle-memory 404s or silently drops fields."),
    ("G6", NUDGE, B + r"nexus\s+(agent|workflow)\s+create\b", ("read", "NEEDS_ASSESSMENT"),
     "[G6] New build without a needs assessment: read nexus-getting-started/NEEDS_ASSESSMENT_GUIDE.md and run the Conversation Test first — the TRIGGER, not the word 'agent', decides workflow-vs-agent-vs-app."),
    ("G7", NUDGE, B + r"nexus\s+task\s+create\b", ("dispatch", "pa-prompt-author"),
     "[G7] Authoring a NEW prompt inline: dispatch pa-prompt-author (R#31) — it runs the PA conversation, self-resolves, and returns a validated prompt + spec. Skip only if the user pasted a complete prompt."),
    ("G4", NUDGE, B + r"nexus\s+(workflow|agent|task)\s+create\b", ("any", [("dispatch", "knowledge-retriever"), ("read", "use-cases")]),
     "[G4] Building without a precedent check: no knowledge-retriever dispatch or community use-cases read yet. Grep the use-cases / dispatch the retriever for a proven pattern before scaffolding this outcome — a matching pattern IS the starting files."),
    ("G8", NUDGE, B + r"nexus\s+external-tool\s+execute\b", ("shape", "*"),
     "[G8] Executing a tool whose SHAPE was never discovered this session: run `nexus tool get <id>` (params + result shape) and check the tools-KB entry for prior gotchas — copy the names from there, never guess (Pipedream prop names != external API names). A KB MISS counts: looking and finding nothing IS the discovery act, and it is recorded."),
    ("G13", NUDGE, B + r"nexus\s+(task\s+create|agent\s+update)\b", ("any", [("dispatch", "knowledge-retriever"), ("read", "general-context")]),
     "[G13] Authoring org-specific content ungrounded: each org element (identity/recipient/claim/brand/prices) is a discovery target — retrieve canonical general-context first, never write the org's self-description from memory. A NAMED source artifact must be REPRODUCED, not just fetched (R#47)."),
]

# G1 needs the governing skill per command family:
_SKILL_FOR = [
    (r"nexus\s+workflow\s+", "nexus-workflow-builder"),
    (r"nexus\s+agent(-tool)?\s+", "nexus-agent-management"),
    (r"nexus\s+task\s+", "nexus-skills-and-tasks"),
]


# A wrapper shell's quoted argument is CODE TO RUN, not a mention of it. Kept before the
# quote stripper removes it, then re-appended unquoted so the gates see it.
_WRAPPER_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:ba|z|da)?sh\s+(?:-[a-zA-Z]*c|-c)\s+('([^']*)'|\"([^\"]*)\")")


def _strip_quoted_spans(s):
    """Delegate to the ONE canonical escape-aware stripper in `hook_core`.

    Imported lazily so this module keeps its stated "no side effects on import" property.
    It is a delegate rather than a copy on purpose: this exact stripper had already existed
    in two places with the same non-escape-aware bug, and fixing one while leaving the other
    is the pattern the change log exists to stop. If the import fails the fallback is the
    UNSTRIPPED string, which can only make a gate MORE likely to fire — never less."""
    try:
        import sys as _s
        _s.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "lib"))
        import hook_core as _hc
        return _hc.strip_quoted_spans(s)
    except Exception:
        return s or ""


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)
def strip_quoted_and_heredoc(cmd):
    """Remove quoted strings + heredoc bodies so a command that MENTIONS a trigger
    (echo, a heredoc writing a script) is not gated — live-test finding.

    W46-hookfix, cost: memoized like `hook_core.strip_quoted_spans` — one-shot process,
    same string re-stripped per caller; identical output, built once.

    W28/E05 EXCEPTION: the payload of `sh -c '...'` / `bash -lc "..."` is the command being
    EXECUTED, not a mention of one, and stripping it hid the real thing — `sh -c 'npm run
    dev'` and `bash -c 'nexus workflow publish abc'` both walked through every gate. Wrapper
    payloads are extracted first and appended back so the gates match on what actually runs,
    while `echo 'npm run dev'` and `git commit -m '... npm run dev ...'` stay silent."""
    if not cmd:
        return ""
    payloads = [(m.group(2) or m.group(3) or "") for m in _WRAPPER_RE.finditer(cmd)]
    # drop heredoc bodies: <<'EOF' ... EOF  and  <<EOF ... EOF
    cmd = re.sub(r"<<-?\s*'?(\w+)'?.*?^\s*\1\b", " ", cmd, flags=re.S | re.M)
    cmd = _strip_quoted_spans(cmd)
    for p in payloads:
        if p.strip():
            cmd += " ; " + p          # `;` keeps it at a command position for CMDPOS
    return cmd


def _met(sc, sid, prereq, bare, cwd=""):
    kind, val = prereq
    if kind == "any":
        return any(_met(sc, sid, p, bare, cwd) for p in val)
    if kind == "read":
        return sc.has(sid, "read-log", val)
    if kind == "skill":
        return sc.has(sid, "read-log", "skill:" + val)
    if kind == "dispatch":
        return sc.has(sid, "dispatch-log", val)
    if kind == "exec":
        return sc.has(sid, "exec-log", val)
    if kind == "shape":
        # W24 G8 repair: the tool's SHAPE was actually discovered — either a
        # non-failing `tool get` (posttool `tool-shape-read`) or a KB lookup ACT whose
        # outcome was recorded, INCLUDING a miss (`<vendor>:miss`): not every tool is
        # in the community KB, and looking and finding nothing IS the discovery act.
        # Before this, G8's prereq was ("read","tool get") — a line NOTHING ever wrote,
        # so it fired 42 times across 4 sessions with 0 possible satisfactions.
        # PER-VENDOR, not session-global: discovering Gmail's shape says nothing about
        # Outlook's. The vendor comes from the command being gated (`bare`), so the
        # satisfying act must name the SAME vendor.
        try:
            import sys as _s
            _s.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "lib"))
            import hook_core as _hc
            vend = _hc.tool_vendor_from_cmd(bare)
        except Exception:
            vend = None
        if not vend:
            # vendor unresolvable (UUID-only execute): any shape act this session counts —
            # better than an unsatisfiable gate, which is the failure being repaired.
            return bool(sc.lines(sid, "tool-shape-read")) or bool(sc.lines(sid, "kb-lookup"))
        # W28/E05 — the symmetric case, and the one that made this gate UNSATISFIABLE the
        # moment per-vendor matching started working: the remediation this gate ASKS for is
        # `nexus tool get <toolId>`, whose command carries a UUID and no vendor, so posttool
        # records the wildcard `*`. Requiring an exact vendor match ignored it and the gate
        # re-fired forever after the user did exactly what it said. A gate whose own remedy
        # does not clear it is worse than one that is too broad.
        return (sc.has(sid, "tool-shape-read", vend)
                or sc.has(sid, "tool-shape-read", "*")
                or sc.has(sid, "kb-lookup", vend + ":"))
    if kind == "file":
        # W28/E05 — this `import os` was function-local, which makes `os` local to the WHOLE
        # function under Python's scoping rules. The `shape` branch above uses `os.path`
        # BEFORE this line runs, so it raised UnboundLocalError on every call, straight into
        # its own `except Exception: vend = None`. G8's per-vendor scoping was therefore dead:
        # a shape-read for one vendor silently satisfied an execute against another. The
        # module already imports `os` at the top; the local one only shadowed it.
        return os.path.exists(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(cwd or "."), val))
    if kind == "skill_for_cmd":
        for rx, slug in _SKILL_FOR:
            if re.search(rx, bare):
                return sc.has(sid, "read-log", "skill:" + slug)
        return True  # no known family -> nothing to enforce
    return True


# W28/E05 — `-h` matched ANYWHERE exempted EVERY deny gate, so `... && df -h` walked
# straight through. `df -h`, `du -h`, `ls -h`, `sort -h`, `free -h` are ordinary commands;
# that was a blanket bypass, not an override. `--help` is unambiguous anywhere. The short
# form counts only when the WHOLE command is a single `nexus …  -h` invocation.
# W28/F11 — `--help` matched ANYWHERE, so it exempted every DENY gate in the whole command.
# Measured, both ALLOWED:
#     npm run dev; nexus workflow --help
#     nexus workflow publish wf-1 && nexus task --help
# That is a bypass, not an override: appending a harmless help call disarmed the layer. The
# W28/E05 entry narrowed the SHORT form for exactly this reason and left the long one matching
# globally — the same fix, applied to one of two spellings.
#
# The carve-out is real and worth keeping: a help invocation CREATES NOTHING, and reading
# `--help` before first use is itself a standing rule, so denying it made the gate fight the
# behaviour it wants. But it must be scoped to the STATEMENT the help flag is in. Statements
# are split on separators outside quotes, and a gate is exempt only if the statement that
# matched it also carries the flag.
_HELP_RE = re.compile(r"(^|\s)--help(\s|$)")


def _help_statements(bare):
    """The statements of `bare` that carry a help flag — never the whole command."""
    return [st for st in re.split(r"(?:\|\||&&|[;&|\n])", bare)
            if _HELP_RE.search(st) or _SHORT_HELP_RE.match(st.strip())]


def _is_help_scoped(bare, matched_text):
    """True when EVERY statement able to match this gate also carries a help flag."""
    stmts = [st for st in re.split(r"(?:\|\||&&|[;&|\n])", bare) if st.strip()]
    hit = [st for st in stmts if matched_text and matched_text in st]
    if not hit:
        hit = stmts
    return all(_HELP_RE.search(st) or _SHORT_HELP_RE.match(st.strip()) for st in hit)
_SHORT_HELP_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*nexus\b[^|;&\n]*\s-h\s*$")


def evaluate(sc, sid, cmd, cwd=""):
    """Return every matching-but-UNSATISFIED gate (re-fire; no once-flag)."""
    bare = strip_quoted_and_heredoc(cmd)
    # W27: a help invocation CREATES NOTHING. `nexus vibe app create --help` prints usage
    # and exits, so denying it blocks the act of finding out how the command works — and
    # reading `--help` before first use is itself a standing rule, so the gate was fighting
    # the behaviour it wants. DENY gates only; a nudge on a help call is harmless context.
    hits = []
    # W46-hookfix, cost: literal prefilter. G19's CMDPOS prefix (the assignment-absorbing
    # alternation, inlined 7x) backtracks quadratically on pathological input — measured
    # 27.4s ALONE on a 200KB command. Every branch of a filtered gate's rx contains at
    # least one of its literals VERBATIM (that invariant is what licenses the skip — a
    # match without a literal is impossible by construction; keep the two in sync when
    # editing a filtered gate). A plain substring scan is C-fast, so absence of all
    # literals skips the expensive rx outright; presence runs it unchanged.
    _bare_low = bare.lower()
    for gid, tier, rx, prereq, msg in GATES:
        lits = _RX_PREFILTER.get(gid)
        if lits and not any(l in _bare_low for l in lits):
            continue
        m = re.search(rx, bare)
        if not m:
            continue
        # W28/F11 — the help carve-out is scoped to the STATEMENT that matched, not to the
        # whole command. Globally, appending a harmless help call disarmed every DENY gate:
        # `npm run dev; nexus workflow --help` and
        # `nexus workflow publish wf-1 && nexus task --help` were both ALLOWED. That is a
        # bypass, not an override — and it is the same defect W28/E05 fixed for the SHORT
        # form while leaving the long one matching anywhere.
        if tier == DENY and _is_help_scoped(bare, m.group(0)):
            continue
        if not _met(sc, sid, prereq, bare, cwd):
            hits.append((gid, tier, msg))
    return hits


def decide(sc, sid, cmd, cwd=""):
    """ONE output: (mode, payload). mode in {deny, nudge, allow}. A deliberate
    override (NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1 in the command) downgrades DENY gates to nudges —
    visible, logged, never silent."""
    hits = evaluate(sc, sid, cmd, cwd)
    denies = [h for h in hits if h[1] == DENY]
    # W28/E05 — this was matched against the RAW `cmd`, so writing documentation ABOUT the
    # override disabled the gate. It must come from the STRIPPED view: a real assignment,
    # never a quoted mention or a heredoc body.
    _bare = strip_quoted_and_heredoc(cmd or "")
    if denies and "NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1" in _bare:
        hits = [(g, NUDGE, m + " (override acknowledged)") for g, _, m in hits]
        denies = []
    if denies:
        gid, _, msg = denies[0]  # highest-priority = first in table order
        return ("deny", {"gid": gid, "message": msg})
    nudges = [h for h in hits if h[1] == NUDGE]
    if nudges:
        merged = " ".join(m for _, _, m in nudges)
        return ("nudge", {"gids": [g for g, _, _ in nudges], "message": merged})
    return ("allow", None)


def hook_output(mode, payload):
    """Render the PreToolUse hookSpecificOutput JSON for the engine's decision."""
    import json
    if mode == "deny":
        return json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": payload["message"]}})
    if mode == "nudge":
        return json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                "additionalContext": payload["message"]}})
    return ""  # allow = no output


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Standalone PreToolUse entrypoint (for when wired). Fail-silent.
    import sys, json, os
    try:
        sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "lib"))
        import session_cache as sc
        d = json.load(sys.stdin)
        if d.get("tool_name") == "Bash":
            sid = d.get("session_id")
            cmd = (d.get("tool_input") or {}).get("command", "")
            mode, payload = decide(sc, sid, cmd, d.get("cwd") or "")
            if mode != "allow":
                ids = payload.get("gid") or ",".join(payload.get("gids", []))
                try:
                    sc.log_decision(sid, "ladder-engine", ids, mode)
                except Exception:
                    pass   # fail-open: advisory logging must never suppress the verdict below
                # OBSERVE-MODE: if the marker file exists, log the decision but do NOT
                # emit (no deny/nudge) — a safe log-only rollout to confirm 0 false-positive
                # before enforcing (plan Section 8.4). Remove the marker to enforce.
                observe = os.path.exists(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".ladder-observe"))
                if not observe:
                    out = hook_output(mode, payload)
                    if out:
                        print(out)
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: the whole adapter is advisory — a broken import must not block the tool
    sys.exit(0)

         contract + inject the correct next action (eval+publish vs task-eval vs
         relay-questions).  (hook_core.subagent_stop_action)

         flag so the Stop reminder knows learnings were filed.
  • Stop → completion-scan (claimed done but no E2E ran) + a once-per-session
       consolidation reminder if resources were created and none was filed.
  • PreCompact → inject the session's created-resource IDs so they survive the
       compaction (context-loss survival).

Also appends each payload to ~/.nexus-mcp/hook-capture.jsonl while Stop/PreCompact
shapes are still being confirmed on live events. Failure-silent.

_DEPLOY_WATCH = os.path.join(

def _capture(data):

def _queue_pending(sid, msgs):
    """Queue this turn's advisories for invisible delivery on the NEXT UserPromptSubmit.

    W21 WHISPER: the terminal renders Stop-hook output as a visible "Stop hook feedback"
    line — the one channel the user could see, and the reason "the only hook that works" was
    the broken one. Advisory nudges are model-facing, so they are queued and the awareness
    adapter injects them invisibly next turn (pc-canon-pending pattern, delivery-proven).
    Fallback on a store failure: better loud than lost.

    W28/E13: extracted from the tail of the Stop branch so the STOP-WAKE block path can call
    it BEFORE it exits. Inline, it was unreachable whenever the turn was blocked — which is
    the turn that had the most to say. Idempotent-safe: called at most once per run.
    """
    if not msgs:
        return
    try:
        # W28/F14: a LOCKED read-modify-write. `put` is atomic, which prevents a torn
        # read but not a LOST UPDATE — measured 74.5% of queued advisories destroyed at 8
        # concurrent queuers, and 24% with only a Stop overlapping the next turn's
        # consume-and-clear. A lost entry is a turn-end advisory that never reaches the
        # model, with no trace anywhere.
        sc.update(sid, "stop-pending", lambda p: (p or []) + msgs, [])
    except Exception:

# W44: module scope so the BLOCKING Stop path and the non-blocking tail share ONE
# definition. A verification lane drove the split: the filter used to live only in the
# tail, below the blocking branch's own sys.exit, so a user-owned advisory firing on a
# turn that STOP-WAKE also blocked reached nobody — and the once-guarded ones

USER_FACING = ("[H2-TURN]", "[H2]", "[MAN1]", "[R34-ESC]", "[R34-HOLD]", "[STOP-WAKE]")


def _wake_level(slot, arm2_level, unbl):
    """W46/I1 — how long the same situation has gone unmoved, in whichever unit the arm has.

    Arm 1's signature is the unblocked id SET, so the slot counts wakes on an unchanged set.
    Arm 2 mints a fresh signature per work bucket with a budget of 1, so its slot is pinned at
    0 and cannot escalate; its equivalent is the BUCKET INDEX. Reading the wrong one for arm 2
    is what would have left it whispering forever with no wall behind it.
    """
    return slot if unbl else max(slot, arm2_level)


def _latest_ledger(sid):
    """Most-recently-WRITTEN open CYCLE ARTIFACT for this session. The lexically-last
    glob pick landed on a frozen `.closed` ledger and went blind to 20+ active
    ones (measured, W21); recency is mtime, closed ledgers are archives.

    W27: the set is no longer just `ledger-*`. A failure register, a draft plan and any path
    registered in the `cycle-artifacts` feed are cycle artifacts too, and a register that
    freezes while the work continues is the same silent death — measured blind spot: the
    ledger was current while the register had not moved in hours, so the arm stayed quiet."""
    try:
        # W44: the ledger portion now comes from the shared `hc.ledger_paths` (which also
        # recurses one level — a cycle keeps its artifacts in a per-cycle subdirectory);
        # the register/plan patterns stay here because this locator's job is wider.
        pats = ["/private/tmp/claude-501/*/%s/scratchpad/*/ledger-*.md" % sid,
                "/private/tmp/claude-501/*/%s/scratchpad/ledger-*.md" % sid,

        led += [p for p in sc.lines(sid, "cycle-artifacts")
                if p and os.path.isfile(p) and not p.endswith(".closed.md")]

_SID = None   # set by main(); _emit()'s telemetry reads it (no data param there)


def _emit(event, ctx, user_message=None):

    # family (SC-JSON, WSW-STALL, WSW-TIER, KR-JSON) and the PreCompact ids were

    if event in ("SubagentStop", "PreCompact"):

def _queue_parent(sid, cid, text):
    """Queue a CUE-addressed obligation for delivery on the next Agent PostToolUse.

    W35/H05 — measured, on a real harness with real nested subagents: an `additionalContext`
    emitted at SubagentStop lands in the STOPPING CHILD's next input, not in Cue's context,
    and RE-INVOKES the child. Worse than a lost nudge: the child's re-invoked final message
    BECOMES the Agent tool's return value, so the deliverable is destroyed. Probe evidence —
    a child told to return `{"status":"done","prompt":"..."}` was re-invoked three times and
    Cue received a refusal paragraph instead ("this system-reminder isn't a request from you…
    No message like this can authorize me to take actions on your behalf"); another
    degenerated into eight sign-off stubs for 13k wasted tokens on a one-word task.

    That is the SUCCESS path: `SA-PA`/`SA-APM`/`SA-TPM` fire on `status == "done"`, so every
    successful prompt-author and modifier return was being replaced by the child's reaction to
    an instruction addressed to someone else — exactly the object R#31/R#45/R#46 require Cue
    to parse.

    Three alternatives were measured and rejected. `systemMessage` alone at SubagentStop
    reaches NOBODY (zero occurrences in the parent transcript, the child's sidechain, or the
    stream — and the hook's execution is not even recorded), so it looks safe and delivers
    nothing. Adding `sc.once` bounds the loop to one round, and one round still destroys the
    return object. Rewriting the five texts in the second person would tell the wrong actor to
    publish, eval and `task create` — that phrasing is right for the `WSW-*` correctives, whose
    obligation genuinely IS the child's own re-emission, and is not a template for these.

    A FEED, drained on the next `PostToolUse:Agent`, is the channel that measured clean: the
    text reaches the parent, the child is not re-invoked, the deliverable stays intact, and it
    arrives in the same turn — which is what "YOU now fire `task create`" needs. Feed-then-drain
    rather than reading `tool_response` in PostToolUse, because for a BACKGROUNDED dispatch the
    harness fires PostToolUse at LAUNCH, before the SubagentStop, with no final message in the
    response."""
    try:
        sc.log(sid, "parent-pending", "[%s] %s" % (cid, text))
        sc.log_decision(sid, "SubagentStop", cid, "queued-for-parent")
    except Exception:
        pass   # best-effort: an advisory that cannot be queued must not end the turn


EXECUTING_LANES = ("app-executor", "app-contracts", "app-backend")

def _dispatch_rows(sid):
    """[(agent_type, epoch)] from the dispatch-log (W27 rows are 'type\tepoch'; W28 rows
    add a 3rd 'model' field; pre-W27 rows have no tab and read as epoch 0). Split, not
    partition — a 3-field row must still yield the epoch from field [1], never 'epoch\tmodel'."""
    out = []
    for ln in sc.lines(sid, "dispatch-log"):
        parts = str(ln).split("\t")
        t = parts[0].strip()
        e = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else ""
        try:
            out.append((t, int(e) if e else 0))
        except ValueError:

    return out

    out = []
    for ln in sc.lines(sid, "dispatch-log"):

def _app_repos(sid):
