    #
    # Drained here rather than read from `tool_response`, because for a BACKGROUNDED dispatch
    # the harness fires this event at LAUNCH — before the SubagentStop that queues the row — so
    # a response-reading implementation would find nothing. A queue survives that ordering: the
    # row is picked up by the next Agent PostToolUse, or by the Stop path.
    if data.get("tool_name") in ("Agent", "Task"):
        _sid = data.get("session_id")
        # ONE atomic read-and-clear. The first version read with `sc.lines` and cleared with
        # `sc.drop(sid, name)` — which takes a third `substr` argument, so it raised, the broad
        # `except` swallowed the TypeError, and every drain re-delivered the same advisory.
        _q = [str(x) for x in sc.take_lines(_sid, "parent-pending") if str(x).strip()]
        if _q:
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                "additionalContext": "\n".join(_q)}}))
        sys.exit(0)

    if data.get("tool_name") != "Bash":
        sys.exit(0)
    # W28/F19: coerce `cwd` ONCE, at the entry point, rather than at each of its ~12 uses.
    # E09 hardened the TOP-LEVEL payload type but did not carry the argument one level
    # down: with a VALID `tool_name` and `cwd` as an int, the adapter crashed in
    # `app_repo_ctx` on `git push` — and a crashed adapter is a guard that did not run
    # (law 4). `data.get("cwd") or ""` does not help, because a non-empty non-string is
    # truthy and passes straight through.
    if not isinstance(data.get("cwd"), str):
        data["cwd"] = ""
    _ti = data.get("tool_input")
    cmd = (_ti or {}).get("command", "") if isinstance(_ti, dict) else ""
    if not isinstance(cmd, str):
        # W28/E09: a non-string `command` (a dict from a misbehaving MCP server, or a
        # harness payload change) crashed the adapter on the first regex — and a crashed
        # firewall means the destructive-command guard did not run for that call. There
        # is nothing to inspect in a malformed command, so treat it as empty and let the
        # native permission layer decide.
        cmd = ""
    resp = data.get("tool_response")
    # EVERY text-bearing field, whatever the shape. SEC1 previously ran only when `resp` had
    # already been narrowed to a string, which required the dict to carry `stdout` — so a
    # credential arriving in `output` or `stderr` was never scanned (W28/E08).
    resp_text = _resp_text(resp)
    if isinstance(resp, dict) and "stdout" in resp:
        resp = resp.get("stdout")
    parsed = _extract_json(resp)  # may be None (non-JSON output) — hints still run

    # verify-log → lets the Stop completion-scan know an E2E actually ran.
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    # project-scoped state survives a new session_id / sandbox reset (C1).
    project = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or data.get("cwd")
    if sid and re.search(
            r"nexus\s+(execution\s+(get|poll|node-result|list)|task\s+execute|"
            r"emulator\s+send|workflow\s+test|agent-eval\s+run)", hc._strip(cmd)):
        # W32/G04: the ACT view, not the raw text. These two feeds SATISFY denies (G3/G14
        # gate a publish on a real run), so a heredoc documenting `nexus agent-eval run`
        # used to retire the gate without a run ever happening. A feed on the satisfying
        # side of a deny is the dangerous direction of the substring-vs-act class: a false
        # positive here does not add noise, it removes a block.
        sc.log(sid, "verify-log", cmd[:80])
        # W21 ladder feed: G3/G14 read exec-log — a prereq with no live feed is an
        # unsatisfiable deny (Issue F). `execution list` is a metadata read, not a run.
        if not re.search(r"execution\s+list\b", hc._strip(cmd)):
            sc.log(sid, "exec-log",
                   "eval:run" if "agent-eval" in hc._strip(cmd) else "tested:" + cmd[:60])
    # ── W24 FEEDS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Each pairs with a predicate shipped in the SAME cycle: a gate whose prereq has
    # no live writer is unsatisfiable by construction (G8: 42 fires, 0 satisfiable).
    if sid:
        try:
            _ok = not hc.response_failed(data.get("tool_response"))  # failed ⇒ satisfies nothing
            # D2/G8 — tool SHAPE was actually read (non-failing `tool get`).
            if _ok and re.search(r"nexus\s+(external-)?tool\s+get\b", hc._strip(cmd)):
                _v = hc.tool_vendor_from_cmd(cmd) or "*"
                sc.log(sid, "tool-shape-read", _v)
            # D5/EV2 — task-family lifecycle: an edit, and the eval that discharges it.
            _tle = hc.task_edit_events(cmd)
            if _tle and project:
                sc.plog(project, "task-lifecycle",
                        "%s %s %s %s" % (_tle[0], _tle[1] or "*", time.time(), sid or "-"))
            # D6 — PA thread status, so an idle turn can be told a thread is pollable.
            if re.search(r"nexus\s+prompt-assistant\s+(chat|get-thread)\b", hc._strip(cmd)):
                _st = re.search(r'"status"\s*:\s*"([a-z_]+)"', resp or "")
                _th = re.search(r'"threadId"\s*:\s*"([\w-]+)"', resp or "")
                if _st:
                    sc.log(sid, "pa-thread", "%s %s %s"
                           % (_th.group(1) if _th else "*", _st.group(1), time.time()))
        except Exception:
            pass   # fail-open: advisory prompt-compare arm

    # AM7 — Save-transform compare (R#20): after `agent update --prompt <file>`
    # (pretool cached the SENT stats), the next `agent get <id>` is diffed vs
    # what was sent; run/length growth = the server transformed it. Fail-open.
    _m_ag = re.search(r"(^|[\s;&|(])nexus\s+agent\s+get\s+(\S+)", hc._strip(cmd))
    if sid and _m_ag:
        _aid = _m_ag.group(2).strip("'\"")
        try:
            _sent = sc.get(sid, "prompt-sent-" + _aid)
        except Exception:
            _sent = None
        if _sent:
            _ptxt = parsed.get("prompt") if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None
            try:
                sc.put(sid, "prompt-sent-" + _aid, None)   # one-shot compare
            except Exception:
                pass   # fail-open: clearing a one-shot flag; a stale one self-clears next event
            _d = hc.save_transform_verdict(_sent, _ptxt) if _ptxt else None
            if _d:
                print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                    "additionalContext": f"[{_d[0]}] {_d[1]}"}}))
                sys.exit(0)

    # ws-listing-read → powers the retrieve-before-write gate: a workspace directory listing means the
    # agent localised the graph before writing. The legacy boolean drives the soft WSW-RET WARN (pretool);
    # the per-slug log drives the HARD deny in the firewall (a write to slug S is blocked until S was listed
    # this session). Capturing the slug lets a per-tier consolidation agent satisfy the gate per workspace.
    # W32/G04 — TWO parts, deliberately. This feed RETIRES the firewall's hard WSW-RET deny,
    # so a bare substring match on the raw command was a permanent, project-scoped deny
    # bypass: driven, `git commit -m 'doc: workspaces/use-cases/files listing recipe'`
    # flipped a blocked workspace write to allowed, with no read ever performed and no
    # expiry. The ACT (a read verb at a command position) is tested on the act view; the
    # SLUG is read from the RAW text because a real read spells the path inside quotes
    # (`nexus api GET "/workspaces/<slug>/files?path=x"`), which the act view strips.
    # Matching both on one view is what breaks this check in one direction or the other.
    _ws_act = re.search(r"(^|[\s;&|(])(nexus\s+api\s+GET|curl|http|wget)\b", hc._strip(cmd))
    _m_read = re.search(r"workspaces/([^\s/\"']+)/files", cmd) if _ws_act else None
    if sid and _m_read:
        sc.log(sid, "ws-listing-read", "Y")              # legacy boolean (WSW-RET soft warn)
        sc.log(sid, "ws-read-slugs", _m_read.group(1))   # per-slug (session)
    # PROJECT-scoped per-slug flag — powers the firewall HARD deny. Project-scoped (not session) so a read
    # by the knowledge-retriever subagent satisfies the gate for the spine/tier that writes the same slug
    # (subagents may carry distinct session_ids; the project is the shared key).
    if project and _m_read:
        sc.pset(project, sc.WSREAD_FLAG + _m_read.group(1))

    # grounding-log (G-ASSET support): record a general-context read via the BASH surface
    # (signed-URL curl / REST `nexus api`), so grounding is detected even when the mount is
    # wedged and reads bypass the Read tool. Pairs with nexus-pretool.g_asset (R#47).
    # W28/F19: match the STRIPPED command and only CONTENT reads. Writing *about*
    # general-context satisfied the R#47 gate: an `echo` naming the path, and
    # `mkdir -p /tmp/general-context/` both logged grounding. The likeliest case in
    # practice was a LISTING — `files?path=` returns filenames, not content, and it
    # silenced the gate. The bare `/general-context/` alternative is dropped for the same
    # reason. Not "sniff the response for markdown": a signed-URL fetch returns a URL and
    # not the body, so a content sniff reintroduces the false negative the failure-check
    # below was added to fix.
    if sid and re.search(r"workspaces/general-context/file\?|/api/dav/general-context/",
                         hc._strip(cmd)):
        # A FAILED read is NOT grounding (R#47/A7): a 404, timeout, or empty body must not
        # count. Only log when the response shows no failure marker and is non-empty.
        # W28/E08 — this used to re-bind `resp`, which is narrowed to a string near the top
        # of main() and read later by SEC1 as `isinstance(resp, str)`. Re-binding it to the
        # raw dict silently DISABLED the credential-leak check for exactly these commands:
        # workspace reads, the ones most likely to carry an API key inside a URL. Use a
        # local name; never clobber a variable another check depends on.
        _gc_resp = data.get("tool_response")
        rtext = _resp_text(_gc_resp)
        failed = (not rtext.strip()) or re.search(
            r"No such file|not found|Operation timed out|timed out|\b404\b|cannot access",
            rtext, re.I)
        if not failed:
            sc.log(sid, "read-log", "general-context (bash)")

    # EV1 feed (W18): agent-family lifecycle — publish events per agent id + eval-family
    # events (session-global), paired at Stop (published-without-eval warn). Separate log
    # from the workflow `lifecycle` feed so the LC gap check never sees agent ids.
    if project:
        ape = hc.agent_publish_events(cmd)
        if ape:
            sc.plog(project, "agent-lifecycle", f"{ape[0]} {ape[1] or '*'} {time.time()} {sid or '-'}")

    # (W21: the app_build/app_shipped project markers were RETIRED — a durable
    # project flag bled app gates into unrelated sessions (Issue E), and the ship
    # release was unreachable for full apps. App context is now read from the
    # repo the command touches: hook_core.app_repo_ctx.)
    # BLDF (W23): drop the REPO-scoped `.nexus-app` marker at the earliest observable
    # app moment — a successful `nexus vibe app create`, or a `git clone` of a vibe
    # forge repo. Repo-scoped (not project) so it cannot bleed (W21 rule); it makes
    # hook_core.app_repo_ctx true from minute zero, before any docs/ artifact.
    if sid:
        _rtxt = resp if isinstance(resp, str) else ""
        _is_create = re.search(r"nexus\s+vibe\s+app\s+create\b", hc._strip(cmd))
        # W28/F12: the host is `git.<org>.gpt.nexus`, not `git.nexus…`. The old pattern
        # matched only a literal `git.nexus` host, so it missed EVERY real Nexus org — the
        # one arm that puts the marker in a directory that actually exists was dead, while
        # the create arm below put it in the wrong place. Verified against the live remote
        # shape `https://…@git.dao.gpt.nexus/vibe/<slug>-preview.git`.
        _cl = re.search(r"git\s+clone\b[^\n]*?"
                        r"(git\.(?:[\w-]+\.)*(?:gpt\.)?nexus[\w.-]*[:/][^\s'\"]+?)"
                        r"(?:\.git)?(?:\s+([^\s'\"&|;]+))?(?:\s|$|;|&)", cmd, re.I)
        _tgt = None
        # NOT `_is_create`: `nexus vibe app create` creates an app ON THE PLATFORM and
        # provisions NO directory — the skill's own cheatsheet says so ("app ONLY … NO repo
        # is provisioned"). The marker therefore landed in whatever directory Cue happened
        # to be standing in, and permanently converted THAT directory into an app repo for
        # every future session: measured live, a 0-byte `.nexus-app` at this project's root
        # while the real app repo is two levels down, making H1/SPEC1/DL1/BLD1/BLD3 fire on
        # ordinary hook and doctrine work. The honest artifact at create time is the
        # `app-repos` registry row, which this same block already writes and which
        # `hc.resolve_repo` already consumes. The marker belongs where a directory exists.
        if _cl:
            _base = _cl.group(2) or os.path.basename(_cl.group(1).rstrip("/"))
            _base = re.sub(r"\.git$", "", _base)
            _tgt = os.path.join(data.get("cwd") or ".", _base)
        if _tgt and os.path.isdir(os.path.expanduser(_tgt)):
            _mk = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(_tgt), ".nexus-app")
            if not os.path.exists(_mk):
                try:
                    open(_mk, "w").close()
                    sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "BLDF", "marker")
                except OSError:
                    pass
        # W27 app-repos: the appId→repo registry hc.resolve_repo reads. `nexus vibe
        # deploy <appId>` names no path, so without this the deploy gates fell back to
        # the session cwd (often the scratchpad) and ran their file checks against a
        # directory with none of the artifacts — green by absence, measured 3/3.
        # THIS is that feed's only writer; the create response is where the id and the
        # repo are both known.
        #
        # W28/F12: this sits OUTSIDE the marker guard. It used to be nested inside it, so
        # removing the wrong marker write would have taken the registry row with it — and
        # the registry is the artifact that was CORRECT all along. The row records the cwd
        # as the app's working directory, which is a claim about where the developer is
        # working; the marker was a claim that the directory IS the app, which is the part
        # that was false.
        if _is_create and not re.search(r'"success"\s*:\s*false|error', _rtxt or "", re.I):
            try:
                _aid = hc.dsub(json.loads(_rtxt), "data").get("id") \
                    if _rtxt.lstrip().startswith("{") else None
            except Exception:
                _aid = None
            if not _aid:
                _im = re.search(r'"id"\s*:\s*"([\w-]{6,})"', _rtxt or "")
                _aid = _im.group(1) if _im else None
            _cw = data.get("cwd") or ""
            if _aid and os.path.isdir(os.path.expanduser(_cw or ".")):
                _root = hc.repo_root_of(_cw) or os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(_cw))
                sc.log(sid, "app-repos", "%s\t%s" % (_aid, _root))
    # SEC1 (W23): token-shaped values printed to the transcript = BURNED credentials.
    # Pure pattern-on-output (token shapes are identifiers, not language); one warn
    # per session per pattern class.
    # W28/F19: scan the COMMAND as well as the response. A credential typed INTO a
    # command (`git remote set-url origin https://u:TOKEN@…`, `export NEXUS_API_KEY=…`,
    # `curl -u "$KEY:"`) is in the transcript exactly as much as one printed by it, and
    # `git remote set-url` with an embedded token is the STANDARD way a push credential
    # gets configured. Same act, same advice, same once-key — deliberately NOT a second
    # check id, which would double-fire when a command echoes its own credential.
    _sec_text = ((resp_text or "") + " " + (cmd or "")) if sid else ""
    if _sec_text.strip():
        # hex40 alone would flag every git SHA — it counts only in credential
        # position: URL userinfo (://user:HEX@) or a token/password assignment.
        _sec_pats = (("hex40", r"(?::\/\/[^\s\/]*:[a-f0-9]{40}@|"
                               r"(?:token|password|secret|apikey|api_key)[=:\s\"']+[a-f0-9]{40}\b)"),
                     ("slack", r"\bxox[bap]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}"),
                     ("ghp", r"\bghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"),
                     # `_` IS in the class: a real Nexus key is `nxs_<1 char>_<32>`, so a
                     # class of [A-Za-z0-9] hits the SECOND underscore after one character
                     # and never reaches the {16,} bound. Measured against the live
                     # config: every key shares the `3_1_32` skeleton, and the old pattern
                     # missed all of them — the guard was blind to the one credential this
                     # layer most exists to protect. Widening the CLASS (rather than
                     # shortening the bound, which would start matching prose like
                     # `nxs_key_here`) covers every underscore-segmented variant at once.
                     ("nxs", r"\bnxs_[A-Za-z0-9_]{16,}"),
                     ("akia", r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b"),
                     ("pem", r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY"),
                     # W24 (SEC-Y): ANY credential carried in a URL's userinfo — a
                     # `git remote -v` / clone URL prints `https://user:SECRET@host`
                     # verbatim, which burned a live push token in a real session.
                     # hex40 above only caught one shape; this catches the class.
                     ("url-userinfo",
                      r"://[A-Za-z0-9._%-]{2,}:[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{12,}@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+"))
        for _pn, _pr in _sec_pats:
            if re.search(_pr, _sec_text) and sc.once(sid, "sec1_" + _pn):
                sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "SEC1", "warn")
                print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                    "additionalContext":
                        ("[SEC1] a CREDENTIAL-IN-URL was printed (git remote / clone URL "
                         "userinfo). Re-run remote-printing commands through a mask "
                         "(`git remote -v | sed -E 's#//[^@]*@#//***@#'`) — only the "
                         "remote's EXISTENCE is ever needed in-transcript. "
                         if _pn == "url-userinfo" else "") +
                        "[SEC1] token-shaped value printed to the transcript — a "
                        "printed credential is BURNED: rotate it now, and re-run "
                        "credential-printing commands piped through a mask (sed the "
                        "value; only its EXISTENCE is ever needed in-session)."}}))
                break
    # HC1/HC2 evidence feeds (consumed by the pretool dav-PUT write-safety gate):
    # read evidence from workspace file fetches; existence+size evidence from any
    # listing/dav output this session (bounded parse; failure-silent).
    if sid:
        _wsf = re.search(r"file\?path=([^&\s'\"]+)", cmd)
        if _wsf:
            sc.log(sid, "ws-read-paths", ":" + _wsf.group(1).strip("/"))
        _davg = re.search(r"curl\b(?![^\n]*-X\s*(?:PUT|MKCOL|DELETE))[^\n]*"
                          r"/api/dav/([\w.-]+)/([^\s'\"]+)", cmd)
        if _davg:
            sc.log(sid, "ws-read-paths",
                   f"{_davg.group(1)}:{_davg.group(2).strip('/')}")
        if _m_read or "/api/dav/" in cmd:
            _resp = data.get("tool_response")
            _rt = (" ".join(str(_resp.get(k, "")) for k in ("stdout", "output"))
                   if isinstance(_resp, dict) else
                   (_resp if isinstance(_resp, str) else ""))
            if _rt:
                try:
                    # W28/F14: collect into a LOCAL delta, then merge under a lock.
                    # `get`->mutate->`put` lost 79% of entries at 20 lanes and 0% at 2 —
                    # a step function in lane count, invisible at test concurrency and
                    # severe at fleet concurrency. PostToolUse fires inside subagents with
                    # the parent's session id, so any two lanes listing a workspace in the
                    # same window destroyed one another's sizes.
                    _sizes = {}
                    _n = 0
                    for _pm in re.finditer(
                            r'"(?:path|name)"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"'
                            r'(?:[^{}]*?"size"\s*:\s*(\d+))?', _rt[:400000]):
                        _pth = _pm.group(1).strip("/")
                        if not _pth or _pth.startswith("http") or _n > 400:
                            continue
                        _n += 1
                        sc.log(sid, "ws-known-paths", "k:" + _pth)
                        if _pm.group(2):
                            _sizes[_pth] = int(_pm.group(2))
                    if _n and _sizes:
                        sc.update(sid, "ws-sizes",
                                  lambda cur: {**(cur or {}), **_sizes}, {})
                except Exception:
                    pass   # fail-open: optional size cache

    # lifecycle capture (build->test->validate->publish->e2e) for the R#27 gate.
    # Durable (project-scoped) so the gate holds across the build's whole life.
    if project:
        ph = hc.lifecycle_phase(cmd, parsed)
        if ph:
            sc.plog(project, "lifecycle", f"{ph[1] or '?'} {ph[0]}")
            # When a published WF is webhook/plugin-triggered, log a one-off
            # `webhook` token so the gate requires a REAL fired event (C2/C-WF9).
            if ph[0] == "published" and ph[1] and isinstance(parsed, dict):
                if _is_webhook_triggered(parsed) and \
                        f"{ph[1]} webhook" not in sc.plines(project, "lifecycle"):
                    sc.plog(project, "lifecycle", f"{ph[1]} webhook")

    # async-node-test guard (C-NEW): one node test at a time; reading a
    # node-result while PENDING/RUNNING is the fixed-sleep/concurrency bug.
    if sid and re.search(r"workflow\s+node\s+test\b", cmd):
        # W28/F16 — read THIS call's own response first. The flag was set on every node test
        # and cleared ONLY by a later `execution node-result`, so the documented-correct loop
        # (test a node, read COMPLETED, test the next) warned from the second node onward,
        # forever. Measured: 8 node tests in one simulated session produced 6 warns; an
        # isolated 3-call probe produced 2 — and every response said COMPLETED. The check
        # asserted "a prior node test has not been confirmed COMPLETED" about a response
        # that says exactly that, on the single most common thing a user does here.
        #
        # It fired into this audit's own transcript while the defect was being reproduced.
        #
        # The race it names is REAL (`execution list --limit 1` returns the wrong execution
        # while two tests race), so the check stays; the defect was that it ignored the one
        # signal that settles it. FAIL DIRECTION: an unparseable or absent status leaves the
        # flag SET, so a genuinely open async test still warns.
        _nt_rt = _resp_text(data.get("tool_response"))
        if re.search(r'"?status"?\s*[:=]\s*"?(COMPLETED|FAILED|ERROR)\b', _nt_rt, re.I):
            sc.drop(sid, "nodetest-open", "OPEN")
        if sc.has(sid, "nodetest-open", "OPEN"):
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "NT1", "warn")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                "additionalContext":
                "[NT1] a prior node test has not been confirmed COMPLETED; node "
                "tests run one at a time with polling (test_and_inspect), since "
                "`execution list --limit 1` returns the wrong execution while two "
                "tests race (G#37)."}}))
            sc.log(sid, "nodetest-open", "OPEN")
            sys.exit(0)
        sc.log(sid, "nodetest-open", "OPEN")
    if sid and re.search(r"execution\s+node-result", cmd) and isinstance(parsed, dict):
        st = parsed.get("status") or hc.dsub(parsed, "output").get("status")
        if st in ("PENDING", "RUNNING"):
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "NT2", "warn")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                "additionalContext":
                "[NT2] node-result read while status=" + str(st) + "; the result "
                "is trustworthy only once polled to COMPLETED (R#29)."}}))
            sys.exit(0)
        else:
            sc.drop(sid, "nodetest-open", "OPEN")   # this test resolved

    # objective-completion → durable consolidation-due (deterministic twin of
    # LK1; C3). Fires regardless of judge backend.
    # Objective reached OR a discovery event (a learning-heavy session must still trigger consolidation —
    # R#34 fires on LEARNING, not only on publishing) OR a DELIVERABLE ship event (git push /
    # gh pr create|merge): a repo-only deliverable build previously armed NOTHING, so a 15h
    # deck workstream ran with every R#34 backstop out of circuit. Every arm also feeds the
    # EPOCH log (due-log vs ran-log in the Stop check) so a due event AFTER the last
    # consolidation re-arms the nag instead of being swallowed by the boolean latch.
    # CALLER GUARD: a consolidation-FLEET agent's OWN writes are the consolidation happening,
    # not a NEW objective needing one — arming on them makes a running consolidation re-arm the
    # nag against the main loop (its workspace PUTs post-date its own ran-credit), which would
    # solicit a DUPLICATE dispatch (the very thing W7.1 prevents). Skip fleet callers.
    caller = hc.s(data.get("agent_type"))
    # W8 RAN credit-on-completion (probe-verified 2026-07-05): consolidation TEAMMATES are
    # main-loop in their OWN sessions (no agent_type), so the fleet caller-guard below cannot
    # see them — their interleaved workspace PUTs were re-arming the shared due-log while the
    # run itself should settle it (observed: due entries landing while the user session made
    # no pushes/writes). The run's mandatory FINAL write — the `_meta/consolidation-log.md`
    # append — is therefore a RAN credit and never arms, whatever session it runs in.
    if project and "_meta/consolidation-log.md" in cmd and hc.classify_workspace_write(cmd):
        sc.plog(project, "consolidation-ran-log",   # W43: owner-stamped
                "%s\t%s" % (time.time(), sid or "-"))
        # W12 R34-VERIFY completion credit (covers the teammate-in-own-session model too —
        # this write is the run's mandatory FINAL act, whatever session it runs in).
        sc.plog(project, "consolidation-verified-log",   # W33: owner-stamped
                "%s\t%s" % (time.time(), sid or "-"))
    elif project and caller not in hc.FLEET_TYPES \
            and (re.search(r"workflow\s+publish|agent-eval\s+run|emulator\s+send|ticket\s+create|"
                           r"git\s+push|gh\s+pr\s+(create|merge)", cmd)
                 or hc.classify_workspace_write(cmd)):
        sc.pset(project, "consolidation_due")
        sc.plog(project, "consolidation-due-log",   # W43: owner-stamped
                "%s\t%s" % (time.time(), sid or "-"))

    # deliverable authored this session → powers the Stop revision-capture nudge
    # (style/tone/format feedback is a candidate learning for the voice/brand home,
    # found via the retriever). Deterministic, no NLP. Ship commands count: a pushed/merged
    # deliverable was authored by definition.
    if project and re.search(
            r"create-draft-email|gmail-create-draft|document\s+(create|upload)|"
            r"template\s+generate|git\s+push|gh\s+pr\s+(create|merge)", cmd):
        sc.pset(project, "deliverable_authored")

    # H2 (W19): a `git push` from an app-build repo while the PREVIOUS push was never
    # driven (no deploy_watch run since it) → the "can you try pushing again?" class.
    # ANY watch run since the last push clears it — the run IS the driving, whatever
    # its exit (an empty-commit redeploy after a nonzero watch is the CORRECT retry).
    # W27: match the STRIPPED command. This regex ran on the RAW text, so a heredoc or a
    # quoted string that merely MENTIONED `git push` (a doc being written, a message being
    # composed) counted as a push. Audited on one session's feed: 10 of 10 `push-log`
    # entries were mentions, not pushes. That feed is what NP1 reads to decide whether any
    # push happened, so it was answering confidently from forgeries.
    # W28/F03: `push_acts` finds the act AND the repo in one parse, so `git -C <repo>
    # push` — the spelling an agent uses when it is not sitting in the repo, which the
    # corpus says is the normal case — is finally visible. `push_failed` reads the
    # response, so a rejected push, a network failure and an `Everything up-to-date`
    # no-op no longer arm an obligation to verify a deploy that never happened. A
    # `--dry-run` / `--delete` / `--tags` push moves no deployable bytes and is recorded
    # but not treated as deploying.
    _acts = hc.push_acts(cmd, data)
    # W48/MECH-1 — ONE verdict, resolved once, then viewed three ways. The old shape asked
    # three independent predicates (push_failed / push_outcome_unreadable / a local -q regex)
    # that could disagree. The merged classifier answers once: landed|failed|unknown|n/a,
    # 105/105 across the frozen corpus + 40 real git outputs + 30 attacks, ZERO false
    # `landed` — the direction that arms a deploy obligation for a push that never reached
    # the remote. The predicate it replaces produced 8 of those on real output.
    _pv = hc.push_verdict_detail(cmd, data.get("tool_response"), data)
    _push_ok = _pv["verdict"] != "failed"
    # W48/V1 — UNREADABLE IS NOT SUCCESS. `_pushed` previously meant "no failure signature
    # was found", which silently included every response the signature could not be READ
    # from. Adversarially measured: git's rejection signatures sit on lines 2-3 of its
    # 8-line output, and 124 of 176 real push commands in a 12-transcript sample pipe to
    # `tail -1..-5`, which truncates them away; a backgrounded push returns an empty
    # launch-time response. Both were recorded as SUCCESSES — a positive `push-log` row
    # plus an armed H2 obligation to verify a deploy that may never have happened. The
    # third state is required: landed / failed / not knowable from this event.
    # W48/adv-F3 — `-q`/`--quiet` SUPPRESSES THE EVIDENCE ON PURPOSE. A quiet push that
    # succeeds prints nothing at all, which is indistinguishable from a truncated failure by
    # response text alone — so treating it as unreadable would nudge on every quiet push,
    # i.e. fire on correct work. The author asked for silence; the honest reading is that
    # this event carries no evidence either way, and a check that cannot know must not
    # accuse. It is still NOT recorded as landed (`_pushed` stays false below), so nothing
    # downstream claims a deploy happened.
    # W48/MECH-1 — the local `-q` regex is GONE: it matched `-q` anywhere in the command, so
    # a `grep -q` in an unrelated link silenced the check. Silencing is now decided PER PUSH
    # ACT, which is what stops a quoted sample report in docs certifying a deploy.
    _push_unread = _pv["verdict"] == "unknown"
    # W48/battery — H2 ARMS ON AN UNREADABLE OUTCOME, deliberately. `_push_unread` used to
    # gate this too, which silenced H2 for any push whose output was piped through `tail` —
    # the corpus says that is 124 of 176 real pushes, so the check went quiet on the MAJORITY
    # of them. H2 asks "you pushed and nothing verified the deploy"; an unreadable outcome
    # still means a deploy MAY have happened and certainly was not verified, so it must arm.
    # Only a CONFIRMED failure (`_push_ok` false) suppresses it — the original contract, which
    # `test_w19_gates` encodes. `_push_unread` keeps its real job: wording the PUSHFAIL nudge.
    _pushed = bool(_acts) and _push_ok and any(dep for _, dep in _acts)
    # W48/MECH-1/I6 — ATTRIBUTION REFUSED UNLESS KNOWN. Reports pair to acts POSITIONALLY, so
    # a silenced act shifts every later report and the old `next(...)` named the WRONG repo
    # (driven: `git -C /a push -q && git -C /b push` attributed /b's landing to /a).
    # `landed_repos` is non-empty ONLY when every act had its own report and none was silenced.
    _push_repo = (_pv["landed_repos"][0] if _pv.get("landed_repos")
                  else next((r for r, dep in _acts if dep and r), None))
    # W48/I5 — STATE WRITES BEFORE EMISSIONS. This block used to sit AFTER the emitter
    # chain, and every emitter ends in `sys.exit(0)`, so a PUSHFAIL emission terminated
    # the process before the attempt feed was ever written: `push-log` got 0 rows for a
    # real push, starving NP1/H2/H4 downstream. Driven, not reasoned: the real hook on a
    # real payload wrote `decisions` and a flag and NO push-log. The feed depends only on
    # `_acts`/`_push_ok`/`_push_repo`, all resolved above, so it belongs here.
    # W48/battery — ATTEMPT vs OUTCOME, separated. The UNREADABLE state was gating BOTH, and
    # they answer different questions. `push-log`/`v2`/`v3` answer "did a push HAPPEN this
    # session" — `NP1` reads them, and for that question the unit is the ATTEMPT; a push whose
    # output was piped through `tail` still happened. `push-ts-<repo>` answers "is there a
    # deploy OWING verification" — `H2` reads it, and for that question the unit is a push
    # that actually LANDED, or H2 demands verification of a deploy that never occurred.
    # Conflating them broke `test_w27_feed_hygiene`'s "a real push DOES write push-log", a
    # contract that predates this wave and that other checks depend on.
    _push_attempted = bool(_acts) and _push_ok and any(dep for _, dep in _acts)
    if sid and _push_attempted:
        # D4/NP1 feed (W24): push EVENTS as a list — `push-ts` holds only the LAST
        # push, and NP1 needs "were there ANY pushes this session". One line, and it
        # is why NP1's predicate is app-source-WRITES-exist rather than commits-exist
        # (the measured miss: the first commit postdated the complaint by 11 minutes).
        try:
            sc.log(sid, "push-log", str(time.time()))
            # push-log-v2 starts clean at the strip fix: the legacy feed keeps its history
            # (append-only), but a reader that needs TRUSTWORTHY push events reads v2.
            sc.log(sid, "push-log-v2", str(time.time()))
            # W28/F03: v3 carries the REPO. v2 rows are a bare epoch, so the turn-end
            # check took max(pushes) — ONE obligation per session, not per repo — and an
            # earlier repo's unverified push was discharged by a later repo's
            # verification. The fleet builds several repos per session (integration repo
            # + lane worktrees + a starter), so verifying the last one silenced all of
            # them, and the rollback this pair exists for is exactly a repo nobody looked
            # at again. v2 keeps being written unchanged: other readers index it, and
            # rewriting a live feed under fan-out is the data-loss class this estate has
            # already measured once.
            sc.log(sid, "push-log-v3",
                   "%s\t%s" % (time.time(),
                                os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(_push_repo))
                                if _push_repo else "-"))
        except Exception:
            pass   # fail-open: feed write is advisory; the H2 verdict below does not depend on it
    # W48/C2 — A FAILED PUSH WAS SILENT. `push_failed` existed only to SUPPRESS the verify
    # obligation (correctly: a push that never landed cannot owe a deploy verification), so
    # nothing anywhere acted on it. The result is the measured crisis: a background chain's
    # push was REJECTED non-fast-forward, "Pushing." had already been reported as an outcome,
    # and it sat unread for 13 minutes across four owner messages ending "so ??" — until the
    # owner drove the discovery. Cue's own words that turn: "I reported 'pushing' without
    # checking that it succeeded … relaying an intent as an outcome."
    #
    # This is the opposite half of H2. H2 asks "you pushed and nothing verified the deploy";
    # this asks "you did not push at all, and you may have already said you did". Both key on
    # the SAME parsed response, so the failure that suppresses one arms the other and no push
    # outcome goes unread. Bounded to once per minute: a rejected push is followed by a
    # pull-rebase-push cycle, and one nudge per attempt is the false-positive cluster that
    # lands exactly where the reader is already frustrated.
    # W28/F03: the repo the command ACTED ON, not the payload cwd. Measured over 645 real
    # pushes: the two answers disagreed on 63 of the 323 resolvable ones (19.5%) — 46
    # fires where the pushed repo is not an app and 17 silences where it is. And the
    # WRONG NAME is worse than silence: "you pushed appB and nothing verified it" sends
    # the reader to check an app they never touched, and when that comes back clean the
    # real unverified deploy reads as confirmed.
    _h2_dir = _push_repo or data.get("cwd") or ""
    if sid and _pushed \
            and hc.app_repo_ctx(_h2_dir):
        # Public-forge remotes (github/gitlab/bitbucket) don't auto-deploy on our
        # platform — only the tenant vibe git host does. H2 skips them (measured
        # false-fire: starter pushes to github.com nagged for a deploy_watch with
        # no deploy behind it); their CI is the drive-to-green twin there.
        try:
            _rem = subprocess.run(
                ["git", "-C", os.path.expanduser(_h2_dir or "."),
                 "remote", "get-url", "origin"],
                capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3).stdout or ""
        except Exception:
            _rem = ""
        _forge = bool(re.search(r"(github|gitlab|bitbucket)\.", _rem))
        # W28/F03: `push-ts` and the once-key are scoped PER REPO. Session-global, a
        # single push to appA followed by a single push to appB made appB's `_prev`
        # non-zero, so H2 told the reader they were "re-pushing without having driven the
        # previous deploy" of an app pushed exactly once. Same class as the wrong-name
        # defect above: a factually false statement sends the reader hunting for a deploy
        # that does not exist.
        _h2key = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_",
                        os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(_h2_dir)) or "repo")[:40]
        _prev = float(sc.get(sid, "push-ts-" + _h2key) or 0)
        _watch = [float(x) for x in sc.lines(sid, "deploy-watch-runs") if x]
        sc.put(sid, "push-ts-" + _h2key, time.time())
        # `_prev` stays in the predicate DELIBERATELY. W28 probed dropping it (the plan's
        # A10) and measured the result: the first push has no previous deploy to have
        # verified, so H2's own wording would be false there. The push-once-and-stop hole
        # is covered by H2-TURN at Stop instead, whose wording is about THIS deploy.
        if not _forge and _prev and not any(w > _prev for w in _watch) \
                and sc.once(sid, "h2_%s_%d" % (_h2key, int(_prev))):
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "H2", "warn")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                "additionalContext":
                    "⚠ [H2] `%s` — re-pushing without having driven the previous deploy "
                    "to a verified-served state. Run in the background:\n"
                    "  %s \"<publicUrl>\" \"<marker>\" 600 20 <profile> <appId>\n"
                    "· <publicUrl> and <appId>: `nexus vibe app list --json | jq -r "
                    "'.apps[]|\"\\(.id) \\(.name) \\(.publicUrl)\"'`. <appId> is "
                    "positional #6 and is not optional in practice — without it the audit "
                    "poll is org-wide and ANOTHER app's deploy satisfies it.\n"
                    "· <marker>: a string unique to THIS build that the served response "
                    "actually contains; confirm it is absent from the OLD build first.\n"
                    "Then REPORT the served state ('marker confirmed at <url>' / "
                    "'HEALTHY, marker pending — still polling'); only the content marker "
                    "proves the swap (R#20)." % (_h2key, _DEPLOY_WATCH)}}))
            sys.exit(0)
    # DG1-LEDGER (W22): a merge landed in an app-context INTEGRATION repo (non-lane:
    # its .git is a DIRECTORY) while journeys/.last-pass is missing or predates the
    # merged HEAD — the post-merge journey run is due before any completion claim
    # (the journey gate lives at the integration repo's merge; lane worktrees are
    # exempt by construction). Pure file/command state: git verb + repo markers +
    # mtimes vs the HEAD commit time; success-only (a conflicted merge landed nothing).
    # W28/F19: `\bmerge\b` matched inside `git merge-base`, because `-` is a word
    # boundary — a read-only query used constantly during rebases and lane integration
    # was told to run the journey suite. `git merge --abort` fired too, and it lands
    # NOTHING, so no post-merge journey run is due. Not "require 'Merge made by' in the
    # response": a fast-forward prints "Fast-forward" and would be missed, and the
    # conflict case is already correctly excluded by response text below.
    if sid and re.search(r"\bgit\b[^\n|;&]*\bmerge(?![-\w])", hc._strip(cmd)) \
            and not re.search(r"--(?:abort|quit|continue)\b", hc._strip(cmd)):
        _dgcm = re.search(r"cd\s+([^;&|]+?)\s*(?:;|&&)", cmd)
        _dgr = os.path.expanduser((_dgcm.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
                                   if _dgcm else (data.get("cwd") or "")) or "")
        _dgrt = resp if isinstance(resp, str) else ""
        if (_dgr and hc.app_repo_ctx(_dgr) and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(_dgr, ".git"))
                and not re.search(r"CONFLICT|fatal:|error:", _dgrt or "", re.I)):
            try:
                _dgh = float(subprocess.run(
                    ["git", "-C", _dgr, "log", "-1", "--format=%ct"],
                    capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3).stdout.strip() or 0)
            except Exception:
                _dgh = 0.0
            _dglp = os.path.join(_dgr, "journeys", ".last-pass")
            _dgstale = (not os.path.isfile(_dglp)) or (
                _dgh > 0 and os.path.getmtime(_dglp) < _dgh)
            if _dgstale and sc.once(sid, "dg1l_%s" % _dgr):
                sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "DG1-LEDGER", "warn")
                print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                    "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                    "additionalContext":
                        "⚠ [DG1-LEDGER] merge landed in the integration repo without a "
                        "post-merge journey run (journeys/.last-pass missing or older than "
                        "HEAD) — run `npm run journeys` (or dispatch journey-verifier) "
                        "before the next completion claim; the journey gate lives at the "
                        "integration repo's merge."}}))
                sys.exit(0)
    # MAN1 (W21 S6): dropped-features tripwire — before a push lands, diff the
    # standard docs/feature-manifest.md against the last pushed version (set-
    # difference on feature keys; a `removed` Status cell is the deliberate-
    # removal marker). Deterministic: two versions of one file, exact cell
    # matching. Silent when the repo carries no standard manifest. Format
    # contract: nexus-app-builder/references/feature-manifest-format.md.
    # W28/F19 — three defects, one line apart from two already-fixed siblings:
    #  · the RAW command, while `_pushed` and H4 both match `hc._strip(cmd)` after W27.
    #    Measured false fires on a heredoc, an `echo`, and `git commit -m 'explain the
    #    git push flow'` — telling the user they dropped shipped features when no push
    #    happened, which is how a guard earns being ignored.
    #  · the repo came from `data["cwd"]` alone, so `cd <repo> && git push` from
    #    elsewhere was SILENT — the guard missing what it was built for. `resolve_repo`
    #    is the helper written for exactly this and already used by the deploy gates.
    #  · the once-key was the COUNT of dropped rows, so a later push dropping a
    #    different single row was suppressed. Key it on the dropped SET instead. Not
    #    "drop the once-guard": a push loop would then repeat the warn every push.
    if sid and re.search(r"\bgit\s+push\b", hc._strip(cmd)):
        try:
            # `resolve_repo` returns (rdir, how) — a REASONED outcome. `(None, reason)`
            # means "could not evaluate", which its own docstring says callers must not
            # conflate with "not an app repo"; here there is simply no manifest to diff,
            # so the guard stays silent rather than grading the wrong directory.
            _rd, _ = hc.resolve_repo(cmd, data)
            if not _rd:
                raise ValueError("repo unresolved")
            _mp = os.path.join(_rd, "docs", "feature-manifest.md")
            if os.path.isfile(_mp):
                with open(_mp, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as _fh:
                    _new = _fh.read()
                _old = ""
                for _ref in ("@{upstream}", "origin/main", "origin/master"):
                    _r = subprocess.run(
                        ["git", "-C", _rd, "show",
                         "%s:docs/feature-manifest.md" % _ref],
                        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
                    if _r.returncode == 0 and _r.stdout:
                        _old = _r.stdout
                        break
                _gone = hc.manifest_dropped(_old, _new) if _old else []
                if _gone and sc.once(sid, "man1_" + hashlib.sha1(
                        ",".join(sorted(_gone)).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]):
                    sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "MAN1", "warn")
                    print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                        "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                        "additionalContext":
                            "⚠ [MAN1] the shipped-feature manifest LOST %d row(s) "
                            "vs the last pushed version with no `removed` marker: "
                            "%s. A rework wave silently dropping shipped features "
                            "is the regression class users catch (R#50(6)) — "
                            "restore them, or mark Status `removed` deliberately, "
                            "before the next push." % (len(_gone), ", ".join(_gone[:5]))}}))
                    sys.exit(0)
        except Exception:
            pass   # fail-open: cwd may be unreadable in a lane worktree

    # H4 (W19): deploy_watch terminal tokens — deterministic branch guidance on a
    # marker miss (swap lag vs swap failure), never a verdict.
    # W32/G04 — the command must INVOKE the script, not merely name it. W28/F03 moved the
    # credit from the command text to the response token, which was right — but the script's
    # own SOURCE contains that token, so `cat`/`grep`/`less` of it still handed back a
    # "SERVED" response and still credited a deploy. The same defect the earlier wave fixed,
    # surviving its own fix by one indirection: reading about the verification still counted
    # as doing it. Driven: `cat <script>` credited, exactly like a real run.
    #
    # And it fired the OTHER way too — a `grep` of the script during this audit made the live
    # hook announce a FAILED_EVENT for a deploy that never happened, because the failure
    # tokens are in the source as well.
    #
    # An invocation is the script at a command position with an argument after it. A reader
    # verb before it is not an invocation, whatever the response says.
    # The PATH is an OPERAND, so it is matched on the heredoc-stripped RAW text and may be
    # quoted — this repo's own checkout has spaces in it. Running this against the
    # quote-stripped act view deletes the path and silently stops crediting real runs:
    # the same wrong-view error this wave fixed elsewhere, recurring inside its own fix.
    if sid and _DW_INVOKED_RE.search(hc._HEREDOC_RE.sub(" ", cmd)):   # W27: stripped, per H2's note
        _resp = data.get("tool_response")
        _rt = (" ".join(str(_resp.get(k, "")) for k in ("stdout", "stderr", "output"))
               if isinstance(_resp, dict) else (_resp if isinstance(_resp, str) else ""))
        # W28/F03 — THE CREDIT LIVES HERE, and only a real SERVED earns it. The exit
        # token is the only signal in the system that distinguishes "ran" from "typed",
        # and it exists exactly here, where the response does.
        if "DEPLOY_WATCH: SERVED" in _rt:
            sc.log(sid, "deploy-watch-runs", str(time.time()))
        # ...and the four NON-served terminal states no longer pass in silence. H4 read
        # exactly one of them, so `DEPLOY_WATCH: FAILED_EVENT` — the script saying the
        # DEPLOY FAILED — ended the session with every push-verification check green.
        _dw_fail = next((t for t in ("FAILED_EVENT", "EVENT_TIMEOUT", "MARKER_MISS",
                                     "ACCESS_BLOCKED")
                         if "DEPLOY_WATCH: " + t in _rt), None)
        if _dw_fail == "FAILED_EVENT" \
                and sc.once(sid, "h4f_%d" % int(time.time() // 600)):
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "H4", "warn")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                "additionalContext":
                    "⚠ [H4] deploy_watch reported FAILED_EVENT — the deploy itself "
                    "failed, so this is a ROLLBACK decision, not a polling one. Nothing "
                    "new is serving. Read the build log, then either fix forward and "
                    "re-push or roll back to the last good sha; the push obligation "
                    "stays open until something actually serves (R#27)."}}))
            sys.exit(0)
        if _dw_fail in ("EVENT_TIMEOUT", "ACCESS_BLOCKED") \
                and sc.once(sid, "h4t_%s_%d" % (_dw_fail, int(time.time() // 600))):
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "H4", "warn")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                "additionalContext":
                    ("⚠ [H4] deploy_watch ended on EVENT_TIMEOUT — no deploy event "
                     "arrived inside the window. That is not evidence the code is wrong "
                     "and not evidence it served: re-run with a longer window, and check "
                     "the app actually received the push."
                     if _dw_fail == "EVENT_TIMEOUT" else
                     "⚠ [H4] deploy_watch ended on ACCESS_BLOCKED — a 401/403 is an "
                     "ACCESS answer, not a swap answer. The app is PRIVATE by default; "
                     "check visibility and servingDeployment before concluding anything "
                     "about the code.") +
                    " The push obligation stays open until a marker is confirmed."}}))
            sys.exit(0)
        if _dw_fail == "MARKER_MISS" \
                and sc.once(sid, "h4_%d" % int(time.time() // 600)):
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "H4", "warn")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                "additionalContext":
                    "⚠ [H4] deploy_watch ended WITHOUT the served marker — EITHER swap "
                    "lag (re-run the marker check with a longer window; a 0-hit right "
                    "after HEALTHY is not wrong-code evidence) OR a swap failure "
                    "(empty-commit redeploy) OR the marker check never got to READ the "
                    "app: a 401/403 is an ACCESS answer, not a swap answer (the app is "
                    "PRIVATE by default; check visibility and servingDeployment before "
                    "concluding anything about the code). Don't claim live — surface the "
                    "access state (R#27): 'HEALTHY, marker pending' or the rollback plan."}}))
            sys.exit(0)

    # XREF — a workspace file was written → remind to sweep refs + re-index
    # (R#35 #3). Once per session so a bulk PUT loop does not spam.
    if sid and not sc.has(sid, "xref-nudged", "Y"):
        dx = hc.classify_workspace_write(cmd)
        if dx:
            sc.log(sid, "xref-nudged", "Y")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
                "additionalContext": f"[{dx['id']}] {dx['reason']}"}}))
            sys.exit(0)

    # W48/adv-F5,F6 + blind-F9 — PUSHFAIL RELOCATED TO THE END OF THE CHAIN.
    # It was emitted here, immediately after the push verdict, and this file is
    # first-match-wins (`print` then `sys.exit(0)`). So a PUSHFAIL emission STARVED
    # everything below it — and not only advisories: it skipped `push-ts-<h2key>`
    # (H2's own state), DG1-LEDGER, MAN1 (the dropped-features tripwire) and H4,
    # including the `deploy-watch-runs` FEED WRITE. A chained `git push && ./deploy_watch.sh`
    # therefore lost its SERVED credit, which then makes H2 fire falsely on the next push.
    # Whether it starved them at all depended on a wall-clock minute bucket, so the estate
    # behaved differently either side of a minute boundary.
    #
    # A new advisory does not get to jump ahead of feed writes and checks that were already
    # there. The verdict is computed early (it needs the untouched response) and EMITTED
    # last; the trade is explicit — if an older check fires on the same event, PUSHFAIL
    # defers to it that turn, and its once-key is not burned because the guard sits with
    # the emission.

    if sid and _acts and any(dep for _, dep in _acts) and _push_unread \
            and sc.once(sid, "pushunread_%d" % int(time.time() // 60)):
        # W48/V1 — the outcome could not be READ, so nothing is claimed either way. This is
        # the dominant real shape (truncated output, a backgrounded push), and it used to
        # pass as success. Nudge, never block: the push may well have landed — what is
        # missing is the evidence, and only a fresh read can supply it.
        sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "PUSHFAIL", "unreadable")
        print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
            "additionalContext":
                "[PUSHFAIL] that push's OUTCOME is unreadable — the response carries neither "
                "a failure signature nor a ref that moved, so it is not known to have landed "
                "and has NOT been recorded as a deploy. Usual causes: the output was piped "
                "through `tail` (git's rejection lines are at the TOP, the `hint:` lines at "
                "the bottom), or the push was backgrounded and this is only its launch "
                "response. Read the real outcome before you say it is pushed — `git log "
                "origin/<branch> -1` or re-run the push unpiped (R#20: report facts, not "
                "intent)."}}))
        sys.exit(0)
    if sid and _acts and any(dep for _, dep in _acts) and not _push_ok \
            and sc.once(sid, "pushfail_%d" % int(time.time() // 60)):
        # W48/C2: record the verdict. A tagged emission with no decision row is
        # unauditable and uncalibratable — the estate's own `test_w28_emission_observable`
        # suite pins this, and it caught this exact omission on the first battery run
        # after PUSHFAIL landed. It is also precisely the blind spot found in R34-LEDGER
        # hours earlier ("0 rows" was not evidence about firing), committed again here.
        sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", "PUSHFAIL", "nudge")
        print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
            "additionalContext":
                "[PUSHFAIL] that push did NOT land — the response carries a rejection, a "
                "fatal, or `Everything up-to-date`. Nothing was deployed and no remote moved. "
                "Read the response before your next sentence: if you have already told the "
                "owner it is pushed, correct it THIS turn (R#20 — report facts, not intent). "
                "Then diagnose rather than re-fire: a non-fast-forward means someone else "
                "pushed, so fetch and integrate their commits — never force over work you "
                "have not read."}}))
        sys.exit(0)
    # id-capture → reset-survivable id-cache (powers PreCompact carry-forward).
    # Capture the resource type from the `nexus <resource> <verb>` match, NOT by
    # positional split — a `cd "/path with spaces"; nexus …` prefix makes
    # cmd.split()[1] the path fragment, not the resource (live-test bug).
    _m = re.search(r"nexus\s+([\w-]+)\s+(?:create|publish|duplicate)", hc._strip(cmd))
    if project and isinstance(parsed, dict) and _m:
        rid = parsed.get("id") or hc.dsub(parsed, "data").get("id")
        if rid:
            name = parsed.get("name") or hc.dsub(parsed, "data").get("name") or ""
            kind = _m.group(1)
            sc.plog(project, "id-cache", f"{kind} {rid} {name}".strip())
            if sid and kind in hc.E2E_ABLE_KINDS:
                sc.log(sid, "created-session", kind)   # an E2E-able resource created THIS session (PreCompact ledger feed)

    # delete-clearing → a deleted resource no longer carries a build obligation,
    # so drop it from the id-cache + lifecycle log (else the completion gate nags
    # forever about a workflow that was built, deleted, and is gone — live-found).
    # W28/F19: this is the ONLY destructive write in the file and it was the least
    # guarded — it matched the RAW command and never asked whether the delete SUCCEEDED.
    # Measured: a failed delete, an `echo` quoting the cleanup command, a heredoc writing
    # a handover note, and a `--dry-run` each permanently erased the resource's R#27
    # obligations from all three feeds. `pdrop` rewrites in place, so it is irreversible:
    # from that point the agent that still exists, unpublished and unevaluated, is
    # invisible to the completion gate. Both guards are required — dropping only from
    # `id-cache` would just move the bug, since the nag comes from `lifecycle`.
    if project and not hc.response_failed(data.get("tool_response")):
        _sd = hc._strip(cmd)
        # a `--dry-run` deletes nothing, so it discharges nothing.
        _d = (None if re.search(r"--dry-run\b", _sd) else
              re.search(r"nexus\s+[\w-]+\s+delete\s+([0-9a-fA-F-]{8,})", _sd))
        if _d:
            _did = _d.group(1).strip("'\"")
            sc.pdrop(project, "id-cache", _did)
            sc.pdrop(project, "lifecycle", _did)
            sc.pdrop(project, "agent-lifecycle", _did)   # EV1: a deleted agent drops its obligation

    dash = os.environ.get("NEXUS_DASHBOARD_URL", "https://gpt.nexus")
    parts = []
    for d in (hc.classify_execute_result(cmd, parsed),
              hc.classify_command_posthints(cmd, parsed, dashboard_base=dash)):
        if d:
            parts.append(f"[{d['id']}] {d['reason']}")
            # W49 — telemetry. This channel never wrote a decision row, so TE1-TE3 and the
            # WF posthint family were structurally unmeasurable. The classifier JOINS ids
            # ("WF9+WF1+WF10"), so split before logging or the joined spelling becomes an
            # id no registry row carries. Log-only; output byte-identical; a telemetry
            # failure must never cost the advisory.
            try:
                if sid:
                    for _cid in str(d["id"]).split("+"):
                        sc.log_decision(sid, "PostToolUse", _cid, "annotate")
            except Exception:
                pass
    if not parts:
        sys.exit(0)
    print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
        "hookEventName": "PostToolUse",
        "additionalContext": "\n".join(parts)}}))   # W28/F08: one advisory per line
    sys.exit(0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""P6 compaction re-arm (plan Section 3.4) — a SEPARATE, additive PreCompact hook
(does not modify nexus-lifecycle.py). Two effects, both proven this session:

1. READ-LOG RESET: archive the session read-log (read-log -> read-log.pc<n>) so the
   ladder gates RE-ARM after a compaction — a guide/skill "read" before the compaction
   no longer satisfies its gate, forcing the re-read at the next gated action. Fixes the
   measured degradation (read-log survives compaction, content does not).

2. SLIM-SKILL-MAP inject: emit (<=10k additionalContext, model-only) a 1-3 line synthesis
   of every skill + a "re-read the one you need now" directive, so the post-compaction
   window has orientation (WHAT to re-read); the reset + gates force the actual re-read.
   Source = each SKILL.md `synthesis:` frontmatter line (falls back to the skill's first
   purpose line until the frontmatter is added).

Fail-silent: any error -> exit 0 (never blocks a compaction)."""
import sys, os, json, glob, re

HOOKS = os.path.dirname(__file__)
SKILLS = os.path.join(HOOKS, "..", "skills")


def _synthesis(skill_md):
    """One-line purpose for a skill: its `synthesis:` frontmatter if present, else the
    first non-heading / non-table content line."""
    try:
        with open(skill_md, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            lines = fh.readlines()
    except Exception:
        return ""
    for key in ("synthesis:", "description:"):
        for ln in lines:
            s = ln.strip()
            if s.lower().startswith(key):
                return s.split(":", 1)[1].strip().strip('"\'')[:200]
    for ln in lines:
        s = ln.strip()
        if s and not s.startswith("#") and not s.startswith("|") and not s.startswith("---") and ":" not in s[:20]:
            return s[:160]
    return ""


def _loaded_skills(sid):
    """The skills this session ACTUALLY loaded, from the read-log — before it is archived.

    W28/F16. The map used to list EVERY skill in the repo. Measured at one compaction: the
    lifecycle advisories were 613 characters and this map was 4,551 — 7.5x the size of
    everything else in the block, and 27% of a whole session's injected volume, in one turn,
    at the exact moment the model's context has just been destroyed. The load-bearing fact
    was ONE string: re-read `nexus-app-builder`. `PC-CANON`, twelve lines earlier, had
    already named it exactly.
    """
    try:
        sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HOOKS, "lib"))
        import session_cache as sc
        if sid is None:
            return None      # unknown history -> the full map, never silence
        rows = sc.lines(sid, "read-log") if sid else []
    except Exception:
        return None      # unknown -> fall back to the full map, never to silence
    slugs = set()
    for r in rows:
        m = re.search(r"skills/([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)/", str(r)) or \
            re.search(r"^skill:([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*)", str(r).strip())
        if m:
            slugs.add(m.group(1))
    return slugs


def slim_map(sid=None):
    loaded = _loaded_skills(sid)
    entries = []
    for sm in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(SKILLS, "*", "SKILL.md"))):
        slug = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(sm))
        # Filter to what this session actually loaded. The map's own framing concedes the
        # redundancy — "the gates will force the re-read" — so its entire value is telling
        # you WHICH, and listing all of them answers that question by not answering it.
        # `loaded is not None`, NOT `loaded` — an EMPTY set is falsy, and conflating it
        # with "unknown" made a session that loaded no skills fall through to the full
        # 21-skill map: the exact case that should print nothing. Same None-means-broad
        # versus []-is-a-positive-claim distinction this estate already pays for elsewhere.
        if loaded is not None and slug not in loaded:
            continue
        syn = _synthesis(sm)
        if syn:
            entries.append(f"- **{slug}** — {syn}")
    if loaded is not None and not entries:
        return ""        # nothing was loaded -> nothing to re-read -> say nothing
    body = ("SLIM SKILL MAP (a compaction voided your loaded skills; the gates will force "
            "the re-read — this tells you WHICH). Re-read the one your next action needs:\n"
            + "\n".join(entries))
    return body[:10000]


def reset_read_log(sid):
    try:
        sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HOOKS, "lib"))
        import session_cache as sc
        rl = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".nexus-mcp", "cue-session", sc._safe(sid), "read-log")
        if os.path.exists(rl):
            i = 0
            while os.path.exists(f"{rl}.pc{i}"):
                i += 1
            os.rename(rl, f"{rl}.pc{i}")  # archive -> gates re-arm
            return True
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: advisory re-arm adapter — a broken import must not block compaction
    return False


def main():
    try:
        d = json.load(sys.stdin)
    except Exception:
        return
    if not isinstance(d, dict):
        return   # W28/E09: fail-open covered PARSE errors only. A VALID-JSON non-object
                 # (`[1,2,3]`, `"x"`, `42`, `null`) parsed fine and then crashed on `.get`.
                 # A crashed adapter is a guard BYPASS, so shape is part of the contract.
    sid = d.get("session_id")
    # ORDER MATTERS: build the map BEFORE archiving the read-log, because the map is now
    # filtered by what this session actually loaded and that answer lives in the log this
    # very function is about to rename. Computing it after would silently produce the empty
    # set — and the empty set means "say nothing", so the map would vanish entirely.
    _map = slim_map(sid)
    if sid:
        reset_read_log(sid)
    if not _map:
        return   # nothing was loaded this session, so there is nothing to re-read
    try:
        print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreCompact",
                "additionalContext": _map}}))
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: emission is advisory; a failed print must not break compaction


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
    sys.exit(0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Claude Code PreToolUse adapter — Bash reliability checks.

Thin glue: read the hook payload on stdin, call the shared core
(`hook_core.classify_bash_reliability`), emit a CC decision. All logic lives in
hook_core.py (single source of truth, shared with the SDK surface).

  deny → permissionDecision deny (the command WOULD fail/orphan anyway).
  warn → non-blocking additionalContext (advisory; never blocks).
  none → exit 0 (defer to native flow / the firewall / acceptEdits).
"""
import glob
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "lib"))
import hook_core as hc       # noqa: E402
import session_cache as sc   # noqa: E402


def _nexus_json(args, timeout=20):
    """Run a read-only `nexus … --json` from within the hook and parse it.
    Hook subprocesses are not re-intercepted. Fail-silent → None."""
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["nexus"] + args + ["--json"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout).stdout
        data = json.loads(out)
        return data.get("data", data) if isinstance(data, dict) else data
    except Exception:
        return None


def _valid_models(sid):
    """S2 cache + autoload: live NON-deprecated modelNames. None on failure."""
    v = sc.get(sid, "model-names", ttl=3600)
    if v is not None:
        return set(v)
    rows = _nexus_json(["model", "list"])
    if rows is None:
        return None
    names = [m["modelName"] for m in rows
             if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("modelName") and not m.get("deprecated")]
    sc.put(sid, "model-names", names)
    return set(names)


def _action_params(sid, tool_id, action):
    """TG1 cache + autoload: param names for a tool's action. None on failure."""
    key = "tp_" + re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", tool_id + "_" + action)
    v = sc.get(sid, key, ttl=3600)
    if v is not None:
        return set(v)
    root = _nexus_json(["tool", "get", tool_id])
    if not isinstance(root, dict):
        return None
    act = next((a for a in (root.get("actions") or [])
                if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("key") == action), None)
    if not act:
        return None
    params = act.get("parameters") or act.get("configurableProps") or []
    names = [p.get("name") for p in params if isinstance(p, dict) and p.get("name")]
    sc.put(sid, key, names)
    return set(names)


def _agent_census(sid, agent_id):
    """WIR1 cache + autoload: ([collection names], [tool labels]) for an agent.
    (None, None) on total failure (fail-open)."""
    key = "wir_" + re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", agent_id)
    v = sc.get(sid, key, ttl=600)
    if v is not None:
        return v.get("cols"), v.get("tools")
    cols_raw = _nexus_json(["api", "GET", "/agents/%s/collections" % agent_id])
    tools_raw = _nexus_json(["agent-tool", "list", agent_id])
    if cols_raw is None and tools_raw is None:
        return None, None
    cols = [c.get("name") for c in (cols_raw or [])
            if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("name")]
    tools = [t.get("label") for t in (tools_raw or [])
             if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("label")]
    sc.put(sid, key, {"cols": cols, "tools": tools})
    return cols, tools


def _prompt_text_from_cmd(cmd, body):
    """Prompt text from `agent update --prompt <file>` or a body carrying
    `prompt`. None if neither present."""
    pm = re.search(r"--prompt\s+(\S+)", cmd)
    if pm:
        try:
            with open(pm.group(1).strip("'\""), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                return fh.read()
        except Exception:
            return None
    if isinstance(body, dict) and isinstance(body.get("prompt"), str):
        return body["prompt"]
    return None


def round2_warns(cmd, sid):
    """S2 (deprecated model) + TG1 (execute param mismatch). Returns a list of
    (id, reason). Stateful (cache/autoload) so it lives in the adapter."""
    out = []
    _mn = hc.model_name_in_cmd(cmd)
    if _mn:
        d = hc.check_model_name(cmd, _valid_models(sid))
        # W18: once per session×name — a standing repeat on the same name trains
        # blindness (the R34-nag once-per-state pattern).
        if d and sc.once(sid, "s2_" + _mn.casefold()):
            out.append((d["id"], d["reason"]))
    if "external-tool execute" in cmd:
        tm = re.search(r"external-tool\s+execute\s+(\S+)", cmd)
        am = re.search(r"--action\s+(\S+)", cmd)
        obj, _ = hc._body_json(cmd)
        if tm and am and isinstance(obj, dict):
            tool_id = tm.group(1).strip("'\"")
            action = am.group(1).strip("'\"")
            d = hc.check_execute_input_keys(list(obj), _action_params(sid, tool_id, action))
            if d:
                out.append((d["id"], d["reason"]))
    # DEDUP — before `ticket create`, surface existing matches (R#10).
    if re.search(r"(^|[\s;&|(])nexus\s+ticket\s+create", hc._strip(cmd)):
        tm = re.search(r'--title\s+("([^"]+)"|\'([^\']+)\'|(\S+))', cmd)
        title = (tm.group(2) or tm.group(3) or tm.group(4)) if tm else ""
        kw = " ".join(title.split()[:4])
        if kw:
            rows = _nexus_json(["ticket", "list", "--search", kw])
            existing = [f"{t.get('identifier')}: {(t.get('title') or '')[:50]}"
                        for t in (rows or []) if isinstance(t, dict)][:3]
            if existing:
                out.append(("DEDUP", "existing tickets match this title — dedup "
                            "before filing (R#10): " + " | ".join(existing)))
    # WIR1 — `agent update` carrying a prompt: an ATTACHED collection/skill with no
    # %%marker%% / @tag in that prompt would be invisible to the agent at runtime.
    am = re.search(r"(^|[\s;&|(])nexus\s+agent\s+update\s+(\S+)", hc._strip(cmd))
    if am:
        obj, _ = hc._body_json(cmd)
        ptext = _prompt_text_from_cmd(cmd, obj)
        if ptext is not None:
            agent_id = am.group(2).strip("'\"")
            cols, tools = _agent_census(sid, agent_id)
            if cols is not None or tools is not None:
                d = hc.check_prompt_wiring(ptext, cols or [], tools or [])
                if d:
                    out.append((d["id"], d["reason"]))
            # AM5/AM6 — pre-write Save-transform guards (R#20): cap + cascade file.
            # AM7 pairing: cache what was SENT so posttool can diff the next
            # `agent get <id>` against it. Fail-open on any miss.
            st = hc.prompt_stats(ptext)
            for d2 in hc.prompt_precheck(st):
                out.append(d2)
            if st and sid:
                try:
                    sc.put(sid, "prompt-sent-" + agent_id, st)
                except Exception:
                    pass   # fail-open: one-shot dispatch cache
    return out
