def _tools_index_path():
    """Resolve the community tools/ INDEX.md via the workspace mount (reuse the
    awareness mount technique). None if no live mount. Fail-open."""
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".nexus-mcp",
                               "workspace-mounts.json")) as fh:
            mounts = json.load(fh) or {}
    except Exception:
        return None
    # CLI #2486 / NEX-2360 rekeyed the registry to `<kind>:<id>|<slug>`, so indexing the
    # map by the bare tools slug resolved None on every post-rekey machine — and the
    # failure is a silent None, not an error: the INDEX went unread and the vendor path
    # was guessed.
    # `hc.mount_path` matches the row's own `slug` (present in BOTH formats) under the
    # acting org.
    mp = hc.mount_path(mounts, "tools", hc.acting_scope())
    if mp and os.path.isdir(mp):
        idx = os.path.join(mp, "INDEX.md")
        if os.path.isfile(idx):
            return idx
    return None


def _grep_tools_index(vendor):
    """Return the vendor's REAL relative path AS LISTED in the tools INDEX (e.g.
    `plugins/microsoft-outlook`), else None. The INDEX is the canonical map — never
    assume a flat `<vendor>/` (the real layout nests vendors under `plugins/`, and a
    hardcoded flat path read FAILS). Greps the single INDEX.md (NOT a recursive glob).
    A Pipedream toolId is `<vendor>-<action>`; the path's LAST segment is the bare
    vendor, so we match that segment as equality/prefix of the vendor. Fail-open."""
    idx = _tools_index_path()
    if not idx or not vendor:
        return None
    v = vendor.lower()
    try:
        with open(idx) as fh:
            for ln in fh:
                row = ln.strip()
                if not row.startswith(("|", "-", "*")):
                    continue
                # backticked path-or-slug tokens; match on the LAST path segment.
                for tok in re.findall(r"`([a-z0-9][a-z0-9/_-]{1,80}?)/?`", row.lower()):
                    seg = tok.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
                    if seg == v or v.startswith(seg + "-") or seg.startswith(v + "-"):
                        return tok.rstrip("/")              # the REAL relative path
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def kb_on_tool_action(cmd, project, sid_for_feed=None):
    """C6/KB1: on the FIRST action per vendor, nudge Cue to SEARCH the tools KB by the
    tool's NAME for what's been DONE with it (prior gotchas, action shapes already
    discovered) AND inspect the action's RESULT shape via `tool get` before executing —
    so it doesn't re-discover known gotchas by trial-and-error (R#12 + R#48). The vendor
    is the bare slug, derived from --action (`microsoft_outlook-…` → `microsoft-outlook`),
    NOT the UUID toolId. Once-per-vendor durable flag. Fail-open → None."""
    if not project:
        return None
    s = hc._strip(cmd)
    # Node-type family (W18): first use per session of a VENDOR-CLASS native node type —
    # via `workflow node-type <t>` introspection or a node create/update/batch body
    # carrying "type": "<t>". Same once-per durable-flag family, node-framed message.
    nt = None
    mnt = re.search(r"workflow\s+node-type\s+([A-Za-z]+)", s)
    if mnt and mnt.group(1) in hc.VENDOR_NODE_TYPES:
        nt = mnt.group(1)
    if not nt and re.search(r"workflow\s+(node\s+(create|update)|batch)", s):
        obj, _ = hc._body_json(cmd)
        blob = json.dumps(obj) if obj else cmd
        for t in hc.VENDOR_NODE_TYPES:
            if '"type": "%s"' % t in blob or '"type":"%s"' % t in blob:
                nt = t
                break
    if nt and not sc.pis_set(project, "kbcheck_node_" + nt):
        sc.pset(project, "kbcheck_node_" + nt)
        hit = _grep_tools_index(nt.lower())
        where = (f"its tools-KB home is `tools/{hit}/` (config gotchas + crash classes), resolved "
                 f"via the tools INDEX" if hit else
                 f"the tools INDEX has no entry for '{nt}' yet — first integrator; file learnings per R#34")
        return ("KB1", f"first use of native node type '{nt}' this session; {where}; "
                       f"`workflow node-type {nt}` gives the live schema — an org instance "
                       f"supplements the entry, never replaces it (R#12).")
    if not re.search(r"external-tool\s+execute|tool\s+get\s", s):
        return None
    vendor = hc.tool_vendor_from_cmd(cmd)            # from --action (the reliable source)
    if not vendor:                                   # a bare `tool get <vendor>` (non-UUID)
        mg = re.search(r"tool\s+get\s+(['\"]?)([a-z][a-z0-9-]+)\1", s)
        if mg and not re.match(r"^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-", mg.group(2)):
            vendor = mg.group(2)
    if not vendor or sc.pis_set(project, "kbcheck_" + vendor):
        return None
    sc.pset(project, "kbcheck_" + vendor)            # first time only
    hit = _grep_tools_index(vendor)
    # G8 feed (W24): record the KB lookup OUTCOME — hit or MISS. The resolver already
    # ran; logging it turns "I looked and there is nothing" into a satisfying act, per
    # the user's amendment ("not ALL tools are in the community KB, so sometimes we
    # cannot find info genuinely"). Without this G8's prereq is unsatisfiable for every
    # tool the KB has never heard of — which is exactly the first-integrator case.
    try:
        # ONLY a DELIBERATE discovery act satisfies G8 — a `tool get`, never the
        # `external-tool execute` being gated. Logging on the execute made the command
        # satisfy its OWN gate (caught in testing: G8 went permanently silent), which
        # is worse than the unsatisfiable version it replaced.
        if sid_for_feed and re.search(r"\btool\s+get\b", s) \
                and not re.search(r"external-tool\s+execute", s):
            sc.log(sid_for_feed, "kb-lookup",
                   "%s:%s" % (vendor, ("hit:" + hit) if hit else "miss"))
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: optional shape-read feed write
    where = (f"prior usage is documented at `tools/{hit}/` (README + gotchas + actions), resolved via the "
             f"tools INDEX (never assume a flat `tools/{vendor}/` — that read fails)" if hit
             else f"the tools INDEX (`$TOOLS_PATH/INDEX.md`) has no entry for '{vendor}' yet — first "
                  f"integrator; learnings are filed there per R#34")
    return ("KB1", f"this is the first action on '{vendor}' this session; {where}, and the action's "
                   f"RESULT shape is available via `tool get` (guessing the shape then trial-and-erroring "
                   f"through null fields is the antipattern, R#12 + R#48).")


def kb_build_start(cmd, sid):
    """KB2 (W18): FIRST build-class creation per resource class per session while ALL
    community-KB consumption counters are zero — the deterministic proxy for the R#41
    per-problem precedent reflex (a hook sees counters, never 'problems'). WARN once
    per resource class; zz_probe scratch resources excluded."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    m = re.search(r"nexus\s+(workflow|task|agent)\s+create|nexus\s+(vibe)\s+app", hc._strip(cmd))
    if not m or "zz_probe" in cmd:
        return None
    rclass = m.group(1) or "app"
    consumed = (sc.lines(sid, "retriever-dispatched")
                or [l for l in sc.lines(sid, "fastpack-used") if l]
                or [l for l in sc.lines(sid, "ws-file-reads")
                    if re.search(r"/(tools|systems|use-cases)/", l)]
                or [l for l in sc.lines(sid, "read-log")
                    if re.search(r"/(tools|systems|use-cases)/", l)])
    if consumed:
        return None
    if sc.once(sid, "kb2_" + rclass):
        return ("KB2", f"first {rclass} build this session with no community-KB consumption "
                       "on record — the tools/systems/use-cases INDEX scan (or a retriever "
                       "dispatch) precedes design, and it re-fires per NEW sub-problem "
                       "(R#41). Ignore if this build's precedent was checked in another form.")
    return None


def eval_template_first(cmd, sid):
    """TPL1 (W18): `agent-eval run create` carrying inline resolved* prompt keys with no
    `agent-eval template create` seen this session → templates-first nudge (build-order
    step 0; inline = debug-only). Pure command/state logic; once per session."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    s = hc._strip(cmd)
    if re.search(r"agent-eval\s+template\s+create", s):
        sc.log(sid, "eval-template-created", "Y")
        return None
    if not re.search(r"agent-eval\s+run\s+create", s):
        return None
    if not re.search(r"resolved(SystemPrompt|Rubric|Prompt)", cmd):
        return None
    if sc.lines(sid, "eval-template-created"):
        return None
    if sc.once(sid, "tpl1"):
        return ("TPL1", "this run body carries inline resolved* prompts with no template "
                        "created this session — the eval lifecycle builds TEMPLATES first "
                        "(tester persona / judge rubrics / summary), then runs reference "
                        "them by templateId; inline prompts are debug-only "
                        "(nexus-evaluations §Eval lifecycle).")
    return None


def git_add_guard(cmd, sid):
    """GIT1 (W18): `git add -A|--all|.` while `git status --porcelain` shows untracked
    paths matching our OWN session/worker artifact naming → ignore/exclude-before-add
    nudge (R#50(4)). WARN once per repo dir; never a deny (a repo may own such names)."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    s = hc._strip(cmd)
    m = re.search(r"git\s+(?:-C\s+(\S+)\s+)?add\s+(?:-A\b|--all\b|\.(?=\s|$))", s)
    if not m:
        return None
    rdir = (m.group(1) or "").strip("'\"")
    if not rdir:
        cm = re.search(r"cd\s+([^;&|]+?)\s*(?:;|&&)", cmd)
        rdir = cm.group(1).strip().strip("'\"") if cm else "."
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", os.path.expanduser(rdir), "status", "--porcelain"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10).stdout
    except Exception:
        return None
    hits = [ln[3:] for ln in out.splitlines() if ln.startswith("??")
            and any(g in ln for g in hc.SESSION_ARTIFACT_GLOBS)]
    # W24 (Y3): a DATA file or an oversized blob entering commits. Measured: a 223.6MB
    # `.warehouse-command.jsonl` was committed FIVE times, pushed a >1GB pack, and the
    # remote rejected every push — it WAS in .gitignore, but it was committed before
    # that line existed and gitignore never untracks. Size+name are pure file-state.
    big = []
    for ln in out.splitlines():
        if not (ln.startswith("??") or ln.startswith("A ") or ln.startswith("M ")):
            continue
        rel = ln[3:].strip().strip('"')
        base = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(rdir), rel)
        # `git status --porcelain` COLLAPSES an untracked directory to `?? dir/` — the
        # files inside are never listed, so a data file in a NEW folder is invisible
        # unless we walk it (W24: the measured 223MB file happened to sit at the repo
        # root, which is the only reason a name-only check saw it).
        cands = []
        if os.path.isdir(base):
            for root, _d, files in os.walk(base):
                if "/.git" in root or "node_modules" in root:
                    continue
                for fn in files:
                    fp = os.path.join(root, fn)
                    cands.append((os.path.relpath(fp, os.path.expanduser(rdir)), fp))
                if len(cands) > 400:      # bounded: a nudge never walks a huge tree
                    break
        else:
            cands = [(rel, base)]
        for crel, cpath in cands:
            try:
                mb = os.path.getsize(cpath) / 1e6
            except Exception:
                continue
            if mb >= hc.GIT_DENY_MB:
                big.append((crel, "%dMB — never commit this" % round(mb)))
            elif mb >= hc.GIT_WARN_MB or hc.DATA_FILE_RE.search(crel):
                big.append((crel, "%.1fMB data file" % mb))
    if big:
        if sc.once(sid, "git1data_" + rdir):
            return ("GIT1", "data/oversized file(s) staged or untracked here: "
                    + "; ".join("%s (%s)" % b for b in big[:4])
                    + " — a durable store belongs in the platform SPINE, never in git "
                    "(Principle-1). Already committed? `git rm --cached <path>` + .gitignore "
                    "(gitignore alone never untracks). Ignore if this file genuinely ships "
                    "with the repo.")
    if not hits:
        return None
    if sc.once(sid, "git1_" + rdir):
        return ("GIT1", "untracked session/worker artifacts in this repo: "
                        + ", ".join(hits[:5]) + " — R#50(4): ignore/exclude BEFORE `git add -A` "
                        "(an ACTED-ON status glance), and background workers write OUTSIDE repo "
                        "dirs. Ignore if these files belong in this repo.")
    return None


def _lane_output_paths(prompt):
    """Output paths a dispatch prompt CLAIMS for its lane: a report/dossier/output file, or an
    explicitly named capture/artifact directory. Deliberately narrow — a path merely READ is not
    a claim, so only paths introduced by a writing verb or an output-ish label count."""
    prompt = hc.s(prompt)   # totality: a non-string prompt must not raise (exit-1 fail-open)
    out = set()
    pat = (r"(?:write|writes|written|save|saves|output|outputs|report to|dossier(?:\s+file)?|"
           r"put your captures in|land(?:s|ing)? (?:in|at))\b[^\n`]{0,60}?`?(/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]{12,})`?")
    for m in re.finditer(pat, prompt, re.I):
        p = m.group(1).rstrip(".,;:`)")
        if len(p) > 12:
            out.add(p)
    return out


def _lane_owns(prompt):
    """The repo-relative source globs a lane dispatch DECLARES it owns — the vocabulary the lane
    contract and the lane DAG use (e.g. `owns: src/pages/Catalogue.tsx, src/pages/Card.tsx`).
    Distinct from _lane_output_paths (report/dossier OUTPUT files): EXEC1 needs the owned SLICE to
    detect a SAME-slice re-spawn, and slices are relative globs, not absolute output paths. Returns
    a set of globs left in their declared (relative) form so hc._globs_overlap can compare them."""
    prompt = hc.s(prompt)   # totality: a non-string prompt must not raise (exit-1 fail-open)
    out = set()
    # NB: an explicit `owns:`/`owns=` label or `your slice (owns) is` — NOT a bare "you own",
    # which matches prose like "you own it exclusively" and swallows the worktree path. The capture
    # allows dots INSIDE a token (a filename has them) but stops at a sentence-ending period
    # (`. `), a `;`, or end-of-line; the token filter then drops any trailing prose words.
    for m in re.finditer(r"(?:owns?\s*[:=]|your\s+slice(?:\s*\(owns\))?\s*(?:is|:))\s*"
                         r"([^\n;]+?)(?:\.\s|\.$|;|\n|$)", prompt, re.I):
        for tok in re.split(r"[,\s]+", (m.group(1) or "").strip()):
            tok = tok.strip("`'\"").rstrip(".,;:")
            # a token must look like a PATH (has a `/` or a code extension), NOT merely contain a
            # glob char — else a bare `*`/`**` owns matches every other lane (G8). Degenerate tokens
            # are dropped.
            if not tok or tok in (".", "*", "**", ".."):
                continue
            if ("/" in tok) or tok.endswith((".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".css")):
                out.add(tok)
    return out


def lane_path_collision(ti, sid):
    """LP1: this dispatch claims an output path ANOTHER live lane in this session already claimed.

    Measured twice in one session: two retrieval lanes were handed one dossier path and the second
    overwrote the first (recovered only because that lane noticed and preserved the foreign bytes);
    and a duplicate seat instance overwrote a completed task's output. In BOTH cases the lane behaved
    correctly and the DISPATCH was the error — R#50(1) binds the writer, and nothing checked the
    moment the collision was created.

    Warn, never deny: two lanes CAN legitimately share a directory, and a false block on a dispatch
    is expensive. Observe marker: `.lp1-observe` in the hooks dir.
    """
    if not sid:
        return None
    prompt = (ti.get("prompt") or "") if isinstance(ti, dict) else ""
    if not prompt:
        return None
    claimed = _lane_output_paths(prompt)
    if not claimed:
        return None
    hits = []
    for p in sorted(claimed):
        if sc.has(sid, "lane-output-paths", p):
            hits.append(p)
        else:
            sc.log(sid, "lane-output-paths", p)
    if not hits:
        return None
    _obs = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".lp1-observe"))
    reason = ("this dispatch claims an output path another lane in this session already claimed: "
              + ", ".join(f"`{h}`" for h in hits[:3])
              + ". One writer per artifact (R#50(1)) — give this lane its OWN path, or say in the brief "
                "which lane owns the file and what this one may append. A second writer silently "
                "overwrote a live dossier twice in one session; both recoveries were luck.")
    return ("LP1", reason + (" [observe]" if _obs else ""))


def dispatch_gate(st, ti, sid, data):
    """W24 — ONE function, TWO predicates on the SAME event (PreToolUse:Agent), because
    the engine rule is consolidate-don't-accumulate:

    · BOARD-ENTRY — a WORK lane is being dispatched with no task-op since the user last
      spoke. Measured: a redesign, two directors and two executors existed only in
      Cue's head and in SendMessage traffic; because none was ever a board row, an
      owner-arbitrated feature sat behind them and the ordering fix had nothing to
      compare against. Read-only scouts/retrievers are exempt (they are not work
      lanes).
    · BUILT-FILE — a JUDGING dispatch whose prompt names no built judge file. Measured:
      assembling a brief from memory dropped 60% of one method block and 100% of the
      browser toolkit, while a pointed-at file arrived byte-exact. Pure PATH presence
      in the prompt — a string that is a path, never wording judgment.

    NOT here: ORD1 (priority buckets). The harness board carries no `priority` field
    (verified against a live task_reminder: id · subject · status · blockedBy · blocks
    · description · activeForm), so its predicate would have no live state — it stays
    doctrine-only rather than shipping unsatisfiable (the G8 lesson).
    Returns a list of (id, text) warns."""
    out = []
    if not sid or not st:
        return out
    JUDGING = ("app-assessor", "app-reviewer", "app-taste", "app-design-director")
    READONLY = ("knowledge-retriever", "retrieval-reader", "Explore", "claude-code-guide",
                "statusline-setup")
    prompt = hc.s((ti or {}).get("prompt"))   # totality: non-string prompt must not raise
    try:
        if st in JUDGING and "references/built/" not in prompt and "/built/" not in prompt:
            if sc.once(sid, "p3built_%s" % st):
                out.append(("BUILT-FILE",
                            "judging dispatch (%s) names no BUILT judge file — point it at "
                            "`references/built/<category>.md` and let it read the file, rather "
                            "than assembling the method into the prompt: a hand-assembled brief "
                            "measurably drops blocks (60%% of one, 100%% of another) while a "
                            "pointed-at file arrives byte-exact. No built file yet? generate it "
                            "first (scripts/build-judges), then dispatch." % st))
        if st not in READONLY and not st.startswith("nexus-consolidation"):
            _ops = sc.lines(sid, "task-op")
            _last = float(_ops[-1]) if _ops else 0.0
            _b, _gap, _lu = hc.task_gap_state(data.get("transcript_path"), _last)
            if _gap >= 1 and sc.once(sid, "boardentry_%s_%d" % (st, int(_gap))):
                out.append(("BOARD-ENTRY",
                            "dispatching a WORK lane (%s) with no task recorded since you last "
                            "heard from the user — give the lane its board row THIS turn "
                            "(R#9 task-per-ask/lane). A lane that exists only in dispatch "
                            "traffic is invisible to every ordering and completeness check." % st))
    except Exception:
        return out
    return out


# W28/F12: the PRD template presents this requirement INSIDE A TABLE ROW and invites a
# "greppable line", so a bolded label or a table cell is the natural thing to write —
# and both were silently rejected while looking correct to a human reader. Accept
# markdown emphasis, a leading table pipe, and a heading marker.
_ACCESS_RE = re.compile(r"^[ \t>*#|-]*\**Access:?\**\s*[|:]?\s*(PRIVATE|PUBLIC)\b", re.I | re.M)


def _access_recorded(rdir):
    """W26 ACCESS1 predicate — pure file state: does this repo RECORD an access verdict?
    Greps docs/PRD.md then docs/SPEC.md for a machine-readable `Access: PRIVATE|PUBLIC`
    line (prd-template.md "Access + identity"). The LIVE grant is deliberately NOT read:
    the permission routes 403 for an org API key (dashboard-session scoped), so a
    live-state predicate would be an unsatisfiable gate — the Y7 class, one gate over."""
    base = os.path.expanduser(rdir or ".")
    for rel in ("docs/PRD.md", "docs/SPEC.md"):
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(base, rel), encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
                if _ACCESS_RE.search(fh.read()):
                    return True
        except OSError:
            continue
    return False


def _access_observe():
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                                       ".access-observe"))


EXECUTING_LANES = ("app-executor", "app-contracts", "app-backend")
# W48/PART1 — every lane that PRODUCES a user-facing unit, not just the executor family.
# The partition checks keyed on `app-executor` alone, so the work shape that actually
# produced the one-lane complaint — design exploration and craft elevation, dispatched as
# `app-redesigner` — could never reach them, whatever the doctrine said. Measured across
# three replays of a real session under both the old and the corrected wording: zero
# `app-executor` dispatches, zero partition files, and a check that was structurally unable
# to notice. `app-architect` is deliberately EXCLUDED: it is the lane that WRITES the
# partition, so counting it would nag the fix.
PRODUCING_LANES = EXECUTING_LANES + ("app-redesigner", "app-tests")
JUDGING_LANES = ("app-assessor", "app-reviewer", "app-taste", "app-design-director")


def _dispatch_rows(sid):
    """[(agent_type, epoch)] from the dispatch-log. Rows written before W27 carry no
    tab and read as epoch 0, so an old session degrades to "ever dispatched" rather
    than crashing or silently dropping rows."""
    out = []
    for ln in sc.lines(sid, "dispatch-log"):
        parts = str(ln).split("\t")   # W28: rows may carry a 3rd 'model' field — split, not partition
        t = parts[0].strip()
        e = parts[1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else ""
        try:
            out.append((t, int(e) if e else 0))
        except ValueError:
            out.append((t, 0))
    return out


def _executor_repos(sid):
    """Repo roots an executor-family lane was dispatched against (EXEC1's feed)."""
    return {os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(x.strip()))
            for x in sc.lines(sid, "app-executor-repos") if x.strip()}


def _app_repos_pt(sid):
    """App repos this session touched — executor dispatch targets + roots of recorded
    app-source writes (DIRSEQ resolves the repo here, since the dispatch-time cwd is the
    project root, not the app repo where docs/ISSUE-LEDGER.md lives)."""
    seen = set(_executor_repos(sid))
    for fp in sc.lines(sid, "app-src-writes"):
        r = hc.repo_root_of(os.path.dirname(str(fp)))
        if r:
            seen.add(r)
    return seen


def _last_push_epoch(sid, rdir):
    """Epoch of the last push/deploy THIS session evaluated for this repo (BLD2 writes
    it below). 0 = none yet, so the roster question covers the whole session."""
    best = 0
    for ln in sc.lines(sid, "bld2-push"):
        r, _, e = str(ln).partition("\t")
        if r.strip() == rdir:
            try:
                best = max(best, int(e))
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return best


def _appid_map(sid):
    """appId→repo-root from the `app-repos` session feed (writer: posttool BLDF at
    `nexus vibe app create`). Empty dict when the session never created an app —
    resolve_repo then reports `appid-unmapped:<id>`, which is the honest answer."""
    out = {}
    for ln in sc.lines(sid, "app-repos"):
        if "\t" in ln:
            k, v = ln.split("\t", 1)
            out[k.strip()] = v.strip()
    return out


def deploy_gate(cmd, sid, data):
    """DG1 (W19; absorbs MAN1/W18): ONE file-state gate on BOTH deploy paths —
    `nexus vibe deploy` AND `git push` from an app-build repo (git push IS the normal
    deploy: auto-build). Reads the four gate artifacts via hc.gate_artifacts (manifest
    rows w/ empty Primitive not marked mock · docs/DESIGN.md · docs/SPEC.md ·
    journeys/.last-pass). WARN per repo+artifact-set per session; DENY only in a
    STARTER-BORN repo (`.nexus-starter` present — the artifacts were template-shipped,
    so their absence/red there is 100%-sure unverified work, D7 bar). A deliberate
    override re-issues the SAME command with NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1 (visible, logged).
    Returns None | ("warn"|"deny", id, text)."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    s = hc._strip(cmd)
    is_vibe = bool(re.search(r"nexus\s+vibe\s+deploy\b", s))
    if not (is_vibe or re.search(r"\bgit\s+push\b", s)):
        return None
    # W27: ONE resolver for every deploy-path gate (was a cd-prefix regex over the RAW
    # command, measured FALSE-ALLOW 3/3 — see hc.resolve_repo). An unresolvable repo is a
    # REASONED outcome that must be SAID, never a silent "not an app" skip: the gates
    # below evaluate file state, so an unresolved repo means they evaluated NOTHING.
    rdir, _how = hc.resolve_repo(cmd, data, _appid_map(sid))
    if rdir is None:
        if sc.once(sid, "resolve_%s" % _how):
            return ("warn", "RESOLVE",
                    "deploy-path command whose target repo could not be resolved (%s) — "
                    "every file-state gate below (access decision, gate artifacts, "
                    "manifest, journeys) therefore evaluated NOTHING, and silence here is "
                    "not a pass. Name the repo (`cd <repo> && …`) or re-run the deploy "
                    "from inside it." % _how)
        return None
    project = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or data.get("cwd")
    # `nexus vibe deploy` is intrinsically app-context (the marker is set by posttool
    # AFTER a vibe command — the first deploy must not slip the gate on ordering).
    # A bare `git push` requires REPO-level signals (.nexus-starter / docs contracts
    # in THIS repo) — never the project-wide flag alone, which bleeds onto unrelated
    # repos pushed from the same session (measured: a library push nagged for the
    # app gate because a vibe command had run earlier in the project).
    if not is_vibe and not hc.app_repo_ctx(rdir):
        return None
    # W28/F16: and the push must actually REACH the platform that hosts the app. These gates
    # triggered on "a repo carrying docs/PRD.md, and `git push` appears" — so a push of source
    # to a public forge was denied by an APP-DEPLOY gate, with a message that is factually
    # wrong about what just happened. Measured: 4 of 4 pushes in a simulated session denied,
    # the same 686 characters each time. `H2` has carried this exclusion since a measured
    # false fire; its siblings never got the sweep, and one of them sits twelve lines away.
    if not is_vibe and not hc.push_is_deploying(rdir, cmd):
        return None
    # W26 ACCESS1: the app's inbound identity decision must be RECORDED before it ships.
    # DENY from the first violation (owner's call, overriding the violated-twice ladder:
    # an app open to the internet is not a mistake worth measuring twice). Observe marker
    # `.access-observe` degrades it to a warn; override = the SAME command + NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1.
    if not hc.ack_present(cmd, "NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1") \
            and not _access_recorded(rdir):   # W40: act view, not raw
        _amsg = ("deploy with NO recorded access decision. Every hosted app is PRIVATE by "
                 "default and admits people who SIGN IN and are granted it through a user "
                 "GROUP (`vibe_app` x `group` x viewer — granted in the dashboard; an org "
                 "API key 403s, so that step is handed to the owner, never claimed done). "
                 "Write ONE machine-readable line in docs/PRD.md — `Access: PRIVATE - group "
                 "<name>` or `Access: PUBLIC - <owner's quoted go> + in-app auth <method>` — "
                 "and re-issue. PUBLIC never means unauthenticated: it means the app carries "
                 "its own authentication. Deliberate override: re-issue the SAME command "
                 "with NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1 (visible, logged).")
        if _access_observe():
            # W28/F05: NO rate limiter in observe. Measured, 30 identical violations in one
            # session: enforce recorded 30, observe recorded 1 — and the limiter existed
            # ONLY on the observe branch, which is the exact inversion. The window that is
            # supposed to MEASURE the check was the only mode throwing the sample away, and
            # non-uniformly (once per session x repo, so a heavy user is undercounted more
            # than a light one). A window that discards 29 of 30 observations is worse than
            # no window: it produces a number that looks like data. Noise during a rollout
            # window is what the window is for.
            return ("warn", "ACCESS1", _amsg + " [observe: would-deny]")
        else:
            return ("deny", "ACCESS1", _amsg)
    # W24 build-integrity: two checks that ride the SAME deploy trigger but are NOT
    # UI-shaped, so they apply to a headless service exactly as to an app (F-26: the
    # artifact set forks by archetype; these two never do).
    #  · GATE-EXEC — a declared quality command whose script FILE is missing: the
    #    check everyone assumes is running cannot run (measured on a shipped repo).
    #  · EMPTY-TANK — a store FILE that exists at ZERO bytes while the build is being
    #    deployed: "done" over a pipeline that never ran end to end (F-28/F-32).
    #  · TANK-HOME — its twin on the other side of the size split: a DATABASE carrying
    #    rows, homed on the container, where a deploy swap wipes it (SKILL P1). The two
    #    partition the same files by size, so no file ever draws both verdicts.
    try:
        _gaps = hc.declared_gate_gaps(rdir)
        if _gaps and sc.once(sid, "gateexec_%s" % rdir):
            return ("warn", "GATE-EXEC",
                    "package.json declares %s but the script file is MISSING: %s. A "
                    "declared quality command is a check the next person (or lane) will "
                    "trust — write it or drop the entry; do not deploy behind a check "
                    "that cannot run."
                    % (", ".join("`npm run %s`" % g[0] for g in _gaps[:3]),
                       ", ".join(g[1] for g in _gaps[:3])))
        # CODE-LENS (W27): the review crew has a CODE lens, and it is the one that judges
        # whether what shipped is organised well enough to hand over. A round that reviewed
        # only the visual lenses ships code nobody read — the measured complaint was that
        # the code was unreadable at the end of an otherwise-passing build. If this push
        # touches non-CSS source and no `code.json` verdict exists, the lens was unstaffed.
        if hc.code_lens_unstaffed(rdir) and sc.once(sid, "codelens_%s" % rdir):
            return ("warn", "CODE-LENS",
                    "this push changes source but the review round has no `code.json` "
                    "verdict — the CODE lens was never staffed. That lens is what judges "
                    "whether the result is organised well enough to hand over, and the "
                    "visual lenses cannot substitute for it. Fire it, or record the "
                    "owner's decision to ship unreviewed code.")
        _tank = hc.empty_store_paths(rdir)
        if _tank and sc.once(sid, "emptytank_%s" % rdir):
            return ("warn", "EMPTY-TANK",
                    "deploying with a store file at ZERO bytes: %s. A service whose "
                    "pipeline has never persisted a record is BUILT, not COMMISSIONED — "
                    "run it end to end on one real unit and show the count before any "
                    "done/live claim (F-28 done-states). Rows are not the only question: "
                    "if that file lives on the container it is not durable at any size "
                    "(SKILL P1)." % ", ".join(_tank[:3]))
        # TANK-HOME: a database WITH rows beside the app code, and no PRD row saying
        # where reads are homed. The row is the silencer, deliberately — declaring
        # `Read-path: … host <where>` is the decision this check exists to force into
        # an artifact, not a box to tick.
        _home = hc.container_store_paths(rdir)
        if _home and not hc.read_path_row(rdir) and sc.once(sid, "tankhome_%s" % rdir):
            return ("warn", "TANK-HOME",
                    "deploying with a database carrying rows in the app repo (%s) and no "
                    "`Read-path:` row in docs/PRD.md saying where reads are homed. The "
                    "container filesystem is not a store — a deploy swap wipes it — so a "
                    "DB beside the code is a second source of truth that diverges "
                    "silently (measured: an in-process projection hid an open counting "
                    "round from a user while every gate stayed green, and its refresh "
                    "blocked the event loop 2.3-3.1s every 30s at zero traffic). Home the "
                    "read path in a managed store, or declare the local-dev twin: add "
                    "`Read-path: <surface> projection|direct|connector · host <where> · "
                    "divergence <check or none>` to docs/PRD.md "
                    "(references/prd-template.md). NOTE this reads the repo working tree, "
                    "not the container: a store the app creates only at runtime is "
                    "invisible here." % ", ".join(_home[:3]))
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: advisory GATE-EXEC probe; a stat failure must not block the deploy
    # INPROC-DB sits OUTSIDE that blanket handler on purpose. It is the only DENY on this
    # trigger, and a deny folded into a `except: pass` is a deny that a stat error two
    # checks earlier can silently cancel — the same "crash reads as approval" shape the
    # advisories above are allowed to have and a gate is not (law 4). Its own failure
    # degrades to a WARN that NAMES the failure, never to silence.
    #
    # It answers the blind spot TANK-HOME names in its own message: an in-process engine
    # ships to the container whether or not it ever writes a file the repo can see, and
    # the measured defect left no file at all.
    try:
        _inproc = hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(rdir)
    except Exception as _e:
        _inproc = None
        _ierr = type(_e).__name__
    else:
        _ierr = None
    if _ierr is not None:
        return ("warn", "INPROC-DB",
                "the in-process-database check could not read this repo's manifests (%s), "
                "so it proved NOTHING about them. Treat this deploy as unchecked for the "
                "container-store anti-pattern rather than as clean." % _ierr)
    # W48 — THE BUILTIN HALF. The manifest read above assumes an engine must be INSTALLED to
    # reach the container. Node 22 ships one in the runtime: `node:sqlite` needs no dependency,
    # so the manifest has nothing to read and this arm returned CLEAN on apps that write a
    # database beside themselves. Measured on three real builds — all three imported
    # `node:sqlite`, all three shipped a `.db`, all three passed. Same deny, because it is the
    # same anti-pattern; only the declaration moved from the manifest to the import.
    try:
        _binproc = hc.builtin_db_imports(rdir)
    except Exception:
        _binproc = []
    if _binproc and not _inproc:
        _bnamed = ", ".join("`%s` (%s)" % (m, f) for m, f in _binproc[:3])
        _bmsg = ("deploying an app whose SOURCE imports a built-in in-process database "
                 "engine: %s. It needs no dependency, so the manifest check above cannot "

                 "divergence <check or none>` in docs/PRD.md (references/prd-template.md). "
                 "A local-dev twin is declared by WHERE A DEPENDENCY SITS, and a builtin has "
                 "no such line to move — so there is no devDependencies escape here, and an "
                 "app that genuinely needs one is choosing an installable engine on purpose."

        if _observing("inprocdb"):

    if _inproc:
        _named = ", ".join("`%s` (%s, %s)" % (p, m, s) for p, m, s in _inproc[:3])
        _imsg = ("deploying an app whose RUNTIME dependencies declare an in-process "
                 "database engine: %s. That engine runs inside the app's own process on "
                 "the container, so it is a second source of truth the next deploy swap "
                 "wipes, and its refresh competes with the request path on one thread "
                 "(measured: a PGLite projection blocked the Node event loop 2.3-3.1s "
                 "every 30s at ZERO traffic, and the app's own route timing reported 0ms "
                 "throughout — a blocked loop delays the QUEUE, not the handler, which is "
                 "why three separate measurements had to come from outside). TANK-HOME "
                 "cannot see this one: it stats the repo working tree, and a runtime-only "
                 "store leaves no file there. Two ways out, both declarations: move it to "
                 "`devDependencies` if it is the LOCAL-ONLY dev twin the doctrine permits, "
                 "or drop it and home the read path in a managed low-latency store, "
                 "recording the pick as `Read-path: <surface> projection · host <managed "
                 "store> · divergence <check or none>` in docs/PRD.md "
                 "(references/prd-template.md). A cache is a bounded copy of a value you "
                 "already fetched — reach for a caching library, not an engine. NOTE: "
                 "declared dependencies only, never the lockfile, so a transitively pulled "
                 "engine is not covered." % _named)
        if _observing("inprocdb"):
            # No rate limiter on the observe branch, for the reason ACCESS1 records above:
            # a window that discards repeat observations produces a number that looks like
            # data. The enforcing branch keeps `once` because a deny is already terminal.
            return ("warn", "INPROC-DB", _imsg + " [observe: would-deny]")
        if sc.once(sid, "inprocdb_%s" % rdir):
            return ("deny", "INPROC-DB", _imsg)
    items = hc.gate_artifacts_for(rdir)   # W24 F-26: UI artifacts are N/A for a service
    if not items:
        return _trailing_notes(rdir, sid)
    txt = "; ".join(f"{a}: {p}" for a, p in items[:4])
    starter_born = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(rdir), ".nexus-starter"))
    # W22 lane re-target: a LANE WORKTREE (its .git is a FILE containing `gitdir:`)
    # is exempt from the hard gate — journeys are the INTEGRATION repo's merge gate;
    # an isolated lane can never green them, so a deny there only trains routine
    # ACK overrides (measured). Lane pushes get ONE nudge; solo repos unchanged.
    _gitm = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(rdir), ".git")
    _is_lane = False
    if os.path.isfile(_gitm):
        try:
            with open(_gitm) as _fh:
                _is_lane = _fh.read(64).lstrip().startswith("gitdir:")
        except OSError:
            pass
    if starter_born and _is_lane:
        if sc.once(sid, "dg1lane_%s" % rdir):
            return ("warn", "DG1",
                    "lane-worktree push with red/missing gate artifacts — %s. The journey "
                    "gate runs at the INTEGRATION repo's merge (lane pushes are exempt from "
                    "the hard gate): land the lane, then run journeys post-merge before any "
                    "completion claim." % txt)
        return None
    # Y7 (W24) — DEGRADE-TO-WARN when the precondition has NEVER been satisfiable in
    # this repo. Measured: the journey suite had never once passed here (it validated a
    # foreign repo for ~21h), so the deny was unsatisfiable by construction and it
    # blocked a two-file resilience fix while the app was ALREADY DOWN. An
    # unsatisfiable deny teaches nothing and trains routine ACK overrides — the same
    # lesson as G8, one gate over. A journeys dir that has never produced a .last-pass
    # is the file-state proof of "never green here".
    _jd = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(rdir), "journeys")
    _never_green = (os.path.isdir(_jd)
                    and not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(_jd, ".last-pass"))
                    and not glob.glob(os.path.join(_jd, "*.last-pass")))
    if starter_born and _never_green \
            and not hc.ack_present(cmd, "NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1"):   # W40
        if sc.once(sid, "dg1degraded_%s" % rdir):
            return ("warn", "DG1",
                    "deploy gate DEGRADED to a warn: this repo's journey suite has never "
                    "produced a pass, so the hard gate is unsatisfiable here and would only "
                    "train ACK overrides — %s. Fix the suite (that is the real debt) or "
                    "state why this ships without it; if the app is DOWN, say so and ship "
                    "the fix — an unsatisfiable gate must not hold a live outage." % txt)
        return None
    if starter_born and not hc.ack_present(cmd, "NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1"):   # W40
        return ("deny", "DG1",
                "deploy gate — this starter-born repo is shipping with red/missing gate "
                "artifacts: %s. Green them (run `npm run journeys`; commit docs/DESIGN.md "
                "and docs/SPEC.md; wire or mock-mark manifest rows) and re-issue; a "
                "deliberate override re-issues the SAME command with NEXUS_GATE_ACK=1." % txt)
    if sc.once(sid, "dg1_%s_%d" % (rdir, len(items))):
        return ("warn", "DG1",
                "deploy path with missing gate artifacts — %s. These four files are how "
                "'done' stays checkable across sessions (R#27 app twin); a UI capability "
                "with no primitive is ❌ untested — wire it or mark the row mock." % txt)
    return None



def _dual_mode_db_note(rdir, sid):
    """INPROC-DB advisory. A dual-mode driver declared at runtime — remote is correct and
    is the likely case, so this NEVER denies (see `_DUAL_MODE_DB_PACKAGES`).

    LAST in the deploy arm on purpose. A call site is a precedence declaration, not only a
    coverage knob: this arm returns ONE verdict, so anything emitted earlier displaces
    everything after it. A note that fires on correct code must not be able to displace a
    deny, a degraded gate, or a missing-artifact warn — so it speaks only when nothing
    else had anything to say.

    Fail-open and silent on its own error, unlike the INPROC-DB deny two blocks up. The
    asymmetry is deliberate: a deny that a stat error can cancel reads as approval, while
    an advisory that a stat error cancels costs a reminder about a shape that is probably
    fine.
    """
    try:
        hits = hc.dual_mode_db_dependencies(rdir)
    except Exception:
        return None
    if not hits or not sc.once(sid, "dualmodedb_%s" % rdir):
        return None
    named = ", ".join("`%s` (%s, %s)" % (p, m, s) for p, m, s in hits[:3])
    return ("warn", "INPROC-DB",
            "this app declares a dual-mode database driver at runtime: %s. Remote is the "
            "correct shape and is NOT a finding — this is a reminder, not a verdict. The "
            "same driver also opens an EMBEDDED engine from a `file:` URL, and that engine "
            "runs inside the app's own process: a second source of truth the next deploy "
            "swap wipes, on the one thread that also serves requests. Only the connection "
            "URL tells the two apart, and a manifest cannot read it. Confirm the URL points "
            "at the hosted service, and record the store as `Read-path: <surface> "
            "projection|direct|connector · host <where> · divergence <check or none>` in "
            "docs/PRD.md." % named)


def _trailing_notes(rdir, sid):
    """The advisory TAIL of the deploy arm, in precedence order.

    Each note fires on a shape that is very probably CORRECT, so neither may displace a
    deny, a degraded gate or a missing-artifact warn — which is exactly what would happen
    if either were called earlier, since this arm returns one verdict and the first
    non-None wins. Chaining them here keeps that property as the tail grows.
    """
    return _dual_mode_db_note(rdir, sid) or _dev_twin_store_note(rdir, sid)



def _dev_twin_store_note(rdir, sid):
    """TANK-HOME advisory. A database file whose ADDRESS says local-dev twin — `prisma/dev.db`,
    `.data/…`, `*.local.db`. The doctrine permits that twin, so this NEVER demands the
    `Read-path:` row the way TANK-HOME does; it is the file-side `@libsql/client`, correct in
    the likely case and the anti-pattern only once the file reaches the container.

    Fixture-tier files reach neither this nor TANK-HOME. Excluding them silently is the point:
    a fixture is not a store, and a line about one is the over-fire the tiering removed.

    Same fail-open silence and same LAST-in-the-arm placement as `_dual_mode_db_note` above,
    for the reason stated there — one verdict leaves the arm, so an advisory that fires on
    correct work must never be able to displace a deny.
    """
    try:
        hits = hc.dev_twin_store_paths(rdir)
    except Exception:
        return None
    if not hits or not sc.once(sid, "devtwinstore_%s" % rdir):
        return None
    return ("warn", "TANK-HOME",
            "this repo carries a database file whose path reads as the LOCAL-DEV twin: %s. "
            "That twin is permitted and is NOT a finding — this is a reminder, not a verdict, "
            "and no `Read-path:` row is being demanded for it. It becomes the anti-pattern the "
            "moment the file reaches a container: nothing there survives a deploy swap, so a "
            "store beside the code is a second source of truth that diverges silently. Confirm "
            "the deployed image does not carry it (a `.dockerignore`/`.gcloudignore` entry is "
            "the durable answer, not a habit), and home the served copy in a managed store. "
            "The path is the only evidence here — a twin named like a serving store is read as "
            "one, and correctly so." % ", ".join(hits[:3]))


def engine_solo_pulse(fp, rr, sid, caller):
    """BLD1 (W22.7): an app build demonstrably in flight with ZERO crew — ≥5 main-loop
    Write/Edit ops into app-SOURCE files (non-.md; docs/ excluded so P0-P2 artifacts
    never count) of an app-context repo while the session dispatch-log holds no app-*
    dispatch and no solo-ack. The no-fleet INVERSE of C2/EXEC1 (both need dispatches
    to exist before they can fire — a zero-dispatch solo build was invisible). Crew
    callers are exempt: the executor's own writes ARE the engine running. Pure state:
    write-count × repo markers × dispatch-log; NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1 on any Bash command
    marks the user's disclosed solo go for the session."""
    if not sid or (caller or "").startswith("app-"):
        return None
    if not rr or not hc.app_repo_ctx(rr):
        return None
    _n = os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(fp or ""))
    if _n.endswith(".md") or (os.sep + "docs" + os.sep) in _n:
        return None
    sc.log(sid, "app-src-writes", _n)
    if sc.get(sid, "solo-ack"):
        return None
    # W27 ROLE + REPO. The old guard was `any app-* dispatched, ever` — so ONE
    # app-architect (which writes no code at all) excused every main-loop source write
    # for the rest of the session, which is exactly the measured hole. Silence now
    # requires a lane that actually BUILDS, working on THIS repo.
    _rows = _dispatch_rows(sid)
    _has_exec = any(t in EXECUTING_LANES for t, _ in _rows)
    _erepos = _executor_repos(sid)
    # Repo-match is only ENFORCED when the feed has entries: a dispatch whose prompt
    # named no resolvable path records nothing, and absence of evidence there is not
    # evidence of a mismatch.
    _repo_ok = (not _erepos) or (os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(rr)) in _erepos)
    if _has_exec and _repo_ok:
        return None
    _w = len(sc.lines(sid, "app-src-writes"))
    if _has_exec and not _repo_ok and _w >= 5 \
            and sc.once(sid, "bld1r_%s" % os.path.basename(str(rr))):
        return ("BLD1",
                "%d app-source writes in %s, but the executor-family lanes this session "
                "were dispatched against a DIFFERENT repo (%s). Either the writes belong "
                # W44: this ended "— say which.", an imperative whose only discharge is
                # PROSE in the user-visible reply — which leak row 5 forbids. Measured as a
                # driver of the acknowledgement class: a message that arrives where user
                # text arrives and asks a question gets answered where user text is answered.
                # A nudge states the fact and names the action; it does not solicit a reply.
                "in the lane's repo, or this repo has no build lane and the main loop is "
                "hand-editing it. Dispatch the lane against THIS repo, or run any command "
                "with NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1 to record solo. If neither applies: no action, and "
                "do not mention this."
                % (_w, os.path.basename(str(rr)), ", ".join(sorted(
                    os.path.basename(x) for x in _erepos)) or "none recorded"))
    if _w >= 5 and sc.once(sid, "bld1_%d" % (int(time.time()) // 1800)):
        return ("BLD1",
                "app build in flight with NO crew — %d app-source writes this session, "
                "zero app-* dispatches. The ENGINE is the default path (SKILL entry "
                "gate): P1 closes by dispatching app-architect (the plan JSON), the "
                "persistent app-executor builds the surface, review converges it. Solo "
                "is the exception: disclose it, get the user's go, then mark it by "
                "running any command with NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1." % _w)
    return None


def engine_entry_gate(cmd, sid, data, caller):
    """BLD2 (W22.7): first push/deploy from an app-context repo while the session
    dispatch-log holds ZERO app-* dispatches and no solo-ack — the SKILL entry gate's
    off-doctrine line. W23: the ladder condition fired (second measured violation)
    → DENY when the BUILD-MODE card is also absent; card present but zero dispatches
    = warn (the card may quote a solo go the ack flag missed). `.bld2-observe` in the
    hooks dir = observe mode (log would-deny as warn). Crew callers exempt.
    Returns None | ("warn"|"deny", id, text)."""
    if not sid or (caller or "").startswith("app-"):
        return None
    s = hc._strip(cmd)
    if not (re.search(r"nexus\s+vibe\s+deploy\b", s) or re.search(r"\bgit\s+push\b", s)):
        return None
    if hc.ack_present(cmd, "NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1") or sc.get(sid, "solo-ack"):   # W40
        return None
    rdir, _how = hc.resolve_repo(cmd, data, _appid_map(sid))
    if rdir is None or not hc.app_repo_ctx(rdir):
        return None   # DG1 owns the unresolved-repo warning; no double-reporting here
    # W28/F16: and the push must REACH the hosting platform. Same sweep as ACCESS1 above and
    # H2-TURN at Stop — `H2` has excluded public-forge remotes since a measured false fire,
    # and this sibling on the same trigger never got it. A push of source to GitHub deploys
    # nothing, so an app-deploy DENY on it is wrong about the act, and the documented escape
    # trains the reader to carry an override flag on their push command.
    if not hc.push_is_deploying(rdir, cmd):
        return None
    rdir = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(rdir))
    # W27 ROSTER-COMPLETENESS for THIS repo, since THIS repo's last push. "Any app-*
    # dispatched ever" let a single architect — or a lane from another repo, or a crew
    # dispatched three rounds and one repo ago — clear the gate at ship time.
    _rows = _dispatch_rows(sid)
    _since = _last_push_epoch(sid, rdir)
    _erepos = _executor_repos(sid)
    _repo_ok = (not _erepos) or (rdir in _erepos)
    _exec_ok = any(t in EXECUTING_LANES and e >= _since for t, e in _rows) and _repo_ok
    _judge_ok = any(t in JUDGING_LANES and e >= _since for t, e in _rows)
    if _exec_ok and _judge_ok:
        # W28/E03 — the anchor advances ONLY on a push whose roster was COMPLETE.
        #
        # This write used to run unconditionally, BEFORE the verdict, so a push that was
        # WARNED for "no judging seat" still moved the window past the executor that built
        # the wave. Doing exactly what the warning asked — fire a judging seat, push again —
        # then landed on the wrong side of the gate. The gate punished obedience to its own
        # instruction, deterministically at any pace over one second (measured 6/6 at a 2 s
        # gap); below that it was a coin flip on whether a wall-clock second ticked, which
        # is how it read as a flaky test for a release instead of a live defect.
        #
        # "Since the last push" was always meant to ask: has the roster been complete since
        # it last WAS complete? Only a passing push can answer that.
        sc.log(sid, "bld2-push", "%s\t%d" % (rdir, int(time.time())))
        return None
    if _exec_ok and not _judge_ok and sc.once(sid, "bld2j_%s_%d" % (rdir, _since)):
        return ("warn", "BLD2",
                "shipping %s with a build lane but NO judging seat since the last push "
                "(reviewer / assessor / taste all silent). The convergence loop is what "
                "makes a wave shippable — fire at least one judging seat, or record the "
                "user's quotable go to ship unreviewed in docs/BUILD-MODE.md."
                % os.path.basename(rdir))
    _card = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(rdir), "docs", "BUILD-MODE.md"))
    _obs = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".bld2-observe"))
    # W27: say what was actually FOUND. With role-aware predicates the old wording
    # ("ZERO app-* crew dispatches") became a false statement in the common new case —
    # a crew ran, but none of it BUILDS this repo (an architect plans, it does not code).
    _crew = sorted({t for t, _ in _rows if t.startswith("app-")})
    _roster = ("ZERO app-* crew dispatches" if not _crew else
               "app-* crew dispatched (%s) but no lane that BUILDS this repo since its "
               "last push" % ", ".join(_crew))
    _msg = ("pushing/deploying an app repo with %s, no "
            "docs/BUILD-MODE.md card, and no solo go — off-doctrine per the ENGINE "
            "entry gate (SKILL): enter the engine (app-architect → executor → review "
            "wave) and write the card, or — for a user-approved solo build / an "
            "archetype-1/2 service — write the card (Path=SOLO, Authority=quoted go) "
            "and re-issue the SAME command with NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1 (visible, logged)."
            % _roster)
    if not _card:
        if _obs:
            # W28/F05: no limiter in observe — same inversion as ACCESS1, measured 30:1.
            # And a DISTINCT id: this branch and the card-present branch below both wrote
            # `PreToolUse BLD2 warn`, byte-identical, so the live store's single BLD2 warn
            # row cannot say which branch produced it. An observe window whose rows are
            # indistinguishable from an ordinary advisory measures nothing.
            return ("warn", "BLD2-OBS", _msg + " [observe: would-deny]")
        return ("deny", "BLD2", _msg)
    if sc.once(sid, "bld2_%s" % rdir):
        return ("warn", "BLD2", _msg)
    return None

def _repo_root(path):
    """Walk up from a file path to the enclosing repo root (None if none). Pure.
    W23: accepts a `.git` FILE (lane worktree) as well as a directory, and falls back
    to an app-marker root (hc.app_repo_ctx) for pre-`git init` app scaffolds."""
    try:
        d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(path or "")))
        for _ in range(12):
            _g = os.path.join(d, ".git")
            if os.path.isdir(_g) or os.path.isfile(_g):   # dir repo OR lane worktree (gitdir: file)
                return d
            # pre-`git init` app scaffolds: an app marker IS the root signal (W23 —
            # a repo-less directory was invisible to every Write/Edit app gate).
            if hc.app_repo_ctx(d):
                return d
            nd = os.path.dirname(d)
            if nd == d:
                return None
            d = nd
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


_FRONTEND_RE = re.compile(r"\.(tsx|jsx|css|html|vue|svelte)$|/public/|/src/", re.I)


# W28/F12: `prisma/schema.prisma` is the commonest schema file in the Node ecosystem
# and is exactly the irreversible class this gate exists for — `prisma migrate`
# against a changed schema is destructive. Drizzle is the second. Widening the PATH
# set rather than sniffing the diff for DROP/ALTER: a DROP inside a comment or a
# string literal would fire that, which is the substring-instead-of-act class.
_DDL_RE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(migrations?/|drizzle/|schema\.(?:sql|prisma)$|.*\.ddl\.[\w]+$|.*\.migration\.[\w]+$)")


def migrations_lane_gate(fp, rroot, sid):
    """MIGR1: a schema/DDL write in an app repo while no `app-migrations` lane has been
    dispatched. Schema changes are the one class where a wrong autonomous action is easy
    to trigger and impossible to undo, which is why that lane carries a mandatory human
    approval gate no autonomy setting removes. A DDL file edited outside it skips the
    gate entirely. WARN: the write may be legitimate (a fresh scaffold, a fixture)."""
    if not sid or not rroot or not hc.app_repo_ctx(rroot):
        return None
    rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(fp or "")), rroot)
    if not _DDL_RE.search(rel.replace(os.sep, "/")):
        return None
    if any(t == "app-migrations" for t, _ in _dispatch_rows(sid)):
        return None
    if not sc.once(sid, "migr1_%s" % os.path.basename(rroot)):
        return None
    return ("MIGR1",
            "schema/DDL write (%s) with no app-migrations lane dispatched. That lane owns "
            "schema, its reversal path, and backfills, and it carries a MANDATORY approval "
            "gate precisely because this class cannot be undone. Route the change through "
            "it, or say why this file is not a live schema change." % rel)

def open_commitments(sid, exclude=None):
    """[(kind, text)] for every OPEN commitment row in this session's registered cycle
    artifacts. A row is OPEN unless its line carries CLOSED-BY-USER (a PROMISED row closes
    ONLY on a user turn) or, for a DECLINED row, an explicit decision marker.

    `exclude` drops the file currently being written: MAINTAINING the register is how a row is
    recorded in the first place, so firing on that write is noise — and worse, it spends the
    once-key before the write that actually hardens something over the promise."""
    out = []
    _ex = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(exclude)) if exclude else None
    for fp in sc.lines(sid, "cycle-artifacts"):
        fp = str(fp).strip()
        if not fp or not os.path.isfile(fp):
            continue
        if _ex and os.path.abspath(fp) == _ex:
            continue
        try:
            txt = open(fp, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
        except OSError:
            continue
        for m in _COMMIT_ROW_RE.finditer(txt):
            body = m.group("body")
            if re.search(r"CLOSED-BY-USER|DECIDED-BY-USER", body, re.I):
                continue
            out.append((m.group("kind").upper(), body.strip()[:120]))
    return out


def commitment_due(fp, sid):
    """COMMIT1: a write into doctrine or a cycle artifact while an OPEN commitment stands.

    The measured shape: a promise made to the owner, then work continuing over it, and the
    promise surfacing only when the owner remembered it themselves. A promise Cue makes is
    Cue's to return — it cannot be closed by deciding it is no longer needed — and a question
    the owner DECLINED to answer blocks the build that would answer it by default.

    NUDGE only: hardening a write is not wrong, it is wrong to harden it OVER an open promise
    without saying so."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    n = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(fp or "")).replace(os.sep, "/")
    is_doctrine = "/.claude/" in n and any(
        k in n for k in ("/CLAUDE.md", "/skills/", "/agents/", "/hooks/"))
    is_cycle = any(os.path.abspath(str(x).strip()) == os.path.abspath(n)
                   for x in sc.lines(sid, "cycle-artifacts") if str(x).strip())
    if not (is_doctrine or is_cycle):
        return None
    rows = open_commitments(sid, exclude=n)
    if not rows:
        return None
    if not sc.once(sid, "commit1_%d" % len(rows)):
        return None
    kinds = ", ".join(sorted({k for k, _ in rows}))
    first = rows[0][1] or "(row text unreadable)"
    return ("COMMIT1",
            "%d open commitment row(s) stand in this cycle's register (%s) while you harden "
            "another write. The first reads: \"%s\". A PROMISED-BY-CUE row closes ONLY on a "
            "user turn, and a DECLINED-PENDING-CONTEXT row blocks any build that would answer "
            "its question by default — return it to the owner before this write settles, or "
            "say why it does not apply." % (len(rows), kinds, first))


def doctrine_write_p25(fp, sid):
    """P25A: a write into the always-loaded doctrine surface (CLAUDE.md, skills, agents,
    hooks) with no current improvement-cycle artifact registered this session. The
    overfit check is the step that catches a fix aimed at the wrong shape, and doctrine
    is where a wrong-shaped fix is most expensive. NUDGE only — a legitimate hotfix must
    never be blocked."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    n = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(fp or "")).replace(os.sep, "/")
    if "/.claude/" not in n:
        return None
    if not any(k in n for k in ("/.claude/CLAUDE.md", "/.claude/skills/",
                                "/.claude/agents/", "/.claude/hooks/")):
        return None
    if sc.lines(sid, "cycle-artifacts"):
        return None
    # A cycle artifact READ counts as much as one written: this arm fired on its own
    # author's session, where the register and the plan existed but had been authored
    # through the shell, so the write-side feed never saw them. `read-log` is written by
    # the awareness adapter on every Read, which is how a real cycle session looks.
    if any(re.search(r"failure-register|draft-plan|plan-final|-p25-|/ledger-", str(l), re.I)
           for l in sc.lines(sid, "read-log")):
        return None
    if not sc.once(sid, "p25a"):
        return None
    return ("P25A",
            "doctrine write with no improvement-cycle artifact registered this session "
            "(failure register / diagnosis / plan). Doctrine is the most expensive place "
            "to land a wrong-shaped fix, and the overfit check is what catches it: ground "
            "the change in a measured failure first, or say it is a known hotfix.")


def design_lock_warn(fp, rroot, sid, data):
    """DL1 (W19): first frontend-file Write/Edit in an APP-BUILD repo with NO design
    lock on file (docs/DESIGN.md) → once/repo WARN. The measured failure class: whole
    redesign waves burned because no committed visual direction existed before pixels
    (and a fork's donor look is never the canon). File-state only."""
    if not sid or not rroot or not _FRONTEND_RE.search(fp or ""):

    if not hc.app_repo_ctx(rroot):

    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(rroot, "docs", "DESIGN.md")):

    if sc.once(sid, "dl1_" + rroot):

                       "chosen tokens+mockup commit to docs/DESIGN.md BEFORE build "
                       "pixels; 'award-winning' is operationalized by the picked "
