    return None


# W28/F12: the platform's OWN git host was missing, so a real Nexus app repo read as a
# foreign donor codebase — the check that exists to flag "you are building on someone
# else's foundation" greeted you on your own. Live remote shape:
# `https://…@git.<org>.gpt.nexus/vibe/<slug>-preview.git`.
_OWN_FORGE_RE = re.compile(
    r"github\.com[:/](?:NexusGPT|achammah)/"
    r"|git\.(?:[\w-]+\.)*(?:gpt\.)?nexus[\w.-]*[:/]", re.I)


def base_decision_nudge(fp, rroot, sid):
    """BAS1 (W19): FIRST mutation (Write/Edit) inside a FOREIGN-remote repo with no
    base-decision artifact → once/repo NUDGE. A research clone never fires (reading is
    free — the first MUTATION is the adoption tell). Own repos (own forge, or a
    starter-born repo) never fire. Pure git/file state; the fitness judgment itself is
    doctrine's (references/base-decision.md), never the hook's."""
    if not sid or not rroot:
        return None
    # W28/F12: a DOC write is not an adoption tell. BLD1 and BLD3 both apply this
    # exclusion; BAS1 did not, so a README typo fix in a cloned library — where nothing is
    # being adopted — fired the base-decision nudge, as did writing the PRD, which is a P0
    # artifact ONE PHASE BEFORE the adopt-vs-fresh decision this gate polices. The trigger
    # is the first SOURCE write, which is where doctrine puts the decision.
    _n = os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(fp or ""))
    if _n.endswith(".md") or (os.sep + "docs" + os.sep) in _n:
        return None
    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(rroot, ".nexus-starter")):
        return None
    for cand in (os.path.join("docs", "BASE_DECISION.md"), "BASE_DECISION.md",
                 "base-decision.md"):
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(rroot, cand)):
            return None
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", rroot, "remote", "get-url", "origin"],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=3)
        remote = (p.stdout or "").strip()
    except Exception:
        return None
    if not remote or _OWN_FORGE_RE.search(remote):
        return None
    if sc.once(sid, "bas1_" + rroot):
        return ("BAS1", "first mutation in a foreign/donor codebase (%s) with no "
                        "base-decision on file — price the foundation BEFORE building on "
                        "it (references/base-decision.md: stack-vs-goal · LICENSE · "
                        "strip/de-brand surface · build weight · design malleability, "
                        "always priced against build-fresh + org-starter columns; an "
                        "uncertain disqualifier gets a timeboxed spike). Ignore if this "
                        "base was already scorecarded."
                        % re.sub(r"https?://|git@", "", remote)[:60])
    return None


H1_EDIT_CAP = 25


def _surface_runnable(root):
    """[file-state] Is there an app SURFACE a render could show — a package.json
    declaring a runnable script?

    W28/F12. Non-Node caveat, stated rather than hidden: a Python or Go app has no
    package.json and would go silent here. That is a deliberate trade — every archetype
    this skill builds is Node (the starter is a Node package, deploys are git push into a
    Node auto-build), and a missed heartbeat nudge costs far less than the measured cost
    of an unearned one. If a non-Node archetype appears, add Procfile / pyproject.toml as
    further arms of the same `or`."""
    p = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(root or ""), "package.json")
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        return False
    try:
        with open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            scripts = (json.load(fh) or {}).get("scripts") or {}
    except Exception:
        return False    # an unparseable package.json supports no claim either way
    return any(k in scripts for k in ("dev", "start", "preview", "serve"))


def silent_build_pulse(fp, rroot, sid):
    """H1 (W19): a long SILENT build stretch — H1_EDIT_CAP Write/Edits into an
    app-build repo with no render/preview event since the last one → WARN once per
    stretch. The counter resets on any render event (mcp playwright tools · a
    localhost curl · deploy_watch · `npm run journeys` — the last-render feed). The
    build status artifact is a WATCHABLE surface (R#9 build heartbeat), and 'I'm
    getting worried you're not really working' is the measured cost of silence.
    Pure counters + file state."""
    if not sid or not rroot:
        return None
    if not hc.app_repo_ctx(rroot):
        return None
    # W28/F12: an app SURFACE must exist that a render could actually show. `app_repo_ctx`
    # answers "is this an app repo"; H1 is about "is there something to look at", and the
    # doctrine agrees — the heartbeat's object is a SERVING surface (which URL, which copy,
    # which data snapshot), not a repo. Probed against every real directory in this tree,
    # a package.json declaring a runnable script separates 3 real app builds from 2 real
    # non-app cases with no near miss, where the git-remote term fails on 2 of 3 (the
    # remote is wired at provision-repo, later than the first source write).
    if not _surface_runnable(rroot):
        return None
    # ...and a doc write is not build progress. BLD1 and BLD3 both apply this exclusion;
    # H1 was the only one of the three that did not, and it counted every Write/Edit —
    # so editing CLAUDE.md 25 times asked for a localhost preview.
    _n = os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(fp or ""))
    if _n.endswith(".md") or (os.sep + "docs" + os.sep) in _n:
        return None
    now = time.time()
    last_r = float(sc.get(sid, "last-render") or 0)
    sc.log(sid, "app-edits", str(now))
    recent = [x for x in sc.lines(sid, "app-edits") if x and float(x) > last_r]
    if len(recent) >= H1_EDIT_CAP and sc.once(sid, "h1_%d" % int(last_r)):
        return ("H1", "%d edits into the app repo since the last rendered/preview event — "
                      "render + SHARE a watchable surface (localhost URL · screenshot · "
                      "`npm run journeys`) or post a one-line status; a long local-only "
                      "phase offers a localhost preview proactively (R#9 build heartbeat)."
                      % len(recent))
    return None


def _observing(check):
    """[file-state] Is <check> in OBSERVE mode — marker `.<check>-observe` beside
    this file? W45: a new advisory ships observe-first (decision row written, nothing
    surfaced); deleting the marker turns the surface on. Reversible either way, and
    the end state is recorded rather than accidental."""
    try:
        return os.path.exists(os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".%s-observe" % check))
    except Exception:
        return False    # unreadable marker dir → behave as ENFORCING, never silently mute


# Checks whose observe marker SUPPRESSES the surface (decision row only). Opt-in by
# id, deliberately: `LP1` predates this and implements observe INSIDE its predicate by
# APPENDING "[observe]" to a message it still surfaces. A blanket emission-site policy
# silenced it outright — caught by the class sweep across all three `if warns:` sites,
# and the reason this is an allowlist rather than "every id with a marker".
_OBS_SUPPRESSED_IDS = {"CMP1", "MON1", "MON2"}


def _obs_suppressed(check_id):
    return check_id in _OBS_SUPPRESSED_IDS and _observing(check_id.lower())


CMP1_CONTROL_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|[/\\])(?:[A-Za-z0-9_]*"
    r"(?:Table|Filter|Filters|Search|Board|Kanban|Wizard|Form|DataGrid)"
    r"[A-Za-z0-9_]*)\.(?:tsx|jsx)$")


def _inventory_root(rroot):
    """[file-state] Resolve the component-inventory root for this repo, in the
    doctrine's order: INSTALLED package first, then a VENDORED tree carrying a
    provenance marker. Returns the resolved path or None.

    W45/I1. The measured failure: `ux-canon.md` told the reader to open
    `node_modules/@agent-nexus/apps-ui/docs/catalog.json`; npm auth was
    unavailable, the library arrived vendored at `src/ui` with a `.ui-version`
    marker, the prescribed read had nothing to open, and the rule silently
    degraded to 'the app's own components' — reporting GREEN while 20,688 LOC of
    library sat imported 8 times, all one component."""
    r = os.path.expanduser(rroot or "")
    if not r:
        return None
    inst = os.path.join(r, "node_modules", "@agent-nexus", "apps-ui")
    if os.path.isdir(inst):
        return inst
    for cand in ("src/ui", "src/components/ui", "ui"):
        d = os.path.join(r, cand)
        if os.path.isdir(d) and (os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, ".ui-version"))
                                 or os.path.isdir(os.path.join(d, "record-core"))):
            return d
    return None


# W48/H1 — COMMAND POSITION, not mention. The first version matched the tool name after ANY
# whitespace, so `grep -rn playwright docs/` and `echo 'we use playwright here'` both fired.
# Driven on the first run of tests/test_w48_h1.py: 2 false positives out of 5 controls.
#
# A false fire here is worse than noise, because the check is `once` per session: a `grep` in
# the morning BURNS THE FLAG, and the real browser command that afternoon gets nothing. The
# same shape as the URL1 defect two hundred lines down — a substring that merely names a thing
# arming (or disarming) a check that was supposed to be about DOING it.
#
# So the tool must be in COMMAND POSITION: at the start of the command or of a statement
# (`;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, a subshell), optionally behind env assignments, `npx`, or `node`.
# An argument to `grep`/`echo`/`cat` is by construction not in command position.
_STMT = r"(?:^|[;&|(]\s*)(?:\w+=\S+\s+)*"
BROWSER_CMD_RE = re.compile(
    _STMT + r"(?:npx\s+)?(?:playwright|chromium)\b" + r"|"
    + _STMT + r"(?:npx\s+|node\s+)\S*(?:puppeteer|capture\.mjs)" + r"|"
    + _STMT + r"\S*capture\.mjs\b")


def browser_doc_gate(cmd, sid):
    """H1 (W48): a browser-driving command runs while `browser-mechanics.md` is unread this
    session -> NUDGE once per session.

    [pure] Command shape + session read-log. No wording is judged.

    Measured cost of the gap: 34.8 min in one lane, 43% of its drive loop, across four traps
    the shared tool covers NONE of — a space in a path breaking a `file://` URL, a probe
    reading the hidden half of a dual-rendered page, a fixture answering 501, and a capture
    server killed by a sibling lane. Every one presents as an APP defect, so the lane debugs
    the app instead of the harness. The guidance carries all four AND the ruling on when a
    lane may write its own driver, and it was gated REACTIVELY ("when a capture stalls") —
    so a lane that hand-rolled successfully never opened it.

    KEY CHOICE: match the path SEGMENT `references/browser-mechanics.md`, never the bare
    basename and never `browser`. W45/L1 measured the opposite direction: keying CMP1 on a
    2-char basename let an unrelated read silence it for a whole session. A substring that
    DISARMS a guard is the dangerous direction, so the key is made MORE specific, not less.
    """
    if not (sid and cmd):
        return None
    # W48/H1-fp — MASK QUOTED SPANS BEFORE ASKING ABOUT COMMAND POSITION. Found LIVE, in
    # observe mode, firing at its own author: `pgrep -fl "http.server\|vite\|playwright"`
    # tripped it, because the `|` INSIDE the quoted argument matched the statement-separator
    # class and made `playwright` look like the start of a new command. A shell metacharacter
    # inside quotes is a literal, not a separator, and the command-position test is worthless
    # if it cannot tell those apart.
    #
    # This is the second false-positive class on the same predicate: the first build fired on
    # `grep -rn playwright` (a mention as an ARGUMENT), fixed by requiring command position;
    # this one is a mention that FORGES command position. Both matter more than a miss,
    # because the check is once-per-session — a false fire spends the flag on a command that
    # was never going to drive anything.
    _masked = re.sub(r"'[^']*'|\"[^\"]*\"",
                     lambda m: "'" + ("x" * (len(m.group(0)) - 2)) + "'", cmd)
    if not BROWSER_CMD_RE.search(_masked):
        return None
    if sc.has(sid, "read-log", "references/browser-mechanics.md"):
        return None
    # W48/F6 — THE SKILL-LOAD DISARM IS GONE. It read:
    #     if sc.has(sid, "read-log", "skill:nexus-app-builder"): return None
    # justified as "the skill load carries the mechanics block". It does not. The skill file
    # carries a POINTER — one row in a reference table naming `references/browser-mechanics.md`
    # — so loading the skill silenced this gate for the whole session while the agent had read
    # a FILENAME, not the four hazards. That is a proxy that DISARMS a guard, which is the
    # exact direction the docstring above says was refused when choosing the read-log key.
    # Refusing it there and accepting it two lines later is the contradiction, not the rule.
    # The remaining disarm is the real one: the mechanics file itself was read.
    # W48/F4 — NO `sc.once` HERE. This predicate is PURE: it decides, it does not spend
    # state. The once-flag is burned by the EMITTER, only when the advisory actually reaches
    # the reader. Burning it here meant a deny later in the same command exited the adapter
    # first, the nudge was discarded, and the flag was already spent — so H1 stayed silent
    # for the rest of the session, on exactly the browser work it exists to guard. The
    # comment that used to sit at the call site claimed hoisting the check ABOVE the deny
    # sites prevented that. It does not: the hoist guarantees the check RUNS, which spends
    # the flag EARLIER, not later. `nexus-lifecycle.py` fixed this same class and says so —
    # "queue first, then block" — and this adapter's Bash path was the untreated twin.
    # W48 — ID IS `BRD1`, NOT `H1`. This check shipped as H1 for one day and that was an
    # ID COLLISION: `H1` was already taken by the W19 build-pulse check (`silent_build_pulse`,
    # 25 app edits since the last render), one member of the H1/H2/H4 family. Two producers
    # writing the same id makes the decision log AMBIGUOUS — and the decision log is the only
    # evidence the observe ladder reads when deciding whether to enforce. Caught by reading
    # live rows: 22 `H1` warns in one session dated 29-31 July, days before this check existed.
    # The older check keeps the id; a one-day-old check does not get to squat on it.
    _obs = " [observe]" if os.path.exists(os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".brd1-observe")) else ""
    return ("BRD1",
            "you are about to drive a browser and nothing this session has opened "
            "`REF/browser-mechanics.md`. It carries the anti-stall rules, the viewport traps, "
            "and four hazards that all LOOK like app defects (a space in a path breaking a "
            "`file://` URL · a probe reading the hidden half of a dual-rendered page · a "
            "fixture answering 501 · a capture server killed by a sibling lane), AND the "
            "ruling on when you may write your own driver. Read it FIRST — reading it once "
            "already stuck is too late, and that gap measured 34.8 minutes in one lane, 43% "
            "of its drive loop." + _obs)


# W48/B7 — a command that actually FETCHES, as opposed to one that merely NAMES an address.
# `echo "http://localhost:3000"`, a comment, a heredoc and a `grep` for the URL all contain the
# address and fetch nothing; before this gate each of them credited a probe and disarmed URL1.
_FETCH_VERB_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s;&|(])(?:curl|wget|http|xh)\b|"
                            r"\bfetch\(|playwright|puppeteer|capture\.mjs\b")

CMP1_UI_FILE = re.compile(r"\.(?:tsx|jsx)$")
# Control-shaped CODE, in two independent axes. Both must be present, so ordinary
# markup does not trip it: an interactive INPUT surface, and a filtering/sorting
# OPERATION over a collection.
CMP1_SURFACE = re.compile(r"<(?:input|select|textarea)\b|role=[\"']combobox[\"']", re.I)
CMP1_OPERATION = re.compile(r"\.(?:filter|sort)\s*\(|toLowerCase\(\)\s*\.includes\(|"
                            r"\bsearchTerm\b|\bsetFilter|\bfilters\b", re.I)


def _control_shaped(fp, content):
    """[file+content state] Is this file AUTHORING a complex control?

    W45/L4. The first version keyed on the FILENAME (`*Filter*.tsx`, `*Table*.tsx`).
    A live re-test subject wrote the same hand-rolled filter bar into
    `MovementsPage.tsx` — 23 filter/search/select references, its own report saying
    it "implements its own filter logic rather than reuse" — and the check stayed
    silent because the NAME carried no control word. A filename is a proxy; the act
    is authoring the control. Name the act."""
    n = os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(fp or ""))
    if CMP1_CONTROL_RE.search(n):
        return True                      # the name says so outright
    if not CMP1_UI_FILE.search(n) or not content:
        return False
    return bool(CMP1_SURFACE.search(content) and CMP1_OPERATION.search(content))


def component_inventory_gate(fp, rroot, sid, content=None):
    """CMP1 (W45): a COMPLEX CONTROL file is being written into an app repo that
    HAS a resolved component-inventory root, and nothing in this session has read
    that root → NUDGE once per root.

    Pure file + session state: the filename shape (a control family), the root's
    existence on disk, and the session read-log. No wording is inspected."""
    if not (sid and rroot and fp):
        return None
    if not hc.app_repo_ctx(rroot):
        return None
    n = os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(fp))
    if not _control_shaped(n, content):
        return None
    root = _inventory_root(rroot)
    if not root:
        return None                      # nothing to compare against — silent
    if os.path.normpath(root) in n:
        return None                      # writing INSIDE the library is the sanctioned path
    # W45/L1: key on the FULL resolved root, never its basename. The first version used
    # `os.path.basename(root)` — for a vendored tree that is the string "ui", a 2-char
    # substring that `sc.has` matches inside ANY read-log path containing it. Measured
    # live: reading `.../nexus-app-b(ui)lder/references/*.md` silenced CMP1 for the whole
    # session, so a real subagent wrote a hand-rolled filter bar beside the library's own
    # and the check never fired. A substring that DISARMS a guard is the dangerous
    # direction of the substring-not-act class.
    rootkey = os.path.normpath(root)
    if sc.has(sid, "read-log", rootkey) or sc.has(sid, "read-log", "catalog.json"):
        return None                      # the inventory was opened this session
    if not sc.once(sid, "cmp1_%s" % rootkey):
        return None
    return ("CMP1",
            "you are writing a complex control (%s) into an app repo whose component "
            "inventory root resolves to `%s`, and nothing in this session has opened it. "
            "The org library ships matured equivalents (data table · filter/search bar "
            "· kanban · record page · wizard) meant to be IMPORTED and tweaked — "
            "read the root first, then either import from it or record "
            "`not_in_library: <why>` on the todo (ux-canon COMPONENT INVENTORY · "
            "plan-format `component_source`). A vendored tree that arrived with a donor "
            "base IS the library, not the donor's look."
            % (os.path.basename(n), root))


_MON2_UNBOUNDED = re.compile(r"while\s+(?:true|:)\s*(?:;|\n)", re.I)


def watcher_script_gate(fp, content, sid):
    """MON2 (W45): a SCRIPT carrying an unbounded watch loop — `while true` + `sleep`
    with no `break`/`exit` inside it — is being written. Same class as MON1 (a watcher
    armed without its end), different doorway.

    Found live, not by design: a layer-C subject given only "keep an eye on this build
    overnight" wrote `.monitor.sh` (a `while true` loop, 0 break/exit lines) and ran it
    with Bash. MON1 keys on `tool_name == "Monitor"` and never saw it; the loop was
    still running 7.5 minutes later with no terminal condition. Gating one doorway of a
    class is gating none.

    Deliberately NOT fired by R#29's sanctioned short-wait shape — `until <check>; do
    sleep N; done` — which carries a terminal condition by construction. The predicate
    is the UNBOUNDED header, never the presence of a loop."""
    if not (sid and content):
        return None
    n = os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(fp or ""))
    if not n.endswith((".sh", ".bash", ".zsh", ".mjs", ".js", ".py")):
        return None
    if not (_MON2_UNBOUNDED.search(content) and re.search(r"\bsleep\s+\d", content)):
        return None
    if re.search(r"^\s*(break|exit)\b", content, re.M):
        return None                      # it has a way out — not this class
    if not sc.once(sid, "mon2_%s" % os.path.basename(n)):
        return None
    return ("MON2",
            "`%s` carries an UNBOUNDED watch loop (`while true` + `sleep`, no `break` or "
            "`exit` in it). A watcher armed without its end outlives what it watches — "
            "measured: one ran 3 days 7 hours past its target's death, re-running the "
            "test suite every 5 minutes, and 38 of its 73 reports were the session's own "
            "commits reflected back. Give it a terminal condition (exit when the named "
            "target is gone), make its predicate read only that target, and record "
            "`task_id`/PID + target + the stop command where you will find it again "
            "(R#29). R#29's short-wait shape — `until <check>; do sleep N; done` — is "
            "bounded by construction and is not this." % os.path.basename(n))

def dav_overwrite_gate(cmd, sid):
    """HC1/HC2 (W19, DENY-class): write-safety on the server-side workspace write
    vector (`curl -X PUT …/api/dav/<slug>/<path>` — the exact vector that destroyed a
    live PRD by blind full-file overwrite). HC1 read-before-overwrite: the target is
    KNOWN TO EXIST this session (listing/probe feed `ws-known-paths`) with NO read of
    it on record (curl feed `ws-read-paths` · mount feed `ws-file-reads` · own prior
    PUT) → DENY: fetch-then-merge is the contract (R#35 #4). Root-level bare names
    (no `/`) downgrade to WARN — cross-slug listing collisions (every slug has an
    INDEX.md) keep them below the 100%-certainty deny bar (D7). HC2 shrink canary: a
    cached listed size and an upload source <30% of it → DENY as destructive shrink
    unless NEXUS_SHRINK_ACK=1. Unknown/new paths pass silently (safe side)."""
    m = _DAV_WRITE_RE.search(cmd or "")
    if not (sid and m and m.group(1) == "PUT"):
        return None
    pm = re.search(r"/api/dav/([\w.-]+)/([^\s'\"]+)", cmd)
    if not pm:
        return None
    slug, rel = pm.group(1), pm.group(2).strip().strip("/")
    key = f"{slug}:{rel}"
    prior_put = sc.has(sid, "ws-put-paths", "p:" + key)
    sc.log(sid, "ws-put-paths", "p:" + key)
    was_read = (sc.has(sid, "ws-read-paths", key)
                or sc.has(sid, "ws-read-paths", ":" + rel)
                or sc.has(sid, "ws-file-reads", "/" + rel)
                or prior_put)
    known = sc.has(sid, "ws-known-paths", "k:" + rel)
    if known and not was_read:
        if "/" in rel:
            return ("deny", "HC1",
                    "this PUT replaces `%s` in workspace `%s` — a path this session has "
                    "SEEN exists (listing/probe) but never READ. A blind full-file "
                    "overwrite is the PRD-destruction class (R#35 #4): fetch current "
                    "content first (`file?path=` / dav GET / mount Read), merge your "
                    "delta, then re-issue the PUT." % (rel, slug))
        if sc.once(sid, "hc1w_" + key):
            return ("warn", "HC1",
                    "PUT over root-level `%s` in `%s` without a read of it this session — "
                    "read-then-merge before replacing (R#35 #4)." % (rel, slug))
    sizes = sc.get(sid, "ws-sizes") or {}
    old = sizes.get(rel)
    fm = re.search(r"(?:-T|--upload-file|--data-binary\s+@)\s*['\"]?([^\s'\"]+)", cmd)
    if old and fm and not hc.ack_present(cmd, "NEXUS_SHRINK_ACK=1"):   # W40
        try:
            new = os.path.getsize(os.path.expanduser(fm.group(1)))
        except Exception:
            new = None
        if new is not None and old > 2048 and new < old * 0.3:
            return ("deny", "HC2",
                    "this PUT shrinks `%s` from ~%dKB to ~%dKB (>70%% loss) — a replace "
                    "that small is a truncation, not an edit (R#35 #1/#4). Merge into "
                    "current content; a deliberate shrink re-issues with "
                    "NEXUS_SHRINK_ACK=1." % (rel, old // 1024, max(1, (new or 0) // 1024)))
    return None


def pw_ephemeral_path(cmd, sid):
    """PW1: a browser-tool invocation pinning PW= to a path inside a per-session temp dir.

    Those directories are deleted when the session ends, so a brief written today teaches a path
    that breaks for everyone later; the measured failure was a fleet-wide `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`
    naming no remedy. capture.mjs now resolves its own dependency (durable home first), so the
    explicit pin is both unnecessary and actively harmful to copy forward. Warn, never deny: the
    command still works today via fall-through.

    Predicate reads the COMMAND STRING only — no session state, nothing to pre-flight.
    Observe marker: `.pw1-observe` in the hooks dir.
    """
    if "PW=" not in cmd:
        return None
    # only when a browser tool is actually being invoked with it
    if not re.search(r"(capture|probe)\.mjs", cmd):
        return None
    m = re.search(r"PW=(\S+)", cmd)
    if not m:
        return None
    val = m.group(1).strip("\"'")
    # the durable home and a repo-local node_modules are both fine; a session temp dir is not
    if "/.nexus-tools/" in val:
        return None
    if not re.search(r"/(private/)?tmp/claude-\d+/|/scratchpad/", val):
        return None
    _obs = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".pw1-observe"))
    reason = ("`PW=` pins Playwright to a per-session temp path that is deleted when that session ends "
              "— a brief carrying it breaks for every later reader. capture.mjs resolves its own "
              "dependency now (durable `~/.nexus-tools` first), so DROP the `PW=` prefix entirely. "
              "If the tool then errors, run `node <path>/capture.mjs doctor` (it names the exact fix) "
              "or `bootstrap` to repair.")
    # warns entries are 2-tuples (id, reason) — the consumer does `for i, _ in warns` and rebuilds
    # the "⚠ [id] reason" line itself. The 3-tuple ("warn", CODE, msg) form belongs to the gate path.
    return ("PW1", reason + (" [observe]" if _obs else ""))

def _envelope_sig(cmd):
    """W18: base signature for envelope-probe state — a typed `nexus … --json`
    command, or an id-normalized REST path (`nexus api` / curl on the public API).
    None if neither. Shared by feed + nudge so they cannot drift apart."""
    # W28/F06: the class is BOUNDED. `[a-z-]+` followed by `[^|]*` backtracks
    # catastrophically on a long lowercase/hyphen run after `nexus `, and this function is
    # called twice per Bash event. Measured isolated: 4 KB 0.025 s, 8 KB 0.114 s, 16 KB
    # ~0.5 s, 32 KB ~2 s — and end-to-end through the adapter under load the lane measured
    # a 7.2 s stall at 16 KB. There is no timeout anywhere in the adapter, so the user sees
    # a hang with nothing to attribute it to. 16 KB is not exotic: a heredoc'd base64 blob
    # or a long --input payload reaches it. `nexus <resource> <action>` never has a
    # 40-character token, so bounding the class is semantically free. Not "anchor before
    # --json": `[^|]*` would still scan to end-of-string on the NO-MATCH path, which is
    # exactly the path that blows up.
    if len(cmd or "") > 8192:
        return None    # an 8 KB command is not the `--json` shape this advisory is about
    # raw-read: extracts the RESOURCE NAME (an operand) for the feed key.
    m = re.search(r"nexus\s+(?!api\b)([a-z-]{1,40}(?:\s+[a-z-]{1,40})?)[^|]*--json", cmd)
    if m:
        return m.group(1).strip().replace(" ", "_")
    m = re.search(r"nexus\s+api\s+(?:GET|POST|PUT|PATCH)\s+[\"']?(/[\w/?=&.:-]+)", cmd, re.I)
    if not m:
        m = re.search(r"curl[^\n|;]*?(?:api/public/v1|\$NEXUS_BASE_URL)([\w/?=&.:-]*)", cmd)
    if m:
        path = re.sub(r"[0-9a-fA-F-]{16,}", ":id", m.group(1))
        return "rest_" + re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9/_:.-]", "", path.lower()).strip("/").replace("/", "_")[:60]
    return None

_WS_FILE_RE = re.compile(r"workspaces/([\w-]+)/file\?path=([^\s\"'&]+)")

def c3_partial_fetch(cmd, sid):
    """C3 (W10) — a workspace file fetch piped DIRECTLY into a truncating filter: the
    fetched DOCUMENT was not fully read (G#10 partial dump). Pure command mechanics —
    ADJACENCY required: the head/sed stage's immediate upstream pipe segment must be
    the fetch itself (contains `file?path=`, or `curl` + a URL). URL-extraction pipes
    in the blessed recipe (`grep -o 'https://…' | head -1`) and envelope probing
    (`| head -c 300` on a list/get) stay silent by construction."""
    if not sid or not _WS_FILE_RE.search(cmd or ""):
        return None
    # W15 precision: adjacency within ONE STATEMENT only — a captured-var diagnostic
    # (`echo "$RESP" | head -c 300` in an error branch) or an `http*)` case-pattern
    # literal in a later statement is NOT a truncated document fetch.
    # The whole-command _WS_FILE_RE gate already proved a workspace-file fetch happened;
    # the truncation is a C3 hit when head/sed's SAME-STATEMENT upstream is the fetch —
    # a `file?path=` literal OR a `curl` (the signed URL is commonly a variable `$U`, so
    # a literal `http` is NOT required). An `echo "$VAR"|head` diagnostic (upstream not a
    # fetch) stays silent — it truncates the envelope/var, not the document.
    hit = False
    for stmt in hc._stmts(cmd or ""):
        segs = stmt.split("|")
        if any(_TRUNC_HEAD_RE.match(segs[i]) and (
                "file?path=" in segs[i - 1] or "curl" in segs[i - 1])
               for i in range(1, len(segs))):
            hit = True
            break
    if not hit:
        return None
    if sc.once(sid, "c3_partial_fetch"):
        return ("C3", "a workspace document fetch is piped through a truncating filter — the "
                      "document has NOT been fully read (G#10 partial dump); fetch to a local "
                      "file and Read it to completion (R#2: full-read binds to the DOCUMENT, "
                      "not the channel).")
    return None


def kr2_serial_reads(cmd, sid):
    """KR2 (W10) — ≥3 single-file workspace content reads this session with no
    knowledge-retriever dispatch: composite retrieval is the retriever's job (R#48).
    Pure counting (events + path identifiers); the boundary trio (INDEX.md + _meta/*)
    is excluded so the mandated conv-start reads never trip it."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    m = _WS_FILE_RE.search(cmd or "")
    if not m:

    path = m.group(2)
    if path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] == "INDEX.md" or path.startswith("_meta/") or "/_meta/" in path:
        sc.log(sid, "boundary-read", "rest:" + path)   # BND1 feed (W11): the boundary trio was read
        return None
    if "$" in path:

        # If the COMMAND carries the boundary literals anywhere, this loop fetches the
        # boundary trio — feed BND1; either way an unresolvable path never counts toward

        if "INDEX.md" in cmd or "_meta/" in cmd:

    if (len(sc.lines(sid, "ws-file-reads")) >= 3
            and not sc.lines(sid, "retriever-dispatched")

                       "knowledge-retriever dispatch — a composite or multi-file need is served "
                       "consolidated by the retriever (R#48), which reads the indexes fully and "
                       "returns a grounded dossier.")

_WS_FETCH_RE = re.compile(r"workspaces/[\w-]+/files?\?path=")

_SINGLE_FETCH_RE = re.compile(
    r"workspaces/[\w-]+/files?\?path=|external-tool\s+execute\s+\S+\s+--action")

def parallel_serialise_nudge(cmd, sid, cid, caller):
    """PAR1 (W15.3) — a retriever/fleet caller issuing many SEQUENTIAL single-fetch commands
    (one workspace file/listing GET or one CRM `external-tool execute --action` per command),

    CRM query, tool-doc — stacked instead of fanned out in one wave). Counts single-fetch
    commands per caller; nudges once past the threshold if fastpack was not used. NOT a loop
    (FP1 owns loops) and NOT a batched command. Advisory once/caller; fires AFTER the cost, so

                        "lookups in ONE wave (workspace localise ∥ CRM query ∥ tool-doc), "

# PROFSW (W16): a profile switch/login re-points the CLI key but NOT the workspace mounts
# (the registry is org-blind — records no org/profile). A key-only switch leaves every mounted
# slug on the PREVIOUS org → silent wrong-org reads/writes (measured: a whole engagement filed
# into the prior org's KB before the miss surfaced). Nudge once per target profile to remount.
# W28/F20 — the capture was `(\S+)`, so the profile name absorbed whatever source-code
# punctuation followed it. Measured live, this fired three times during an audit on heredocs
# that were WRITING a python fixture file whose contents contained the string, and reported the
# org as `other-org"),` / `nexus_org"),`. Worse than noise: the advisory asserts a FACT about
# session state — "active org → X" — that is false, and instructs a remount of a folder that
# does not exist. A reader who acts on it does the wrong thing. `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` on all three
# regexes (the third already had it), and the match must sit at a COMMAND position.
_PROFSW_PROFILE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\bnexus\s+auth\s+(?:switch|login)\b[^\n;|&]*?--profile\s+([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)")
_PROFSW_BARE_RE = re.compile(r"\bnexus\s+auth\s+switch\s+(?!-)([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)")
# W17: the silent path — the FIRST bare per-call `--profile X` (no auth verb) gets the same
# once-per-profile nudge; hours of correctly-pinned calls against stale mounts fire nothing else.
_PROFSW_ANYUSE_RE = re.compile(r"(^|[\s;&|(])nexus\s+(?!auth\b)[^\n;|&]*?--profile\s+([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)")


def profile_switch_nudge(cmd, sid):
    """PROFSW (W16): a `nexus auth switch/login --profile <p>` (or bare `auth switch <p>`)
    changes the active org on ONE surface only. Nudge once/target-profile to unmount+remount
    every slug for the new org and verify org-by-content before any workspace read/write."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    # W28/F20 — the ACT must sit at a command position; the OPERAND is read from the raw text.
    # Scanning the raw command alone made every MENTION a firing: an `echo`, a commit message,
    # a grep pattern and a heredoc body all reported an org switch that never happened. This is
    # the first consumer of `hc.command_positions`, the shared answer to the question seven
    # checks were each solving privately or not at all.
    _cmd = cmd or ""
    m = next((x for x in (_PROFSW_PROFILE_RE.search(_cmd), _PROFSW_BARE_RE.search(_cmd))
              if hc.at_command_position(_cmd, x)), None)
    if not m:
        m2 = _PROFSW_ANYUSE_RE.search(_cmd)  # W17 first-use path
        if not m2 or not hc.at_command_position(_cmd, m2):
            return None
        p = (m2.group(2) or "").strip().strip("\"'")
    else:
        p = (m.group(1) or "").strip().strip("\"'")
    if not p or p.startswith("-"):
        return None
    if not sc.once(sid, "profsw_" + p):
        return None
    return ("PROFSW",
            "active org → `%s`; a `--profile` switch does NOT re-point the workspace mounts "
            "(the registry is org-blind), so every mounted slug still points at the PREVIOUS "
            "org. Unmount + remount all slugs from `%s`'s folder and verify org-by-content "
            "before any workspace read/write — and decide this org's FILING HOME now "
            "(\"its own GC or a client folder here?\"): every R#34 dispatch inherits the answer." % (p, p))

def _ws_mount_roots():
    """EVERY recorded mount point on this machine, org-blind and deliberately so — the one
    registry reader that does NOT consult `hc.acting_scope()`.

    It asks a different question from `hc.mount_record`. That one resolves a slug TO a
    path the caller then reads and writes under, so it must prove the row is the caller's
    or refuse. This one takes a path the model already chose and asks "is that inside SOME
    workspace mount?", to decide whether `_is_ws_write` treats the call as a workspace
    write and attaches the workspace-write guidance. It hands no path to anybody and
    resolves no slug; the registry is a set of directories here, not a set of owners.

    Org-blindness therefore only ever WIDENS the guard, and widening is the safe
    direction: a stray root from another org's row means one more Write/Edit gets
    workspace treatment. Scoping it would NARROW the guard — and the path that would drop
    out is precisely a write landing inside another org's mount, i.e. the case that most
    needs the guidance, arriving unguarded. `mount_record` refusing an unownable row and
    this returning its mountPath anyway are the same policy read from two ends: refuse to
    hand it over, and still notice when something is standing on it.

    Compare `workspace-mounts.ts findMountsByPath`, which is likewise unscoped, for the
    same reason stated from the CLI side: mount POINTS are machine-wide even though keys
    are org-scoped, so a scope-filtered view of them cannot hold a machine-wide
    invariant.

    Non-dict rows are skipped rather than allowed to raise: a hand-edited registry with
    one string value used to take `.get` on a str, land in the `except`, and return the
    EMPTY list — which is the narrowing direction, so a single malformed row silently
    disarmed the guard for every mount on the machine."""
    try:
        with open(os.path.expanduser("~/.nexus-mcp/workspace-mounts.json")) as fh:
            raw = json.load(fh) or {}
        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
            return []
        return [os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(v.get("mountPath")))
                for v in raw.values()
                if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(v.get("mountPath"), str)
                and v.get("mountPath")]
    except Exception:
        return []


# W28/F08: DELEGATED, not re-declared. This was a FOURTH private copy of the heredoc
# pattern, still the pre-fix shape that requires a newline immediately after the
# delimiter — so it stripped `cat <<'EOF'` but NOT `cat <<'EOF' > file`, `cat <<'EOF' |
# tee`, or an indented terminator. Redirecting a heredoc into a file is how this repo
# writes fixtures, and the hook that instructs the model to do it was blind to the shape.
# The wave that canonicalised this pattern found three copies and swept them; this one
# lived in an adapter under a different name and survived. One definition now.
_HEREDOC_RE = hc._HEREDOC_RE


def _bash_kw(cmd):
    """Strip heredoc bodies so an `-F - <<EOF … EOF` commit message / doc body that MENTIONS a
    curl PUT isn't mistaken for a real write. Quoted URLs are KEPT (a real curl's URL is quoted)."""
    return _HEREDOC_RE.sub(" ", cmd or "")


def _is_ws_write(tname, ti, cmd):
    """Is this tool call a workspace WRITE? A Write/Edit whose file_path is under a mount root,
    OR a real Bash `curl … -X PUT/MKCOL … /api/dav/<slug>` (heredoc-stripped; requires a curl token,
    so a path mentioned in prose doesn't match). Returns (is_write, content_to_scan)."""
    if tname in ("Write", "Edit"):
        # W39/H12: coerced at the READ. `or ""` is the pattern W28/F13's own docstring
        # names as guarding `None` and nothing else — a list or dict `file_path` sailed
        # through it into a path call and exited 1 with a traceback. A crashed adapter is
        # an ABSENT adapter: this one owns the workspace-write guard on every Write/Edit,
        # and it is also wired to `mcp__.*`, whose inputs are shaped by third-party
        # servers. No decision row, non-blocking exit, the tool call proceeds.
        fp = hc.s((ti or {}).get("file_path"))
        if fp:
            t = os.path.normpath(os.path.expanduser(fp))
            if any(t == r or t.startswith(r + "/") for r in _ws_mount_roots()):
                return True, ((ti or {}).get("content") or (ti or {}).get("new_string") or "")
        return False, ""
    if re.search(r"\bcurl\b[^\n]*-X\s*(PUT|MKCOL)\b[^\n]*/api/dav/", _bash_kw(cmd)):
        return True, cmd or ""
    return False, ""


def ws_selfcontain(tname, ti, cmd, sid, caller=""):
    """WSW-SC: a workspace write whose content references a LOCAL/tmp/CODE-FORGE path
    (self-containment, DT-2 / consolidation §12 deliverable preservation). Coverage (each a
    real observed miss): (a) inline Write/Edit bodies on a mount; (b) Bash PUT bodies — the
    HEREDOC segments only (the @file args/key-reads around them are transport, the prior
    whole-command scan false-positived on them) PLUS the `--data-binary @<file>` SOURCE files
    read server-side (≤300KB — pointer-only filings travelled exactly here); (c) a FLEET
    caller's STAGING Write/Edit to ANY path (staged files are PUT verbatim later, so they ARE
    workspace content). Once per CALLER (agent_id) — a session-wide once is consumed by the
    main loop and starves subagent runs of the warn. Returns (id, msg) or None."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    is_w, content = _is_ws_write(tname, ti, cmd)
    if not is_w and caller in hc.FLEET_TYPES and tname in ("Write", "Edit"):
        is_w = True
        content = ((ti or {}).get("content") or (ti or {}).get("new_string") or "")
    if not is_w:
        return None
    src = ""
    if tname == "Bash":
        hit = any(hc.selfcontain_hits(b) for b in hc.heredoc_bodies(cmd))
        if not hit:
            ps = hc.put_body_selfcontain(cmd)
            if ps:
                hit, src = True, " (source file: %s)" % ps[0]
    else:
        hit = hc.local_file_source_ref(content)
    if not hit:
        return None
    if sc.once(sid, "wsw_sc_" + (caller or "main")):
        return ("WSW-SC", "this workspace write references a file OUTSIDE the workspace (a local/tmp "
                          "path or a code-forge repo URL)%s. An org-produced artifact or deliverable the "
                          "entry depends on is UPLOADED (DT-2 artifacts/ co-location; deliverables per "
                          "consolidation §12 preservation) and referenced by its WORKSPACE path — "
                          "repo/local/tmp paths are provenance only, never the home. Upload is a COPY "
                          "(`--data-binary @<source>`): file size / context limits are never a reason "
                          "to point instead of upload." % src)
    return None


def fleet_retrieve_gate(cmd, sid, caller, cid):
    """FW1 (W8: DENY, was WARN): a consolidation-FLEET caller's workspace PUT/MKCOL with no
    retrieval consumed IN ITS OWN RUN (per-caller marker set by: its knowledge-retriever
    dispatch · a dossier/tasks-output read · a workspace file/listing GET). Per-caller twin of
    WSW-RET, whose session-wide flag is satisfied by the MAIN loop's reads and so never
    protects a subagent run (spine §0 step 2 retrieve-first). SELF-HEALING: the agent
    retrieves/reads, the marker sets, the same write passes — so the deny repeats until
    healed (no once-gate). Main-loop writes keep the advisory WSW-RET path. Returns
    (id,msg)|None; caller emits deny."""
    if not sid or caller not in hc.FLEET_TYPES:
        return None
    if not re.search(r"-X\s*(PUT|MKCOL)\b[^\n]*/api/dav/", cmd or ""):
        return None
    if sc.lines(sid, "fleetr_" + cid):
        return None
    return ("FW1", hc.fleet_retrieve_deny_text())


def ws_retrieve_gate(tname, ti, cmd, sid):
    """WSW-RET: the FIRST workspace write this session with no listing-read logged → localise/dedup
    first (R#34 retrieve-first). Soft WARN; once/session."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    is_w, _ = _is_ws_write(tname, ti, cmd)
    if not is_w or sc.has(sid, "ws-listing-read", "Y"):
        return None
    if sc.once(sid, "wsw_ret"):
        # W28/F05: `WSW-RETN`, not `WSW-RET`. The firewall's DENY on a dav PUT and this
        # ADVISORY warn shared one id across two adapters, both wired to PreToolUse:Bash,
        # so both run on the same command — and the registry lists WSW-RET in the blocking
        # tier only. An analyst reading the live store's three `WSW-RET warn` rows concludes
        # the blocking check was downgraded to observe. It never was; they are a different
        # check. This estate already treats a PREFIX overlap as a defect class (it cost one
        # mis-attribution of 10 rows); an EXACT collision across two classes is worse.
        return ("WSW-RETN", "first workspace write this session with no prior listing-read — localise the "
                           "existing graph (INDEX + `nexus api GET \"/workspaces/<slug>/files?path=<dir>\"`) "
                           "and dedup before writing (R#34 retrieve-first); on shared drives, re-list the "
                           "target dir before a FIRST write whose create-vs-update call predates concurrent "
                           "activity — a stale 'this is new' belief is the data-loss vector.")
    return None


def ws_xorg_ref(tname, ti, cmd, sid):
    """WSW-XORG: a COMMUNITY workspace write whose content references a general-context/private path.
    Community KB is cross-org; the org<->community bridge lives on the T0 side only (community-kb-hygiene
    §1). Prompt-style reminder (additionalContext), NOT a deny. Once/session. Returns (id, msg) or None."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    is_w, content = _is_ws_write(tname, ti, cmd)
    if not is_w:
        return None
    # target slug: Write/Edit -> mount path; Bash -> /api/dav/<slug>/ or workspaces/<slug>/
    # W39/H12: coerced at the READ — a non-string `file_path` crashes the adapter,
    # and a crashed adapter is an absent one for that whole tool call.
    where = (hc.s((ti or {}).get("file_path")) if tname in ("Write", "Edit")
             else hc.s(cmd))
    m = re.search(r"/api/dav/([^\s/\"']+)", where) or re.search(r"workspaces/([^\s/\"']+)/", where)
    slug = (m.group(1) if m else "")
    community = slug not in ("", "general-context") and "general-context" not in slug
    if community and "general-context/" in (content or ""):
        if sc.once(sid, "wsw_xorg"):
            return ("WSW-XORG", "this community write references a private path (general-context/...). "
                                "Community KB is cross-org — strip it; the org<->community bridge lives on "

_GNU_ONLY = [
    (r"\bxargs\b[^|<>]*\s-d(\s|=)", "xargs -d → use `find … -print0 | xargs -0`"),
    (r"\bfind\b[^|<>]*\s-printf\b", "find -printf → use `-print0` / `-exec`"),
    # W28/F20 — this arm is evaluated on the RAW command by `shell_portability`, not on the
    # stripped view every other row uses. It has to be: the discriminator between the correct
    # BSD form (`sed -i ''`) and the GNU-only form (`sed -i`) IS a quoted empty string, and
    # `_strip` replaces every quoted span with a space — deleting exactly the thing this row
    # exists to see. Fed the stripped view, it fired on BOTH forms, and its advice ("BSD needs
    # a suffix arg: `sed -i ''`") was a verbatim restatement of what the user had already
    # typed. Measured live: 45 commands contain `sed -i`; 32 are the correct form; the check
    # fired on all 32 and on 0 genuine defects. **100% false, zero true.**
    #
    # Reading the raw command ALONE is not enough — it makes `echo "use sed -i on linux"` a new
    # false positive. Command position is what makes raw-operand reading safe, which is why
    # this row is anchored rather than merely re-pointed.
    (r"(?:^|[;&|(){}]\s*|\n\s*|\bdo\s+|\bthen\s+|\belse\s+|"
     r"(?:xargs|env|sudo|nohup|command|time)\s+(?:-\S+\s+)*)"
     r"sed\s+-i(?![\w.])\s+(?!(?:''|\"\")(?:\s|$))",
     "sed -i → BSD needs a suffix arg: `sed -i ''`"),
    (r"\bgrep\b\s+-[A-Za-z]*P", "grep -P → use `-E` or perl"),
    (r"\breadlink\b\s+-f\b", "readlink -f → not on BSD; use a python one-liner"),
    (r"\bdate\b\s+-d\b", "date -d → not on BSD; use `date -j` or python"),
    # `timeout N …` is GNU coreutils — absent on macOS (`command not found`, so a defensive probe
    # silently no-ops). Anchored so `--connect-timeout 5` / `--timeout 30` / `gtimeout 3` / `timeout=30` do NOT match.
    (r"(?<![\w./-])timeout\s+\d", "timeout(1) → not on macOS; use `gtimeout` (coreutils) or a python `signal.alarm` / `perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV'`"),
]


def shell_portability(cmd, sid):
    """SHELL-PORT: a GNU-only flag on this darwin/BSD host (silently fails or errors). Warn with the
    portable substitute. Once/session. Returns (id, msg) or None."""
    if not sid:
        return None
    # W28/F20 — TWO views, chosen per row. Five of the six rows key on a FLAG whose presence
    # survives quote-stripping (`grep -P`, `readlink -f`, `date -d`, `find -printf`,
    # `timeout N`), so the stripped view is right for them: it keeps a flag mentioned inside a
    # string from firing. The `sed -i` row is the exception — its discriminator IS a quoted
    # empty string, so the stripped view deletes the only thing that tells the correct BSD form
    # from the broken GNU one. Row-by-row rather than one global choice, because the two
    # requirements genuinely conflict and picking either alone breaks half the rows.
    # Verified: `sed -i` is the ONLY operand-sensitive row of the six.
    s = hc._strip(cmd)
    for pat, fix in _GNU_ONLY:
        if re.search(pat, cmd if fix.startswith("sed -i") else s):
            if sc.once(sid, "shell_portability"):
                return ("SHELL-PORT", f"GNU-only flag on a darwin/BSD host (silently fails/errors): {fix}.")
            return None
    return None

_LANE_MD_VETO_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:^|[\s'\"`=(])((?:[\w.~/-]*/)?(?:REPORT|SUMMARY|FINDINGS|ANALYSIS)[\w.-]*\.md)\b",
    re.I)


def lane_md_name_gate(ti, data, sid):
    """LANE-MD (W50): the dispatch prompt names an artifact file the harness will refuse
    to let the lane Write. Returns None | ("deny"|"warn", id, msg).

    [pure + file-state] Identifier match on the dispatch INPUT (filename tokens) plus an
    existence stat — never prose judgement.

    Claude Code >= 2.1.220 rejects a SUBAGENT Write whose basename matches
    /^(REPORT|SUMMARY|FINDINGS|ANALYSIS).*\\.md$/i ("Subagents should return findings as
    text..."; telemetry id tengu_subagent_md_report_blocked; predicate read from the
    shipped 2.1.223 binary 2026-08-06, present since 2.1.220). Measured twice in one week
    before this arm existed: a consolidation lane's report-1-*.md and an app lane's
    REPORT.md, each surfacing only as a mid-flight tool error INSIDE the lane. The
    dispatch is the cheapest catch point: the name is visible before the lane exists.

    TWO TIERS BY FILE STATE, because the hook cannot read intent and must not guess it:
      - the token resolves to a file that DOES NOT EXIST -> the lane can only be meant to
        CREATE it -> DENY, with the rename in the message (a deny names its own fix and is
        re-issued corrected the same turn — the rename is made by the dispatcher, who
        knows the intent, never silently by this hook);
      - the token resolves to an EXISTING file -> probably a READ-reference, which the
        veto does not cover -> WARN once, so an intended overwrite is on record before
        the harness kills it mid-lane.
    Silent auto-rewrite (updatedInput) was considered and REJECTED: at dispatch it cannot
    distinguish read-refs from write targets, and inside the lane it desyncs the path the
    lane believes from the path on disk.

    The regex embeds the harness's own basename-start rule: the banned word sits either
    at a boundary or right after the '/' of an optional directory prefix, so
    weekly-report.md (allowed by the harness — its basename starts with 'weekly') never
    fires."""
    prompt = hc.s((ti or {}).get("prompt", ""))
    if not prompt:
        return None
    cwd = hc.s((data or {}).get("cwd")) or "."
    missing, present = [], []
    for m in _LANE_MD_VETO_RE.finditer(prompt):
        tok = m.group(1)
        cands = [os.path.expanduser(tok)] if tok.startswith(("/", "~")) \
            else [os.path.join(cwd, tok)]
        (present if any(os.path.isfile(c) for c in cands) else missing).append(tok)
    missing = sorted(set(missing))
    present = sorted(set(present))
    if missing:
        return ("deny", "LANE-MD",
                "this dispatch names %s, and no such file exists — so the lane is being "
                "told to CREATE it, and the harness will REFUSE that Write (subagent .md "
                "basenames starting with REPORT/SUMMARY/FINDINGS/ANALYSIS are vetoed "
                "since Claude Code 2.1.220; the lane would only discover it mid-flight "
                "as a tool error). Rename it in the brief — dossier-<topic>.md, "
                "entry-N-<slug>.md, or HANDOFF.md; directory names are unaffected — and "
                "re-issue." % ", ".join(missing[:3]))
    # NOT hash(): str hashing is per-process randomized (PYTHONHASHSEED), and each hook
    # invocation is a fresh process — a randomized once-key re-arms every call, which the
    # contract suite caught on its first run. A digest is stable across processes.
    _pk = hashlib.md5("|".join(present).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
    if present and sc.once(sid, "lanemd_%s" % _pk):
        return ("warn", "LANE-MD",
                "this dispatch names %s — an EXISTING file, so likely a read-reference, "
                "which is fine. But if the lane is meant to OVERWRITE it, the harness "
                "will refuse that Write (subagent .md basenames starting with "
                "REPORT/SUMMARY/FINDINGS/ANALYSIS are vetoed since 2.1.220): brief a "
                "write to dossier-<topic>.md / entry-N-<slug>.md instead."
                % ", ".join(present[:3]))
    return None

            pass   # fail-open: advisory watcher-lifecycle nudge
