                                          + "; ".join(_gprobs[:3])
                                          + ". Enumerate before you partition — shared "
                                          "foundation as a DISPATCHED lane, one lane per "
                                          "screen (a viewport is a screen), one per "
                                          "interaction that owns state, one per produced "
                                          "artifact set; then write `unsplittable_reason` on "
                                          "every unit you merged (`REF/plan-format.md`, "
                                          "\"HOW TO DECOMPOSE\")."))
                        # W48/SHAPE1 — the CUT, which neither of the two above can see.
                        # `partition_valid` asks if the partition is well-formed; GRAN1 asks if
                        # it is fine-grained. A partition can pass both and still be the wrong
                        # cut. Measured on two rollouts of one build, neither seeing the other:
                        # one declared 4 lanes, validated them, DISPATCHED NONE and built solo
                        # (every partition gate fires AT dispatch, so a declared-then-bypassed
                        # partition passes them all by never arriving); the other dispatched
                        # correctly and still lost 49min against a 32min solo build, because
                        # all three lanes re-read the same ten root files and rediscovered the
                        # same six harness traps independently. Its lanes then diverged exactly
                        # where the contract was SILENT — three escaping policies, one of them
                        # none. Four arms, all arithmetic: declared-vs-dispatched · inputs
                        # declared by >1 lane · frozen files no lane owns · worktrees not
                        # provisioned. ADVISORY: a bad cut is a slow plan, not an invalid one.
                        # Count dispatches since the DAG FILE was written — not since the
                        # session began. A build phase that rewrites its partition re-arms the
                        # arm, which is what makes this work across several build phases in one
                        # session rather than only the first.
                        _ndisp = None
                        _dmt = 0        # bound BEFORE the try: the once-key below reads it,
                        try:            # and an unbound name there would raise inside a hook
                            _dmt = os.path.getmtime(_dagf)
                            _ndisp = len([x for x in sc.lines(sid, "agent-dispatch")
                                          if x and float(x) >= _dmt])
                        except Exception:
                            _ndisp = None          # unknown -> that arm declines to judge
                        _sok, _sprobs = hc.partition_shape(_dag, dispatched=_ndisp,
                                                           repo=_ekey)
                        if _sok:
                            sc.log_decision(sid, "PreToolUse", "SHAPE1", "ok")
                        # KEY ON THE DAG VERSION, never the repo. A session can hold several
                        # build phases, and each one writes a NEW partition; a repo-keyed flag
                        # would fire on phase one and stay silent for every later phase in the
                        # same session — silent on exactly the re-partitions most likely to be
                        # rushed. The mtime changes when the partition is rewritten, so a new
                        # cut re-arms and an unchanged cut stays quiet.
                        _sk = "shape1_%s_%d" % (os.path.basename(_ekey), int(_dmt or 0))
                        if not _sok and sc.once(sid, _sk):
                            warns.append(("SHAPE1",
                                          "the partition is valid but the CUT costs more than "
                                          "it saves: " + "; ".join(_sprobs[:3])
                                          + ". Hoist the shared prologue into the root and hand "
                                          "lanes its RESULT; provision every worktree before "
                                          "lane one; give every frozen file an owner. A cut "
                                          "that makes each lane repeat the same reading is "
                                          "slower than not splitting at all."))
                        if not _pok and sc.once(sid, _pw):
                            warns.append(("PARTITION-VALID",
                                          "the lane DAG (docs/lane-dag.json) is invalid before "
                                          "fan-out: " + "; ".join(_pprobs[:3]) + ". Fix the partition "
                                          "(acyclic · pairwise glob-disjoint owns · closure · roots "
                                          "carry no deps · no dup ids) so lanes merge cleanly."))
            if _ekey:
                sc.log(sid, "app-executor-repos", _ekey)
        # W42/OUTPATH v2 (advisory — a nudge has no enforcement to withhold, so no observe
        # marker): a REPORT-producing judging lane (reviewer/assessor/tester/director) whose
        # brief BINDS no output destination. v1 asked "does the brief MENTION a path" and was
        # defeated three measured ways in one session: (1) an unfilled `<reviews-dir>` template
        # was its highest-scoring match; (2) any rich brief's incidental .json/slash token
        # suppressed it; (3) once-per-lane-TYPE-per-SESSION gave a 22-seat wave ≤4 evaluations
        # ever. v2 demands a BINDING (writing verb/label + concrete path, placeholder-free —
        # hc.lane_output_bound, proven 8/8 on the real failing + real clean briefs) and windows
        # the once-key per 30min (the EXEC1 pattern), so every round is actually evaluated.
        # The executor stays EXEMPT (it commits a diff, not a report).
        if st in ("app-reviewer", "app-assessor", "app-tester", "app-design-director"):
            _rpr = hc.s(ti.get("prompt", ""))   # totality: non-string prompt must not raise
            _ow = "outpath_%s_%d" % (st, int(time.time()) // 1800)
            if not hc.lane_output_bound(_rpr) and sc.once(sid, _ow):
                warns.append(("OUTPATH",
                              "this %s brief BINDS no output destination — a path that is "
                              "mentioned but unfilled (`<reviews-dir>`) is a placeholder, not "
                              "a destination (measured: three council waves shipped that way — "
                              "9 verdicts permanently lost, 5 prior-round files overwritten). "
                              "Add a literal filled line — `Reviews dir: _review/round<N>/` "
                              "(the convention) or `WRITE TO <path>` — so every seat writes "
                              "to one named place that survives the lane." % st))
        if st == "app-design-director":
            # DIRSEQ (W28/I): the design director CONSUMES the collated council
            # (docs/ISSUE-LEDGER.md) as its diagnosis, so a dispatch before ANY collate has
            # nothing to read (measured: it ran concurrently with still-running assessors).
            # Repo resolved from app-src-writes, not the dispatch-time cwd (the project root).
            # Advisory (a wave-order nudge, never a block); fires only when NO touched repo has
            # collated — the exact failure, not a multi-repo false positive.
            _repos = _app_repos_pt(sid)
            if _repos and not any(hc.council_collated(_r) for _r in _repos) \
                    and sc.once(sid, "dirseq_%d" % (int(time.time()) // 1800)):
                # W48 — the shared emission loop below logs every warn, so logging here too
                # wrote TWO rows per DIRSEQ warn against one per any single-logged check.
                # Found by tests/test_w48_selfclasses.py on its first run: pre-existing, not
                # introduced by this cycle, and invisible to every count that reads these rows.
                warns.append(("DIRSEQ",
                              "app-design-director dispatched but no touched app repo has a "
                              "collated council (docs/ISSUE-LEDGER.md) — the director consumes "
                              "the collated council as its diagnosis; run the review wave + "
                              "collate FIRST, then dispatch it (SKILL pipeline: director after "
                              "collate)."))
        if st == "knowledge-retriever":
            sc.log(sid, "retriever-dispatched", "Y")   # WL1 evidence: retrieval ran this session
            if caller in hc.FLEET_TYPES:
                sc.log(sid, "fleetr_" + cid, "Y")      # FW1: this fleet run consumed retrieval
            prompt = hc.s(ti.get("prompt", ""))   # totality: non-string prompt must not raise
            if not re.search(r"dossier\s+file\s*:", prompt, re.I) and sc.once(sid, "kr_path"):
                warns.append(("KR-PATH",
                              "the retriever brief carries no `Dossier file:` line — R#48: every "
                              "brief passes an explicit dossier path; the retriever creates that "
                              "file FIRST and appends per finding, so the caller can Read partial "
                              "results mid-run and delivery survives any final-message failure."))
            # W15 KR-BRIEF (once/session, factual): the R#48 lane brief contract. A brief
            # missing the exact `--profile <slug>` is the measured #1 reliability defect
            # (one wrong/absent profile line → wrong-org reads that look plausible), so the
            # profile clause is stated whenever the flag is absent from the brief.
            if sc.once(sid, "kr_brief"):
                _noprof = not re.search(r"--profile\s+\S", prompt)
                warns.append(("KR-BRIEF",
                              "the R#48 lane brief carries: the 4 workspaces each in-scope or "
                              "ruled-out (a NEED is never scoped to one workspace), ask-class packs "
                              "(SoW/pricing → commercial-model; authoring → precedent+voice+canon), "
                              "the exact `--profile <slug>` verified against `auth list`"
                              + (" — ABSENT here" if _noprof else "")
                              + ", and a lane choice; mechanical known-path facts ride a fastpack, "
                              "not the judge."))
            # BND1 (W11, pure events): a retriever dispatch while NO boundary read
            # (INDEX.md / _meta — mount Read or REST fetch) is on record this session.
            # The boundary read is the session's OWN full read; the retriever
            # supplements orientation, never substitutes (measured live: a whole
            # deliverable session ran with zero INDEX/IDENTITY reads). Silent in
            # embedded sessions (no general-context mount registered).
            try:
                with open(os.path.expanduser("~/.nexus-mcp/workspace-mounts.json")) as _mfh:
                    # NOT `"general-context" in mounts`: CLI #2486 keys the registry on
                    # `<kind>:<id>|<slug>`, so bare-slug membership went permanently False
                    # after the rekey and BND1 fell silent on every mounted machine.
                    _gc_known = hc.mount_record(json.load(_mfh) or {}, "general-context",
                                                hc.acting_scope()) is not None
            except Exception:
                _gc_known = False
            if _gc_known and not sc.lines(sid, "boundary-read") and sc.once(sid, "bnd1"):
                warns.append(("BND1",
                              "no boundary read (INDEX.md / _meta) has run this session; "
                              "the boundary read is the session's OWN full read (mount or "
                              "REST `file?path=…`) — the retriever supplements orientation, "
                              "never substitutes."))
            # (W10: the KR-BREADTH audit-shaped-brief check was removed — it interpreted
            # brief wording; hooks are purely logic. §6b fan-out guidance is doctrine.)
            # W8 KR-SHARD (advisory): a 2nd retriever dispatch inside the window from the
            # MAIN loop smells like one brief sharded across peers (the spine's single
            # nested retrieval never shards — skip fleet callers). Pure event/time logic.
            _now = time.time()
            _prior = [float(x) for x in sc.lines(sid, "kr-ts") if x]
            sc.log(sid, "kr-ts", str(_now))
            if caller not in hc.FLEET_TYPES and _prior \
                    and (_now - _prior[-1]) <= hc.SHARD_WINDOW_S and sc.once(sid, "kr_shard"):
                warns.append(("KR-SHARD", hc.kr_shard_text()))
        if st == "nexus-consolidation":
            # Epoch feed: a DISPATCH credits the nag window immediately (the spine's own stop
            # appends the ran-log later) — otherwise the Stop nag re-fires while a spine is
            # still IN FLIGHT and solicits a duplicate dispatch (observed live, W7 day one).
            # Self-healing if the spine dies: the NEXT due event re-arms regardless.
            project = os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR") or data.get("cwd")
            if project:
                # W43-b: ONE clock read for the PAIR. Two adjacent `time.time()` calls skewed
                # the dispatch-time ran-credit from its own dispatched row by ~0.4 ms, so a
                # KILLED dispatch could not be matched by epoch to the credit it created —
                # and the due-check therefore kept counting a killed run as filed.
                _cts = time.time()
                sc.plog(project, "consolidation-ran-log",   # W43: owner-stamped
                        "%s\t%s" % (_cts, sid or "-"))
                # W12 R34-VERIFY feed: the dispatch-time ran-credit above MASKS a dead run
                # (a spine killed mid-flight still looks "ran" to R34-DUE). The dispatched-log
                # pairs with the completion-side verified-log (lifecycle spine-stop + posttool
                # _meta-write) so the Stop check sees dispatch-without-completion past a grace.
                # W33: the row carries its OWNER. This feed drives R34V, which tells a
                # conversation to verify or RE-DISPATCH the spine — an operation only its
                # owner may act on. Unowned, the newest row nagged whichever conversation
                # ended next: measured, one conversation was told to re-dispatch a spine
                # belonging to another, which is both the cross-conversation bleed the
                # owner ruled out and a way to run two spines over one workstream.
                sc.plog(project, "consolidation-dispatched-log",
                        "%s\t%s" % (_cts, sid or "-"))   # W43-b: same epoch as its credit
            # W10 TXP rework (pure logic): the trigger is the ABSENCE of the actual
            # transcript path in the brief — a string-containment check against a value
            # only the hook layer knows — never an interpretation of the brief's wording.
            prompt = hc.s(ti.get("prompt", ""))   # totality: non-string prompt must not raise
            _tp = data.get("transcript_path") or ""
            if _tp and _tp not in prompt and sc.once(sid, "txp"):
                warns.append(("TXP",
                              "session transcript: %s — a brief that needs verbatim user feedback "
                              "passes this path (targeted grep of user turns; never a full read). "
                              "Ignore if this dispatch doesn't sample the transcript." % _tp))
        _lm = lane_md_name_gate(ti, data, sid)   # LANE-MD (W50) harness write-veto pre-catch
        if _lm and _lm[0] == "deny":
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PreToolUse", _lm[1], "deny")
            print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                "permissionDecision": "deny",
                "permissionDecisionReason": f"[{_lm[1]}] {_lm[2]} "
                                            "The corrected form can run immediately in this turn."}}))
            sys.exit(0)
        if _lm:
            warns.append((_lm[1], _lm[2]))
        lg = consol_ledger_checkpoint(st, hc.s(ti.get("prompt", "")), sid)
        if lg:
            warns.append(lg)
        warns.extend(consol_brief_lint(st, hc.s(ti.get("prompt", "")), sid))  # W9 R34-MAT/R34-LEDG
        bh = consolidation_brief_homes(st, hc.s(ti.get("prompt", "")), sid)
        if bh:
            warns.append(bh)
        nm = hc.dispatch_named_bg_warn(st, ti)   # KR-NAME: named bg return-contract agent idles
        if nm and sc.once(sid, "kr_name"):
            warns.append(nm)
        if warns:
            # W45: OBSERVE policy lives HERE, at the emission site, never inside a
            # predicate. A check whose observe-gate sits inside its own function can
            # never be contract-tested for FIRING — measured on CMP1's first run, where
            # three fire assertions returned None and read as defects in the predicate.
            # Pure predicates, one emission policy. Applied at BOTH emission sites in
            # this adapter, not only the one CMP1 rides (R#33 code twin).
            for i, _ in warns:
                sc.log_decision(sid, "PreToolUse", i,
                                "observe" if _obs_suppressed(i) else "warn")
            _surf = [(i, r) for i, r in warns if not _obs_suppressed(i)]
            if _surf:
                print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                    "additionalContext": "\n".join(f"⚠ [{i}] {r}" for i, r in _surf)}}))
        sys.exit(0)
    if tname != "Bash":
        sys.exit(0)
    # We do NOT step aside in bypassPermissions: the deny-class checks below are
    # would-fail-anyway / correctness guards (not permission prompts) and a hook
    # `deny` is honored even in bypass. The warns are advisory context. Bypass
    # users still get the reliability layer; they only skip permission prompts.
    _ti = data.get("tool_input")
    cmd = (_ti or {}).get("command", "") if isinstance(_ti, dict) else ""
    if not isinstance(cmd, str):
        # W28/E09: a non-string `command` (a dict from a misbehaving MCP server, or a
        # harness payload change) crashed the adapter on the first regex — and a crashed
        # firewall means the destructive-command guard did not run for that call. There
        # is nothing to inspect in a malformed command, so treat it as empty and let the
        # native permission layer decide.
        cmd = ""
    sid = data.get("session_id")
    # CAP1 feed (W24): record the org-capability lookups that SATISFY CAP1. Without
    # this the gate is unsatisfiable by construction — the exact class that made G8
    # fire 42 times with 0 possible satisfactions. The satisfying line is named here,
    # in the same file as the predicate, so the pair can never drift apart.
    try:
        if sid and hc.PLATFORM_CHECK_RE.search(cmd):
            sc.log(sid, "platform-check", cmd[:80])
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: optional platform-check feed write
    # Resolve the body: inline JSON, else read the --body <file> so body-shape
    # checks cover file bodies too (the common, docs-recommended case).
    body, _ = hc._body_json(cmd)
    if body is None:
        path = hc.body_file_path(cmd)
        if path:
            try:
                with open(os.path.expanduser(path)) as fh:
                    body = json.load(fh)
            except Exception:
                body = None
    d = hc.classify_bash_reliability(cmd, body=body)

    # DENY wins and short-circuits (the would-fail-anyway set).
    if d and d["decision"] == "deny":
        sc.log_decision(sid, "PreToolUse", d["id"], "deny")
        print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
            "permissionDecision": "deny",
            "permissionDecisionReason": f"[{d['id']}] {d['reason']} "
                                        "The corrected form can run immediately in this turn."}}))
        sys.exit(0)

    # W28/F08 — the ACT view, computed ONCE. Seven nudge checks matched the RAW command,
    # so a heredoc that WRITES a file fired on the file's CONTENTS. Driven: a probe script
    # containing `nexus auth switch`, a recursive grep and a fetch loop drew CP1, FP1 and
    # KR1 — advisories about work that is not happening — and one live incident named an
    # org that does not exist, because the regex group carried the closing quote and comma
    # out of a python list literal. Writing a fixture, a probe or a doc that quotes CLI
    # examples is ordinary work here.
    #
    # This is the "guard names a substring rather than an act" mechanism in its OTHER form:
    # the earlier instances were ANCHORING failures inside one view; this is a VIEW-SELECTION
    # failure — the right view exists and the call site passes the wrong one. Cheaper to fix
    # and easier to regress, because nothing structurally forces the choice. `CHECK 3` in the
    # feed-contract suite is what now forces it.
    #
    # NOT a blanket rebind of `cmd`: `aw5` deliberately tests `"/api/dav/" in cmd` on the RAW
    # string because the dav URL is quoted and would be stripped away, and the deploy and
    # engine gates read `NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1` / `NEXUS_GATE_ACK` from the raw command. Rebinding
    # would silently disarm those. Two named views, each call site stating which it wants.
    # The HEREDOC-only view. Not `hc._strip`, which also removes quoted spans: these seven
    # checks read their evidence OUT of quotes — a workspace URL in a `nexus api GET
    # "..."`, a grep pattern, a profile name — so stripping quotes deleted the very text
    # they match on. Measured: routing them through the quote-stripping view silenced CP1
    # and FP1 on a REAL command, trading a false positive for a false negative. `_bash_kw`
    # exists for exactly this and says so: "Quoted URLs are KEPT (a real curl's URL is
    # quoted)."
    cmd_act = _bash_kw(cmd)

    # W28/F06 — THE LADDER DECISION IS COMPUTED HERE, ABOVE EVERY WARN.
    #
    # It used to run last. A ladder DENY prints and exits, discarding every warn computed
    # above it — but those checks had ALREADY SPENT their one-shot `once()` flags. Obeying
    # the deny and re-issuing the identical command, which is exactly what the deny message
    # instructs, then found them silent for the rest of the session.
    #
    # Measured, driven end to end: `nexus workflow create` is THE build-start command and
    # is denied by G2 on its first call, because G2 requires the design guide to have been
    # read. On that call `flag_kb2_workflow` and `flag_aw5_nexus-workflow-builder` are both
    # burned while neither check emits, and the decision log records only `G2` — so the
    # loss is invisible to the volume audit too. KB2 exists to catch exactly "first
    # workflow build this session with no community-KB consumption on record", which makes
    # it UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION on its own trigger. AW5 goes the same way.
    #
    # This is the shape of the earlier deploy-gate defect one level up: there a gate
    # punished obedience to its own instruction; here a gate consumes its siblings' single
    # shot, and obeying it destroys them. The decision depends only on (sc, sid, cmd, cwd)
    # — nothing the warns produce — so computing it early is a move, not a rewrite. The
    # NUDGE branch stays where the warns are emitted and reads what this block set.
    #
    # NOT applied to the other four in-block deny sites: `engine_entry_gate` reads
    # `solo-ack` and `fleet_retrieve_gate` reads `fleetr_<cid>`, both WRITTEN by the warn
    # block above them, so hoisting those changes what they see. That is the same class and
    # it needs its own cycle — recorded as O35 with the dependency map.
    _lmode, _lpay, _lobs = "allow", {}, None
    try:
        import importlib.util as _ilu
        _hdir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
        _lobs = os.environ.get("NEXUS_LADDER_OBSERVE_MARKER") \
            or os.path.join(_hdir, ".ladder-observe")
        _lspec = _ilu.spec_from_file_location(
            "_ladder_eng", os.path.join(_hdir, "nexus-ladder-engine.py"))
        _leng = _ilu.module_from_spec(_lspec)
        _lspec.loader.exec_module(_leng)
        _lmode, _lpay = _leng.decide(sc, sid, cmd, data.get("cwd") or "")
        if _lmode != "allow":
            sc.log_decision(sid, "ladder-engine",
                            _lpay.get("gid") or ",".join(_lpay.get("gids", [])), _lmode)
            if _lmode == "deny" and not os.path.exists(_lobs):
                print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                    "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                    "permissionDecision": "deny",
                    "permissionDecisionReason": _lpay["message"]}}))
                sys.exit(0)
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: the ladder adapter is optional; its absence must not block the tool

    # BATTERY (W46-hookfix): `git commit` with HOOK SOURCES staged while the green battery
    # stamp is missing or stale for the CURRENT tree — the commit would ship untested
    # guards. Pure state: the staged list (git) × tests/.last-battery {tree} vs the live
    # hash (hc.battery_stamp_state — same definition the runner writes). The stamp is
    # written ONLY by a green tests/run_all_suites.py run; narration is not proof (the
    # measured class: "the battery is running" claimed while the run had died at exit
    # 144). KNOWN limitation for the flip review: the act is matched on the quote-stripped
    # view only, so a HEREDOC body mentioning `git commit` can reach the staged-files
    # check; it then fires only if hook sources are genuinely staged AND the stamp is
    # genuinely stale — a state in which the nudge text is true anyway. Observe marker
    # `.battery-observe` ships PRESENT (record-only) until a layer-C window clears it.
    try:
        _bm = re.search(r"(?:^|[;&|(]\s*)git\s+(?:-\S+\s+)*commit\b",
                        hc.strip_quoted_spans(cmd or ""))
        if _bm:
            _st = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", data.get("cwd") or ".", "diff",
                                  "--cached", "--name-only"],
                                 capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
            _staged = [l for l in (_st.stdout or "").splitlines()
                       if ".claude/hooks/" in l and l.endswith(".py")]
            if _staged:
                _state, _detail = hc.battery_stamp_state()
                if _state != "fresh":
                    _obs = os.path.isfile(os.path.join(
                        os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".battery-observe"))
                    sc.log_decision(sid, "PreToolUse", "BATTERY",
                                    "observe" if _obs else "deny")
                    _bmsg = ("[BATTERY] committing %d hook source file(s) with the battery "
                             "stamp %s (%s). Untested guard changes ship broken guards: run "
                             "`python3 tests/run_all_suites.py` from .claude/hooks (watch "
                             "progress: `tail -f tests/battery-progress.txt`); a GREEN run "
                             "writes the stamp and this same commit then passes. The stamp "
                             "is the only accepted proof — a claimed run without it did not "
                             "happen. A live forced-block subagent trip is owed too before "
                             "any works/done claim on a changed gate."
                             % (len(_staged), _state, _detail))
                    if _obs:
                        print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                            "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                            "additionalContext":
                                "⚠ " + _bmsg + " (observe mode: record-only)"}}))
                    else:
                        print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
                            "hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
                            "permissionDecision": "deny",
                            "permissionDecisionReason": _bmsg}}))
                        sys.exit(0)
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: a broken battery check must never block an unrelated commit

    # Otherwise collect all non-blocking warns into one context block.
    warns = []
    # W48/H1 — collected here so the advisory is available to the emitter below.
    #
    # THE EARLIER COMMENT HERE WAS WRONG and is corrected rather than deleted, because the
    # wrong version is the instructive part. It claimed this hoist PREVENTED the once-flag
    # being burned by a deny later in the same command. It cannot: hoisting guarantees the
    # check RUNS, which spends the flag EARLIER. The flag is now spent by the emitter (see
    # the `_ONCE_KEYS` filter at the bottom of this function), so an exit above it leaves H1
    # armed. The hoist still earns its place — it keeps the collection point above every
    # early return — but it is not the mitigation, and saying so let a real defect sit behind
    # a confident comment for hours.
    _h1 = browser_doc_gate(cmd, sid)
    if _h1:
        warns.append(_h1)
    if d and d["decision"] == "warn":
        # W15: TE5 is once/session — a standing repeat on an already-correct pattern

    # above, before any check spends a once-key; only the nudge merge remains here, reading
    # what that block computed. Observe-gated by `.ladder-observe`. Fail-silent.
    try:
        if _lmode not in ("allow", "deny") and _lobs and not os.path.exists(_lobs):
            _lids = _lpay.get("gid") or ",".join(_lpay.get("gids", []))
            _m = _lpay["message"]
            _bkt = _m.find("] ")
            if _m.startswith("[") and 0 < _bkt < 12:
                _m = _m[_bkt + 2:]                          # strip [Gx] (warns re-adds the id)
            warns.append((_lids, _m))
    except Exception:
        pass   # fail-open: a malformed ladder payload must not block the tool
    # W48/F4 — SPEND ONCE-FLAGS HERE, at the point the advisory actually reaches the reader,
    # never inside a predicate. Everything above this line can still exit via a deny; a flag
    # spent before that exit is spent on a message nobody saw. Only H1 uses this today, but
    # the filter is written so a future once-bounded warn joins by adding one row.
    if warns:
        _ONCE_KEYS = {"BRD1": "brd1_browserdoc"}
        warns = [w for w in warns
                 if w[0] not in _ONCE_KEYS or sc.once(sid, _ONCE_KEYS[w[0]])]
    if warns:
        for i, _ in warns:
            sc.log_decision(sid, "PreToolUse", i, "warn")

        # change reached ONE of four emitters — and it was the smallest one, carrying a
        # single block per turn, while these carry every deny and every warn (2,283 C1 +
        # 859 TE5 + the rest). Two spaces run the advisories together into a paragraph:
        # measured, two advisories arrived as one 748-char run-on. Costs nothing — a
        # newline replaces two spaces, one character less per advisory.
        body = "\n".join(f"⚠ [{i}] {r}" for i, r in warns)
        print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {
            "hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "additionalContext": body}}))
    sys.exit(0)

    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live-wiring + contract test for INPROC-DB — the deploy DENY that reads package.json.

    python3 hooks/test_inprocdb.py hooks/nexus-pretool.py

Drives the REAL entry point as a subprocess. An import-level test proves a helper
returns the right value; only a subprocess proves the entry point wires that helper to
stdin, the session store and the emission fold. A fresh HOME (hence a fresh session
store) PER CASE, so case N cannot discharge case N+1's one-shot key.

Every fixture carries an `Access:` line AND `NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1`, for the reason
test_tankhome.py records: ACCESS1 and BLD2 both DENY above this block, and a deny
short-circuits before INPROC-DB is ever reached. A fixture that trips an earlier gate
proves nothing about this check and reads as a clean pass.

WHY THIS CHECK EXISTS, restated because the suite is only meaningful against it:
TANK-HOME stats the repo working tree for a `.db`/`.sqlite` carrying rows, and names
that limit in its own message — a store the app creates only at RUNTIME is invisible.
The measured defect was exactly that shape: a PGLite projection that lived only in the
container's memory, left no file to stat, and blocked the Node event loop 2.3-3.1s
every 30s at zero traffic. So case 1 and case 5 together are the point of the file:
the engine is caught, and it is caught with NO store file anywhere in the repo.

WHAT LAYER 1 CANNOT PROVE, stated because a suite that overclaims is worse than a
small one. Layer 1 asserts the wiring and the verdict CLASS. It cannot see the
section split (`dependencies` vs `devDependencies`) once the emission is silent for
both a devDependency and a clean repo — silence has one shape. Layer 2 drives the
pure helper directly, which is the only place that split is observable, and the only
place the package list and the depth bound can be read at all.

TWO TIERS, and the split is the thing to keep straight while reading. `_INPROC_DB_PACKAGES`
DENIES and holds only engines that are unconditionally in-process. `_DUAL_MODE_DB_PACKAGES`
WARNS and holds drivers whose documented purpose is a hosted service but which also open an
embedded engine from a `file:` URL — `@libsql/client` is the whole set. Only the connection
URL separates the two uses and a manifest cannot read one, so denying there would refuse the
correct user in order to catch the incorrect one. Cases 10 and 11 are that tier; case 10
asserts BOTH that it speaks and that it does not deny, since either half alone passes while
the tier is broken.

Mutation-proven, both layers together (scripts/mutate.py, or by hand):
  · `_RUNTIME_DEP_SECTIONS`: add "devDependencies"   → layer 1 red (case 3), layer 2 red
  · `_INPROC_DB_PACKAGES`: drop "@electric-sql/pglite" → layer 1 red (cases 1, 5)
  · `inprocess_db_dependencies`: return [] always      → layer 1 red (1, 2, 5), layer 2 red
  · `_INPROC_DB_PACKAGES`: re-add "@libsql/client"     → layer 1 red (10, on the verdict
    class, not on the fire), layer 2 red on the Turso case AND on the disjointness check
  · `_dual_mode_db_note`: unwire both call sites       → layer 1 red (10), layer 2 GREEN —
    the one mutation the contract layer structurally cannot see, which is why case 10
    drives the real entry point rather than the helper
"""

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HOOK = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.join(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "nexus-pretool.py")
HOOKS_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(HOOK))
FAILS = []

ACCESS = "Access: PRIVATE — group ops\n"


def case(name, manifest, want_fire, want_verdict=None, extra_files=(), subdir=None,
         want_msg=None):
    """One deploy through the real hook. `manifest` is the package.json dict (or None
    for a repo with no manifest at all); `subdir` places it one level down."""
    home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="inprocdb-home-")
    repo = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="inprocdb-repo-")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(repo, "docs"), exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", repo], check=True, capture_output=True)
    with open(os.path.join(repo, "docs", "PRD.md"), "w") as fh:
        fh.write("# PRD\n" + ACCESS)
    if manifest is not None:
        target = os.path.join(repo, subdir) if subdir else repo
        os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(target, "package.json"), "w") as fh:
            json.dump(manifest, fh)
    for fn, body in extra_files:
        dest = os.path.join(repo, fn)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
        with open(dest, "w") as fh:
            fh.write(body)

    sid = "inprocdb-%d" % time.time_ns()
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(home, ".nexus-mcp", "cue-session", sid), exist_ok=True)

    env = dict(os.environ, HOME=home, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=sid,
               CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=repo, NEXUS_HOOK_DEBUG="1")
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, HOOK], input=json.dumps({
        "hook_event_name": "PreToolUse", "session_id": sid, "cwd": repo,
        "tool_name": "Bash",
        "tool_input": {"command":
                       "cd %s && NEXUS_SOLO_ACK=1 nexus vibe deploy" % repo}}),
        capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=90)

    blob = p.stdout + p.stderr
    fired = "INPROC-DB" in blob
    ok = fired == want_fire
    # The verdict CLASS matters as much as the fire: this is the only deny on the
    # trigger, and a deny silently demoted to a warn is the failure mode the observe
    # marker exists to make deliberate rather than accidental.
    verdict_ok = True
    denied = p.returncode == 2 or '"permissionDecision": "deny"' in blob \
        or '"permissionDecision":"deny"' in blob
    if want_verdict == "deny":
        verdict_ok = denied
        ok = ok and verdict_ok
    elif want_verdict == "warn":
        # The advisory tier. A note that fires on correct code must NOT deny — that is
        # the entire distinction it exists to draw, and it is invisible to `fired`.
        verdict_ok = not denied
        ok = ok and verdict_ok
    # Both halves of INPROC-DB emit the SAME id and the SAME verdict class, so `fired`
    # and `denied` are identical whichever one spoke. When the case is about WHICH half
    # answered, the message body is the only observable that differs.
    if want_msg is not None:
        ok = ok and (want_msg in blob)
    print("  %-6s %-56s (fired=%s want=%s%s)"
          % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", name, fired, want_fire,
             " %s=%s" % (want_verdict, verdict_ok) if want_verdict else ""))
    if not ok:
        FAILS.append(name)
        print("      rc=%s stdout: %s" % (p.returncode, p.stdout[:700]))
        print("      stderr: %s" % p.stderr[:400])
    elif fired:
        msg = next((l for l in blob.split("\n") if "INPROC-DB" in l), "")
        print("      → %s" % msg.strip()[:200])
    return ok


print("LIVE-WIRING — INPROC-DB driven through the real hook entry point\n")

BASE = {"name": "demo", "version": "1.0.0"}


def mf(**sections):
    m = dict(BASE)
    m.update(sections)
    return m


# 1. FIRES, and DENIES: the measured engine in runtime dependencies.
case("pglite in dependencies → FIRES, deny",
     mf(dependencies={"@electric-sql/pglite": "^0.2.0", "react": "^18.0.0"}),
     True, want_verdict="deny")

# 2. FIRES: optionalDependencies install at runtime too — same image, same defect.
case("better-sqlite3 in optionalDependencies → FIRES",
     mf(optionalDependencies={"better-sqlite3": "^11.0.0"}), True)

# 3. SILENT when the prerequisite is met — the local-dev twin the doctrine permits.
#    This is the case that decides whether the check is usable at all: the corpus
#    explicitly allows PGLite as a LOCAL-ONLY parity twin, so firing here would
#    refuse correct work, and a gate that refuses correct work gets removed.
case("pglite in devDependencies (the permitted local twin) → silent",
     mf(devDependencies={"@electric-sql/pglite": "^0.2.0"}), False)

# 4. SILENT on look-alikes: a CLIENT library talks to a store that outlives the
#    container. That is the CORRECT shape and must never be confused with an engine.
case("pg / mysql2 / redis / mongoose clients → silent",
     mf(dependencies={"pg": "^8.0.0", "mysql2": "^3.0.0", "redis": "^4.0.0",
                      "mongoose": "^8.0.0", "@tanstack/react-query": "^5.0.0"}), False)

# 5. THE POINT OF THE FILE: fires with NO store file anywhere in the repo — the exact
#    blind spot TANK-HOME names in its own message and cannot cover.
case("engine declared, ZERO store files on disk → FIRES (TANK-HOME's blind spot)",
     mf(dependencies={"@electric-sql/pglite": "^0.2.0"}), True, want_verdict="deny")

# 6. SILENT on the ordinary clean app — the starter's own dependency set.
case("clean app (react-query, zod, react) → silent",
     mf(dependencies={"@tanstack/react-query": "^5.101.4", "zod": "^3.23.0",
                      "react": "^18.3.1"}), False)

# 7. Depth: a nested server manifest is the conventional layout and must be read.
case("engine in server/package.json (one level down) → FIRES",
     mf(dependencies={"duckdb": "^1.0.0"}), True, subdir="server")

# 8. NO OPINION, never a pass: a repo with no manifest at all is outside the
#    predicate. Silence here is correct and is asserted so the empty-parse path is
#    exercised rather than assumed.
case("no package.json at all → silent (no opinion)", None, False)

# 10. THE DUAL-MODE TIER, end to end. `@libsql/client` is the Turso driver: remote use
#     is correct and common, embedded use is the anti-pattern, and only the connection
#     URL says which — so the deploy must go through with a note attached. Both halves
#     are asserted, because either alone would pass while the tier was broken: a silent
#     hook would satisfy "did not deny", and a denying hook would satisfy "fired".
#
#     The fixture carries the four DG1 artifacts, unlike every case above. It has to:
#     the deploy arm returns ONE verdict, the note is deliberately LAST in it, and DG1
#     would otherwise answer first and the note would never run. That is the intended
#     precedence, not a workaround — a reminder about a probably-correct driver must not
#     displace a repo with no design lock and no green journey suite. DG1 keeps a
#     one-shot key, so on a repo that does trip it the note simply lands on a later
#     deploy instead of never.
GATE_ARTIFACTS = (("docs/feature-manifest.md", "# Features\n"),
                  ("docs/DESIGN.md", "# Design\n"),
                  ("docs/SPEC.md", "# Spec\n"),
                  ("journeys/.last-pass", ""))

case("dual-mode @libsql/client → FIRES as a note, and does NOT deny",
     mf(dependencies={"@libsql/client": "^0.15.0", "react": "^18.3.1"}),
     True, want_verdict="warn", extra_files=GATE_ARTIFACTS)

# 11. The control for case 10, and the case that decides whether the tier is worth
#     having: the SAME clean fixture with no dual-mode driver stays silent. Without it,
#     a note that fired on every deploy would satisfy case 10 just as well.
case("the same repo without the driver → silent (the note is not unconditional)",
     mf(dependencies={"react": "^18.3.1"}), False, extra_files=GATE_ARTIFACTS)

# 9. Malformed JSON must not crash the hook NOR silently cancel the deploy gate.
#    The predicate skips an unreadable manifest; the emission site must still run.
case("unparseable package.json → silent, hook does not crash",
     None, False, extra_files=[("package.json", "{ this is not json ")])

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the BUILTIN half
# 12-13. The manifest cases above all assume an engine must be INSTALLED to reach the
#     container. Node 22 ships one in the runtime: `node:sqlite` needs no dependency, so
#     every case above returns CLEAN on an app that writes a database beside itself.
#     Measured on three real builds — all three imported `node:sqlite`, all three shipped
#     a `.db`, all three passed both this check and TANK-HOME. Same anti-pattern, same
#     deny; only the declaration moved from the manifest to the import.
case("node:sqlite imported in source, manifest CLEAN → FIRES, deny",
     mf(dependencies={"react": "^18.3.1"}), True, want_verdict="deny",
     extra_files=[("src/db.js",
                   "import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite';\n"
                   "export const db = new DatabaseSync('app.db');\n")])

# 13. `require` is the same declaration in the other module system, and a check keyed to
#     one spelling is a check an ordinary variation walks past.
case("node:sqlite via require() → FIRES, deny",
     mf(dependencies={"express": "^4.19.0"}), True, want_verdict="deny",
     extra_files=[("server/store.cjs",
                   "const { DatabaseSync } = require('node:sqlite');\n")])

# 14. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the case that decides whether the arm is worth having:
#     the same repo shape with ordinary source stays silent. Without it, an arm that
#     fired on every deploy would satisfy cases 12 and 13 just as well.
case("ordinary source, no builtin import → silent",
     mf(dependencies={"react": "^18.3.1"}), False,
     extra_files=[("src/app.js", "import React from 'react';\nexport default React;\n")])

# 15. A near-miss that must NOT fire: `sqlite3` (the installable driver, caught by the
#     manifest arm) and the word `node:sqlite` inside a COMMENT are different things
#     from an import, and only the import declares the engine ships.
case("the string in a comment is not an import → silent",
     mf(dependencies={"react": "^18.3.1"}), False,
     extra_files=[("src/notes.js",
                   "// we deliberately do NOT use node:sqlite here — see docs/PRD.md\n"
                   "export const NOTE = 1;\n")])

# 16. node_modules is never walked. A vendored dependency importing the builtin is not
#     this app's declaration, and walking it would deny on somebody else's code.
case("node:sqlite inside node_modules → silent",
     mf(dependencies={"react": "^18.3.1"}), False,
     extra_files=[("node_modules/some-pkg/index.js",
                   "const x = require('node:sqlite');\n")])

# 17. PRECEDENCE. When BOTH halves have something to say, the manifest arm must be the
#     one that speaks — it names the package the owner can actually move to
#     devDependencies, while the builtin message says there is no such line. Asserted on
#     the message text, because both halves emit the same id and the same verdict class,
#     so `fired` and `deny` are identical either way.
case("manifest AND builtin → one verdict, the manifest one",
     mf(dependencies={"@electric-sql/pglite": "^0.2.0"}), True, want_verdict="deny",
     extra_files=[("src/db.js", "import 'node:sqlite';\n")],
     want_msg="RUNTIME dependencies declare")

print("\nlive-wiring: %s" % ("PASS — all 17 cases" if not FAILS
                             else "FAIL — " + ", ".join(FAILS)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- layer 2
# CONTRACT — the pure helper, driven directly. Layer 1 cannot distinguish "silent
# because devDependencies are exempt" from "silent because nothing ran": silence has
# one shape. Everything below is invisible to layer 1 by construction.

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HOOKS_DIR, "lib"))
import hook_core as hc                                        # noqa: E402

print("\nCONTRACT — inprocess_db_dependencies, driven directly\n")
C_FAILS = []


def hcase(name, got, want):
    ok = got == want
    print("  %-6s %-56s (got=%r, want=%r)" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", name, got, want))
    if not ok:

def _repo(manifest=None, at="package.json", raw=None):
    r = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="inprocdb-unit-")
    p = os.path.join(r, at)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
    with open(p, "w") as fh:
        fh.write(raw if raw is not None else json.dumps(manifest or {}))
    return r


def _names(hits):
    return sorted(pkg for pkg, _m, _s in hits)


def _sections(hits):
    return sorted(sec for _p, _m, sec in hits)


# The section split — the belt layer 1 is blind to.
hcase("dependencies are runtime",
      _names(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(
          _repo({"dependencies": {"@electric-sql/pglite": "1"}}))),
      ["@electric-sql/pglite"])
hcase("devDependencies are EXEMPT (the permitted local twin)",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(
          _repo({"devDependencies": {"@electric-sql/pglite": "1"}})), [])
hcase("optionalDependencies ship, so they count",
      _sections(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(

hcase("peerDependencies are the consumer's, not the image's",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(
          _repo({"peerDependencies": {"better-sqlite3": "1"}})), [])
hcase("the same engine in BOTH sections still reports the runtime one",
      _sections(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(
          _repo({"dependencies": {"lowdb": "1"}, "devDependencies": {"lowdb": "1"}}))),
      ["dependencies"])

# The package list — engines in, clients out.
hcase("wa-sqlite is an engine",
      _names(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"wa-sqlite": "1"}}))),
      ["wa-sqlite"])
hcase("classic-level is an engine",
      _names(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(
          _repo({"dependencies": {"classic-level": "1"}}))), ["classic-level"])
hcase("pg is a CLIENT, not an engine",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"pg": "1"}})), [])
hcase("redis is a CLIENT, not an engine",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"redis": "1"}})), [])
hcase("a name merely CONTAINING sqlite is not matched by substring",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(
          _repo({"dependencies": {"eslint-plugin-sqlite-lint": "1"}})), [])

# The two entries that were wrong on the first pass, pinned by name. They fail
# silently in OPPOSITE directions: `loki` denies a correct app (Storybook
# visual-regression tooling, not a database), and `pglite` can never match at all
# (no such npm package) while padding the list.
hcase("Storybook's `loki` is NOT an engine — listing it would deny correct work",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"loki": "^0.35.0"}})), [])
hcase("`lokijs` IS the database",
      _names(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"lokijs": "1"}}))), ["lokijs"])
hcase("`@lokidb/loki`, its successor, is covered",
      _names(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"@lokidb/loki": "1"}}))),
      ["@lokidb/loki"])
hcase("the non-existent `pglite` is gone; the real package is the scoped one",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"pglite": "1"}})), [])

# DUAL-MODE. `@libsql/client` is the Turso driver and remote is its documented
# purpose — the same shape `pg` and `redis` have, and those are never denied.
# Denying it refuses correct work, which is how a gate gets switched off. The
# engine it depends on, declared DIRECTLY, is a different claim and stays denied.
hcase("the remote Turso driver is NOT denied — the deny would refuse correct work",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"@libsql/client": "^0.15.0"}})), [])
hcase("`libsql` declared directly IS denied — that package is the engine",
      _names(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"libsql": "^0.5.0"}}))),

hcase("the dual-mode driver is reported as an advisory instead",

hcase("optionalDependencies reach the image, so the advisory reads them too",

hcase("devDependencies are exempt from the advisory, exactly as from the deny",
      hc.dual_mode_db_dependencies(_repo({"devDependencies": {"@libsql/client": "1"}})), [])
hcase("a real engine is not ALSO reported as merely dual-mode",
      hc.dual_mode_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": {"@electric-sql/pglite": "1"}})), [])
hcase("the two sets are disjoint — nothing is both denied and advised",
      sorted(hc._INPROC_DB_PACKAGES & hc._DUAL_MODE_DB_PACKAGES), [])

# Empty parse means no opinion — never a pass, and never a crash.
hcase("unparseable manifest yields no opinion",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo(raw="{ nope ")), [])
hcase("a manifest that is a JSON array, not an object, yields no opinion",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo(raw="[1,2,3]")), [])
hcase("dependencies as a string instead of an object yields no opinion",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(_repo({"dependencies": "pglite"})), [])
hcase("a repo with no manifest yields no opinion",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="inprocdb-bare-")), [])

# Depth bound — one level down is read, deeper is not walked.
hcase("server/package.json is read",
      _names(hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(
          _repo({"dependencies": {"nedb": "1"}}, at="server/package.json"))), ["nedb"])
hcase("node_modules is never walked",
      hc.inprocess_db_dependencies(
          _repo({"dependencies": {"pglite": "1"}},
                at="node_modules/x/package.json")), [])

# ------------------------------------------------- layer 2b: the BUILTIN half
# `builtin_db_imports` reads SOURCE, not a manifest, so none of the section/package
# reasoning above transfers to it. Its own two questions are: does an import declare the
# engine, and does anything that merely mentions the name get denied.
print("\nCONTRACT — builtin_db_imports, driven directly\n")


def _srcrepo(*files):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="inprocdb-src-")
    for rel, body in files:
        dest = os.path.join(d, rel)
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest), exist_ok=True)
        with open(dest, "w") as fh:
            fh.write(body)
    return d


def _mods(hits):
    return sorted({m for m, _ in hits})


hcase("an ESM import declares the engine",
      _mods(hc.builtin_db_imports(_srcrepo(
          ("src/db.js", "import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite';\n")))),
      ["node:sqlite"])
hcase("a require() declares it too — one spelling is not the check",
      _mods(hc.builtin_db_imports(_srcrepo(
          ("server/store.cjs", "const s = require('node:sqlite');\n")))),
      ["node:sqlite"])
hcase("double quotes are the same import",
      _mods(hc.builtin_db_imports(_srcrepo(
          ("src/db.ts", 'import "node:sqlite";\n')))), ["node:sqlite"])
hcase("a bare mention in a comment is NOT an import",
      hc.builtin_db_imports(_srcrepo(
          ("src/notes.js", "// not using node:sqlite here\n"))), [])
hcase("the installable driver is the MANIFEST arm's, not this one",
      hc.builtin_db_imports(_srcrepo(
          ("src/db.js", "import sqlite3 from 'sqlite3';\n"))), [])
hcase("node_modules is never walked — a vendored import is not this app's declaration",
      hc.builtin_db_imports(_srcrepo(
          ("node_modules/p/index.js", "require('node:sqlite')\n"))), [])
hcase("non-source extensions are not read",
      hc.builtin_db_imports(_srcrepo(
          ("docs/PRD.md", "we import 'node:sqlite'\n"))), [])
hcase("the FILE is named, so the message can point at it",
      sorted(f for _, f in hc.builtin_db_imports(_srcrepo(
          ("src/a.js", "import 'node:sqlite';\n"),
          ("src/b.mjs", "import 'node:sqlite';\n")))),
      ["src/a.js", "src/b.mjs"])
hcase("a repo with no source at all yields no opinion",
      hc.builtin_db_imports(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="inprocdb-nosrc-")), [])

print("\ncontract: %s" % ("PASS — all 36 checks" if not C_FAILS
                          else "FAIL — " + ", ".join(C_FAILS)))

total = FAILS + C_FAILS
print("\n%s" % ("ALL GREEN — 17 live-wiring + 36 contract"
                if not total else "RED — %d failing: %s" % (len(total), ", ".join(total))))
sys.exit(1 if total else 0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""MOUNTREG — the workspace-mount registry reader, across BOTH on-disk formats.

    python3 hooks/test_mountreg.py

CLI PR #2486 (NEX-2360 / NEX-2372) rekeyed `~/.nexus-mcp/workspace-mounts.json` from
BARE-SLUG keys to `<kind>:<id>|<slug>` keys. Every reader that indexed by bare slug then
resolved NOTHING — and the failure mode is a null, not an error, so a live mount read as
"no workspace mounted" and the layer went quiet on the machines that had the feature
working. This suite is the thing that would have caught it.

The rekey exists because two orgs may now hold one slug, so reading the registry is two
questions, not one: does a row for this slug exist, and is it THIS caller's. Getting the
first right and the second wrong is worse than the silence it replaced — a resolver that
answers "the only row for the slug, whatever its owner" hands an unidentified caller
another tenant's mountPath, and these callers do not print it, they read and write under
it. The `otherorg`/`otherprof` fixtures and the "uniqueness is not ownership" parity
block pin that refusal on both ladders.

Five sections, and the split is deliberate:

  A. the PURE resolver (`hook_core.mount_record` / `mount_path`) over a matrix of both
     formats × acting scopes — exact, so org ROUTING can be asserted by value;
  B. the same matrix through the jq `ws_mount` EXTRACTED FROM `nexus-workspaces/SKILL.md`
     — not a copy of it. A doc snippet the agent pastes into a real shell is executable
     code; testing a transcription would prove only that the transcription works;
  C. LIVE WIRING through the real hook entry points as subprocesses. A resolver can be
     right while nobody calls it — which is exactly the bug: `mount_path` did not exist,
     the call sites indexed a dict;
  D. PARITY — the same HOME + env through BOTH resolvers, asserting they answer
     identically. A and B are two implementations of one ladder; nothing else notices
     when they drift, and they HAVE drifted (the jq de-duplicated the requested FIELD
     while the Python de-duplicated whole RECORDS, so a two-org tie answered from a
     shared `baseUrl` on one side and refused on the other). D also pins the identity
     resolution itself: `NEXUS_API_KEY` bypasses profiles in the CLI, so a resolver that
     reads `config.activeProfile` anyway resolves another tenant's row;
  E. the two OWNER-FIELD predicates both ladders now ask OWNED/OWNERLESS through, pinned
     by value. D proves the ladders agree; E pins WHAT they agree on, so a later edit
     cannot go green on D by relaxing both sides at once — which is how the `false` owner
     stayed invisible while parity was perfect.

Mutation-proven, and these are measured counts, not estimates (re-run them before
changing this paragraph):

  reader reverted to a bare-slug dict index      A 13, C 5
  SKILL.md snippet reverted to a bare-slug jq    B 12, D 62
  jq de-dups the FIELD instead of the record     D 1
  `NEXUS_API_KEY` branch removed · jq            D 3
  `NEXUS_API_KEY` branch removed · py            A 3, D 3
  "unique slug match, whatever its owner" tier re-added:
      to the PYTHON ladder only                  A 9, C 4, D 51
      to the JQ ladder only                      B 9, D 51
      to BOTH                                    A 9, B 9, C 4, D 102

The last block is the correction of a claim this header used to make: that re-adding
that tier "to either ladder turns A, B, C and D red together". It does not. A and C read
the Python ladder, B reads the jq one, and only D reads both — so reverting ONE ladder
turns that ladder's sections red plus D, and all four go red only when both are reverted.
The distinction matters because it is precisely the single-ladder regression that D
exists to catch.

NOTE ON QUOTING — this file SHIPS, and the rule is DESCRIBE, NEVER SPELL. `nexus
claude-code install` writes the whole hooks/ tree to the user's machine
(`bundle-skills.ts` calls `collectFilesMatching(hooksRoot, /.*/)` — an everything
matcher, so .py included; only dotfiles, `__pycache__` and `.pyc` are skipped), and the
CLI's `workspace-registry-skill-compat` tripwire scans that bundle for LITERAL broken
reader strings. A quoted example of the broken form is byte-identical to the broken form,
so this suite names the old shapes in prose and builds its fixtures from `_row()` rather
than pasting registry snippets. The rule admits no exemption for a NEVER-warning, and
none for a RESPELLING that dodges a needle by moving a bracket: both leave the construct
in a shipped file, and the second additionally teaches the next editor how to silence a
real regression.

This header used to add that the broken form was spelled in exactly one place — the
tripwire's needle list, which does not ship. That was false when it was written: two
shipped hook comments spelled the old lookup in subscript notation, which the needle list
does not carry, so the scan was green over them. They describe now, and the preamble in
`lib/hook_core.py` records what the scan does and does not enforce. The CLI-side tripwire
does skip `test_*.py`, scoped to the hooks/ bundle it is about (`isUpstreamTestHarness`
tests the bundle AND the filename, verified against NexusGPT/nexus#2668) — which is what
lets this file describe the shapes at all.
"""

import importlib.util
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "lib"))
import hook_core as hc       # noqa: E402

SKILL = os.path.join(ROOT, "skills", "nexus-workspaces", "SKILL.md")
FAILS = []


def ok(section, name, got, want):
    good = got == want
    print("  %-4s %-58s got=%r want=%r" % ("PASS" if good else "FAIL", name, got, want))
    if not good:
        FAILS.append("%s/%s" % (section, name))
    return good


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── fixtures ────────
# Every shape a real machine can have: pre-rekey, post-rekey, and the MIXED registry a
# mid-upgrade machine actually has (old rows are not rewritten — they migrate on first
# touch, so both live side by side for as long as a slug goes un-remounted).

def _row(slug, path, **kw):
    r = {"slug": slug, "engine": "webdav", "mountPath": path,
         "baseUrl": "https://api.nexusgpt.io", "mountedAt": "2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z"}
    r.update(kw)
    return r


FIX = {
    # pre-NEX-2360: bare-slug keys, no org recorded anywhere.
    "legacy": {
        "general-context": _row("general-context", "/leg/gc"),
        "tools": _row("tools", "/leg/tools"),
    },
    # post-rekey, one org.
    "scoped": {
        "org:org_A|general-context": _row("general-context", "/A/gc", orgId="org_A",
                                          orgName="Acme", profile="acme", readOnly=True),
        "org:org_A|tools": _row("tools", "/A/tools", orgId="org_A", orgName="Acme",
                                profile="acme"),
    },
    # THE case the rekey exists for: two orgs holding one slug at once.
    "twoorg": {
        "org:org_A|general-context": _row("general-context", "/A/gc", orgId="org_A",
                                          orgName="Acme", profile="acme"),
        "org:org_B|general-context": _row("general-context", "/B/gc", orgId="org_B",
                                          orgName="Bee", profile="bee"),
    },
    # mid-upgrade: a legacy gc row alongside a rekeyed tools row.
    "mixed": {
        "general-context": _row("general-context", "/leg/gc"),
        "org:org_A|tools": _row("tools", "/A/tools", orgId="org_A", profile="acme"),
    },
    # mounted before login filled in orgId → keyed and owned by the PROFILE.
    "profkey": {
        "profile:acme|tools": _row("tools", "/P/tools", profile="acme"),
    },
    # raw --api-key / NEXUS_API_KEY, no resolvable org → the anonymous url: bucket.
    "urlkey": {
        "url:https://api.nexusgpt.io|tools": _row("tools", "/U/tools"),
    },
    # THE cross-tenant case. ONE row, owned by org_B, and a caller who is not org_B.
    # Being the only row for the slug is not proof of ownership: `unique` is a property
    # of the registry, `orgId` is a property of the row, and only the second says whose
    # mount this is. A resolver that answers here hands the session another tenant's
    # mountPath, which these callers do not print — they READ and WRITE under it.
    "otherorg": {
        "org:org_B|tools": _row("tools", "/B/tools", orgId="org_B", orgName="Bee",
                                profile="bee"),
    },
    # Same, owned by a PROFILE rather than an org (mounted before login filled in orgId).
    # `ownerConflictsWithScope` treats an unmatched profile as a conflict too, so the
    # profile half of the refusal has to be pinned separately from the org half.
    "otherprof": {
        "profile:bee|tools": _row("tools", "/P/bee/tools", profile="bee"),
    },
}

# (fixture, scope(orgId, profile), slug, expected mountPath)
MATRIX = [
    ("legacy-under-org",      "legacy",  ("org_A", "acme"), "general-context", "/leg/gc"),
    ("legacy-no-identity",    "legacy",  ("", ""),          "general-context", "/leg/gc"),
    ("legacy-tools",          "legacy",  ("org_A", "acme"), "tools",           "/leg/tools"),
    ("scoped-acting-org",     "scoped",  ("org_A", "acme"), "general-context", "/A/gc"),
    ("scoped-tools",          "scoped",  ("org_A", "acme"), "tools",           "/A/tools"),
    ("scoped-other-org",      "scoped",  ("org_B", "bee"),  "general-context", None),
    # An UNIDENTIFIED caller gets nothing from an owned row. This case asserted "/A/gc"
    # until 2026-08 — the expectation encoded the bug (see "the cross-tenant read" below).
    ("scoped-no-identity",    "scoped",  ("", ""),          "general-context", None),
    ("twoorg-picks-A",        "twoorg",  ("org_A", "acme"), "general-context", "/A/gc"),
    ("twoorg-picks-B",        "twoorg",  ("org_B", "bee"),  "general-context", "/B/gc"),
    ("twoorg-tie-refuses",    "twoorg",  ("", ""),          "general-context", None),
    ("twoorg-third-org",      "twoorg",  ("org_C", "cee"),  "general-context", None),
    ("mixed-legacy-half",     "mixed",   ("org_A", "acme"), "general-context", "/leg/gc"),
    ("mixed-scoped-half",     "mixed",   ("org_A", "acme"), "tools",           "/A/tools"),
    ("profkey-by-profile",    "profkey", ("", "acme"),      "tools",           "/P/tools"),
    ("profkey-org-and-prof",  "profkey", ("org_A", "acme"), "tools",           "/P/tools"),
    ("profkey-wrong-profile", "profkey", ("org_A", "zzz"),  "tools",           None),
    ("urlkey-ownerless",      "urlkey",  ("org_A", "acme"), "tools",           "/U/tools"),
    ("urlkey-no-identity",    "urlkey",  ("", ""),          "tools",           "/U/tools"),
    ("absent-slug",           "scoped",  ("org_A", "acme"), "systems",         None),

    # ── the cross-tenant read ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    ("otherorg-wrong-org",    "otherorg",  ("org_A", "acme"), "tools",  None),
    ("otherorg-org-only",     "otherorg",  ("org_A", ""),     "tools",  None),
    ("otherorg-prof-only",    "otherorg",  ("", "acme"),      "tools",  None),

for name, fx, scope, slug, want in MATRIX:

ok("A", "baseUrl-field",

# NEX-2372's readback: mode and org ARE on the record (the runbook now says so).

# acting_scope reads env + config the way resolveProfile → actingScope does.
SCOPE_ENV = ("NEXUS_PROFILE", "NEXUS_ORGANIZATION_ID", "NEXUS_API_KEY")


def _cfg_home(cfg):

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(h, ".nexus-mcp"))

_h = _cfg_home({"activeProfile": "acme",
                "profiles": {"acme": {"apiKey": "nxs_x", "orgId": "org_A"},

                     "profiles": {"default": {"apiKey": "nxs_d", "orgId": "org_D"}}})

_env0 = {k: os.environ.pop(k, None) for k in SCOPE_ENV}
ok("A", "scope-from-activeProfile", hc.acting_scope(_h), ("org_A", "acme"))
ok("A", "scope-default-profile-fallback", hc.acting_scope(_hdef), ("org_D", "default"))

os.environ["NEXUS_PROFILE"] = "bee"

def extract_ws_mount():
    """The fenced bash block in SKILL.md that DEFINES ws_mount. Extracted so the suite
    tests what the agent actually pastes into a shell — a transcription would only ever
    prove the transcription."""
    with open(SKILL, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        lines = fh.read().split("\n")
    block, inside = [], False
    for ln in lines:
        if ln.startswith("```"):
            if inside:
                if any("ws_mount()" in b for b in block):
                    return "\n".join(block)
                block, inside = [], False
                continue
            inside, block = True, []
            continue
        if inside:
            block.append(ln)
    return None

# ──────────── B2 · every published `ws_path` snippet carries its definitions ──
#
# `ws_path` calls `ws_mount`, and NEITHER is a shell builtin. A doc snippet is pasted
# into a FRESH bash invocation, so a snippet that names `ws_path` without carrying the
# `ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}` elision is not runnable — and its failure is the silent
# one this whole file is about: `$(ws_path tools …)` with `ws_path` undefined expands to
# the empty string, `grep … ""/plugins/*/README.md` finds nothing, and 0 hits reads as
# "nothing filed" instead of "the command was broken".
#
# The sweep that added `ws_mount` to these snippets rewrote every site that already said
# `ws_path(){…}` and missed every site that carried NO elision at all — a search-and-
# replace can only find what it is replacing. So the invariant gets a check instead of
# another sweep: it enumerates the shipped surfaces itself, and a new doc is covered the
# day it is written.
#
# Judged per BACKTICK SPAN / fenced block, not per line: two snippets can share a line
# (the ✗/✓ contrast pairs do), and an agent pastes one span, not a line. `$(ws_path` is
# the marker for "executable" — a command substitution never appears in prose, while
# `ws_path` bare or with a placeholder arg routinely does. A snippet whose argument is
# the literal `<slug>` placeholder is the REWRITE RULE itself, not a call site, and is
# not runnable by construction.
print("\nB2 · shipped `ws_path` snippets carry `ws_mount(){…}; ws_path(){…}`\n")

_DOC_FILES = [os.path.join(ROOT, "CLAUDE.md")]
for _r in _DOC_ROOTS:
    for _dp, _dn, _fn in os.walk(_r):
        _DOC_FILES += [os.path.join(_dp, f) for f in _fn if f.endswith(".md")]

_SPAN = __import__("re").compile(r"`{1,3}[^`]+`{1,3}|```[a-z]*\n.*?\n```",
                                 __import__("re").S)
_bare = []
_covered = 0
for _f in sorted(_DOC_FILES):
    try:
        with open(_f, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            _txt = fh.read()
    except Exception:
        continue
    for _m in _SPAN.finditer(_txt):
        _s = _m.group(0)
        if "$(ws_path " not in _s:

        if "$(ws_path <slug>" in _s:      # the rewrite rule's own placeholder
            continue

def _home_with(mounts, org="org_A", prof="acme", make_dirs=(), identity=True):
    """A HOME the hooks will read. `identity=False` writes NO config.json — the state a
    machine is in when the CLI was never logged in on it, when the config is unreadable,
    or when a raw NEXUS_API_KEY is in play: `acting_scope()` returns ("", "") and the
    hooks must fall back to ownerless rows only, never to whatever row is there."""
    home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mountreg-live-")
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(home, ".nexus-mcp"))
    with open(os.path.join(home, ".nexus-mcp", "workspace-mounts.json"), "w") as fh:
        json.dump(mounts, fh)
    if identity:
        with open(os.path.join(home, ".nexus-mcp", "config.json"), "w") as fh:
            json.dump({"activeProfile": prof, "profiles": {prof: {"orgId": org}}}, fh)
    for d in make_dirs:
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(d, "INDEX.md"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write("# INDEX\n")
    return home


def run_hook(hook, payload, home, sid):
    env = dict(os.environ, HOME=home, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=sid)
    for k in SCOPE_ENV:
        env.pop(k, None)
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(HERE, hook)],
                       input=json.dumps(payload), capture_output=True, text=True,
                       env=env, timeout=90)
    return p.stdout + p.stderr

def firewall_scope(label, cmd, mounts, want, identity=True):
    """`nexus-fs-firewall.py`'s WORK-DIR set — the ALLOW side of the registry, and the
    one reader whose org-blindness could NOT be waved through.

    Everywhere else in this adapter the mount roots feed a DENY (WSW, the protected-root
    containment), where reading them org-blind only ever WIDENS a guard and a stray root
    is harmless. `work` is the opposite polarity: the adapter's terminal branch turns
    "every target is under a work dir" into `allow`, and an `allow` SUPPRESSES the host's
    own permission prompt. So a foreign org's mount root in `work` widens the
    AUTO-APPROVAL, and this file's own rule is that an allow is worse than a miss.

    WSW already denies a mutating op whose WRITE TARGET is a mount path, org-blind, which
    is why this went unnoticed: the reachable shape is a mutating command whose write
    target is elsewhere and which names the foreign mount as a READ SOURCE. Driven, on
    the tree before the fix, acting as org_A with org_B also mounted:

        cp <org_B mount>/INDEX.md /tmp/x.md      ->  allow      (prompt suppressed)

    The mount roots here must sit outside /tmp, $TMPDIR, /mnt/workspace, the project dir
    and cwd — all unconditional work dirs. The first version of this probe put them under
    /tmp and measured no difference between the broken and the fixed tree."""
    home = _home_with(mounts, identity=identity)
    proj = os.path.join(home, "proj")
    os.makedirs(proj, exist_ok=True)
    env = dict(os.environ, HOME=home, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=proj)
    for k in SCOPE_ENV + ("TMPDIR",):
        env.pop(k, None)
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(HERE, "nexus-fs-firewall.py")],
                       input=json.dumps({"tool_name": "Bash", "cwd": proj,
                                         "tool_input": {"command": cmd}}),
                       capture_output=True, text=True, env=env, timeout=90)
    out = p.stdout or ""
    got = "allow" if '"allow"' in out else ("deny" if '"deny"' in out else "defer")
    ok("C", label, got, want)

# ─────────── D · parity — one HOME + env, both resolvers, same answer ────────
#
# A and B are two implementations of one ladder. Nothing else in either repo notices when
# they drift, and they DID drift three times:
#
#   * the jq de-duplicated the REQUESTED FIELD (`[$pick[]|.value[$f]] | unique`) while the
#     Python de-duplicated whole RECORDS. Two orgs holding one slug share a `baseUrl`, so
#     `ws_mount <slug> baseUrl` ANSWERED on a tie the Python refused — and the bulk-PUT
#     recipe treats a non-empty BASE as permission to upload;
#   * `acting_scope` read `config.activeProfile` even under `NEXUS_API_KEY`, which the CLI
#     ignores profiles for entirely. On a machine with two orgs' rows that resolved the
#     logged-in org's mount while the CLI acted as nobody;
#   * both ladders then AGREED on a wrong answer — a last tier that returned the unique
#     slug match whatever its owner, so an unidentified caller resolved another org's row.
#     Parity found nothing because parity was never the property at stake.
#
# All three are cross-tenant reads, and none is visible from inside one implementation, so
# parity is asserted here against a WANT — agreement on a wrong answer is not the bar, and
# the third drift is the proof of that: two ladders in perfect agreement, both wrong.

print("\nD · parity — identical HOME + env through the Python ladder and the jq ladder\n")

    def _parity(label, mounts, cfg, env_over, slug, field, want):
        home = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="mountreg-par-")
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(home, ".nexus-mcp"))
        with open(os.path.join(home, ".nexus-mcp", "workspace-mounts.json"), "w") as fh:
            json.dump(mounts, fh)
        with open(os.path.join(home, ".nexus-mcp", "config.json"), "w") as fh:
            json.dump(cfg, fh)

        saved = {k: os.environ.get(k) for k in SCOPE_ENV}
        for k in SCOPE_ENV:
            os.environ.pop(k, None)
        os.environ.update(env_over)
        try:
            rec = hc.mount_record(mounts, slug, hc.acting_scope(home))
            raw = (rec or {}).get(field)
        finally:
            for k in SCOPE_ENV:
                os.environ.pop(k, None)
            for k, v in saved.items():
                if v is not None:
                    os.environ[k] = v

            env.pop(k, None)

            "org:org_B|tools": _row("tools", "/B/t", orgId="org_B", profile="bee")}

    _parity("legacy ownerless row · no identity → still resolved",
